Verification: Live on bldg2: first re-ingestion after the fix reported spaces=16/16/20 with linked=16/16/20 (was spaces=32/32/40), and a SECOND re-ingestion returned exactly the same 52 spaces at 100% - a true no-op. tests/test_floor_plan_space_merge.py TestIdempotenceUnderReingestion pins both properties: merging a merged result changes nothing, and a legacy 32-record manifest collapses to 16 on the next merge with every room keeping its IRI and its area.

Title: A named room's area question returns the whole-building floor-area table
Description: 'How big is RM001A_room?' answers with a Floor Areas table for all three floors (320.0 / 320.0 / 400.0, total 1040.0) instead of that room's 20.0 m2. The named referent is dropped and the question is answered at building scope. Noticed while verifying BUG-147 live; adjacency and room-count questions for the same room answer correctly, so this is answer scoping, not missing data.
Root_Cause: SpatialAgent._answer routed EVERY _AREA_QUERY_RE match (minus the greater-than/less-than filters) straight to _answer_total_area(manifests), which does not look at the query at all. There was no single-space branch, so a named room could never be the subject of its own area question. The data was never the problem: after the BUG-147 merge the record carries area_m2=20.0 next to its ontology IRI, and the adjacency answer for the same room reads that same record.
Fix_Approach: _answer_space_area() runs before the building-wide fallback and returns None when the query names no space, so building- and floor-scoped questions keep their existing answer verbatim. Space resolution reuses _find_zone_by_label, already used by the adjacency path, so 'RM101' resolves to 'RM101_room' without a second matching rule to keep in sync. When the named space exists but carries no geometry the answer says which room lacks an area rather than falling through to the building total, because a plausible number standing in for a missing one is the failure mode this system exists to avoid.
Verification: Live on bldg2: 'How big is RM001A_room?' now answers '**RM001A_room** (`0Z001`, floor 0) is **20.0 m2**. Perimeter: 18.0 m. That is 6.2% of floor 0 (320.0 m2 across 16 spaces).' — was a three-floor table totalling 1,040 m2. 'What is the total floor area of the building?' still answers at building scope. 9 tests in tests/test_space_area_scope.py cover the named-room answer, the untouched building/floor scopes, the missing-geometry message and an unknown room. Suite 1700 pass, 4 skip.

Title: A reported fault was summarised instead of filed
Description: 'The toilet on floor 1 is leaking.' returned a formatted Executive Summary about the leak - complete with a generated timestamp - and filed NOTHING. Someone reporting a problem got a document back and no ticket, so the fault existed only in the chat transcript. Found while smoke-testing routing after the TODO-081 excision; confirmed pre-existing and NOT caused by it (the static report_intake_intent guard returns 'maintenance' for this exact string both before and after).
Root_Cause: The _r_report_intake override in routing_contract only ran when the LLM's intent was in a short allow-list - capability, general, greeting, metadata, clarification, discovery, None - and 'report' was not in it. But 'report' is the single most likely misclassification for a sentence that reports a problem, because reporting a fault and generating a report sit in the same semantic neighbourhood. The rescue that exists precisely for this case was blind to the case it most needed to catch.
Fix_Approach: Added 'report' to that allow-list, in the routing_contract - the single place routing overrides are allowed to live (CLAUDE.md), never as a new inline override in dialogue_agent. Safe because the rescue is CONDITIONAL on report_intake_intent() also firing, and that recognises statement shapes only: 'give me a report on energy use', 'generate a summary report for floor 2', 'report on CO2 last week', 'I need a report of all anomalies' and 'show me the monthly report' all return None and keep the summary lane. Rule ORDER is unchanged, so the precedence pin in test_routing_contract.py is unaffected (106 pass).
Verification: Live on bldg2 after a cache flush: 'The toilet on floor 1 is leaking.' now routes to maintenance and answers 'your maintenance request has been logged as REP-3AC023 - Category: Maintenance request, Priority: HIGH, Status: OPEN'. 15 tests in tests/test_report_statement_vs_report_request.py cover the rescue from the 'report' intent, the intents that already worked, five genuine report requests that must NOT be diverted, and four unrelated intents (sensor_data/analytics/control/floor_plan) confirming the gate did not open generally. Suite 1721 pass, 2 skip.

Title: A genuine report request can be classified as capability
Description: 'Give me a report on energy use last week.' routes to capability and answers with the building's sustainability blurb instead of generating a report over energy data. Noticed while verifying BUG-200. NOT caused by that fix and not reachable by it: _r_report_intake returns None for this query (verified by test), so no override runs and the LLM's own 'capability' classification stands.
Root_Cause: TWO causes, and the second is why the obvious fix did nothing. (1) The ontology holds a KnowledgeTopic whose lay terms cover 'energy', and the query names no sensor, so capability was a plausible classification. (2) More importantly, dialogue_agent's capability short-circuit RETURNS intent='capability' before the LLM is called, and apply_contract(stage='parse') runs inside _parse_llm_response - which that return never reaches. A parse-stage rule alone was therefore correct and unreachable: 18 unit tests passed while the live answer was byte-identical.
Fix_Approach: report_request_about_data() is a PUBLIC predicate in routing_contract, consulted by both the new report_request_not_capability rule AND the short-circuit's bypass chain in dialogue_agent, so the two cannot drift. Three conditions keep it narrow: the query must ask for a DOCUMENT (the noun report/summary/breakdown, not merely the verb, so 'report the average temperature' stays a reading question); it must name something MEASURED (SENSOR_METRIC_KWS - the same vocabulary the other data-promotion rules use, so 'a report on the parking policy' correctly keeps its prose answer); and it must not be a fault STATEMENT, so intake still wins. The rule sits directly after report_intake_statement and the precedence pin in test_routing_contract.py was updated in the same change, per CLAUDE.md.
Verification: Live on bldg2: 'Give me a report on energy use last week.' now routes to report and returns a Building Management Summary Report which HONESTLY states 'No energy-usage data were collected' - bldg2 has no energy submeter data, and saying so is the correct answer where the sustainability blurb was not. Capability questions are untouched: the prayer room and lift questions still answer from ontology triples. 24 tests in tests/test_report_request_routing.py, including one asserting the short-circuit consults the shared predicate rather than duplicating the logic. Suite 1759 pass, 2 skip; routing contract 106 pass with the updated pin.

Title: The floor overview announced a different building than the one running
Description: With BUILDING_NAME='BuildSys Building (bldg2)' in .env, GET /api/v1/floor-plans/overview returned markdown headed '## Abacws Building - Floor Overview'. Users of bldg2 were shown another building's name in a served answer. The same literal also anchored PDF discovery, so on any building whose floor-plan files are not named after that building, FloorPlanService discovered NO floors at all - the failure was silent because the newer floor_plan_registry path found them independently. Found while clearing CAVEAT-094, which had been filed as a style issue and was verified 'inert'; it was not inert.
Root_Cause: floor_plan_service.py held _BUILDING_NAME as a MODULE CONSTANT set to one building's name. It fed six sites: the discovery regex, three markdown headings, and a payload field. Being a module constant it also froze at import, so even a correct value could not survive a building swap without a restart.
Fix_Approach: Replaced the constant with _building_name(), which reads settings.BUILDING_NAME at CALL time (falling back to BUILDING_ID, then the generic 'Building' - never to a real building), so a swap is reflected without a restart. Discovery now uses _PDF_FILE_RE = '^(?P<building>.+?)\\s+floor\\s+(?P<floor>\\d+)\\.pdf$', the same shape BuildingRegistry already used, so any building's files are found. An assertion in the patch script confirmed no usage of the old constant survived.
Verification: Live on bldg2 after restart: the overview heading is now '## BuildSys Building (bldg2) - Floor Overview' and floors [0, 1, 2] are discovered. 14 tests in tests/test_floor_plan_service_building_name.py cover the name following the active building, being re-read per call so a swap is reflected, the id and generic fallbacks, a guard that the frozen constant cannot come back, discovery of four different building filename shapes, and four non-floor-plan files that must not match.

Title: Triples in the DEFAULT graph cannot be corrected by re-uploading the TTL
Description: After retyping 420 instances in the source TTLs and re-uploading (ttl_uploader reported uploaded=3), the live graph reported BOTH the old and the new types: 52 brick:Sound_Level_Sensor AND 52 ontosage:Sound_Level_Sensor, on the SAME 52 subjects. The TTL fix looked applied and was not - had the audit query not been re-run, TODO-181 would have been closed on a graph that still failed it.
Root_Cause: All 56 stale type triples live in the DEFAULT graph, not in any named graph: a GRAPH-scoped query for them returns nothing while an unscoped one returns 56. ttl_uploader publishes each file with PUT ?context=urn:ontosage:ttl:<file>, which REPLACES that named graph and by construction cannot touch anything outside it. So any triple that reached the default graph - from an earlier context-less ingestion - is immune to every subsequent TTL correction, forever. Same family as BUG-194, where a stale default-graph copy shadowed a corrected policy: the named graph was right, the answer was wrong.
Fix_Approach: Two parts. (1) The residue itself: a scoped SPARQL UPDATE deleting ONLY the stale type triples and ONLY where the same triple is absent from every named graph (FILTER NOT EXISTS { GRAPH ?g { ?s a ?t } }), so nothing a TTL legitimately owns is touched. Safe because all 52 subjects were first verified to ALREADY carry the correct type from the named graph, making the stale one pure residue rather than the only assertion about them. (2) The guard, so this is detected rather than stumbled on: ttl_uploader.audit_undeclared_types() runs after every upload and reports instances typed with a class NOTHING declares. That question was chosen AFTER a first attempt failed usefully: asking 'what lives outside every named graph?' returned 1,576,783 findings - GraphDB's inferred superclass types plus Brick's own SHACL vocabulary - and a guard nobody can act on is worse than no guard (lessons.md #20). The undeclared-type question is the symptom BOTH failure modes produce, does not drown in inference, and is scoped to the namespaces this system mints into (brick:, ontosage:, and the active building's namespace from settings.BUILDING_NAMESPACE - so it is building-agnostic), leaving third-party vocabulary out. Read-only and non-fatal: a failed audit never blocks startup.
Verification: Live on bldg2 at boot: '[ttl_uploader] type audit clean - every instance carries a declared class'. The same query shape returned exactly the 56 defective instances before TODO-181 was fixed, so it is demonstrated to detect the real case rather than merely to pass. 10 tests in tests/test_undeclared_type_audit.py cover counting, the warning text, the top-N preview, the clean case being REPORTED rather than silent, three non-fatal failure paths (HTTP error, exception, malformed rows), and three scoping assertions including that the active building's namespace is included and SHACL is not. Suite 1794 pass, 2 skip. BLDG1 LEG 2026-08-20: the guard proved itself on a second building, and the repair needed generalising. Two of bldg1's noise sensors were stale in a urn:ontosage:ds:noise NAMED graph - written by sensor registration, which no TTL owns either - so 'default graph' was too narrow a scope. scripts/cleanup_default_graph_types.py now targets everything a TTL re-upload cannot reach (default graph plus any non-urn:ontosage:ttl: graph) while leaving file-backed graphs alone, since rewriting those would be undone on the next upload. It also RESCUES rather than deletes: 3 subjects whose stale type was their ONLY type were given the correct type first, because deleting it would have left untyped ghosts no query can reach and no file can restore. bldg1: 253 stale assertions cleared, 3 rescued, audit now clean. BLDG3 LEG: 143 stale assertions cleared, 0 needing rescue; audit clean afterwards. The guard has now found real, DIFFERENT defects on all three buildings — 253 / 143 / 56 — which is the case for keeping it on every boot rather than running it once.

Title: PostgreSQL/Timescale adapter crashed on phantom settings when a field was omitted
Description: PostgreSQLAdapter._build_dsn filled missing arguments from settings.PG_HOST, PG_PORT, PG_USER, PG_PASSWORD and PG_DATABASE. None of those attributes exist — the settings are named POSTGRES_USER_*. Any caller that omitted a single field got AttributeError: 'Settings' object has no attribute 'PG_PORT' instead of a connection or a usable message. Affects the PostgreSQL adapter (which bldg3 uses) as well as the TimescaleDB adapter that subclasses it.
Root_Cause: The fallback was never exercised: the adapter registry always passes all five values from the datasource entry, so the code path only runs when an adapter is constructed directly. Nothing did that until TODO-143 added the first test that builds one from a partial config — which is exactly the class of defect zero test coverage hides.
Fix_Approach: Fall back to the settings that actually exist (POSTGRES_USER_HOST / _PORT / _USER / _PASSWORD). ``database`` is deliberately made REQUIRED with an explicit ValueError naming the fix, rather than defaulting: the only Postgres this deployment knows about holds users and conversation memory, so silently pointing a SENSOR adapter at it would connect successfully and return nothing — the worst of the three possible outcomes, because it looks like a building with no data.
Verification: 4 tests in tests/test_timescale_cassandra_adapters.py::TestTheDsnFallback cover the filled-from-settings path, explicit values winning, the refused missing database, and the exact construction that crashed before the fix (TimescaleDBAdapter(database=...) with no host or port). Suite 1833 pass; bldg2 unaffected.

Title: Table 4 sensor counts: measured, decided to correct the table (not the fixtures)
Description: Table 4 states Building A 680, B 329, C 597 sensors. TODO-143 recorded the fixtures as 'roughly 306 and 300' — that was STALE. Measured with rdflib over each building's TTL: A base 1221 / saturated 2584; B base 326 / saturated 751; C base 600 / saturated 1527 (counting instances carrying ref:hasExternalReference, the property that makes a sensor answerable). Also measured: bldg2 has 52 spaces AND 52 HVAC zones, where the table says 47.
Root_Cause: The table's B and C figures are very nearly the BASE building models (326 vs 329, 600 vs 597 — within 1%), so they were right when written. What changed is SATURATE (V4-T08/T09), which provisions synthetic sensors to fill modality gaps and roughly doubles each fixture. The table never mentions that, so a reader who counts sensors in the artifact finds 751 and 1527 and concludes the table is wrong.
Fix_Approach: DECISION: correct the table, do NOT seed more sensors. Three reasons. (1) Seeding is impossible in the required direction — the fixtures already EXCEED the claimed counts, so there is no 'seed up to 329' when 751 are present. (2) The claimed numbers are not actually wrong; they describe the base model, and the honest repair is to say so rather than to change a number that was accurate. (3) Regenerating fixtures to hit a target count would invalidate every measurement already recorded against them — corpus coverage 63.8%/70.4%, the certified bldg2 scorecard, the 240-question replay baselines — which is a far larger cost than a table edit, and would make the artifact LESS reproducible, not more. Table 4 will report base and saturated counts with a note explaining the augmentation. USER CONFIRMED 2026-08-20 that the table figures were tentative and should track the fixtures as sensors are added, which settles the direction. Delivered: (1) Table 4's Total Sensors row now reports the measured totals SPLIT into base model and SATURATE-provisioned additions, with a footnote defining what is counted and why (instances a question can actually reach) — quoting only the total invites 'where did the extra sensors come from?'. Zones/Spaces corrected to the measured room counts. (2) scripts/building_stats.py regenerates every figure in one command, reading TTLs directly so it works for PARKED buildings, with a --live mode for the active graph. That matters because the numbers will change again: recounting by hand is how this row started, when a grep of OCCURRENCES reported 'roughly 306 and 300' for buildings holding 751 and 1527.
Verification: Counts measured and cross-checked against the LIVE bldg2 graph (751 sensors with a timeseries id, matching the 751 counted on disk). A's 680 cannot be verified from the repo — it plausibly describes the PHYSICAL Abacws sensor count rather than the fixture, which only the author can confirm. Table edit deferred until bldg1 and bldg3 have been booted and measured live, so the table is corrected once with verified numbers for all three rather than twice. FINAL MEASURED FIGURES (all three buildings, verified live during their swaps): A/bldg1 2584 sensors (1221 base + 1363 saturated), 233 spaces, 39 zones; B/bldg2 751 (326 + 425), 52 spaces, 52 zones; C/bldg3 1527 (600 + 927), 132 spaces, 132 zones. A sensor-TYPES count is deliberately NOT produced by the script: buildings whose TTL embeds the Brick vocabulary also assert every superclass on each instance, so a file-based count is inflated (bldg2 read 274) in a way that cannot be unpicked reliably — printing a number known to be wrong is worse than printing none, so that row of the table is left as the author wrote it.
Refs: TODO-143; paper/research paper FINAL.tex Table 4 (tab:building-characteristics) line 840

Title: Real CAD exports lost their rooms: named but un-outlined rooms were dropped
Description: After ingesting bldg1's six floors, 219 of 558 spaces (39.2%) resolve to an ontology IRI, against 100% on bldg2. Not a regression and not the same defect as BUG-147: bldg2's DWG labels each polygon with the room name (RM001A_room), so the label merge pairs geometry with identity. bldg1's DWG labels are POSITIONAL only - 'Zone 2Z001' with a real area of 11.62 m2 - while the room identity ('2.35') comes from PDF text extraction. There is no shared key, so the merge correctly refuses to pair them rather than guess. BLDG3 COMPARISON 2026-08-20: bldg3 re-ingested to 81% (132/163) with floors 1, 2 and 3 at 100% — so the merge itself is sound and bldg1's 39% really is a property of its CAD. bldg3's floor 0 is the only weak floor (2/33) and for a THIRD reason again: its CAD labels rooms 'R003 Kitchen' while the ontology names them 'RMxxx_room'. Checked rather than assumed — the ontology contains no RM003/RM004/RM006 at all, so those ground-floor rooms are simply not modelled and there is nothing to link them to. 6% is the CORRECT rate for that floor; forcing a match would invent rooms.
Root_Cause: Re-diagnosed by reading the actual DWG rather than inferring from the manifests, and the earlier 'the CAD has no room names' conclusion was WRONG. Converting Abacws floor 5 with dwg2dxf and inspecting it with ezdxf shows the drawing names every room: 51 TEXT entities matching the building's own zone pattern, all on layer A-AREA-IDEN (the AIA area-identification layer), each with exact model-space coordinates. The same holds on other floors (16 on floor 0, 48 on floor 3). What the drawing does NOT contain is per-room boundary polygons: its only closed polylines are the gross-internal-area outline, USABLE areas, building access and 1,254 furniture outlines, with walls drawn as 490,405 loose LINE segments. The pipeline associated labels to polygons by point-in-polygon and discarded any label no polygon contained -- so every room name was thrown away -- while the fallback 'use all closed polylines' promoted FURNITURE to rooms under positional ids. The manifest therefore held dozens of furniture spaces that can never match the ontology, and none of the rooms that can.
Fix_Approach: Three changes, all building-agnostic. (1) _spaces_from_unclaimed_labels: a label matching the building's zone_id_pattern that no polygon claims becomes a POINT SPACE -- identity and position from the drawing, polygon None and area_m2 None so nothing downstream can mistake it for measured geometry, confidence 0.9 rather than 0.98. Only pattern-matching text qualifies, so legend entries, fire-alarm annotations and title-block text cannot become rooms. (2) The 'no room_boundary layer matched' fallback no longer sweeps in every closed polyline: layers positively identified as furniture, annotation, gross-area or circulation are excluded, while UNCLASSIFIED layers are still admitted -- not knowing a layer is a reason to consider it, knowing it is furniture is a reason not to. The furniture pattern was broadened from A-FURN to any discipline prefix because interiors drawings use I-FURN, and GIA/USABLE/BUILDING_ACCESS were added to the vocabulary. (3) A floor with NO room polygons at all no longer returns early and loses its labels; it normalises against the labels' own extent, which is the only extent left once the polygons are gone. (4) PDF TEXT LANE, 2026-08-20: the extractor also made a space out of ANY text containing a facility keyword, so 'Office' and '10P PHD Students' became rooms with ids like fp.5.office that no ontology entry can ever match. Deleting them would have lost real information — a drawing writes a room as TWO pieces of text placed together inside it, the number and the name — so _attach_names_to_zones folds a descriptive label into the nearest zone within 0.03 normalised units instead: the zone gains the room's name, its type and an alias, and the duplicate disappears. Proximity is trustworthy here precisely where it was not between DWG and PDF: both pieces come from the SAME page, so their coordinates are directly comparable. A label far from every zone id is KEPT as its own space, because a room the drawing names but never numbers is still a room.
Verification: Live on bldg1, all six floors re-ingested from the real 8-31 MB DWG/PDF pairs: link rate 39.2% -> 46.5%, and floor 0 -- which had produced 1 linked space out of 15 -- now yields 16 of 16, 100%, because its PDF has no text layer at all and its rooms exist ONLY as DWG labels. Every one of floor 5's 50 recovered rooms resolves to its ontology room (5.51 -> abacws#Room5.51, 5.50 -> Room5.50, ...), so identity recovery is exact rather than approximate. ~100 furniture polygons stopped being counted as rooms (568 -> 482 spaces). 16 tests in tests/test_dwg_unclaimed_room_labels.py, including five kinds of legend text that must NOT become rooms, and a regression test for the crash this work introduced and fixed: point spaces broke the implicit invariant that `spaces` and `polygons_raw` are index-parallel, so adjacency walked off the end and every real DWG ingest failed with 'list index out of range' AFTER the rooms had been recovered. Suite 1868 pass. REMAINING DRAG, not fixed here: the PDF text-extraction lane still emits descriptive text ('Office', '10P PHD Students') as spaces -- 27-42 per floor -- which never link. Applying the same zone-pattern requirement to that lane is the next obvious step and should lift the rate substantially again. AREAS for these rooms remain unavailable: obtaining them needs the wall LINE soup polygonised, which is a separate and much larger piece of work. TEXT-LANE RESULT: 46.5% -> 57.7% on bldg1, with the unlinkable text spaces collapsing from 27-42 per floor to 3-20 (floor 5: 27 -> 7). Full progression on the real building: 39.2% -> 44.6% (room labels recovered) -> 46.5% (furniture excluded, label-only floors kept) -> 57.7% (names folded into their zone). 9 tests in tests/test_pdf_label_attach.py cover the fold, the nearest-zone choice, an existing name not being overwritten, and the three cases that must survive on their own: a distant legend entry, an unnumbered room, and a label with no position. Suite 1877 pass. REMAINING: ~19 spaces per floor are still DWG polygons on unclassified layers (USABLE/access) that are not rooms; and per-room AREAS remain unavailable without polygonising the wall lines, or without a room-boundary layer in the source CAD.

Title: bldg1 carries TWO CO2 scales, so no single anchor band can serve it
Description: CAVEAT-162 assumed bldg1 needed one recalibrated CO2 band. Measured live, it needs more than that. 'Which room is stuffiest right now?' returns three rooms ALL scoring exactly 1 on CO2 values of 53.4, 47.7 and 81 - the saturation this caveat predicted. But 'What is the CO2 level on floor 5?' answers 845 ppm ranging 419-1162, and the narrow co2_data table measures 400-2510 ppm (mean 713). Both are correct on their own terms: the wide sensor_data table is the REAL Abacws hardware snapshot, whose sensors publish an air-quality INDEX, while the SATURATE-provisioned sensors publish ppm.
Root_Cause: Traced end to end rather than assumed, and the first two hypotheses were WRONG. It is not the 34 'Air Quality Level (low/medium/high)' sensors — those are typed brick:Air_Quality_Sensor, which no modality claims. Nor is it the wide sensor_data table, whose CO2 columns read a normal 391-1896 ppm. The actual split: the co2 modality matches 1,272 points, of which 1,062 are hardware labelled 'CO2 Level Sensor installed-node <room>' whose readings live in database1_floors04 (table sensor_data_floors04, measured 0-150 with a mean of 49 over 3.2M rows -- an INDEX), and 210 are SATURATE-provisioned '... co2 (simulated) [ppm]' in co2_data at 400-2510 ppm. Both carry a Brick CO2 class, so class alone cannot separate them. Scored against the ASHRAE 420-1500 band, every index reading falls below 420 and the whole population clamps to one utility. The clinching evidence was the two lanes disagreeing about the SAME room: asked directly, 'CO2 in room 0.01' answered 428 ppm from the provisioned sensor, while the ranking used 62 from the hardware one.
Fix_Approach: Two parts, both config-driven. (1) ModalitySpec gained `label_excludes`, the mirror of the existing `label_contains` and the piece needed to SPLIT one Brick class rather than merely name one population. Exclusion is checked FIRST and wins, so a sensor named by both lists is left out: ambiguity should narrow a ranking, never silently corrupt one. (2) A per-building overlay (input/saturation_modalities.yaml) sends each population to its own modality -- co2 keeps the ppm sensors and the standards band, co2_index takes the hardware. The index band (lo=0, hi=150) was NOT inferred from the data: which end of an index means better air is unknowable from the numbers, and reversing it would rank the stuffiest room as the freshest, so it was CONFIRMED BY THE BUILDING OWNER (higher = worse) before being written. (3) co2_data had stopped on 2026-08-13 while the hardware table kept writing, so after the split nothing ppm was recent enough to answer 'right now' and every space was excluded -- correct behaviour, useless outcome. scripts/refresh_narrow_table.py tops a narrow table up to now for the uuids ALREADY in it, continuing each series from its own last value inside the range that table already exhibits, and never rewriting history.
Verification: Live on bldg1, the same question before and after. BEFORE: 'Which room is stuffiest right now?' returned three rooms with IDENTICAL scores on index values 62 / 75.833 / 79.417 -- a tie broken alphabetically. AFTER: distinct scores 0.9086 / 0.9072 / 0.9063 on real ppm values 518.7 / 520.268 / 521.171, ranked against the band that actually describes them. The two lanes now agree: the direct question answers 935 ppm from the same population the ranking uses. co2_data refreshed to the current minute (393,690 rows). 8 tests in tests/test_modality_label_split.py cover the partition (no sensor in both modalities, none in neither), exclusion winning over inclusion, and loading from an overlay.

Title: Hand-drawn room boundary dropped unless AutoCAD's closed flag was set
Description: Two of sixteen rooms drawn by the building owner on A-AREA-ROOM produced no polygon and no area: 0.01 (a 184.5 m2 lecture theatre) and 0.17. Both survived as point spaces via the CAVEAT-206 label fallback, so the floor looked merely under-surveyed rather than mis-read, and the floor total read 718 m2 instead of 912 m2.
Root_Cause: _extract_polygons required entity.closed. AutoCAD sets that flag only when a polyline is finished with the Close option; the two rooms that are not rectangular were drawn with PLINE and ended by snapping the last vertex back onto the first, which is the same ring with the flag unset. Measured endpoint gaps were 1.4 mm on a 55.9 m perimeter (0.0025%) and 15 mm on 14.3 m (0.10%) - drafting closures, not open paths. Separately, only LWPOLYLINE was queried at all, so a heavy POLYLINE written by a different exporter would have been invisible regardless of its flag.
Fix_Approach: _iter_closed_rings() yields rings from BOTH polyline flavours and accepts one when it is flagged closed OR its ends already meet within _RING_CLOSURE_TOLERANCE (1%) of its own perimeter. Relative, not absolute, because a drawing may be in mm or m and the same slip means different things at different scales. Open wall runs and leader lines have a gap comparable to their own length - orders of magnitude away from 0.1% - so they cannot become rooms. 3D/polyface entities are excluded, and a malformed entity is skipped rather than aborting the whole floor.
Verification: Live on bldg1 floor 0: 20/20 spaces now carry a polygon and an area (was 18), floor total 911.8 m2 (was 718.4 - exactly the 184.5 + 8.9 being dropped), 17 with adjacency. 'How big is room 0.01' answers 184.5 m2, perimeter 55.9 m, matching the pre-ingest DXF validation to the decimal. 12 tests in tests/test_dwg_ring_closure.py, including the two real-world gap ratios as parameters.

Title: A TTL in an input SUBDIRECTORY halted startup though it is never loaded
Description: The orchestrator entered a restart loop (16 auto-restarts) after a downloaded sample landed at input/floors/examples/synthetic_building.ttl. The whole stack was down and the health endpoint never came up.
Root_Cause: The boot gate was stricter than the thing it gates. ttl_uploader.discover_ttls() globs *.ttl in the building dir and never descends, so a TTL in a subdirectory is never uploaded to GraphDB and cannot corrupt it - but validate_building_ttls() globbed **/*.ttl and hard-failed on one. The sample declares another building's prefix, which is correct for a sample and irrelevant to this building.
Fix_Approach: The validator now globs *.ttl, matching the uploader exactly. Chosen over widening the existing scaffolding-directory exclusion list (_templates/, documents/, data/, personas/), which would only have postponed the next directory name nobody thought of. A wrong TTL at the top level - one that WILL be loaded - still halts startup.
Verification: Container healthy with RestartCount 0 and the sample TTL still in place. 3 tests in tests/test_ttl_validator_scope.py, one of which pins the invariant itself: the validated set must be a subset of what the uploader loads, so the two cannot drift apart again.

Title: Boot-time ingest never linked DWG spaces to the ontology; /reingest did
Description: After a boot ingest, bldg1 floor 0 had 20 spaces with geometry and 0 linked to the ontology. The same inputs re-ingested through POST /api/v1/floor-plans/reingest gave 16 linked. Building-wide the gap was 208/380 (54.7%) versus 224/392 (57.1%).
Root_Cause: Ontology linking ran inside the PDF pipeline over PDF spaces only, so a DWG space acquired an IRI purely by merging with a PDF space that already had one. A floor whose PDF carries no text layer - floor 0's has zero characters - had nothing to inherit from and linked nothing, however well its CAD named the rooms. The merged-set linking step existed ONLY as a private block inside the /reingest endpoint in main.py, so the outcome depended on which ingest path happened to run.
Fix_Approach: Moved to FloorPlanRegistry.link_unlinked_spaces(), called from the merge in ingest_all(); the reingest endpoint now calls the same method instead of its copy. The ontology_links map is REBUILT after linking rather than patched, since it was assembled at merge time from the spaces that had IRIs then. A linker failure warns and leaves the manifest usable - a floor plan with unresolved IRIs is still a floor plan, and losing it is worse.
Verification: Boot log now reads 'Ontology linking floor 0: 16/20 spaces linked' with no manual reingest; floor 0 is 80% linked, the highest of the six floors. 6 tests in tests/test_floor_plan_merge_linking.py, one asserting BOTH call sites use the shared method and that main.py has not re-grown a private copy.

Title: 'What is the area of room X' answered 'no information on record'
Description: A room whose measured area sat in the manifest returned the honest-no-data reply, which then invited the user to go add data the system already held. 'How big is room X' answered correctly, so the failure depended purely on phrasing.
Root_Cause: Two independent narrow gates. (1) The classifier read the question as capability, and the capability short-circuit's is_spatial_query() bypass tested a phrase list carrying 'how big is' but not 'area of room'. (2) Even on reaching the spatial agent, _AREA_QUERY_RE admitted only floor-shaped phrasings, so the named-space handler written for exactly this case was unreachable.
Fix_Approach: SemanticRouter.is_space_geometry_question() tests a measurement word AND a space noun, and is consumed by BOTH the capability bypass and a new routing_contract rule 'room_geometry_spatial' - one definition, so the two cannot disagree again. Nouns are generic on purpose: a room identifier is the stronger signal, but its shape differs per building and hard-coding one would put a building literal into shared routing code. The rule claims WEAK intents only, so no working route is broken, and adjacency is left to the rules that already own it. The agent's own gate gained the missing words (dimensions, perimeter, floor space).
Verification: Live on bldg1: 'area of room 0.34' -> 195.0 m2, perimeter 58.5 m, 21.4% of floor 0; 'dimensions of room 0.10' -> 68.0 m2 (previously dumped all 392 spaces); floor totals and adjacency unchanged. 33 tests across tests/test_routing_room_geometry.py and tests/test_spatial_area_gate.py, plus the pinned precedence order updated in tests/test_routing_contract.py in the same change, as the routing contract requires.

Title: One boundary around two rooms gave one of them the other's floor space
Description: Found while validating six hand-drawn floor-boundary DXFs before ingest. On floor 2 a single 22.8 m2 outline was drawn around BOTH 2.15 and 2.24, two adjoining rooms of about 11 m2 each. The extractor would have reported one of them as 22.8 m2 - double its real size, and entirely plausible.
Root_Cause: _associate_labels() scanned the labels inside a polygon and broke at the FIRST one matching the building's zone-id pattern, attributing the polygon's whole area to that room. With one room number inside a polygon that is correct and is the overwhelmingly common case; with two it silently picks a winner. A floor plan is one of the few places the system states a number with no sensor able to contradict it, so a believable wrong area survives review in a way a wrong reading would not.
Fix_Approach: Count the room numbers inside a polygon before naming it. With more than one, the outline is kept as an UNNAMED space - so the floor total stays correct - and its room numbers are left unconsumed, so each becomes a point space through the existing CAVEAT-206 fallback: known to exist, known where, honestly carrying no area. Rejected the alternatives of splitting the area evenly (invented geometry) and of dropping the outline (loses the floor total). Only ROOM NUMBERS are counted, so a room that is both numbered and named on the drawing is still one room. A log line names the rooms involved and says how to recover the areas, since the fix is thirty seconds of CAD work.
Verification: Live on bldg1: the guard fired exactly once across six floors, on floor 2 for (2.15, 2.24), as the pre-ingest validation predicted. Both rooms are in the manifest, linked to the ontology, with area None; the outline survives as unnamed space 2Z028 at 22.8 m2, so floor 2's total is unchanged at 1,020.7 m2. 6 tests in tests/test_dwg_multiroom_boundary.py, including that the single-room case is untouched and that a room number plus a descriptive label is not treated as ambiguous.

Title: An intent name no registry defines bypassed every deterministic routing rule
Description: 'What is the area of room 3.50' was answered out of sensor counts while the floor plan held that room's measured 8.87 m2. Reproduced three times in a row, so not a flake. The same question about room 2.15 answered correctly, which made it look like a data gap rather than a routing fault.
Root_Cause: The model answered with the literal intent 'failure' - a name that exists in no intent registry. It parses as valid JSON, so none of the classification_failed paths fire and nothing downstream treats it as an error. But it matches no route, and critically it is not in the WEAK set the routing contract is permitted to override, so every deterministic rule declined it and the question fell through to the default data lane. An unknown intent was thus treated as MORE authoritative than 'general', when it carries strictly less information.
Fix_Approach: Validate the parsed intent against the intent registry before the contract runs: if resolve_name() does not recognise it, log a warning and demote to 'general' with classification_failed set. Demotion rather than rejection because the ordinary unclassified path already exists, is tested, and lets the deterministic rules do their job; classification_failed additionally keeps the bad completion out of the response cache, so one malformed answer cannot pin a wrong route to a question for the full hour TTL. Validation is wrapped so it can never itself break routing, and the registry is resolved per building, so an intent defined only in a building's overlay stays valid.
Verification: Live on bldg1: 'area of room 3.50' now routes spatial_query and answers 8.9 m2, perimeter 12.1 m; 'area of room 2.24' answers 11.0 m2. Logs show the full chain - undefined intent 'failure' -> unclassified -> room_geometry_spatial -> spatial_query. 9 tests in tests/test_dialogue_unknown_intent.py, including that a REAL intent is left untouched and that the demoted result is marked uncacheable.

Title: Hardcoded Abacws sensor inventory injected into the recommendation prompt
Description: workflow/_orchestrator.py builds a _sensor_context string asserting 'This building (Abacws) does NOT have energy meters or power consumption sensors' and enumerating an explicit sensor list, then injects it into the recommendation prompt whenever an energy-focused query returns no energy rows. Three faults at once: it names a specific building in core code; the claim is now FALSE for that building (bldg1 has energy_data plus a per-floor energy_submeter modality since V5-T09/T10, and water flow sensors); and it is emitted for ANY active building, so bldg2 and bldg3 would be told they are Abacws and given a sensor list that is not theirs.
Root_Cause: A building-specific fact was written into a prompt template rather than derived from the active building's graph. Nothing re-checked it when the building gained energy metering, because a literal in a prompt string has no test and no owner.
Fix_Approach: Derive the note from the live coverage audit for the ACTIVE building: which modalities are declared and which have data. The absence_guard/coverage_audit path already answers exactly this question and is building-agnostic, so the fix is to call it rather than to correct the literal. Add the phrase to the T63 static literal scan so a prompt string can never re-acquire a building name.
Verification: Fixed and verified live on bldg1. GROUND TRUTH proves the removed claim was false: a live SPARQL count returns 172 energy/power/electric-typed instances, and the capability lane now answers 'Meter 28, Electrical Meter 27, Energy Sensor 6, Building Electrical Meter 2' counted from the ontology. The prompt note now describes the RETRIEVED DATA ('the data retrieved for this question contains no energy or power readings') instead of asserting what the building owns, so it is true by construction and cannot go stale. Regression-tested in tests/test_building_agnostic_v6.py against the executable source with docstrings and comments stripped - the fix deliberately quotes the old string in a comment, and a naive substring test would have pushed a maintainer to delete that explanation.

Title: Alert store falls back to the literal 'bldg1' instead of the active building
Description: The user-alert node resolves building_id as `state.building_id or "bldg1"`. On any building where state.building_id is unset, alerts are read from and written to bldg1's store - silent cross-building contamination of user data.
Root_Cause: A convenience default written when bldg1 was the only building. The correct fallback is settings.BUILDING_ID, which resolves to whichever building is active.
Fix_Approach: Replace the literal with settings.BUILDING_ID (the same resolution every other service uses). Covered by the T63 scan thereafter.
Verification: Fixed: state.building_id or settings.BUILDING_ID. Regression-tested in tests/test_building_agnostic_v6.py; the static literal gate now fails the build on any 'or "bldgN"' fallback.

Title: Six floors carry TWO rdfs:labels each, fanning out every label query
Description: Every storey in this building is labelled twice - e.g. 'Floor 1' and 'Floor 1 (First Floor)' - from two TTL sources that were both loaded. A SPARQL SELECT with an OPTIONAL label therefore returns one row PER LABEL: a six-storey building reports 14 floors, and the same fan-out inflated a space count from 301 to 341.
Root_Cause: NOT two TTL files, which is what it looked like. Traced properly: only SIX floor-label triples exist in any named graph, all plain xsd:string, all from bldg1_abacws_metadata.ttl. The duplicate set was six LANGUAGE-TAGGED labels ('Floor 1'@en, 'Floor 5 (Top Floor)'@en) living only in the DEFAULT graph and reproduced by NO current input file - stale residue from a load predating the present file set. Two labels that print the same are still two distinct RDF terms when one is @en and the other plain, which is why Floor0 duplicated despite identical text.
Fix_Approach: Consumer half: discovery queries GROUP BY subject and SAMPLE the label, pinned by a test. Data half: a SURGICAL delete of exactly the six orphans - language-tagged floor labels existing in no named graph - backed up first to volumes/backups/orphan_floor_labels_*.json. Renaming a TTL file was considered and REJECTED because there was no second file to rename; and a wholesale default-graph purge was rejected because that graph also holds materialised inference and hasPart structure, so deleting it would have removed real data to fix a cosmetic duplicate.
Verification: Live: 8 label triples across 8 distinct floors, ZERO floors with more than one label (was 14 rows for 8 floors). Floor 0-5 plus Parking and Rooftop, each labelled once. Discovery now reports 8 floors / 301 spaces (was 14 / 341). Nothing re-adds the orphans because no input file contains them. No code referenced the short form (grepped). Synthetic files regenerated so none carries the removed 'Top Floor' text.

Title: Spatial adequacy picked an arbitrary proxy, and called it 'the nearest'
Description: Two defects in one path, both found by the acceptance-scenario-1 test rather than by the unit tests written alongside the module. (1) best_verdict() resolved ties among EQUAL grades by list order, so with two proxies the answer depended on SPARQL result ordering - the exact failure the function's own docstring said it prevented, guarded only ACROSS grades. It named a neighbouring ROOM rather than the corridor. (2) The proxy wording said 'the nearest reading is from X' in a module that deliberately has no notion of distance, so the sentence whose job is to be precise about spatial support contained an unsupported spatial claim.
Root_Cause: The unit tests asserted order-independence only for the case they were written against - an in-room sensor versus a proxy, which differ in GRADE. Equal-grade ties were never exercised. The wording defect came from copying the Master Report's own phrasing ('the nearest corridor observation') into output text, where it stops being a description of the problem and becomes a claim.
Fix_Approach: Ties among the best grade are broken by point IRI - deterministic, reproducible, and explicitly NOT by any ranking, since the only thing that could rank two proxies is distance and this module refuses to consider it. Wording changed to 'the reading is from X, which is not the space asked about'. Both pinned by regression tests, including one asserting no proxy reason may contain the word 'nearest'.
Verification: best_verdict returns the same evidence_space for a candidate list and its reverse. 44 tests pass across spatial adequacy, acceptance scenario 1 and narration. Worth noting the composed test found what three separate unit-test files did not: the pieces were each correct and the composition was not.

Title: One incidental shared word lets an unrelated document answer a question
Description: Found by reading the rows behind a baseline number rather than by any test. 'Which carpets are due deep cleaning this month?' and 'Which anchor points are certified for the abseil window clean?' were both answered with the building's HVAC CO2/TVOC threshold table, under the heading 'Here is what I found in Abacws Building documentation'. The content is real, so no guard aimed at fabrication fires - but an unrelated document presented under that heading READS as an answer, which is the failure the grounding guard exists to prevent. Reproduced live. 377 of 1529 baseline answers (25%) cite a document, so the exposed surface is substantial; the share that is off-topic is not yet measured. [2026-08-21] BLAST RADIUS NOW MEASURED: 148 of 377 document-citing answers (39.3%) are confidently off-topic, 42 arguable, 187 on-topic -- i.e. 9.7% of all 1,529 answered questions. HONEST RESIDUAL: the shipped signal addresses about a quarter of it. The other ~74% share a genuinely rare term with the passage and are SEMANTIC failures (homonymy: 'monitor' the verb vs the screen, 'book' the verb vs the noun, 'privacy' acoustic vs data-protection); no word-overlap rule separates those. The next lever is document_score_floor (0.45), calibrated for a different embedding model than the BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 now running -- 377 answers were drawn from just 11 chunks of 5 documents, which is prima facie evidence the floor is too low. Tracked as TODO-222.
Root_Cause: grounding_guard.is_on_topic keeps a passage when ANY distinctive query term appears in it: `return bool(q_distinctive & p_terms)`. The carpets question's distinctive terms are {carpet, clean, deep, due}; the HVAC document contains 'Heat recovery wheel: Inspected quarterly, CLEANED annually'. One common operational word therefore clears the whole passage while the salient term ('carpet') is absent. The guard weights a rare, decisive term and a ubiquitous one identically. NOT a bypass - the filter runs and returns True, which is why no 'dropped off-topic' log line appears.
Fix_Approach: The proportional-overlap fix proposed in this row was MEASURED AND REJECTED. Swept against a hand-labelled set of all 377 document-citing baseline answers (148 off-topic / 42 arguable / 187 on-topic, base rate 39.3%), it flags 70% of off-topic answers but also 44% of on-topic ones -- 51.0% precision, barely above chance. Shipping it would have traded a fabrication-shaped failure for a coverage collapse. SHIPPED INSTEAD: (1) a per-building corpus document-frequency table (orchestrator/services/corpus_stats.py) computed from the building's own uploaded documents, so it carries no domain word list and no building literal; (2) grounding_guard.match_strength() grading a hit as distinctive / common / none against that table; (3) capability_agent using that grade to choose the ANSWER'S FRAMING rather than to filter -- a distinctive match keeps 'Here is what I found in X documentation', a common-terms-only match is introduced as 'I could not find a passage that directly addresses this; the closest related material is below'. Framing rather than filtering because at 6% false-positives hedging costs a softer heading on ~11 correct answers where dropping would cost the answers themselves; (4) missing_fact_caveat now applied on the document path, where it was absent (it was already wired on the graph path), so a question asking for a date is told when the passage holds none.
Verification: Measured on this repository, not taken from the investigation: DF limit<=1 = 48.5% precision, limit<=2 = 70.4% (shipped, = COMMON_TERM_FRACTION 0.4 on a 5-doc corpus), limit<=3 = 66.7%. Rejected on the same data: 'question names a term absent from the corpus' 38.8% (flags 99% of CORRECT answers), overlap>=2 52.4%, proportional 51.0%. NOTE the investigating agent's reported DF for 'clean' (4 of 5) did not reproduce -- the real corpus has 1 -- so the motivating carpets example is NOT among the cases this catches. 14 new tests in tests/test_corpus_stats.py; full suite 2462 pass. [2026-08-22] LIVE RE-PROBE after deploy: the motivating carpets question STILL returns the confident heading, because its only overlap term ('clean') has DF=1 in the real corpus and so grades as distinctive. Broader rules were then measured against the same labelled set: '>=3 distinctive query terms but <=1 matched' catches the carpets case and 80% of all off-topic answers -- but hedges 47% of the CORRECT ones (52.4% precision). REJECTED: the hedge asserts 'I could not find a passage that directly addresses this', which on a correct answer is false. At 47% false-positives the system would disclaim nearly half its right answers -- a new honesty defect rather than a fix for one -- and would train readers to skip the qualifier exactly when it is true. Kept the 70.4%-precision / 6%-false-positive operating point. Sensor-count answers verified live in the same probe (280 CO2, 276 temperature), confirming CAVEAT-039 + TODO-223 end to end. [2026-08-22c] RE-MEASURED after the routing fixes: answers citing a document fell from 24.7% to 12.6% of the corpus -- the routing work halved the exposure without touching the guard, which is why it was sequenced first. The new hedged framing is firing on 3.2% of answers. Still PARTIALLY_FIXED: the residual is semantic, and the open decision is whether to take the 0.55 retrieval floor (TODO-222), which costs 18% of correct document answers. || RE-MEASURED 2026-09-02 on the 240-question replay: the shipped filter is visibly working on real questions. 'Do the seating arrangements accommodate different user privacy needs?' was answered on 2026-08-28 by dumping the Governance & Privacy Statement and now returns 'Abacws Building's documents do not answer this. I searched Building Policies; none of them contains the answer.' Same for 'is any equipment experiencing unusual vibrations?', previously answered with the Maintenance Log. These account for a large share of the 20 answers the comparator labelled 'tightened' - they were WRONG answers before, and removing them lowers the computed-answer rate while improving the system. || RE-ASKED LIVE 2026-09-30, occupant01 via /v1 streaming: BOTH MOTIVATING QUESTIONS NO LONGER REPRODUCE, and neither now reaches the document path. 'Which carpets are due deep cleaning this month?' routes to metadata (the register lane) and answers 'I did not find any carpets in the building's cleaning task records', then gives the two records that genuinely hold 'deep' and 'month' (CLN-0017 deep-cleaning, Room 4.02, next due 17 September 2026; CLN-0003 monthly, Room 0.04, next due 15 October 2026) and closes 'No carpet-related data is present in the register.' Correct and well-formed. 'Which anchor points are certified for the abseil window clean?' also routes to metadata and declines honestly; its 'closest this building keeps' pointer names an INSTANCE label ('Kitchen extract duct clean') rather than a register, which is weak but is not this defect. NEITHER answer carries the heading this row was opened about ('Here is what I found in Abacws Building documentation') and neither cites an unrelated document. Across all 11 live asks, ONE reached the capability document lane at all and it declined. The row's own 2026-08-22c prediction is what happened: the routing work removed the exposure without the guard being touched. THE SHIPPED SIGNAL'S NUMBER IS NOW STALE AND IS LOGGED AS CAVEAT-1334: COMMON_TERM_FRACTION 0.4 was calibrated on a FIVE-document corpus where it gave a limit of 2; input/documents now holds 41 files, so the limit is 16 and only **59 of 4,625** distinct terms (1.28%) exceed it. Questions that can therefore only ever grade COMMON: 96 of 7,151 real survey questions (1.3%) and 7 of 4,060 catalogue questions (0.2%). The signal is mostly switched off, and the 70.4% precision figure quoted above does not describe today's system. DO NOT re-tune it without a fresh hand-labelled set -- the 59 COMMON terms already include room, lift, fire, water, alarm, floor, access, maintenance and the building's own name, so tightening the fraction walks straight back into the 47%-false-positive hedge this row measured and rejected.

Title: --resume could never retry the rows it exists to retry, and a resumed run overwrote the whole-run tallies
Description: Found by using the feature rather than by a test. After the 1,580-question golden baseline finished with 51 rows quarantined (22 LLM-DEGRADED, 29 TIMEOUT), `--resume 20260821_124529` reported '1580 already captured, 0 to go' and exited. The script's own closing line tells the operator to 'RE-run with --resume to retry the non-OK rows', so the documented remedy was inert. A second defect sat behind it: the meta tallies were accumulated from the current invocation's loop, so a resume that re-asked 51 questions would have written ok=51 over a 1,580-question run in the metadata file - the file a supervisor reads.
Root_Cause: _done_qids() collected every qid present in the CSV regardless of status, so a quarantined row - a row that records an OUTAGE and holds no answer - counted as a capture. Same class as BUG-176 / BUG-177 / BUG-191: the measurement apparatus reporting a completeness it had not achieved, and again in the flattering direction. Separately, ok/degraded/failed were loop counters written straight into meta rather than derived from the file.
Fix_Approach: _done_qids(path, retry_failed=True) counts only status=='OK' as done, with an explicit --no-retry-failed to freeze a run as it fell. _drop_rows() removes the rows about to be re-asked so a retry REPLACES rather than duplicates them (temp file + atomic replace, so an interrupted rewrite cannot truncate the capture; only ever asked to drop answer-less rows). _tally() derives the counts from the whole file, and the run now prints this-run and capture-total separately so a resume can never read as the entire run.
Verification: tests/test_baseline_capture_harness.py - 12 tests, all passing, asserting both properties directly plus that a retry cannot eat a healthy answer and the harness carries no building literal. Live: on the real capture, _done_qids now returns 1529 (was 1580) and the resume picked up exactly the 51 quarantined rows. Capture backed up to *.csv.bak first.

Title: An integration test file nobody runs drifted two routing expectations behind the pinned contract
Description: Found incidentally while running a -k selection during V6-T44. Two cases in tests/test_integration_mock_building.py::TestDialogueIntentDetection asserted routing targets that the routing contract had since deliberately changed: 'check for any anomaly in humidity sensors' expected 'anomaly' (contract rule anomaly_history_to_events sends it to 'events', V5-T21) and 'list all CO2 sensors on floor 2' expected 'metadata' (rule inventory_to_discovery sends it to 'discovery'). Both redirects are logged, deterministic and intended. Neither test was wrong about the system -- both were stale about the design.
Root_Cause: The file is not in the unit marker set (14 of 14 cases deselected under -m unit) and needs the container network to reach rag-service, so it is absent from `pytest -m unit -q` and from CI's deterministic suite. A test that nothing runs cannot fail, so it cannot signal drift; the routing-contract changes that superseded these expectations were each pinned by tests/test_routing_contract.py, which is why the contract itself stayed correct throughout.
Fix_Approach: Corrected both expectations to the contract's actual targets, with an inline comment naming the rule and why it exists, so the next reader sees the design rather than assuming a regression. NOT fixed here: the structural problem that this file runs in no routine suite. Marking it integration and adding it to a live-stack job is the real remedy and is left as a decision rather than made silently -- the file needs services this repo does not start in CI.
Verification: tests/test_integration_mock_building.py::TestDialogueIntentDetection 8 passed against the live local model. Confirmed not a regression from this session's work: the redirects come from routing_contract.py, which was not touched, and both are emitted as explicit [routing-contract] log lines.

Title: BUG-188's context-window fix never reached bldg1, so the entire golden baseline ran at 8192
Description: Found while reviewing timeout behaviour. `.env` (bldg1, the ACTIVE building) had OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=8192 while `.env2` and `.env3` both had 16384. BUG-188 diagnosed empty completions from a 29,705-char prompt against an 8192 window and raised the value -- but bldg2 was active at the time, so the change landed only in that building's env file. The comment immediately above the line read 'parity with the bldg2/bldg3 era', asserting a parity that did not exist. Consequence: the whole 1,580-question golden baseline ran on the configuration BUG-188 identified as faulty, which is the most likely explanation for its 12 LLM-DEGRADED rows.
Root_Cause: Per-building .env files are parked and swapped by rename, so a fix applied to the active building's .env does not propagate to the parked ones -- or, as here, vice versa. Nothing compares them, so a divergence is invisible until someone greps all three.
Fix_Approach: Set OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=16384 in .env, matching .env2/.env3, and replaced the false 'parity' comment with the actual history. Not done here, and worth doing: a check that flags LLM-tuning divergence across the parked env files, since this class of drift is silent by construction.
Verification: Confirmed before and after by grepping all three env files AND the running container (`docker exec ontosage-orchestrator sh -c 'echo $OLLAMA_NUM_CTX'` returned 8192). Takes effect on the next `docker compose up -d` -- `restart` silently keeps the old environment (CAVEAT-178).

Title: Re-derive document_score_floor for the embedding model actually running
Description: The BUG-218 measurement surfaced this: all 377 document-citing answers in the baseline were drawn from ELEVEN chunks of FIVE documents. A retrieval floor that admits the same eleven passages for hundreds of unrelated questions is too low for this model and corpus. document_score_floor is 0.45 and was calibrated for a different embedding model than the BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 now in use. This is the layer that should be rejecting most of the off-topic hits; the grounding guard is currently being asked to do retrieval's job. [2026-08-22] MEASURED. Retrieval was re-run for all 377 labelled questions (embedder + Qdrant only, no LLM) and each hit's real cosine score recorded. THE HEADLINE: at 0.45 the floor admits EVERY hit -- 148/148 off-topic and 187/187 on-topic clear it. It was not under-filtering, it was filtering nothing, which is why 377 answers came from eleven chunks of five documents and why the grounding guard was doing retrieval's job.
Root_Cause: A cosine floor is model-specific and the model changed under it.
Fix_Approach: Raised bge-large from 0.45 to 0.50 and recorded the full sweep in the constant's comment. 0.50 costs almost nothing (-9 off-topic, -2 on-topic). 0.55 is the strongest defensible point -- it removes 80 of 148 off-topic answers (54%) for 34 of 187 on-topic (18%), a 2.35:1 trade, far better than any lexical rule managed -- but it is a real coverage change and is deliberately NOT shipped in a constant. It belongs behind the same shadow-mode/regression-gate review every other V6 tightening goes through.
Verification: Sweep table (off-topic kept / on-topic kept of 148 / 187): 0.45 -> 148/187; 0.50 -> 139/185; 0.55 -> 68/153; 0.60 -> 13/79; 0.65 -> 1/16. Full unit suite passes with the new floor. Live effect not yet measured -- it lands with the next deploy and will show in the regression-gate comparison against the golden baseline. [2026-08-23] DECIDED: KEEP 0.55. The regression gate PASSES on the clean re-capture with 0 regressions and 8 tightenings, every one naming the gate responsible. All 8 removed an answer that was wrong: Q911 'which anchor points are certified for the abseil window clean' was being answered with the building's HVAC CO2 threshold table (BUG-218's own motivating example), and Q861/Q906/Q531 likewise. Raw Qdrant scores confirm the mechanism -- the retrieval-floor cases sit at 0.5125/0.5139/0.5364 against the 0.55 floor while an on-topic control question scores 0.6254 and still clears it. The predicted 2.6:1 removed-wrong to removed-right did not merely hold, it was pessimistic: on this subset it is 8:0. Ten answers moved the other way (declines that became answers) and were reviewed -- they are honest declines phrased as answers, not fabrications, though two show the BUG-192 pattern of asserting absence from the RAG window.

Title: Class-listing query truncates at LIMIT 50 with no DISTINCT, so counts undercount
Description: Surfaced by CAVEAT-039 but independent of it. The SPARQL agent's class-listing template selects sensor rows with an OPTIONAL join and LIMIT 50, without DISTINCT. Any one-to-many join therefore consumes the limit, and the answer reports whatever survived truncation as though it were the population. Even with the duplicate references removed, a 50-row limit cannot report a 280-sensor population. [2026-08-22] CONFIRMED as the dominant defect once CAVEAT-039's structural damage was cleaned: fan-out fell to the expected 2.0 and the query still reported only 13 of 280, because a LIMIT 50 over a one-to-many join is a row cap being asked to answer a population question.
Root_Cause: A row limit is being used where a count is wanted. The two are different questions and the template answers only the first.
Fix_Approach: Rewrote the class-listing template in sparql_agent to GROUP BY ?sensor with SAMPLE over each OPTIONAL projection -- the same pattern already used in this codebase to fix the floor-label fan-out. SAMPLE is correct rather than lossy here: each projected property is single-valued per sensor, and the multiplicity came from the join, not from the data. The row cap moved to a named constant _CLASS_LISTING_LIMIT = 500 with its reasoning stated: 50 could not express a real population (bldg1 alone has 280 CO2 sensors), so any 'how many / which floors have X' answered from a 50-row result was reporting the truncation as the population. Still bounded, per the project's no-unbounded-query rule.
Verification: Measured live against the repository, all three stages: 50 rows/1 distinct sensor before the CAVEAT-039 cleanup; 50 rows/13 distinct after the cleanup alone; 280 rows/280 distinct after this fix, against a true population of 280 (276 of them carrying a timeseries id). Both fixes were necessary and neither was sufficient alone. Full unit suite 2462 pass, 0 fail.

Title: 90 points were described in the ontology but connected to no database
Description: Found by the sensor-connectivity audit the user asked for. bldg1 held 2,705 Brick points, of which 113 carried no ref:hasTimeseriesId: 23 legitimately (8 CCTV cameras, 6 humidity setpoints, 9 lighting commands -- a command is written, not read) and 90 that should have data and did not. Among them: 6 EV-charger power meters, 2 lift power meters, 2 PV arrays, 17 occupancy counters, 7 intrusion detectors, 5 CO2 sensors in named rooms (3.13, 5.15, Lab 3.01, Lab 4.01), 5 water level sensors, the green roof's soil-moisture and rainfall sensors. Design contract 8 requires BOTH halves -- the triple and the rows -- so all 90 were describable and unanswerable. Separately, one sensor (Illuminance_Sensor_Floor5) had a UUID whose table held zero rows.
Root_Cause: The enrichment TTLs were authored to describe the building's assets, and nothing in the pipeline required a described point to be connected to a stream. The gap was invisible because no query asks 'which points have no data' -- an unanswerable question simply produced an honest decline, which looks like correct behaviour rather than missing wiring.
Fix_Approach: New scripts/link_unlinked_sensors.py. Discovers unlinked points by SPARQL against whatever building is active, maps each Brick class to a table via config/saturation_modalities.yaml (the canonical map, not a second copy), mints uuid5 identifiers from the point IRI so the script is idempotent, writes a TTL of ref:hasExternalReference links, and seeds the tables. Three safety properties: it REFUSES to write into any datasource the registry declares nature: real, so the genuine Abacws snapshot cannot be diluted; every generated stream carries ontosage:isSimulated true, so declared simulation never passes as measurement; and a point whose class has no mapping is REPORTED rather than routed on a guess. Twelve modalities were added to the modality config to cover the classes involved, each Brick class verified present in Brick+extensions.ttl first. Two classes Brick 1.4 does not define (soil moisture, rainfall) were declared in the OCBV TBox as ontosage: terms, following the BUG-179 precedent, rather than minting names inside Brick's namespace.
Verification: Measured before and after against the live graph and MySQL. Points without a UUID: 113 -> 23, and the remaining 23 are exactly the non-timeseries set (cameras, setpoints, commands). UUID-to-data coverage: 2,597/2,598 (99.96%) -> 2,688/2,688 (100.0%) across 15 storage keys. 388,890 rows seeded across 90 streams plus 4,321 for the empty illuminance stream. The linker's own dry run reports 0 unmapped. 19 tests in tests/test_sensor_linking.py; full suite 2,488 pass. The scope-vocabulary test caught a real error during the work (scope: space, which the coverage auditor silently treats as non-room) before it shipped.

Title: A measurement question about EQUIPMENT never reaches the data lane, only rooms do
Description: Found immediately after TODO-224 connected 90 previously-unlinked sensors: the data is now there and the questions still cannot reach it. Probed live after deploy, all four routed to 'capability' (the amenity/document lane) instead of sensor_data: 'What is the power draw of the EV charging stations?', 'How much power are the lifts using?', 'What is the soil moisture on the green roof?', 'Are the intrusion detectors reporting anything?'. The first was answered with the building's TRANSPORT AND PARKING blurb; the third with the sustainability blurb. No [routing-contract] override fired -- the LLM classified them as capability and nothing redirected them. Connecting a sensor is necessary and not sufficient; this is the other half.
Root_Cause: semantic_router.is_data_query() recognises a data question by (1) an explicit sensor id, (2) an explicit zone id, (3) a ROOM-or-FLOOR locator plus a measurement word, or (4) a known data phrase. An asset is not a locator, so 'power draw' + 'EV charging station' fails test 3 and the capability->sensor_data promotion rule (routing_contract._r_data_query_promotion) never gets its trigger. The assumption baked in is that measurements happen in ROOMS; the newly linked sensors measure EQUIPMENT -- chargers, lifts, PV arrays, a green roof -- which the locator test cannot see.
Fix_Approach: New concept-stage rule `capability_measurand_is_data` in routing_contract.py. A capability question naming a measurand the building instruments routes to sensor_data, or to analytics when the phrasing asks for an aggregate over a period. The place requirement is dropped FOR THIS INTENT ONLY: it exists so a definitional question ('what is stuffiness?') stays open-domain, but such questions classify as `general`, not capability -- the capability intent is already building-scoped, so within it the place test was doing no work and was costing the entire sensor estate. Building-agnostic by construction: the test is has_measurand_concept over HBCO concepts resolved from the building's own ontology plus its overlay, so a building that measures noise recognises 'noisy' and one that does not, does not. Two exclusions: questions about what a DOCUMENT says keep their lane, and census questions ('how many CO2 sensors') are left to the existing _is_countable_meta guard rather than given a second owner. Ranking questions were deliberately NOT handled here -- _WEAK_INTENTS already includes capability and DELIBERATE_RE already claims the superlative shapes; only 29 of 424 slip past, and the fix for those is that regex.
Verification: Measured on a 316-question stratified capture against the golden baseline. Capability 88.4% -> 59.3% (-85 questions). Questions reaching a DATA lane: 6.0% -> 34.2%, a 5.7x increase. sensor_data 0 -> 77, analytics 1 -> 9. Regression gate: 76 route-changed, 14 loosened, and 5 regressions -- all five are the SAME rows the previous gate run flagged (score-floor casualties from TODO-222), so this change introduced ZERO new regressions. Of the 77 new sensor_data answers, 57 (74%) are substantive: a formaldehyde/TVOC time series replacing an HVAC threshold table, '21.8 degC' for a creche floor-temperature question that previously returned a generic sensor census, a ranked room table for a seminar-booking question that previously returned an accessibility blurb. The remaining 20 decline, and 12 of those are BUG-232, not this rule. The capture also ran 0 degraded and slowed from 5.8 to 15.7 s/question, which is itself evidence the data pipeline is now doing work it previously skipped. Unit: 13 new tests; concept-stage precedence is now pinned (it was not before). Full suite 2535 pass.

Title: The regression gate cannot tell a config-driven tightening from a silent degradation
Description: Found by running the gate for real for the first time. A 316-question post-fix capture against the golden baseline returned 6 REGRESSION verdicts, all capability->capability answers that became declines. Checked against the BUG-218 hand labels, they are not one thing: 3 (Q426, Q651, RS-056) are OFF-TOPIC answers the raised retrieval floor correctly removed -- wins -- 1 is ARGUABLE, and only 2 (Q1036, Q1066) are genuine coverage loss. The gate called all six the same thing.
Root_Cause: The gate's central rule is that a worsening is a TIGHTENING if some gate fired and a REGRESSION if none did, read from the capture's `gates` column, which is populated from EvidenceRecord.gates_applied. document_score_floor is not a gate -- it is a retrieval config value applied inside search_documents, long before any evidence gate runs -- so a suppression it causes names nothing and is indistinguishable from an unexplained decline. The same blind spot applies to every other config-driven behaviour change.
Fix_Approach: The floor is now applied in PYTHON rather than server-side. Qdrant's score_threshold returns only survivors, so 'nothing was retrieved' and 'everything fell below the floor' are indistinguishable from outside -- and only the second is attributable to a threshold. Retrieving with score_threshold=0.0 and filtering locally costs nothing (same query, same top_k) and makes the distinction available. When the floor suppresses EVERY candidate, the capability lane declares `retrieval_floor` on the evidence partial. The assembler now UNIONS lane-declared gates with gates that fired instead of overwriting them, which it was doing -- that would have silently discarded the declaration and put the record back to being unable to explain its own change.
Verification: 3 tests in tests/test_evidence_chokepoint.py: the declared gate survives assembly, it survives ALONGSIDE a fired gate (the overwrite path), and the floor is applied where the suppression can be seen. A test double in test_capability_bare_building.py needed its signature updated for the new out-parameter -- caught by the suite, fixed rather than worked around. Full suite 2575 pass. The practical effect: the next threshold change can be read off the gate instead of hand-classified against a labelled set, which is what 0.45 -> 0.50 required.

Title: The evidence chokepoint could not see three of its ten lanes, and nothing failed
Description: V6-T02's chokepoint was written, deployed and reported working. It was not. `_LANE_SEMANTICS` in assemble.py named `sparql_results` and `sql_data` -- strings that appear NOWHERE in the pipeline, because the lanes write `sparql_result` and `sql_result` (singular). The plural form is assigned exactly once, as `[]`, which is falsy and so cannot trigger inference either. Consequently every sensor-reading and metadata answer carried an evidence record saying 'no lane produced evidence for this answer, so nothing supports it' -- a confident, wrong statement about the system's own grounding, emitted by the component whose whole job is to describe grounding honestly. Separately, `_spatial_query_node` wrote `floor_plan_result`, so geometry it COMPUTED was recorded as a drawing it looked at.
Root_Cause: The lane table was written from CLAUDE.md's reserved-key list rather than from the code, and that list was itself wrong. The unit tests could not catch it: test_evidence_assembly.py was written against the same fictional key, so the table, the tests and the documentation all agreed with each other and none of them agreed with the pipeline. This is the failure assemble.py's own docstring says it exists to prevent -- BUG-210 was two copies of one step drifting -- reproduced inside T02's own implementation, in triplicate.
Fix_Approach: Corrected the names to what the lanes actually write. Gave the spatial lane its own `spatial_result` key, rendered it in _response_node (writing only the new key would have blanked every spatial answer) and added it to the per-turn cleanup so stale geometry cannot bleed into a later turn. Declared T02_LANES beside the table. Corrected the reserved-key lists in CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/agent-patterns.md, which is where the wrong names came from. Re-derived the test's parametrised lane list FROM _LANE_SEMANTICS so a third copy cannot drift again.
Verification: tests/test_evidence_chokepoint.py (26 tests). The load-bearing one -- test_every_lane_key_is_actually_written -- scans the orchestrator for every `intermediate_results["x"] =` assignment and fails if a lane key is not among them; reintroducing `sql_data` on purpose makes it fail with an actionable message, so the guard is proven to bite. Live: scripts/probe_evidence_lanes.py exercises 10 distinct lanes and all 10 now carry a record with a status, operations correctly differentiated across authoritative_lookup / observation / calculation / forecast / recommendation. Full suite 2522 pass.

Title: The discovery census answered from the graph and told the record it had no evidence
Description: Found by the T02 acceptance probe. 'What sensor types does this building have?' returns a correct live census -- 280 CO2 sensors, 276 air temperature, figures independently verified against GraphDB -- and its evidence record said NOT_ASSESSABLE, 'nothing supports it'. The census runs inside the dialogue node, queries the ontology, and leaves only `dialogue_response` on the bus, so the chokepoint saw no lane key. A false negative of this kind is worse than no record at all: a record that defames a well-grounded answer trains people to skip it, the same way a warning with a 12% true-positive rate did in lesson 27.
Root_Cause: A lane that queries the graph but does not declare that it did. The chokepoint was behaving correctly on the information available to it.
Fix_Approach: The census declares `sparql_result` with its shape (source, class count, total). setdefault rather than assignment, so a real sparql-node result is never overwritten by the census summary.
Verification: Live: the same question now returns status=observed, operation=authoritative_lookup, with the census answer unchanged.

Title: The report-intake lane emits no evidence record; its semantics belong to V6-T23
Description: Found while probing T02. A report-intake turn ('the tap in X is dripping') routes to the maintenance lane, writes `report_intake_result`, and produces a fail-closed record: 'no lane produced evidence'. This is an ELEVENTH lane -- T02's objective names ten and report intake is not among them -- so it is out of that task's scope, and the fail-closed behaviour is the chokepoint working as designed.
Root_Cause: `report_intake_result` is not in _LANE_SEMANTICS, deliberately: a human-reported ticket is not an observation BY THE BUILDING, and none of the six AnswerStatus members cleanly describes 'a person told us this and we logged it'.
Fix_Approach: Do NOT force it into an existing category to make a probe go green -- that would blur a human report into a sensor reading, which is exactly the distinction the Master Report insists on. V6-T23 ('human-reported evidence bound to space and time') exists to design this properly; assign it there and add the lane once the status semantics are decided. [2026-08-27] The status semantics did NOT need designing -- this codebase had already decided them twice and used neither. evidence/precedence.py grades a human_report as 'inference: a person's account is evidence, not a measurement', and EvidenceSource.kind has documented 'human_report' since the model was written while nothing ever emitted one.
