'water refill station' is in neither that table nor any later branch, so the query fell past wayfinding, adjacency, area, blocks and count to _answer_list - the default - and returned '## All spaces'. So it was the second of the two candidates the row named: _answer_nearest did not claim it and _answer_list took it.
Fix_Approach: Trace which handler claims it, then either match the amenity or decline naming what is missing. A fall-through to list-all is the wrong shape for a nearest question and should not be reachable.
Verification: A nearest-question now either locates the thing or declines; it can no longer reach the list-all default. The decline NAMES what the building can locate, read from the floor-plan manifests rather than a constant, so another building advertises its own amenities with no code change - verified by a test using prayer_room/bike_store. It also states that an unlabelled amenity is a gap in the PLAN rather than a claim the building lacks it. Known amenities (toilet/lift/fire exit) still reach the nearest handler. 8 tests in tests/test_nearest_target_unknown.py.

Title: A room-level reading for a recent date returns no rows although the data exists
Description: 'What is the temperature in room 5.04 on 29 August 2026?' returns 'No data found' from a single resolved uuid, while sensor_data_floors04 holds rows from 2026-07-16 to 2026-08-31. The same question answered earlier the same day.
Root_Cause: DIAGNOSED 2026-08-31, and the previous hypothesis is REFUTED. Room 5.04 has TWO temperature points, not one: Air_Temperature_Sensor_5.04 -> database1 (the WIDE sensor_data, which holds 585,002 non-null readings for that uuid including 1,045 on 29 August and is current to today), and Room5.04_sat_temperature -> temperature_data (a narrow table frozen at 2026-08-26, CAVEAT-361). The lane resolved the SATURATION point, whose store cannot cover the requested window, while the real sensor holding the data was never consulted. So this IS related to CAVEAT-361, but not as recorded: the point is not 'registered to the wrong table' - there are two points and the lane picked the dead one. The adapter is NOT at fault: MySQLAdapter.build_timeseries_query emits a correct query for the live uuid (verified by building it directly against database1).
Fix_Approach: Do not widen the query - the design contract is that a point reads from the store it is registered to. The defect is SELECTION: when several points serve the same space and modality, the lane must not choose one whose store holds nothing in the requested window. Preferred fix is to make selection window-aware and, when the chosen point yields nothing, say which point was read and that a sibling point exists rather than reporting 'No data found'. Deferred: this changes answer behaviour and must not land mid-regression-capture.
Verification: SELECTION HALF DONE AND VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-01, no LLM needed). Adapters gained latest_timestamp(); probed live it correctly separates current stores (database1 2026-09-02 01:07, light_data, energy_data) from frozen ones (temperature_data, co2_data, humidity_data, contact_data all 2026-08-26 13:36). Run on the REAL room-5.04 uuids the lane keeps Air_Temperature_Sensor_5.04 and drops Room5.04_sat_temperature with the reason 'temperature_data holds nothing after 2026-08-26 13:36', and discloses the omission by name. REMAINING HALF IS BUG-388, and it is TTL not code: a question about 'room 5.04' resolves ONLY the saturation point, because the real sensor's hasLocation is Zone_5.04 while the overlay's is Room5.04 and the graph holds ZERO links between 39 zones and 234 rooms. With no second candidate there is nothing for the selection to choose between. || BOTH HALVES NOW DONE AND VERIFIED END-TO-END (2026-09-02, no LLM). With the zone<->room links asserted (BUG-388), a traversal from Room5.04 now finds FOUR temperature points where it found one: Room5.04_sat_temperature (temperature_data, frozen), AHU_F5_Return/Supply_Air_Temperature (plant_data, frozen) and Air_Temperature_Sensor_5.04 (database1, LIVE). Running the lane's selection over those four READS the live sensor alone and sets aside the three frozen ones, naming each with its store and cut-off. The question that opened this bug - 'temperature in room 5.04 on 29 August' - now reaches the 1,045 readings that were there all along.

Title: The regression gate cannot tell a good route change from a bad one
Description: The gate classifies a changed answer as 'route-changed' and passes. On the 26-question partial run, 2 of 7 route-changes were regressions (wayfinding questions pulled into the register lane by BUG-374) and the gate reported PASS.
Root_Cause: A route change is not intrinsically better or worse; the gate has no expectation of which lane SHOULD answer a given question, so it can only report that the lane moved.
Fix_Approach: The bank now carries a declared operation per catalogue question (V7-T22). Pair each with an expected lane and the gate can classify a route change as intended or not. Until then, route-changed rows must be READ, not counted — a PASS with route changes is not a pass.
Verification: config/routing_expectations.yaml declares the lane a class of question SHOULD reach; a move INTO a declared lane is ROUTE_INTENDED (attributable, non-blocking), a move OUT is ROUTE_REGRESSION (BLOCKING). An unmatched route change keeps the old non-blocking verdict, so the file can only make the gate stricter - pinned as a property by test_expectations_can_only_add_blocking_never_remove_it. 16 tests in tests/test_gate_route_expectations.py.

Title: 113 of 203 user reports carry no location, so most of the intake data cannot show recurrence
Description: The recurrence lane groups reports by place, and 113 of bldg1's 203 reports have neither location nor space_iri. They are excluded and their count is stated in the answer, but it means recurrence is computed over 44% of the intake data.
Root_Cause: The intake path does not require a location, and a report filed without one cannot be attributed to anywhere afterwards.
Fix_Approach: Ask for a location at intake where the reporter can supply one, and resolve it to a space_iri. Retrofitting the existing 113 is not possible and should not be attempted.
Verification: Intake now ASKS for a place when neither a free-text location nor a resolved space_iri was obtained: the acknowledgment names the gap and says why it matters ('that is what lets the building notice when the same problem keeps coming back in the same place'). Asked, never demanded - a placeless safety report is worth more than no report, so the report is still logged and an URGENT one still gets its emergency notice. Fixes new reports only; the existing 113 are not retrofittable and were not touched. 6 tests in tests/test_report_intake_asks_for_place.py; existing 10 intake-evidence tests still pass.

Title: The probe harness cannot tell an intended tightening from a regression
Description: The final 111-question run scored 29.7% computed against 36.0% for the previous run, which reads as a regression and is not one. Of the 17 answers that stopped counting as computed: 4 were TIMEOUTs on a loaded machine (3 of 4 answer when re-asked; p90 latency doubled 35s -> 83s between the runs), 4 returned nothing (BUG-355), and 5 now decline honestly where they had previously answered FROM THE WRONG SOURCE — 'which infrastructure investments should be prioritised' was answered from risk-assessment records, and 'how do today's room conditions compare' from asset condition-survey grades.
Root_Cause: The probe counts grades and nothing else. A confidently wrong answer and a correct one score identically, so removing wrong answers looks like losing good ones. The regression GATE makes this distinction — an intended tightening names the gate that fired — and the probe does not.
Fix_Approach: Carry the gate's tightening/regression classification into the probe comparison, and record machine load or per-run p50/p90 beside every score so a latency-confounded run is visible rather than read as a capability change. Until then two runs are only comparable when their latency profiles are.
Verification: corpus_replay gained run_health() (p50/p90/max/timeouts/degraded + a 'fit to compare' verdict printed in every report) and --compare BEFORE.csv AFTER.csv, which classifies each changed grade as broke / tightened / requoted / lost / gained. Run on the two real V7 probes the 43.2%->36.0% 'drop' decomposes to 15 tightened, 12 re-graded quotations (BUG-370), 20 GAINED and exactly 1 lost. 11 tests in tests/test_replay_run_comparison.py.

Title: A rejected graph upload was reported as a successful lift
Description: On bldg2, nine record documents each logged 'lifted N records' and three were missing from the graph. GraphDB had rejected them with HTTP 500 'Couldn't precommit transaction'. The register looked present, the question looked answerable, and any answer would have been computed over nothing.
Root_Cause: upload_ttl reports a non-2xx by RETURNING {'ok': False}; it does not raise. The caller only caught exceptions, so a rejected upload took the success path.
Fix_Approach: Check the result, not the absence of an exception. The 500 is a transient precommit conflict while another writer holds the repository, so it is retried three times with backoff before being reported as a failure.
Verification: All nine registers present on bldg2 after the fix; 7 tests.

Title: The document SHA cache suppressed a lift that had never succeeded
Description: After BUG-382, the three rejected registers were skipped on the next boot with 'sha match — skip' and never retried, because the file had not changed. A failed lift was therefore permanent.
Root_Cause: The SHA records that the PROSE was indexed and says nothing about the lift. This is the trap CLAUDE.md already documents for TTL uploads — the SHA skip suppressing a re-upload that is still needed — reappearing in a second place.
Fix_Approach: On a SHA skip the lift is still attempted when its named graph is EMPTY, checked with one ASK per document. The check errs towards 'present' on any failure, because wrongly believing a graph is empty would rewrite every register on every boot.
Verification: The three missing registers self-healed on the next boot: bookings 16, sustainability 5, warranties 7. bldg2 readiness 8 DATA/19 ABSENT -> 16 DATA/11 ABSENT.

Title: The why-question direction is invented when the asker gave none, and is dead weight that looks meaningful
Description: is_why_question() returns (modality, direction). When a question names a modality but no direction - 'why does the temperature keep changing?' - _MODALITY_NAMES supplies a DEFAULT of 'high', so a variability question is labelled as a high-level one. Harmless TODAY only because the direction word is no longer asserted in the answer: a previous fix removed '(higher now)' from the output because it contradicted the matched comparison sitting directly below it. All other callers (routing_contract, dialogue_agent) use the function as a BOOLEAN, and diagnosis.py unpacks direction and never reads it.
Root_Cause: A default direction is a guess presented as an extracted value. It is currently unused, which makes it a latent trap rather than a live defect: anyone re-asserting the direction in the prose immediately turns an invented 'high' into a false claim about a question that never mentioned a level.
Fix_Approach: Either add a 'variability' direction and detect 'keep changing'/'fluctuating'/'unstable'/'swinging' - a variability question IS diagnosable, just not as a high/low one - or return None for the direction when the asker gave none, so a consumer must handle the absence rather than receive a guess. Do NOT simply re-assert the current value.
Verification: A 'variability' direction is now detected (keep changing / fluctuating / unstable / swinging / up and down / erratic) instead of defaulting to 'high'. Pinned expectations in test_diagnosis_modality_names.py updated in the SAME commit - they encoded the invented direction. See BUG-387, found while fixing this.

Title: The regression gate's blocking count tracks its refusal regex, not the system
Description: Four gate runs over ONE unchanged capture produced 3, 19, 22 and 22 blocking regressions. The only thing that changed between them was the _DECLINE regex. Manual review of all 32 distinct candidates across the runs found ZERO genuine regressions: 26 were decline -> decline (the two runs phrase a refusal differently, so recognition rates differ between the two FILES and the asymmetry manufactures answered->declined), and 6 were genuine changes that were all IMPROVEMENTS.
Root_Cause: Standing is inferred from non-deterministic LLM prose. Any regex has different recall on the two files, and that difference alone produces or hides blocking findings. Two structural traps were found and fixed inside this: matching ANYWHERE in the answer scored Q658 - a thorough register answer with a definitive negative and a table of the nine records consulted - as a refusal because a later clause said 'there is no information about whether any such failures were later fixed'; and 'there is no data' without a trailing qualifier scored 'There is no data loss in this series; completeness is 100%' as a refusal. answer_status does NOT discriminate - it reads 'observed' on both sides for every candidate checked, including the real ones.
Fix_Approach: Do not keep tuning the regex; the count can be moved to almost any value that way, which is the failure this project keeps repeating. The structural fix is BUG-386: make the lanes DECLARE a refusal so the gate reads a field instead of guessing from prose. Until then, treat the blocking count as a CANDIDATE LIST to be read, not a verdict, and say so wherever it is quoted.
Verification: Fixed by making the SYSTEM honest rather than by changing the gate - the gate already reads gates_applied, and needed no edit at all. ROOT CAUSE FOUND: the referent-existence gate wrote its refusal into sparql_result and declared nothing else, so 'what is the temperature in Room 99.99?' was correctly refused and recorded as status=observed, operation=authoritative_lookup, gates_applied=[]. The regression gate's rule is 'worse, and no gate fired = REGRESSION', so every such refusal read as silent breakage - which is why four runs over ONE unchanged capture reported 3/19/22/22 blocking findings that were all, read by hand, deliberate declines. The gate now names itself: verified live, the same question returns status=not_assessable, gates_applied=['referent_existence'] and a reason naming the missing referent, while a real answer is untouched. SECOND DEFECT FOUND BY THE UNIT TEST AFTER THE LIVE CHECK PASSED: a lane hands up plain JSON, so 'not_assessable' was stored as a raw str. It serialises to byte-identical JSON - the API looked right while `rec.status is AnswerStatus.NOT_ASSESSABLE` was False. Enum fields are now coerced when a lane partial is applied, which fixes it for every lane, and an unknown value is ignored rather than stored. 7 tests in tests/test_referent_gate_names_itself.py.

Title: A lane can refuse in prose while the evidence record declares the answer OBSERVED
Description: Checked across the V7 gate candidates: for Q393 ('There is no information in the provided ontology that indicates any bin has reported full'), Q424 ('No information is available in the provided ontology'), Q404, AO-035, Q041 and others, answer_status is 'observed' on BOTH sides. The prose is a refusal and the record claims an observation.
Root_Cause: AnswerStatus.NOT_ASSESSABLE exists and the assembly sets it when NO lane produced evidence - but a lane that runs, returns an empty or irrelevant result, and then has the model write a refusal around it still reports the lane's own status. The refusal is composed downstream of the point where status is decided.
Fix_Approach: Set NOT_ASSESSABLE where the refusal is composed, not only where no lane ran. This is worth more than the gate fix it enables: an evidence record that labels a refusal as an OBSERVATION is wrong on its own terms, and every consumer of that record - the provenance answer, the precedence tiers, any downstream audit - inherits the error.
Verification: Root cause was ONE line: infer_lane() returned the first lane whose result dict was TRUTHY, and a result with zero rows is truthy - so 'ran and found nothing' and 'observed something' were the same to the record. Now judged STRUCTURALLY from the success flag and row count the lanes already report (lane_produced_evidence), never from the prose: reading the text is what the regression gate does and that moved its own count 3->22 over one unchanged capture. Row-bearing lanes only; prose lanes (capability/document) are exempt because their evidence IS the passage. Second defect fixed by the same change: an empty EARLIER lane in the ordered table used to mask a later one that had found something. 10 tests in tests/test_empty_lane_is_not_an_observation.py; full suite 4,086 pass.

Title: A direction the user stated was overridden by a lay term default
Description: Found while fixing CAVEAT-384. 'Why is the humidity LOW today?' returned ('humidity','high'), and 'why does the CO2 swing up and down' returned ('co2','high'). Several _MODALITY_WORDS patterns also match the bare modality NAME - 'co2' sits inside the stuffy alternation, 'noise' inside the loud one, and 'humid' was widened to catch 'humidity' - and that pass returns early with a FIXED direction before any direction detection runs.
Root_Cause: The lay-term pass was written on the premise that a lay word carries its own direction, which is true of 'chilly' and 'stuffy' and false of a bare quantity name. The premise was never checked against the patterns, which had since been widened to match the names.
Verification: A lay match whose matched TEXT is a bare modality name now breaks to the name pass so the stated direction wins; a directional lay term still returns its own reading. Verified across 8 phrasings: humidity+low->low, co2+swing->variability, stuffy->co2/high, chilly->temperature/low, noise level+high->high, loud->high. 36 tests pass.

Title: bldg1's spatial graph is two disconnected overlays: 39 HVAC zones, 234 rooms, ZERO links
Description: Measured live on GraphDB: 39 brick:HVAC_Zone, 234 brick:Room, and a query for ANY predicate joining a Room to an HVAC_Zone in either direction returns 0. The real abacws sensors hang off Zones (Air_Temperature_Sensor_5.04 -> brick:hasLocation Zone_5.04, label 'installed-node 5.04') while the synthetic saturation overlay hangs off Rooms (Room5.04_sat_temperature -> brick:hasLocation Room5.04, rdfs:comment 'synthetic-saturation-v4', ontosage:isSimulated true). Nothing in the graph says these describe the same physical place.
Root_Cause: The two overlays were authored independently against different space individuals and no TTL asserts the correspondence. It is a data gap, not a code defect.
Fix_Approach: THIS IS THE REMAINING HALF OF BUG-378 and it is TTL-first, not code. A question about 'room 5.04' resolves only the saturation point, because that is the one whose hasLocation is Room5.04 - so the live sensor is never a candidate and store-coverage selection (already implemented and verified live) has nothing to choose between. Asserting the zone<->room relationship would make both points candidates, and the existing selection would then prefer the live store automatically, with NO further code change. NEEDS USER CONFIRMATION before authoring: deriving Zone_5.04 <-> Room5.04 from parallel naming is a factual claim about the physical building, and asserting a false one into the source of truth is worse than the gap. If confirmed, assert it with provenance marking the link as derived rather than surveyed.
Verification: User approved the derivation 2026-09-02. scripts/derive_zone_room_links.py reads zones and rooms from the LIVE graph, matches on the trailing identifier, and asserts brick:hasPart/isPartOf only where ONE zone and ONE room share it: 24 pairs, 0 ambiguous, 10 zones with no room and 201 rooms with no zone deliberately left alone. Every triple carries rdfs:comment 'derived-zone-room-link-v1 ... not surveyed' and lives in its own named graph so it can be dropped. Graph now reports 96 room<->zone links where it reported 0. First version emitted full IRIs and was HARD-FAILED at boot by ttl_validator (missing @prefix bldg:); the namespace is now read off the entities so the declaration cannot disagree with them, and 9 tests in tests/test_zone_room_link_derivation.py pin it - including one that parses the output as Turtle.

Title: Two evidence-policy tests were passing against an EMPTY policy
Description: test_narrow_table_staleness_is_detected.py used `EvidencePolicy.load() if hasattr(...) else EvidencePolicy()`. EvidencePolicy has no load() classmethod, so it silently constructed an EMPTY policy whose every gate defaults to advisory. The tests passed, but they were asserting against a policy with no config in it - they would have passed whatever config/evidence_policy.yaml said. Caught only because a new test asserted mode is ENFORCING and failed.
Root_Cause: A hasattr() fallback written defensively without checking whether the attribute exists. The fallback path was the only path taken, and it was silent.
Verification: Both files now call the real module-level load_policy(), which reports sources=['config/evidence_policy.yaml']. A comment in each explains why the empty-policy fallback made the tests vacuous.

Title: Only 19 of ~933 narrow points are live; the "current" tables are current for a handful of sensors
Description: Measured per-uuid: noise_data 236 uuids with 1 written in the last 24h; light_data 242 with 1; occupancy_data 280 with 6; energy_data 8 with 6; iaq_data 11 with 2; water_data 7 with 1; equipment_data 16 with 2; temperature_data 67 with 0; co2_data 66 with 0. That is exactly the 19 sensors in the publisher's uuid map. CAVEAT-361 called noise/light/occupancy 'current' because MAX(datetime) over the table reports today - one live sensor is enough to do that. Consequence: 'which public space on floor 2 is quietest right now' excludes all 47 floor-2 spaces as having no scorable data (leak-bank P002, P006), because every floor-2 noise point stopped on 2026-08-25.
Root_Cause: The narrow tables were bulk-loaded once and only the 19 points named in bldg1_timeseries_extension_uuids.json are topped up. Store-level freshness cannot see this because a narrow table's sensors are ROWS, so one writer keeps the table's MAX current.
Fix_Approach: Detection is fixed: MySQLNarrowAdapter.latest_by_uuid() reports per-sensor freshness in one GROUP BY and the SQL lane prefers it over the store-level figure. The DATA gap itself is the same open decision as CAVEAT-361 - the user chose not to generate synthetic readings for uncovered points, so these sensors stay dead and questions about them are now honestly downgraded rather than answered from 8-day-old rows.
Verification: Live: for 4 noise sensors latest_by_uuid returns 2026-08-25 02:24 while the store's MAX is 2026-09-02 10:13. A failed per-uuid probe returns an EMPTY map, never all-None, so a transient DB error cannot mark every sensor dead - pinned by test_a_failed_per_uuid_probe_must_not_mark_every_sensor_dead. || DATA HALF FIXED on the user's instruction 2026-09-02: the publisher now tops up EVERY point the ontology registers to a narrow store, not the 19 hand-listed ones. scripts/generate_publisher_map.py reads the narrow stores from database_registry.yaml and the points from the live graph (1,528 across 15 tables) - it invents nothing, a point appears only if the ontology already says where its readings live. Live coverage went from 19 to 1,528 (98.1%; the 30 short are plant_data uuids that have rows but NO ref:storedAt binding - data without ontology, the reverse gap). Ranges added for temp_c/rh_pct/co2_ppm/contact because the (0,100) fallback is impossible for those modalities - 12 ppm CO2 is below outdoor air. Inserts batched per table with executemany, and the loop now sleeps the REMAINDER of the interval: measured cadence was drifting to ~40s (30s sleep + ~10s work) and is now exactly 30s. Symptom cleared: 'which public space on floor 2 is quietest right now' ranked all 47 spaces with real readings where it had excluded every one.

Title: Enforcing a gate made the evidence record LESS informative than leaving it advisory
Description: gates_advisory recorded 'gate: reason' while gates_applied recorded only 'gate'. Promoting freshness from advisory to enforcing therefore replaced 'freshness: the newest co2 reading is 7390 minutes old, beyond the 15-minute limit' with the bare word 'freshness' - the age disappeared at exactly the moment the gate started acting on it. Caught by an existing test whose message read 'the verdict does not state the age'.
Root_Cause: Two lists built from the same verdicts with different formats, and only the advisory one carried the reason.
Verification: gates_applied now carries 'gate: reason', de-duplicated on the gate name so a lane's own declared gate is not doubled. The user's decision for CAVEAT-361 was to report the last recorded reading WITH its age, which this restores. Pin in test_evidence_assembly.py updated in the same commit.

Title: A lane's answer outlived its turn and was served for the NEXT question
Description: Reproduced live, one session, two turns. Turn 1 'Which public space on floor 2 is quietest right now?' answered from the deliberate lane. Turn 2 'What is the temperature in Room 5.04 right now?' was classified CORRECTLY as sensor_data and returned turn 1's answer verbatim - a confident, specific noise ranking for floor 2 in reply to a floor-5 temperature question. The response cache then stored that under turn 2's key, so the wrong answer outlived the session and was served to a FRESH one, which is how it was noticed. Found while verifying BUG-390.
Root_Cause: A resumed conversation is loaded from Redis with its whole intermediate_results intact and only user_message replaced, so every lane result from the previous turn was still on the bus. _response_node collects the first lane it recognises and checks deliberate_result long before sql_result.
Verification: _clear_stale_lane_results() runs at the single chokepoint (WorkflowOrchestrator.execute) and drops every per-turn lane key, preserving forecast_result/analytics_result which turn_memory carries forward by design. Verified live: the same two-turn sequence now returns turn 2's own k-anonymity refusal. NOTE ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT: it derived the key list from _LANE_KEYS_FOR_DIAGNOSIS - a list written for a different purpose that does NOT contain deliberate_result - so it deployed, ran, cleared nine keys and changed nothing. The list is now explicit, and test_every_lane_result_the_response_node_reads_is_cleared greps the response node for every *_result key it reads and fails if one is not cleared. 30 tests in tests/test_stale_lane_results_cleared.py.

Title: The anomaly grader silently tested fewer detectors as the round number grew
Description: _pick_sensor selected its victim with OFFSET round_no * len(INJECTION_PLAN) + i and no wrap, so the cursor walked off the end of every small table as rounds accumulated. At round 8 the offset was 72+, past co2_data's 66 eligible sensors, humidity_data's 72 and temperature_data's 67 - and those injections were skipped with 'no sensor with enough rows'. The message blames the data; the data was there and the cursor had run past it. Round 8 injected 4 of 9 planned faults; with the wrap it injects 9.
Root_Cause: An unbounded rotation offset used against tables whose sensor counts differ by two orders of magnitude.
Fix_Approach: Wrap the offset modulo the number of eligible sensors in that table.
Verification: Round 9 injects 9 of 10 (only pm25_data skips, and it genuinely holds zero rows). This matters beyond the count: recall was being computed over whichever detectors happened to survive the offset, so two rounds were not comparable - the tenth time in this project that the measurement apparatus was the thing that was wrong.

Title: Both bldg1 data gaps are bldg1-only; bldg2 and bldg3 are already correct
Description: Checked by swapping to each building and running the same two generators. ZONE<->ROOM: bldg2 already holds 208 links across 52 zones / 52 rooms, bldg3 holds 528 across 132/132, and derive_zone_room_links reports 'this building already links rooms to zones; nothing to derive' for both - the guard behaving as intended rather than a no-op by luck. PUBLISHER COVERAGE: bldg2 runs a different publisher (generate_dummy_timeseries.py) already tracking all 425 of its narrow points, and per-sensor liveness measured 418/418; bldg3 measured 924/924. Neither needed the widened map, so the redundant bldg2_narrow_publish_map.json was deleted rather than left looking authoritative.
Root_Cause: bldg1 is the oldest building and was assembled by hand before the onboarding generators existed. Its HVAC zones and its synthetic room overlay were authored independently, and its narrow publisher map was written with 19 entries. The later buildings were generated and carry neither defect.
Verification: Also a portability check of this session's own code: latest_by_uuid() ran unchanged against bldg2's and bldg3's adapters and reported per-sensor freshness correctly on both.

Title: "any energy spikes" no longer reaches the anomaly lane
Description: Found in the post-V7 240-question replay by reading the rows behind a score change. On 2026-08-28 the question returned an executive summary naming 72 anomalies, 49 of them high-severity spikes against a 45 kW mean; on 2026-09-02 it returns the generic 'I don't have that specific information on record ... contact your facilities team'. energy_data holds 8 sensors and ALL 8 are live, and the anomaly scanner reported 24,317 spike findings in the same hour, so the data is there and the detector works - the question stopped reaching them.
Root_Cause: DIAGNOSED, and it was TWO defects wearing one symptom. (1) THE ANSWER WAS DISCARDED: 'are there any energy spikes?' resolves 288 sensors, over MAX_FETCH_UUIDS=200, so the SQL lane declined correctly and said why - and the anomaly node handed the resulting empty row set to the detector, which reported 'No sensor data available for anomaly detection'. A different and untrue claim: all 8 energy sensors are live and the scanner found 24,317 spike findings that hour. The analytics lane ALREADY checked too_broad, so the shape existed and one lane had not followed it. (2) ROUTING: the terse forms 'any energy spikes' and 'show me energy anomalies in the last day' land in the CAPABILITY lane, not anomaly - still open.
Fix_Approach: Trace which rule claims it in routing_contract.py. If a terse noun-phrase question falls through to capability, that is a whole class, not one question - 'any energy spikes' and 'unusual vibrations' share the shape.
Verification: Half 1 FIXED and verified live: 'are there any energy spikes?' now returns the breadth decline naming 288 sensors and the narrowing to try, and 'are there any energy spikes on floor 2 today?' returns a real answer - 49 energy anomalies, 25 high-severity, largest jump 0.432 -> 20.875 kW. The capability was never missing; the question needed narrowing and the system had been claiming the opposite. 5 tests in tests/test_upstream_decline_is_not_overwritten.py, including one parameterised over BOTH consumers of the fetch lane so a third cannot repeat it. Half 2 (routing of terse noun-phrase questions to capability) REMAINS OPEN - it needs a routing_contract rule and the pinned precedence test updated in the same commit. || ROUTING HALF: code fixed and PROVEN, live behaviour still blocked upstream. _r_capability_measurand_is_data could only ever return sensor_data or analytics; it now returns 'anomaly' when the question is anomaly-shaped (_ANOMALY_SHAPE_RE). Deliberately NOT a new rule - widening the lane an existing rule may choose leaves the pinned precedence order untouched, and this file's own history is that placement is where routing goes wrong. Proven by calling apply_contract directly: 'any energy spikes' -> anomaly, 'show me energy anomalies in the last day' -> anomaly, 'what is the energy use right now' -> sensor_data (not diverted). 214 routing tests pass, order unchanged, plus 11 new ones. STILL BLOCKED: live, both questions remain in capability because the CONCEPT RESOLVER returns no concept for them, so the rule's has_measurand_concept() guard is never satisfied and the rule never runs. Missing HBCO lay terms were the first suspect and are now added to ontology/hbco_mappings.ttl ('energy', 'electricity', 'power', 'energy spike(s)', 'power spike', 'energy anomaly/anomalies') and CONFIRMED present in GraphDB - but resolution still does not fire for 'any energy spikes'. NEXT STEP: determine how ConceptResolver matches (substring vs token vs embedding threshold) - a lay term that exists in the graph and still does not match means the matcher, not the vocabulary, is the constraint. Do NOT add more lay terms until that is known. || BOTH HALVES NOW FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE. The blocker was NOT the routing rule and NOT the vocabulary: ConceptResolver caches the whole HBCO lay-term map in REDIS, which a container restart does not touch, so the new lay terms were in GraphDB and verifiable there while the resolver kept reading the old map. Clearing cache:concept:hbco_all made it work immediately. Live now: 'any energy spikes' and 'show me energy anomalies in the last day' both reach the ANOMALY lane and return the honest breadth decline naming 288 sensors, while 'what is the energy use right now' still answers with real figures (Floor 3 highest at 5.35 kWh). See BUG-398 for the cache defect, which was the actual cause and would have silently broken every future ontology change.

Title: "No sensor data available for anomaly detection" hides WHY there is none
Description: 'Is there a Voltage fluctuation that could put our hardware at risk?' returns 'No sensor data available for anomaly detection.' bldg1 has no voltage sensors at all, so declining is CORRECT - but the message describes the lane's internal state rather than the building's. 'This building has no voltage sensors' is the same refusal and tells the user something they can act on; the current wording reads like a temporary outage.
Root_Cause: The anomaly lane reports that its input was empty without asking why it was empty.
Verification: Code fixed and unit-tested; NOT verified end-to-end on the question that motivated it, and the row says so rather than claiming otherwise. The anomaly node now distinguishes NOTHING RESOLVED (the building does not instrument that quantity) from points that resolved and returned no rows (readings not loaded) - different situations with different remedies - and rewrites only the first, naming the quantity asked about and stating it is not a fault. An unrecognised phrasing yields '' rather than the nearest modality, because matching 'radon' to CO2 is the fabrication this subsystem exists to prevent. 8 tests in tests/test_anomaly_says_why_there_is_nothing.py. WHY UNVERIFIED: the motivating question ('is there a Voltage fluctuation...') now routes to general_knowledge and 'any radon anomalies' to capability, so neither reaches the detector any more. The message is right where it lives; the questions that should reach it do not. See BUG-399. || CORRECTED 2026-09-02 after CAVEAT-400 was refuted. The reason given above - 'neither reaches the detector any more' - was right about the fact and WRONG about the cause: I implied routing had drifted. Measured over 5 rounds it is 100% stable, so 'is there a voltage fluctuation...' reaches general_knowledge deterministically, because of changes I made. This is therefore a ROUTING question with a definite answer, not variance: a question naming a quantity this building does not instrument should reach a lane that can say so, and general_knowledge cannot. That is the next step, and it is actionable. || CLOSED. Two changes, both narrow. (1) ROUTING: a new concept-stage rule `unmeasured_quantity_is_reach` sends a measurement-shaped question naming a quantity with NO resolved measurand to the observability lane. It sits LAST in its stage on purpose - `capability_measurand_is_data` above it claims everything the building DOES measure, so only genuinely unmeasured quantities reach it - and a word that names no quantity ('any', 'unusual', 'current') is excluded outright, because reporting "'any' is not measured here" would answer about a word rather than the building. The pinned precedence test was updated in the SAME commit, per the repo rule. (2) The observability lane no longer demands a space when the quantity is instrumented NOWHERE: the answer is identical in every room, so asking for one made the user supply information that cannot change it. VERIFIED LIVE: 'is there a voltage fluctuation that could put our hardware at risk?' now returns 'No - voltage is not measured in this building. There is no point of that kind located there, so any figure I gave you would be invented', followed by what IS measured. 'can you measure CO2 in Room 5.04' still answers Yes with its source, and 'is there a temperature fluctuation in Room 5.04' still reaches sensor_data - the rule diverts nothing real. TWO OF MY OWN DEFECTS CAUGHT BY THE PROJECT'S OWN GUARDS: the routing contract's building-agnostic test rejected a docstring in which I had written 'bldg1', and load_modalities returns ModalitySpec objects rather than strings, so sorting them raised TypeError and the lane fell back to 'I could not build the coverage picture' - an infrastructure message for a question it could answer. 10 new routing tests; 224 routing tests pass with the order unchanged.

Title: The building's own descriptive facts are the WORST-served class, not the sensor questions
Description: From the 2026-09-02 240-question replay, split by the corpus's own answerability label: questions marked FULL (fully answerable with what the building has) compute at 21% (8 of 38), LOWER than the 25% for questions marked requires_extension. The system answers more of what it supposedly cannot than of what it supposedly can. Reading the 25 full-answerability questions it does NOT compute, almost none are sensor questions - they are static building facts and self-description: 'Is this a commercial building?', 'Can you tell me who built the building?', 'How old is the building?', 'Does the building have a green roof?', 'are visitors allowed?', 'is visitor check in automated or human?', 'Do you have a name?', 'What is your purpose?'
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED, but the data is present and unreachable rather than absent. bldg1 ships bldg1_description.ttl, bldg1_site.ttl, bldg1_abacws_metadata.ttl and bldg1_greenroof_types.ttl, and a direct SPARQL query returns GreenRoof_SoilMoisture_Sensor and related entities - so 'does the building have a green roof?' is answerable from the graph today and is not being answered.
Fix_Approach: Highest-value coverage work available, and TTL-first: these are descriptive triples the ontology already holds. Establish first whether the gap is retrieval (the lane never queries site/description graphs), routing (they land in capability and get the 'contact your facilities team' fallback), or self-description (a distinct class - 'what is your purpose?' is about the ASSISTANT, not the building, and belongs to the self_description intent that already exists). Do not add sensor work for this: no sensor is missing.
Verification: input/bldg1_building_facts.ttl added (17 triples), extending bldg1_description.ttl rather than duplicating it. Verified live 8/8 on the questions that previously failed, including the SECOND-PERSON forms the corpus is full of - 'how old are you?' answers from the same triple as 'how old is the building?'. Self-description ('what is your purpose?', 'do you have a name?') is held as its own subject because it asks about the ASSISTANT, and answering it with the building's purpose is a wrong answer to a question that was understood. THREE SELF-INFLICTED CONTRADICTIONS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE SHIPPING, each found by asking the question rather than by reading the file: opening hours (this file said the building closes at 19:00 while bldg:Cap_working_hours said 22:00), visitor policy (already held by bldg:Cap_visitor_guest_policy and richer there), and floor area/storeys (the metadata lane computes 6,129 m2 across 6 floors and 8 Floor instances LIVE, while the draft asserted 11,400 m2 and 6 storeys). The rule the file now states: a recorded fact earns its place only where nothing computes it.

Title: An ontology change had no effect until someone manually cleared an undocumented Redis key
Description: ConceptResolver caches the HBCO lay-term map in Redis under cache:concept:hbco_all. ConceptResolver.invalidate_cache() exists and its own docstring says 'call after HBCO TTL is re-uploaded' - and NOTHING called it. Found while fixing BUG-395: lay terms were added to ontology/hbco_mappings.ttl, uploaded, and confirmed present in GraphDB by direct SPARQL, and the question still routed to the wrong lane through TWO container restarts. Only a manual DEL of the key made the change take effect.
Root_Cause: The thirteenth instance in this project of a capability built, correct, and never invoked. A restart refreshes process state but not Redis, so nothing in the normal deploy path could ever have cleared it.
Verification: ttl_uploader now calls concept_resolver.invalidate_cache() after a successful upload, gated on summary['uploaded'] so a boot that uploads nothing pays nothing, and wrapped so a cache failure cannot stop a boot. PROVEN END TO END: a stale marker was planted in cache:concept:hbco_all, hbco_mappings.ttl was touched to force a new SHA, and on restart the log shows 'hbco_mappings.ttl uploaded' followed by 'concept cache cleared' with the key gone. This matters beyond one question: design contract 2 promises 'extend the TTL and the system answers', and a vocabulary addition that lands in the graph, verifies in the graph and changes nothing made that promise false in a way that looks like the ontology being wrong. 4 tests in tests/test_concept_cache_invalidated_on_upload.py.

Title: The events lane answered about a floor that does not exist, with a modality nobody asked for
Description: 'are there any vibration anomalies on floor 9' returned 'at least 500 anomaly episode(s) recorded today - dropout: 472, spike: 28' and listed spikes in Room4.35 (OCCUPANCY), Room3.06 (HUMIDITY), Room5.69 (OCCUPANCY). Two things are wrong at once: bldg1 has no floor 9, and none of the episodes are vibration. The answer is confident, specific and about a different question entirely - the shape this project guards hardest against.
Root_Cause: DIAGNOSED. _anomaly_summary fetched every episode in the window and narrowed by NOTHING, although each episode already carried its room and its modality from self._points. Separately, the referent-existence gate lives INSIDE the sparql node, so any lane that does not pass through sparql - events among them - never gets it. That is why 'floor 9' was not claimed.
Fix_Approach: Two separate checks. (1) The referent gate must claim a non-existent floor whichever lane the question is heading for; it already produces the right refusal for 'Room 99.99' on the sensor path. (2) The events lane must filter episodes by the modality and space asked about, or say it is listing everything - reporting occupancy spikes to a question about vibration is worse than reporting nothing.
Verification: WRONG-MODALITY HALF FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE. _narrow_to_question() filters episodes by the modality and floor the question names. The exact reported question now returns 'This building does not monitor vibration, so there are no vibration anomalies to report - that is a statement about what is connected here, not a fault', in place of 500 episodes of occupancy and humidity. Both filters FAIL SAFE: a modality the building's own points do not use narrows nothing rather than guessing at the nearest one, and an unrecognised room-label shape disables the floor filter instead of emptying the result, so a differently-named building gets the old behaviour and not a blank answer. 13 tests in tests/test_events_narrow_to_question.py. REMAINING: the referent gate still only runs on the sparql path. Moving it to a shared chokepoint would fix a whole class at once and is the right architecture, but it changes behaviour for every lane simultaneously - this project's own rule is to switch one guard at a time so a change stays attributable. Left for a focused pass. || REFERENT HALF NOW FIXED TOO, and structurally rather than by a third copy. The gate is extracted into apply_referent_gate(), ONE implementation any lane can call; the events lane calls it and a test asserts no lane constructs its own ReferentResolver, because the third copy is always the one that drifts. It FAILS OPEN - a check that could not run passes the question through, since refusing a legitimate question on an infrastructure fault is the worse trade. VERIFIED LIVE: 'are there any vibration anomalies on floor 9' now returns "'floor 9' does not exist in this building, so there is nothing to report about it", and 'any anomalies on floor 4 today' returns 159 episodes ALL in Room4.* where it previously returned 500 across every floor. TWO OF MY OWN DEFECTS WERE CAUGHT ON THE WAY: (1) the helper referenced _active_namespace without importing it, which raised, failed open as designed, and would have left the events lane carrying a gate that never once fired while logging a line nobody reads - failing open is right, failing open silently on a coding error makes a guard decorative; (2) narrowing the episodes without rebuilding by_detector left the prose quoting unfiltered totals, and the GROUNDING GUARD rejected the answer live with 'a number in the text could not be traced back to the underlying data'. That is the guard doing exactly its job on my change. 22 tests across test_events_narrow_to_question.py and test_referent_gate_is_shared.py.

Title: REFUTED - routing is deterministic; the lane changes were my own deployments
Description: Observed repeatedly while verifying BUG-395/399. 'any anomalies this week' reached the events lane on one run and the capability lane on the next; 'are there any energy spikes on floor 2 today' reached anomaly once and sensor_data later; 'is there a Voltage fluctuation...' moved from anomaly to general_knowledge. The deterministic routing CONTRACT is stable - it only fires on what the LLM classified - and the LLM's classification of a borderline question is not.
Root_Cause: Intent classification is an LLM call, and the routing contract's rules are mostly conditioned on the intent it returns. A question that classifies differently between runs therefore reaches a different rule set.
Fix_Approach: Do not chase individual questions. Measure it first: ask a fixed set N times and count lane changes, so the rate is known before anything is changed. It also means a single live probe is not evidence a routing fix works or fails - several runs of this session's verification were confounded by exactly this.
Verification: MEASURED AND REFUTED 2026-09-02. scripts/measure_routing_variance.py asked 12 borderline questions 5 times each, flushing the response cache between rounds (without that flush the script would measure the CACHE and report perfect stability regardless): 12/12 consistent, 100%. Routing does not vary within a deployment. THE CAVEAT WAS WRONG AND THE ERROR WAS MINE. Every lane change I attributed to LLM nondeterminism happened ACROSS deployments in which I had changed the very things that drive classification. 'any energy spikes' moved capability -> anomaly because I added the HBCO lay terms and cleared the concept cache - that was the fix working. 'energy spikes on floor 2' moved anomaly -> sensor_data across the same change. 'voltage fluctuation' moved anomaly -> general_knowledge after the building-facts TTL and lay terms landed. I compared runs either side of my own edits and called the difference noise. CONSEQUENCE FOR EARLIER CONCLUSIONS: the claim that CAVEAT-396 could not be verified because 'the questions moved' is wrong - they move deterministically, to a lane my changes sent them to, and that is a routing question with an answer rather than variance to be tolerated. Corrected on that row. The script is kept: it is the cheap way to establish that a lane change is real before attributing it to anything.

Title: A sample-count fetch limit silently becomes a shorter time window when cadence rises
Description: The anomaly scanner fetched a fixed 600 samples per sensor. That is a window only in combination with the publish cadence, and the cadence changed underneath it: at 30 seconds, 600 samples is 5 hours, less than the 6 hours stuck() requires. Nothing in the code connected the two numbers, so raising the publisher's coverage (BUG-390) silently shortened every detector's view.
Root_Cause: A limit expressed in samples where the requirement is expressed in hours.
Verification: per_uuid_limit is now derived from the longest detector window and the fastest publish cadence rather than written as a constant, with the arithmetic stated at the definition so the coupling is visible. Worth re-checking whenever either the cadence or a detector threshold changes - the same class of defect recurs silently.

Title: The points the system WATCHES are not the points it FEEDS
Description: The dev publisher writes the 1,528 points listed in bldg1_narrow_publish_map.json every 30 seconds. The anomaly scanner watches the 1,859 points the capability schema attaches to a space. The two sets overlap but are not the same: injections into scanner-visible sensors found only ~27 rows across 7 hours (a 15-minute backfill cadence, not the publisher's 30-second one), and a dropout injection was skipped outright for having no rows in its window.
Root_Cause: REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-03, and the reconciliation that 'found' it was itself the defect. The premise came from comparing publisher MAP FILES, and there are three of them, none aware of the others: a narrow map (1,528), an extended map (628, carrying per-Brick-class value ranges), and the wide table's columns, which no map describes. Reading only the first found 605 'unfed' watched points. 509 of those are fed by the extended map and 96 are wide COLUMNS written by the same INSERT every tick - all 96 measured as receiving values. Asking the question that has one answer - per-uuid, through the adapters, independent of any map - returns 1,859 watched / 1,859 fresh / 0 stale / 0 silent. Every point the scanner watches is fed. TWO REAL DEFECTS were found underneath the false one, both now fixed: (1) generate_publisher_map matched ref:storedAt (a registry KEY) against the store's TABLE NAME, which coincide for 15 of 17 stores and silently dropped the two that differ - a building whose keys and tables differ throughout would have written an EMPTY map with no error; (2) the far more damaging BUG-403, which is the actual cause of the '27 rows across 7 hours' this caveat was written from.
Fix_Approach: Ask freshness per uuid through the adapters rather than reconciling map files. scripts/reconcile_watched_and_fed.py is now that check and exits non-zero when a watched point has produced nothing, so it stands as a gate rather than a report nobody reruns. The generator matches the registry key, emits the real table name, and defers to any map the publisher loads ALONGSIDE it - explicitly NOT to the legacy map, which is loaded only INSTEAD of it and would have left 19 points fed by nobody. The publisher drops a uuid claimed by both maps so an overlap can never double a point's sampling rate.
Verification: Live on bldg1: 1,859 watched points, 1,859 with a reading inside 30 minutes, 0 stale, 0 silent, across 10 stores (509 database1_floors04, 448 contact_data, 224 noise_data, 224 occupancy_data, 201 light_data, 96 database1, 64 co2_data, 64 humidity_data, 28 temperature_data, 1 plant_data). The wide store is reported per-store and the narrow stores per-uuid because their timestamps mean different things, and the tool states which it used rather than implying it. The fixed generator reproduces the deployed 1,528-point map exactly, so the map is now DERIVABLE rather than accidental. 8 tests.

Title: Writer and reader disagreed about the clock by one hour, in opposite directions
Description: OntoSage stores time-series as naive UTC. mysql_adapter pins each of its sessions to +00:00 and its comment asserts that 'the dummy-data generator writes UTC'. It did not. The publisher wrote narrow rows with SQL NOW() on a session that inherited the MySQL server's SYSTEM zone - BST, UTC+1 - into DATETIME columns, which store what they are handed without converting it. Measured live: container utcnow 11:02:57, MySQL session tz '+00:00', NOW() == UTC_TIMESTAMP() == 11:02:57, and noise_data's newest row stamped 12:02:49. One hour ahead, on all 18 narrow tables.
Root_Cause: The wide table concealed it for as long as it has existed. sensor_data's timestamp column is TIMESTAMP, which MySQL converts on write using the writer's zone and again on read using the reader's, so the identical NOW() landed correctly there. The 18 narrow tables use DATETIME, which does not convert. One table type was right and eighteen were wrong - and the one that was right is the one anybody spot-checking would have looked at. The deeper cause is that the UTC convention was enforced in exactly one connection and merely ASSUMED at the other eighteen call sites, including in that connection's own comment. AND THE READER WAS WRONG TOO, IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION. Evidence assembly's _as_datetime localised every naive timestamp to BUILDING_TIMEZONE, with a comment arguing that 'the reading belongs to the building'. For narrow rows that exactly cancelled the writer's BST stamp, which is why neither half was ever noticed. Pinning the publisher to UTC therefore BROKE freshness rather than fixing it: measured live within minutes of the deploy, a co2 reading taken three minutes earlier came back as 2026-09-03T11:49:35+01:00 and was scored 63 minutes old against a 5-minute policy, downgrading a current answer to INFERRED. Fixing a clock at one end and not the other is worse than leaving both wrong.
Fix_Approach: Pin every MySQL session to UTC from one shared constant (shared/db_clock.py UTC_SESSION_INIT) and assert it at every call site, because the cost of the next one forgetting is not an error - it is an hour of silence that looks like data. On the reader side, split the two meanings rather than flipping a default: _as_observation_time reads a STORED reading as naive-UTC, _as_datetime keeps building-local for a time a human or the ontology expressed, because 'between 9 and 5' means nine and five in the building.
Verification: VERIFIED LIVE. Publisher image rebuilt (it is a build: context, not a mount - a restart would have changed nothing, BUG-343) and recreated; new rows now land at or before UTC now and are visible to a NOW()-bounded window: noise_data newest<=now 11:11:17 with 7 rows in the last 4 UTC minutes, same for contact_data and sensor_data_floors04. 19 call sites pinned across orchestrator/, shared/, scripts/ and the publisher; tests/test_db_sessions_pin_utc.py walks the source of every connect call and fails the build on an unpinned one - it found 7 sites I had not, two of them in orchestrator/ (synthetic/generator.py writes readings; admin_config.py). WHAT IT COST: any window bounded by NOW() dropped the newest hour of narrow data, which is exactly the '27 rows across 7 hours' and the dropout skipped for 'no rows in the window' recorded against BUG-360; and the freshness gate, ENFORCING since 2026-09-02, read a future timestamp as current and would have gone on calling a dead point fresh for a full hour after it stopped. READER HALF VERIFIED LIVE after flushing resp_cache and restarting: the same co2 question now returns observed_at 2026-09-03T11:54:05Z with status=observed and an empty gates_applied, where minutes earlier it returned +01:00 and status=inferred. 10 further tests in test_observation_times_are_utc.py pin both halves so neither can be corrected alone again. NOTE the first live probe read the RESPONSE CACHE (plan_trace decision_source=cache) and quoted a reading from the previous day - a cached answer is not evidence about a code change.

Title: Roughly 25M existing narrow rows remain stamped one hour ahead
Description: BUG-403 fixes the WRITER; it does not move rows already written. Every narrow row the publisher or the backfill produced carries the +1h stamp: ~24.7M rows across 18 tables (sensor_data_floors04 10.7M, contact_data 3.3M, occupancy_data 2.2M, sensor_data_synth 2.2M, light_data 1.8M, noise_data 1.8M, and 12 smaller). scripts/backfill_narrow_gap.py used datetime.now() on a BST host, so its 1,093,208 rows are shifted the same way and in the same direction - the history is uniformly offset rather than discontinuous, which is the better of the two ways to be wrong. sensor_data (wide, TIMESTAMP) is unaffected.
Root_Cause: A writer and a reader that disagreed about the clock for as long as both existed.
Fix_Approach: Two options, and the choice is the user's because one of them rewrites 25M rows of their data. (1) Leave it: the offset is uniform, the data is dev-mode top-up, and it ages out of every window that matters within hours. (2) Shift the narrow tables back one hour so the whole store agrees with the wide table and with wall-clock history. Also transient and worth knowing: for about an hour after the fix rows exist BOTH at correct-UTC (new) and up to +1h (old), so the newest hour looks stalled and the detectors may read the overlap as a flat run. Do not grade a detector round inside that hour.
Verification: USER DECISION 2026-09-03: keep the +1h stamps; option (1), leave it. The offset is uniform rather than discontinuous, the rows are dev-mode top-up, and it ages out of every window that matters within hours. No rewrite of 25M rows. The WRITER is fixed (BUG-403) so nothing new is stamped ahead, and tests/test_db_sessions_pin_utc.py keeps it that way. Recorded so a future reader does not mistake the historical offset for a live defect: rows older than 2026-09-03 11:07 UTC in the narrow tables are one hour ahead of the clock they should be read in, and that is known and accepted, not pending.

Title: The spike detector fires on roughly 64 findings per point against generated data
Description: Every sweep returns ~124,000 spike findings across 1,859 points, stable across rounds 15-19 and unchanged by the clock fix, so it is not an artifact of the BUG-403 cutover. The dev publisher draws each value uniformly at random from the modality's range with no autocorrelation, so the series is white noise and a deviation-from-recent-behaviour detector fires almost everywhere. Injected spikes are still found 2/2 and precision against the labels is 1.0, so this does not affect the graded result - but 'organic context: 8,289 episodes on 1,835 sensors in the same hour' is not a building, it is a random number generator.
Root_Cause: MY FIRST ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG AND I TESTED IT RATHER THAN SHIPPING IT. I wrote that white noise makes a deviation detector fire everywhere. Measured: spike() returns the SAME 2 findings on 720 samples of uniform noise and on 720 samples of shaped signal, even though the mean step per sample falls from 34.1% of the range to 1.1%. The reason is in the detector - a spike must clear max(8.09*MAD, 0.05*range), and uniform noise has an enormous MAD, so it SUPPRESSES ITSELF. Pure noise is not spike-prone. What is spike-prone is MIXING TWO REGIMES: a 12-sample window sitting entirely in smooth 15-minute backfill has a tiny MAD, and the next 30-second live sample from the white-noise generator lands far outside it. Measured on constructed series - backfill only: 0 episodes; backfill + white-noise live tail: flags; backfill + SHAPED live tail: 0. The production magnitude (~67 episodes per point rather than 1) then comes from _episodes splitting a run whenever two flags are more than 2*cadence = 60s apart, which intermittent flagging at a 30s cadence does constantly. || THE ACTUAL CAUSE, FOUND 2026-09-04, AND IT WAS NEITHER OF MY FIRST TWO GUESSES. I said white noise; measured, noise and shaped signal give the same 2 findings. I then said regime mixing; the shaped publisher ran 14 hours and the sweep count did not fall (124k -> 133k). Measuring PER STORE over one 36-hour window settles it: contact_data 247.8 spike episodes per sensor against occupancy 17.5, light 4.2, floors04 4.2, noise 4.0, co2 3.8. With 466 contacts that is ~115,000 of the sweep's 133,663 - the whole flood, from one signal type. A CONTACT IS A STATE, NOT A MEASUREMENT: it sits at 0, the rolling MAD over a 12-sample window collapses to zero, the spread falls to its 5%-of-range floor, and a legitimate door opening clears that floor twentyfold. spike() was working exactly as designed on a signal it was never designed for, and a user asking 'any anomalies this week' was reading a count of doors being opened.
Fix_Approach: Give the live publisher the same shaped signal the backfill already generates, so there is ONE regime rather than two. Done: mysql-dummy-publish-dev/sensor_signal.py - first-order mean reversion toward a diurnal centre, a per-sensor phase derived from the uuid (stable across restarts, so drift_vs_peers has peers that differ without wandering), bounded per-step noise, and binary points that hold state and flip rarely instead of coin-flipping every write. Per-modality cadence in the same module (CAVEAT-233): co2/occupancy/noise 60s, voc/lux 120s, temp/rh/flow/vib/pm25/contact 300s, runtime 600s, kwh 900s - roughly 80% fewer writes than every point every 30 seconds, and a test asserts no cadence is so slow that stuck's 6-hour window holds fewer than the 12 samples the detectors need. || AND the real fix: spike() now returns nothing for a signal taking three or fewer distinct levels across its whole history. Keyed on the SIGNAL, never on a modality name, so a building whose binary points are called something else is covered without a literal. Not a loss of coverage - schedule_violation catches a door open out of hours and stuck catches one held open, and both still run.
Verification: Publisher image rebuilt and recreated (a restart would not have carried it - the Dockerfile needed COPY sensor_signal.py, and a test asserts that, because source correct with the image stale is this project's BUG-343 pattern). VERIFIED LIVE on bldg1 past the restart seed: consecutive-step as a share of range is now co2 1.4%, occupancy 3.3%, noise 1.7%, contact 0% - against roughly 33% before. Cadence verified live: co2/occupancy/noise 6 rows per 5 minutes, temperature/energy 2. 15 tests. NOT YET CONFIRMED and deliberately not claimed: the sweep's spike count. The detectors look back 12-40 hours, so most of the fetched window is still the old white-noise data; the count cannot fall until shaped history fills it. Re-measure the sweep after roughly two days of uptime and compare against the 124,299-124,442 baseline. A module named signal.py was renamed to sensor_signal.py before it shipped: it would have shadowed the stdlib signal module the publisher uses for its SIGTERM handler, silently. || 8 tests, including that a genuine 99999 outlier in a continuous series is still caught (the shape the fault injector uses) and that the guard reads len(set(values)) rather than the modality string. The shaped-signal work stands on its own merits - consecutive steps fell from ~33% of range to 1.4-3.3%, and the wide table's 450 untyped sensors got physical ranges (CAVEAT-410) - but it was NOT what caused the spike count, and I should not have written that it was before measuring per store. || VERIFIED LIVE BY SWEEP 2026-09-04. findings 139,384 -> 19,348 (86% down); spike 133,663 -> 13,409 (90% down). EVERY OTHER DETECTOR IS UNCHANGED - dropout 5,654 -> 5,653, stuck 19 -> 19, drift_vs_peers 20 -> 11, schedule_violation 282 -> 256 - so roughly 120,000 spurious findings were removed without losing coverage anywhere. Sweep duration also fell 540s -> 281s (the fetch halving from CAVEAT-414 compounding), which directly relieves the GraphDB contention behind CAVEAT-415's 52 silent capability fallbacks. The remaining 7.2 spike episodes per point is plausible for generated data; occupancy at 17.5 per sensor is the next candidate to look at, and it does NOT hit the three-level rule because it ranges 0-30.

Title: The hosted provider was unreachable on three of four buildings, by stale env override
Description: MODEL_PROVIDER=cloud sends every call to OLLAMA_CLOUD_BASE_URL. .env1, .env3 and .env4 all set it to https://api.ollama.ai/v1, which has NO DNS RECORD - measured today, getaddrinfo failure - while https://ollama.com/v1 answers in 0.7s. Only .env2 had been hand-corrected, which is why every hosted run in this project's history happened on bldg2 and why the hosted arm read as a quota problem elsewhere. All three tracked .env*.example files carried the dead host too, so a fresh clone gets it for every building.
Root_Cause: The DEFAULT in shared/config.py was already correct: BUG-175 fixed it and left a comment saying the old host has no DNS record. A default only takes effect where nothing overrides it, and every env file overrode it. This is the third instance of the same pattern - BUG-221 (.env at OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=8192 while the fix sat in .env2/.env3) and BUG-343 (source fixed, image stale). The override files are part of the fix.
Fix_Approach: Point every env file and every tracked example at the working host, and guard the TRACKED examples with a test, since the live .env files are gitignored and a clone only ever sees the examples.
Verification: Verified live BEFORE the fix: https://api.ollama.ai/v1 -> URLError getaddrinfo failed on both model names; https://ollama.com/v1 -> HTTP 200 in 0.6-0.7s on both gpt-oss:120b and gpt-oss:120b-cloud. Fixed in .env1, .env3, .env4 and in .env1/.env2/.env3.example (.env.example does not set the key and inherits the default). 7 tests in test_env_examples_have_no_dead_hosts.py: no example may configure a non-resolving host, the code default must not be one, and any example that sets the key must AGREE with the default - a comment naming the dead host is allowed, since that is documentation.

Title: A feed-registered point declares a storage location that has no column
Description: One of the 2,734 declared streams cannot ever return data: uuid dc7e9d93-9398-a722-2e27-3747a644212c, bldg:feed_synthetic_timetable ('Sensor feed synthetic_timetable'), carries ref:storedAt database1 while sensor_data has no column of that name. Found by checking the wide store column by column rather than accepting its table-level timestamp. It appears in no input/*.ttl and in no publish map, so it was created at runtime by the V3 feed framework's point auto-registration.
Root_Cause: The feed registry writes ref:storedAt when it registers a point but does not create or verify the storage the reference names. Contract 8 requires BOTH halves - a triple in the graph AND rows in a registered store - and this satisfies only the first.
Fix_Approach: Root cause addressed rather than the symptom deleted. The feed registry auto-registers a POINT for every feed and types it brick:Sensor, so a TIMETABLE feed produced a phantom sensor declaring ref:storedAt database1 against a table with no such column - a stream that could never return data, counted among the building sensors. The feed itself had never produced a row (NOTE-413) and the same CSV is now lifted as a record register of 675 sessions, so the feed is disabled with the reason written into feeds.yaml, and the phantom point deleted. The registry typing a non-sensor feed as a sensor is the deeper defect and is NOT fixed here - it will recur for any future non-sensor feed.
Verification: Live: triples matching feed_synthetic_timetable = 0. Sensors declaring an archival interval fell from 2,728 to 2,727 - exactly the phantom, and the metrology generator now reports 2,727 from the graph, so file and graph agree.

Title: Tests marked unit make real LLM calls, so the suite's result depends on the provider
Description: test_capability_bare_building.py::test_uploaded_document_source_is_not_preempted passed for months under MODEL_PROVIDER=local and failed the moment the provider moved to the hosted 120B for the stakeholder-catalogue replay. It asserted provenance == 'document_kb'; the hosted model took the LLM-synthesis path and returned 'document_answered'. A BETTER answer failed a test written around a weaker model. The test's own docstring states the invariant as 'an uploaded-manual match must be returned even when metrics and triples both miss' - which both labels satisfy - so the assertion was over-specified rather than the behaviour wrong.
Root_Cause: `pytest -m unit` is documented as the fast/offline suite, and some of its tests reach the configured LLM. Confirmed from the run log: httpx POST https://ollama.com/v1/chat/completions during collection of the unit selection. So the suite's result is a function of .env, which makes a green run on one machine no evidence about another - and makes a provider switch look like a code regression.
Fix_Approach: Two things, and only the first is done. (1) DONE: the assertion accepts either document-sourced provenance and says why, with the content assertion ('north car park') left as the real proof - it holds on both paths. (2) NOT DONE and the larger job: find every unit-marked test that reaches a live LLM and either stub the client or re-mark it integration. Worth doing before any claim that the unit suite is offline, and worth doing with a network guard fixture rather than by inspection, since inspection is what let this sit. || PART 2 DONE 2026-09-05, with the guard fixture the row asked for rather than by inspection. tests/conftest.py blocks outbound NON-LOOPBACK sockets for any test marked `unit`, naming the offending test in the failure, with one explicit escape hatch (@pytest.mark.allow_network, registered in pytest.ini). Loopback stays allowed: a test talking to 127.0.0.1 is a different problem and conflating them would hide both. A second hook watches COLLECTION, because the original observation was an import-time call that a per-test fixture cannot see.
Verification: The one failing test is fixed and the suite is green again (4,286 pass / 3 skip). The provider-dependence itself is unmeasured: I do not know how many other unit tests reach the network, only that at least one did and that nothing prevents it. || MEASURED 2026-09-05 with the guard active: 4,965 unit tests pass and ZERO reach a non-loopback address, at collection or execution. That claim rests on a POSITIVE CONTROL (tests/test_zz_network_guard_selfcheck.py) which deliberately opens an outbound socket and asserts the guard stops it - a guard that catches nothing and a suite that reaches nothing look identical without one. The original ollama.com call was from an earlier state; the guard is what keeps it from returning unnoticed.

Title: The committed V7 tracker drifts behind the live one by design
Description: tasks/ is gitignored by the user's decision, so docs/V7_TRACKER.csv is the only record of V7 progress a clone or a supervisor sees. Measured 2026-09-03: it was five rows behind - reporting 16 done against a real 17, with V7-T02, V7-T04 and V7-T40 shown as untouched when all three were in progress, and V7-T43 shown as todo when it was done.
Root_Cause: build_v7_tracker.py writes BOTH copies, but only when the generator runs. The session protocol flips status and notes directly in tasks/V7_TRACKER.csv, so nothing propagates until someone happens to regenerate. Regenerating is also the wrong remedy: it rebuilds every column from the TASKS definitions and preserves only status and notes, so a hand-edit anywhere else in the live file is silently reverted.
Fix_Approach: A small explicit mirror of exactly the two progress columns, with a --check mode that exits non-zero on drift so it can gate a commit rather than be remembered.
Verification: scripts/sync_tracker_to_docs.py mirrors status and notes only, refuses to run when the two files hold DIFFERENT TASKS (that is a definition change and belongs to the generator), and --check reports drift without writing. Ran it: 5 rows updated, then --check clean. Worth running before any commit that touches a tracker.

Title: 450 of 1,218 wide sensors reported numbers with no physical meaning
Description: get_realistic_value() was an if-chain of nine name rules and returned None for anything it did not name, falling through to gen_value's TYPE fallback - where tinyint becomes rand_int(0, 1). Measured: 450 of bldg1's 1,218 wide sensor names (37%) reached that fallback, i.e. twelve whole sensor classes across 34 rooms each. The visible failure: 'what is the PM2.5 level in Room 5.04' answered 1. Grounded in a real, live column and nonsense as a reading - worse than declining, and the failure contract 4 exists to prevent. The affected classes are PM1/PM2.5/PM10, CO, NO2, formaldehyde, oxygen, four MQ-series gas sensors, ethyl alcohol, floor energy, wind speed and electricity price - and PM2.5, CO, NO2 and formaldehyde are named DIRECTLY by the stakeholder catalogues.
Root_Cause: A per-name if-chain with a silent None default. Every class anyone forgot to add became a column generated from its SQL type, and a type is not a physical range. The narrow tables had modality ranges (BUG-390 added the missing ones for exactly this reason); the wide table never got the same treatment.
Fix_Approach: Replace the chain with a data table of (name substring, modality, lo, hi, decimals) so adding a class is one line, and route the value through sensor_signal so the wide table is shaped like the narrow ones (CAVEAT-405) instead of white noise. Two traps had to be held by tests rather than care: 'pm10' contains 'pm1', so the wrong order types every PM10 sensor as PM1 in silence; and a range with decimals written into an integer column is truncated, so 0.25 into a tinyint stores 0 and a correct range still yields an implausible reading - the column's own scale therefore wins over the table's fallback.
Verification: 0 of 1,218 names now fall through, from 450. VERIFIED LIVE after rebuilding the publisher image (a restart would not have carried it): PM2.5 23 ug/m3, PM10 34, PM1 10 - correctly ordered, since the finer fraction is part of the coarser - oxygen 20.80%, formaldehyde 33.28 ppb, electricity price 0.3121, wind 7.43 m/s. 18 tests, including the PM10/PM1 ordering trap, the integer-truncation trap, the air-quality enum not being swallowed by the air-quality-index rule, and oxygen never wandering below 20%.

Title: A capture did not record which model answered, while being deliberately split across two
Description: The stakeholder-catalogue run (stamp 20260903_152449, 2,480 questions) is deliberately split: hosted gpt-oss:120b until its rolling call budget runs out, then local gpt-oss:20b on the freed GPU, at the user's instruction. The capture's columns were qid, source, role, question, intent, answer, shas, status, gates, length, elapsed - and NO provider and NO model. Nothing in the artifact would have said the second half was answered by a different system, so a later reader or a regression comparison would treat the whole file as one homogeneous baseline.
Root_Cause: The harness was written when the provider never changed within a run. It reads .env nowhere and the running config nowhere, so a provider switch is invisible to it. Same family as BUG-359 (grading bldg1 against bldg2's injections) and CAVEAT-393 (recall over whichever detectors survived an offset): the harness reporting a completeness it had not achieved, in the direction that looks like success.
Fix_Approach: Stamp provider and model on EVERY row, read from the running system's /api/v1/admin/ai-config rather than from .env - .env is what someone intended and the container holds what is loaded (BUG-406 was exactly that gap; CAVEAT-178 the same shape). Re-poll every 25 questions so a mid-run switch is located to within 25 rows and announced, not absorbed. Rows written before the columns existed are labelled 'unrecorded' rather than blank, because blank reads as 'answered by no model', which is a claim, while unrecorded is the truth.
Verification: 12 tests, including that an admin 403 labels the run rather than killing a multi-hour capture, that an unknown provider is named rather than guessed, and that _drop_rows' rewrite carries the labels onto old rows. THE HOSTED HALF OF RUN 20260903_152449 WILL CARRY 'unrecorded' - it was already in flight when this landed, and its provider was cloud / gpt-oss:120b-cloud, recorded here so the provenance exists even though the rows do not carry it. The local half will be stamped.

Title: Readiness reported DATA for two sources that hold no data
Description: source_system_readiness.py decided 'if count or rows or feeds: DATA', so an ENABLED FEED alone was enough - a switch treated as a proxy for the data it is meant to produce. Measured on bldg1: 'timetable' reported DATA on 0 triples, 0 Postgres rows and 0 rows in the events store that feeds.yaml's own comment says it writes to; its 55 KB CSV has never been ingested. 'weather_external' the same. The report read 26 DATA / 1 ABSENT; the truth is 24 DATA / 2 WIRED / 1 ABSENT.
Root_Cause: The feeds clause was added for a good reason - an earlier version reported ABSENT for systems whose data genuinely arrives by feed - but it was written as a proxy rather than a measurement. This is not cosmetic: V7 uses readiness to decide which questions it believes it can answer, so a false DATA inflates the coverage ceiling AND routes a question to a lane that holds nothing. Same family as CAVEAT-402 (reconciling map files instead of asking the store) and CAVEAT-411 (a capture that did not record its own model).
Fix_Approach: Measure the feed's OUTPUT, per system, where feeds.yaml says it lands. Keep DATA when the output cannot be measured at all - None is UNKNOWN, and demoting on unknown would re-introduce the under-reporting the clause was added to fix, turning a connection hiccup into a planning decision. Add a fourth state WIRED for 'configured and has produced nothing', ranked BELOW prose, because a document you can quote answers more questions than a feed that is switched on and empty.
Verification: Re-ran live: 24 DATA / 2 WIRED / 1 ABSENT. The single ABSENT is hr_identity, which V7-T35 holds deliberately (the catalogues forbid exposing who holds what). 12 tests, including that an unmeasurable feed keeps DATA, that an unreachable store reports unknown rather than zero, and that an unknown state added upstream takes the WORST rank rather than a middling one - the scorecard's default was hardcoded to 2, so a new state would have ranked better than ABSENT and quietly raised the reported ceiling. TWO REAL GAPS ARE NOW VISIBLE rather than hidden: the timetable feed does not ingest, and the weather feed registers no points.

Title: The timetable and weather feeds are enabled and have never produced a row
