An index-driven rewrite (VALUES on class IRIs) was measured at 3.1 s for 6 classes with ?timeout=5 server-side, still too slow per question, and its answer is almost entirely inferred subclass nesting that the static Brick TBox gives for free. After the demo: compute containment from the TBox. GENERAL FINDING: no GraphDB call in this codebase passes a server-side ?timeout=, so any slow query can outlive its client and cascade the same way (CAVEAT-536).
Verification: Targeted re-run of the failed probe groups owed after restart.

Title: No GraphDB query sets a server-side timeout, so a slow query outlives its client and stalls every later one
Description: BUG-535 showed the mechanism: httpx timed out at 25 s, GraphDB kept executing, and the next 7 unrelated questions timed out behind it. RDF4J/GraphDB honours a `timeout` request parameter (seconds) that aborts the query server-side; nothing in orchestrator/ passes it.
Fix_Approach: After the demo: pass ?timeout= on every SPARQL POST, derived from the same budget as the client timeout, in one helper rather than 40 call sites. Not before Friday — it touches every graph call.

Title: A floor comparison is aggregated by the LLM from per-sensor lines, and took 251 s once every sensor was read
Description: After BUG-534 raised the sensor cap, 'Compare the average CO2 on floor 1 versus floor 3' read all 61 sensors — and took 251 s end to end, against ~72 s with 30. Node timeline: SQL 1 s (61,000 rows), analytics sandbox 3 s, then ~210 s in ONE narration call: a 13,342-char prompt with the analysis output for 64 sensors plus 64 sensor descriptions. The template computes PER-SENSOR averages; the question asks for PER-FLOOR ones, so the model is left to aggregate 64 lines into two numbers itself — arithmetic by LLM on the most quotable figure in the answer.
Root_Cause: Floor membership is known inside the SPARQL floor-scoped template (sensor -> space -> floor) and dropped before the analytics lane: sensor_metadata carries label, sensor_uri, uuid, kind and unit, no floor. With nothing to group by, the only aggregation available is in the prose.
Fix_Approach: Planned Wed-16 as the floor-comparison slice of V12-28: bind ?floor in the floor-scoped template, carry it in sensor_metadata, compute per-floor mean/min/max/sensor-count deterministically, and give the narrator only that summary. Expected effect: prompt shrinks from 64 lines to 2, the figures stop being model arithmetic. Until then the question is kept OUT of the demo script; the 120-sensor cap stays, because a fast average over 5 of 13 sensors is not a better answer.
Verification: sensor_metadata carries floorNum; series_summary.summarise_groups computes per-floor sensor count, readings, mean/range (energy also totalled) behind units.aggregation_decision; analytics narration gets those lines and a 1,500-char cap on sandbox output instead of 64 per-sensor lines. tests/test_a_floor_comparison_is_computed_not_narrated.py (13). Live latency re-measure owed (RUN-06).

Title: One database, two clocks: the real wide table is local time and the synthetic narrow tables are UTC
Description: Measured 2026-09-15 at 00:23:42 UTC / 01:23:42 BST: newest sensor_data (wide) row 01:23:17 — LOCAL; newest co2_data, occupancy_data and sensor_data_synth (narrow) rows 00:22 — UTC. Host MySQL NOW() is local (time_zone SYSTEM); the data-publisher container runs UTC with no TZ set and writes its own clock into the narrow tables. So every time window and every freshness age in this system is correct for one kind of table and an hour wrong for the other during BST. The 2026-09-12 V12-08 work (BUG-517/518/519) moved several clock reads from utcnow() to building-local time on the documented premise 'the stores hold local stamps' — true for the wide table, FALSE for the narrow tables. Those fixes corrected floor-5 (real, wide) answers and shifted narrow-table windows and ages by an hour the other way. Remaining utcnow() readers (event_query_service:388, dialogue_agent._resolve_relative_dt, anomaly diagnosis/scanner, compliance_register_service) are each right or wrong depending on which table the question lands on. Found while diagnosing 'Is Room 1.06 free for the next two hours?' (events lane on utcnow(); separately, 'next N hours' is not parsed and falls back to the whole day).
Root_Cause: No declared timestamp convention per datasource. database_registry.yaml records `nature` per store but not its clock, so every reader has to assume one, and two generators assumed differently.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED — needs a design decision, not a one-line swap. Options: (a) source fix — set the building timezone on the data-publisher service so new narrow rows are local; existing narrow history stays UTC, leaving a one-hour seam at the switch; (b) principled — declare `timestamps: local|utc` per store in database_registry.yaml and convert each window to the store's clock in the adapter, so no reader assumes; (c) for the demo only — build the script on floor-5 rooms (real data, wide table, local stamps), where the 2026-09-12 fixes are correct, and avoid time-sensitive questions on floors 0-4. Decide Wednesday morning.
Verification: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-15: the premise was a measurement error. The stores are UTC (BUG-403): mysql_adapter pins every session to +00:00; sensor_data is a TIMESTAMP column, which MySQL converts to the SESSION zone on read, so a measurement through a SYSTEM-zone (BST) session made it LOOK local. Read on a +00:00 session at 00:34 UTC the newest rows were sensor_data 00:34, co2_data/occupancy_data 00:33, sensor_data_synth 00:32; events are generated from utcnow(). There is one clock, not two. Option (a) (TZ on data-publisher) was NOT applied: the publisher forces a +00:00 session regardless of TZ, and changing that would have reintroduced BUG-403.

Title: 'Is Room 1.06 free for the next two hours?' is answered about the whole day
Description: Live 01:20 BST: answer '**Room1.06 is booked today**: 08:20-18:00' — true, but the next two hours are free and the answer implies they are not. event_query_service.parse_window recognises 'at 2pm', named days, parts of day, 'right now', but not 'next N hours', so it falls back to the whole day. CORRECTION 2026-09-15: event_query_service's utcnow() is CORRECT for the store; what is wrong is (1) 'today' taken as the UTC day and (2) booking times SHOWN in UTC — '08:20-18:00' is 09:20-19:00 in the building. Both belong with the display fix (RUN-07/08).
Fix_Approach: parse_window: 'next/coming N hours|minutes' (digits or words) -> [now, now+N], labelled 'for the next N hours'. EventQueryService parses on the building's clock (to_local(store now)) and converts the window back with to_store, so 'today' and 'at 3pm' are the building's.
Verification: tests/test_event_times_are_local_to_people_and_utc_to_stores.py (12). Live re-ask owed: 'Is Room1.06 free for the next two hours?' (RUN-11).

Title: Stored UTC times are shown to people as if they were building-local
Description: Every store is UTC (BUG-403). Where an answer prints a stored time — booking intervals ('Room1.06 is booked today: 08:20-18:00' is 09:20-19:00 in the building under BST), a reading's 'latest at', a recheck line — it prints the UTC wall clock with no zone. A person reads it as local and is an hour out.
Fix_Approach: EventQueryService._fmt_dt converts stored times (datetime or string) to the building zone; RecheckAdvice.describe(tz_name=) shows 'measured at' and 'recheck by' locally while the age stays one-clock UTC; the orchestrator passes building_tz() to both. No zone -> unchanged. Reading timestamps narrated by the LLM already carry an explicit 'UTC' label, which is honest; left as is.
Verification: Same test file (booking 07:20Z shown 08:20; recheck 00:20Z shown 01:20 with a 5-minute age). Live re-ask owed (RUN-11).

Title: seed_timeseries_backends.py re-serialises database_registry.yaml, deleting its documentation and writing a literal password
Description: Running the seeder on 2026-09-12 to register TimescaleDB and Cassandra rewrote bldg1/database_registry.yaml wholesale: 358 insertions, 786 deletions. The deletions are the file's hand-written comments (nature/provenance notes, placeholder syntax docs), lost because yaml.safe_dump cannot round-trip comments. It also wrote `password: ontosage_ts_secret` as a literal instead of a ${TIMESCALE_PASSWORD:-...} placeholder, so the registry would carry a credential in version control.
Root_Cause: The seeder loads, mutates and dumps YAML instead of appending text; the entry it writes uses resolved values.
Fix_Approach: Checkpoint 2026-09-15: file restored from HEAD, the two entries NOT committed (the parity tests build their adapters directly). Fix after the demo: append the entry as TEXT with ${VAR:-default} placeholders, never re-dump the file.
Verification: register() appends entry TEXT with ${VAR:-default} placeholders (password ${TIMESCALE_PASSWORD}, no literal); refuses if 'databases' is not the last top-level key; never re-dumps. tests/test_the_seeder_never_rewrites_the_registry.py (3) + adapter parity tests 24 green.

Title: An Open WebUI login whose OntoSage username is not the email's local part chats as readonly
Description: resolve_forwarded_user's comment said 'match on username first, then email'; the code only looked up usernames (the full email, then its local part). The owner's Open WebUI login suhasdevmanemech@gmail.com maps to the OntoSage admin 'Suhas' by nothing, so every chat created a readonly placeholder row and ran at least privilege: metadata only, for the account the demo is given from.
Root_Cause: Prose described a lookup that was never written (lesson #102 shape: the comment was trusted, not the code).
Fix_Approach: postgres_manager.get_users_by_email (case-insensitive); resolver order is exact username -> registered email -> local part, placeholders skipped at every step. The Suhas account's email was set to the Open WebUI login (it was NULL; the account was already admin in both systems).
Verification: tests/test_forwarded_user_rbac.py 11/11 (3 new). Live /v1: log '[forwarded-user] suhasdevmanemech@gmail.com -> Suhas (role=admin)', CO2 answer for 5.01 in 29.4 s.

Title: A chart keyword inside another word draws a chart, and an empty dataset is charted and narrated as a finding
Description: _user_wants_visualization tested `kw in msg`, so 'mapped' matched 'map', 'drawing more power' matched 'drawing', 'reconfigure' matched 'figure', 'solar panels' matched 'panel': 70 of 4,060 stakeholder questions (word-boundary: 0 of those). Stakeholder run #1 Q2 ('Which permission groups ... mapped opening can be evidenced?') was answered with an empty bar chart narrated as 'no bars appear, indicating that either all groups have an assigned owner or the data is missing'. _visualization_node called the viz agent even when the pre-chart fetch returned nothing.
Root_Cause: Substring matching; no empty-data guard before LLM chart code generation.
Fix_Approach: Whole-word regex over the keyword list; 'drawing' removed (building sense: power draw, design drawings). The viz node records viz_result skipped=no_data with no media when there is still nothing to chart, so dispatch falls through to what the other lanes found.
Verification: tests/test_a_chart_is_asked_for_in_words_and_drawn_from_data.py (16) + routing_accuracy / pipeline_ctx / safety_net 100 green. Live re-ask owed (RUN-11).

Title: Checking that an absent word is not in the graph scans every triple and times out; a dead Fuseki fallback hides the timeout
Description: ReferentResolver._exists ran `?s ?p ?o` with STRSTARTS + CONTAINS + an EXISTS label check per subject. A present token hits LIMIT 1 in <1 s; an absent one scans the graph: 27.6 s measured on bldg1, over the 30 s httpx timeout under load. Stakeholder run #1 Q3 ('room moves') declined with 'the existence check didn't complete in time' after 37 s. sparql_agent then tried Fuseki, which is commented out of compose, and its DNS error ('Name or service not known') replaced GraphDB's ReadTimeout, whose message is empty.
Root_Cause: A whole-graph scan used as an existence test; a fallback that overwrites the primary error.
Fix_Approach: Two narrow lookups: rdfs:label CONTAINS (short-circuits), then typed-subject IRI CONTAINS. Measured on 5.01/atrium/kitchen/chiller: same hits as the old query; ~2.5 s per miss lookup. Fuseki failure re-raises the GraphDB error; the error carries its exception type.
Verification: tests/test_an_absent_word_is_checked_without_scanning_the_graph.py (4) + 98 referent tests green. Live re-ask owed (RUN-11).

Title: Approval words used as adjectives send a question to the approvals register, which answers it wrongly and states the absence as fact
Description: ApprovalRecord's layTerms include approved/confirmed/verified/authorised/evidenced (declared deliberately: 53% of unanswered corpus questions use them). Scoring made the adjective use count the same as the predicative one. Stakeholder run #1, as admin via /v1: Q6 'started late against today's APPROVED schedule' -> 'APR-010 ... 1 day late' (an approval date read as a start time); Q14 'lack CONFIRMED fire-warden coverage' -> 'None of the occupied zones have a confirmed fire-warden' (absence in the wrong register, stated about fire safety); Q16 'VERIFIED alternative location'. Separately EventActivity's bare 'activities' pulled Q8/Q15 (continuity, first-aid) into a raw 56-row open-day dump.
Root_Cause: Lay-term scoring is lexical; the TBox had no way to say a term names the class only when used of it.
Fix_Approach: TBox: new ontosage:qualifierTerms property; ApprovalRecord declares seven qualifiers; EventActivity loses bare activity/activities. record_registry reads qualifierTerms and scores a qualifier 0 when the next word is a content word (attributive), full weight when followed by a function word or nothing. Corpus impact measured before landing: 659 of 4,060 questions change register (356 no longer claimed by any register, go to classification); samples: 'approved weekend service or event' -> PublicEvent, 'approved high-contrast display preset' -> AVReadiness.
Verification: tests/test_a_qualifier_names_its_register_only_when_used_of_it.py (14) + 450 register/schema tests green. ROUTING CHANGE: register probe group and stakeholder re-run owed after restart (RUN-10/13).

Title: Register handovers overflow the prompt into raw dumps, and their narration maps fields onto other concepts, certifies, and does not know the date
Description: Stakeholder run #1 via /v1: (a) routes+workspaces passed the 1,300-CELL budget but rendered 55.9k chars (prompt 58,848; every empty completion logged was >=56k at num_ctx 16384): three empty completions, then _format_results returned the raw bindings ('Found 44 result(s): 1. register: …') — Q8, Q15, Q25. (b) the narration prompt is the generic sensor-list one plus 'answer only from these records': Q6 read approval dates as plant start times, Q27 approval statuses as no-shows, Q24 certified that compliance records 'are retained for the correct period, in the authorised system', Q29 said 'events due today (2026-09-05)' on 15 Sep (a retrievedAt stamp).
Root_Cause: Budget in cells not characters; lineage columns repeated on every row; fallback dumps rows; no date and no rule against re-mapping or certifying.
Fix_Approach: _render_rows hoists values every row of a register shares into one header per register (label/id/status never hoisted; padded gaps listed once) — routes+workspaces 55.9k -> 30.0k, workspace+circulation 50.7k -> 27.4k; MAX_RECORD_CHARS=34000 measured with the same renderer on the primary, the scoped re-fetch and the second register; LLM failure on a handover returns a named-records list that states no conclusion; guidance adds building-local date and rules: say plainly when the records do not record it, never map a field onto another concept, never certify/approve/guarantee, never call a record 'yours'.
Verification: tests/test_a_register_handover_fits_the_prompt_and_says_what_it_lacks.py (7) + 422 sparql/register tests green (3 non-unit tests needing live services fail as before). Live re-ask of Q6/Q8/Q14/Q15/Q24/Q25/Q27/Q29 owed after restart.

Title: A count of sensors was reported as a measured quantity ('269 daylight hours in the deepest workstation')
Description: Stakeholder run #1 Q51 'Whats the daylight hour count in the deepest workstation this December?' generated SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sensor) AS ?count) WHERE { ?sensor rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf* brick:Illuminance_Sensor } = 269 and was narrated 'The deepest workstation recorded 269 daylight hours during December'. The numeric guard passed it because 269 is in the result; the meaning was invented.
Root_Cause: The generic SPARQL narration prompt gives rows with no statement of what an aggregate counts.
Fix_Approach: _count_meaning parses COUNT aggregates (and GROUP BY) from the executed query and prefixes the rows with what each alias counts and that a count is not a reading, measurement, duration or amount; the model must say the model does not hold the asked quantity.
Verification: tests in test_a_register_handover_fits_the_prompt_and_says_what_it_lacks.py (4). Live re-ask of Q51 owed.

Title: A question queued an actuation command, and another question filed a maintenance report
Description: Stakeholder run #1 as admin via /v1. Q57 'Which shutters or doors fail open versus fail locked on power loss?': LLM said metadata; routing_contract actuation_control overrode to control because _CONTROL_VERB_TARGET_RE matched 'open ... lock(ed) ... power'; ControlAgent._queue_pending_approval then fell back to writable_caps[0] and value 'as specified' and answered 'Command queued for approval (ID 11a94eda). Target: urn:bldg1:AHU-F5-SP -> ``' — one 'approve' from a sim write of an AHU setpoint. Q56 'Which drains have needed jetting more than twice this year?': classified maintenance ('a maintenance history query'), and _report_intake_node's classify_action defaults to create, so REP-452756 was written to user_reports. Any maintenance-schedule question the contract routes to maintenance does the same.
Root_Cause: Verb/keyword command detection with no notion of a question; unsafe defaults (first point, placeholder value; create).
Fix_Approach: semantic_router: is_information_question (wh-word, or auxiliary + subject); fail-open/locked/safe phrases stripped; information questions are never commands (ensure/'can you' requests still are; phrase list now also behind the question check). ControlAgent queues only for a device token that identifies a writable point (generic words ignored) AND a value, else status needs_detail listing the writable points, nothing queued. Report intake: an information question that is not a report statement is answered through the SPARQL lane and files nothing.
Verification: tests/test_a_question_is_never_an_actuation_command.py (17), test_control_execute.py (21; three fixtures corrected — they passed only via the first-point fallback), 821 routing/intake unit tests green. Live re-ask of Q56/Q57 owed. REP-452756 and approval 11a94eda left in place as evidence (the approval expires in 15 minutes).

Title: 'Is tap water free somewhere, or do I have to buy bottles?' was routed to room bookings
Description: Stakeholder run #1 Q59: LLM said capability; routing_contract event_store_query overrode to events because EVENTS_RE matched 'is <1-3 tokens> free'; classify_event_question -> availability_check; answer 'I couldn't match that room name' to an occupant asking where to get water (bldg1 holds potability triples).
Root_Cause: 'free' read only in its availability sense.
Fix_Approach: COST_SENSE_OF_FREE_RE (buy/pay/cost/charge/price/fee/for free/free to use/complimentary): when present without booking vocabulary, the contract rule does not claim the question and the events classifier returns None.
Verification: tests in test_event_times_are_local_to_people_and_utc_to_stores.py (5) + 244 events/routing tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: A grounded recommendation was discarded because its prose said 'the data you shared'
Description: Stakeholder run #1 Q67 'can you provide energy saving suggestion?': recommend lane produced recommendations; verifier grounded=True confidence=0.88 (12 sensors, 6,000 rows); the response node's meta-answer guard matched 'the data you shared' and replaced the whole answer with 'I understood the question but could not put an answer together for it'.
Root_Cause: The guard treats phrasing markers and substance markers alike and only ever suppresses.
Fix_Approach: grounding_guard.reword_handover_phrasing rewords the two phrasing-only markers ('the data you provided/shared', 'based on the data provided') and returns text only if no other marker remains; the response node applies it only when verification.grounded is True, otherwise suppresses as before.
Verification: tests/test_a_grounded_answer_is_not_discarded_for_its_phrasing.py (4) + 29 meta-answer tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: A bare 'schedule' lay term sends plant-schedule questions to the room-booking topic
Description: Re-ask of Q6 after BUG-545: 'Which systems started late or stopped late against today's approved schedule?' no longer went to approvals but hit bldg1 capability 'Bookings Reservations' via its lay term 'schedule' and returned room-booking policy prose. OperatingRegime (service windows) had no lateness vocabulary.
Root_Cause: Generic single-word lay term on a KnowledgeTopic; missing TBox vocabulary.
Fix_Approach: bldg1_capabilities.ttl: 'schedule' -> 'booking schedule', 'room schedule'. TBox OperatingRegime layTerms + plant/hvac/heating/ventilation schedule, started/stopped late, ran late/early.
Verification: TTL parses; vocabulary tests 19 green. Live re-ask owed after restart.

Title: An alert created with no value became 'threshold 0.0' and fired every cycle, filing 621 reports
Description: _alert_mgmt_node defaulted threshold to 0.0 when no number was parsed and the concept to 'sensor' when none resolved. bldg1 held seven such user rules (busyness>0, crowded>0, lift_status>0 x2, sensor>0 x3, all by the probe login admin@ontosage). Each cycle each fired and filed a '[RULE ALERT] ... > 0.0' row in user_reports: 621 between 2026-09-07 10:35 and 2026-09-15 01:41, polluting any 'recurring problems' or 'open reports' answer.
Root_Cause: Unsafe defaults on a write path (same shape as BUG-548).
Fix_Approach: The node creates an alert only when a measurement resolved (not the 'sensor' fallback) AND a threshold was parsed; otherwise it asks for the missing part. The seven existing rules were set enabled=false through the store's own encoding with their TTLs kept (reason recorded on each); the 621 reports were NOT deleted.
Verification: tests/test_an_alert_needs_a_measurement_and_a_value.py (3). Rules disabled live; takes effect at orchestrator restart (the engine caches loaded rules).

Title: 'Can my manager see when I badge in and out?' was answered 'Yes' from access-permission records
Description: Stakeholder run #1 Q58 (occupant): dialogue_agent's held-record short-circuit matched AccessPermission and skipped the LLM call AND the routing contract, whose privacy rule runs first by design; the register lane answered 'Yes – if your manager has the appropriate role they can view the badge-in/out logs', an assertion about surveillance of a person built from permission-group rows. classify_inference also did not recognise badge/access tracking phrasing ('when I badge in', 'who badged into', 'my access history').
Root_Cause: A pre-contract short-circuit with exceptions for reports and readiness but not privacy; tracking vocabulary gaps.
Fix_Approach: INDIVIDUAL_PATTERN_RE: who badged/swiped/clocked in; when [did] <subject> badge/swipe in/out; <possessive> access/door/badge [access] history/logs/records; see/view/monitor ... badge/access logs ... my/staff/person. The held-record short-circuit now also yields when classify_inference fires. Corpus: 1 of 4,060 questions newly classified (this one); entitlement and aggregate questions ('who can badge into the lab?', entrance counts) unaffected.
Verification: tests/test_tracking_a_person_by_badge_is_refused_before_any_register.py (12) + 431 privacy/routing tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: Energy recommendations saw the last five rows of one meter and were told there was no energy data
Description: Re-ask of Q67 'can you provide energy saving suggestion?' (after BUG-550 stopped its suppression): SQL fetched 6,000 rows from six floor energy meters, but _recommend_node put rows[-5:] in the prompt (all one meter), and _has_energy_data looked for 'energy' in COLUMN NAMES, which narrow rows (timestamp, uuid, value) never have, so the prompt also said the data 'contains no energy or power readings'. Answer: 'the building's data only shows values for the sensor on Floor 4 (UUID f72eafc6-…)', recommending collecting the other floors' readings.
Root_Cause: A sample chosen by row position; a presence test on schema instead of on what the series are.
Fix_Approach: services/series_summary.summarise_series: one line per series (label, count, min/mean/max with unit, span and latest in building time, night vs working-day means) plus energy detection from unit/kind/label; the recommend prompt uses it, instructs comparison across series and forbids identifiers.
Verification: tests/test_a_recommendation_sees_every_series_it_fetched.py (4) + 188 recommend/energy unit tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: 'You mentioned a sensor fault earlier - has it been fixed?' on a first turn was answered 'the earlier fault has been resolved'
Description: Stakeholder run #1 Q54 (single-turn conversation): capability short-circuit -> capability_measurand_is_data -> sensor_data on 'Air Quality Level Sensor 5.14'; narration: 'So, the earlier fault has been resolved and the sensor is functioning correctly.' — a false premise accepted and a resolution invented.
Root_Cause: Nothing checks that a reference to the assistant's earlier words has a referent.
Fix_Approach: SemanticRouter.refers_to_earlier_reply (you mentioned/said/flagged/recommended, earlier/last time you, the X you mentioned); _dialogue_node, before intent detection: with no earlier assistant message, returns a clarification saying nothing was said earlier and asking which sensor/room/fault is meant. Corpus: 2 of 4,060 match, both genuine.
Verification: tests/test_a_reference_to_an_earlier_reply_needs_one.py (10) + 347 dialogue/router tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: 'Which floor used the most energy yesterday?' got a canned 'comparison requires sensors' message
Description: Re-ask 3: compare intent, class brick:Electrical_Energy_Sensor resolved, but _floor_scoped_sparql requires a floor NUMBER, so the generic 'list floors' template ran (8 floor labels, no sensors); with no uuids the compare lane returned 'Comparing the requested sensor or zone requires sensors with linked time-series data. Floor-level energy or zone comparison works best when referencing specific zone IDs…' plus an unrelated meter-boundary note.
Root_Cause: Floor-scoped resolution only for named floors.
Fix_Approach: _ACROSS_FLOORS_RE (which/what floor, each/every/per/by floor, all/across/between floors, floor-by-floor): with a resolved metric CLASS the floor-scoped template runs across every floor (no floorNum filter, LIMIT 500 so the top floor is reached).
Verification: tests/test_a_floor_comparison_is_computed_not_narrated.py + 106 template tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: 'Where's the coolest place to work today?' was claimed by the workspace register, which records no temperature
Description: Re-ask 3: held-record short-circuit matched WorkspaceProfile ('place to work') before the routing contract; register narration said no temperature data; absence_guard corrected to a decline ('this building does have 288 temperature sensors… try narrowing').
Root_Cause: The pre-contract register short-circuit does not yield to rankings by measured conditions.
Fix_Approach: dialogue_agent: the short-circuit yields when DELIBERATE_RE matches AND _MEASURED_CONDITION_RE (thermal/air words) matches; power/Wi-Fi/noise/daylight questions stay with the register.
Verification: tests (7 new in test_tracking_a_person_by_badge_is_refused_before_any_register.py) + 462 deliberation/register tests green. Live re-ask owed — the deliberation lane's own 120-sensor budget may still decline building-wide (RUN-09).

Title: Reading narration states times in UTC ('509 ppm as of 02:20 UTC' at 03:20 BST)
Description: Re-ask 3: 'What is the CO2 level in room 5.01 right now?' answered correctly but 'as of 02:20 UTC on 15 September 2026'. sql_agent._format_results put stored UTC timestamps into the prompt unchanged; the model labelled them honestly as UTC. For a building-site audience the clock is wrong by an hour under BST (BUG-540's display rule, missed in this lane).
Root_Cause: Display conversion applied in events and recheck, not in the SQL narration.
Fix_Approach: _format_results converts datetime values and timestamp-named fields to building local time via requested_interval.to_local(building_tz), labels the header with the zone, and instructs the model to state times as given and never label them UTC.
Verification: test in test_event_times_are_local_to_people_and_utc_to_stores.py + 215 sql-agent unit tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: 'How do I get to the seminar room from reception?' was answered from the public-event register
Description: Demo pass 1: held-record short-circuit matched PublicEvent ('seminar') before the routing contract's wayfinding rule; answer 'These records do not contain any information about how to get from reception to the seminar room'. The regression probe's capability-bypass case had passed.

Fix_Approach: dialogue_agent: the held-record short-circuit also yields when WAYFIND_RE matches.
Verification: routing unit tests green; live re-ask owed.

Title: 'What is this building and who runs it?' answered with one ungrammatical line
Description: Demo pass 1: detect_facet returned the operator facet only; render produced '**Operated by** for **<building>**: <operator>'.
Root_Cause: Single-facet template not a sentence; 'what is this building' not treated as a profile request.
Fix_Approach: _WHOLE_PROFILE matches 'what is/what's this building' (not '... for/used/called'); single-facet render is '**<building>** — <label>: **<value>**.'
Verification: tests/test_building_profile.py (+2), 201 profile tests green.

Title: 'Open the windows on floor 3' suggested a command for an unrelated writable point
Description: Demo pass 1 (after BUG-548): 'Nothing has been queued… For example: set AHU-F5-SP to 21' — inviting actuation of a point the user never named.
Root_Cause: Generic needs-detail message used for a named, non-writable device.
Fix_Approach: When a device is named but matches no writable point: 'I can't control <device> — it isn't a point this building lets me write, so nothing has been queued', listing writable points with no example command.
Verification: tests/test_control_execute.py 21 green.

Title: A comfort ranking scored every floor-5 room on one air-handler series ('temperature: 0.416')
Description: Live check: 'Where's the coolest place to work on floor 5 right now?' ranked 51 rooms, all 'temperature: 0.416', score 1, source table plant_data. coverage_audit.discover_points joins sensors to spaces through ?sensor brick:isPointOf ?eq . ?eq brick:feeds ?space, so an AHU's own points (return-air temperature etc.) became each fed room's 'temperature' and, with freshness preferring whatever reported recently, won over the rooms' own sensors.
Root_Cause: No notion of HOW a point reaches a space; plant-side points admitted as room measurements.
Fix_Approach: discover_points binds ?via (direct / equipment / feeds) per UNION branch; audit() orders candidates direct → equipment → feeds and drops a feeds-path point unless its class names the zone (Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor on a VAV still counts).
Verification: tests/test_a_room_is_measured_by_its_own_sensor_not_its_air_handler.py (3) + 145 coverage tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: 'Which rooms on floor 5 are stuffy right now?' calls 571 ppm stuffy and reports one room
Description: Live check: sensor_data lane returned Room 5.16 only and narrated 571 ppm as 'moderately high, suggesting it may feel a bit stuffy', adding 'No other floor-5 rooms have recent CO2 data in the provided results'. The HBCO 'stuffiness' recipe threshold is not applied in this lane and the row sample reaching the narrator is one room's.
Root_Cause: Lay-term judgement left to narration; row sample not per room.
Fix_Approach: Kept out of the demo script. Route 'which rooms … <comfort adjective>' through deliberation (floor-scoped) or apply the concept recipe threshold deterministically.
Verification: DELIBERATE_RE gains the filter shape (which <plural space> ... are|feel <condition adjective>). LIVE 2026-09-15: "Which rooms on floor 5 are stuffy right now?" -> ARBITER list_matching over 46/46 rooms (was one room + "no other rooms have data"). Routing tests 238 green; "Is room 5.01 stuffy?" and "which rooms are booked" unchanged.

Title: A whole-register answer was suppressed 1 run in 3 by the pivot marker the BUG-546 rule makes it write
Description: Demo rehearsal (81 asks): 'How many open work orders are there, and which are overdue?' 2/3 — run 2 replaced with 'I understood the question but could not put an answer together' after meta_answer_reason matched 'What I can tell you is'. BUG-546 instructs register narration to say what the records do not hold and name what they DO record; the pivot guard reads that as a pipeline pivot.
Root_Cause: Two guards written for different lanes contradict on one.
Fix_Approach: Response node ignores meta markers when sparql_result.method == 'whole_register' (the rows are the building's records, deterministic handover).
Verification: test added; meta-answer tests green. Live re-ask owed.

Title: Single-room lookups on floors 0-4 resolved to another floor's sensor ('room 2.01' -> Room5.01)
Description: _resolve_entities_by_label split 'Room_2.01' into room/2/01 and dropped the 1-char '2'; CONTAINS(room)&&CONTAINS(01) matched Room5.01/Room0.01 and narrowing chose Room5.01_sat_co2. Answer: 'no recent CO2 readings for Room 2.01' plus a 5.01 reading.
Fix_Approach: Tokenise with \d+(\.\d+)+ kept whole; never drop digits.
Verification: tests/test_a_room_number_resolves_to_that_room.py; live re-ask owed (WB-08).

Title: Building-wide rankings declined at 234 spaces although every floor is instrumented and live
Description: MAX_FETCH_CANDIDATES=120 spaces; NOW rankings fetched 24 h x 500 rows per series. SQL lane likewise capped 200 sensors x 1,000 rows.
Fix_Approach: Row budgets: deliberation fetch_plan (NOW 3 h/90 rows; windows hours*60 up to 500; 400k rows; 800-space ceiling), SQL lane rows_per_uuid_for (now 60, else 1000; 200k rows; 600 sensors). No sample shrinking (a latest-n sample would relabel a window mean).
Verification: tests/test_breadth_budget.py (+5); live re-ask owed (WB-08).

Title: Rankings on simulated-only evidence (noise, light, occupancy) could never answer
Description: scorer evidence_mode defaulted to operational and no caller set scenario; simulated verdicts excluded every candidate.
Fix_Approach: Scenario fallback only when the operational ranking is empty on provenance; '**Simulated readings.**' note printed above the ranked list (guidance notes previously reached declines only).
Verification: tests/test_a_building_wide_ranking_answers_and_says_what_it_used.py; live re-ask owed (WB-08).

Title: '...in the building' produced a clarification about room 'None' / 'Room'
Description: The compiler emitted IN_SPACE anchors 'None' and 'Room'; admission searched spaces for them.
Fix_Approach: _WHOLE_BUILDING_ANCHORS (generic scope words) are not space anchors.
Verification: same test file; live re-ask owed (WB-08).

Title: 'Highest PM2.5' listed rooms alphabetically once utilities clamped at the band edge
Description: Equal totals broke by label.
Fix_Approach: Tie-break on the raw value of the first criterion in the direction asked, then label.
Verification: same test file; live re-ask owed (WB-08).

Title: Per-floor temperature included AHU supply/return air sensors; warmest-floor timed out at 150 s
Description: Floor-scoped template joined plant points located on floors (plant_data); analytics then generated and sandbox-ran Python over 17,160 rows (~95 s).
Fix_Approach: Template excludes plant-side Brick classes (supply/return/mixed/discharge/outside air temperature and humidity, entering/leaving water temperature); analytics narrates from series_summary per-floor figures without code generation when rows span floors.
Verification: tests/test_a_floor_comparison_is_computed_not_narrated.py (+2), test_floor_scoped_sparql.py; live re-ask owed (WB-08).

Title: Modality config re-read 287 times for one building-wide question
Description: load_modalities parses YAML on every call; unit lookup calls it per sensor.
Fix_Approach: mtime-keyed single-entry cache.
Verification: coverage/modality tests green; live re-ask owed (WB-08).

Title: UTC shown to people in readiness footer, forecast header and exports; 'Unknown Source' chip on real data
Description: Container clock UTC used for display; provenance mapped only datasource tables.
Fix_Approach: requested_interval.local_stamp(); readiness shows building_local_now; provenance falls back to database_registry nature (real -> Live Sensor Data, synthetic -> simulated), undeclared still Unknown.
Verification: tests/test_a_database_key_carries_its_declared_nature.py; test_provenance.py hermetic; live re-ask owed (WB-08).

Title: PM2.5 for floors 0-4: 210 simulated sensors (SATURATE)
Description: User asked for synthetic sensors so the whole building answers. Coverage audit showed floors 0-4 already instrumented and live for temperature/CO2/humidity/air quality (sensor_data_floors04, 522 sensors) and simulated noise/light/occupancy; PM2.5 was the only gap.
Fix_Approach: saturate_building.py --only pm25 -> input/bldg1_saturation_pm25.ttl (210 sensors, uuids, storedAt pm25_data, isSimulated); 1-week backfill 211,680 rows; generate_publisher_map.py (1,738 points); publisher recreated.
Verification: pm25_data: 210 uuids fresh within 1 h; building-wide PM2.5 ranking 234/234 instrumented live.

Title: Room-name resolution required 'room' in sensor names that say 'installed-node 2.01'
Description: Second live check: 'CO2 level in room 2.01' found only simulated Room2.01_* points (no CO2) and answered from a floor-2 server-room sensor.
Fix_Approach: With a dotted identifier present, location kind-words (room/zone/space/node/area) are not required tokens.
Verification: tests/test_a_room_number_resolves_to_that_room.py; live re-ask owed.

Title: 'Best air quality' could not rank: air_quality mixes ppm and index sensors and has no band
Description: Live: 'no scorable data on any criterion' building-wide.

Title: 'Coolest place to work in the building' ranked a male restroom first
Description: Live after row budgets.

Verification: test added; live re-ask owed.

Title: The SQL node invalidated caches for every sensor it READ; the anomaly scanner ran its detectors on the event loop
Description: 'Which floor is the warmest right now?' timed out twice: after the fetch, smart_cache.on_new_readings ran per uuid (~100 ms x 274), and the hourly anomaly sweep (2,084 series, ~5 min, also 3 min after boot) ran CPU detection on the event loop, stalling every request.
Fix_Approach: Removed the ingestion hook from the read path; scanner detection moved to asyncio.to_thread.
Verification: scanner tests 38 green; live re-measure owed. Row decoding of the sweep's fetch still runs on the loop.

Title: Deliberation windows longer than 8.3 h are read as their latest 500 rows under a 'window mean' label
Description: fetch_plan (and the pre-existing code) caps per-series rows at 500; at one-minute cadence a 24 h or 72 h window is truncated to its newest ~8.3 h. Pre-dates WB-04; now visible.
Fix_Approach: Fetch aggregated means in SQL (AVG per uuid over the window) instead of raw rows, or state the truncation.
Verification: fetch_plan reads the whole window at one-minute cadence (<=3 days) where the row budget allows; otherwise the bounded read is kept and window_coverage_note adds "**Partial window.** k of n series ... newest N readings (from about HH:MM building time)". tests/test_breadth_budget.py (+4). LIVE CHECK OWED on a "yesterday" ranking.

Title: Every floor 0-4 CO2 sensor was excluded from CO2 by a stale scale split
Description: bldg1 saturation_modalities.yaml (CAVEAT-207, 2026-08-20) excluded 'installed-node' sensors from co2 as an air-quality INDEX (0-150). Measured 2026-09-15 through the UTC-pinned connection: CO2_Level_Sensor_2.01 daily ranges 685-948 (means 790-847) every day 2026-09-06..15 — a ppm concentration. Live: 'best air quality in the building' had co2 for 73/234 rooms and ranked floor-5 rooms (~950 ppm) above floors 0-4 (~820 ppm).
Root_Cause: A data-scale decision recorded as config and never re-measured after the publisher changed.
Fix_Approach: Overlay: co2 takes both populations; co2_index (0-150 band) removed; supersession note with the measurement. Old-scale readings are still caught by the physical band (350..40000 ppm).
Verification: modality tests 242 green; live re-ask owed.

Title: A count of readings was flagged as an impossible humidity value
Description: Live: 'Which floor has the lowest humidity right now?' correct per-floor figures, prefixed with '⚠️ The recorded humidity value (1020) is outside the range…' — 1,020 was the number of readings.
Root_Cause: plausibility._is_reading looked two characters past a number, so it could not see a count noun.
Fix_Approach: 24-character lookahead; a number followed by a count noun (readings, sensors, rooms, samples, rows, …) is not a reading.

Title: Three file-graph pairs still disagree on shared subjects (shadowing sweep)
Description: After BUG-529: Brick+extensions.ttl | bldg1_expanded_protege_clean.ttl (2,675 shared, 2,114 disagree); Brick_v1.4.ttl | bldg1_expanded_protege_clean.ttl (2,671/2,113); bldg1_abacws_metadata.ttl | bldg1_zone_room_links.ttl (48/24). Root_Cause: The audit could not tell a COMPLEMENTARY split from a CONTRADICTION. Its test — the predicate single-valued in BOTH files, values differing — is a fair proxy and still flags a predicate that is multi-valued BY NATURE when each file happens to assert one value of it. Nothing in the graph settles which predicates are functional: a query for `?p a owl:FunctionalProperty` returns ZERO.
Fix_Approach: The audit now NAMES the predicates driving each count, so a reader judges in a second instead of taking a number on trust. Inventing owl:FunctionalProperty axioms to make the check exact was rejected: it would assert something about the ontology to satisfy a tool.
Verification: All three pairs are explained and none is a real conflict. Brick+extensions and Brick_v1.4 against the building's Protege export: label x2,093 (spelling variants of one name — 'Active_Energy' vs 'Active Energy', 'CO2Concentration' vs 'CO2 Concentration'), hasQuantity x196, subPropertyOf x24, deprecationMitigationMessage x16 — all TBox vocabulary, no building fact among them. bldg1_abacws_metadata against bldg1_zone_room_links: isPartOf x24, which is 'Room5.01 is part of Floor5' AND 'Room5.01 is part of Zone_5.01' — both true, because a room is part of its floor and of its zone. Description: Probe: 'Which rarely visited plant areas have the longest blind intervals?' named the two meters whose inspection INTERVAL is 365 days, neither of them due, and omitted the exhaust fan at parking level which was 369 days unseen against a 180-day interval (AEP-017, last visited 2025-09-12).
Fix_Approach: register_facts._elapsed_lines: where a register records a last-something date and an interval, the system computes days elapsed per record and how far that passes the interval, longest first, and says that a long interval still within itself is not overdue.
Verification: tests/test_a_register_answer_is_counted_not_narrated.py (+3). LIVE 2026-09-16: AEP-017 named with 369 days against its 180-day interval. Residual: the narration still lists the largest-interval asset first, which is a defensible reading of the phrase.

Title: A comparison the building cannot measure asked the stakeholder for zone IDs
Description: Stakeholder run #3 #21/#49: 'How do observed route lengths, waits and hand-offs compare with the design assumptions?' answered 'comparing observed_route_lengths ... requires sensors with linked time-series data ... give me zone IDs' — demanding a zone id about walking routes, and implying the building might measure route length if only the user named a sensor.
Root_Cause: The compare lane's no-data fallback had ONE canned message, written for a sensor-vs-sensor comparison. Every comparison that reached it was answered as though the only missing thing were a sensor identifier.
Fix_Approach: _orchestrator compare fallback rewritten: says there is no measured series for what was asked, names what the building DOES measure (from its own modalities, not a written-in list), and offers the records path for a quantity that is recorded rather than measured.
Verification: tests/test_not_every_comparison_is_a_sensor_comparison.py (6 tests, incl. a guard that the message names no building literal).

Title: A 23-column register handed all 23 columns to the narrator
Description: The continuity register hands over 23 fields per record, eight of them provenance stamps (retrievedAt, liftedByMapping, derivedFromDocument, isSimulated ...) that say where the record came from and nothing about what it says.
Root_Cause: The whole-register lane had a cell and character budget but no column budget, so width grew with the register's schema rather than with the question.
Fix_Approach: sparql_agent._project_columns: identity and status always kept, then columns whose words the question names (singular/plural equal — 'services' must keep servesService), then the rest in order, provenance last; capped at MAX_HANDOVER_COLUMNS=12. What was dropped is NAMED in the guidance so the answer can say the register holds more than it showed.
Verification: tests/test_a_register_hands_over_the_columns_asked_for.py (10 tests). LIVE 2026-09-16: the continuity question answers in 38.2s — 12 records, six verified, with the alternative location/path/capacity table. NOTE: this was first pursued as the CAUSE of the narration failure and it was NOT — see CAVEAT-619. It stands on its own as a narrower handover.

Title: The local model runner dies with a CUDA fault, and three retries all land inside its reload
Description: Register narration fell back to 'I found 12 records ... couldn't summarise them' while the provider looked healthy. Ollama's server log: 'ggml_cuda_compute_forward: ADD_ID failed / CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered', llama-server then terminating with 0xc0000409 (stack buffer overrun), ~12 times in a ten-minute burst on 2026-09-16 09:50-10:00, after which it recovered on its own.
Root_Cause: NOT ours and NOT prompt size: the crashing task was 155 tokens, and direct calls at 14k/47k/117k/211k/351k chars (with the same num_ctx=16384 and keep_alive) all succeeded, as did concurrent pairs. ADD_ID is the MoE expert-routing kernel gpt-oss uses; this is a llama.cpp/CUDA-level fault on this GPU. OUR half of it: after the crash Ollama respawns llama-server on a new port taking 5.0-14.0s, while the retry backoff was 1s then 2s — so all three attempts hit a refused port and a correct answer degraded to a fallback.
Fix_Approach: llm_manager._looks_like_a_dead_local_runner + LLM_RUNNER_RESTART_WAIT_S (default 10s, env-driven): a refused loopback port is read as a dead runner and waited out rather than raced. A merely slow or busy provider keeps the short backoff. The underlying CUDA fault is not fixable from here; if it recurs on demo day the mitigation is to restart Ollama.
Verification: tests/test_a_crashed_runner_is_waited_out.py (10 tests). Evidence: %LOCALAPPDATA%/Ollama/server.log lines 407692-411286. LIVE 2026-09-16: the question that failed all night now answers in 38.2s.

Title: The building recorded no service continuity position
Description: Stakeholder run #3 #16 asked which services have a verified alternative if the server room is unavailable, and was answered with 21 lab spaces — true as a list of rooms and read as a list of options, which is the most dangerous shape of wrong answer a continuity question can get.
Root_Cause: The building modelled rooms and equipment. Nothing recorded which service depends on which space, whether an alternative exists, or whether anyone had proved it.
Fix_Approach: ontosage:ContinuityProvision in the shared schema + ontology/record_documents/continuity_provision.yaml + input/documents/continuity_provision_register.md (12 records, placeholder data treated as the building's own). Verified, unverified, overdue and none are four different recorded states; 'none identified' is a row, not an omission.
Verification: LIVE 2026-09-16: 12 records, six verified, named with their alternative location, path and capacity. Lay-term collision on 'recovery time' with WorkspaceProfile found and removed by the conformance guard.

Title: A focused-work question matched none of the workspace register's lay terms
Description: 'Which spaces are suitable for quiet focused work for a group of four?' (run #3 #21) routed to sensor_data and returned nothing, from a building holding a 28-record workspace register with a noise profile and a seat count per space.
Root_Cause: The register declared 'quiet study', 'quiet space' and 'space for', all of which need adjacency the sentence does not have. It knew no term for focused work at all, and lay terms are matched as whole phrases by design.
Fix_Approach: WorkspaceProfile layTerms extended with 18 multi-word phrases: focused/focussed/deep work, work quietly, somewhere to concentrate, group work, for a group of, suitable for work/study. Multi-word deliberately — a bare 'quiet' or 'group' would claim any question mentioning either.
Verification: Conformance suite green (66 tests, no lay-term collision). LIVE 2026-09-16: 16 spaces named with noise profile, group-friendliness and seat count, by floor.

Title: The column cap made the system deny data the building holds
Description: With MAX_HANDOVER_COLUMNS=12, the workspace question was answered 'The records do not contain any field that records whether a space is quiet or suitable for focused work' — while the register records noiseProfile, quietestPeriod and seatCount for all 28 spaces. The projection had dropped exactly those three.
Root_Cause: Two faults in the cap added hours earlier (BUG-618). (1) It was set at 12 to fix a narration failure that turned out to be a CUDA crash (CAVEAT-619), so the cost was real and the benefit imaginary. (2) Column relevance was whole-word overlap, which cannot match 'quiet' to `quietestPeriod`. Worse, `_primary_rows` was taken AFTER the projection, so the facts counted in code — completeness, passed-due — were computed from rows the system had just discarded, and stated with authority.
Fix_Approach: Cap raised to 24 (no content column is dropped in any register here); provenance stamps always leave the narration since they say nothing about content; relevance matched on stems and prefixes; and the counted facts are taken from the FULL rows before any projection.
Verification: tests/test_a_register_hands_over_the_columns_asked_for.py — 12 tests, including 'a content column is never dropped while a provenance stamp survives' and 'the real registers lose no content at all'. LIVE 2026-09-16: 16 quiet group-friendly spaces named; the continuity register still answers (38.2s).

Title: A new lay term stole the deliberation lane's two probe cases
Description: Adding 'focused work' to the workspace register (BUG-621) made it claim 'Which space has the best conditions for focused work this afternoon?' and the Floor 3 variant. Both had answered with ARBITER's scored best match; both dropped to a list of what spaces are like. Probe 59/60 -> 58/60.
Root_Cause: The term names a WAY OF WORKING, not a kind of record. A live reading describes 'focused work this afternoon' at least as well as a register does, so the term matched a question the register cannot answer.
Fix_Approach: focused/focussed/focus/deep work and 'quiet focused work' removed; the space-shaped phrases that made BUG-621's question work ('for a group of', 'suitable for work', 'somewhere to concentrate') stay.
Verification: tests/test_a_lay_term_does_not_steal_the_deliberation_lane.py (8 tests): the two deliberation questions must NOT resolve to the register, the register question must, and each removed term is named so re-adding it fails. Terms are read from the schema, not copied. LIVE 2026-09-16: 'best conditions ... this afternoon' -> Best match Room 5.13, score 0.6676; 'quiet focused work for a group of four' -> 16 spaces by floor.

Title: A same-floor route was counted as a floor pair where step-free is slower
Description: 'On which floor pairs is the step-free route slower than the stair route?' answered '15 of the 21 records'. Six of those fifteen are same-floor routes (Level 0 to Level 0), which have no stair route to be slower than. The same register answered 'nine' the day before, from the same 21 rows.
Root_Cause: The comparison was left to the narration. register_facts counted records and statuses and said nothing about the comparison the question asked for, so the answer depended on whichever way the model read 'floor pair' that run — the failure BUG-581 exists to prevent, in a register it had not yet reached.
Fix_Approach: register_facts._comparison_lines: where a question carries a comparative ('slower/faster than'), the register holds exactly two numeric measures, and the question names one of them, the count is computed in code. Endpoint columns are found by their VALUES (two columns drawn from the same repeated vocabulary), rows with identical endpoints are excluded as not being a pair, and the exclusion is stated rather than hidden.
Verification: tests/test_a_comparison_between_two_columns_is_counted.py (11 tests, including the register's REAL shape: floors recorded as bare numbers, which the first endpoint finder excluded as 'not a place' and so found nothing live while passing every test). LIVE 2026-09-16: 'nine floor-pairs', listed correctly, in 32.3s (was 102.9s).

Title: Six gases were measured on one floor only, and the user could not tell
Description: Measured from the graph's own topology (sensor -> space -> floor, not parsed out of sensor names): CO, NO2, PM1, PM10, formaldehyde and TVOC existed ONLY on the floor carrying the real instrumentation snapshot. 'What is the NO2 on floor 2?' answered honestly that nothing was measured while the same question about floor 5 answered with a figure — an asymmetry a stakeholder cannot see or predict.
Root_Cause: The existing coverage audit derives a sensor's floor from its URI text, so ~4,000 sensors landed in 'F?' and no gap list could be trusted. The gaps were real and invisible.
Fix_Approach: Six modalities added to config/saturation_modalities.yaml with scope: floor, then scripts/saturate_building.py --only + backfill_saturation.py. Config-driven and building-agnostic: no code change, no building literal. Units and bands match each measurand's declared physicalUnit (BUG-609). scope: floor deliberately — per room these six would add ~1,400 points and slow every query, and one node per floor is how a multi-gas IAQ unit is actually deployed.
Verification: 36 points, 181,440 readings over 5 weeks. Coverage matrix: all six now on every occupied floor. LIVE 2026-09-16: 'average TVOC on floor 3 today' -> 181.86 ppb, honest that it is a single sensor. NOTE: for a readonly role the k-anonymity floor (14 sensors / 7 spaces) still refuses a one-sensor floor aggregate — that is the policy behaving as authored, not a defect.

Title: A carbon monoxide reading was answered from the sustainability target register
Description: 'What is the carbon monoxide level on floor 1?' was answered with Scope 1 and 2 emissions baselines and percentage reduction targets.
Root_Cause: The register declared the bare lay term 'carbon', which matches carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide — two gases the building MEASURES, with sensors and readings. The word they share is the first half of two different nouns.
Fix_Approach: Bare 'carbon' removed; 'carbon emissions', 'carbon footprint', 'carbon reduction' and 'carbon neutral' added so the register keeps the questions it does own.
Verification: tests/test_a_measured_gas_is_not_a_sustainability_target.py (10 tests): four gas questions must NOT reach the register, four target questions must, and the bare term is named so re-adding it fails. Terms read from the schema, not copied.

Title: A question about how something changed was answered from a single mean
Description: 'How has the temperature on floor 3 changed over the last week?' answered 'No change data available for floor 3 over the last week' — from a week of readings that had been fetched, clamped by policy and handed over. 'Compare this week's electricity use with last week' likewise reported per-floor latest values and never compared the two weeks.
Root_Cause: The only deterministic summary was per FLOOR (series_summary.summarise_groups, WB-14): one mean per floor across the whole window, which cannot show a change within it. The narrator was then asked a temporal question about non-temporal figures and correctly said it could not answer.
Fix_Approach: series_summary.summarise_periods + asks_how_it_changed: the same rows bucketed by hour/day/week (bucket chosen from the period the question names, else the span), with the change across the window, the highest and lowest period, and energy SUMMED rather than averaged. Counting stays in code (BUG-581).
Verification: tests/test_a_question_about_time_gets_a_shape_over_time.py (24 tests). LIVE 2026-09-16: floor 3 temperature 'decreased by 0.5 degC from 23.3 on 09-09 to 22.8 on 09-16' with daily means; electricity 'increased by 1,181 kWh (+55.0%) from week 36 to week 37'.

Title: A partial day was compared with a partial day and reported as +291.7%
Description: The first per-period answer for 'compare this week with last week' read 'electricity use increased by 639 kWh (+291.7%) from the first day to the last day'. The first day began mid-evening and the last day was today, still running: both hold a fraction of a day's readings.
Root_Cause: A window almost always starts mid-bucket and ends now, so its edge buckets are partial. Comparing them states a change in the MEASUREMENT WINDOW as though it were a change in the building.
Fix_Approach: _complete_buckets drops an edge bucket holding materially fewer readings than the median bucket; the change is measured between whole periods and the excluded ones are NAMED, with an instruction not to present a partial period as a whole one. Separately, a question naming weeks is now bucketed by week rather than by day.
Verification: 4 further tests in the same file. LIVE 2026-09-16: '+55.0% from week 36 to week 37 ... Week 38, with only 288 readings, is not comparable to a full week and is excluded from this comparison'.

Title: The building said it keeps no record of how many rooms a floor has
Description: 'How many rooms are on floor 2?' answered 'the building model doesn't keep a record of how many rooms are on a specific floor' — seconds after 'What is the total area of floor 4?' answered '1,149.0 m2, 57 rooms' from the same manifests.
Root_Cause: The classifier called it sensor_data. `countable_metadata` correctly DECLINED it (a room count is geometry, not a SPARQL census) but declining only leaves the classifier's answer in place. Declining to force the wrong lane is not the same as naming the right one.
Fix_Approach: New parse-stage rule `room_count_is_spatial`, placed directly after countable_metadata: a COUNT whose subject is a room or space goes to spatial_query; a device count stays a graph census (BUG-045); a room superlative keeps the deliberation lane (BUG-163). test_precedence_order_is_pinned updated in the same change.
Verification: tests/test_a_room_count_is_a_geometry_question.py (12 tests) + the 175-test contract suite green. LIVE 2026-09-16: 'Floor 2 — 71 rooms'.

Title: A whole-building comfort question refuses instead of ranking
Description: 'Is it stuffy anywhere in the building?' reaches 274 sensors and returns the row-budget refusal, which explains itself and offers narrowing ('one floor, or one room'). 'Which room is the warmest right now?' answers the same shape of question by ranking, because it reaches the deliberation lane.
Root_Cause: The question classifies as `capability`, which is not in _SUPERLATIVE_TAKEOVER_INTENTS, and DELIBERATE_RE does not match the 'is it X anywhere' shape — it requires a superlative or an explicit should-I form.
Fix_Approach: Three changes, because the question failed three times over. (1) Parse-stage rule `existential_comfort_is_deliberate`: a CONDITION word plus an EXISTENTIAL scope ('is it stuffy anywhere') is a ranking question, claimed whichever lane the classifier guessed. (2) The same guard inside the concept-stage capability_measurand_is_data, because the capability intent is assigned AFTER the parse stage runs. (3) compiler._is_whole_building_scope: 'anywhere in the building' is the ABSENCE of a spatial anchor, not a term the compiler failed to map — recorded as unmapped it made the query unexecutable and asked the user to drop the only word that said 'look everywhere'. It also replaces a local pattern anchored on '^anywhere$', which matched the bare word only, so one decision now has one owner.
Verification: tests/test_asking_without_knowing_the_building.py (22 tests) + the contract suite (188 green, precedence pinned). LIVE 2026-09-16, all first-pass: 'Is it stuffy anywhere in the building?' -> Room 5.59 at 1113.8 ppm CO2, ranked, with the stated assumption 'stuffy scored as above co2 against the 420-1500 band'; 'Is there anywhere quiet I can work?' -> Room 0.18, noise 57.19 dB, minimised; 'Is it too warm anywhere right now?' -> Room 5.26 at 25.04 degC.

Title: The compliance lane answered 'No question was provided.'
Description: 'Is it too warm anywhere right now?' was classified `compliance` and came back, after 116 seconds, with 'No question was provided.' followed by follow-up suggestions and a source list. The sentence is the MODEL's: it was handed a prompt with no question in it and said so.
Root_Cause: NOT REPRODUCED, and the reason it cannot be is itself the finding: every lane logs the query it RECEIVED, never the prompt it RENDERED, so a prompt that lost its question between the two leaves no trace. Seven builders interpolate a question into a prompt; any of them dropping it produces this answer. Ordinary compliance questions do NOT reproduce it — 'Are we compliant with CO2 limits on floor 5?' and 'Is room 5.01 compliant with the temperature standard?' both answer correctly with named standards — so it needs the shape that question had (an unresolvable scope).
Fix_Approach: A detector at the ONE place every prompt passes through (llm_manager.generate): a question label with nothing after it is logged as a warning naming the calling frame. It only warns — a caller with a genuine reason to prompt without a question keeps working — so the next occurrence identifies its own builder instead of being unreproducible after the fact. Separately, TODO-629's routing now takes comfort questions out of the compliance lane, so the shape that triggered it no longer goes there.
Verification: 4 tests in tests/test_a_crashed_runner_is_waited_out.py: three empty-slot shapes flagged, three populated ones ignored, the check is called from generate(), and it warns rather than raises. The underlying defect stays OPEN in substance — this makes it findable, not fixed.

Title: Every floor-scoped query was rejected as malformed, and the fallback answered about a different floor
Description: 'What is the air quality on floor 3?' was answered from sensors labelled 5.02 and 5.03 — the right class, the wrong floor, with a confident figure. GraphDB was rejecting the floor-scoped template outright: MALFORMED QUERY: Multiple prefix declarations for prefix 'ref'. Nothing surfaced that; the agent fell back, and the fallback (_get_instances_for_class) takes the first 40 instances of the class with NO spatial constraint — which on this building are the densely instrumented floor's.
Root_Cause: _floor_scoped_sparql appended 'PREFIX ref:' with a comment saying it was absent from the standard prefix block. It had since been added to that block. The code remembered what the block used to declare instead of asking it.
Fix_Approach: Declare ref: only when the block does not already: `if 'PREFIX ref:' not in _prefixes`. The fallback's willingness to substitute an unconstrained instance list is what turned a failed query into a wrong answer, and is logged separately.
Verification: tests/test_the_floor_scoped_query_is_valid_sparql.py (17 tests). Executed against the live store: air quality floor 3 -> 100 rows all floorNum=3; CO2 floor 1 -> 14 rows all floorNum=1; temperature floors 1 and 5 -> 100 rows, floorNum in (1,5). LIVE 2026-09-16: 'average CO2 on floor 1' -> 801.5 ppm from sensors 1.38-1.40; 'humidity on floor 2' -> all 2.xx sensors. WORTH KNOWING: rdflib's parser ACCEPTS a duplicated prefix and GraphDB does not, so a parse check alone would never have caught this — the duplicate-prefix test is the one with teeth.

Title: A composite concept collapses to one class, and its floor rows do not reach the data lane
Description: After BUG-631, 'What is the air quality on floor 3?' resolves and the SPARQL returns 100 floor-3 rows — and the analytics lane still receives 68 floor-5 sensors, answering 'No air quality data available for floor 3. The dataset supplied contains ... sensors on floor 5.' Honest now, and still not the answer. Separately, hbco:iaq_composite maps 'air quality' to CO2_Level_Sensor, PM2.5_Level_Sensor, TVOC_Sensor AND Air_Quality_Sensor, but _most_specific_class picks ONE — so the answer reports an opaque 'level' instead of the pollutants a person means.
Root_Cause: The modality REPAIR replaced the result. Measured: '[modality_repair] want=air_quality rows=107 miss=True' then 'no air_quality sensors from retrieval (107 rows); replaced with 400 from the graph'. Two faults in one line. (1) The miss was false: the catalogue defines air_quality as Air_Quality_Sensor alone while the HBCO composite defines it as CO2 + PM2.5 + TVOC + that, so 107 genuine air-quality rows read as a total miss — one concept with two incompatible definitions. (2) build_modality_query is building-wide BY CONSTRUCTION, so the replacement silently dropped the floor the question named.
Fix_Approach: build_modality_query takes `floors` and applies the same sensor->space->floor pattern the floor-scoped template uses; the caller passes the floors the question named. needs_repair/results_match_modality take `extra_classes` — what the concept resolver actually resolved to — with a lower token threshold for those only, because being generous about a deliberate resolution can prevent a wrongful replacement but never cause one. A repair may widen the CLASS it looks for, never the PLACE it looks in.
Verification: tests/test_a_repair_keeps_the_question_scope.py (9 tests, including that the scoped repair is valid SPARQL and that an unrelated modality still triggers a repair). Live 2026-09-16: 'What is the air quality on floor 3?' -> 'PM2.5 Level Sensor — Floor 3: 18.00 ug/m3'. The scoped repair returns 107 floor-3 rows where the unscoped one returned 400 building-wide.

Title: Every floor now carries every quantity a floor can carry
Description: Measured by QUANTITY KIND rather than Brick class, which is what a person asks about: 7 of 25 kinds were absent from some floors. Multi-gas detection and colour temperature existed on one floor; power was metered for the building while energy was metered per floor; occupancy status covered four floors of six.
Root_Cause: Coverage had only ever been measured per Brick class, where equipment-scoped points (vibration, run time, damper position) look like floor gaps and hide the real ones.
Fix_Approach: config/saturation_modalities.yaml: `gas` added; `electric_power` and `water_level` moved from building scope to floor; `water_flow_rate` added for flow rate alongside the meter that records volume. Provisioned via saturate_building.py (510 points) and backfilled two weeks (1,028,160 rows). Config, not code: no building literal, no new adapter.
Verification: 20 of 25 quantity kinds are now on ALL six floors. The five that are not are correctly place-specific and were deliberately NOT filled: rainfall, soil moisture and solar irradiance are rooftop; water temperature is plant flow and return; vibration is equipment. A rainfall sensor on floor 2 would be a fabrication, which is the failure design contract #4 forbids.

Title: A point the graph declared was never fed, so it answered as a dead sensor
Description: 498 points were provisioned, uploaded and answered 'no recent reading'. The graph knew them; the publisher did not. To a stakeholder a point that never reports is indistinguishable from a broken sensor, and nothing in the answer said otherwise.
Root_Cause: The publisher reads a map of points to feed, and that map was a script somebody had to remember to run. Adding sensors was three steps with the third outside the system.
Fix_Approach: orchestrator/services/publisher_map.py + a call in the boot sequence: whenever the TTL uploader actually ingests something, the map is rebuilt from the graph and written atomically. The derivation stays in scripts/generate_publisher_map.py so one decision has one owner. `docker compose up -d` is now genuinely all you need, for this building and the next.
Verification: tests/test_a_provisioned_point_is_fed.py (6 tests). LIVE 2026-09-16: boot logged 'uploaded=2' then '[publisher_map] 2844 point(s) across 18 table(s) — 12 new'. Measured in MySQL with the session pinned to UTC: every narrow table has sensors reporting within the last 10 minutes (equipment_data 250, occupancy_data 514, iaq_data 53, waterflow 20, submeter 16).

Title: Carbon monoxide was published at 204 ppm because it shared a column with TVOC
Description: 'What is the carbon monoxide level on floor 2?' answered 204.00 ppm. The building declares CO's ordinary range as 0-5 ppm; 200 ppm is a level a person evacuates a building over. Every gas in this building writes to `iaq_data.voc`, and the publisher picks its value range by COLUMN NAME.
Root_Cause: A narrow table holds one value column for a whole family of quantities, so the column cannot identify the quantity — the uuid does. Ranges keyed by column gave carbon monoxide the range for volatile organic compounds.
Fix_Approach: The publish map now carries each point's own ordinary band, read from the ontology's typicalMin/typicalMax/typicalDecimals per measurand, and the publisher prefers it over the column default. A class that declares no measurand keeps the column default rather than being guessed at. 2,587 of 2,844 points carry a declared band.
Verification: LIVE 2026-09-16: CO band 0.0-5.0 and latest reading 2.6 ppm; NO2 band 5-40 and 25.0; TVOC band 0-500 and 267. 13,818 rows published during the mis-ranged window were deleted (value beyond its declared band, written after 16:00 UTC) so no average carries them. The question now answers '2.60 ppm'.

Title: 'Carbon monoxide' resolved to an electrical energy sensor
Description: 'What is the carbon monoxide level on floor 2?' matched the HBCO concept `carbon_footprint`, which maps to brick:Electrical_Energy_Sensor, and returned nothing. A gas measured on all six floors could not be asked about by name.
Root_Cause: `carbon_footprint` declared the bare lay term 'carbon'. Exactly the collision BUG-625 fixed in the record registers, one layer down in the concept resolver — the word is the first half of two different nouns.
Fix_Approach: Bare 'carbon' replaced with 'carbon emissions' and 'carbon output', and six gas concepts added to ontology/hbco_mappings.ttl (carbon monoxide, nitrogen dioxide, formaldehyde, PM10, PM1, combustible gas), each mapping to the Brick class that records it.
Verification: LIVE 2026-09-16: 'carbon monoxide level on floor 2' -> 2.60 ppm from the Floor 2 sensor; 'NO2 level on floor 4' -> 206 ppb (pre-cleanup) then within band, from Floor 4's own point.

Title: Answers no longer caption the building's own data as synthetic
Description: User decision 2026-09-16: every reading in this deployment is placeholder data standing in for the building's own feed and is replaced wholesale when the real source is connected. Captions like ' · simulated', 'declared synthetic' and the '_**Synthetic demonstration record**_' banner on 38 registers therefore described the deployment STAGE, and reached stakeholders as statements about the building.
Root_Cause: The provenance machinery labelled at render time rather than only recording. 1,610 point labels also carried '(simulated)' and a label is quoted verbatim in answers.
Fix_Approach: Captions removed from the provenance chip, the evidence record, the asset-state lane and the locked-capability message; '(simulated)' stripped from 1,610 labels and from the generator that writes them; the banner removed from 38 record documents and from generate_record_documents.py. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the `isSimulated` triples, the `simulated:` front matter and the `synthetic` flag on a provenance tag all stay, so the declaration is still where an auditor reads it; and the system still never invents a figure, still names each source, and still reports an absence as an absence.
Verification: tests/test_no_answer_calls_the_data_fake.py (12 tests) — each retired caption named individually so re-adding one fails, no point label carries the marker, no record document opens with a disclaimer, AND the front-matter declaration is asserted to still be there. Three existing tests updated to the new contract rather than deleted.

Title: The publisher overwrote a correlated plant series and collapsed the delta-T
Description: After every narrow point was handed to the publisher, the heating circuit's delta-T fell from 11.08 degC to 0.12 degC: 'Heat Pump 1 Leaving 22.62 degC - Entering 22.50 degC'. The boiler flow, which runs at about 69 degC, was being published at 22.5.
Root_Cause: Two faults. (1) BAND INHERITANCE: a boiler flow is typed both Temperature_Sensor and Leaving_Water_Temperature_Sensor, and the band attachment took whichever class came back -- the shallow one carries the AIR range 18-28 because that describes a room. This is BUG-609's mistake in a new place. ontosage:WaterTemperature declares a PHYSICAL band and no typical band, so no specific range exists to prefer. (2) CORRELATION: flow and return are generated from ONE seed so their difference is a real delta-T; a per-point publisher draws each independently and the difference becomes noise with a plausible shape.
Fix_Approach: The band query now ranks declaring classes by hierarchy depth and takes the deepest (COUNT(DISTINCT ?anc) / DESC(?depth)), the same rule physical_bands.py uses. Tables whose series are correlated (plant_data) are left out of the publish map entirely and keep the history their own generator wrote. 4,648 rows written by the per-point publisher were deleted and the plant points re-provisioned with 51,072 correlated rows.
Verification: 3 tests in tests/test_a_provisioned_point_is_fed.py. LIVE 2026-09-16: 'What's the delta-T across the heating circuit?' -> 11.08 degC at Heat Pump 1, Boiler 2 9.73 — the same figures the question gave this morning before the publisher touched the series. RESIDUAL: ontosage:WaterTemperature still has no typicalMin/Max, so any water point that IS published would fall back to the air band; logged here rather than guessed at.

Title: A register's own date was stripped as a lifter stamp, so 'when' questions had no answer
Description: 'When was the last project handover, and what was handed over?' answered 'The records do not contain dates for handovers, so I cannot tell when the last handover occurred' — from a register whose every row carries an `issued` date (2024-09-30, 2026-05-03 ...).
Root_Cause: The handover mapping sends `issued` to ontosage:effectiveFrom, and TWO consumers treat effectiveFrom as a lifter stamp and strip it before the narration: register_facts._PROVENANCE_FIELDS and sparql_agent._PROVENANCE_COLUMNS. TEN mappings use it for a real column — permits, bookings, competency, condition surveys, contracts, incidents, public events, risk assessments, handovers — so every 'when' question about those registers was answered from a column the system had just hidden from itself.
Fix_Approach: Judge it by its VALUES, not its name. record_documents.py already makes the distinction at lift time — it stamps effectiveFrom from the front matter ONLY when the row has no mapped column of its own — so a column whose value is identical on every record is a stamp and one that varies is that record's own fact. register_facts.provenance_fields(rows) computes the stamp set per call and the projection uses the same rule.
Verification: 2 tests in tests/test_a_register_hands_over_the_columns_asked_for.py: a varying date is kept while retrievedAt is still dropped, and one date repeated on every record is still a stamp. LIVE 2026-09-16: 'The most recent handover recorded ... was on 3 May 2026 ... thorough examination record for Passenger lift 1', 9 records, 6 held, 3 outstanding.

Title: A superlative could not be compiled, so the extreme form of a question failed
Description: Found in the demo-script rehearsal: 'Which rooms in the building are the stuffiest right now?' reached the ranking lane and then failed to compile — 'I couldn't map part of your request (stuffiest)' — while the same question with 'stuffy' compiled cleanly to co2. After that, the same question failed again on 'rooms in the building'.
Root_Cause: Two layers of vocabulary, each complete only in the plain case. (1) The compiler's lay-term hints list 'stuffy, fresh air, ventilation' and no inflection, so the compile step emitted 'stuffiest' as a modality name and the closed-vocabulary check rejected it. People ask for the EXTREME far more often than the plain adjective. (2) The whole-building scope test knew 'anywhere' and 'all rooms' but not a bare plural space noun, so 'rooms in the building' was recorded as a place it could not resolve.
Fix_Approach: The reduction belongs in code, not in a longer list: _base_form() reduces -iest/-ier/-est/-er to the form the table lists, and _modality_from_lay_term() maps the result — but ONLY when it names a modality this building actually has, so translating is not guessing. A bare PLURAL space noun now counts as whole-building scope; the singular deliberately does not, because 'room 5.01' and 'the room' do name somewhere.
Verification: tests/test_the_extreme_is_how_people_ask.py (20 tests): thirteen inflections resolve, five non-lay words resolve to nothing, the stem must survive with two letters ('driest' -> 'dry', which an earlier bound dropped), and the fallback is asserted to check the building's own modality set. LIVE 2026-09-16: 'Which rooms in the building are the stuffiest right now?' -> Room 4.02 at 800.6 ppm, ranked, 'stuffiest scored as maximize co2 against the 420-1500 band'.
