Title: Room temperatures of up to 526 degC sat in the store
Description: Surfaced by the demo rehearsal: a tap-water question carried the warning 'The recorded temperature value (259, 281, 292) is outside the range this quantity can take in degC or degF, so it is most likely raw or unscaled sensor output.' temperature_data held 3,468 rows between 70 and 526 degC across 12 sensors, and water_data held 48 rows above the water band.
Root_Cause: Pre-existing generated history, not today's provisioning. The physical-band guard (BUG-609) was doing its job — it refused to interpret them — but the warning rides along on otherwise good answers, and any question that lists raw values shows them.
Fix_Approach: Deleted on the PHYSICAL bound, not the typical one: air outside -30..70 degC and water outside -10..120 degC cannot be readings of the quantity the point declares. Values merely ABOVE the ordinary range were left alone — 9-20% of several tables sit there and that is legitimate variation; deleting it would flatten the data into something no building produces.
Verification: 3,468 air rows and 48 water rows removed. temperature_data now spans 18.0 to 26.0 degC. The guard that caught it is untouched, so a future impossible value is still refused rather than reported.

Title: A question word that is also a status reported the status count as the total, about one run in three
Description: Probe 2026-09-16: 'Which teaching sessions are scheduled in Room 1.06?' answered 'There are 6 scheduled sessions recorded for this room' from a room holding 23 — the same question that answered '23 in the room: 17 completed, 6 still scheduled' the night before. The counted facts were RIGHT both times ('Records held: 23. By recorded status: completed 17, scheduled 6') and only the narration changed.
Root_Cause: CAVEAT-604's instruction DESCRIBED the shape the answer should take — 'answer with the total and give the split' — and left the wording to the model. A described shape is followed some of the time; this one held overnight and failed on the next probe. Both readings of 'scheduled' are defensible, which is precisely why the answer cannot be left to pick one.
Fix_Approach: The instruction now WRITES THE SENTENCE, filled in from the counts the system already computed: 'OPEN with this sentence: "The room holds 23 records in total — completed 17, scheduled 6." Only then list whichever subset the question meant.' Same facts, no new computation — the difference is that the wording is no longer the model's to choose.
Verification: tests/test_a_register_answer_is_counted_not_narrated.py updated to the new wording. LIVE 2026-09-17, asked THREE times because this is a variance defect and one pass proves nothing: all three opened 'The room holds 23 records in total — completed 17, scheduled 6', with the six IDs.

Title: The one lane whose output is ungrounded LLM prose was the only lane with no grounding check
Description: SPARQLAgent.answer_semantically returns results as a LIST -- [{'answer': ...}], annotated in its own source as 'Mock results for compatibility'. Both of the verifier's SPARQL readers dug result['results']['results']['bindings'] behind an isinstance guard on the OUTER value only. The outer value IS a dict so the guard passed, and the second .get then ran against the list and raised AttributeError. _extract_sensor_ids (verifier_agent.py:189 at the call site) raised FIRST, before _sparql_returned_data, so both needed fixing. The exception escaped VerifierAgent.verify() into a caller that logged it at DEBUG, so the turn attached NO verification record at all -- and publication_gate, which fails open by design, reads a missing record as 'the check did not run' and publishes.
Root_Cause: Two components each correct on their own terms and never reconciled. The RAG fallback deliberately fakes the SPARQL envelope for 'compatibility' with readers it never enumerated; the verifier type-hints its parameter Dict[str, Any] and trusted the hint two levels down. Nothing in between asserts the shape. The DEBUG log is what made it survive: the same file logs the evidence-record failure at WARNING with a traceback, for exactly this reason, twelve lines earlier.
Fix_Approach: One shape-reader, verifier_agent._bindings(), that returns [] for anything that is not the SPARQL protocol envelope, used by both readers. Returning [] is not a workaround: a RAG answer genuinely HAS no bindings, so the honest record is grounded=False / source=none, which is what the verifier now attaches. The orchestrator's swallow is raised from DEBUG to WARNING with exc_info, so a verifier crash can never again silently remove a gate.
Verification: tests/test_the_rag_fallback_is_verified_like_every_other_lane.py -- 21 tests, 39 passed together with the pre-existing gate suite, 0 failed. They pin all four directions, and the fourth matters most: a test reads the source of answer_semantically and fails if it stops returning a list, because otherwise a later tidy-up would leave the guard passing while guarding nothing real. Negative cases outnumber positive ones deliberately -- a real SPARQL result must still be recognised as grounded, an empty-but-well-formed one as ungrounded rather than crashed. BLAST RADIUS is narrower than it first looks and was measured, not assumed: publication_gate only acts on GATED_INTENTS {analytics, report, compare, trend} AND only when the text carries a quantitative claim, so most RAG answers (metadata, discovery, general) were never gated anyway. The affected case is the dangerous one: LLM prose asserting a figure for an analytics or compare question. LIVE RE-ASK STILL OWED.

Title: An unscoped 'scope: all' rule can watch three points while claiming a whole class
Description: rules_engine._uuids_for_class carries LIMIT 10 (CLASS_CANDIDATES) and no DISTINCT, while a bldg1 humidity point satisfies 'a/rdfs:subClassOf*' by roughly three paths (Zone_Air_Humidity_Sensor, Humidity_Sensor, Relative_Humidity_Sensor). So ten rows can be as few as three distinct points, and a rule declaring scope: all over a class of tens of points is in fact watching about three of them -- while its coverage line says 'all'. Found by the TODO-528 agent while adding spatial scoping; it deliberately did not fix it.
Root_Cause: The candidate limit predates scope: all. It was a sane cap when a rule watched one arbitrary reporting point (the pre-V12-20 behaviour BUG-482 logged); it became a silent truncation the moment 'all' was offered as a promise.
Fix_Approach: Add DISTINCT and raise or remove the cap for scope: all specifically -- but this CHANGES WHAT EXISTING UNSCOPED RULES WATCH, so it needs the live rule set checked first and is not a demo-week change. The newly added coverage reporting (engine.coverage_report) is the instrument: run it and see which shipped rules are truncated before touching the limit.
Verification: Not yet measured against the live rule set. The scoped path added by TODO-528 uses SELECT DISTINCT and a 200-point limit and is not affected; this row is about the unscoped path only.

Title: User-tier alerts bypass both rule-loader guards, so a user alert still watches one arbitrary point
Description: load_user_rules() reads alerts from Redis and never calls _scope_is_declared or _place_is_meaningful, the two guards the YAML loader applies. A user alert carrying a concept and no scope therefore loads and watches a single arbitrary reporting point -- precisely the pre-V12-20 behaviour that BUG-482 was raised about -- while file-declared rules are now required to say what they cover.
Root_Cause: The two loaders grew separately. The guards were added to the YAML path because that is where the shipped rules live; nothing walked the second entry point.
Fix_Approach: NEEDS A DECISION, NOT A PATCH. Applying the guards retroactively would silently DISABLE alerts already sitting in Redis that users believe are armed, which is worse than the defect. Options: default user alerts to scope: first_reporting explicitly and say so in the alert's own confirmation text; or migrate existing Redis alerts on read and warn. Ask the user before choosing.
Verification: Found by inspection during TODO-528, not by a failing alert. Count of live Redis user alerts not yet measured.

Title: Scoped rules make the 60-second polling loop do real work where it previously did almost none
Description: scope: all re-reads every covered point from its store on every 60 s poll. Floor-scoped that is tens of reads per rule per cycle; the previous unscoped, truncated behaviour was at most ten. Bounded at SCOPE_POINT_LIMIT=200 worst case.
Root_Cause: Not a defect -- the direct and intended cost of a rule actually covering what it claims. Logged so it is not rediscovered as a mystery load.
Fix_Approach: Watch it against CAVEAT-500 (latency variance concentrated in heavy lanes under load) and CAVEAT-502 (the API became unreachable while background loops kept running, feed/rules polling the strongest candidate). If either recurs after this lands, this is the first thing to measure -- the rules engine now shares the event loop with request handling and does more per cycle than when those rows were written.
Verification: OBSERVED LIVE 2026-09-17: the scoped rule evaluates 49 points per 60 s poll where the unscoped version evaluated at most 10 candidates. This is the predicted cost arriving, not a surprise. Watch it against CAVEAT-500/502 when timing lanes. || PRIOR: Not yet observed live; recorded at the moment the cost was introduced rather than after it surprised someone.

Title: Every asset status is frozen at provisioning time, so the freshness caveat fires on all of them forever
Description: bldg1_synthetic_status.ttl stamps ontosage:statusObservedAt once, at generation. All lift, network and AV statuses currently read 2026-09-06, so on 2026-09-17 'Are the lifts working?' answers 'All 2 lift(s) are operational (last checked 11 days ago)' and that number grows by one every day -- 12 on demo day. The lane's own docstring records the same problem being hit before at five days: the caveat fires on every answer and therefore stops carrying information.
Root_Cause: A status is not a fact. It is the current value of something that changes, and the provisioner writes it as a fact. asset_state_service._open_outages says exactly this and is the partial fix -- episodes in the event store say what is HAPPENING to an asset -- but the base status triple is still a single frozen literal.
Fix_Approach: DO NOT refresh the timestamps to make the demo look better: asserting an observation time when nothing observed anything is the fabrication design contract 4 forbids, and it would make a stale value read as current -- which the lane's own comments call out as worse than reporting staleness honestly. The system's behaviour here is CORRECT and is worth demonstrating rather than hiding. The real fix is that a status should be refreshed by the same placeholder-data path that keeps sensor readings current, so that when a real lift-controller feed replaces it the graph shape does not change. NEEDS THE USER'S CALL, because refreshing a status timestamp asserts more than refreshing a sensor reading does.
Verification: Measured live 2026-09-17: STALE_AFTER_HOURS = 24.0 degrades the wording to a last-known state but NEVER refuses, so nothing breaks on demo day -- the answer is correct and honest, just visibly old. Confirmed by direct query: all status timestamps in the file are 2026-09-06.

Title: The lift modality asked for a Brick class that does not exist, so it matched nothing
Description: config/saturation_modalities.yaml declared lift_state over brick:Availability_Status and brick:Elevator_Status. MEASURED 2026-09-17 against the live graph: zero points carried either, so the modality resolved to NOTHING and every lift-availability question fell through it. brick:Elevator_Status is worse than unused -- it does not exist in the loaded Brick TBox at all (zero owl:Class declarations in both the brick and bldg repositories), so it could never have matched anything in any building. Meanwhile bldg:Lift_1_Status_Sensor was sitting there with a timeseries reference and 28,134 rows, typed brick:Occupancy_Status.
Root_Cause: A declared class nobody checked against the TBox, plus a point typed for what it physically reports (a car's idle/travelling/door-open state reads like occupancy) rather than for what it MEANS (whether the lift is in service). Neither side was wrong on its own terms and nothing compared them. Found by the stakeholder-coverage sweep, which reported it as blocking 26 of 37 stakeholder roles.
Fix_Approach: TTL-FIRST, not a config widening: brick:Availability_Status is a real Brick class and is what the point means, so Lift_1_Status_Sensor now carries it ADDITIVELY -- Occupancy_Status is kept so Brick-aware readers already using it do not break. The phantom Elevator_Status is removed from the config with the measurement recorded inline. Because the point now sits in two class populations, occupancy_status gains label_excludes [lift, elevator] -- the documented CAVEAT-207 split -- so a lift's door state is not counted as a room's occupancy. Occupancy_Status is deliberately NOT added to lift_state: each modality claims one side.
Verification: Measured before and after, not inferred. BEFORE: SPARQL COUNT over brick:Availability_Status and brick:Elevator_Status returned zero rows; Lift_1_Status_Sensor's rdf:type set was {NamedIndividual, Occupancy_Status}. The point's data was confirmed present first, so this unblocks real readings rather than an empty point: 28,134 rows in sensor_data_synth, earliest 2026-07-16 14:54:59, latest 2026-09-16 17:22:39, measured through a session pinned to +00:00 (the CLOCKS trap). AFTER: the TTL re-parses at 1,081 triples with types {NamedIndividual, Occupancy_Status, Availability_Status}; the YAML re-parses at 45 modalities with lift_state ['Availability_Status'] + contains [lift, elevator] and occupancy_status excludes [lift, elevator]. LIVE RE-ASK AND TTL RE-UPLOAD STILL OWED -- the running container holds the old graph until the next restart. NOTE Lift_2 has a power sensor but NO status sensor, which BUG-497 makes visible now that the building is known to have two lifts; that asymmetry is BUG-649's neighbour and is not fixed here.
Refs: config/saturation_modalities.yaml; input/bldg1_enhancements.ttl; orchestrator/services/deliberation/coverage_audit.py (matches); CAVEAT-207; BUG-497; V5-T10; docs/STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE_2026-09-17.md

Title: Three declared modalities have no points at all, so declaring the domain was recorded as covering it
Description: waste_fill, waste_weight and damper_position resolve to ZERO points in the live graph (measured 2026-09-17: Waste_Fill_Level_Sensor 0, Waste_Weight_Sensor 0, Damper_Position_Sensor 0). Unlike lift_state (BUG-648) this is not a vocabulary error -- the classes are right and the instruments are absent. The stakeholder sweep counts these among the only gaps that need points provisioned rather than vocabulary corrected.
Root_Cause: The modalities were added by V6-T43 and V6-T26 as the DECLARATION half of the work and the provisioning half never followed. The config entry reads as though the domain is handled; a reader skimming the file would reasonably think so.
Fix_Approach: Provision points for the three, the same way the 510+36 points were provisioned across floors 0-5 earlier this week, OR state the absence in the config so nobody reads the declaration as coverage. The second half is done: the file now records, inline and with the measurement, that these three resolve to zero. Provisioning is the open part and is a deliberate post-freeze decision -- it adds graph and DB writes, and today's remaining hours are better spent verifying what already exists.
Verification: PROVISIONED AND LIVE 2026-09-17. 6 outside-air dampers (one per air handling unit, brick:Outside_Damper + brick:Damper_Position_Sensor) and 12 waste bins (a general and a mixed-recycling bin per floor, each with BOTH a fill level and a weight), by scripts/provision_damper_and_waste_points.py, which DISCOVERS its anchors -- the AHUs from the graph, each floor's bin room from that floor's own rooms by a stated preference order -- so it runs for another building unchanged. Every class was verified present in the loaded ontology BEFORE anything was written, because brick:Elevator_Status was declared in this same config file and does not exist in Brick at all (BUG-648). || HISTORY SEEDED, not just live values: 21 days at 30-minute spacing, 12,108 rows per waste table, and 30,841 damper rows derived from each AHU's OWN fan-status rows timestamp by timestamp -- so the seeded history already carries the correlation the publisher keeps writing and there is no discontinuity where live publishing takes over. || BOTH HALVES OF CONTRACT 8 WERE NEEDED AND I ONLY DID ONE AT FIRST: registering the tables in database_registry.yaml is not enough, they must also be in building.yaml storage.databases. The registry warning says so verbatim, and the building.yaml comment above the list describes this exact failure from V6-T26 -- and it still happened, and the first live ask died on "Unknown column '<uuid>' in 'field list'". || LAY TERMS WERE ALSO REQUIRED: with the points live and reachable, 'what is the bin weight in the Floor 3 kitchen' still went to the DOCUMENT lane and answered from the Waste Collection Register. Three concepts added to ontology/mining/concept_terms_raw.csv and regenerated (the file says do not hand-edit the TTL), after checking every proposed term against all 72 existing concepts for collisions. That is TODO-651's finding in miniature: provisioning data does not make it reachable. || MEASURED AFTER: 3,507 declared references, 0 with no rows, 0 stale. Bin weight and damper position both answer live from real readings. || STILL OPEN: floor-scoped plant questions (BUG-667). || PRIOR: The honesty half is done and measured; the data half is not started. Counts above are from direct SPARQL COUNT(DISTINCT ?s) against the live bldg repository, not from the sweep's own classifier -- the sweep's author states a 29% miss rate on its register matching and asks that its question counts be treated as +/-30%, so its numbers were re-derived rather than quoted.
Refs: config/saturation_modalities.yaml; scripts/provision_synthetic_sources.py; V6-T43; V6-T26; BUG-648; docs/STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE_2026-09-17.md

Title: One register of forty wins a quarter of all register selections
Description: The stakeholder sweep ran all 2,960 catalogue questions through the live register lane's own scorer inside the container. ApprovalRecord was selected for 498 of 1,979 selections -- 25.2%. One register out of roughly forty taking a quarter of everything is a routing distribution worth explaining before it is trusted. The same run found the scorer selects NO register at all for 981 of 2,960 questions (33.1%), worst for BMS-HVAC operators and researchers at 53.8%.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. BUG-545's qualifier fix is in and this survived it, so it is not that. Candidates: ApprovalRecord's lay terms are generic enough to match approval/permission /sign-off language that belongs to several registers; or the scorer lacks a tie-break that would prefer a more specific register.
Fix_Approach: Before the demo, check what ApprovalRecord is actually winning -- sample the 498 and read them. If they are genuinely approval questions the distribution is a property of the corpus, not a defect, and this row closes as explained. Do NOT retune the scorer on a distribution alone; this project's record is that the measuring instrument is wrong more often than the system (lessons.md #20-22), and the sweep's author reports a 29% miss rate on the very matching this number comes from.
Verification: ADDRESSED OFFLINE 2026-09-17 (VOCAB agent), measured with scripts/register_reach.py over the 2,960 catalogue questions (baseline reproduces the sweep's 33.1% / 25.2% exactly). ApprovalRecord's bare generic terms removed (evidence, verified, confirmed, proof, owner, accountable, governance, assurance, certificate, permitted, 'is this allowed', bare authorised) and replaced by phrases ('approved by', 'who signed off', 'approval status'). ApprovalRecord 25.2% -> 6.0%; largest class now WorkspaceProfile 10.2%. Also narrowed AccessPermission, ContinuityProvision, AccessibleRoute, PublicEvent, EventActivity, CoordinationFunction, WasteCollectionPoint, WorkspaceProfile, CostLine, ConditionSurvey, ClosurePeriod, StakeholderGroup, IncidentRecord, DoorHardware. Guard set (124 questions, derived mechanically BEFORE any edit) 0 violations throughout. HELD selections 1,979 -> 1,140, i.e. the no-register share ROSE 33.1% -> 61.5% - read, not assumed: of 30 selections that disappeared, 24 were wrong and 1 right; of 30 new ones, 13 right, 3 partial, 14 wrong. What those questions now receive live is measured by the Phase 0 re-run, not by this harness. || PRIOR: Not yet sampled. The 33.1% no-selection figure is the sweep's strongest number because it comes from the live scorer rather than from the sweep's own classifier; the 25.2% concentration comes from the same source. Role counts saturate at 37 and survive the noise; question counts do not.

Title: Twenty-three of the top twenty-five stakeholder gaps are vocabulary, not missing instruments
Description: The 37-catalogue sweep extracted 2,960 questions (all 37 catalogues, zero extraction failures; the 38th PDF is the Master Technical Report and correctly yields none) and classified 56 gap rows: 39 VOCABULARY, 17 DATA -- and 23 of the top 25 by roles blocked are VOCABULARY. The widest gaps are registers that exist and hold instances but cannot be REACHED by the words stakeholders use: CoordinationFunction (33 roles: casualty, responder, fire appliance, assembly point), PatrolCheckpoint (33), AssetEngineeringProfile (30), AccessPermission (31). Candidate lay terms per register, distinctiveness-weighted rather than frequency-ranked, are in the sweep's CSV.
Root_Cause: Registers were authored with the vocabulary of the people who built them rather than of the people who query them. This is the cheap fix and the wide one at the same time, which is unusual and worth acting on.
Fix_Approach: Add lay terms per register from the candidate column, ONE register at a time with the probe green before and after -- the same discipline the routing contract requires. Do NOT bulk-load all 39 rows' terms at once: a term that overlaps an existing register moves questions off a register that was answering them, and CAVEAT-650 shows the distribution is already skewed. Sequence AFTER the demo unless a specific register is needed for it.
Verification: Not started. The 56 rows and their candidate terms are in docs/stakeholder_coverage.csv. TREAT THE QUESTION COUNTS AS +/-30%: the sweep's author hand-graded a seeded sample of 24 and found the right register missing from the top-3 for 7 of them, and states the role counts (which saturate at 37) are the figures to rank on. The sweep also has no notion of the capability/amenity lane's 93 Amenity/KnowledgeTopic triples, so amenity coverage is unmeasured by it.

Title: Three event registers hold zero instances while being demanded by twenty-five roles
Description: AlarmEvent, AnomalyEvent and AccessEvent hold NO instances (demanded by 25, 21 and 20 stakeholder roles respectively). Worse than the emptiness: the honest-absence path barely fires for them -- absent_record_class names them for 24 questions out of the ~295 that demand them, so most such questions get something other than a clean 'this building records no alarm events'.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. The registers were defined and never populated; separately, the absence guard appears not to recognise most phrasings that demand them.
Fix_Approach: Two independent halves, and the SECOND is the one that matters for honesty: an empty register that declines cleanly is acceptable, an empty register that produces some other answer is not. Fix the absence path first and measure it; populating the registers is a data decision for after the demo.
Verification: PREPARED 2026-09-17, NOT LOADED (DATA agent). scripts/provision_event_and_capacity_data.py emits input/bldg1_alarm_events.ttl (271 alarms on 97 discovered assets; 263 cleared, 6 never acknowledged, 2 acknowledged-still-active; clustered, e.g. AHU_F4 31; slower acknowledgement out of hours read from the building's openingHours) and input/bldg1_door_access_events.ttl (679 events at 7 controlled openings: 470 denied, 189 held open, 20 forced; role templates from the building's own 12 grantedToRole values; nothing names a person). Every event declares isSimulated; deterministic re-run is byte-identical; every referenced IRI exists in the live graph; 0 dangling references across 64 files. tests/test_event_and_capacity_provisioning.py 32 passed; 5 of 5 deliberate generator mutations caught. ANOMALIES DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED -- see BUG-670. RISKS TO CHECK AT LOAD: both registers exceed the whole-register handover limit (120 rows / 1,300 cells); a small role template plus door plus timestamp could narrow to one person, so the k-anonymity floor must be confirmed to apply; times are building-local wall clock like the existing registers, while stores are UTC. Six predicates were undeclared and have been handed to the VOCAB agent. || PRIOR: From the stakeholder sweep; the instance counts are structural and reliable, the question counts carry the sweep's stated +/-30%. Not independently re-measured yet.

Title: A query that ran and found nothing was retried three more times, and could be mutated into a different question
Description: SelfCorrectionEngine has a fast path whose own comment states the reasoning exactly: an empty result is a data-absence, not a query bug, so stop and let the caller fall through. It compared against the literal 'Empty result set' -- a string the engine SYNTHESISES itself, and only when the executor reported no error at all: error = result.get('error') or ('Empty result set' if is_success and count == 0 else None). The sparql lane reports its own for this case ('error': None if bindings else 'Empty results'), that value is truthy, the or short-circuits, and the literal tested never matched. THE BRANCH NEVER FIRED on the main path.
Root_Cause: Two modules agreeing on a magic string, with nothing checking that they still agreed. The engine's own fallback spelling and the lane's spelling differ by three characters.
Fix_Approach: Branch on the CONDITION rather than on either spelling: is_success and result_count <= EMPTY_RESULT_THRESHOLD. The string is no longer the contract, because the string is what failed. Found by the pipeline-planning audit, which proposed widening the comparison to match both literals; branching on the condition is the same size and removes the coupling instead of extending it.
Verification: tests/test_an_empty_result_stops_the_correction_loop.py -- 7 passed, asserting on real executor CALL COUNTS through the public entry point rather than on the string, since rebuilding the same coupling in the test suite would prove nothing. Before: up to four executions at a 30 s correction timeout each. After: exactly one, and the query is never mutated. Negative cases pinned too: a query that FAILS to parse still goes through all the strategies, and one that fails then succeeds still uses the rows. CORRECTNESS, NOT ONLY LATENCY: success=True with zero rows means the query parsed and ran, so the syntax and prefix strategies cannot be repairing anything -- they can only mutate a valid query into a different one, and if that mutation returns rows those rows become the answer to a question the user did not ask. || ONE CLAIM CORRECTED WHILE TESTING: the engine stamps success=False and 'please try rephrasing' onto this result, which is the wrong kind of nothing -- the query ran, the building holds nothing, and the user's phrasing is not at fault. It is currently HARMLESS because sparql_agent ignores both fields and re-reads the bindings itself. Not fixed here: changing success for this path changes what every downstream reader sees, which is not a freeze-day change. LIVE RE-ASK OWED.

Title: Every honest 'no data' question is routed into the least grounded lane in the system
Description: sparql_agent, on zero bindings, unconditionally calls answer_semantically -- the semantic-RAG fallback, which is LLM prose over retrieved ontology text with no SPARQL bindings behind it. So the questions where the building genuinely holds nothing are systematically answered by the one lane that cannot ground an answer, rather than by the absence machinery built for exactly this (the four-kinds-of-nothing distinction: graph-absence, window-absence, retrieval failure and forbidden access are different facts).
Root_Cause: The fallback predates the absence guard and was never revisited when it arrived. Nobody compared 'we found no rows' with 'we should say we found no rows'.
Fix_Approach: Do NOT remove the RAG fallback wholesale before the demo -- it is currently answering questions, and this project's expensive failure mode is a guard that takes something else with it. The measured order is: (1) BUG-643 is fixed, so a RAG answer now carries grounded=False and a quantitative claim under a gated intent is withheld rather than published -- that is the bleeding stopped; (2) then decide, per intent, whether an empty result should reach RAG at all or should produce a typed absence. Sequence after the demo.
Verification: FIXED OFFLINE 2026-09-17 (SPARQL agent). A typed absence (retrieval_outcome NOT_DECLARED, method typed_absence, shaped like the referent gate's) replaces the semantic-RAG fallback ONLY when ALL hold: the intent reads data (sensor_data, analytics, compare, trend, anomaly, report, export, compliance, visualization); the deterministic floor-scoped query selected by class; it RAN and returned empty (not failed); and it covered EVERY class the concept resolved to. The last condition prevents a false 'no data': 'noise on floor 4' targets the keyword map's bldg:Noise_Level_Sensor (1 instance) while 52 ontosage:Sound_Level_Sensor points sit on floor 4. RAG stays for metadata/discovery/general and for empty LLM-generated or label-matched queries, which prove nothing absent. verifier._bindings reads the result as []. The remedy text is stored, not shown. No dedicated reader of method=typed_absence yet; text reaches the user via the existing formatted_response path. || PRIOR: Found while verifying BUG-653: sparql_agent.py:563-565 falls through on 'not has_results' with no intent test and no absence check. Severity is materially reduced by BUG-643's fix landing the same day -- before it, these answers reached the user with no grounding record at all.

Title: The inherited-state guard is wired to the one endpoint that needed it least
Description: prune_inherited runs on /v1/chat/completions ONLY (main.py:3736-3742). /chat, /chat/stream and the /stream websocket each call redis_manager.load_state and prune NOTHING -- verified by mapping every load_state call to its enclosing route: 2413 /chat, 2668 /chat/stream, 3220 websocket, 3712 /v1. load_state restores the WHOLE intermediate_results dict, and five keys survive the response node's cleanup (_orchestrator.py:5649-5669): forecast_result, anomaly_result, deliberate_result, evidence_record, visualization_path. All five are in PLACE_BOUND_KEYS. context_switch.py even says of them 'the rest are listed because the same rule applies if they are ever carried' -- they ARE carried, on the endpoints the guard was never wired to. Meanwhile /v1 inherits a STRICT SUBSET: a fresh state plus two keys, both pruned.
Root_Cause: The guard was added where the conversational feature was added. Nobody checked the other three entry points, and the comment quoted above shows the author believed those keys were not being carried anywhere.
Fix_Approach: Wire prune_inherited into the three unguarded routes, or move it into the workflow so an entry point cannot omit it -- the second is better and is why this is not a freeze-day change: it is a shared-path edit with no green probe on either side of it, which V12-01's ordering rule forbids this close to a demo. SECOND DEFECT, independent: prune_inherited compares ADJACENT turns, so in 'room A' -> 'how has that changed?' -> 'room B' the middle turn names no place, switched() returns None, and nothing is pruned on /v1 either.
Verification: FIXED OFFLINE 2026-09-17 (ENDPOINT agent). One helper, main._prune_inherited_state (~2401), now runs on /chat (~2516), /chat/stream (~2757), the /stream websocket (~3322) and /v1 (~3840, replacing its inline copy), before the new message is appended, and never fails a turn. The SECOND defect is fixed too, without touching context_switch.py: _last_place_named (~2386) compares against the most recent earlier user turn that NAMED a place, so room A -> 'how has that changed?' -> room B now prunes (this deliberately changes /v1 as well). tests/test_every_chat_entry_point_prunes_inherited_state.py 28 passed, driving each real route; disabling the helper fails 10, restoring the adjacent comparison fails the 4 look-back tests. || CORRECTION TO THIS ROW: 'five place-bound keys survive' overstated the live exposure. _clear_stale_lane_results already clears anomaly_result, deliberate_result, evidence_record and visualization_path at the start of every run; only forecast_result actually reached the workflow unpruned on /chat. MULTI-TURN LIVE CHECK OWED. || PRIOR: MY OWN PREMISE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. I briefed this work believing the DEMO endpoint was the unguarded one; on the carry-forward axis it is the probe's endpoint, /chat, that is unguarded. I re-derived the route mapping myself rather than accept either version. The other half of BUG-524, the rewrite guard rewrite_is_safe, is in dialogue_agent.py:668 INSIDE the workflow, so both endpoints do have that one. NOT OBSERVED LIVE: no multi-turn conversation has been run through either endpoint under test, which is the actual gap.

Title: The demo streams, and the streaming branch is covered by no automated test at all
Description: Open WebUI streams by default, and the streaming response is a SEPARATE branch of /v1/chat/completions (main.py:3781-3907) that reconstructs the final state from last_step.items() rather than from the workflow's returned state. The 60-case regression probe does not stream; it posts to /chat. The new endpoint-parity harness does not stream either. So the code path the demo will actually run on Friday is exercised by nothing automated -- only by manual runs of scripts/ask_questions.py --v1 --stream.
Root_Cause: Not a defect yet -- an unmeasured path. It is recorded as P1 because of what it is measuring: the demo path itself, two days out.
Fix_Approach: Run the demo path AS THE DEMO WILL RUN IT before the freeze: /v1/chat/completions with stream=true, against a handful of the questions the demo will use, and compare the reconstructed answer with the non-streamed one for the same question. A divergence here is worth more than another green run of the non-streaming probe. Do not add streaming to the regression probe today -- that changes the instrument on freeze day.
Verification: RUN LIVE 2026-09-30, and this row's own headline was WRONG by then -- corrected here rather than quietly. 'Covered by no automated test at all' stopped being true when TODO-657 added tests/test_v1_reports_the_lane.py, which exercises the streaming branch through the real main.py framing (role chunk, delta shape, final chunk, [DONE]). What was genuinely missing was PARITY coverage -- nothing compared the two branches to each other -- and that is now tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py, 12 tests, 6 of them red before today's fixes. || LIVE COMPARISON, 7 questions asked BOTH ways against bldg1 with resp_cache flushed before each cold ask: LANE AGREED 7/7 (analytics, observability, analytics, observability, compare, analytics, capability). TEXT IDENTICAL 6/7 once the <details> progress panel -- which only the streamed body carries -- is stripped. The one difference was BOTH-COLD generation nondeterminism, not a path divergence: 'which floor used the most electricity last week' returned the same conclusion (Floor 4) and every figure identical (2196/2023/173/2118/2074/2102/2057 kWh) in different words, which is CAVEAT-891's shape and not this row's. Evidence: scratchpad caveat656_live.json + caveat656_coldcold.json. || THE ANSWER TO WHAT THIS ROW WAS OPENED ABOUT: the honesty guards DO apply on the streaming path. The publication gate, the answer-relevance gate, the grounding guard and the claim binder all run inside _response_node, which is INSIDE the LangGraph state machine; both branches run that same graph (stream_execute vs execute) and both take the answer from the finished state rather than assembling one of their own. Neither branch of /v1/chat/completions applies a gate of its own -- pinned by test_main_py_applies_no_gate_of_its_own, which fails the moment one is added to main.py where it could only be wired into a single branch. So the non-streamed quality numbers are NOT describing a code path users do not use. || WHAT THE TWO PATHS DID DIVERGE ON, three defects found and fixed today: BUG-1211 (P1 -- a failed turn streamed the user's own question back as the assistant's answer, at 200, with finish_reason stop), BUG-1212 (ontosage_llm_degraded and ontosage_evidence_record rode only the non-streamed body, confirmed live 7/7), BUG-1213 (an exception mid-stream truncated the SSE body with no error chunk and no [DONE]). All three are SOURCE-ONLY: the orchestrator runs uvicorn without --reload, so the container is still on the pre-fix code and a restart is owed before live re-verification. || PRIOR: INSTRUMENT BUILT 2026-09-17 (ENDPOINT agent), NOT YET RUN LIVE. endpoint_parity_probe.py --stream asks each case unstreamed then streamed on /v1 and compares the reconstructed answers (_run_stream_mode ~1199), reusing ask_questions._ask_v1_stream rather than a second client. That client does not read ontosage_intent, so --stream compares text markers only; it also forwards only X-OpenWebUI-User-Email, so --stream exits 2 under any other FORWARDED_USER_HEADER. tests/test_endpoint_parity_stream_mode.py 29 passed, including a stream generated by the real main.py framing. Stays open until it runs live; the manual 44/44 streamed demo-script run earlier today is the only live evidence. || PRIOR: Gap identified 2026-09-17 by the endpoint-parity work. The streamed path HAS been exercised manually in earlier sessions via ask_questions.py --v1 --stream, so it is not unexercised -- it is untested, which is a different and weaker claim, and the weaker one is the true one.
Refs: orchestrator/main.py:3781-3907; scripts/ask_questions.py; scripts/endpoint_parity_probe.py; scripts/regression_probe.py; docs/ENDPOINT_PARITY_2026_09_17.md; DEMO-05; DEMO-07

Title: The demo endpoint does not report which lane answered, so lane assertions cannot be checked on it
Description: /v1/chat/completions returns no intent field, so every lane assertion in the regression corpus is unevaluable against the endpoint the demo uses. The parity harness SKIPS those assertions and reports the skipped count rather than passing them -- passing would flatter /v1 for telling us less. The class of defect this blinds the harness to is BUG-631: a correct-looking answer produced by the wrong lane.
Root_Cause: The OpenAI-compatible response shape has no field for it and none was added.
Fix_Approach: Add intent to the /v1 response body. It is ADDITIVE -- one field, no existing consumer reads it, no shared path touched -- which is why it is the one orchestrator change worth arguing for before Friday rather than after. Open WebUI ignores unknown fields.
Verification: FIXED OFFLINE 2026-09-17 (ENDPOINT agent). /v1 now reports the lane as `ontosage_intent` (same prefix as the two existing extension fields; a bare `intent` could collide with a future OpenAI field): top level of the non-streamed body (main.py ~4108), None on the timeout body (~4047), and ONLY on the final finish_reason=stop chunk of a stream, never inside `delta` (~4004), read from the same final state the answer text comes from. Open WebUI reads delta.content/role and ignores unknown top-level keys; role chunk still first, [DONE] still last, and tests assert the reassembled text is byte-identical. tests/test_v1_reports_the_lane.py 9 passed. The parity harness's unstreamed client now reads it, so lane assertions are evaluated on /v1. LIVE CHECK OWED. || PRIOR: Not started. Blocks the parity harness from evaluating lane assertions on the demo endpoint.
Refs: orchestrator/main.py (/v1/chat/completions response body); scripts/endpoint_parity_probe.py; BUG-631; docs/ENDPOINT_PARITY_2026_09_17.md

Title: Readings of any age could be narrated as the current value, with nothing recorded that a substitution had happened
Description: When the requested window returned no rows, sql_agent built a fallback query with NO date bound at all -- ORDER BY Datetime DESC LIMIT 200 -- and narrated those rows as the answer. The guard was a hardcoded keyword list (today, yesterday, last week, hour, day, week, month, year, since, before, after, between, from, until) which omits every present-tense phrasing: 'right now', 'currently', 'latest', 'live', 'at the moment', 'now'. Confirmed mechanically against git show HEAD: all seven present-tense phrasings returned False. NOTHING WAS RECORDED ANYWHERE -- two log lines and no bus marker -- so no gate, disclosure or evidence record could know it had happened.
Root_Cause: TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS, one narrowing and one widening. NARROWER: the 'now-1d'/'now-24h' arms of _is_default_range are effectively dead, because dialogue_agent resolves relative phrases to absolute stamps before the SQL lane sees them, so the branch fires only when the dialogue node extracted NO bounds at all. WIDER, and why it still matters: 'unspecified' is not 'unbounded' -- with no bounds the primary query still applies >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY), so it asks a real question and returns nothing for any point whose store has had no data in 30 days. And _orchestrator.py states outright that a live question carries no start_date. So present-tense questions are PRECISELY the ones that land here.
Fix_Approach: Three parts, and the keyword list is the least important. (1) THE MARKER: sql_result['window_substituted'], a sub-key of an existing reserved bus key following the precedent of window_mask/rows_capped/points_capped/resolution_clamp_s, carrying the requested bounds AND the actual earliest/latest of the rows returned. The span is the honest part: 'we substituted' is weak, 'these readings run to a date months behind your question' lets the reader judge. requested_label passes through the same _sanitize_datetime the query builder uses, so a bound the query DISCARDED is never named as though it had been honoured. (2) THE DISCLOSURE: detection and wording in disclosure_gate, reading the structured marker only, never prose. (3) THE GUARD: the inline list replaced by names_a_period(), reusing the _NOW_RE and _PERIOD_RE already in the file, so the two readings of a question can no longer disagree about whether it said 'now'. A future missing keyword now produces a DISCLOSED substitution rather than a silent one -- that, not the vocabulary, is the protection.
Verification: tests/test_sql_window_substitution_is_disclosed.py -- 27 passed (re-run by me after renumbering, not taken on trust). The load-bearing test is the one where the guard CORRECTLY permits a question that names no period and the disclosure must still fire. Both negatives pinned: data-in-window untouched, explicit past window unchanged. Wider slices measured: -k sql 100 passed 1 skipped; -k 'sql or disclosure or policy_governs' 135 passed 1 skipped; -k 'evidence or window or time or freshness or narration or response' 731 passed 3 skipped. black/isort/flake8 clean. LIVE RE-ASK OWED. || A TRADE-OFF THE USER MAY WANT TO FLIP: widening the guard means a present-tense question with no recent data now gets the honest no-data path instead of a DISCLOSED stale reading. Disclosed-stale is arguably more useful to a facility manager. Reverting is one line (drop _NOW_RE from names_a_period and rely on the disclosure alone).

Title: The response node preferred the analytics lane and dropped every disclosure the SQL lane had attached
Description: _response_node's dispatch takes analytics_result['formatted_response'] before sql_result['formatted_response']. The SQL lane appends its disclosures to its OWN prose, so whenever the analytics lane ran, the figures survived and the disclosures did not: the new window-substitution note (BUG-658), and equally the pre-existing 'window applied', sensor-cap and resolution-clamp notes. Stale or capped figures narrated without their caveat, the warning removed in the last step before the user sees it.
Root_Cause: Identical in shape to the exclusion-note defect already fixed in this same function on 2026-09-07, where 1,000 excluded readings became invisible because the compare and analytics lanes re-narrate from rows and emit their own text. That fix appended after the dispatch; nothing generalised the lesson to the other disclosures, so the next one added inherited the same gap.
Fix_Approach: Append after the whole dispatch, beside the exclusion note and for the same stated reason, reading the STRUCTURED marker via disclosure_gate.window_substitution_in over the whole bus -- so it survives whichever lane narrated, not just analytics. De-duplicated on the note's own text so a reworded note cannot slip a duplicate past a marker-based check. The pre-existing window-mask, sensor-cap and resolution-clamp notes are NOT yet routed this way; they are prose-embedded in the SQL formatter and need structured notes of their own first. That part stays open.
Verification: The substitution note is routed and the module parses and is flake8-clean at F821/F823. NOT YET EXERCISED BY A TEST OR A LIVE TURN -- the response node's dispatch is not unit-testable in isolation without a full state, and the live re-ask is owed together with BUG-658's. The three older disclosures remain exposed to the same drop.
Refs: orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py (_response_node dispatch); orchestrator/services/disclosure_gate.py; BUG-658; .claude/rules/agent-patterns.md (step 3 -- a lane can compute the right answer and nobody sees it)

Title: The empty-window fallback queries the wide table on the default adapter, whatever store the points actually live in
Description: The fallback hardcodes FROM sensor_data and runs through self._execute_query, which calls adapter_registry.get() -- the DEFAULT adapter -- ignoring the group's storage_key. For a group whose points live in a narrow table or a non-default backend it therefore runs a wide-shaped query against the wrong store. Worse, _execute_query RAISES on adapter failure, and that escapes fetch_data_for_uuids and turns the whole turn into {'success': False} rather than an honest no-data answer.
Root_Cause: The fallback was written when the wide table was the only store and was never revisited when the adapter registry and the narrow tables arrived. Design contract 9 says a new backend is a new adapter and never edits to the agents; this path edits around them.
Fix_Approach: Build the fallback through adapter.build_timeseries_query like every other read, and decide separately whether a failed fallback should degrade to 'no data' rather than failing the turn. Both need a live re-ask, so not a freeze-day change. Pre-existing and unchanged by BUG-658's fix, which reduces how often the fallback fires but does not touch what it queries.
Verification: FIXED OFFLINE 2026-09-17 (SQL agent), live re-ask owed. The empty-window fallback no longer hand-writes FROM sensor_data or runs on the default adapter: new SQLAgent._latest_rows_from_store asks the GROUP's own adapter to build and run a newest-first, per-sensor-limited query, passing a far-past start bound (_FALLBACK_FLOOR) because every adapter adds its own 30-day lookback when given none and would otherwise re-ask the question that just came back empty. It never raises: no adapter, a builder that declines or throws, an unsuccessful result or an exception all return no rows with a WARNING naming the store, so a failed fallback ends as an honest no-data instead of success=False. The BUG-658 window_substituted marker still carries the span of rows ACTUALLY returned. A full 200-row fallback sample is now flagged as capped (it was compared against 1,000). || TESTS: new tests/test_the_empty_window_fallback_reads_the_right_store.py 15 passed (10 failed on the old code), including one that runs the real wide and narrow MySQL builders. THREE tests in tests/test_sql_window_substitution_is_disclosed.py then failed because their fake MODELLED THE DEFECT - the adapter declined to build and _execute_query was patched to serve fallback rows. Rewritten by the lead: the fake adapter now builds both queries and recognises the fallback by the floor bound it alone passes, and _execute_query is patched to RAISE, so a fallback that regresses to the default adapter fails loudly and the negative tests observe a real record rather than an empty list nothing could fill. 42 passed across both files. || FOUND AND NOT FIXED: sql_agent._build_uuid_union_query still names sensor_data with MySQL backticks as the path an adapter takes when it returns None from build_timeseries_query - already wrong for Postgres/Timescale wide tables (suggest P3); generate_and_execute and _generate_sql use the default adapter by design but still raise out of _execute_query; _get_all_db_columns has no callers. Influx, Mongo and Redis-TS builders reject a YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS bound (Influx defaults to 1 day), so their fallback will return no rows with a WARNING - as their main query already does. Wide-table fallback speed with the added Datetime floor is unmeasured.

Title: Three statements in the repo described behaviour the code does not have
Description: Found by the pipeline-planning audit and each re-derived from the code before being corrected, not taken on the audit's word. (1) CLAUDE.md said the routing contract holds 36 parse-stage rules; the module holds 40. That line had already been wrong once -- it said 17+1+1 for weeks -- so this is the same failure twice. (2) shared/config.py's workflow-deadline validator stated that 'llm_manager retries each call up to MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS times'. It does not: MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS is declared in config.py and read by NOTHING, and llm_manager does not mention it. (3) orchestrator/services/self_correction_policy.py opens by saying 'SQL has NO repair loop -- this module adds that gap', and nothing in orchestrator/, shared/ or scripts/ imports the module; its only reader is a test.
Root_Cause: All three are the same species: a claim written when it was true, or when it was about to be true, and never re-derived. lessons.md already carries this as 'a static completeness claim rots' -- and CLAUDE.md's own snapshot block carries a warning about exactly this, three lines above one of the wrong numbers.
Fix_Approach: Corrected in place, each with the measurement and the date, and CLAUDE.md now carries the one-line command that COUNTS the rules rather than a number to be read. The self-correction-policy docstring now states the third state explicitly -- code exists, tests pass, behaviour absent -- and says to wire it or delete it rather than leave it. Deliberately NOT deleted today: removing a module on freeze day to fix a docstring is the wrong trade.
Verification: Each claim re-derived before editing: routing rules counted from the imported module (PARSE 40 / POST 1 / CONCEPT 3); MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS grepped across orchestrator/ and shared/ with llm_manager returning zero hits; self_correction_policy importers grepped with the module itself excluded, returning none. Both edited modules re-parsed. A fourth audited claim -- that there is no GraphDB circuit breaker -- is also TRUE (circuit_breaker.py is used by llm_manager, main and mysql_adapter, not by the graph path) but is a design gap rather than a false statement, so nothing was edited for it.

Title: The regression probe never flushes the response cache, so a hand-asked question is scored as a cache hit
Description: scripts/regression_probe.py contains no reference to resp_cache, redis or any flush -- grepped, zero hits. So any case whose question was asked by hand shortly before a run is answered from Redis resp_cache (1h TTL) instead of by the pipeline. OBSERVED 2026-09-17 in probe v14: 'Is the lift working?' reported PASS in 0.0 s, having been asked twice by hand a few minutes earlier while verifying BUG-497. Exactly one case was affected in that run and it was the one I had touched.
Root_Cause: CLAUDE.md instructs flushing resp_cache before any testing, and every debugging procedure in it says so. The probe was written as a client and never adopted the rule, and because a cache hit PASSES it has never drawn attention to itself.
Fix_Approach: TWO harms, and the first is the serious one. (1) A cached answer produced BEFORE a code change will pass a case that the change has broken -- the probe's whole purpose is to catch that, and this is the one condition under which it cannot. (2) It corrupts the latency percentiles CAVEAT-500 now depends on: a cached case contributes ~0 s to p50. v14's ALL LANES p50 was 10.0 s against v13's 12.5 s, and one free case is part of that gap. FIX: flush resp_cache at the start of a run, or refuse to start when the cache is non-empty and say so. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE TODAY -- changing the measuring instrument on code-freeze day is how a green run stops meaning anything. Flush by hand before each run until then.
Verification: FIXED OFFLINE 2026-09-17 (ENDPOINT agent). regression_probe.flush_response_cache (~234) scans then DELs resp_cache:* in batches via `docker exec redis-memory-store redis-cli` with no shell, printing how many keys went; --no-flush and --redis-container flags. A failed flush prints a banner before any case and opens the report with a WARNING block. It deliberately does NOT use CLAUDE.md's `--scan | xargs DEL` pipeline: if the scan cannot reach Redis, xargs still exits 0 and reports '0 removed', indistinguishable from an empty cache. Any passing case under 1.0 s is marked 'possible cache hit' in console, table and a summary line; the quoted `N/M pass in X min` line is unchanged. tests/test_the_probe_flushes_the_response_cache.py 26 passed. || THE PARITY HARNESS HAD THE SAME DEFECT, worse: every mode asks the same question twice, and the cache key is question+building+user+role, so the second ask was served the first's answer and the two endpoints agreed BY CONSTRUCTION. It now flushes before every ask and turn. One real probe run to confirm the flush count is owed. || PRIOR: The affected case was independently verified UNCACHED before the probe ran: after the restart and a resp_cache flush, 'Is the lift working?' answered 'All 2 lift(s) are operational (last checked 11 days ago)' in 13.6 s on /v1 and 7.6 s on /chat, and its new markers were checked against that fresh answer using the probe's OWN _matches function rather than by eye. So v14's 60/60 stands -- but it stands on that separate check, not on the 0.0 s case.
Refs: scripts/regression_probe.py; CLAUDE.md (flush resp_cache before testing); CAVEAT-500; BUG-497; lessons.md (the measurement apparatus is usually the bug)

Title: The answer that refuses to invent a figure invented a capability instead
Description: Measured live on the demo script 2026-09-17 through the STREAMING demo endpoint. 'What is the radiation level in the atrium?' answered 'No - radiation is not measured in this building. There is no point of that kind located there, so any figure I gave you would be invented.' and then listed, under 'What IS measured there', the modality damper_position. brick:Damper_Position_Sensor and brick:Damper_Position_Command each have ZERO instances in the graph. waste_fill and waste_weight are in the same state and would be listed the same way. So the sentence whose whole purpose is to avoid inventing a figure invented a capability, in the answer a demo would show as the honesty story.
Root_Cause: The building-wide branch built alternatives from load_modalities() - the DECLARED config in config/saturation_modalities.yaml - with nothing checking that a point of the modality exists. The PER-SPACE branch twelve lines below had always done it correctly via present_modalities(), which keeps only entries whose coverage status is 'present'. Two notions of 'measured' in one function, and the looser one was used for the wider claim. Same root as BUG-649: declaring a modality was treated as covering the domain.
Fix_Approach: Reuse the honest filter rather than write a second one: the building-wide set is the union of present_modalities() over every space in the coverage schema. An EMPTY union omits the sentence entirely, because Reach.describe guards on 'if self.alternatives' - saying nothing about alternatives is honest, listing the config is not. load_modalities is still used to BUILD the schema; declaring a modality is what makes it auditable, and it was only as evidence of MEASUREMENT that it was wrong.
Verification: VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-17 through the streaming demo endpoint, cache flushed: the offer now reads 'air quality, co2, door contact, humidity, illuminance, lighting cct, noise, occupancy and more' - damper_position is gone and every name left is genuinely measured. No latency cost: 17.4 s warm against 18.6 s before the change (the 49.8 s first ask was cold start after the restart, re-measured rather than reported). || A LIMITATION I INTRODUCED AND AM NOT HIDING: the fix unions coverage over ROOM-LIKE SPACES, so a FLOOR-SCOPED modality is now omitted even though it is measured. Confirmed: brick:CO_Level_Sensor has 40 instances and carbon monoxide no longer appears in the offer. That trades a fabrication for an understatement, which is the right direction and not a clean result - the list is explicitly partial (it ends 'and more') so nothing false is asserted, but a reader could infer CO is unmeasured. THE BETTER FIX, post-demo: decide presence from whether a modality resolves to at least one point ANYWHERE - one SPARQL with VALUES over every declared class answers it exactly - rather than from room coverage, which is the wrong denominator for a building-wide question. Not done today: it is new code in a lane I had just changed, on freeze day. || PRIOR: tests/test_the_alternatives_offered_are_measured_not_declared.py - 8 tests; 74 passed together with the existing observability and absence-guard suites. Behavioural tests cover the filter, the cross-space union, and that 'stale' is not claimed as measured (a different kind of nothing from 'present'). One SOURCE-level test reads the expression after 'alternatives=' and fails if load_modalities returns - because the behavioural tests keep passing while the live answer resumes inventing capabilities, which is exactly how this survived. The first version of that test read too small a window and failed on my own comment; the window now starts at the expression so a comment can neither satisfy nor defeat it. FOUND ONLY BY RUNNING THE DEMO PATH AS THE DEMO WILL RUN IT (CAVEAT-656) - 60/60 on the probe did not surface it, because no probe case asks for an unmeasured quantity building-wide and then reads the offer. LIVE RE-ASK OWED.

Title: The heating circuit reported a delta-T of 0.04 C and recommended a repair for it
Description: Asked on the demo path 2026-09-17: "What's the delta-T across the heating circuit, and is it healthy?" answered '**Delta-T across the heating circuit: 0.04 C**' and went on to recommend 'Inspect the pump speed and check for flow restrictions'. A maintenance action invented from a generator artefact, on demo script question 57. MEASURED CAUSE: plant_data had received no rows since 2026-09-16 20:32 -- 30 points, the only stale points in the building -- and the last rows written had all decayed to ambient: every boiler point ~23 C, Boiler_1 delta -0.31 K, and Chiller_1 INVERTED (leaving 24.08 warmer than entering 23.28, which is not a chiller). The healthy history was still there underneath: boiler delta median +11.0 K over 2,644 paired rows.
Root_Cause: MY OWN FIX FOR BUG-638 STOPPED THE BLEEDING AND THEN BLED. Publishing correlated series as independent random walks collapsed delta-T from 11.08 to 0.12, so I excluded plant_data from the publish map -- which stopped the corruption AND the data. An excluded series does not hold still; it keeps whatever corrupted values it last received and ages. Removing a bad writer is not the same as fixing the write.
Fix_Approach: Publish plant per EQUIPMENT GROUP from one seed instead of per point: a lead value walked inside the band that point's own history occupied, and the follower derived as lead minus a delta drawn from the delta distribution that PAIR's history held. Parameters measured from the healthy period and explicitly NOT from the decayed tail -- continuing from `last` would have cemented the defect. Delta is drawn TRIANGULAR about the historical median rather than uniform across the band: uniform kept every sample in range while moving the AHU typical value by 2 K, and staying in range is not the same as continuing the series. Air temperatures now stay in band whatever the fan does (about half the stored history wrote ~0 C with the fan off, which is why the supply-air mean reads 8 C against a 20 C median of its non-zero rows); flow and filter pressure still collapse with the fan, because that part IS physical. Cadence PLANT_INTERVAL=300 s -- a boiler's water temperature does not move meaningfully in 30 s, and writing it that often adds load to the same MySQL the queries read.
Verification: VERIFIED LIVE after a container REBUILD (a source fix is not deployed until the image carries it, BUG-343). 38 plant points written per tick, latest timestamp current, Boiler_1 delta-T +11.58 K and Boiler_2 +11.18 K straight from the table. The demo question now answers 'Boiler 1 delta-T is 11.58 C ... the values are close, indicating a consistent temperature rise' -- and the invented repair recommendation is gone. BUILDING-WIDE SWEEP BEFORE AND AFTER: 3,477 declared timeseries references, 0 with no rows, and stale-over-one-hour went 30 -> 0. || tests/test_plant_points_are_published_as_correlated_groups.py, 8 passed, pinning the RELATIONSHIP rather than the values: sign per pair (a chiller must leave colder), no collapse below 0.5 K, the band, the typical value, and both directions of the fan rule -- temperatures must NOT fall to zero, flow MUST. Every individual value was plausible in the broken version too, which is why nothing caught it. || RESIDUAL, stated rather than buried: the generated AHU air-side delta medians about -4.2 K against a historical -2.9 K. Both are 'return air a few K warmer than supply' and the sign and band are right, but the triangular mean of a skewed band cannot reproduce its median exactly. Boilers, chiller and heat pump match to within 0.1 K.
Refs: mysql-dummy-publish-dev/mysql_dummy_publisher.py (publish_plant, load_plant_groups); input/bldg1_plant_publish_map.json; docker-compose.yml (data-publisher); BUG-638; BUG-343; CAVEAT-500; demo script Q57

Title: Every answer footed its sources with the words 'Simulated sensor data'
Description: The source chips rendered under each answer read '*Sources: `Building Ontology` `Simulated sensor data` `Analytics Engine`*', and nine datasource labels in input/datasources.yaml began with the word 'Simulated' ('Simulated Temperature Sensing', 'Simulated CO2 Sensing', ...). Seen on the demo path, in the streamed answer to the delta-T question.
Root_Cause: The labels were written when the distinction being drawn was real-vs-generated for the scorecard. But this building's sensor data is a PLACEHOLDER for the real feeds the owner will connect, and the chip describes the development fixture rather than the system being demonstrated. Standing user instruction, given twice: nothing a user can see may call this data synthetic, simulated or fake.
Fix_Approach: Rename the nine labels onto the convention the OTHER EIGHT entries in the same file already used ('Occupancy Sensing System', 'Energy Metering System'), so the file ends up internally consistent instead of carrying two styles, and change the code fallback from 'Simulated sensor data' to 'Sensor data'. WHAT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CHANGE: the `nature:` field, the `synthetic=True` flag on the tag, the grey chip colour, and every ontosage:isSimulated triple. Provenance accounting and the scorecard's real/synthetic share are untouched -- only the words a reader sees.
Verification: VERIFIED LIVE after restart and a cache flush: the same question now foots '*Sources: `Building Ontology` `Sensor data` `Analytics Engine`*'. YAML re-parses; all 17 provenance_system labels listed and none contains 'Simulated'. || THE TRADE, stated plainly: the chip TEXT no longer distinguishes placeholder data from real, so a reader who relied on that word loses it. The colour and the internal flag still carry the distinction, and the honest disclosures that matter -- staleness, absence, substituted windows -- are untouched. If the intent were to hide the data's nature rather than to stop mislabelling a placeholder, this would be the wrong change.

Title: Two publishers wrote the same series and the frequent, wrong one won
Description: Within minutes of provisioning the waste points, a recycling bin with a 28 kg capacity was reporting 60.0 kg and a general bin 52.8 kg at 57% full (expected ~34). CAUSE: the orchestrator's boot-time publish-map refresh swept the 24 new waste points into the NARROW map (2,756 -> 2,780) with value_col 'generic' and no band, so publish_narrow wrote a uniform 0-100 into wastefill_data AND wasteweight_data every 30 s, while the waste generator wrote the correct sawtooth every 300 s. The frequent writer won and fill stopped being a sawtooth at all.
Root_Cause: The refresh is correct and deliberate -- 498 points once existed, were uploaded and answered 'no recent reading' because the map was a manual step, and automating it is what makes 'docker compose up -d' true. It simply had no way to know these two tables already had a generator that understands them. TWO WRITERS ON ONE SERIES IS THE DEFECT, not the values either chose.
Fix_Approach: Add the two waste tables to publisher_map._CORRELATED_TABLES, the existing mechanism by which a series says 'one generator already understands me' -- the same door plant_data went through after BUG-638. Then delete the rows written during the overlap and let the correct generator refill.
Verification: VERIFIED: refresh now logs '68 point(s) left to their own generator (plant_data, wastefill_data, wasteweight_data)' -- 44 plant + 24 waste -- and the narrow map is back to 2,756 with zero waste uuids in it. 108 rows per table written during the overlap were deleted (the seed cut-off is exact, so nothing legitimate was lost). All 12 bins re-checked against their own stream capacity afterwards: 0 over capacity, weight 5.0-27.0 kg against fill 9.8-45.3%. || WORTH NOTING FOR NEXT TIME: the publish-map refresh only runs when a TTL was actually uploaded, so a restart that changes no TTL does not re-derive the map. Forcing it needs refresh_publish_map() through the service, not scripts/generate_publisher_map.py directly -- the SERVICE applies the correlated-table exclusion and the raw generator does not.
Refs: orchestrator/services/publisher_map.py (_CORRELATED_TABLES); orchestrator/main.py (refresh call site); mysql-dummy-publish-dev/mysql_dummy_publisher.py; BUG-638; BUG-649

Title: A floor-scoped question cannot reach plant points, and answers from a room sensor instead
Description: 'What is the outside air damper position on floor 3 right now?' returns nothing: the concept resolves ('damper_position'), the class resolves (brick:Damper_Position_Sensor), and the floor-scoped SPARQL then walks sensor -> space -> floor and finds nothing, because the damper hangs off an AHU. AHU_F3 declares 'brick:feeds bldg:HVAC_Zone_F3' and has NO brick:hasLocation -- it serves floor 3 from a plant room, it is not on floor 3. Asked by equipment instead ('on AHU F3') the same question answers correctly: 50.7%, from 989 readings. || WORSE, AND THE REASON THIS IS NOT MERELY A GAP: 'What is the supply air temperature on floor 3 right now?' does NOT decline -- it answers 24.1 C from 'Air Temperature Sensor installed-node 3.66', a ROOM sensor. A plant quantity was answered with a room quantity that happens to share the word temperature.
Root_Cause: The floor-scoped traversal only follows location. For equipment that SERVES a floor rather than sitting on it, the edge is brick:feeds (via the HVAC zone), and nothing follows it. PRE-EXISTING and not introduced by the damper points: it affects every plant point the building has. It went unnoticed because the plant questions that are asked name equipment or a circuit ('what's the delta-T across the heating circuit'), not a floor.
Fix_Approach: Follow brick:feeds -> zone -> floor in the floor-scoped resolve, in ADDITION to location, so a unit that serves a floor is in scope for that floor. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE TODAY: _floor_scoped_sparql is a shared path used by every floor question in the system, and V12-01's rule is that no change like it lands without the probe green before and after, one rule at a time -- which is not a code-freeze-day activity. Do NOT 'fix' it by asserting hasLocation on the AHUs: the building says they feed those zones from a plant room, and writing a location it does not have would trade a gap for a falsehood. The substitution half (a room sensor answering a plant question) is the more serious half and should be measured first.
Verification: FIXED OFFLINE 2026-09-17 (SPARQL agent). THE ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT LOCATION, correcting this row: AHU_F3_Supply_Air_Temperature explicitly has brick:hasLocation Floor3 and AHU_F3 brick:isPartOf Floor3, so the old walk reached it. The 24.1 C room answer came from (1) the HBCO temperature_reading concept (Outside_Air/Temperature/Zone_Air) REPLACING the supply-air class and matching 49 room sensors, and (2) the room-question rule that excludes plant points removing the supply-air point itself ('return air temperature on floor 2' returned 0 for the same reason). The damper WAS a location gap: its point has no location and hangs off an AHU that brick:feeds zones. Verified with explicit-triple SPARQL: 39 brick:feeds AHU->HVAC_Zone; zone<->floor written both ways (39 each); isFedBy only by inference. FIX in sparql_agent.py: a point is on a floor if located there OR a point of Equipment that feeds a Location on that floor (Systems and equipment-to-equipment feeds excluded); a named plant quantity uses its class alone (plus only same-modality classes such as damper Sensor+Command) and drops the room exclusion; no plant point on the floor -> empty, never room sensors. Measured with read-only queries: damper floor 3 0 -> 1 row; supply air floor 3 49 room sensors -> 1 AHU point; return air floor 2 0 -> 1; all other checked cases identical rows. COST: the UNION branch roughly doubles some floor queries (CO2 floor 1 vs 3 median 3.3 s -> 6.4 s; energy across floors 0.02 -> 0.18 s; AHU run-time 0.78 -> 1.51 s; noisy, GraphDB shared) - watch in the probe. tests/test_plant_questions_are_answered_by_plant_points.py 28 tests executing the floor query with rdflib against a real-shaped fixture; -k 'sparql or floor' -m unit 503 pass/1 unrelated fail -> 543 pass/0. The agent ran black over the WHOLE of sparql_agent.py (large diff, no behaviour change) and made one exact-string edit via a heredoc. LIVE RE-ASK OWED. Remaining room-sensor substitution path in _orchestrator's modality repair handed to ORCH-2; keyword map beating the concept handed back to SPARQL. || PRIOR: Both behaviours measured live 2026-09-17 with the cache flushed. The damper data itself is confirmed present and reachable: 5,146 rows per damper, values 0-79%, latest current, and the by-equipment question answers from it.

Title: A follow-up question is served another conversation's cached answer
Description: Confirmed by reading the code 2026-09-17 (reported by the ENDPOINT agent; not yet reproduced live). WorkflowOrchestrator._serve_from_cache runs at the very start of execute() and stream_execute(), BEFORE the dialogue node's co-reference rewrite, and looks up `state.messages[-1].content` -- the RAW user text. response_cache keys on normalise_query(question) + building + user + role, with no conversation and no prior turn. So for one user: chat A asks 'What is the CO2 in room 5.01?' then 'How has that changed over the last week?'; chat B asks 'What is the temperature on floor 3?' then the same follow-up -- and chat B is answered from chat A's cache entry, instantly, about the wrong room and the wrong quantity. The same holds inside one conversation for a repeated follow-up about a different referent within the 1 h TTL.
Root_Cause: The cache predates co-reference rewriting and was designed for standalone questions. A follow-up's meaning lives in the turns before it, which the key never contained. The role partition (added after an occupant was served a facility manager's reading) shows the same class of fix was made once for WHO is asking and never for WHAT was asked before.
Fix_Approach: Fold the prior user turns into the cache key, both on get and put, for exact and fuzzy lookups alike: an opening question keeps its context-free key (so demo-script questions still reuse the cache), and a later turn only matches an entry made with the same preceding questions. No anaphora word list -- lists decay, and a standalone question asked second merely loses cross-conversation reuse, which costs time, never correctness. Touches _orchestrator.py; sequenced after the DECLINES agent finishes editing that file.
Verification: FIXED OFFLINE 2026-09-17 (ORCH agent), live two-conversation reproduction on /chat and /v1 owed. THE DIAGNOSIS WAS INCOMPLETE: put stored under messages[-2].content, which by the response node has been REPLACED by the dialogue node's co-reference rewrite (or typography-folded / affirmation-rewritten / translated text), while get looked up the raw words - so get and put already disagreed on every rewritten turn, and rewritten answers were filed under standalone wording; one bad rewrite (BUG-524) could be served to anyone later typing that wording as a fresh question. FIX: response_cache.CONTEXT_TURNS=3 with context_turns/context_fingerprint/cache_hash (~219-252); an opening question keeps exactly query_hash(question) (cross-conversation reuse and pre-existing entries still match); a later turn hashes the normalised question plus a fingerprint of the last 3 earlier USER questions in order; get/put take context=; the fuzzy index is per partition AND per context (resp_cache:fuzzy:<partition>|c<fp>). _orchestrator computes question+context once from the rawest recorded wording (typed_query > original_query > text) in _serve_from_cache (~9111) and the store (~5686) reads it back and removes it. Bound of 3 = the rewrite's own window (format_conversation_history max_messages=6). No anaphora list. tests/test_a_follow_up_is_not_served_another_conversations_answer.py 23 passed; 912 related passed (was 835). RESIDUAL: carried forecast/analytics results older than 3 questions are not in the key; invalidate(question=...) now reaches only opening-question entries (no caller uses it). Tests were NOT re-run against the old code; checked by reading. || PRIOR: Code-verified: _orchestrator.py _serve_from_cache (~9004) reads messages[-1]; execute() calls it immediately after _clear_stale_lane_results (~9077), stream path ~9248; response_cache.query_hash normalises the question text alone. Live reproduction owed.
Refs: orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py (_serve_from_cache, response_cache.put ~5623); orchestrator/services/response_cache.py; BUG-655; BUG-524; CAVEAT-035

WHAT IS TRUE: effectiveFrom/effectiveTo are declared with domain ConfigurationPeriod and aboutEquipment is declared TWICE (domain Capability and domain IntervalRecord) while registers use all three - on a deployment running a full RDFS ruleset every record would be mis-typed. Kept: the generator now emits ontosage:alarmPriority (correct regardless). tests/test_event_and_capacity_provisioning.py: a passing check that records never carry ontosage:priority, plus a STRICT xfail pinning the domain debt so it alerts when the schema domains are widened. 46 passed, 3 xfailed. Neither supersedes the other and quoting one as 'the' number would be wrong.

=== CORRECTION TO THIS MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-30, AND IT IS MINE ===
I recorded tail N as 'asked as facility01@example.com (facility_manager)'. **It was not.** `scripts/ask_questions.py` reads `--email` ONLY inside its `if args.v1:` branch. Without `--v1` -- which is how I ran it -- the flag is parsed and silently discarded, the script calls `capture_golden_baseline._login()`, and that uses `ADMIN_USERNAME` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env` (`admin@ontosage`) and posts to **`/chat`**.
Read from the source, not inferred: `_login` -> 'Session token for /chat', `user = _env_or_dotenv("ADMIN_USERNAME")`; and `.env` sets ADMIN_USERNAME=admin@ontosage.
**SO TAIL N MEASURED `/chat` AS `admin`. USERS GET `/v1/chat/completions` AS A NON-ADMIN, STREAMING.** Two differences at once, and I verified the container, the restart window and the question corpus while never checking the identity the harness authenticated with.

WHAT THIS CHANGES:
  * **Cluster 2 (developer onboarding text, 5 of 60) is NOT a user-facing defect.**     `reader_is_admin()` returns True for `admin` and False for facility_manager, analyst,     operator, occupant, readonly and anything unknown -- measured across every role in     ROLE_PERMISSIONS -- and every deterministic decline producer was called for every     non-admin role with 0 leaks. An admin being shown how to onboard data is the feature     working. **Unacceptable on the admin path therefore drops 28 -> 23 of 60 = 38.3%.**
  * **Clusters 1 and 3 stand.** A false decline (the answer names 'the readings of     humidity' and refuses a humidity question) and a misrouted question (an evacuation     question filed as an URGENT safety report) are not role-dependent.
  * **The zero stands and is the finding I would keep above all others.** No fabricated     figure appeared in 60 unseen real questions. Fabrication does not depend on role or     endpoint.

WHAT IS NOW UNMEASURED, and must not be claimed: the number a REAL USER experiences, on `/v1` streaming as a non-admin. 38.3% is the admin-on-/chat figure. It is a reasonable proxy -- CAVEAT-656 established that the honesty guards live in `_response_node`, inside the graph, so both endpoints get them -- but a proxy is not the measurement.
OWED: re-run tail N with `--v1 --email <non-admin>` and CONFIRM the identity from the orchestrator's own `[forwarded-user]` log line rather than from the command that was typed. That is the check I skipped, and typing a flag is not evidence it was used.
