Title: "This room" / "here" with no room named was guessed at or declined, never asked about
Description: Phase 0 hand re-read (READER-2, docs/phase0/phase0_rerun_read.md class C6b), rows 74, 100, 101, 137. Four unbound deictics, four different wrong moves: row 74 declined outright; row 100 bound "here" to an arbitrary sound sensor and failed to build a series for it (125 s); row 101 read "this room" as the whole building and refused the fetch as reaching 296 sensors; row 137 declined a question about meeting rooms the building instruments. Rows 14 and 137 returned in under 1.5 s, i.e. from a probe that decides before classification.
Root_Cause: No component treated a deictic as an UNRESOLVED referent. The referent gate only knows named things, so a deictic reached whichever lane the classifier picked and each lane did its own worst thing with it. The co-reference rewrite could have bound it in a conversation that named a room, but _is_followup_query carries no spatial-deixis marker, so the rewrite was never even attempted on these shapes.
Fix_Approach: referent_resolver.detect_space_deixis / names_a_specific_space / ask_which_space; a gate in dialogue_agent.detect_intent placed BEFORE every pre-classification short-circuit, which asks which room only when neither the question nor an earlier USER turn named one; _is_followup_query now treats spatial deixis as a follow-up marker so a bound reference is rewritten instead.
Verification: tests/test_a_question_names_its_own_subject.py (63 pass): the four live questions return intent=clarification through the real detect_intent entry point with no LLM call; a room named in an earlier user turn suppresses the ask and the rewrite binds it; an assistant turn listing rooms does not. Title: "Who operates" in any question returns the BUILDING's operator, whatever the question is about
Description: Phase 0 hand re-read class C19, row 14. The WHOLE answer to "For each local, shared or inherited control, who operates, monitors and evidences each component, and what must be tested within this unit?" was "**<building>** - operated by: **<operator>**." (0.85 s, so from the pre-classification capability-triple probe, not from any routing rule).
Root_Cause: building_profile._FACET_PATTERNS maps the bare phrase "who (runs|operates|manages)" to the operator facet, and capability_agent._building_profile_answer calls detect_facet DIRECTLY as the first step of the capability chain - so no routing rule can reach it. The _NOT_PROFILE veto only excludes questions about the building's CONTENTS or live state, not questions whose subject is a component, control, asset or unit.
Fix_Approach: PROPOSED (outside this agent's file allowlist): extend building_profile._NOT_PROFILE so a question whose subject is a sub-part - control, component, asset, equipment, device, system, unit, circuit, room, zone - is not a building-profile question; "who runs this place?" is unaffected. The routing-contract side (_r_building_profile) would inherit the same guard for free because it calls the same detector.
Verification: Not fixed here: building_profile.py and capability_agent.py are owned by other agents this session. Detector behaviour confirmed offline: detect_facet(row 14) == 'operator'.

Title: "Network-I/O pressure" resolves as the measurand PRESSURE and is answered with the building's live figures
Description: Phase 0 hand re-read class C19, row 47. "Which hosts, clusters or hypervisors face sustained CPU, memory, storage-I/O or network-I/O pressure, and which services are exposed?" was answered "**Live building figures for <building>** ... Sensors declared in the building model: 3,248 ... Floors: 8" (34 s). No routing rule fires on this question at all.
Root_Cause: capability_agent gates its live-metrics block on measurand_of(query) OR _is_metrics_question. plausibility.measurand_of matches the word "pressure" inside "network-I/O pressure", so an IT-infrastructure question satisfies the metrics gate and is answered with a building census.
Fix_Approach: PROPOSED (outside this agent's file allowlist): measurand_of must not match a quantity word that is the head of a compound naming something else ("network-I/O pressure", "time pressure", "peer pressure"); failing that, the live-metrics block should require the question to ask about the building's own contents or extent, not merely to contain a measurand. The honest lane for this question is observability, which can say the quantity is not measured here.
Verification: Not fixed here: plausibility.py / capability_agent.py are outside the allowlist. Confirmed offline: measurand_of(row 47) == 'pressure'; no PARSE/POST contract rule claims the question.

Title: A decline names every register the retriever touched, however unrelated to the question

Fix_Approach: Name only the passages the strength test calls MATCH_DISTINCTIVE; when none is, state the boundary with no list. What was searched stays on the evidence record (capability_result["documents"]) and the named subset is added as ["documents_named"].
Verification: capability_agent.py:1030-1056 (the _named subset) + :977-991 (_distinctive kept as a list). tests/test_a_decline_names_only_what_it_searched.py: 15 new unit tests incl. the verbatim row-86 passages. Title: Every register's clock stopped on the day it was authored
Description: The washroom-servicing question reached the right register and read correct rows: 30 CleaningTask records saying lastCompleted 2026-09-03 / nextDue 2026-09-04 for tasks whose serviceFrequency is TWICE DAILY — 26 missed visits on the face of it. Measured across the live graph the same day: lastCompleted newest 2026-09-04 (85 values), statusObservedAt ALL 2026-09-06 (58), completedDate newest 2026-08-26 (97), nextDue oldest 2026-08-30 (111). A reader concludes the system is broken; the lane was correct throughout.
Root_Cause: A register document and its lifted triples carry absolute dates fixed at authoring time. Nothing ages them, and the anchor a generator used is invisible to every reader. The defect is not in any lane — it is that a frozen date is read as a live one.
Fix_Approach: scripts/refresh_record_dates.py: per record, measure staleness against the record's OWN cadence (serviceFrequency / inspectionIntervalDays / the gap the row declares between its last and next columns) and advance by whole cadence periods only. Whole-day shifts, so time of day and the weekday of week-multiple cadences survive and the declared last-to-next gap is preserved exactly. Declared statuses are never rewritten and the run exits non-zero if any count moves. An open record is anchored on its DUE date so it lands still due by the same margin (--freeze-held leaves them untouched instead). Predicates that are not cadenced obligations — calibratedOn, approvedOn, evidenceDate, surveyedOn, isolationProvenOn, locationVerifiedOn, effectiveFrom/To, targetDate — are out of scope by construction and --explain prints why for each.
Verification: --apply on 2026-09-17: 295 date literals across 11 files. Status counts identical before and after in every file (cleaning 24 scheduled/2 suspended/3 added/1 handed over; service 12 active/3 overdue/2 due; fire 24/4/2; coshh 8/2/2; patrol 12 current/3 overdue/1 due/2 unverifiable; waste 22/1/1; av 19 ready/1 failed/1 degraded/1 unevidenced; asset 22 active/2 degraded; compliance 72 done/10 open; amenity 28 operational/8 out_of_service; status 19/1 degraded/2 unverified). Re-run is a no-op (idempotent). All 8 changed registers re-lift offline with unchanged record counts (30/17/18/24/30/12/22/24); all 3 changed TTLs re-parse (564/260/220 triples). 40 unit tests in tests/test_record_dates_roll_by_their_own_cadence.py. Title: A spatial anchor the model left EMPTY counted as an ambiguity and refused a whole-building ranking
Description: Measured live 2026-09-17 after the row-117 compiler fix had landed and the question was STILL refused: "I'm pregnant and overheating - where's the coolest place to work today?" -> "I couldn't map part of your request (coolest place to work today; pregnant)". Replaying the cached compile showed constraints=[('temperature','minimize')] — the compile was right — and signals=[('unresolved_anchor','coolest place to work today'), ('unmapped_term','pregnant')].
Root_Cause: The model emitted in_space with anchor '' for a question that names no space. That became an unresolved_anchor signal; CQIR.is_executable() is false while ANY signal stands, and clarify_policy.absorb_unmapped (which would have dropped and declared 'pregnant', since real constraints existed) returns early whenever a non-unmapped signal remains. One phantom anchor blocked a ranking over every room.
Fix_Approach: A valid space relation with an empty anchor whose phrase names no space (no digit, no capitalised proper name) is the DEFAULT whole-building scope, not an ambiguity; a phrase that does look like a named space still raises the signal, and an unknown relation still does whatever its anchor.
Verification: tests/test_an_empty_anchor_is_not_an_ambiguity.py 8 passed (built from the cached live compile); deliberation/compiler/cqir/clarify sweep 158 passed. LIVE RE-ASK OWED — the fix went in after the restart that served this batch. NOTE: the code comment cites BUG-752, which a concurrent agent had taken for the register-clock fix; this row is the correct id.

Title: Floor energy meters were generated from a cumulative-register band, so week-on-week electricity use read +160.9%
Description: Demo rehearsal 1: 'Compare this week's electricity use with last week' answered 'rose by 20,424 kWh (+160.9%)'. The figure matched the store, so nothing was fabricated — the STORE changed scale. Measured: the six floor submeters averaged 3.4 kWh per 15-minute interval read from 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-16 18:00 UTC, then 30-75 kWh from that moment on (day means 3.4 -> 11.1 -> 51.3). Sample counts per day also swing 96-768, so any raw SUM is partly a count artefact.
Root_Cause: ontosage:ElectricalEnergy declared typicalMax 100 — a CUMULATIVE REGISTER's range — and the floor submeters joined the publish map at that instant, so the generator drew interval reads from a register-sized band.
Fix_Approach: Band narrowed to 0-8 kWh with the measured basis recorded (interval reads ran 1.9-4.9); publish map refreshed (hi=8.0 confirmed for all six meters) and data-publisher recreated. The 594 rows written inside the break were RESCALED per meter to that meter's own pre-break mean by scripts/rebase_energy_interval_reads.py — a constant factor per meter, which keeps the diurnal shape and only moves the scale. Deleting them was rejected: the demo asks about 'yesterday', which falls inside the break.
Verification: Day means after the rebase: 3.19, 3.49, 3.40, 3.33, 3.63 kWh across 13-17 Sep. Publish map hi=8.0. LIVE RE-ASK of both energy questions owed in rehearsal 2.

Title: The intent prompt asks the model for three fields nothing reads
Description: Found by ARCH-01 while deriving a JSON schema from the parser: the dialogue prompt requests export_format, report_type and recommendation_domain; _parse_llm_response reads none of them, so they are generated every turn and dropped.
Root_Cause: Fields added to the prompt when a lane needed them and never removed when the lane stopped reading them.
Fix_Approach: Either consume them or delete them from the prompt; the schema derived in ARCH-01 makes the mismatch visible, so fix it there.
Verification: AST comparison of the prompt's fields against the parser's reads.

Title: The project's quality grader pointed the WRONG WAY: kappa 0.116 against human labels
Description: ARCH-03 calibrated three graders on 294 hand-labelled answers. Old heuristic: accuracy 40.5%, kappa(weird/not) 0.116, WEIRD recall 21.8%. New deterministic grader: 68.0%, kappa 0.419, recall 65.5% at 94.7% precision. DECISIVE: between the two runs the humans read, the humans said quality got WORSE (72.8% -> 76.9% weird); the old grader said BETTER (19.7% -> 13.6%) — opposite direction; the deterministic grader said worse by the same 4.1 points.
Root_Cause: The old grader reads answer SHAPE (digits present, length, phrases). A fluent answer that is untrue about the building has the right shape.
Fix_Approach: scripts/grade_answers_rubric.py replaces it for gating; every quality claim made before 2026-09-17 that rests on the old grader is unsupported and must be restated or withdrawn.
Verification: docs/EVALUATION_CALIBRATION_2026-09-18.md; 48 tests; artifacts in scripts/outputs/rubric_calibration*. The grader's LEVEL is still wrong (51.7% vs the human's 74.8%); only its DIRECTION is calibrated.

Title: Kappa is class-balance sensitive, so graders must be ranked on the SAME rows
Description: ARCH-03: on the 20-row LLM smoke sample (30% weird) the ranking inverted — old 0.583, deterministic 0.524, LLM 0.432 — while on the full 294 rows (74.8% weird) the deterministic grader wins by 0.303. Ranking graders measured on different row sets is invalid.
Root_Cause: Cohen's kappa depends on the prevalence of the class being judged.
Fix_Approach: The script now decides a winner only on rows every grader scored, and says so when that set is a sample. Full LLM-judge calibration over all 294 rows is owed and needs an exclusive GPU slot.
Verification: Measured on both row sets.

Title: The grader's residual misses are one shape: fluent, well-formed, and untrue about the building
Description: 55 of 76 misses by the deterministic grader are answers whose text gives no signal — e.g. a chain-of-custody question declined from the WASTE register. Text alone cannot see this.
Root_Cause: The signal is not in the answer; it is in whether the evidence used matches the subject asked about.
Fix_Approach: Feed the ARCH-02 claim/evidence record into the grader once it lands, and re-measure kappa with it.
Verification: ARCH-03 error analysis.

Title: 8.2% of the figures the system states are not in the evidence it fetched
Description: ARCH-02 measured claim binding offline over the 147-question rerun, using the orchestrator's own per-turn evidence captures: 92 of 147 turns had recorded evidence (71 complete). Of 709 assessed claims, 58 are UNBOUND — 8.2% — spread across 22 of 71 answers (31%). By kind: 43 numeric, 7 universal ('all/every/none'), 8 inference ('so/therefore'). 11 of the 17 hand-read C7 rows are flagged, including the headline defect, which the binder reports as turning 'on terms no fetched field records: ownership…'.
Root_Cause: Nothing checked that the prose says only what the evidence supports; the dossier recorded what was FETCHED, not what was CLAIMED.
Fix_Approach: orchestrator/services/claim_binder.py at the single response chokepoint. Record-only by default; CLAIM_BINDING_ENABLED removes the sentence carrying an unbound figure and says so, and caveats (never deletes) universals and inferences, because a lexical test is strong enough to flag and not to delete prose. No retry: a second LLM call at the chokepoint doubles worst-case latency on a shared GPU with no reason to converge.
Verification: 36 new tests + 372 adjacent pass; measurement script scripts/measure_claim_binding.py and evidence docs/phase0/phase0_rerun_evidence.jsonl. OWED LIVE: one turn confirming the report reaches the evidence record; probe + rehearsal with the flag off, then on. Partial-evidence turns (21) bind at 56% and are reported separately rather than folded in.

Title: A stem alias matched inside another word, so the false-absence guard replaced three good answers with non-answers
Description: Run 3 (147 questions, after the night's fixes): three answers came back as 'I can't complete that request as asked. To be accurate about one thing: this building does have 296 temperature sensor(s)...'. The questions were about authorised TEMPORARY controls, accessible arrangements, and whether bins were handed back as recorded. 'temp' matched inside 'temporary'; the other two matched 'occupant'/'bin' the same way. The calibrated grader caught all three as regressions.
Root_Cause: absence_guard._MODALITY_ALIASES holds stems (temp, humid, occupant, bin) and detect_absence_claim interpolated them with no word boundary; its first pattern also did not require a sensing noun, so 'does not contain any information about X' counted as 'this building cannot sense X'.
Fix_Approach: Alias tokens are now wrapped in (?<![a-z])...(?![a-z]), and the first pattern requires a sensing noun (sensors/readings/measurements/data/points/monitors/meters) after the modality.
Verification: tests/test_absence_guard.py 21 passed including the three live sentences; the BUG-192 defect this guard exists for is still caught. This is the C1 class the hand read flagged, now closed at the detector. LIVE RE-ASK OWED for the three rows.

Title: A forecast below zero was printed as the evidence behind a recommendation
Description: Run-3 row 99: a visitor asking where to sit was answered 'Best match: Room 4.03' with the evidence 'occupancy: -7.719, co2: -260.986'. Minus eight people and a negative carbon dioxide concentration, from the ranking lane's tier-2 forecaster; a least-squares trend on a falling series extrapolates straight through zero.
Root_Cause: The plausibility bands exist and are loaded (physical_bands, 2919 sensors carry one), but the only callers are the two SQL-lane guards, which resolve a band PER UUID. The ranking lane works in modalities, has no SPARQL executor in its signature, and never checked.
Fix_Approach: physical_bands gains an offline, TTL-backed lookup (declared_bands / band_for_measurand / band_for_modality) resolving modality -> Brick class (building config) -> measurand -> band. plan_executor.execute checks every value AFTER the forecast overwrites it, drops the impossible ones, and carries excluded_sentence() on ExecutionOutcome.impossible_readings -> EvidenceDossier -> render_answer. The criterion then reads as a data gap and the scorer renormalizes, as it does for a sensor that returned nothing.
Verification: tests/test_run3_figures_that_cannot_be_true.py (33 tests) + 1255 adjacent unit tests pass. Uses row 99's own values. LIVE RE-ASK OWED.

Title: Every flow point was narrated in m3/s, so a water answer recommended plant off 292 m3/s
Description: Run-3 row 132: 'Floor 4 has the highest mean flow rate (14.2 m3/s) and the highest peak (292 m3/s)' used as the basis for recommending filtration stations and a leak-detection routine. 292 m3/s is a river.
Root_Cause: A UNIT defect, not a data defect. ontology/measurand_kinds.ttl declares WaterFlow in L/min with physicalMax 2000 and config/saturation_modalities.yaml declares L/s; both figures sit inside those bands. The string came from _unit_for_kind in the metadata builder, a last-resort table that returned 'm3/s' for any label containing 'flow' whenever the SPARQL projection did not bind the sensor's class.
Fix_Approach: _unit_for_kind no longer guesses for flow (the coarse kind cannot tell water from air, which the ontology distinguishes); the narration prompt already says to state the unit is not recorded rather than invent one. modality_units.unit_for_sensor now falls back to the measurand's declared physicalUnit where the modality config names none.
Verification: tests/test_run3_figures_that_cannot_be_true.py asserts both of row 132's figures are possible readings of the declared quantity, so the fix is the unit and not the number. LIVE RE-ASK OWED.

Title: The oldest reading was labelled 'Latest snapshot' in the SQL narration lane (BUG-520, second site)
Description: Run-3 row 120: '**Latest snapshot (2026-09-12 17:50:00)**' over a window the same answer described as running to 17 Sep, with 'so the heating circuit is healthy' attached to a five-day-old number.
Root_Cause: BUG-520 was fixed in report_agent._summarize_readings, which this lane does not use. sql_agent._format_results sliced results[:10] in arrival order while telling the model those rows were 'the newest'. The rows are newest-first from ORDER BY timestamp DESC until a privacy resolution clamp sends them through _coarsen, which rebuckets them oldest-first -- and row 120 carried the clamp disclosure.
Fix_Approach: _format_results sorts by each row's own timestamp before slicing, states the newest stamp in the header instead of leaving it to be read off row 1, and instructs the model to reserve latest/current/most recent/snapshot for that reading. Rows with an unreadable timestamp keep their order at the end rather than being promoted by a failed comparison.
Verification: tests/test_run3_figures_that_cannot_be_true.py asserts the header stamp and record 1 are one reading, using row 120's own window. LIVE RE-ASK OWED.

Title: The TBox's own design notes were quoted to readers as answers
Description: Run-3 rows 139 and 146: a person asking about a barometric meter was shown the WasteCollectionPoint rdfs:comment verbatim, including 'what the SYSTEM records it as' and 'makes that disagreement unrepresentable when the disagreement IS the answer'.
Root_Cause: rdfs:comment / skos:example on OntoSage's own record classes are schema documentation written for developers. They arrived in the SPARQL bindings and _format_results passed them into the narration prompt with no distinction from a Brick definition.
Fix_Approach: sparql_agent builds the set of annotations whose subject is in the ontosage namespace inside ontology/, and redacts those exact literals from the bindings BEFORE they become either the prompt or the deterministic fallback. Retrieval is untouched -- a design note is still a legitimate signal for choosing a query. Brick's own definitions are not in the set and still reach readers.
Verification: tests assert row 139's exact comment is recognised and withheld, that a Brick-style definition survives, and that the redaction happens before the prompt is built. Row 146's quote is a SECOND source -- input/documents/av_readiness_register.md, the document lane -- and is NOT covered by this fix.

Title: Internal storage vocabulary in a user-visible decline
Description: Run-3 row 80: '**The building's events store doesn't record that.**' The reader does not know what an events store is; the sentence after it already lists what the building keeps.
Root_Cause: The decline was written in the pipeline's vocabulary rather than the reader's.
Fix_Approach: Reworded to 'This building doesn't keep a record of that.' The read-failure message on both copies (the service and the orchestrator node) now says 'the building's records'. The 'source' provenance key still records the store, which is internal and correct.
Verification: tests assert no reader-facing sentence in the service names a store, and the existing test_event_query_service assertion was updated to the new sentence.

Title: The modality config gives a flow RATE sensor a volume unit, contradicting the ontology
Description: brick:Water_Flow_Sensor is listed under the water_flow modality (unit: L, a volume) which matches before water_flow_rate (unit: L/s), so unit_for_sensor returns 'L' for a rate sensor. ontology/measurand_kinds.ttl declares that class measures WaterFlow in L/min. The file's own comment says water_flow records VOLUME and water_flow_rate the RATE.
Root_Cause: Two declarations of the same thing disagreeing -- config and ontology -- with the config winning by list order.
Fix_Approach: Either drop Water_Flow_Sensor from water_flow.brick_classes, or make the ontology's declared physicalUnit win outright (TTL-first, contract 2). Not done tonight: it changes units across saturation and the coverage audit hours before a demo.
Verification: Found while fixing BUG-764; does not affect row 132, which never bound a class at all.

Title: Claim binding in ENFORCE mode deleted correct figures, because some lanes' evidence never reaches the bus
Description: Enabled live 2026-09-18 00:00 and measured immediately with the 60-case probe: 5 first-pass failures where the answer had been right. 'How many CO2 sensors are there?' lost the number 280 entirely; two deliberation rankings lost 'best match' and their scores. Per-turn logs show unbound rates of 17/19, 99/123, 9/16 on lanes that COMPUTE their figures live (graph COUNT, ranking scores) and never write them to the evidence record in a form the binder reads.
Root_Cause: The binder assesses what it can see. A lane that computes a figure without recording it looks, to the binder, exactly like a lane that invented it.
Fix_Approach: REVERTED to record-only within 25 minutes (CLAIM_BINDING_ENABLED=record). Enforcement must be conditional on the turn having COMPLETE evidence — A2 measured that at 71 of 147 turns — and live-computed counts and scores must be recorded as evidence before it can be switched on.
Verification:
Offline replay over 441 recorded answers (3 bank runs) plus the counts lanes rendered from their real figures: reverted behaviour removes a figure from 58 answers and destroys every count in both counting answers including the 280 the probe asserts; with the recording and the completeness condition, 26 answers lose a figure, ZERO of them hand-read GOOD, and zero probe markers lost. scripts/measure_claim_binding.py --replay-enforcement -> docs/phase0/claim_enforcement_replay.json. 37 new tests + 73 binder tests + 763 adjacent pass. OWED LIVE: probe and rehearsal with the flag still off, then one probe run with CLAIM_BINDING_MODE=enforce, comparing per-turn enforced/withheld counts. The flag has NOT been enabled.
LIVE RE-ASK 2026-09-30, discharging a check owed since 2026-09-17. Caches flushed (`resp_cache:*`, `cache:sparql*`), fresh chat id per question, asked on a HEALTHY orchestrator -- the first attempt failed outright because the process was in the runaway logged as BUG-1194 (40 GiB, unresponsive), which is itself the reason to state the process's state when reporting a live result. Memory held 1.33-1.59 GiB throughout.
Q: 'How many CO2 sensors are there?' -> 14.1 s. The figures are PRESENT, not deleted: a live class census naming 'CO2 Sensor - 280' and 'CO2 Level Sensor - 274' among 3,248 sensors. This row was about claim binding in ENFORCE mode DELETING correct figures and leaving nothing; nothing is missing here.
ONE RESERVATION, recorded rather than smoothed over: the answer gives a class census rather than the single number asked for, and it lists two overlapping CO2 classes without saying they overlap. That is a different (and milder) complaint than this row's and is not treated as reopening it.

Title: Rolling dates forward erased a deliberately designed finding, and left the record contradicting its own note
Description: Probe v20 failed 'Which rarely visited plant areas have the longest blind intervals?': the answer named AEP-016 (338 days) because AEP-017's lastVisited had been rolled from 2025-09-12 to 2026-09-07. AEP-017's own note still read 'THE LONGEST BLIND INTERVAL IN THE BUILDING: last physically visited 2025-09-12 ... a life-safety interlock nobody has looked at in nearly a year', and its locationVerifiedOn stayed 2025-09-12 — so one record carried two different last-visit dates and the designed case was gone.
Root_Cause: scripts/refresh_record_dates.py rolls ontosage:lastVisited as a completion predicate. For an asset whose STALENESS IS THE FINDING, the roll removes the finding; the note is free text and does not move with it.
Fix_Approach: input/documents/asset_engineering_register.md restored to its authored dates. Follow-up (TODO-771): the refresh must not roll a completion date when the row's own note declares that date or an unvisited state.
Verification: Restored file has zero 2026-09-07 tokens and keeps 2025-09-12; re-probe owed.

Title: A date refresh must not move a date the record's own prose cites
Description: Generalisation of BUG-770 and of CAVEAT-754 (six note cells citing pre-roll dates): free text and structured dates drift apart because only the structured ones move.
Root_Cause: The roll is field-level; notes are prose.
Fix_Approach: Skip a row whose note contains the date being moved or declares an unvisited/overdue state, and report those rows as deliberately frozen.
Verification: Found by the probe, not by the tests.

Title: Two probe failures were model variance, not regressions
Description: Probe v20 reported 3 first-pass failures. Re-asked immediately and by hand: the network-contact answer gives the 8-hour target, and the workspace answer names 1.06 and 1.25 — both marked missing by the probe minutes earlier. Only the third (AEP-017) was a real defect (BUG-770).
Root_Cause: Single-ask first-pass measurement over a non-deterministic generator; CAVEAT-500 is the same shape.
Fix_Approach: Keep reporting first-pass failures honestly and re-ask each one before calling it a regression; do not weaken the probe's expectations to match an answer.
Verification: Both re-asks recorded in the session scratchpad.

Title: A data fix stays invisible until the QUERY-RESULT cache is flushed, not just the response cache
Description: After restoring the asset register and confirming the graph held the corrected dates, three consecutive live asks still answered from the old values, and the deterministic register facts listed dates the graph no longer contained. 52 Redis keys under cache:sparql* held the executed query's ROWS (sparql_validator.validate_and_execute(use_cache=True)). Flushing them made the answer correct immediately: AEP-017, 371 days against a 180-day interval.
Root_Cause: Two caches with different keys: resp_cache:* (the answer) and cache:sparql* (the rows). Every runbook and habit in this project flushes only the first.
Fix_Approach: Flush BOTH after any data or ontology change: redis-cli --scan --pattern 'resp_cache:*' and --pattern 'cache:sparql*'. Added to the demo runbook.
Verification: Verified live: same question wrong before the flush, right after.

Title: An alarm-records question is answered 'could not put an answer together' while 270 alarm events are held
Description: Conformance run 2026-09-18 (36 generated questions, asked live as facility01): 'What alarm event records were logged recently?' returned the unanswered fallback in 24 s. The same building answers 'Are there any unacknowledged alarms?' correctly (6 unacknowledged), and the graph holds 270 AlarmEvent instances.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. The events lane answers one phrasing and not the other; 'recently' with no bound may be the difference.
Fix_Approach: Find which lane claims it and why it produces nothing; a question about a record class the building HOLDS must never reach the unanswered fallback.
Verification: Conformance question set events-0x; reproduced once. | RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim, STILL REPRODUCES: 'What alarm event records were logged recently?' -> 'I couldn't answer that from Abacws Building's records. The nearest things I can answer are the Access event, Alarm activation and Interval record records...'. The decline NAMES the register that holds the answer, in the same sentence as the refusal (the Wave B false-decline shape). Verified in the graph: 270 ontosage:AlarmEvent, and every one of the 270 carries effectiveFrom, rdfs:label, alarmCondition, alarmPriority and aboutEquipment, so 'recently' is answerable from fields that all exist. Route: intent=metadata -> metadata, node=sparql, overrides=[]. The companion phrasing this row said worked has REGRESSED -- see BUG-955.

Title: A one-room, one-measurement comparison hits the whole-building fetch refusal
Description: Conformance run: 'How does humidity in Telecommunications Room this week compare with last week?' answered 'more than I can read and summarise in one request'. One room, one measurement, two weeks — the narrowest shape the refusal tells the user to ask for.
Root_Cause: The refusal's breadth estimate does not account for the named space, so a scoped question is measured as if it were building-wide.
Fix_Approach: Scope the estimate to the resolved space before refusing; this is the same family as C2 in the hand reads.
Verification: Conformance question set comparison_over_time-0x. | RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim. The REFUSAL IS GONE: 'How does humidity in Telecommunications Room this week compare with last week?' now answers via intent=compare, with both windows stated ('Mon 28 Sep 00:00 to Wed 30 Sep 05:27 against the same period shifted back') and a differing-basis disclosure (468 -> 311 readings). The breadth estimate no longer refuses a scoped question. A DIFFERENT defect replaces it, logged as BUG-960: the building holds SIX Telecommunications Rooms (Telecom_Room_F0..F5, verified in the graph), the answer silently read all six, and the series labels collapsed to bare digits -- '0 mean: 49.7', '1 mean: 49.5' ... '5 peak: 57.9' -- with no statement that the name was ambiguous or which room each digit is.

Title: The conformance generator built a question from a document HEADING, not a topic
Description: Two of 36 generated questions read 'What does the building's documentation say about About this assignment?' and '... about Lighting?'. The first is a section heading; the second returned 'I don't have that specific information' in 1 s.
Root_Cause: The document question template fills from headings without filtering structural ones.
Fix_Approach: Filter headings that are not topics (about/introduction/scope/contents) and prefer a heading that a reader would ask about; re-generate.
Verification: docs/CONFORMANCE_bldg1_2026-09-17_questions.jsonl rows document_answer-01/02.

Title: The digits inside a measurand name were read as figures, and enforcement deleted the counts beside them
Description: Measured offline on the census this building renders: the 2 of CO2, the 2.5 of PM2.5 and the 2 of NO2 were extracted as the numeric claims 2, 2.5 and 2. No row records them, so in enforce mode the binder deleted the whole bullet each sat in - taking 280, 274 and 245 with it. This is a direct cause of the CAVEAT-769 revert and it is independent of whether the lane records anything.
Root_Cause: The masking pass covered hyphenated equipment codes but nothing covered a digit glued to the letters of a word. A quantity in these answers is always separated from the word before it; a digit that is not, is part of a name.
Fix_Approach: claim_binder._NAME_DIGIT_RE masks a digit run immediately preceded by a letter.
Verification: tests/test_a_computed_figure_is_evidence.py::test_the_digits_inside_a_measurand_name_are_not_a_claim; offline replay keeps all 19 census counts under enforcement (docs/phase0/claim_enforcement_replay.json). OWED LIVE: one probe run with the flag on.

Title: A narrow no-break space between a figure and its unit hid every such unit from the claim binder
Description: The model writes '115 minutes' and '1 hour 55 minutes' with U+202F. _unit_at tests for the space character and then for a letter, and a narrow no-break space is neither, so the figures carried no unit at all. Measured on a correct recorded answer: the duration rule could not see the hour/minute pair and enforcement deleted the 55.
Root_Cause: Typographic dashes were normalised when they shattered dates (the same class of bug); the equivalent space characters never were.
Fix_Approach: claim_binder._SPACES folded into the same same-length translation table as the dashes, so every span still indexes the original string.
Verification: tests/test_a_computed_figure_is_evidence.py::test_a_narrow_no_break_space_does_not_hide_a_unit; 73 binder tests pass.

Title: Two lanes still compute figures the evidence record never sees: the deterministic graph COUNT and the deliberation ranking scores
Description: The counts lanes owned by this workstream (building_metrics, ontology_inventory) now file what they compute. The sparql lane's deterministic COUNT path and the deliberation lane's ranking scores were the other two CAVEAT-769 failures (17/19 and 9/16 unbound on CORRECT answers) and are owned elsewhere. The completeness condition withholds enforcement on both today, so they are safe but unbound - coverage is left on the table, not correctness.
Root_Cause: Each composes its answer without leaving the computed figure on the bus.
Fix_Approach: One call to evidence.computed.record(source, {field: value}) at the point the figure is computed - or leave the COUNT row in sparql_result. Plus: pass the user's question into claim_binder.run(question=state.user_message) at the response chokepoint, so a figure the ASKER stated is not judged as one the building claimed.

Title: The source chip under every answer said 'Building Ontology'
Description: Run 4 hand read: 'ontology' appeared in 9 answers, up from 7. Most were the provenance chip rendered under data answers (*Sources: `Building Ontology`*). A facility manager does not know what an ontology is; the word makes the building's own model of itself look like a system component.
Root_Cause: The chip's label was written for developers (datasource_registry.BUILTIN_PROVENANCE).
Fix_Approach: Label is now 'Building model'. source_id, colour, lookup keys and the synthetic flag are unchanged — only the words a reader sees. Test updated in the same edit.
Verification: tests/test_provenance.py 12 passed, asserting the new label and that 'ontology' does not appear in a chip.

Title: Three 'ontology' phrasings and one passive misattribution got past the output rewrite
Description: Run 4: "the building's ontology", "the current ontology", "the building's ontology data" and "The building's records THAT WERE PROVIDED" — the first pass covered only 'the/this/our ontology' and the active 'you provided'.
Root_Cause: Patterns written from run 3's wording; run 4 produced new surface forms of the same two defects.
Fix_Approach: Determiner list widened to allow a possessive and 'current'; the supplied pattern accepts the passive. A sentence genuinely about the modelling ('we model the building with an ontology') is still left alone, and is pinned by a test.
Verification: tests/test_answer_wording.py — 4 new cases, file green.

Title: A restored register reintroduced a forbidden 'Synthetic demonstration record' disclaimer
Description: Restoring input/documents/asset_engineering_register.md from git to recover deliberately-stale dates (BUG-770) brought back its opening line '_**Synthetic demonstration record** - fictional commissioning figures, not a real O&M file._', which the owner's standing rule forbids in anything a reader can see. tests/test_no_answer_calls_the_data_fake.py caught it.
Root_Cause: A git restore returns the WHOLE file, including text later fixes had removed.
Fix_Approach: Line removed; no other register carries it; the test passes 12/12. When restoring a file to recover data, diff it for prose that later work deleted.
Verification: tests/test_no_answer_calls_the_data_fake.py 12 passed.

Title: A confidentiality question is answered from a boolean that every room satisfies, ignoring the field that separates them
Description: Probe v23 (59/60): 'Which bookable rooms are suitable for a confidential call?' answered 'All 18 of those are also marked as suitable for calls (calls_ok = true) … Therefore every bookable room in the building is suitable for a call', then listed 18 rooms. The probe expects WS-27/WS-28 (rooms 5.17/5.18). Nothing is fabricated — the register does mark 18 calls_ok — but the register ALSO carries a noise profile where 5.17 and 5.18 are the only 'silent' rooms, and two notes that name acoustic separation explicitly (WS-06, WS-10).
Root_Cause: The narration takes the one boolean whose name matches the question and stops; the discriminating field (noise profile) and the free-text notes are not used to rank.
Fix_Approach: When a boolean is satisfied by every record, it cannot be the answer to a question that asks which are SUITABLE: rank on the field that separates them and say which field was used. This is a register-facts computation (ARCH-style), not a prompt instruction.
Verification: LIVE 2026-09-18 08:00, after the suitability computation landed. The answer no longer says 'therefore every bookable room is suitable': it now states that all 18 record calls_ok and that only WS-06 carries the confidential designation, which is literally true — WS-06's note reads 'Acoustically separated; suitable for confidential calls'. It does NOT surface WS-27/WS-28, the only two rooms whose recorded noise profile is 'silent', which is what the probe case expects. PROBE CASE LEFT FAILING ON PURPOSE: the expectation encodes a judgement (silent rooms answer 'confidential') that the data supports a second way (an explicit note), and weakening a probe expectation to match an answer is how a probe becomes decoration. The computation deliberately does NOT hard-code confidential->silent: 'confidential' appears in no noise value, so that mapping would be a building literal wearing a general name and would not survive another building. It belongs in the concept layer (HBCO), not in register facts. || PRIOR: OFFLINE. Computed in register_facts._suitability_lines: a suitability question ('suitable/best/most appropriate/ideal/recommend') first has its SCOPE found from a question word that matches a recorded VALUE - without that scope the check never fires, because calls_ok is true on 18 of the register's 28 records and only uniform inside the 18 the question asked about. Any question-named field that then holds ONE value across the whole scope is reported as unable to rank ('a value shared by all of them is a PRECONDITION, not an answer to which is best; never conclude that every record therefore qualifies'), and every field that DOES separate the scope is handed over with its distinguished records named, smallest group first. On the real lifted register this puts 'groupFriendly: False 2 (WS-27, WS-28)' and 'noiseProfile: silent 2 (WS-27, WS-28)' in front of the narration - the two rooms the probe expects, named twice. A uniformly NEGATIVE field gets the opposite sentence ('none of them records it'), which is the eight computer labs all recording group-friendly false. WHICH field to rank on is deliberately NOT chosen in code: mapping 'confidential' to 'silent' is a concept mapping, and hard-coding one would be a building literal wearing a general name - so the system says the matched field ranks nothing and hands over the separators. 5 unit tests on the real rows; 86 pass across the four register files, 777 across all register-marked unit tests. NOT RE-ASKED LIVE - the probe result is the lead's to measure.

Title: The calibrated grader is gamed by our own new wording: honest declines 42 -> 75 in one night

Title: The register census is printed to the reader on 23 answers, and six regressions are downstream of it

Title: WITHDRAWN: schema-constrained generation WORKS on this model — the negative was a wrong-endpoint error
Description: ARCH-01 acceptance, measured directly against the provider 2026-09-18 05:50 (gpt-oss:20b, Ollama 0.34): a call carrying a JSON SCHEMA in `format` returns 0 response characters with done_reason='stop' in 0.8-1.0 s — with num_predict 512 and 4096, and with think:false. The same prompt WITHOUT a schema answers in 1.6 s. format:'json' (no schema) also produces text. In the 132-ask acceptance run the flag produced 196 dialogue_intent and 27 cqir_compile provider-stage failures and opened the circuit breaker 286 times; no answer broke, because a structured failure falls back to deterministic routing — the system stayed up with its classifier effectively disabled, which is good fault handling and NOT a passing acceptance.
Root_Cause: The grammar constraint appears to conflict with this reasoning model's output format: the model emits a short thinking block and stops without content.
Fix_Approach: Flag left OFF (STRUCTURED_PLAN_ENABLED=false) and the code kept: it is correct, tested, and provider-agnostic. To make constrained decoding real, either serve the model where grammars work (vLLM/TGI with GBNF or outlines), or use a non-reasoning model, or fall back to format:'json' plus the existing validator — each is a measurable experiment, not a preference.
Verification: WITHDRAWN 2026-09-18 by the architecture audit and re-verified by the lead on the live provider. Measured: POST /api/chat with a JSON schema in `format` returns valid JSON ('{"intent":"real_time_temperature_query","entities":[...]}', 83 chars, 38.2 s). POST /api/generate with the SAME schema returns 0 characters (16.3 s) — and /api/generate is the endpoint langchain's OllamaLLM uses and the only one the original test exercised. think:false, which the original row offered as a diagnostic, is what BREAKS it: /api/chat + schema + think:false returns 0 characters. Both remedies the row proposed (serve on vLLM; use a non-reasoning model) are therefore unnecessary, and the third (format:'json' + validator) returns reasoning prose rather than JSON on the endpoint in use. The row's cited acceptance artifact (struct_accept.md.jsonl, 132 asks) was written to a session scratchpad and is NOT in the tree — a negative result presented in a viva needs its raw rows retained like any positive one. ACTION: switch the local client from OllamaLLM (/api/generate) to ChatOllama (/api/chat) and re-run the ARCH-01 acceptance with CQIR_COMPILE_CACHE=false. || ORIGINAL (wrong): Four direct provider calls recorded; acceptance run docs/…/struct_accept.md.jsonl (132 asks, 0 broken, median 9 s — fast BECAUSE the classifier was being skipped).

Title: The calibrated grader's ANSWERED bucket is now inflating too — both buckets are unreliable in the same direction
Description: READER-6: the grader reports 27.9% weird against a hand-measured 65.3%, and agreement has fallen for a fourth consecutive run (weird-or-not 54.4%). Its HONEST_DECLINE bucket holds 69 rows of which 40 (58%, up from 48%) are weird by hand, 19 of them denying something another run-6 answer holds; its GOOD_ANSWER bucket rose 28 -> 37 and 21 of those 37 are weird — the 296-sensor breadth refusals and bare closure lists now score as answers. | CONFIRMED AND WIDENED 2026-09-30 over 1,997 hand labels from 27 paired runs (the row and its fix_approach both speak of 441; there are 1,115 beyond the 882 the calibration audit uses). Pooled precision: GOOD_ANSWER 300/839 = 35.8%, GOOD_DECLINE 169/536 = 31.5%, WEIRD 401/622 = 64.5%; exact 3-way agreement 870/1,997 = 43.6%, weird-or-not 59.7%, kappa 0.190. Title: The headline quality improvement is not statistically significant, and high-confidence defects are flat across all six runs
Description: Paired exact McNemar over the six hand-read label files (n=147, same questions, same method): run1->run6 28 improved / 17 regressed, p=0.135 — NOT significant. run5->run6 5/11 p=0.210. run3->run6 16/16 p=1.000. Title: A register narration can deny a field or record the census itself found present
Description: 38 of 96 weird answers in the 2026-09-18 hand read (run 6) denied something a register actually holds: 'the register does not record whether a shared desk is officially available' over 28 workspace rows that do; 'no field states how the consequence of a leak is minimised' printed above the isolation-point column that names it. Six prompt-wording waves (_term_census_lines in register_facts.py) asked the model not to do this and measurably slowed it without stopping it, because a prompt is a request and the model is free to ignore it -- correct ANSWERING did not move in six waves (9 gained / 11 lost, p=0.82, run1-6 McNemar).
Root_Cause: The model composes the narration freely from a census block that is advisory, not enforced. There was no check run on the FINISHED narration against what the census itself already computed.
Fix_Approach: New function register_facts.false_absence_corrections() (W19, IMPROVEMENT_PLAN_2026-09-18.md Stage 1): recomputes the same term census used to build the prompt (factored out as _census_terms()), splits the narration into blank-line-delimited paragraphs, and for any paragraph that both (a) reads as an absence claim and (b) names a term the census placed in as_field/as_text, APPENDS a system-written correction naming the real field/record -- same pattern as the existing completeness_line() guard, never edits the model's sentence. Deliberately paragraph-scoped and fails open (empty inputs, no absence phrase, or a genuinely absent term all leave the narration untouched). Wired into sparql_agent.py's register-lane narration pipeline, right after completeness_line.
Verification: 6 new unit tests + 118 existing register-lane tests, all pass, 0 regressions. Deployed live via bind-mount restart, both caches flushed. FULL live re-ask complete: 39 questions from the false-absence pool asked as facility01 via /v1 (5 direct + 34 batched). Guard fired 11 times; every firing checked correct against the actual rows returned (zero false positives). On inspection ~5 of the 11 are useful corrections that change answerability; ~6 are low-value (a real but coincidental word match, e.g. 'talk' matching an activity record's own label) -- the guard is precise, not always informative. True conversion rate (weird->good) needs a fresh hand read, not this firing count. 1 unrelated timeout (150s, a large-occupancy-scan question) observed during the batch -- see CAVEAT-793.

Title: A developer tracker id was returned as the whole answer: 'How busy is the building right now?' -> **BUG-606**
Description: Live, unscripted, via /v1 streamed as facility01. The answer body was the token '**BUG-606**' above the usual footers. 250 occupancy streams (15,000 rows) had been fetched correctly.
Root_Cause: The analytics narration prompt ended rule 9 with 'say which property they do carry and stop (BUG-606)'. The prompt was ALSO 64,436 characters against a 16,384-token model, so the model saw only its tail, which held that rule (BUG-802). The tag was the visible symptom; the overflow was the disease.
Fix_Approach: Three layers. (1) prompt_hygiene.strip_tracker_ids at all three LLMManager entry points, so the model never sees a tracker id and source comments keep their citations. (2) prompt_hygiene.scrub_answer in polish_answer, so no answer reaches a reader carrying one; an answer whose body was only a tag becomes an honest fallback and loses its footers. (3) rule 9 reworded: the NUMBER OF SENSORS is not a reading, but a counting sensor's reading IS.
Verification: 20 unit tests (tests/test_tracker_ids_never_reach_a_reader_or_the_model.py), incl. a walk of every id-shaped token in the shipped TTL proving none is mistaken for a tracker id. Live re-ask after deploy: see docs/READINESS_2026-09-18_STAGE2.md.

Title: The W19 note printed internal field names and restated evidence the answer had already shown
Description: Found by reading BUG-792's own live output: 'see dependsOnLift' shown to a visitor (codebook class C3); and 'Where do I put batteries?' cited WCP-017 then received a note saying 'batteries appears in WCP-017'.

Title: Redis conversation state is unbounded by design and was at 99.77% of its cap under allkeys-lru
Description: 2.135 GB of a 2.00 GB cap: ~16,000 harness conversations (some over 1 MB) never deleted, against CONVERSATION_TTL=0. At the cap the next write evicts, first the warm answer cache; sessions and users are evictable too under allkeys-lru.
Root_Cause: Harnesses ask every question in a new conversation and never cleaned up. Separately, in production the number of real conversations is unbounded and each can be large.
Fix_Approach: Cleared the residue (2.135 GB -> 5.7 MB; 5 real chats, 68 sessions, 57 users kept). ask_questions.py now flushes the row cache once per run and purges only the conversations it created. scripts/redis_hygiene.py reports headroom and purges harness-prefixed keys only; --check exits 1 over 60%. OPEN for the owner: the production policy (a conversation TTL, or volatile-lru so sessions cannot be evicted) is a design decision, not made here.
Verification: Hygiene gate: 0.9% after the run. 8 unit tests prove a real chat id never matches a purge pattern.

Title: A narration prompt of 64,436 characters overflowed a 16,384-token model, which then saw only the tail of it
Description: 'How busy is the building right now?' fetched 250 occupancy streams; the analytics ran correctly; the narration prompt held 250 sensor lines and 30 KB of output. Ollama drops from the FRONT of an overflowing prompt, so the question and instructions vanished. The answer was a ticket id (BUG-795), then, with that stripped, 'I'm ready to help'.
Root_Cause: Nothing bounded a narration prompt. The per-floor branch (BUG-537) shortened it only for series that span floors; series without a floor grouping listed every sensor.
Fix_Approach: Three defences. (1) series_summary.summarise_latest_overview: past 40 series the per-sensor block is replaced by a code-computed overview (spread, extremes, zero count; never a total, because a room and its floor can both be present). (2) The fallback listing is capped at 40 with 'and N more'. (3) LLMManager cuts the MIDDLE of any prompt over 2.75 chars per token of the configured window, keeps both ends, and says so in the prompt; hosted providers are left alone.
Verification: 16 unit tests. Live: 'How busy is the building right now?' answered with the busiest room and the spread; 'How many people are in the building at the moment?' answered 133 (six floor counts, rooms not added).

Title: 'How much electricity did the building use yesterday?' reported 17.08 kWh, the sum of the six LATEST readings, over a fetched day of 144
Description: Found while verifying BUG-797. Once the concept resolved and the right meters were fetched, the analytics lane's default stats template printed the latest reading per meter and the narrator added them. The day's total was 513 kWh. A confident wrong figure, worse than the 'no data' it replaced.
Root_Cause: There is no total template: the keywords current/latest/now pick one and this question has none.
Fix_Approach: summarise_energy_totals sums every reading of energy series in summable units (units.aggregation_decision); a power series or a mixed set is never totalled. asks_for_a_total recognises the question by shape and leaves average/latest/peak/compare questions alone. The block carries the span and tells the narrator to state it and to say when it is shorter than the period asked.
Verification: 22 unit tests incl. the exact live shape (6 meters x 24 readings = 432, not 17.08). Live: 513 kWh for yesterday. 'Last month' correctly states a ~11-day span (the store holds about 11 days of energy).

Title: Model-written SPARQL lost its store routing: every sensor read 'Storage: N/A' and the answer said 'no readings available'
Description: 'How many people are in the building at the moment?' found 250 occupancy sensors and answered 'no readings from any of them are available to me'.
Root_Cause: The SPARQL prompt tells the model to bind ref:storedAt as ?database. The UUID-to-store map recognised only a variable containing 'storage'. Only queries that happened to use ?storage (our own repair template) routed correctly.
Fix_Approach: _is_storage_variable accepts both names; a `?store` alias is still not a store (the original regression in test_sparql_projection_contract, whose source-string pin was updated to describe the new reader).
Verification: 17 unit tests. Live: 133 people, by floor.

Title: Modality repair took its 'unknown modality: never guess' exit for a name the catalogue lacks, although the concept resolver had named the class
Description: 'How much electricity...' resolved concept energy_consumption -> brick:Energy_Sensor (six meters) and fetched eight AIR QUALITY sensors; the analytics ran over 'low/medium/high'.
Root_Cause: The wanted modality is inferred from query text ('energy'); the catalogue key is energy_submeter. needs_repair and build_modality_query consulted only the catalogue.
Fix_Approach: modality_repair.classes_for: the catalogue wins whenever it knows the name (nothing that repairs today changes); otherwise the concept-resolved classes are used. Only opens a case that used to do nothing. The orchestrator now passes the resolved classes to the query builder.
Verification: 9 unit tests incl. 'the catalogue wins whenever it knows the name'. Live: repaired to the six meters.

Title: 'Is tap water free somewhere, or do I have to buy bottles?' (a demo-script question) went to the recommend lane and said no sensor tells whether tap water is free
Description: The building has bottle-refill points on every floor and a potability statement.
Root_Cause: The capability route runs before the LLM but declines a question whose content words the amenity's terms do not explain ('free', 'buy'); the LLM then chose recommend.
Fix_Approach: Class-level DrinkingWater terms extended in the building-agnostic TBox: free water, free drinking water, free tap water, bottled water, buy water, buy bottled water, buy bottles. Measured on the 2,960-question corpus and the 124-question guard set: 0 moves, 0 violations.
Verification: LIVE 2026-09-18 on the final build: the scripted tap-water question answers from the bottle refill points in 1-9 s (demo runs 2 and 3, capability lane); 'Is the tap water safe to drink?' answers from the potability triples. The answer does not say 'free of charge' in words. Guard harness 0 moves / 0 violations.

Title: 'Are there any showers in the building?' fell to a generic decline once the deleted document stopped answering it
Description: The authored topic says 'Shower facilities are located on Floor 1'; its terms were the singular 'shower'.
Root_Cause: Single-word terms match whole words; 'showers' matched none. A plural-tolerant matcher was tried in code and REJECTED: it moved 1 corpus question and broke 3 guard questions, including 'Are the lifts working?' (the asset-state lane owns it). Reverted.
Fix_Approach: Plural and phrase forms added to the topic's own terms in the building data (showers, shower rooms, shower cubicle(s), any showers).
Verification: LIVE 2026-09-18: 'Shower facilities are located on Floor 1' in under a second (earlier run); guard harness 0 moves / 0 violations with the data loaded. Not re-asked in the final battery.

Title: A whole-building 'has X been high anywhere this week?' is refused as 'That question reaches 280 sensors'
Description: 'Has CO2 been high anywhere this week?' and 'Plot CO2 for the last 24 hours in the atrium.' (the atrium was not resolved to Room 1.04, so it fell to the whole building). Defect class C2.
Root_Cause: A deliberate budget (V7-T24): reading every row of 280 sensors is slower and, if truncated, wrong. The missing capability is an aggregate the store computes (MAX/exceedance count per sensor) rather than rows.
Fix_Approach: Workaround did NOT hold on the final build: 'Which floor had the highest CO2 this week?' is refused with the same 'reaches 276 sensors' text (guardrail G01). The scripted 'What is the average CO2 on each floor right now?' does work. Real fix: a SQL aggregate lane for exceedance questions.
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30, both phrasings, NO LONGER REPRODUCES. 'Which floor had the highest CO2 this week?' -- the phrasing this row recorded as still refused with 'reaches 276 sensors' -- now answers with a per-floor peak table (Floor 5 1,179 ppm at HVAC Zone 5.05, then 1,163 / 1,143 / 1,143 / 1,131 / 1,129) and states its own basis: 'Based on 276 CO2 sensors on 6 floors ... each sensor's maximum, COMPUTED IN THE STORE'. That is exactly the SQL aggregate lane this row named as the real fix. 'Has CO2 been high anywhere this week?' also no longer refuses (routes to anomaly). Residual, not this row: the anomaly lane reports a 46% DROP as an answer to 'has it been high', and appends uncited norms -- see BUG-832.

Title: 'Which rooms are empty at the moment?' answers with lane jargon
Description: 'I understood the question but could not put an answer together ... could not match moment or empty'. Occupancy sensors exist (250).
Root_Cause: 'Empty' is a FILTER (occupancy = 0), which the ranking compiler cannot express, and 'at the moment' is not recognised as 'now' by the compiler although other lanes recognise it.
Fix_Approach: Workaround did NOT hold: 'Which rooms are occupied at the moment?' and 'How many people are in Room 1.06 right now?' both fail (guardrail G03, G04); 'Which floor has the most people?' says it cannot tell and asks for sensors (G02).
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim. THE LANE JARGON IS GONE: 'Which rooms are empty at the moment?' no longer says 'could not match moment or empty'; 'at the moment' is now recognised and the zero-occupancy FILTER is expressed. (One of two asks returned a 'request took too long' timeout; the other answered, so the timeout is not the row's defect.) But the ANSWER IS WRONG: it states '6 rooms are empty' over '467 sensors', while the store's latest reading per uuid gives 131 of 514 occupancy series at zero (measured in-container, MySQL session pinned +00:00). Logged as BUG-954 (P1) with the companion 'occupied' phrasing, which is wrong by ~190x.

Title: Wayfinding to an amenity or a room type misroutes: lifts, computer labs, 'nearest accessible toilet'
Description: 'How do I get to the lifts from the entrance?' asks for a room number; 'Which floor are the computer labs on?' returns a prose topic with no floor; 'Where is the nearest accessible toilet?' returned ranking jargon in one run and a floor-based answer in another.
Root_Cause: The lay-term capability route and the deliberation lane claim these before a spatial lookup does.
Fix_Approach: Partly holds: 'Where are the lifts?' answers (G05, lift printed twice); 'Which rooms are computer laboratories?' answers with facility descriptions and no room list (G06).
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30, all three phrasings. TWO OF THREE NO LONGER REPRODUCE: (1) 'How do I get to the lifts from the entrance?' no longer asks for a room number -- it names Passenger Lift 1 and Passenger Lift 2 / Goods Lift, says which floor they serve, and states honestly that the catalogue records floors not distances. (2) 'Which floor are the computer labs on?' no longer returns a prose topic with no floor -- it answers floors 1, 2, 3 and 4 with the room numbers (1.06-1.09, 2.07-2.08, 3.05-3.06, 4.05-4.06). THE THIRD STILL FAILS, in a new shape: 'Where is the nearest accessible toilet?' now DECLINES outright ('I couldn't answer that from Abacws Building's records'), and the decline offers 'Accessible route' records in the next sentence. The graph holds 12 ontosage:AccessibleToilet and 16 AccessibleRoute, so the absence is false. Note the FLOOR-SCOPED form now works (see BUG-827), so it is the unscoped form that declines.

Title: Maintenance and asset-history questions: false absence, an add-data instruction, fragments, raw dumps
Description: 'Which assets are overdue for maintenance?' -> 'records do not contain any information about maintenance status' plus 'you'll need to add a maintenance-related property' (133 s); 'When was the lift last serviced?' -> 'I don't hold a specific date' above a raw dump of rows that carry dates; 'Are there any open faults?' -> '4 still open.'; 'who do I tell about a flickering light?' -> generic decline though a department register holds Estates contacts.

Fix_Approach: Workaround did NOT hold: 'Which maintenance tasks are overdue?' says the records hold no maintenance information (G12). The scripted register questions are the only tested form. Largest remaining source of weird answers (W20/W23).
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30, all four phrasings. (4) 'who do I tell about a flickering light?' still declines generically ('please contact your building's facilities / estates management team') and then offers Fire safety asset records. The graph holds a 20-row Department register including 'Mechanical and Electrical Maintenance' and 'Estates Operations', AND ontosage:MaintenanceIssue Issue_BrokenLight 'Broken or faulty light' -- so both halves of the answer exist and neither was read. Title: Out-of-scope questions are handled inconsistently: a financial-advice paragraph, and a weather forecast that asks 'which city?'
Description: 'Should I buy Bitcoin?' answered from general model knowledge, unlabelled (98 s). 'What's the weather forecast for tomorrow?' asked for a location as though it could forecast anywhere.
Root_Cause: The general_knowledge and clarification lanes do not decline out-of-scope requests (defect classes C11, C12).
Fix_Approach: Not fixed. Boundary questions in the demo script (privacy, actuation, absence, report intake) are unaffected.
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30, both phrasings, NO LONGER REPRODUCES. Both now route to a new scope_boundary lane and decline in scope, labelled. 'Should I buy Bitcoin?' -> 'I can't advise on investments or other financial decisions. I'm the assistant for Abacws Building...' (the unlabelled financial-advice paragraph is gone). 'What's the weather forecast for tomorrow?' -> 'I don't hold a weather forecast. Abacws Building's outdoor sensors report what the weather is doing NOW -- outdoor temperature, outdoor humidity, wind speed and solar irradiance -- not what it will do tomorrow', and suggests the answerable form. It no longer asks which city. That decline is also correct against the new Open-Meteo feed (CAVEAT-844): the feed carries current conditions, not a forecast.

Title: 'Is there a quiet room I can use?' calls 26 rooms quiet because each has a quietest-period field
Description: The presence of a field is not a verdict; computer labs are listed as quiet.
Root_Cause: Register narration infers a property from a field that merely exists (class C7).
Fix_Approach: Not fixed.
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim: the SYMPTOM reproduces exactly (26 quiet rooms, computer labs among them) -- but THIS ROW'S STATED ROOT CAUSE IS WRONG and must not be fixed as written. It says the narration 'infers a property from a field that merely exists'. It does not. The register carries an explicit ontosage:noiseProfile, and its literal value for the computer labs IS 'quiet': WS-02 'Level 1 computer lab 1.06' noiseProfile=quiet, WS-03/04/05 likewise; only WS-01 (Atrium open study) and WS-19 (Staff common room) read 'conversational'. The answer reports the field faithfully and even names the two exceptions. So this is an OWNER DATA DECISION (Wave H), not a narration defect: either the register's noiseProfile for teaching labs is wrong, or calling a computer lab quiet is acceptable. Residual narration defect, small: the answer says 26 quiet rooms 'that you can use' and only later admits it cannot see availability or permission.

Title: 'How much water did we use this week?' gives a flow rate in m3, says it cannot answer, and tells the reader to install a meter
Description: The energy total is now computed in code; water has no cumulative meter and flow readings are rates.
Root_Cause: No cumulative water series; flow-rate units (see W09).
Fix_Approach: Confirmed on the final build (G13): flow rate only, 'integrate the flow rate ... or add a volume-measuring sensor'. The energy total is right.
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim. TWO OF THREE SYMPTOMS GONE: the m3 flow-rate units are gone (now litres/day), and the 'integrate the flow rate ... or add a volume-measuring sensor' instruction to the reader is gone. It now answers '177 litres/day latest, mean 256.5, median 262, min 157, max 341' and states plainly 'these figures show the spread of daily usage but do not provide a weekly total', under a 'Boundary: not declared' caveat that says it cannot say what the meter covers. So the dishonesty is fixed; the question is still not answered, which is the data fact this row records. Two residuals: the closing sentence repeats the opening one verbatim, and the statistics are over 823 readings for a question that named ONE WEEK -- the named window was ignored (BUG-939's mechanism).

Title: 'What can you tell me about this building?' answers with a list of measurand names

The measurand list (pm1, tvoc, lighting cct ...) is gone; the observability lane no longer claims this question.

Title: Answer latency: p50 ~25 s, p90 ~45 s, and single answers of 99-192 s
Description: Demo-script read: p50 25 s, p90 45 s, max 99 s. Tail A: 5 answers over 60 s, 2 over 120 s (192 s for a two-floor comparison, 133 s for an overdue-maintenance question). The hourly anomaly sweep, which runs ~5 min from 3 min after every boot, roughly doubles latency while it runs.
Root_Cause: A 20B local model on one GPU; some lanes make three model calls.
Fix_Approach: Declared, not fixed. For a recording: restart 15+ minutes before, check the sweep is not running, warm the slow questions.

Title: The control lane lists internal writable point identifiers to the role that may write them
Description: 'Open the windows on floor 3' and 'Turn off the lights in Room 1.06' answer 'Nothing has been queued ... the points this building lets me write are: AHU-F5-SP, LIGHTING-3F-SP, VAV-501-SP'.

Fix_Approach: Declared. Say on camera that actuation needs a named point and value.

Title: The demo-script question 'Is tap water free somewhere, or do I have to buy bottles?' was still answered as a room-booking question after BUG-549 was fixed
Description: BUG-549 taught the events rule and the event service that 'free' can mean no cost. The capability route's veto in dialogue_agent imported the raw EVENTS_RE and had no such exclusion, so the same sentence was vetoed as a booking question and never reached the amenity route. Found by reading which of nineteen vetoes fired (demo rehearsal run 1, item 3).
Root_Cause: Two consumers of one question ('is this a booking question?') each held their own answer; the fix for one did not reach the other.
Fix_Approach: routing_contract.events_question(query) is now the single predicate: COST_SENSE_OF_FREE_RE without booking vocabulary is not a booking question. The events rule and the capability veto both call it; a test pins that neither may use the raw regex again.
Verification: Live 2026-09-18 on the final build: tap-water question -> capability lane (bottle refill points, 2 s); 'Is the tap water safe to drink?' -> capability; 'Is Room 1.06 free for the next two hours?' -> events lane. 12 tests in test_the_capability_route_and_the_events_rule_agree_on_free_of_charge.py; guard harness 124 questions, 0 moves, 0 violations.

Title: The 'Also recorded in this register' note restated what the answer had just said, in different word order
Description: Scripted HVAC answer ended 'exception - recorded as approved exception; approved - recorded as approved exception' under bullets that began 'Exception approved'.
Root_Cause: The 'answer already shows the field' test was a contiguous substring: 'approved exception' is not in 'Exception approved'.
Fix_Approach: register_facts._answer_names_field: every word of a multi-word field name present in the positive text counts as shown. A negative test pins that one word of two is not enough.
Verification: scratchpad verify_final (11 questions, final build, read by hand); the HVAC question now answers with a clean table and no note. 2 new tests in test_a_denied_register_field_gets_corrected.py.

Title: 'Compare this week's electricity use with last week', asked on a Friday, reported a 34-36% FALL from comparing five days with seven
Description: Answered 'fell by 4,318 kWh (-34.1 %) ... an unintended outage'. Week 38 held five days of readings, week 37 seven; per day the two were within 5%. Present in both demo rehearsals; run 1 was labelled GOOD in error.
Root_Cause: The partial-bucket test keeps anything above 60% of a typical bucket and does nothing with two buckets, so the shorter current week survived and its smaller total was read as a change.
Fix_Approach: series_summary.summarise_periods measures each bucket's real time coverage; for ENERGY, when an endpoint bucket covers under 90% of its nominal length the change is compared as a rate per day (per hour for a day) and the narrator is told the bucket is in progress. Means are untouched.
Verification: scratchpad verify_final (11 questions, final build, read by hand); now 'Daily average electricity use fell by 86.2 kWh per day (-4.7 %) ... 2026-W38 covers only 117 of 168 hours'. 9 new tests; the existing period-summary tests pass unchanged.

Title: Booking answers printed 'Room1.06' and 'Room2.13' without the space
Description: The room's graph local name has no space; the same room is 'Room 1.06' everywhere else.
Root_Cause: The resolved id was printed as the display name.
Fix_Approach: event_query_service._room_name applies at the four print sites; the id that keys the booking lookup is unchanged.
Verification: scratchpad verify_final (11 questions, final build, read by hand); 'Room 1.06 is free for the next 2 hours' and 'Room 2.13 is free right now'. 7 new tests; 220 events/booking tests pass.

Title: 'The toilet on floor 2 is leaking.' was filed with no location and answered 'I couldn't tell where this is'
Description: The orchestrator already recognised that the message names a place (so it did not ask), but never passed that place to the report; recurrence tracking loses every report filed this way.
Root_Cause: The 'do not ask where' decision and the stored location were two separate decisions.
Fix_Approach: WorkflowOrchestrator._stated_place keeps the room code, floor or named space the reporter wrote; nothing is invented when none was named.
Verification: scratchpad verify_final (11 questions, final build, read by hand); the confirmation now shows 'Location: floor 2' and no request for it. 11 new tests, including one that ties the ask-logic and the record-keeping together.

Title: 'Which rooms have the worst air quality right now?' returned the room with the LOWEST CO2: the best air in the building
Description: Held-out tail B item 3: top room 692 ppm CO2, below the building average of ~850. Assumptions line read 'worst air quality scored as minimize co2'.
Root_Cause: deliberation.compiler._fold_air_quality always minimised, ignoring the question's own words.
Fix_Approach: The fold reads the phrase: worst / poorest / unhealthiest / most polluted -> maximise both pollutants; anything else as before.
Verification: scratchpad verify_final (11 questions, final build, read by hand); now 'scored as maximize co2 ... maximize pm25', top room 833 ppm. 7 new parametrised tests (the model's own direction is varied both ways per case). The routing guard harness was not re-run for this change: it does not touch routing.

Title: The correction note printed 'service - appears in ?, ?' and repeated words the answer had just used
Description: Under a correct 'no lifts out of service' answer, and under a planned-maintenance table that had just listed the two events.
Root_Cause: Records with no identifier are cited as '?'; and a text term the answer already uses outside a denial was still corrected.
Fix_Approach: A note with no identifier the reader can look up is not printed; a term the answer uses outside a denial counts as shown (same rule as status values).
Verification: scratchpad verify_final (11 questions, final build, read by hand); the lift-status and planned-maintenance questions are clean. 2 new tests.

Title: Room-level and occupancy questions are answered 'the building model only records how many sensors are installed'
Description: 'How stuffy is Room 1.06 at the moment?' and 'Which rooms are occupied at the moment?' answer that real-time readings are not stored, sourced only to the building model. Hourly readings and named occupancy sensors exist (tail B item 9 and the demo's per-room answers).
Root_Cause: Unverified. Likely: the model-written SPARQL is a COUNT over sensors, so no time-series id comes back; the modality repair does not run when no measured quantity is inferred from the words, and a room-bound repair is exactly where a wrong-subject answer would be produced.
Fix_Approach: Not fixed. A repair must bind to the room asked, never the building. Ask the named quantity and a scripted room instead.
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30, both phrasings. PART 1 NO LONGER REPRODUCES: 'How stuffy is Room 1.06 at the moment?' answers 746 ppm CO2 from that room's own sensor at 05:35:27 today, with 60 readings over the last five hours (742 mean, 704-768) -- the 'the building model only records how many sensors are installed' answer is gone, and the repair binds to the room asked, which this row said was the risk. PART 2 CHANGED AND IS NOW WRONG: 'Which rooms are occupied at the moment?' answers 'Two rooms are occupied' while the store shows 383 of 514 occupancy series non-zero at their latest reading. Logged as BUG-954 (P1).

Title: 'What will the temperature be tomorrow in Room 2.01?' answers 'No sensor data available for forecasting ... try a sensor with recent data (e.g. temperature)'
Description: Room 2.01 has a temperature sensor with current readings; the forecast lane found no series and then recommended asking for what was asked.
Root_Cause: Unverified: sensor binding in the forecast lane for a room referent.
Fix_Approach: Not fixed.
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim. THE BINDING FAILURE IS GONE: 'What will the temperature be tomorrow in Room 2.01?' no longer says 'No sensor data available for forecasting' -- it binds Air Temperature Sensor installed-node 2.01, fits Linear Trend against SeasonalNaive on a 20% hold-out (SeasonalNaive wins, MAE 0.194 C), reports walk-forward measured skill (MAE 1.4047 C at ~24h, raw 95% interval covered 0.6448 of actuals so intervals widened x2.12) and gives hourly predictions with CIs. The self-defeating 'try a sensor with recent data (e.g. temperature)' recommendation is gone. RESIDUAL: the question said TOMORROW and the horizon starts 2026-09-30 05:00 -- it forecasts today. Logged as BUG-961.

Title: Amenity and location questions ignore the floor or the kind asked
Description: 'Where are the toilets on floor 2?' lists toilets on floors 0, 1, 3 and never says none is recorded on floor 2; 'Which floor is the server room on?' returns a menu of floors; 'What's the biggest room?' returns a 354-row unsorted table; 'nearest lift to Room 4.01' says none on that floor and lists two records that are not lifts; 'nearest accessible toilet on floor 1' asks for a starting point.

The 354-row unsorted table is gone and the superlative exists. (4) 'What is the nearest lift to Room 4.01?' no longer says none is on that floor and no longer lists non-lifts -- it names both lifts, says they serve floor 4, and declines the distance ranking honestly. Title: Wrong lane or wrong window for 'this week', 'this afternoon' and 'when' questions
Description: 'Has anything been reported broken this week?' answers from a 2 September asset record; 'Which meeting rooms are booked this afternoon?' answers from a register of six August-September bookings instead of the live booking store; 'When is the atrium busiest?' ranks rooms by current occupancy.

(3) STILL FAILS, in a new shape: 'When is the atrium busiest?' no longer ranks rooms by current occupancy -- it now DECLINES, 'There is no occupancy measurement for the atrium (Room 1.04) recorded for this building, so I have nothing to read', and then lists 'occupancy status' among what the atrium DOES record, two sentences later. Title: A confident compliance conclusion the records do not support
Description: 'Is the building up to date with its fire safety inspections?' answers 'up to date ... none are overdue' from the inspection-schedule register while the fire-safety asset register shows FSA-027 overdue (due 2026-05-05, no evidence).
Root_Cause: One register answers for the whole subject.
Fix_Approach: Not fixed. The scripted fire-safety question names the overdue asset correctly.
Verification: RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim, NO LONGER REPRODUCES, and VERIFIED AGAINST THE GRAPH.
