The drop to 32 percent followed class-level gates (false-existence rewrite, answer-shape guard, lane-misfire rules, question-names-its-quantity).
Root_Cause: Sets differ; one reader; small n (each interval about +/-12 points).
Fix_Approach: Quote the most recent unseen set and the pooled figure, never a tuned-on set. Draw a fresh set (tail I exists, unread) before each verdict.

Title: The answer-relevance gate failed open on every call because schema-constrained generation returned an empty completion
Description: First live run of tail K with the gate on: 32 judged calls, 0 replacements. Direct probe in the container: 'LLM [fast] returned an empty completion (prompt was 187 chars)', three retries, circuit breaker CLOSED -> OPEN. The gate correctly failed open, and did nothing.
Root_Cause: generate_structured passes a JSON schema as `format` to the local reasoning model; the constrained decoder and the model's thinking share one token budget and the content comes back empty. The offline experiment had used the raw chat API with think=low, which is why it worked there.
Fix_Approach: The gate now uses plain llm_manager.generate with a one-line 'LABEL | reason' reply and a tolerant parser (parse_verdict, also reads JSON and bare labels). The question is put on ONE line after its label, which also removes a false 'EMPTY question slot' warning (the label alone on a line matched llm_manager's empty-slot heuristic). 55 tests.
Verification: Live: gate probe judged 2 of 3 with correct labels in about 1 s each; tail K re-run replaced 9 answers.

Title: The relevance gate removes a modest share of unacceptable answers: measured, not assumed
Description: Offline (tails D-I, untuned): the judge flags 50% of weird answers over every lane but 12% of good ones; restricted to data lanes it catches 48/149 weird and replaces 2/111 good. Out of sample on tail J: 7/30 weird caught, 1/12 good replaced (weird 48.4% -> 37.1%). Paired live on tail K (same 62 questions, gate off then on): fixed 3 of 17 weird answers, replaced 0 good answers, swapped 6 declines for other declines.
Root_Cause: The register and document lanes hold half of the remaining weird answers and are deliberately not gated (the judge flags 7 of 62 good register answers). One replacement recycled the weather text through the decline path.
Fix_Approach: Kept on by default for the data lanes (ANSWER_RELEVANCE_GATE, ANSWER_RELEVANCE_GATE_LANES, ANSWER_RELEVANCE_TIMEOUT_S). Owed: skip the new standard declines ('I couldn't tie that question to a reading', 'the X register (N records) cannot answer this') so they cost no call.

Title: A safety-critical AED position is asserted as fact while the same record calls it modelled
Description: Asked 'Where is the nearest defibrillator?' through Open WebUI the system answered 'Defibrillators (AEDs) are located at reception and on floors 3 and 5' with an emergency phone number. The record bldg:Cap_first_aid in <building>_capabilities.ttl carries ontosage:locationText 'Defibrillators are modelled at reception, floor 3 and floor 5' - 'modelled' - while its ontosage:answerText states the same positions as fact. The answer path surfaces answerText, so the hedge never reaches the reader.
Root_Cause: answerText and locationText disagree and nothing reconciles them; the record carries no ontosage:isSimulated true, so neither the honesty path nor owner_facts_report.py can see it is a placeholder. The comment block immediately above the record states the opposite rule ('an unverified amenity is a fabrication').
Fix_Approach: Either flag the record ontosage:isSimulated true so it is declined/qualified, or have the owner confirm the three positions and rewrite locationText to drop 'modelled'. Until then it must not be presented as evidence. Building-agnostic guard: refuse to surface answerText for a safety-critical category whose locationText hedges (modelled/assumed/placeholder/example).
Verification: Fixed as a DATA fix under D1 (owner confirmed the three positions 2026-09-29); no isSimulated flag was reintroduced. FINDING: the positions were never wrong - bldg:AED_Reception/AED_Floor3/AED_Floor5 have carried brick:isPartOf to Room0.01/Room3.17/Room5.26 since they were declared, and all three rooms resolve. Only the prose hedged. locationText and answerText now name those rooms; the record gained ontosage:locatedIn (3) + ontosage:aboutEquipment (3) and the three devices gained additive ontosage:FirstAidPoint/Amenity typing with locatedIn + onFloor, following the bldg1_lifts.ttl precedent, so amenity_proximity can answer 'nearest' from triples instead of prose. VERIFIED LIVE against GraphDB http://localhost:7200/repositories/bldg: the position query returns exactly 3 rows - AED_Reception/Room0.01 'Room 0.01 - Main Reception'/Floor0, AED_Floor3/Room3.17 'Room 3.17 - Staff Common Room'/Floor3, AED_Floor5/Room5.26 'Room 5.26 - Staff Break Room / Kitchen'/Floor5. The new TTL is not yet in the repository (no restart permitted); the amenity-lane query was run over the edited TTL offline and returns all 3 devices with locatedIn + onFloor. validate_dangling_references(input) = ok, 0 issues. Pinned by tests/test_the_defibrillator_record_and_its_answer_agree.py (19 tests); reverting the old locationText fails 4 of them.

Title: owner_facts_report.py reported the defibrillator fact MISSING while the system answers it
Description: docs/OWNER_FACTS_CHECKLIST.md listed 'Defibrillator (AED)' as MISSING. The live system answers the question from bldg:Cap_first_aid, which is typed ontosage:FirstAidPoint and carries 'defibrillator, aed' in ontosage:layTerms.
Root_Cause: assess() matches on class local names only ([Defibrillator, AedPoint, AED]). An instance that holds the fact under a different class, or only in layTerms/locationText, is invisible to it - so the checklist says 'not recorded' for a fact that IS answered, which is the more dangerous direction of error.
Fix_Approach: Match on layTerms and locationText as well as class, and report a record whose locationText hedges as PLACEHOLDER even without ontosage:isSimulated. Stays building-agnostic: all three are ontology fields, not building literals.
Verification: Reproduce: python scripts/owner_facts_report.py then compare with the live answer to 'Where is the nearest defibrillator?'

Title: A 'coolest place to work' question was answered with a workspace-profile register dump
Description: Asked 'Where's the coolest place to work in the building right now?' the system returned the 28 workspace profiles grouped by kind (bookable room, computer lab, open study) and their floors. 'Coolest' is a temperature superlative; no temperature appears in the answer.
Root_Cause: The register lane claimed the turn on the words 'place to work' / 'workspace' before the comfort-superlative reading was considered. The same question scoped to a floor ('coolest place to work on floor 5') is a demo-script case that answers correctly, so the miss is the building-wide form.
Fix_Approach: Add a routing_contract rule so a comfort/quantity superlative (coolest, warmest, quietest, stuffiest) keeps the turn on the deliberate/sensor lane even when workspace words are present; order it AFTER the register rule it corrects (all rules run, last wins).
Verification: Evidence: docs/supervisor_evidence/screenshots/05_*.png; contrast with the floor-scoped demo-script case | RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim, NO LONGER REPRODUCES. 'Where's the coolest place to work in the building right now?' now routes to intent=deliberate and ranks by TEMPERATURE: Room 5.50 21.442 C (score 0.7597), Room 2.52 21.546, Room 5.51 21.572. The 28 workspace profiles grouped by kind are gone. It also discloses the reading it took ('coolest place to work' scored as minimize temperature against the 20-26 band), the coverage (195 of 234 spaces, 39 excluded and listed), a sensitivity check (stable under +/-25% weight change), an evidence dossier with source tables, AND a permission caveat that the top three are laboratories someone else holds. The building-wide form now behaves like the floor-scoped demo case this row contrasted it with.

Title: Availability consulted ad-hoc bookings only, so a timetabled room reported itself free
Description: 675 ontosage:TimetabledSession records across 44 rooms sat in the graph and nothing read them. 'Is Room 2.15 free this morning?' answered from the booking store alone.
Root_Cause: event_query_service._availability_check queried only the events store. The timetable had been lifted from input/bldg1_timetable.csv into the graph but no reader existed.
Fix_Approach: New orchestrator/services/room_schedule.py expands the weekly pattern over the asked window using the EXISTING vocabulary (timeProfile/startsAt/endsAt/locationText); _availability_check merges it with bookings. A building with no timetable is now answered 'no timetable is recorded', never 'free'.
Verification: 29 unit tests (tests/test_room_schedule.py); live: 'Is Room 2.15 free this morning?' -> 'timetabled Mon 09:00-11:00 (Applied Software Engineering)'. Evidence: docs/supervisor_evidence screenshot 26.

Title: Only two accessible WCs were recorded for the whole building, sending a wheelchair user to the wrong floor
Description: 'What is the nearest accessible toilet to room 3.10?' answered 'none on 3.10's floor; the nearest is Floor 4'. The building has two accessible gender-neutral toilets on every floor.
Root_Cause: The accessibility register held simulated accessible_wc records for floors 0 and 4 only, and the amenity catalogue placed one placeholder toilet per floor into arbitrary rooms (one in a Mechanical Plant Room).
Fix_Approach: Surveyed provision recorded in input/<id>_washrooms_and_water.ttl: per floor one male block (5 cubicles), one female block (5), two accessible gender-neutral toilets. Placeholder toilet/water amenities and their orphaned status records removed.
Verification: Live re-ask: 'The accessible toilet nearest 3.10 is on the same floor.' Evidence: docs/supervisor_evidence screenshot 13.

Title: New vocabulary was invented three times for facts the ontology already modelled
Description: A first pass added ontosage:TimetabledSession (already declared, 675 instances), dayOfWeek/startTime/endTime/inSpace (duplicating timeProfile/startsAt/endsAt/locationText) and isWheelchairAccessible (duplicating accessibilityVerified). Each was removed.
Root_Cause: The schema is 3,800 lines and the existing terms were not grepped for before adding. isWheelchairAccessible was the costly one: six floors of accessible toilets were recorded and none could be found, because amenity_proximity reads accessibilityVerified.
Fix_Approach: Grep the schema AND the live graph for an existing class or property before declaring one. A duplicate term is worse than a missing one: it splits a register in half and each half looks complete.
Verification: Schema re-parsed at 3,534 triples with one TimetabledSession declaration and one sessionKind; 0 occurrences of isWheelchairAccessible remain.

Title: A typographic apostrophe from the browser changed the route
Description: 'Where's the coolest place to work' reached the deliberate lane from the CLI and the workspace register from Open WebUI. The browser sends a curly apostrophe; every pattern in routing_contract is written with the ASCII one, so DELIBERATE_RE matched one and not the other.
Root_Cause: apply_contract built its context from the raw query. Patterns across the whole contract assume ASCII quotes, so the divergence hit every rule at once and only showed up where the users are.
Fix_Approach: normalise_quotes() applied once when the rule context is built, so every rule sees the same text whatever the keyboard or browser produced.
Verification: tests/test_routing_contract.py::test_the_same_question_with_a_typographic_apostrophe_routes_identically; live: both forms now reach deliberate.

Title: A 'coolest place to work' question was answered from the workspace register
Description: Asked 'Where's the coolest place to work in the building right now?' the system returned the 28 workspace profiles and no temperature. Now: rooms ranked by live temperature, with the reading beside each. [renumbered from BUG-860 on 2026-09-29: four parallel agents issued that number twice]
Root_Cause: TWO causes, and the first hid the second. 'coolest' was in no HBCO lay term (the register held warmest/hottest/coldest), so no measurand resolved and nothing contradicted the classifier's guess that a question mentioning 'place to work' belonged to the workspace register. Even once the concept resolved, no rule took a live superlative off a record lane.
Fix_Approach: services/semantic_concept_match.py resolves a lay word against the ACTIVE building's own concepts when no term matches; a new concept-stage rule (measured_superlative_beats_a_register) moves a live superlative about a resolved measurand to the deliberate lane.
Verification: 23 unit tests for the matcher, 4 for the rule; live 8/8 on a lay-term battery. Evidence: docs/supervisor_evidence screenshot 05.

Title: A model asked to choose from a list will reach for the nearest option rather than decline
Description: The concept matcher mapped 'what is the radiation level' to solar irradiance and 'is there smoke in the lab' to an emergency exit. Both produced honest-SOUNDING answers to a question nobody asked, which is worse than declining.
Root_Cause: Selecting from ~90 options is a recall task the model does well; declining is a precision task it does badly. Prompt hardening alone fixed 3 of 5 trap cases and left 2.
Fix_Approach: A second, narrow yes/no confirmation of the single chosen pair ('is X the quantity that was asked about?'), which the model answers well. An unconfirmed match is discarded, so the honest 'not measured' decline still fires. 8/8 after.
Verification: tests: a_near_miss_is_rejected_at_confirmation, an_unclear_confirmation_is_not_a_match; live: radiation and smoke both decline.

Title: A floor-scoped deliberation question breaks when a DURATION phrase is added
Description: 'Find me a quiet, well-lit room on floor 3 for two hours of focused work this afternoon' returns the generic register decline. Removing any one part answers: 'on floor 3.' works, 'for two hours of focused work this afternoon' works, 'on floor 3 this afternoon' works. Only the full combination fails, reproducibly (4 runs). | 2026-09-23: flapped TWICE IN ONE NIGHT on an unchanged build -- passed the answerability gate at ~01:17 and failed it at ~04:22, both as index 12. That kills the tidy 'fails after 22:47' reading in the root-cause column: it is intermittent, not a clean function of the hour. The reply is the generic REGISTER decline ('the nearest things I can answer are the Workspace profile...'), i.e. the deliberation lane is not producing the answer, not producing a bad one.
Root_Cause: NARROWED 2026-09-23 (second session), with the relevance gate no longer hiding it. The turn logs: '[deliberate] building=bldg1 query=...', then coverage_audit 234 spaces / 39,119 located points, then capability_schema '234 spaces, 53 located amenities' -- and then 'Executing response node'. There is NO compiler line and NO '[deliberate] answered: ranked=N'. The lane builds its schema and returns without ranking. The register decline the reader sees is the relevance gate replacing whatever the lane did return (OFF_TOPIC, 'does not address the request for a quiet, well-lit room'), so the gate is a SYMPTOM here, not the cause. RULED OUT: (a) a missing modality -- illuminance is 233/234 present and noise 233/234, so admission cannot be declining for want of a backed sensor; (b) the new tie disclosure (BUG-868), which renders different text; (c) BUG-873's replacement of an evidence-backed answer -- the fix correctly stands aside here because the lane produced no dossier at all. PRIME SUSPECT, and it fits the row's own evidence: the AVAILABILITY constraint. This row already records that 'on floor 3' alone works, 'for two hours of focused work this afternoon' alone works, and 'on floor 3 this afternoon' works -- only the full combination fails. A free-window check over 'two hours ... this afternoon' is also the one part of the question whose result legitimately depends on the hour it is asked, which is the intermittency nothing else explains.
Fix_Approach: Next step, now cheap: log what the deliberation lane RETURNS between build_schema and the response node -- the admission verdict and the candidate count -- because the one thing still invisible is which of validate() / enumerate_candidates / the event fold ended the turn. Then re-run the four variants at an afternoon hour and at an evening one. Do not change the relevance gate for this row: it is downstream and its behaviour here is now correct.
Verification: Reproduced on the answerability gate 3 times on 2026-09-23 (index 12), and passed it once the same night at ~01:17, on an unchanged build.

Title: The answerability gate can report a false regression for a question carrying a relative time window
Description: Index 12 asks about 'this afternoon'. Asked at 18:00 and at 23:00 the same phrase resolves to different windows, so the same build can answer it and then decline it with nothing having changed.
Root_Cause: The gate compares the KIND of reply against a baseline captured at one hour of the day. A question whose answer legitimately depends on when it is asked has no single correct kind.
Fix_Approach: Either run the gate at a fixed hour, or mark time-relative questions in the pack so their result is reported separately rather than counted as a regression.
Verification: Observed on index 12; the other 50 are time-insensitive or were unaffected.

Title: A tie across every candidate is presented as 'score 1 out of 1, fits everything you asked for'
Description: 'Which rooms are both warm and stuffy right now?' answers 'Best match: Room 2.24, score 1 out of 1, where 1 fits everything you asked for' with the top three at 22.675 / 22.652 / 22.635 C against a 20-26 band -- mid-band, tied, and presented as a perfect match. The floor-3 form of the same question ranked 0.3647 / 0.3627 / 0.3552, which discriminates.
Root_Cause: CORRECTED 2026-09-23 -- the first cause filed here ("the band's lower bound as the threshold") was wrong; measured over 16 compiles, 32 constraints, NOT ONE carried a threshold at all. The real cause: 'above' with no threshold is a filter direction with nothing to filter against, so the scorer substitutes the band edge and every candidate lands on the pass side at exactly 1.0. BUG-197 diagnosed this and folds ABOVE->MAXIMIZE for RANKING decisions, deliberately excluding LIST_MATCHING because an unbounded filter there is genuinely under-specified. These questions compile as list_matching ('Decision: list_matching over 195 ranked candidates'), so the fold does not reach them. The compiler is right to preserve the ambiguity. The defect is that nothing downstream DISCLOSES it: the ambiguity is kept and then reported as a discriminating best match.
Fix_Approach: Surface the tie rather than resolve it in the compiler -- the compiler's choice to keep the ambiguity is deliberate and correct. Where every scored candidate satisfies a constraint identically, say so ('all 195 rooms are above the 20 C band floor; ordered by how warm') and do not call the head of an alphabetical tie a best match. This is honest for any modality and any building, where folding the direction would only help words that carry their own polarity. Ordering underneath is already correct; the SCORE and its wording are what overstate. LANDED: the guard for this already existed and was one-sided -- render_answer suppressed 'Best match' when every total was <= 0 (row 58) and said nothing when every total was 1.0, which is the same failure at the other end of the range. Now fires on a TIE at any value: all ranked totals identical and more than one ranked.
Verification: Reproduced live 2026-09-23 on /v1/chat/completions with isolated chat ids. Direction tally over 4 repeats x 4 questions: above 22, minimize 4, below 4, maximize 2; thresholds present: 0. Two asks of the identical question minutes apart named DIFFERENT best matches (Room 3.12, then Room 2.24), both at score 1. The readings also moved between the asks, so this is consistent with an unstable tiebreak and with live data and does not by itself prove either; a controlled repeat against a frozen window would separate them, and is worth doing before quoting this. | 2 tests added (tie at 1.0 disclosed; a near-miss at 0.999 still names a best match, so the guard fires on a tie and not on a high score); 15 pass in that file. LIVE VERIFICATION OWED -- re-ask the four cross-modal questions after the answerability gate finishes. | VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-23: the two questions that compile unbounded now answer 'The readings don't separate these spaces' instead of 'Best match ... score 1 out of 1'; the two that compile maximize/minimize still rank with discriminating scores (0.3761/0.3759/0.3723 and 0.7667/0.7588). The guard fires on a tie, not on a lane.

Title: A cross-modal comfort question was refused when the model omitted the direction
Description: 'Which rooms are both warm and stuffy right now?' compiled with direction 'none' for both modalities and was refused with "I couldn't map part of your request (warm; stuffy)" -- naming, in the refusal, the two words whose polarity the compiler already records. 'Is anywhere both hot and noisy' asked a minute later compiled both directions and ranked the rooms correctly.
Root_Cause: _LAY_POLARITY knows warm is the high end of temperature and stuffy the high end of CO2, and _constraint_from_phrase already trusts it for phrases the model leaves in 'unmapped'. It was never consulted on the other path, where a MAPPED constraint arrives without a direction. The refusal was manufactured out of temp-0 provider wobble.
Fix_Approach: _direction_from_phrase_polarity(phrase), consulted after _infer_direction returns None. Declines on an avoidance phrase ('less stuffy'), on two words pulling opposite ways, and on any word with no polarity of its own -- so 'temperature' and 'occupancy' stay refusable, which is the boundary that keeps this a robustness fix rather than licence to guess.
Verification: 4 unit tests in tests/test_cqir_compiler.py covering the fix and all three declines; live: all four cross-modal questions now compile executable and are answered with two-modality rankings, coverage and a dossier.

Title: The word 'both' kept two-modality comfort questions out of the only lane that can rank on two modalities
Description: 'Which rooms on floor 3 are warm and stuffy?' routed to deliberate and was answered. 'Which rooms are both warm and stuffy right now?' routed to sparql and declined. The two questions differ by the word 'both'. Separately, 'Where is it cool and quiet enough to work?' compiled to a perfectly executable two-modality plan and matched no routing branch at all.
Root_Cause: The CAVEAT-563 branch of DELIBERATE_RE requires the condition adjective immediately after the verb, so a quantifier between them ('both', 'all', 'either') fell outside it. The branch also carried its own inline copy of the condition-adjective list while _CONDITION_ADJECTIVES sat six lines above it. The 'where is it <adjective>' shape had no branch and no 'anywhere' for EXISTENTIAL_COMFORT_RE to catch.
Fix_Approach: Allow an optional quantifier before the adjective; add a 'where is it <adjective>' branch needing the dummy subject AND a condition adjective; point both at _CONDITION_ADJECTIVES so there is one list rather than three that diverge. No rule was added or reordered, so the pinned precedence order is unchanged.
Verification: 13 unit tests: 5 shapes admitted, 7 near-misses still excluded, 1 proving the adjective list is named once. 186 existing routing tests pass. Live: all four route to deliberate.

Title: Asking probe questions in one chat lets the co-reference rewrite change a question's routing
Description: 'Where is it cool and quiet enough to work?' routed to deliberate when asked alone and to sparql when asked as turn four of the same chat. The rewrite resolves 'it' against the previous answer's room, which changes the question's SHAPE, so it no longer matches the routing pattern.
Root_Cause: Working as designed for a real follow-up, and wrong for a probe: a harness that reuses one chat measures the rewrite as well as the change under test, and reports the difference as a routing failure.
Fix_Approach: Send a distinct X-Chat-Id per question in any probe that is not deliberately testing follow-ups. Worth checking whether the pronoun-led shapes should survive the rewrite at all, since a question naming two conditions is rarely a follow-up about one room.
Verification: Both routings reproduced on the same build, one minute apart.

Title: A correct humidity forecast was topped with a false 'check the sensor scaling' warning
Description: A forecast for room 2.01 opened with "The recorded humidity value (193, -0.029) is outside the range this quantity can take in %, so it is most likely raw or unscaled sensor output ... the sensor's scaling should be checked before this reading is relied on". 193 is the answer's own 'History used: 193 data points'; -0.029 is the Linear Trend R-squared in the model-selection table. The stored series is a clean 30-70 %RH with ZERO impossible values over 29,667 rows, and the forecast's own predictions were 52.66 %RH. A false data-quality alarm on correct data is the failure that teaches readers to ignore the real ones.
Root_Cause: Two, both in plausibility.py, and the first is the sharper lesson. (1) _in_metric_context exists precisely to stop this and looks back _METRIC_LOOKBACK=320 characters for a metric header -- and the CALL SITE sliced 90. The constant's own comment says the R-squared header sits ~130 characters back, so the fix written for the identical CO2 case was handed a third of the window it needed and was dead on arrival. (2) _COUNT_NOUN_RE listed 'points' but not 'data points', so a row count qualified by a noun was judged as a reading.
Fix_Approach: Slice _METRIC_LOOKBACK at the call site, not 90. Allow an optional 'data ' qualifier before the count noun. Both are one-line changes to code that already existed.
Verification: 4 tests added, built from the VERBATIM rendered answer rather than a shortened stand-in -- the six existing tests all passed while this shipped, because their sample put the R-squared within 90 characters of its header. One test pins the lookback by DISTANCE so the constant cannot be silently under-fed again; one proves a genuinely impossible predicted value is still caught. Live: warning gone over 3 asks.

Title: The answer-relevance gate discards a correct forecast and leaves nothing in its place
Description: Measured: the forecast lane completed successfully -- 'Done. Model=Holt-Winters (seasonal=24) MAE=0.473%RH RMSE=0.641%RH', success=True -- and the next log line is 'relevance gate replaced a trend answer: OFF_TOPIC (does not provide mean humidity for tomorrow afternoon.)' followed by 'nothing to say: intent=trend ... error=none'. The reader gets 'I couldn't answer that from Abacws Building's records.' This is the SECOND recorded instance of this gate replacing a correct answer; CLAUDE.md records the first, after which CONTRADICTORY was stopped from replacing. OFF_TOPIC still does.
Root_Cause: _maybe_replace_irrelevant returns _unanswered_response(state, ctx) on any replacing verdict. Its own except branch is commented 'the gate must never cost an answer' -- which is exactly what the success path does. The gate's judgement is not wrong here (see BUG-874: the answer really does not give the MEAN that was asked for), but its ACTION is: a partial answer about the right sensor, right quantity and right horizon is replaced by no answer at all, which is strictly less useful and no more honest.
Fix_Approach: LANDED, narrowest option (c'): the gate keeps its judgement and loses ONE action, in ONE case. When the turn produced visible evidence -- a dossier with ranked candidates or readings, or figures computed in the store -- the answer is kept and the objection is recorded on the bus instead. The reason is not that the gate is wrong: it is that `_unanswered_response` says "I couldn't answer that from <the building>'s records", which is FALSE precisely when a lane has just answered from them, so the replacement asserts a falsehood and discards the evidence disproving it. With no evidence visible it replaces exactly as before -- the case it was built for, a model generalising from a retrieval window. | SECOND PASS, same day: the first version checked the dossier, the aggregate lane and the comparison lane and MISSED `forecast_result` -- the lane this bug was first observed in. Completed forecasts went on being replaced, and the answerability gate caught it on pack index 6 during the very run meant to confirm the fix ('[forecast_agent] Done. Model=SeasonalNaive MAE=8.681ppm' then 'nothing to say'). The lane keys are now named in one place and a test asserts all four are listed, so a fifth lane has somewhere obvious to be added.
Verification: 12 unit tests covering both directions, including that an empty or absent dossier is NOT evidence so the original behaviour is intact, and that a malformed state reports no evidence rather than raising. LIVE: 'Which rooms are both warm and stuffy right now, and what do the two together suggest?' previously logged '[deliberate] answered: ranked=195 guard_violations=0' followed by 'relevance gate replaced' and 'nothing to say'; it now reaches the reader with the ranking, both bands and the dossier. | index 6 now logs: 'relevance gate OBJECTED to a trend answer but did not replace it: OFF_TOPIC (Does not address tomorrow afternoon, gives wrong time range.) -- the turn produced a fitted SeasonalNaive forecast over 24 steps, so the decline would have been untrue'. 18 unit tests, including that a FAILED or empty forecast is not evidence and cannot shelter its own non-answer.

Title: A forecast asked for a MEAN over a named window returns an hourly table instead
Description: 'Based on the last two weeks, what is the expected mean humidity in room 2.01 tomorrow afternoon?' produces a 24-row hourly prediction table. It never states the expected mean for tomorrow afternoon, which is the only number asked for. The relevance gate notices and discards the whole answer (BUG-873), so the reader sees neither.
Root_Cause: The forecast lane's output shape is fixed: horizon, model selection, per-step predictions with intervals. Nothing reads the AGGREGATE the question names ('mean') or the sub-window it names ('tomorrow afternoon') and reduces the prediction to it.
Fix_Approach: W2-02 landed the aggregate-over-SENSORS half: a floor or building question is now forecast from one folded series and states its denominator. The other half is still open and is what this row was opened for -- reducing the predicted SERIES to the aggregate over the WINDOW the question names ('the expected MEAN ... tomorrow afternoon'), instead of returning an hourly table and leaving the reader to average it. Owner: W2-02 follow-up or a new row; no longer urgent, because BUG-873 means an incomplete forecast now reaches the reader instead of being replaced by a false decline.
Verification: Rendered answer captured verbatim 2026-09-23; predictions 52.66 %RH hourly, no mean.

Title: Evidence-pack question #1 answers only about half the time
Description: Index 1 of docs/supervisor_evidence_pack is recorded GOOD/answered. Measured over 9 clean asks (cache flushed, fresh chat id each): roughly half decline. The cause is BUG-873 -- a successful forecast discarded by the relevance gate -- not a data or routing fault. The pack's screenshot is a true record of one run, and the question is not reliably answerable.
Root_Cause: The pack records ONE run per question. A question whose lane succeeds and is then intermittently discarded downstream looks identical to a stable one in a single capture.
Fix_Approach: Fix BUG-873, then re-ask index 1 several times and only then treat it as evidence. More generally: ask each pack question at least twice when capturing, and mark any that disagree, so a screenshot is never the only measurement behind a claim.
Verification: 9 asks: 4-5 answered, 4-5 declined, depending on the batch.

Title: The answerability gate scored a decline as an answer when the decline named the room
Description: 'I couldn't answer that about **Room2.01** from Abacws Building's records' was classified 'answered'. The decline marker is the literal 'i couldn't answer that from', and the referent is inserted in the middle of it, so no fixed substring spans the phrase.
Root_Cause: classify() matched decline wording by literal substring only. A decline counted as an answer is the direction that HIDES a regression rather than inventing one, which is the worse direction for a gate that exists to catch regressions.
Fix_Approach: Add _DECLINE_PATTERNS: regexes for declines that carry the referent in the middle, checked alongside the literal markers.
Verification: The variant now classifies as 'declined'. Swept the shipped pack: ZERO stored answers use this variant, so no recorded count is affected; and zero stored answers scored 'answered' while opening like a decline.

Title: The answerability gate now confirms a regression before reporting one
Description: Index 1 reported REGRESSED on a build whose changes provably cannot reach it (the routing pattern does not match the question; the other three changes are deliberation-lane only). Re-asked, it answered.
Root_Cause: One run is not a measurement of an intermittent lane, and a gate that cries regression at a flake gets switched off -- which costs far more than the flake.
Fix_Approach: On a regression, re-ask once. If the re-ask matches the recorded kind, report FLAKY and count it in its own category. AN INTERMITTENT IS NOT AN OK: it is never folded into 'still behave as recorded', because a retry that succeeds is still a first-pass failure. Exit code stays 0 -- the behaviour is not gone; the line stays visible -- it is not well either.
Verification: Retry path exercised live on index 1; two consecutive failures still report REGRESSED.

Title: A confident false negative: 'all rooms have a temperature sensor', narrated from a total sensor count
Description: 'Which rooms have no temperature sensor?' answered "All of the rooms that are recorded in the building model have at least one temperature sensor", citing "Room0.01 has 15 sensors, Room0.04 has 11" and "Total spaces recorded: 100". The query behind it returned a TOTAL sensor count per room, which cannot distinguish a temperature sensor from a door contact, so the conclusion does not follow from the evidence at any strength -- and the 100 is wrong, the building has 234 spaces. Two other phrasings gave two further wrong answers: one honestly admitted the query had no types, one returned a table of sound LEVELS for a question about noise SENSORS.
Root_Cause: The set difference was left to an LLM to express as SPARQL, and the retrieved context it got back could not support the question. Nothing checked that the evidence could bear the conclusion.
Fix_Approach: orchestrator/services/coverage_gap.py -- a deterministic lane over the EXISTING deliberation/coverage_audit.py, whose first line of documentation is this question verbatim ('which spaces lack which sensor modalities?'). It is already subclass-closure-aware, already handles both location idioms, already takes its modality list from config with a per-building overlay, and was built for SATURATE in V4. Nothing asked it. It also reports UNBACKED separately from MISSING, which a set-difference query would have collapsed -- 'no sensor' and 'a sensor reporting nothing' lead to different repairs.
Verification: 23 unit tests. LIVE: 'no temperature sensor' -> '234 of 234 have one', independently confirmed by a differently-shaped SPARQL (FILTER NOT EXISTS over both location idioms) returning 0. 'without a noise sensor' -> '1 of 234 ... Room 1.04 - Common Area / Atrium', and the independent query returns exactly Room1.04 and nothing else. 'no radiation sensor' correctly stands down, so the honest not-measured decline still fires.

Title: The absence guard replaced a correct COUNTED absence with a building-wide correction
Description: The coverage-gap lane answered 'Are there any rooms without a noise sensor?' with '1 of 234 spaces have no noise sensor. 233 have one that reports readings' -- verified against the graph -- and absence_guard replaced the whole answer with "this building does have 235 noise sensor(s) -- the limitation isn't a lack of sensing. Try narrowing the request". The correction is true, answers a question nobody asked, and discards the one that was asked. THIRD guard this session to destroy a correct answer (BUG-868, BUG-873).
Root_Cause: detect_absence_claim read the whole answer as ONE string, so '...no noise sensor...' matched wherever it appeared. The guard exists to catch a claim about the BUILDING; an absence COUNTED against a population ('1 of 234 spaces') is a claim about part of it, and the very next clause named the 233 spaces that have one.
Fix_Approach: Judge sentence by sentence, and stand down on a sentence that counts the absence against a population (_SCOPED_ABSENCE_RE). This does not weaken the guard's purpose: the claim it was built for -- 'the ontology data you provided does not contain any temperature sensors' -- carries no count of spaces, because a model generalising from a retrieval window has none to give.
Verification: 9 tests: 4 building-wide claims still caught (incl. the bldg2 original), 4 scoped answers pass through, and one proving a scoped sentence does not shelter an unscoped one beside it. 31 pass in that file, 168 across the absence suites. LIVE: the noise answer now reaches the reader intact.

Title: A two-period comparison of a NAMED ROOM still declines
Description: 'Compare the average CO2 in room 5.01 this week against last week' declines. The new comparison lane resolves both windows correctly and calls the aggregate lane twice, and the aggregate lane refuses BOTH calls with 'not claimed: measurand=co2 place=True'. Building-wide comparison of the same quantity works end to end.
Root_Cause: TWO gates, and the first fix moved only one. (a) The aggregate lane vetoed any question naming a place. Lifting that veto behind an explicit caller flag made summary_ok True and changed NOTHING, because (b) summary_ok only ever reaches wants_lane's sixth case, which fires when the question parses to no statistic in particular. 'Compare the AVERAGE CO2 in room 5.01...' parses cleanly to stat=mean/group=building, so it skipped that case, matched none of the five others, and was declined for a reason that had nothing to do with the place veto.
Fix_Approach: Both halves. (a) aggregate_lane.try_answer takes keyword-only allow_named_place, and lifting it REGROUPS building->room|floor so _group_key names the place and the figure cannot claim a scope it lacks (the BUG-883 shape). (b) When the flag is set AND summary_ok holds, a parsed intent that wants_lane declined is claimed by the caller: the comparison lane has already scoped both windows to one place and has nothing to fall back on. Gated on summary_ok, so every honesty test guarding the summary path guards this too. comparison_lane is the only caller that lifts it, pinned by a test that greps the tree.
Verification: Offline 18 tests, incl. one pinning the PREMISE of the second half (the question parses, so wants_lane's summary case is unreachable for it) so the second fix is deletable if that stops being true. LIVE 2026-09-29 after rebuild, caches flushed, fresh chat: 'Compare the average CO2 in room 5.01 this week against last week' ANSWERS in 16.9s, and every figure is labelled 'HVAC Zone 5.01 mean/peak/lowest' -- the ROOM, not the building, so the regroup held and the label follows the scope. It also disclosed unprompted that the two windows rest on 3830 vs 296 readings. Converts W1-04 and W2-03 from PARTIAL.

Title: An energy question resolves no measurand, so no aggregate lane will claim it
Description: 'How does energy use yesterday compare with the same day last week?' and 'Compare energy use this month and last month' both decline. The aggregate lane logs 'not claimed: measurand=None' for both: the measurand is voted from the labels of the sensors the pipeline bound, and for these questions it comes out empty.
Root_Cause: Not yet attributed. Either the binder is returning no energy sensors for these phrasings, or the labels it returns do not vote to a measurand `measurand_key` knows. The building HAS energy submeters -- the decline itself lists 'the readings of energy submeter' among what it can answer, which is the system contradicting itself in one sentence.
Fix_Approach: Log the bound uuids and their labels for one of these turns before changing anything; the decline names energy submeters as available, so the two halves disagree and one of them is wrong. Fix the one that is.
Verification: Live 2026-09-23, both phrasings, measurand=None in both. | RE-ASKED 2026-09-30, both phrasings: STILL DECLINES, but the cause this row names is GONE and the replacement is a FALSE ABSENCE, which is worse. measurand=None no longer applies: both answers now bind the energy meters and print the Boundary disclosure naming all six (Energy_Meter_Floor0..5). Instead: (1) 'How does energy use yesterday compare with the same day last week?' -> 'Because there are no separate readings for 2026-09-29 (yesterday) and 2026-09-22 (the same day last week), a direct day-over-day comparison cannot be calculated.' FALSE: sensordb.energy_data holds 528 rows dated 2026-09-29 and 426 dated 2026-09-22 (measured in-container, session +00:00). (2) 'Compare energy use this month and last month' -> 'The data set contains daily energy totals only for 2026-09-18 through 2026-09-30 ... no August figures are present.' FALSE: energy_data runs from 2026-06-04. Both are the clipped fetch window being narrated as the building's absence -- see BUG-956 and BUG-939. Also: 'No month-over-month comparison available' is printed twice in one answer, and 2.59 kWh is described as a floor's 'cumulative' reading when the stored values are 1.3-6.5 rates.

Title: 'Is the ventilation keeping up with occupancy on floor 2?' answered 'No readings were found for Floor_2'
Description: Evidence pack #27. Classified `compare` and sent to the single-sensor path, which resolved 'Floor_2' to eight F2-named METERS (access reader, entry counter, HVAC meter, lighting meter...) and reported 'No readings were found for Floor_2' -- of a floor with 47 spaces, 42 of them instrumented for both CO2 and occupancy.
Root_Cause: The question is about the RELATIONSHIP between two measured quantities, which is a ranking on two modalities at once and belongs to the deliberation lane. No rule recognised that shape, and the entity resolver's fallback to label-matching 'F2' produced a plausible-looking but wrong sensor set.
Fix_Approach: New routing rule `one_quantity_judged_against_another`, guarded twice: a RELATIONAL phrase ('keeping up with', 'adequate for', 'coping with') AND two of this building's own quantities, counted in both forms they arrive in -- a literal modality name and a resolved lay concept. IN THE CONCEPT STAGE: see BUG-882.
Verification: 11 unit tests (3 firing phrasings, 5 near-misses excluded, one proving it never moves a question already going to deliberate, one proving the rule names no modality). 210 routing tests pass. LIVE: now routes to deliberate, scopes to floor 2 (42 of 47 spaces), and names both quantities with the band each was judged against.

Title: A rule needing resolved concepts passed its offline tests in the parse stage and never fired live
Description: `one_quantity_judged_against_another` was written into PARSE_STAGE_RULES. Its unit tests supplied `concepts` in the normalized dict and it passed them all. On a live turn it never fired once: concepts are resolved AFTER the parse stage, so the field it read was empty and its two-quantity guard could never be satisfied.
Root_Cause: A test that constructs the rule's input can construct an input the pipeline never produces at that point. The offline test proved the rule's LOGIC and said nothing about whether the data reaches it.
Fix_Approach: Moved to CONCEPT_STAGE_RULES, whose whole purpose is rules needing lay-term resolution. General guard: a rule reading `normalized['concepts']` belongs in the concept stage, and its pinned-order comment now says so in the test that would otherwise be the only place a reader looks.
Verification: Caught by asking the live system; offline tests were green in both stages.

Title: A forecast of one sensor was presented as the answer for a whole floor or building
Description: 'Predict the average CO2 on floor 3 for tomorrow afternoon' returned '## Forecast: CO2 Level Sensor installed-node 3.58' -- one room of the 45 instrumented on that floor. "What will the building's energy use be tomorrow?" returned '## Forecast: Electrical Energy Meter - Floor 0' -- one floor of six, and for an ADDITIVE quantity, so the figure was roughly a sixth of the answer. Both were correct forecasts of the wrong thing, with every digit right and nothing anywhere in either answer saying that a substitution had been made.
Root_Cause: `_select_primary_sensor` picks the single sensor whose label best matches the question's discriminating words, and is called unconditionally. That is right for 'the CO2 in room 5.01' and wrong for every question naming a floor or the building. The chosen sensor IS named in the heading, so the substitution is not concealed -- but a reader who asked about floor 3 has no reason to read that heading as a correction of their question.
Fix_Approach: services/forecasting/scope.py: detect an aggregate scope from the question, fold every bound sensor's readings into one series per time bucket, and state the denominator in the answer. MEAN OR TOTAL COMES FROM THE QUANTITY, never from the wording -- a floor's CO2 is the mean of its rooms and its energy the sum of its meters, and 'total co2 on floor 3' must still average, because summing 45 rooms of concentration gives 33,000 ppm. The folded series runs through the existing preprocessing and model selection unchanged.
Verification: 30 unit tests. LIVE: floor 3 -> '_This forecast is of one series averaged over 50 sensors for average floor 3._' with the heading 'floor 3 (average)'; the building -> 'summed across 6 sensors', heading "the building's (total)", and the kWh figures rose accordingly (7.8 RMSE against 1.4 for the single meter). A test also caught an over-match before it shipped: 'the noise LEVEL IN the atrium' was read as a floor scope, so the floor word now has to carry a number.

Title: Naming a floor bound the sensors NAMED for it, not the sensors ON it
Description: 'Will floor 3 be warmer than floor 4 tomorrow?' resolved to eight floor-3 METERS -- access reader, entry counter, HVAC meter, lighting meter, plug-load meter, fire-exit door sensor -- with nothing at all from floor 4 and not one temperature sensor. The same shape answered 'No readings were found for Floor_2' for evidence pack #27, of a floor with 42 instrumented spaces. Asked structurally the graph yields 48 temperature sensors on floor 3 and 56 on floor 4.
Root_Cause: `_resolve_entities_by_label` matches an entity by text against IRIs and labels, so a floor resolves to whatever is NAMED for it. The graph has held the structure all along -- floor -> spaces -> points, through the two location idioms coverage_audit has always covered -- and no resolution path used it.
Fix_Approach: `_resolve_floor_structurally`: for a floor entity ONLY, traverse floor -> spaces -> points and filter by the Brick class the lay-term resolver already produced. Returns [] for a non-floor entity, for a building that models floors differently, and CRUCIALLY when no class is resolved -- binding arbitrary points off a floor would be worse than the behaviour it replaces.
Verification: 19 unit tests. LIVE: floor 3 -> 48 temperature points, floor 4 -> 56, 104 bound. INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED against MySQL over 24h: floor 3 mean 22.877 (9,792 readings from 48 sensors), floor 4 mean 22.817 (10,200 from 56) -- the answer's 23.0 vs 22.9 and its direction match; the small offsets are a different window.

Title: A 0.06 C difference between two floors is reported as 'Floor 3 is warmer than Floor 4'
Description: With the binding fixed (BUG-884) the comparison is computed over the right 104 sensors and reads '**Floor 3 is warmer than Floor 4 (mean 23 C vs 22.9 C)**' -- twice, in bold, opening and closing the answer. The measured difference is 0.06 C against a within-floor spread of 3.9 C and 4.2 C. Nothing in the answer suggests the two floors are indistinguishable, which on this evidence they are.
Root_Cause: The comparison is narrated by the model from two sets of summary statistics. Nothing asks whether the difference is larger than the noise, so any non-zero gap becomes a finding. `evidence/matched_comparison.py` was built for exactly this -- it reports an effect WITH a confidence interval and says when the interval spans zero -- and has one caller, which is not this path.
Fix_Approach: Route a two-entity comparison through a lane that can state an interval, and say 'these two floors are not distinguishable on this evidence' when it spans zero. Blocked by BUG-879 the same way W1-04's room case is: the aggregate lane declines any question naming a place, so the comparison cannot reach a lane that computes rather than narrates. Fix BUG-879 first; W2-03 then becomes small.
Verification: NO LONGER REPRODUCES. Live 2026-09-29, caches flushed, after restart: 'Is floor 3 warmer than floor 4?' -> '**Floor 3 and Floor 4 are tied at a mean temperature of 23 C.**' It names both means, gives each floor's range and sensor count, and declines to pick a winner -- which is exactly what this row asked for. The duplicated bold assertion is gone. NOT CLAIMED AS A TARGETED FIX: no change was made against this row specifically. It is reported as verified because the behaviour it describes was re-measured and is absent, and the same answer was read closely enough to find a DIFFERENT defect in it (BUG-937: a spread of 4.0 quoted from a range of 20.4-25.4, with the opposite conclusion drawn from it), which was fixed and verified. If the tie here is an artefact of the two floors genuinely being equal today rather than of the verdict logic, a future re-ask on a day they differ will say so.

Title: The answerability gate scored an honest decline as an answer when its wording changed
Description: 'What is the air pressure in room 2.01 right now?' answered "there is no air-pressure sensor INSTALLED IN Room 2.01, so I can't provide a current pressure reading" -- a correct, honest decline about a quantity this building does not measure. The gate scored it ANSWERED and reported a regression on pack index 70. The decline marker is the literal 'there is no air-pressure sensor DATA', and the system had simply worded it differently.
Root_Cause: A decline recognised by one fixed string is a decline recognised in one phrasing. The system is free to reword an honest decline and does; the gate is not tracking it. Scoring a decline as an answer is the direction that HIDES a regression, which for a gate is the worse of the two.
Fix_Approach: A narrow regex for the 'no <quantity> sensor installed/fitted IN|AT|FOR <place>' shape. DELIBERATELY narrow, and two broader attempts were rejected for concrete reasons: `there (is|are) no .{0,40} sensors?` also matched 'there are no GAPS IN SENSOR COVERAGE' (a completeness answer asserting the opposite), and keying on `installed` alone matched the LABEL 'CO2 Level Sensor installed-node 3.07'. Both would have manufactured regressions, which is how a gate gets switched off.
Verification: 12 unit tests in tests/test_the_answerability_gate_reads_a_decline_correctly.py, pinning both directions and the shipped pack's distribution (57 answered / 14 declined / 2 refused over 73 answers). All 73 stored answers classify EXACTLY as before the change; the rejected broader pattern moved two of them (57/14 -> 55/16) and that is what caught it. Live: index 70 back to 'declined'.

Title: Marker-based decline detection cannot keep up with a system free to reword its declines
Description: ONE question -- 'What is the air pressure in room 2.01 right now?' -- produced THREE different honest declines in a single day: 'there is no air-pressure sensor DATA available for room 2.01' (the stored pack answer), 'there is no air-pressure sensor INSTALLED IN Room 2.01', and 'I DON'T HAVE ANY air-pressure data for Room 2.01' followed by a list of the room's other sensors. Each needed its own marker or pattern, and each was found only when the gate reported a false regression.
Root_Cause: `classify()` decides the KIND of a reply from a list of literal markers plus a few regexes. The wording of a decline is generated, so the list is chasing a moving target and will keep losing. Every miss is scored as an ANSWER, which is the direction that hides a regression.
Fix_Approach: The durable test is not the phrasing but the CONTENT: did the reply give a figure FOR THE QUANTITY ASKED? That is close to what the answer-relevance gate already judges on live turns, and its verdict is already recorded on the bus as `relevance_gate`. Two options worth weighing: (a) have the capture harness store the lane's own outcome alongside the text so the gate compares a recorded FACT rather than re-deriving a kind from prose; (b) keep the classifier but add a measured-quantity check. Until then the marker list stays, with the standing rule that every change to it is verified against all 73 stored answers -- which is now a test.
Verification: Three wordings observed on 2026-09-23 on pack index 70, each on a separate gate run; the pack's own stored answer is a fourth variant of the same decline.

Title: The intent cache is keyed on the PROMPT, so it never hits and contributes nothing to determinism
Description: Measured on a full 51-question gate run 2026-09-29: 'Cache hit for intent detection' 0 times against 38 LLM classification calls. W6-01 exists because six of fifty answers differed between two identical runs; this is why.
Root_Cause: dialogue_agent.detect_intent keys the cache on generate_hash(prompt), and the prompt is built from user_query PLUS ontology_context, conversation_history and memory_context. Those three vary per conversation, so the same question in a new chat produces a different prompt, a different hash, a miss, and a fresh LLM call that may classify differently. It is a prompt cache, not a decision cache.
Fix_Approach: LANDED: `decision_cache_key(query, building_id, persona)` keyed on the NORMALISED REWRITTEN query + building + persona + a routing-contract fingerprint, with typographic forms folded so a browser's curly apostrophe and a CLI's straight one reach ONE decision (BUG-864 class). Excluded: ontology context, conversation history, memory context -- the three that varied. Safe to key on the question because rewrite_to_standalone replaces messages[-1].content before detect_intent.
Verification: 15 unit tests. LIVE 2026-09-29: same question asked 3x in fresh chats with resp_cache flushed each time -> 2 cache hits / 1 LLM call. Before the fix a full 51-question gate produced 0 hits / 38 calls.

Title: Every narrow table has a 5-day hole because the publisher does not run when the stack is down
Description: Day 0 boot found energy_data with 396 rows on 09-23, 144 on 09-24, NOTHING 09-25..09-28, and 18 on 09-29. All 16 narrow tables are affected; the WIDE table is continuous (2025-01-01..now, 733,450 rows). The answerability gate read 49/51 and BOTH 'regressions' (#11 electricity chart yesterday, #20 which floor used most energy yesterday) are CORRECT declines over absent data, not code defects.
Root_Cause: The narrow tables are filled forward by data-publisher only. Stack down = no rows. Nothing monitors or reports the resulting hole, so it presents to a user as the system being broken rather than as a gap in the record.
Fix_Approach: Two separable things. (1) Finish the backfill for the four missed tables, with the owner's decision on sensor_data specifically. (2) The CAUSE is unchanged and is by design in dev: `data-publisher` writes only while the stack is up, so every pause makes a new hole. The durable fix is not more backfilling but a COVERAGE CHECK that runs before any measurement and states the days it found, so a hole is reported rather than silently averaged over.
Verification: TWO backfills, and the record of why there were two is kept deliberately. The first (1,253,980 rows) is driven by `input/bldg1_narrow_publish_map.json` and so covered 15 of 19 tables; I then wrote 'all 19 tables now hold 7 distinct days' having checked TEN, and the check over all of them contradicted me a minute later. The four it missed are in other maps or another mechanism entirely: plant_data (bldg1_plant_publish_map.json), wastefill_data and wasteweight_data (bldg1_waste_publish_map.json, a different shape), and sensor_data, the WIDE table. SECOND BACKFILL 2026-09-29 on the owner's explicit instruction ('backfill all four'), 37,248 rows: plant_data 22,272 across 58 series, the two waste tables 4,608 each across 12, and sensor_data 5,760 rows at 60 s intervals across 703 value columns. Values are never invented: each is sampled from that same series' OWN history at the SAME HOUR OF DAY from the fortnight before the hole, so a drift detector or a peer comparison sees shape rather than uniform noise; an ENUM column's value is copied verbatim. Insert-only, and only at timestamps the table did not already hold. RE-CHECKED after: all 19 narrow tables AND the wide table cover 10 of 10 days over 20-29 Sep. One honest difference: the backfilled days of sensor_data hold 1,440 rows (60 s) against a live ~2,500 (~35 s), so they are LESS dense than the days either side. Stated in the script rather than hidden. STILL MITIGATED, NOT FIXED: the cause is unchanged and by design in dev -- `data-publisher` writes only while the stack is up, so the next multi-day pause makes a new hole. The durable fix is a coverage check that runs BEFORE any measurement and states the days it found, because a hole is invisible to a question: a lane reasoning from a window cannot tell 'the building was quiet' from 'nothing was written'.

Title: W6-01's premise is half right: ROUTING is already deterministic; the variation is downstream
Description: W6-01 says 'six of fifty answers differed between two identical runs'. Measured 2026-09-29 with a purpose-built probe -- 10 questions x 5 cold asks each (50 turns, resp_cache flushed before every ask, a fresh chat id per ask so the co-reference rewrite cannot change the question's shape): UNSTABLE 0 of 10. Every question took exactly one route on all five asks. Latency over the same 50 asks: median 21.0s, p95 79.4s, max 100.4s -- against the row's claim of 'median 100 s, slowest 273 s'.
Root_Cause: The row conflates ANSWER variation with ROUTE variation. Routes are stable; the differing answers come from somewhere after routing. Three candidates, none yet separated: the deliberation COMPILE (observed 2026-09-23 producing `above` for a question that compiled `maximize` moments later, which changes the scoring semantics), the narration, and the building's data genuinely moving between asks.
Fix_Approach: Re-scope W6-01 before building anything: measure ANSWER variation directly (same question N times, compare the figures and the compiled plan, not the prose), and target whichever of compile / narration / data movement dominates. The plan_fingerprint already exists for exactly this comparison (BUG-184: compare plan_fingerprint across runs, plan_hash is provenance). Do not re-derive it.
Verification: scratchpad/determinism_probe.py, 50 cold turns, 2026-09-29.

Title: The dev publisher overwrites the live weather feed's own columns, so every outdoor reading answered is fabricated
Description: input/feeds.yaml declares three Open-Meteo rest_poll feeds for Cardiff (51.481, -3.179). They poll every 300 s and their rows DO land: 105,361 non-null values per column since 2026-06-11, newest 2026-09-29 15:28 UTC. But data-publisher writes a generated value into the SAME three wide-table columns every PUBLISH_INTERVAL=30 s. Measured 2026-09-29 against the live store and the live API: at 15:26:15 UTC the columns held 21.90 degC / 71.00 % / 19.40 km/h and Open-Meteo reported 22.0 / 70 / 19.4; at 15:26:41, 15:27:11, 15:27:41 and 15:28:11 they held 24.06-24.31 degC / 55.8-56.9 % / 7.0 km/h. Ten samples in eleven are fabricated, so services/outdoor_readings.py -- which binds these points correctly, by Brick class -- quoted 'outdoor temperature 23.8' for a Cardiff afternoon that was 22.0. The feed, the write path, the graph registration and the routing were all already built and working; only the data was wrong (lessons #133, #136).
Root_Cause: mysql_dummy_publisher.load_columns() reads every column of the wide table from information_schema and gen_value() invents a value for each one. It has no notion that a column might already have a live source. Worse, the three feed UUIDs are NAMED in the publisher's own sensor_uuids.json (Outside_Air_Temperature_Sensor_Exterior, Outside_Air_Humidity_Sensor_Exterior, Wind_Speed_Sensor_Exterior), so get_realistic_value produced plausible-looking weather rather than obvious noise -- which is why it survived. PUBLISH_WIDE=true is a deliberate dev top-up for sensors with NO live source (BUG-144); a generated value on top of a source that IS live is not a top-up, it is a fabrication, and design contract 4 forbids it.
Fix_Approach: load_columns() now holds back every column a live feed owns. feed_owned_uuids() reads the active building's feeds.yaml and derives each enabled rest_poll feed's UUID as md5('<BUILDING_ID>:<feed_id>') -- the same derivation as FeedRegistry._derive_uuid, asserted equal by a test so the two cannot drift -- honouring an explicit `uuid:` when the YAML pins one. No building literal: the ids come from that building's own feeds.yaml. It reports the count it ACTUALLY removed, and warns when feeds are declared but none of their UUIDs is a column, because a wrong BUILDING_ID derives well-formed UUIDs that match nothing and would otherwise look like success (lesson #126). PyYAML added to the publisher image; BUILDING_ID passed to the service in docker-compose.yml (the flat input/ layout carries the id nowhere in the path). Pre-existing rows in those columns are a mix of real and generated and are NOT purged -- CLAUDE.md is explicit that sensor_data must not be purged or relabelled.
Verification: 8 unit tests in tests/test_a_live_feed_column_is_not_overwritten.py, plus 102 pre-existing publisher tests still green. Checked against the LIVE store: the exclusion set is exactly 3 of sensor_data's 704 columns, 0 declared-but-missing, so it is not a no-op. NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE: applying it needs `docker compose build data-publisher && docker compose up -d data-publisher`, and this session was not permitted to restart containers. After the rebuild, confirm the boot line 'live-feed columns held back from the wide table: 3' and then that the three columns change only every ~300 s and match api.open-meteo.com. | VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-29 after `docker compose build data-publisher && up -d data-publisher`: publisher boots at 700 value columns (was 703, 3 held back). Over a 2-minute window the table took 5 rows (publisher every 30s + one feed write) and each of the three weather columns was non-null in exactly 1 row with 1 distinct value. Before the fix they changed on every 30s publisher row.
Refs: mysql-dummy-publish-dev/mysql_dummy_publisher.py (feed_owned_uuids, load_columns); mysql-dummy-publish-dev/Dockerfile; docker-compose.yml data-publisher; orchestrator/services/feeds/registry.py::_derive_uuid; tasks/PRODUCTION_TRACKER.csv W3-01

Title: 'Outdoor temperature' binds a synthetic green-roof proxy, not the Outside_Air_Temperature_Sensor the concept resolver just identified
Description: Live 2026-09-29, fresh chat, cache flushed. 'What is the outdoor temperature right now?' and 'how warm is it outside right now?' both answered from **Ambient Temperature Sensor - Green Roof (outdoor reference)** (bldg:GreenRoof_Ambient_Temp_Sensor, storedAt bldg:temperature_data -- a synthetic narrow table). The building holds exactly ONE brick:Outside_Air_Temperature_Sensor, the Open-Meteo feed point, and it was never bound. The log shows both facts one millisecond apart: '[sparql] resolved [Outdoor_Temperature_Sensor] -> 1 point(s), e.g. [bldg:GreenRoof_Ambient_Temp_Sensor]' at 15:32:41,804 and '[sparql] class from HBCO concept 'outdoor_temperature': brick:Outside_Air_Temperature_Sensor' at 15:32:41,805.
Root_Cause: The resolved class was handed to _resolve_entities_by_label as class_hints and used only on the floor path, so a label match beat it. THE FIRST FIX MADE IT WORSE: it put every hinted class in ONE VALUES, and class_hints is every Brick class of every resolved concept flattened -- Outside_Air_Temperature_Sensor AND Air_Temperature_Sensor AND Temperature_Sensor. Measured against the live graph 2026-09-29: the specific class has exactly ONE instance (the Open-Meteo feed); GreenRoof_Ambient_Temp_Sensor is NOT that class but IS an Air_Temperature_Sensor. The broad class admitted it, and the token filter (requires 'outdoor') then EXCLUDED the correctly typed feed, whose label says 'outside'.
Fix_Approach: Two narrowings. (1) Use the most specific hinted class that has READABLE instances, not their union; specificity is asked of the graph (_count_readable_instances, one grouped COUNT over points carrying a timeseries reference) rather than guessed from the name, because class_hints carries no ordering and a class the building never instantiated must rank nowhere. At most 3 classes are tried. (2) At or below _CLASS_IS_THE_ANSWER_CAP=12 readable instances the class IS the answer and the token filter is dropped -- the tokens restate the class, so below the cap they can only lose a correctly typed point to a vocabulary difference. Above it they still narrow.
Verification: CORRECTION KEPT ON THE RECORD: this row once read FIXED on a hand-run SPARQL query that returned feed_outside_weather_temp. That query was NOT the one the code sent -- it carried one class, the code sent eight -- so it verified the intent, not the code, and the live re-ask afterwards still bound GreenRoof (lessons #145). Offline now 16 tests. LIVE 2026-09-29 after rebuild, caches flushed, fresh chat: 'What is the outdoor temperature right now?' binds 'Outside Air Temperature Sensor feed outside_weather_temp' at 21.9 C -- the Open-Meteo feed. GreenRoof no longer appears.
Refs: orchestrator/agents/sparql_agent.py::_resolve_entities_by_label (~line 4132) and its call site (~line 631); orchestrator/services/outdoor_readings.py; BUG-884; BUG-888

Title: Four ordinary English words turned the calibration register off
Description: Two phrasings of one question, routed IDENTICALLY (intent=metadata -> metadata node=sparql overrides=[]), disagreed about whether the building records calibration at all. 'How many sensors are overdue for calibration?' -> '268 sensors ... of the 1,929 that have a calibration regime recorded'. 'How many sensors are overdue for calibration, and what does that mean for the answers you give me?' -> 'it does not contain any field that records whether a sensor is overdue for calibration, nor does it record a calibration schedule or status', followed by a list of 50 sensors. The graph holds ontosage:calibratedOn, calibrationDueOn and calibrationMethod on 1,929 subjects each. Recorded in the supervisor evidence pack as #49 (answers) against #33 (denies) - the tracker row W3-02 cited #40/#49, which is the wrong pair; #40 is the Room 5.01 instance question and it was always correct.
Root_Cause: sparql_agent._measurand_tokens is a DENYLIST: any word not in a hand-written stopword set becomes a sensor-name scope. 'mean', 'answers', 'you' and 'give' survived it, so the metrology lane built FILTER(CONTAINS(...,"mean") || ... || CONTAINS(...,"give")), which returns zero rows; _instrument_metrology then returned None and the question fell through to a generated query that cannot see these properties and denied they exist. The lane's own guard acted too widely - 'I scoped it wrongly' was indistinguishable from 'nothing is declared' (lesson #135). A denylist over English cannot be finished; the next phrasing finds the next gap.
Fix_Approach: The GRAPH decides what scopes, not a word list. New SPARQLAgent._tokens_present_in_register runs one VALUES query asking the active building's own register which of the candidate tokens name an instrument it holds; a token matching nothing is dropped and the question is answered building-wide from the same register instead of being abandoned. A scope the USER named that matches nothing is still answered building-wide, and the narration is told to say so. Fails CLOSED: a scope check that errors keeps the scope unchanged.
Verification: tests/test_calibration_is_one_register_one_lane.py (11), incl. a teeth test that restores the denylist and asserts the defect returns. Verified against the LIVE GraphDB (localhost:7200/repositories/bldg) by driving _instrument_metrology from the host: four phrasings - both pack wordings plus 'which sensors are overdue for calibration and should I trust their readings?' and 'how many sensors need recalibration and how does that affect your answers?' - now build the identical counted query and return 268 overdue / 1,929 with a regime / 2,727 with a declared interval, while 'When was the CO2 sensor in Room 5.01 last calibrated?' still scopes to 28 sensors. LIVE RE-ASK THROUGH THE ORCHESTRATOR IS OWED: uvicorn runs without --reload and this session was forbidden to restart it, so the narrated answer has not been seen. Re-ask both phrasings after the next restart.

Title: 'Where can I park and do I need a permit?' answered from the permit-TO-WORK register
Description: Asked live 2026-09-29: 'The building's records do not contain any information about parking spaces or parking permits. What the register does hold are 15 permit-to-work entries...' - then a table of hot works, roof access and confined space permits. The first sentence is FALSE. The building holds bldg:Amenity_Parking_GroundLevel (ontosage:ParkingArea, six EV chargers), bldg:Parking_Level_Ground (brick:Parking_Level), bldg:Cap_transport_parking whose layTerms include 'parking', 'disabled parking' and 'blue badge' and whose text says the university car park requires a permit for staff, and bldg:building_sat_parking_free, a parking-occupancy point. Asked 'Where can I park my car?' the same system answers correctly from the amenity, so the register match is what loses it.
Root_Cause: A greedy lay-term match on the word 'permit' claimed the question for the PermitToWork register and outranked a capability the building demonstrably holds - the exact failure record_registry.py's own header docstring warns about ('A greedy lay-term match must not outrank a class the building demonstrably holds'). The register then declined honestly about ITSELF and the decline was narrated as a fact about the building. | TRACED 2026-09-29, and the concept resolver was NOT at fault. The log carries both facts: `[concept_resolver] semantic match 'Where can I park and do I need a permit?' -> ['parking_availability']` and, 27ms later, `[sparql] whole-register fetch: Permit (15 instances, 9 fields) - no SPARQL generated`. `held_record_class` ranks record classes on the question's words alone and never consults the resolved concept, so a keyword match on 'permit' took a question the resolver had already understood. The building holds Parking_Level_Ground and EV_Charger_1 ('EV Charging Station 1 - Parking Level'), so the denial is false as well as off-topic.
Fix_Approach: Not attempted here: the fix is a routing/record-matching change and orchestrator/services/routing_contract.py is owned by another task this session. Candidate: a permit question that also names a PLACE-kind amenity the building holds should not be claimed by a work-permit register, and a register decline must not be narrated as 'the building's records do not contain' when another held record carries the term. | DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED 2026-09-29, with the reason recorded rather than the work half-done: the register lane answers a dozen questions in the evidence pack, and this was found with five other changes already made and none yet verified live. Stacking a sixth change onto an unverified lane is how a session ends with everything moved and nothing proved. Shape of the fix when it is taken: `_whole_register` has `state`, so it can read the resolved concepts; stand down when a concept resolved, the chosen register's vocabulary shares none of that concept's lay terms, AND the concept's classes have instances in this building -- three conditions, so a register that genuinely answers still claims.
Verification: Reproduced live 2026-09-29 verbatim: 'The building's records do not contain any information about parking spaces or whether a parking permit is required' followed by 15 permit-to-work records. Route: intent=metadata -> metadata, overrides=[]. | RE-ASKED 2026-09-30 verbatim. THE FALSE DENIAL IS GONE: the answer no longer opens "The building's records do not contain any information about parking spaces or whether a parking permit is required". THE MISROUTING IS NOT: the turn is still claimed by the PermitToWork register (route intent=metadata -> metadata, overrides=[]) and answers with 15 permit-to-work records broken down by status and kind, then every record's location (hot works, roof access, ceiling void, confined space, electrical isolation, work at height). Not one word about parking. So the honesty half of this row is fixed and the routing half -- the greedy lay-term match on 'permit' outranking a class the building demonstrably holds -- is untouched, as this row's Fix_Approach said it deliberately left it. The three-condition stand-down described there is still the shape of the fix.

Title: The parking-cost decline points at the expenditure ledger, not at the record that speaks to parking
Description: 'How much does it cost to park here for a day?' (evidence pack #67) declines against the 24-line cost register: 'The register does not contain any information about parking costs ... 19 open, 3 query, 2 closed'. True, and a mis-pointer: ontosage:CostLine is what the building PAYS OUT (electricity supply, cleaning contract, lift maintenance, security staffing), owned by 'Estates Finance Business Partner' and authorised by 'Cardiff University Finance - Estates ledger extract'. It is not a price list and could not hold a visitor tariff whatever was added to it. Meanwhile bldg:Cap_transport_parking does speak to paying to park - permit required for staff at the Corbett Road car park, on-street pay-and-display nearby - and is never reached.
Root_Cause: The whole-register path resolves a record class from the word 'cost' before the capability lane gets a turn, so the closest-record pointer is chosen from the registers rather than from everything the building holds.
Fix_Approach: MITIGATED rather than fixed. The absence is now a STATED fact on bldg:Amenity_Parking_GroundLevel - answerText says no parking charge is recorded, names the two registers checked, and gives the arrangement the building does record - so the question is answerable from the amenity the 'where can I park' lane already reads. The pointer itself is unchanged, for the same reason as BUG-894.
Verification: tests/test_parking_cost_is_a_recorded_absence.py (10 pass / 6 skip); the absence phrasing and the no-invented-price tripwire were both shown to FAIL when a GBP 4.50/day rate was injected, and to pass when it was removed. The TTL edit is in input/bldg1_amenity_stated.ttl and is NOT yet in GraphDB: ttl_uploader runs at boot and this session could not restart the orchestrator.

Title: The safety-critical checklist looked for three defibrillator classes that do not exist
Description: config/safety_critical_facts.yaml listed classes [Defibrillator, AedPoint, AED] for the defibrillator fact. Verified 2026-09-29: none of the three is declared in ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl (0 occurrences each) and none has a single instance in the live graph. The class this ontology actually declares is ontosage:FirstAidPoint. scripts/owner_facts_report.py::held() counts instances of ontosage:<cls>, so the fact could only ever be matched by lay term and would report 0 instances however many defibrillators a building declared. [renumbered from CAVEAT-893 on 2026-09-29: four parallel agents issued that number twice]
Root_Cause: The checklist names classes as strings and nothing checks that the strings correspond to declared classes. A config that points at a non-existent class fails silently and in the WRONG DIRECTION for this file: it under-reports what the building holds, on the one page whose own note says 'minutes matter; a wrong position is worse than none'.
Fix_Approach: FirstAidPoint added at the head of the list; the three unused names kept so a building that types its devices differently still matches. THE WIDER FIX IS OWED: a test, or a check inside owner_facts_report, that every class named in this file is declared in the schema -- the other facts in the file have not been audited and may name phantom classes too.
Verification: Counted occurrences in ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl and instance counts via SPARQL against the live graph for all four class names. Found by the W0-08 agent while fixing BUG-858 and verified independently before changing anything.

Title: 'Which sensors stopped reporting and when?' answered with a confident all-clear
Description: Asked live 2026-09-29, one question, two non-answers. 'Which sensors have stopped reporting, and when was each last seen?' -> 'To determine which sensors have stopped reporting, we would need a complete log that shows the most recent timestamp for every sensor ... With the information at hand, I can't identify any sensors that have gone silent.' The reworded 'Which sensors stopped reporting and when?' -> 'All of the sensors listed have a reading at the most recent timestamp, 2026-09-29 16:33:41. Because every sensor in the dataset reports a value at that time, none of them appear to have stopped reporting.' The second is the dangerous one: an all-clear over a building that at that moment held a sensor 12.9 days dead (Water Main Flow Sensor, sensor_data_synth, last row 2026-09-16 17:22:39 UTC, confirmed by hand with the MySQL session pinned to +00:00). Pack #31. Both turns routed intent=sensor_data -> sparql, with no routing rule fired. [renumbered from BUG-895 on 2026-09-29: four parallel agents issued that number twice]
Root_Cause: A window of readings cannot evidence silence: a sensor that stopped is simply absent from it. So any lane that reasons from readings can only ever conclude that everything is fine, and that is verbatim what it concluded. The 'complete log' the first answer said it would need is one query -- MAX(timestamp) GROUP BY sensor -- and no lane owned it. The pieces existed and nothing joined them: MySQLNarrowAdapter.latest_by_uuid, /api/v1/admin/sensors/health (admin only, and reports the wide store as 'not probed per sensor'), and building_metrics.reporting_uuids_by_store, which answers fresh/not-fresh and never WHEN.
Fix_Approach: W3-05.
