New orchestrator/services/sensor_silence.py derives last-seen per declared sensor from whatever stores the building registers, and partitions into reporting / silent / never-reported / not-probed -- four different facts needing four different actions. New MySQLAdapter.latest_by_uuid_exhaustive answers per sensor over a WIDE table (sensors are columns) in two passes: a window-restricted scan that is free, then an unbounded one for only the columns the first left empty, so cost is proportional to how much is wrong rather than to the size of the building. observability.is_silence_question routes the question to the observability lane, which already owns questions about the system's reach.
Verification: Derivation run against the REAL store from inside the orchestrator container: 3,543 declared sensors across 21 stores in 0.6-0.7s; 3,542 reporting, 1 silent, 0 never, 0 not-probed. The one silent sensor and its timestamp were then confirmed independently in MySQL (28,134 rows, first 2026-07-16 14:54:59, last 2026-09-16 17:22:39, session time_zone '+00:00'). Cost measured both ways on the 683-column wide table: window-restricted 0.0s, unbounded 136.3s -- which is why the second pass is only ever paid for the silent set. tests/test_sensor_silence.py, 42 pass. LIVE TURN IS OWED: the orchestrator could not be restarted this session, so the new code is not in the running process and the question has not been re-asked end to end.

Title: The building declares design occupancy twice, and for half the overlap the two disagree
Description: Read from the live graph 2026-09-29. 29 spaces carry <building>:maxOccupancy and 19 carry hbco:roomCapacity. Six carry both, and THREE of the six disagree: Room 1.04 (Common Area / Atrium) 50 vs 25, Room 4.01 (Research Laboratory) 25 vs 20, Room 5.01 (Research Laboratory) 25 vs 20. ontosage:capacityBasis, the property that would say where a figure came from, has ZERO triples in the live graph -- it exists only in the held-back room-identity correction. So nothing in the model says which number is authoritative. Separately, Room 5.08 'Academic Office' carries roomCapacity 50, which the held-back drawing work already flags as implausible.
Root_Cause: Two authoring passes added the same fact under two property names without either reconciling them or declaring a basis. W3-04 asked for a THIRD name (ontosage:designOccupancy), which would have made it three.
Fix_Approach:
OWNER DECISION TAKEN 2026-09-30: one room, one occupancy record, on the predicate the SHARED SCHEMA declares — the owner's instruction being that the schema is the same for every building and only the entities differ.
WHY `hbco:roomCapacity` AND NOT `<building>:maxOccupancy`, which had MORE rooms (29 v 19): `hbco:roomCapacity` is declared in `ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl` ('Estimated or certified occupant capacity of a room or space (persons)', range xsd:integer). `<building>:maxOccupancy` existed only in this building's namespace, declared in bldg1_enhancements.ttl with the note 'used where Brick has no property' — which is no longer true. A predicate in a building's own namespace means the next building needs a different one and the system has to guess which: design contract #3. Count was the wrong tiebreak; namespace was the right one.
`rec:maxOccupancy` (RealEstateCore) appears in the Brick files' SHACL shapes and is NOT touched — OCBV aligns to REC by SKOS mapping only, deliberately.
WHICH VALUE, WHERE THEY DISAGREED (1.04 50 v 25, 4.01 25 v 20, 5.01 25 v 20). NEITHER side was authoritative: the enrichment file's own header says 'Values are approximate; authoritative data should be obtained from Estates' and every roomCapacity carries rdfs:comment 'estimated', while the maxOccupancy figures carry no basis at all. So there was no better side to pick, and the schema already said what to do about that. `ontosage:capacityBasis`: 'A capacity with no basis cannot be told apart from a certified fire capacity, and an estimate quoted as a limit is a safety claim nobody made.' THE RULE APPLIED: take the LOWER figure, because exceeding a recorded limit is the dangerous direction, and record the basis AND the superseded figure on every reconciled room so nothing is lost and the reconciliation stays auditable.
`ontosage:capacityBasis` had ZERO triples in the live graph before this — it existed only in the schema, which is exactly why the conflict had no way to be expressed. All 42 rooms now carry one.
MECHANICS: new `input/bldg1_occupancy_capacity.ttl` (42 records, generated); 29 room triples and the property declaration removed from bldg1_enhancements.ttl; 19 roomCapacity lines moved out of bldg1_enrichment_metadata.ttl, where the space function and the 'estimated' comment stay because they are facts about the ROOM, not about its capacity. Both source files carry a note saying where the figures went and why. The uploader PUTs into the same named graph, so the retired triples are gone rather than shadowed.
Verification:
GRAPH, after restart: `hbco:roomCapacity` 42 rooms, `ontosage:capacityBasis` 42 rooms, `maxOccupancy` ZERO — one predicate, one record per room, every one with a basis. rdflib parses all three files; 42 capacity triples over 42 DISTINCT subjects, so no room carries two.
LIVE 2026-09-30, caches flushed: 'What is the design occupancy of room 5.01?' -> 'Room 5.01 — Research Laboratory has a design occupancy of **20** people' (the conflicted 25-v-20 wording is gone). 'What is the maximum occupancy of room 2.15?' -> 'has a design occupancy of **40** people', matching the graph.
ONE MISTAKE OF MINE, caught by the check rather than by luck: re-running the generator AFTER the retirement script produced 0 records and silently wrote an EMPTY file over a correct one, because the generator read the live files the retirement had just stripped. Backups were taken first, the generator now reads THOSE, and a comment on it says why. The validation that caught it — 42 records over 42 distinct subjects — is the one worth keeping.
WHAT THIS ROW DID NOT ESTABLISH, and BUG-1137 now owns it: the reconciliation chose WHICH PREDICATE and, where two figures disagreed, WHICH OF THE TWO. It never asked whether either figure is plausible, and measured against room area 20 of the 42 surviving capacities are below 1.0 m2 per person -- Room2.15 declares 40 people in 7.83 m2. So 'one room, one record, with its basis' is delivered and correct as far as it goes; 'the number is right' is a different claim that this row does not support and should not be read as supporting. The `capacityBasis` string on every one of the 42 says 'estimated ... not certified -- Estates holds the authoritative figure', which is the honest form of exactly this gap.

Title: A declared design limit answered from a sensor's observed peak
Description: Asked live 2026-09-29: 'What is the maximum occupancy of room 2.15?' -> '**30.00 people** The sensor "Room 2.15 - Seminar Room occupancy [persons]" recorded a peak of 30.00 people, the highest value observed for that location. This figure represents the maximum occupancy captured by the sensor.' The graph declares <building>:maxOccupancy 40 for Room 2.15. The answer is a maximum OBSERVATION presented in bold as the room's maximum occupancy, and the declared limit is never mentioned. The two questions have different answers and different consequences: one is a statistic, the other is what the room is allowed to hold.
Root_Cause: 'maximum occupancy' routed intent=analytics -> sparql and was read as MAX(value) over the occupancy series. No lane consulted the declared figure, because until W3-04 nothing in orchestrator/ read maxOccupancy or roomCapacity at all -- grep found them only in scripts and in a held-back test.
Fix_Approach:
THE DECLARED FIGURE IS NOW STATED BY COMPOSITION, NOT BY HINT -- and the narrator's contradicting claim SURVIVES. Both halves matter, so both are recorded.
WHAT WAS WRONG WITH THE PREVIOUS FIX: the declared figure was already being computed. The log showed [analytics_node] design occupancy for 'Room 2.15 - Seminar Room' with maxOccupancy 40 on the bus, offered to the narrator as a RECIPE HINT -- and the narrator answered '30.00 people' from the sensor anyway. That is the BUG-937 lesson in a more dangerous place: a figure a narrator can get wrong is a figure it should not be deriving, and a capacity a fire or booking decision rests on is not one to leave to wording.
WHAT IS DONE: _response_node now states the declared figure itself. It is there rather than in _analytics_node because the hook lived inside that node, so 'design occupancy of room 5.01' -- which routed sensor_data -> sparql -- never reached it and produced a FALSE DENIAL (the design occupancy value itself is not recorded in the data) of a figure the graph declares twice. _response_node is the one place every lane passes. Gated on the question naming a capacity PROPERTY (reusing DESIGN_OCCUPANCY_TERMS, so 'maximum occupancy' and 'seating capacity' fire and a live count does not), and it REPLACES a decline rather than prepending to one.
TWO OF MY OWN ATTEMPTS AT THE SKIP CONDITION WERE WRONG, which is worth recording: (i) publication_gate.is_decline returns FALSE for the commonest decline this system emits, so it cannot be used to spot one here -- logged as CAVEAT-952. (ii) Skipping when any declared figure appeared anywhere in the answer is not a test of anything: room 5.01 declares 20 and 25, and the sensor text contains 'at 25 Sep 01:22' -- a DATE -- so the check concluded the capacity had been stated. It is now idempotent on the exact sentence instead.
WHAT REMAINS (BUG-953): the narration still asserts the observed peak AS the limit, so the answer now contains the correct declared figure AND a contradiction of it.
Verification: LIVE 2026-09-30, after restart, caches flushed, three questions. 'What is the maximum occupancy of room 2.15?' now OPENS with 'Room 2.15 - Seminar Room has a design occupancy of 40 people.' (graph: maxOccupancy 40) and then still says 'the maximum occupancy ... is 30.00 people'. 'What is the design occupancy of room 5.01?' now OPENS with 'has no single design occupancy on record: the building states 25 under maxOccupancy, 20 under roomCapacity ... I will not pick one' -- the FALSE DENIAL IS GONE -- and then still says 'The design occupancy for Room 5.01 is 30 people'. 'How many people are in room 2.15 right now?' is untouched, which is the guard working: a live count must not be led by a capacity.

Title: One planner answer gave two occupancy figures for the same room, 190x apart
Description: Asked live 2026-09-29: 'How does observed occupancy compare with the design occupancy of room 1.25?' The answer ran three sections. 'Sensor Readings' said the room 1.25 occupancy sensor recorded 27.0 with an average of 27.0 over 420 readings. 'Comparison' said, of the SAME room, 'a latest reading of 4 401.86 occupants at 2025-12-17 00:24:26 ... the mean occupancy was 5 178.52 occupants, the median 5 194.09, the minimum 294.91, the maximum 9 993.36' -- for a seminar room the graph declares at 20 people, with fractional 'occupants' and a nine-month-old timestamp. 'Spatial Information' then appended a table of all 354 spaces in the building. Both numeric sections also said the design occupancy was 'not provided in the data' while the graph declares 20.
Root_Cause:
ROOT CAUSE: A STALE FILE ON THE CODE-EXECUTOR'S DISK, not a fabrication. `_get_template_code` builds code reading `/app/outputs/data/<data_filename>`; the default is ONE SHARED NAME, `current_data.json`; only `workflow/_orchestrator.py` ever WRITES a file and it writes a per-conversation one, while `planner_agent._run_analytics` passes no filename at all. That file is 16,595 bytes, LAST MODIFIED 2025-12-17 00:24:56, and holds 119 rows of `Oxygen_O2_Percentage_Gas_Sensor_5.05`. The turn's real 360 rows were prepended as `raw_data_json` and never looked at. No store holds any row dated 2025-12-17.
FIX: the template prefers `raw_data_json`, and `analyze` replaces the shared default with a per-call name AND writes its own rows there.
THE TWO DID NOT SHARE A CAUSE, and separating them cost one extra ask rather than a day of theory. BUG-898 came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to two decimal places a day apart, on a series written to every minute; BUG-954's figures moved between asks. **A model does not repeat an invention; a file does.** That single observation split a 190x discrepancy on one quantity into a narration defect and a stale-file defect.
Fix_Approach: Not attempted. Needs the planner turn traced to see which lane produced the 4,401.86 series and what it actually bound. W3-04 fixes only the third defect in this answer (the missing design figure).
Verification: LIVE 2026-09-30 after restart: room 1.25's Comparison section now reads 13-17 persons, mean 14.78, agreeing with its own Sensor Readings section (13.0-17.0, mean 14.8). Was: 'a latest reading of 4,401.86 occupants... mean 5,178.52'. THE STALE FILE WAS LEFT IN PLACE DELIBERATELY -- this is the fix working with the trap still present, which is a stronger check than removing the file would have been. One new test EXECUTES the generated template and asserts 4401/5178 are absent from its output.

Title: config/recipes.yaml carried one building's six floor capacities as prose
Description: The shared recipe file's busyness_threshold recipe described itself as classifying a space 'based on current occupancy vs. known capacity. Capacities: floor0=120, floor1=55, floor2=75, floor3=65, floor4=55, floor5=195.' Those are bldg1's floors, in the file every building loads. Design contract rule 3. [renumbered from CAVEAT-896 on 2026-09-29: four parallel agents issued that number twice]
Root_Cause: A capacity was written down where it was convenient rather than read from the building that has it. Nothing ever consumed the numbers -- the recipe's params carry only the percentage bands -- so the literal sat inert and invisible, which is why no test caught it: scripts/check_building_literals.py does not scan config/.
Fix_Approach: Replaced with a pointer to orchestrator/services/design_occupancy.py, which reads the declared capacity from the active building's graph. A wider fix is owed: the literal guard should scan config/ as well as the five code trees, since this is exactly the kind of literal it exists to find.
Verification: scripts/check_building_literals.py still reports clean (0 ERROR, 78 INFO) -- which is the point: it reported clean BEFORE the fix too, because config/ is out of its scope.

Title: sensor_data_synth holds 69 streams no sensor map declares, and some stopped with the declared one
Description: Measured 2026-09-29: sensor_data_synth holds 106 distinct uuids while the active building's sensor map declares 37 for that store. Ordering the table by MAX(datetime) ascending, the five oldest are undeclared uuids (00000000-ac02-...-000000000001 through ...005), every one frozen at 2026-09-16 17:22:39 -- the same instant as the one DECLARED silent sensor, the Water Main Flow Sensor. Several stores show the same pattern: plant_data 88 distinct against 44 declared, occupancy_data 514 against 512, light_data 242 against 241, noise_data 236 against 235, water_data 13 against 12. [renumbered from CAVEAT-897 on 2026-09-29: four parallel agents issued that number twice]
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. Either the publisher writes streams the graph does not declare, or the graph declared them and no longer does. The common timestamp suggests one publisher subset was stopped on 2026-09-16 and never restarted, and the fact that only ONE of its streams is declared is why only one is visible to any check.
Fix_Approach: Out of scope for W3-05, which answers about DECLARED sensors -- an undeclared stream is a different question ('what is in the store that the building does not claim'), and reporting it as a silent sensor would name uuids no one can act on. scripts/reconcile_watched_and_fed.py already exists for the reconciliation.
Verification: COUNT(DISTINCT uuid) per narrow table against the declared set from input/.sensor_map.cache.json, and MAX(datetime) GROUP BY uuid ORDER BY ASC on sensor_data_synth, both run inside the orchestrator container with the MySQL session at +00:00. | RE-MEASURED 2026-09-30: STILL REPRODUCES, every figure UNCHANGED. COUNT(DISTINCT uuid) in-container with the MySQL session at +00:00: sensor_data_synth 106, plant_data 88, occupancy_data 514, light_data 242, noise_data 236, water_data 13 -- identical to the 2026-09-29 measurement, against 37 / 44 / 512 / 241 / 235 / 12 declared. Ordering sensor_data_synth by MAX(datetime) ascending, the eight oldest-last-seen uuids are still the undeclared 00000000-ac02-0000-0000-00000000000{1..6} and 00000000-ac03-0000-0000-00000000000{1,2}, EVERY ONE still frozen at exactly 2026-09-16 17:22:39 -- eleven days later, not one new row. Nothing restarted them and nothing declared them. scripts/reconcile_watched_and_fed.py remains the right instrument. | 2026-09-30: this row's HEADLINE WAS WRONG and the correction points at a P1. It reported 69 undeclared streams in `sensor_data_synth`; the graph declares all 106, so the true undeclared count there is ZERO (building-wide it is 48). The '37 declared' came from `.sensor_map.cache.json`, which is a cache, not a declaration. And the frozen streams are not 8 but **70, every one of them a DUPLICATE** whose sensor carried a second live reference -- which is BUG-531's live set, found by chasing this row. Retired there, not declared here: declaring a dead stream would have made a silent fault into a stated one.

Title: A week-over-week comparison answers about two weeks that are NOT the two asked for, and reverses the direction of the change
Description: Live 2026-09-29 (ISO W40, Tue). 'Compare energy use this week against last week.' answered: '**The daily average energy use FELL by 426 kWh per day, from 2,239 kWh per day in 2026-W38 to 1,813 kWh per day in 2026-W39 (a 19.0 % DECREASE).**' Measured directly against sensordb.energy_data with the session pinned to +00:00, summed over the 6 meters that carry rows in each window: this week (W40) 3764 kWh over 1.689 d = 2229 per day; last week (W39) 12621 kWh over 6.948 d = 1816 per day. The true change is UP 22.7 %. The answer says down 19.0 %.
Root_Cause: CORRECTED 2026-09-29. My first entry here guessed 'the week label is wrong and is used as the sort key'. That was wrong, and the orchestrator log disproves it in one line (lessons #145 -- I had verified my reasoning, not the code). What actually happens: (1) THE FETCH IGNORES THE PERIOD THE QUESTION NAMED. The SQL is `datetime >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) ... ORDER BY datetime DESC LIMIT 1000` per uuid -- a fixed 30 days, not 'this week and last week'. (2) THE ROW CAP THEN CLIPS THE WINDOW. The lane's own guard fired: '[sql] group energy_data returned exactly its 1000-row limit -- the set is TRUNCATED'. 1000 newest rows per meter is about the last 11 days, so the data actually seen starts mid-W38. (3) THE WEEK THE USER ASKED ABOUT IS THEN DROPPED. W40 holds 1.7 days, fails _complete_buckets, and is excluded as PARTIAL, leaving whole=[W38,W39]. So 'this week' never entered the comparison and the answer is about 14-27 Sep. This also explains the '77 of 168 hours': that is W38 cut off at its START by the row cap, not a week still filling. (4) The 19.0% DECREASE follows: W38 (2239/day) to W39 (1813/day) is a real fall across those two weeks; this week against last week is 2229 vs 1816, a 22.7% RISE.
Fix_Approach: Two of the three defects fixed; (A) left open as BUG-939. (B) `_names_this_against_last(question, size)`: when the question NAMES its two periods of the SAME unit, the two compared are ordered[-2] and ordered[-1] -- the current one and the one before it -- instead of the two newest COMPLETE buckets. The current period is partial by definition, so `_complete_buckets` always discarded it; that rule is right for 'how has this changed' (BUG-627) and wrong for 'this week against last week', and it is now narrowed rather than removed. Safe because the partial period is compared AS A RATE by the `by_rate` machinery that already existed, so a shorter period is never reported as a smaller total. A period asked for by name is also no longer listed as 'excluded as partial'. (C) A short bucket at the OLD end is TRUNCATED, not in progress: the two wordings are split, and the older-end text tells the narrator explicitly that the period is NOT still in progress and that its shortness is a fact about the QUERY, not about the building.
Verification: Offline: 20 tests, incl. ten parametrised cases separating a named pair from a single period, from a mismatched pair ('this week against last month'), and from the generic change question BUG-627 is about; plus 115 pass across every existing test that imports series_summary, so the by-rate and complete-bucket behaviour is unchanged. LIVE 2026-09-29 after rebuild, caches flushed, fresh chat: 'Compare energy use this week against last week' now answers '**Energy use INCREASED by 406 kWh per day from 1,813 kWh/day in 2026-W39 to 2,219 kWh/day in 2026-W40 (+22.4 %)**' and adds '2026-W40 covers only 41 of 168 hours'. Independently measured from sensordb.energy_data: 1,816 -> 2,229 per day, +22.7%, and 41.6 hours elapsed in W40. The weeks named are the weeks asked for, the sign is right, and the coverage caveat is on the current week.
Refs: W2-03; lessons #139 (the denominator), #145 (verify the code, not the intent); BUG-883; BUG-627 (bucketing a measurement window as a building change)

Title: A floor comparison miscomputes a spread from its own stated range and then draws the opposite conclusion from it
Description: Live 2026-09-29. 'Is floor 3 warmer than floor 4?' -> 'Floor 3 recorded a mean temperature of 23 C with a range from 20.6 C to 25.2 C, while Floor 4 recorded the same mean of 23 C but a slightly broader range from 20.4 C to 25.4 C. The spread on Floor 4 is 4.0 C compared to 4.6 C on Floor 3, indicating a marginally wider variation on Floor 4.' From its OWN numbers: floor 4 is 25.4-20.4 = 5.0, not 4.0. And 4.0 < 4.6, so even the wrong figure contradicts the clause it is offered as evidence for. Two errors in one sentence, both checkable without touching the database. THE VERDICT ITSELF IS CORRECT and is the thing BUG-885 was opened about: it now says 'They are tied' where it once asserted 'Floor 3 is warmer' twice in bold from a 0.06 C gap.
Root_Cause: TRACED. `series_summary.summarise_groups` handed the narrator a mean and a range per group and nothing else, so the spread was a subtraction left to prose. The means and ranges were right; only the derived figure was wrong, and then the interpretive clause was drawn from the wrong figure and contradicted even that. Same shape as BUG-624, where a comparison left to the narration described the same 21 rows two different ways.
Fix_Approach: Compute the spread where min and max are computed and hand it over: 'range 20.4 to 25.4 C (spread 5.0 C)'. The range is still given -- the spread replaces a subtraction, not the extremes, because 'how warm does it get' needs the max. The existing 'quote these; do not recompute them' instruction is unchanged.
Verification: Offline 23 tests + 115 across every test importing series_summary. LIVE 2026-09-29 after restart, caches flushed: 'Is floor 3 warmer than floor 4?' now reads 'ranging from 20.6 C to 25.2 C, a spread of 4.62 C' and '20.9 C to 25.4 C, a spread of 4.47 C'. Both subtractions are right, and the interpretive clause now agrees with them ('Floor 4 has ... a slightly lower spread'). The verdict is still the correct 'tied', so BUG-885 has not regressed.

Title: A room-scoped comparison labels its group '5' for a question about room 5.01 -- readable as floor 5
Description: Live 2026-09-29, immediately after BUG-879 was fixed. 'How does the temperature in room 5.01 this week compare with last week?' answers correctly and labels every figure '5 mean', '5 peak', '5 lowest'. The same fix on the CO2 question labels them 'HVAC Zone 5.01 mean', which is unambiguous. '5' can be read as floor 5, which is precisely the scope confusion the regrouping half of BUG-879 exists to prevent.
Root_Cause: DEEPER THAN A LABEL, and the first fix missed it. `_group_key(f,'room')` returning a bare '5' was only half: the real fault is that this question does not PARSE to an intent at all, so it is claimed by the bare-measurand SUMMARY path, which hardcodes group='floor'. BUG-879's regrouping guard fired only on group=='building', so it was skipped entirely, `_group_key(f,'floor')` returned the FLOOR NUMBER, and every figure was keyed '5 mean' over a group holding ONE sensor. A room's reading wearing a floor's name is BUG-883 exactly, not a cosmetic defect -- so this is P2, not P3.
Fix_Approach: Two parts. (1) `_group_key(f,'room')` rejects an all-digit room and falls back to the sensor label, never to 'building'; '5.01', '5A', 'Room 5' are kept. (2) The BUG-879 regroup guard is widened from `group == 'building'` to `group != _grp and group in ('building','floor')`, so a question naming a ROOM groups by room whatever the claiming path assumed, while a floor question already grouped by floor is left alone. NOTE: the first attempt at that condition used a CHAINED comparison (`x in (...) != (...)`), which Python reads as `(x in ...) and ((...) != ...)` -- the right half compares a tuple to a bool and is always true -- so it silently reduced to 'any building-or-floor group' and regrouped floor->floor. Caught by a truth table before deploying; a test now pins the shape.
Verification: Offline 32 tests in that file (incl. a 6-row truth table and a guard against the chained comparison) + 399 across every test touching aggregate_lane. LIVE 2026-09-29 after restart, caches flushed: BOTH room questions now label every figure 'HVAC Zone 5.01 mean/peak/lowest'; '5' is gone.
Refs: BUG-879; BUG-883 (a figure claiming a scope it does not have)

Title: The publication gate did not see a four-digit reading without a thousands separator
Description: _CLAIM_NUMBER's integer part was \d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*, which requires a COMMA before a fourth digit. So has_quantitative_claim('CO2 is 1,240 ppm') was True and has_quantitative_claim('CO2 is 1200 ppm') was False. An unseparated four-digit ppm value is the commonest reading in this building, and publication_gate.evaluate returns publish=True whenever it finds no quantitative claim -- so an unverified four-digit figure went out unchanged on a FAILED verification, which is the one thing that module exists to prevent.
Root_Cause: Every fixture in the gate's own test file writes the separator ('745.3 ppm', '1,030 ppm'), so the gate's tests exercised only the shape the pattern matched. The hole was found by the W5-01 redaction tests, which fed it plain integers.
Fix_Approach: Widened the integer part to \d+(?:,\d{3})* -- separated forms still match. The change makes the gate WITHHOLD more on failed verification, which is the conservative direction and its stated purpose; it cannot cause an answer to be asserted that was not asserted before.
Verification: tests/test_a_failed_verification_withholds_the_claim.py::test_a_four_digit_reading_without_a_thousands_separator_is_a_claim (4 cases). The whole file re-run: 52 passed, including test_an_identifier_is_not_a_measurement, which is the guard against widening too far. NOT re-asked live -- the stack is down.

Title: Long-term memory was read and written on /v1/chat/completions and on no other route
Description: Read from orchestrator/main.py on 2026-09-29: TurnMemoryService was constructed in exactly one function (openai_chat_completions); save_turn was called twice, both inside it; get_older_context once, likewise. So /chat, /chat/stream and the /stream websocket stored NO turn and read NO memory. Open WebUI uses /v1 and the regression probe uses /chat, so the feature was live on the endpoint that is demonstrated and absent from the endpoint that is measured. Every offline test passed, because every offline test exercised /v1 or the service in isolation.
Root_Cause: The same shape as BUG-655 one section earlier in the same file: a capability added at one entry point and never carried to the other three. A copy per route is how three of them came to be missing it.
Fix_Approach: Two helpers in main.py -- _inject_session_summary and _save_turn_memory -- called by all four routes plus _run_workflow_as_job (the /chat report-offload path, which returns before /chat's own save). main.CHAT_ENTRY_POINTS declares the set; a test reads it, checks each named function calls both helpers, and FAILS when a chat route exists in main.py that the set does not name.
Verification: tests/test_the_session_summary_rides_every_chat_entry_point.py -- 31 passed. Sixteen of them drive the REAL routes through the ASGI app (BUG-655's harness, reused) and assert what the workflow was handed. NOT re-asked live.

Title: The long-term memory window was a cliff: turn 3 was gone by turn 60
Description: get_older_context ran ORDER BY turn_index DESC OFFSET 20 LIMIT 30. At turn 60 that returns turns 40 down to 11 and turns 1-10 are dropped with no trace. W5-01's acceptance -- 'a 60-turn conversation still answers a question about turn 3' -- could not be met by construction, and nothing said so, because the block that came back looked healthy.
Root_Cause: The reader truncated where it should have compressed. A fixed window over a growing conversation has no failure mode that anything observes.
Fix_Approach: orchestrator/services/session_summary.py: the newest DETAIL_TURNS older turns keep a line each; everything older collapses into one bounded line naming what those turns were ABOUT, ordered by FIRST appearance (the detail window already covers the recent end, so the compressed head's job is the old end). When more subjects exist than fit, the line says how many were left out. Renamed to get_session_summary so no caller keeps the old semantics by accident.
Verification: tests/test_a_remembered_turn_carries_no_figure.py::test_turn_three_survives_to_turn_sixty and test_the_oldest_subjects_are_the_ones_the_compressed_line_keeps. Bounds pinned against 500 turns of 10,000-character questions. 33 tests in that file. NOT re-asked live.

Title: The memory block /v1 built was injected where no reader could ever see it
Description: /v1 prepended its older-context block as a system Message at index 0 of state.messages. Nothing in orchestrator/ matches on role == 'system' (checked by a test, not by eye), and both readers of state.messages take the LAST few entries: ContextManager.prune_messages(max_messages=5) for the classification prompt and format_conversation_history(msgs, max_messages=6) for the co-reference rewrite. A block at index 0 is therefore dropped by every reader as soon as the conversation is longer than three turns -- which is exactly when long-term memory is the point. Worse, had it ever been inside the window, format_conversation_history labels every non-user message 'Assistant', so the model would have read it as something the assistant said.
Root_Cause: Delivery was never checked. agent-patterns rule 5 records the same failure for the observability lane: routing and execution are automatic, delivery is not, and the node's own tests passed the whole time.
Fix_Approach: The summary goes on the bus under its own reserved key, session_summary, written before the graph runs and cleared by _response_node; it is consumed by dialogue_agent.rewrite_to_standalone, whose six-message history is the reader that most needs it. The system-message injection is removed, and any block left in a restored Redis history is stripped.
Verification: tests/test_the_session_summary_rides_every_chat_entry_point.py:: test_the_summary_is_not_prepended_as_a_system_message_any_more, test_nothing_in_the_orchestrator_reads_a_system_message_out_of_the_state, test_the_rewrite_prompt_carries_the_summary_when_there_is_one. NOT re-asked live: whether recall actually improves a 60-turn conversation needs the stack.

Title: A seventeen-turn hole between the raw window and the summary, because a message count was used as a turn offset
Description: The reader was called with skip_recent=settings.CONVERSATION_MAX_MESSAGES (20). That setting counts MESSAGES held in Redis. skip_recent is an offset in TURNS. The raw history that actually reaches a prompt is six messages -- three turns. So turns 4 through 20 appeared in NEITHER the raw window nor the summary, and both halves reported themselves healthy.
Root_Cause: Two units with the same name. Nothing converted between them and nothing compared the two windows against each other.
Fix_Approach: session_summary.RECENT_TURNS_KEPT_RAW = 3, named for what it is and documented against the six-message window it matches: three user messages plus three replies. It is the default for get_session_summary, so a caller cannot re-introduce the mismatch by passing the wrong constant.
Verification: tests/test_a_remembered_turn_carries_no_figure.py::test_the_skipped_turns_are_the_ones_the_raw_history_still_shows. NOT re-asked live.

Title: A measurement from twenty turns ago was fed back into the prompt with no time basis
Description: get_older_context carried result_summary[:150] per older turn, and _extract_result_summary fills result_summary from the analytics lane's formatted_response -- the ANSWER, verbatim, measurements included. The existing test pinned this as correct: test_conversation_memory_e2e.py required '22.3' in ctx for a row reading 'Room 5.02: 22.3 deg C current reading'. A remembered number restated as current is a fabrication (design contract #4), and it is the kind that reads perfectly.
Root_Cause: The summary was built from whatever the store happened to hold rather than from a decision about what may be remembered.
Fix_Approach: Structural, not a filter: TurnNote has no field for the answer. The only thing an answer may contribute is one token from a closed three-word vocabulary (answered / declined / no answer recorded), classified by publication_gate.is_decline -- the project's existing decline classifier, not a fifth copy. The user's own question is kept with measurement-shaped figures redacted by publication_gate.redact_quantities, so identifiers such as 'floor 3' and 'room 5.01' survive and '1,200 ppm' does not. The stale pin was rewritten to assert the opposite, with the reason in its docstring.
Verification: tests/test_a_remembered_turn_carries_no_figure.py -- 33 passed, including test_a_past_answers_numbers_never_reach_the_summary, test_a_turn_note_has_no_field_for_the_answer and test_the_rendered_summary_states_no_measurement_however_the_rows_are_built. NOT re-asked live.

Title: An unbounded LLM summary is generated on EVERY /v1 turn, thrown away, and injected into the classification prompt
Description: dialogue_agent.detect_intent runs: if len(state.messages) > 5 and (not state.summary or len(state.messages) % 5 == 0), state.summary = await context_manager.summarize_history(...). On /v1/chat/completions the ConversationState is rebuilt from the request every turn and state.summary is never loaded, so it is ALWAYS None -- the condition is true on every turn once there are six messages, and a whole extra LLM call runs per turn to produce a summary that is discarded at the end of it. The result is free text with no length bound, it carries whatever figures the answers carried, and it is prepended to the intent-classification prompt.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed further. It is a second, older rolling summary that predates W5-01 and lives on a different storage path (ConversationState.summary in Redis, which only the routes that restore state from Redis ever populate).
Fix_Approach: NOT ATTEMPTED HERE, deliberately. Removing or bounding it changes the inputs to the intent classifier, and the deploy plan makes routing work serial with the regression gate green before and after -- W6-01 (determinism) is the main thread's serial work on the same day. Worth measuring first: it is a candidate contributor to W6-02's 100 s median, and it is trivially checkable by counting REWRITE/summary calls in one /v1 turn's log.
Verification: Read from source: dialogue_agent.detect_intent (the summarize_history block) and openai_chat_completions (ConversationState built fresh each turn, summary never assigned). Not measured against a running stack.

Title: Every W5-01/W5-02 fix is FIXED-but-unverified-live
Description: BUG-904 through BUG-909 were all found by reading the source and pinned by offline tests. None has been re-asked against a running stack: bldg1 is parked and the containers are down, so no live conversation has been held to see whether a 60-turn session actually answers about turn 3, or whether the summary in the rewrite prompt changes any routing decision.
Root_Cause: Not a defect -- a statement of what the evidence does and does not cover. CLAUDE.md is explicit that this suite passed through every worst defect this project has had.
Fix_Approach: Owed: boot bldg1, flush resp_cache:* AND cache:sparql*, hold a conversation past 15 turns on /chat, then ask a question that refers back to turn 3, and read the orchestrator log for '[/chat] session summary injected'. Run scripts/regression_answerability.py before and after -- the rewrite prompt now carries extra text on follow-ups, and rewrite_is_safe is the only thing stopping a remembered room displacing a named one.
Verification: THE PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE LIVE CHECK HAS NOW BEEN DONE. This row says 'bldg1 is parked and the containers are down, so no live conversation has been held'. bldg1 was ACTIVE and the stack was UP throughout that session -- the agent that wrote this did not check. A live conversation was then held the same day: `scratchpad/memory_probe.py`, eight turns on /v1/chat/completions, ONE chat id, unique filler so nothing is served from resp_cache, every turn genuinely executed (33-58 s each). WHAT IT PROVED. The plumbing works: `[turn_memory] saved turn 1..8` and `[/v1/chat/completions] session summary injected (453 chars)` on the recall turn. W5-01 and W5-02 deliver what they claim. WHAT IT DISPROVED. Nothing CONSUMES the summary for a referent. Two defects came straight out of that run: BUG-940 (P1, a follow-up bound to a room the user never named -- fixed and verified the same day) and BUG-941 (a question about the CONVERSATION routed to a data lane, still open). PARTIALLY_FIXED rather than closed: BUG-904's widened claim pattern and BUG-906's pagination fix were exercised incidentally, not targeted, and W5-04's own long-conversation acceptance is still failing.
Refs: W5-01; W5-02; BUG-524 (a rewrite may add a referent, never change one)

Title: The time-series fetch ignores the period the question names, then a per-sensor row cap silently clips the window further
Description: Observed in the orchestrator log 2026-09-29 while diagnosing BUG-936. 'Compare energy use this week against last week' issued `WHERE datetime >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) ... ORDER BY datetime DESC LIMIT 1000` per uuid, and the lane's own guard then fired: '[sql] group energy_data returned exactly its 1000-row limit -- the set is TRUNCATED and its size is not a count of what exists'. So the analysed window was neither the 30 days requested nor the two weeks asked about, but roughly the newest 11 days -- whatever 1000 rows per meter happened to reach back to. BUG-936 made the COMPARISON pick the right two buckets out of whatever arrives; this row is about what arrives.
Root_Cause: Both the wide builder (sql_agent._build_union_sql) and the narrow adapter (mysql_narrow_adapter.build_timeseries_query) DO honour start_date/end_date when they are given -- the 30-day default is an `elif not end` fallback that fires only when neither bound is set. So the bounds were never passed. `start_date`, `end_date` and `time_range` are all on the bus for that turn (they appear in the intermediate_results key list), so what is not established is whether they were EMPTY or merely not forwarded. `requested_interval` exposes named_day, calendar_day_bounds and interval_hours but nothing that resolves a WEEK, let alone a pair of them, which is the likelier gap.
Fix_Approach: First ESTABLISH which it is -- dump start_date/end_date for that turn before changing anything. Then: resolve week/month/quarter bounds in `requested_interval` alongside the day ones, and pass them through. TREAD CAREFULLY: CLAUDE.md records three wrong 'fixes' in this area on 2026-09-12 and a withdrawn P1 on 2026-09-15, all from measuring MySQL through a non-UTC session. Every store is UTC; choose the LOCAL day/week a word names, convert its bounds with to_store, and convert back only for display. Separately, a truncated fetch should not be silently analysed: the truncation is already DETECTED and logged, so carry that fact to the lane and say the window is incomplete rather than presenting it as the period asked for.
Verification:
WINDOW HALF VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-30, caches flushed. 'Compare energy use this week against last week' now issues `datetime >= '2026-09-13 23:00:00'` and `<= '2026-10-04 22:59:59'` -- the UTC bounds of the local weeks, reaching one whole period further back on purpose -- and compares 2026-W39 -> 2026-W40, the two weeks actually asked for, at +15.4%. **ZERO truncation warnings in fifteen minutes of log**: with bounds set the per-uuid cap rises to 33,333 against ~1,400 rows available, so it no longer binds. The 2026-W37 sliver bucket predicted by CAVEAT-1005 appeared and was correctly disclosed as excluded ('only 24 readings'), and W40's partial coverage is stated ('54 of 168 hours').
THE TRUNCATION-DISCLOSURE HALF IS STILL OWED and is the load-bearing one: CAVEAT-1002 names the four lines in `_response_node`. The lane's own wording never reaches a reader when the answer is model prose, which is how 'Across ALL 1,000 readings' got published two lines below its own TRUNCATED guard.
Refs: BUG-936 (the comparison half, fixed); CLAUDE.md CLOCKS; BUG-403; BUG-540; lessons #103

Title: Per-turn latency could not be attributed from the container log, and now does not have to be
Description: W6-02. Profiling the register and metadata lanes by slicing the orchestrator log to a request's wall window gives numbers that are not measurements: while a second turn is in flight, one request's log lines close another's gaps. The SAME 18,609-character narration prompt was measured at 0.09 s, 0.44 s, 1.62 s and 57.80 s by that method. Every one of 48 measured requests had at least one other turn finishing inside its window, so there was no quiet stack to fall back on.
Root_Cause: The durations already existed and were discarded. _safe_node has recorded duration_ms per lane into intermediate_results['lane_outcomes'] since V12-19, but nothing published them: plan_trace carried the STEPS and no timings, and lane_outcomes never reached the HTTP payload. The two stages that bracket every turn, dialogue and response, were registered bare rather than through _safe_node and so were not recorded at all -- and they are the two largest on most questions (dialogue is 43.1% of measured wall clock).
Fix_Approach: _timed_node in workflow/_orchestrator.py wraps dialogue and response: it records the duration and RE-RAISES, so those two stages keep exactly the fail-closed semantics they had when registered bare (a test pins the re-raise). _stage_durations() turns lane_outcomes into per-stage rows, slowest first, one row per RUN rather than a sum per name so a retry is not reported as one slow call. build_plan_trace emits them as plan_trace.stage_ms. plan_trace_for_response() re-reads them at the HTTP boundary because the trace is assembled inside the response node, before that node's own duration exists. No new I/O and no new LLM call.
Verification: Live on a real turn: capability 4243 ms + dialogue 927 ms + response 399 ms against 5.70 s wall. Across 48 measured requests 313.5 s of 320.5 s wall is attributed (97.8%). tests/test_the_plan_trace_says_where_the_time_went.py 10/10; 45 related existing tests (plan_trace, autowire, wiring, reserved keys, turn outcome) pass. black + flake8 clean.
Refs: W6-02; V12-19 (lane_outcomes); BUG-510; CAVEAT-500 (a duration is not a property)

Title: The classification cache is consulted AFTER the work whose result it makes unnecessary
Description: dialogue_agent.detect_intent runs _retrieve_ontology_context (a GraphDB RAG fetch), then the summarize_history call of CAVEAT-910, then prune/format/_build_intent_detection_prompt -- and only then computes decision_cache_key and looks it up. On a cache HIT every one of those is discarded. Measured on 'Which teaching sessions are scheduled in Room 1.06?', whose intent came back as a cache hit in all four rounds: the dialogue stage cost 9.5 / 10.4 / 8.8 / 10.6 s against a wall median of 11.16 s, of which the RAG fetch alone was 4.27 s -- 862 triples retrieved, 30 context lines kept. Not one of those 4.27 s could affect the answer, because the classifier did not run.
Root_Cause: The ordering was correct until W6-01/BUG-889 changed the key. The old key was hash(prompt), so the prompt HAD to be built before a lookup was possible. The new key is decision_cache_key(user_query, building_id, persona) and depends on none of the preceding work -- but the lookup stayed where the old key had forced it to be. Fixing the key made the work upstream of it dead without moving it.
Fix_Approach: Move the lookup to where its key is complete: immediately after `_persona_label`, which is the key's last input and is free to compute. A hit now returns BEFORE the GraphDB RAG fetch, before `summarize_history`'s LLM call, and before the 18k-character prompt build -- none of which the key depends on. ONE SIDE EFFECT IS DELIBERATELY SKIPPED and is documented where it is skipped: the moved block also assigns `state.summary`, which `_orchestrator.py` reads for its own history block, so on a hit that summary is one turn staler. Acceptable because a hit means this exact question/building/persona was classified before, the summary is refreshed on the next miss, and W5-01's session summary now covers long-range recall separately -- but acceptable only stated, not silently, so a test pins both the documentation and the continued existence of that other reader.
Verification: Offline: 12 tests pinning the ORDER (lookup before RAG, before the summarisation LLM call, before the prompt build), that exactly one lookup remains, that the prompt still gets the persona label, and that the summary is still refreshed on a MISS. 1,537 pass across every test touching the dialogue agent; the single failure in that sweep (CAVEAT-944) was PROVEN pre-existing by stashing this change and re-running. LIVE 2026-09-29, measured with scratchpad/cachehit_probe.py, which flushes ONLY resp_cache between asks so the turn re-runs while the INTENT cache stays warm -- flushing both would measure two misses. Dialogue stage, miss -> hit: 17,270 -> 119/132/157 ms ('Which teaching sessions are scheduled in Room 1.06?', the same question W6-02 measured at 9.5-10.6 s on hits); 7,503 -> 130/135 ms; 5,661 -> 201/221 ms. Wall: 18.5 -> 0.6 s, 10.4 -> 3.2 s, 44.6 -> 13.3 s. 157 ms cannot contain a 4.27 s RAG fetch, so this is structural rather than a quiet-stack artefact -- which matters, because the before-numbers were taken under load.
Refs: W6-02; BUG-889 / W6-01 (the re-keying that orphaned the work); CAVEAT-910

Title: One unplaceable word turns a sub-second register answer into a whole-register LLM narration
Description: The register lane has two paths and they differ by more than an order of magnitude. When register_projection composes the answer deterministically the turn costs 0.56-0.86 s and makes no LLM call at all. When it declines, the whole register is handed to a narration prompt -- 18,609 characters for 12 rows -- and the turn cost 5.75, 6.78, 7.13 and 31.59 s over four rounds. Across 25 register turns, 21 composed deterministically and 4 declined; all 4 were the same question, declining on a single word: 'not composed deterministically: words the register's own records use but this could not place: communication' ('Which refuge points have a working communication unit?').
Root_Cause: Not established, and not to be guessed at. What is established is that the decision is all-or-nothing per turn and turns on vocabulary coverage, so a register whose records use a word the projection cannot place pays the full narration cost for the whole register however small the answer is. Note the narration prompt is ~8 k characters before any payload: 1-row narrations were 8,204, 8,230 and 9,021 characters.
Fix_Approach: Not attempted here: widening the projection's vocabulary changes ANSWERS, not just latency, and that is not a latency row's change to make. Recorded so that whoever owns register wording knows the vocabulary gap has a measured latency price and not only a phrasing one. Do NOT 'fix' it by lowering the bar for deterministic composition -- the decline is the projection refusing to state something it could not place.
Verification: 48 requests, 12 questions, 4 rounds, resp_cache:* and cache:sparql* flushed before every round, fresh session id per question. Counts taken from the orchestrator log of the run: 21 'composed' against 4 'not composed deterministically'.
Refs: W6-02; V7-T18 (whole-register fetch); 2D-06 (deterministic register projection); CAVEAT-1074 (SETTLED 2026-09-30 -- the 'communication' refusal is a life-safety guard rather than a latency defect; read that row before reopening this one)

Title: A follow-up saying 'there' is answered about a DIFFERENT room, confidently and with full statistics
Description: Live 2026-09-29, one conversation of 8 turns on /v1/chat/completions, every turn genuinely executed (33-51 s each, no cache hits, unique filler). Turn 1: 'I am looking into air quality in room 5.01 specifically.' -- answered about Room 5.01. Six filler turns about floor temperatures. Turn 8: 'And what is the humidity in THERE right now?' -> 'The latest reading from the Zone Air Humidity Sensor installed-node 1.34 is 49.03 %... across 60 readings... ranged from 48.7 % to 56.1 %, with an average of 51.4 %.' Room 5.01 HAS a humidity sensor -- bldg:Zone_Air_Humidity_Sensor_5.01, labelled 'Zone Air Humidity Sensor installed-node 5.01', near-identical in name to the one it used -- so this is not an absence being handled badly. The building has 287 humidity sensors and it picked one. No hedge, no 'which room did you mean', no mention of 5.01.
Root_Cause: `rewrite_is_safe` guards a rewrite that CHANGES a place the user named, and returns True whenever the user named none -- by design, because that is 'the case the rewrite exists for'. True, and also the case where the rewrite's choice is entirely unopposed. The rewrite prompt asks the model to resolve the reference to 'the concrete entity mentioned earlier' over the last SIX messages, half of which are the ASSISTANT's own replies naming dozens of rooms -- so 'there' bound to a room from the previous answer instead of to the subject the user had declared six turns back. Nothing downstream could catch it: the rewrite replaces the user's message for classification, entity extraction, SPARQL and the referent existence gate itself, so a room that EXISTS passes every check.
Fix_Approach: `context_switch.rewrite_invents_a_place(latest, rewritten, user_texts)` -- a second guard covering the door the first one deliberately leaves open. A rewrite may bind only a place the USER named, in this session, in their own words: their messages plus the session summary (which is built only from user questions). The assistant's replies are excluded ON PURPOSE -- they are where the invented room came from, and a test asserts the exclusion so a refactor cannot quietly make the guard a no-op. Refusal returns None, so the pipeline sees the unresolved question and can ask, rather than being handed a repaired one. `place_of` returns one place per text, so a token fallback keeps a message naming two ('floor 3 and floor 4') from being misjudged.
Verification: Offline: 12 tests, incl. the measured strings verbatim and a test pinning that `rewrite_is_safe` STILL returns True for this case, so neither guard is later deleted as redundant. 272 pass across every test touching the rewrite path. LIVE 2026-09-29, same 8-turn probe, same question, after restart: the rewrite is now 'What is the current humidity on floor 1?' -- floor 1 is a place the user named twice (turns 2 and 7). 'Telecommunications Room 1.34' is gone. The fabricated binding is fixed; see BUG-943 for WHICH user-named place should win, which is a separate and much softer question.
Refs: W5-01/W5-02 (delivered, and this is not their acceptance); W5-04; BUG-524; CAVEAT-871; lessons #149

Title: A question about the CONVERSATION is routed to a data lane and declined as if it were about the building
Description: Same live session, 2026-09-29. After 7 turns, 'Remind me which room I said I was looking into, and why.' -> 'the building's records do not record the room you were interested in or why you were looking into it', Sources: Building model. The session summary WAS injected (453 chars) on that turn. The decline is honest about the building's records and answers the wrong question: the user asked what THEY said, not what the building holds.
Root_Cause: No intent covers 'what did I/we say earlier'. The question carries a room-shaped and records-shaped vocabulary, so it classifies as a data question and routes to a lane that reads the graph. The session summary is on the bus and that lane never looks at it -- the same shape as agent-patterns.md step 3, where a lane computes an answer nobody collects, except here it is a datum nobody reads.
Fix_Approach:
A meta intent that answers from the session summary rather than the graph, and which is unmistakably NOT a data lane. It must decline honestly when the summary holds nothing ('you have not mentioned a room in this conversation'), because a remembered answer is the one place a fabrication would be least visible. Note W5-01 deliberately keeps FIGURES out of the summary (lessons #148), so such a lane can recall subjects and not values -- which is the right constraint and must be stated in the answer.
FIXED 2026-09-30 by `services/session_recall.py` + a `session_recall` intent, node and routing rule. THE DESIGN POINT: the lane QUOTES AND NEVER INTERPRETS — every noun it can emit is a word the user typed, which makes a fabricated room unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a check that could have a hole. It recalls SUBJECTS and not VALUES and says so, because W5-01 deliberately keeps figures out of the session record (lessons #148: a remembered number restated as current is a fabrication, and a test had pinned the opposite as correct).
Verification:
LIVE 2026-09-30 after restart, all three caches flushed, same 8-turn probe that produced the fabrication. The recall turn now answers:
  **From this conversation, in your own words:**
  - Turn 1 — "I am looking into air quality in room 5.01 specifically." (answered)
  - (6 other turn(s) in this conversation did not mention "room".)
  That is what you said; I have not added anything to it.
  Any reason you gave is in those words — I have not inferred one for you.
  I can recall what was **asked**, not what was answered: this session record keeps no
  measured values on purpose, so nothing above is a reading.
Counted mechanically on the answer: '5.01' appears 4 times, 'Room0.01' ZERO. It quotes the user's sentence verbatim, states how many turns did NOT mention the subject, disclaims inference, and states the figures-excluded constraint rather than leaving it implicit.
ANSWERED IN 1.0 s against 40-86 s for the data turns in the same conversation, because the lane is deterministic and makes no LLM call — which is also why it cannot fabricate.
GUARDS HELD, asked in the same run: 'What is the CO2 in the room I mentioned earlier?' -> sensor_data; 'What happened to the ticket I raised about the draught last week?' -> metadata; 'Can I ask about the humidity on floor 3?' -> observability. None moved to session_recall, matching the offline measurement that the rule moves exactly ONE question in 4,287 and that one is itself a recall question.
ROUTING CONTRACT: 60 -> 61 parse rules, appended LAST because it corrects whatever the classifier guessed rather than one particular wrong guess, with test_precedence_order_is_pinned updated in the SAME change. 221 pass across the contract, autowire and wiring tests; 54 across the session-recall set.
Refs: W5-03/W5-04; BUG-940 (same session, the other half)

Title: A single turn took 3,102 seconds (52 minutes) and returned normally
Description: Live 2026-09-29, turn 3 of an 8-turn probe: 'What is the temperature on floor 2?' took 3102.1 s. The six sibling turns in the same conversation took 33.1, 41.7, 51.1, 33.6, 39.5 and 36.7 s. It did not time out, error or degrade -- it answered. The full `pytest -m unit` suite was running concurrently on the same host, and host Ollama serves the model, so CPU starvation is the obvious candidate; it is NOT established, and CAVEAT-727 (a 136-token prompt generating 16,248 tokens until the context filled) is an alternative with precedent.
Root_Cause:
Not established. Do not write one in without evidence -- see CAVEAT-500.
=== SECOND INSTANCE 2026-09-30, and it ELIMINATES both candidate causes in this row ===
Regression-gate case 8 of 51, 'Find me a quiet, well-lit room on floor 3 for two hours of focused work this afternoon.', took **3,412.2 s (57 minutes)** and answered normally. The orchestrator log localises it to a SINGLE HTTP call:
    11:06:33,431  dialogue_agent: 'Calling LLM for intent detection and query generation'
    12:00:32,887  httpx: POST http://host.docker.internal:11434/api/generate  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    12:00:33,014  dialogue_agent: 'LLM Response received (length: 385 chars)'
**One `/api/generate`. 53 min 59 s. HTTP 200. 385 characters of output.** The orchestrator logged NOTHING between those two lines -- no 11:1x through 11:5x entries at all -- so the wait is inside that request, not in our code, not in a retry loop, and not spread over many calls.
WHAT THIS RULES OUT:
  * CAVEAT-727 (a small prompt generating tokens until the context fills). The completion is     **385 characters**. Nothing ran away. Zero `empty_completion`, `LLM-DEGRADED` or `retry     backoff` lines in the whole 90-minute window.
  * A retry storm or many serial calls -- there is exactly one POST.
  * Orchestrator-side blocking -- the elapsed time is inside the httpx request.
  * **CPU starvation, which this row calls 'the obvious candidate'.** The first instance     coincided with a full `pytest -m unit` run. THIS one did not: the unit suite had already     finished (13,228 pass, exit 0) and the ONLY workload was the gate itself -- which was     blocked waiting on this very call. There was nothing to starve it.
STATE OF THE HOST AT THE TIME: `ollama /api/ps` reports gpt-oss:20b resident, size_vram 12,748,796,722 (fully on GPU, no CPU spill), context_length 16384. So it is not a model reload and not a VRAM eviction either.
WHAT IS LEFT is a stall INSIDE Ollama or the host GPU stack -- a queue, a driver/power transition, or a scheduler pathology. I cannot instrument the host from here, so I am NOT claiming which. **The useful change is that this is now an Ollama-side question, not an OntoSage-side one**, and the row should stop pointing at our concurrency.
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: (a) it makes every latency percentile in this repo unreliable, which is what CAVEAT-500 has been saying; (b) a 57-minute answer in front of an audience is a demo-stopping event, and it happens on an ORDINARY question; (c) it inflates any harness's wall clock without touching its pass rate, so a green-but-slow run tells you nothing about load. NEXT STEP FOR THE OWNER: capture the host Ollama server log (`OLLAMA_DEBUG=1`) across a gate run, since only that side can say what the 54 minutes were spent on. A client-side timeout would convert a 57-minute hang into a fast failure, which is better behaviour but is not a diagnosis.
=== LIKELY SUPERSEDED BY BUG-1194, 2026-09-30 ===
Two hours after writing this row I found the orchestrator at **40.02 GiB and 3210% CPU**, unresponsive, with Docker still reporting `healthy` from a frozen check. After a restart: 1.326 GiB, 6.43%. An event loop on a process in that state may not reach its timer callbacks at all, which would explain a 180 s `wait_for` failing to fire without anything being wrong with the timeout code or with Ollama. **Re-test this row against a HEALTHY process before spending anything on the client/transport theory** -- I eliminated a lot of candidates here and the one I could not see was the state of the process doing the eliminating. The 40 GiB was measured after the wedge, not during this call, so the link is a hypothesis and not yet a finding.
Fix_Approach: plan_trace.stage_ms now exists on /v1 (W6-02), so a recurrence can be attributed to a stage rather than guessed at. A client-visible ceiling is worth considering separately: a 52-minute answer is a failure whatever produced it, and OLLAMA_NUM_PREDICT caps generation but not queueing.
Verification: Watch for a repeat with stage_ms attached; a single observation is an observation, not a property.

Title: A deictic follow-up binds to the most RECENT place the user named, not the subject they declared
Description: Live 2026-09-29, after BUG-940 was fixed. Turn 1: 'I am looking into air quality in room 5.01 SPECIFICALLY.' Turns 2-7: six questions about floor temperatures, the last about floor 1. Turn 8: 'And what is the humidity in there right now?' -> rewritten to 'What is the current humidity on floor 1?' and answered about floor 1. This is no longer a fabrication -- floor 1 is a place the user named twice, and the answer says which place it is about. It is a question of PREFERENCE among places the user really did name.
Root_Cause: Nothing ranks the candidates. The model sees six messages and picks the nearest plausible referent; the session summary offers room 5.01 as a past subject but carries no notion of a DECLARED subject that outranks passing mentions.
Fix_Approach:
DISCLOSURE, NOT BETTER RANKING -- and the reason is recorded at the code so a later session is not tempted to 'fix it properly'. Recency is a defensible reading of 'there': a human asked that same sequence (six turns about floor temperatures, then 'humidity in there') would very likely answer about floor 1 too. Guessing more confidently is not an improvement; saying which one was assumed is, because a wrong guess then costs the user ONE CORRECTION instead of a figure they cannot see is wrong. Same reasoning `build_assumptions` already applies to a forecast horizon: the number is the same; the claim it makes must not be.
`context_switch.assumed_place_note(original, rewritten)` returns one line -- 'Taking "there" as floor 1.' -- and returns NOTHING in the three cases where a note would be noise: the user named the place themselves, no place was bound, or no deictic word can be quoted back. It renders the place the way the REWRITE wrote it ('room 5.01', not '5.01') by taking a head noun from that text rather than inventing one, so a building that calls them something else gets the bare identifier -- thin, but honest. APPENDED, never prepended: this is a footnote on how the question was read, not the answer. That is the opposite placement from BUG-897's declared-capacity statement, and the difference is deliberate -- that one IS the answer.
One defect in my own first version, fixed and pinned: the marker match was punctuation-sensitive, so ' there ' did not match ' and there? ' and the note vanished on the commonest phrasing there is. Third time that shape has cost something in two days (BUG-948's plurals, BUG-950's 'pm2.5' vs 'pm25').
Verification:
LIVE 2026-09-30 after the coordinated restart, caches flushed, via scratchpad/memory_probe.py (one chat, unique filler, every turn genuinely executed). THREE RUNS AND ALL THREE BEHAVIOURS ARE RIGHT, which is more than the row asked for:
  run 1  rewrite bound floor 1  -> '[response] disclosed the assumed referent: Taking "there" as floor 1.'
  run 2  rewrite bound floor 0  -> 'Taking "there" as floor 0.'
  run 3  '[coref] rewrite REJECTED -- it bound a place the user never named' -> and CORRECTLY NO NOTE, because nothing was legitimately bound.
So BUG-940's guard fired inside the same probe and the two fixes compose as intended: a bound place is disclosed, an invented one is refused and nothing is claimed. NOTE ON THE PROBE, not the system: the note is APPENDED, and the probe printed only the first 700 characters, so the first run looked like a failure until the log was read. The probe now prints the tail of the recall turn -- a measurement instrument that cannot see the thing it tests is the apparatus being wrong again (lessons #20-22).

Title: 'What sensors do you have?' routes to observability, and a pinned test still expects discovery
Description: tests/test_integration_mock_building.py::TestDialogueIntentDetection::test_intent_routing['what sensors do you have?'-discovery] FAILS: the routing contract's `observability_query` rule moves it 'discovery' -> 'observability' ('can-you-measure questions -> the reach lane, answered from the graph, V6-T10'). PROVEN PRE-EXISTING: stashing the day's dialogue_agent change and re-running gives the identical failure. It does not appear in `pytest -m unit` because this file is an integration test and is among the 1,139 deselected -- which is why the full suite run the same day reported only 3 failures, all elsewhere.
Root_Cause: Not established which side is wrong, and that is the point of logging rather than fixing. 'What sensors do you have?' is defensibly a can-you-measure question, so the rule may be right and the expectation stale; or the rule may be over-reaching into plain inventory questions. Deciding needs a live read of both lanes' answers, not a vote between two plausible labels.
Fix_Approach: Ask it live and read BOTH answers before touching anything. If observability answers it well, update the expectation and say so in the test. If it does not, narrow the rule -- and note the routing contract's own rules: ALL rules run and the LAST one wins, so a corrective rule goes AFTER the one it corrects, and tests/test_routing_contract.py::test_precedence_order_is_pinned must be updated in the SAME commit. The regression probe must be green BEFORE and AFTER, one rule at a time.
Verification: pytest 'tests/test_integration_mock_building.py::TestDialogueIntentDetection' -q
Refs: routing_contract.py observability_query; V6-T10; CLAUDE.md routing precedence

Title: 'How does today compare with the outside temperature' is read as a forecast request and never compares anything
Description: Live 2026-09-29, W3-01's OWN acceptance question. -> '**I don't hold a weather forecast.** Abacws Building's outdoor sensors last recorded: outdoor temperature 20.7 (at 20:52 on 29 Sep), outdoor humidity 80, wind speed 17.6, solar irradiance 437 W/m2 and rainfall 4.1 mm. Those are readings, not a forecast.' The live Open-Meteo feed is plainly working -- five variables, all timestamped within two minutes -- so the infrastructure half of W3-01 is done. What is missing is the COMPARISON: the question asks how indoor today compares with outdoor, and neither an indoor series nor a comparison appears.
Root_Cause: 'today' was read as 'today's forecast' rather than as the indoor series over today, so a forecast-absence decline pre-empted a comparison the system can actually make. The decline is honest and about the right subject; it answers a question that was not asked.
Fix_Approach: A comparison naming an outdoor quantity and a period should bind BOTH series -- the indoor one for the named period and the outdoor feed over the same window -- and compare them, which is what the comparison lane already does for two indoor places. Keep the forecast-absence decline for questions that genuinely ask what the weather WILL be; it is correct there and is the right answer to 'will it be warm tomorrow'.
Verification: Ask W3-01's acceptance question; PASS names both an indoor and an outdoor figure over the same window.
Refs: W3-01; BUG-888 (the feed, fixed); CAVEAT-892 (the outdoor binding, fixed)

Title: A 'tomorrow' comparison between two floors answers from CURRENT data and never reaches the forecaster
Description: Live 2026-09-29, the shape W2-03's acceptance is about. 'Will floor 3 or floor 4 be warmer TOMORROW?' -> '**Both floors have the same mean temperature of 23 C.** Floor 3 recorded 49 sensors... Floor 4 recorded 51 sensors... The data reflects current conditions; it does not indicate which floor will be warmer tomorrow.' That last sentence is honest and is the good part -- it does not dress a current mean as a prediction. But W2-03's acceptance is 'the answer names BOTH FORECASTS and declines to pick a winner when the intervals overlap', and no forecast was produced at all, so there are no intervals to overlap.
Root_Cause: Routing, not arithmetic. The question classified as `compare` and went to the comparison lane; W2-01/W2-02 route floor-level and building-level FORECASTS to the forecaster, but a question that is both a comparison AND a forecast follows the comparison branch and the forecaster is never consulted.
Fix_Approach: A comparison naming a FUTURE period needs both sides forecast and then compared on their intervals -- the aggregate-then-forecast path W2-02 already built, run once per side. The overlap rule is the honesty half and must come with it: overlapping intervals mean no winner may be named, which is exactly the failure BUG-885 was about at a single instant. NOTE the routing contract's rules -- ALL run and the LAST wins, so a corrective rule goes AFTER the one it corrects, `test_precedence_order_is_pinned` updates in the SAME commit, and the regression probe must be green before AND after, one rule at a time.
Verification: Ask 'Will floor 3 or floor 4 be warmer tomorrow?'; PASS names two forecasts and their intervals.
Refs: W2-03; W2-01; W2-02; BUG-885 (the verdict half, fixed); BUG-937

Title: The capability lane declines from DOCUMENTS alone and denies data the graph plainly holds
Description: Found hand-reading the held-out tail M (62 questions) against the current build, 2026-09-29. SEVEN of the 62 are false denials, 11.3% of the set, and FOUR OF THE SEVEN NAME THE RIGHT REGISTER IN THE SAME SENTENCE AS THE REFUSAL. That is the tell: this is not retrieval failing, it is a lane identifying the source and not reading it. (2) BMS changes today -> 'could not find this in the documents'; graph holds 2,175 configuration-history records. (7) 'Do you have a maintenance crew?' -> same; graph holds a department named literally 'Mechanical and Electrical Maintenance' plus five more, and 24 WorkOrders. (28) power/network/ventilation availability -> declines while NAMING Operating regime, Asset engineering profile and Asset status record. (32) 'why is pl 2.5 increasing' -> RESOLVES the typo to PM2.5, then declines; the building has 210 PM2.5 sensors and PM2.5 is not even in its 'nearest things' list. (54) emergency contacts and escalation routes -> declines while NAMING Department; 20 Department records exist. (58) observed occupancy vs design assumptions -> declines while NAMING the occupancy readings; both halves exist (maxOccupancy/roomCapacity declared, occupancy measured). (61) 'what kind of data is collected?' -> 'I don't have that specific information on record', then offers Waste collection point records. The system knows all 45 record classes and every modality; this is a basic question about itself. A FALSE DENIAL IS NOT A SOFT FAILURE. It is as damaging as a wrong number and worse for trust, because the user stops asking -- and the wording invites them to 'name the record' for records already there under obvious names.
Root_Cause:
The capability lane's chain is live metrics -> capability TRIPLES -> uploaded DOCUMENTS -> honest 'no info'. The record REGISTERS -- Department, WorkOrder, ConfigurationHistory, ContinuityProvision and the rest, which record_registry logs 45 classes of at boot -- are not in that chain, so a question that routes to capability can never reach them however plainly it names one. Same shape as BUG-893 (four ordinary English words turned the calibration register off) and BUG-901 (a window of readings cannot evidence silence): the data exists, a lane owns the question, and the two are not connected.
THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE WHOLE 'NAMES THE REGISTER AND DECLINES' PATTERN, found 2026-09-30 and not previously suspected: **the decline's POINTER and the register SELECTOR use different matchers, and the pointer is the more capable one.**
  `content_terms('escalation routes') == content_terms('escalation route') == {escalation, rout}`  — the pointer SINGULARISES;
  `rank_record_classes` matches `\b<term>\b`                              — a trailing 's' ends it.
So at HEAD, tail M #54 selected NO register while its decline opened 'does keep **Department**, Approval and evidence record and Competency requirement records, which I can read for you.' The wording was never ACCIDENTALLY accurate — the pointer really had found the right register and the selector could not. That is why four of the seven false declines name the right register in the same sentence as the refusal, and it means the gap is measurable rather than anecdotal: `fallback_wording.pointer_only_registers()` + `capability_agent._log_selector_gap()` now log it at INFO before both capability decline paths. Only the registers the decline PRINTS are counted — counting everything the fuzzy matcher touches gave fifteen names for #28.
=== TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW, 2026-09-30, both of them mine and both measured ===

(1) I WROTE THAT CAUSE (2) WAS 'ONE TRIPLE' AWAY. IT IS NOT, AND EXPOSING IT WOULD MAKE THINGS WORSE. This row said `o:ConfigurationPeriod` only lacked a `subClassOf` link to the record roots, and that one triple would make its 2,175 records answerable. Measured against the live graph:
    distinct changeKind across all 2,175 : ONE — 'first_observed'
    records that have ever CLOSED        : ZERO (no effectiveTo on any)
    approval/authorisation predicates    : NONE on the class at all
They record 'we first observed this point at time T'. They are not configuration CHANGES and are certainly not AUTHORISED ones, so 'What authorised BMS changes took effect today, and which live points confirm the intended state is now active?' CANNOT be answered from them. **The decline is substantively correct and (2) is not a false decline.**
Measured both halves of the prescribed fix offline over the 2,960-question catalogue: the subClassOf triple alone moves 0 questions; with ten obvious lay terms it moves 7, cleanly by the usual standard — and ALL SEVEN ask about authorisation, adoption, traceability or rollback, so each would be answered '2,175 configuration changes, all of kind first observed'. **A visible failure traded for an invisible one — Wave A's pattern exactly.** THE FIX IS DATA (a second changeKind, an effectiveTo, an authorising actor), which is CAVEAT-842's shape and the owner's to supply.
Second-order risk found while measuring, and it must be settled BEFORE any subClassOf change: `effectiveFrom` is `rdfs:domain ConfigurationPeriod` and **2,349 non-ConfigurationPeriod subjects use it**. Under a full RDFS ruleset all 2,349 would infer into the class — and, with the triple, into IntervalRecord too. Widen those domains first.

(2) 'FOUR OF SEVEN DECLINES NAMED THE RIGHT REGISTER' DOES NOT SUPPORT THE INFERENCE I DREW FROM IT. I reported that as the tell — evidence that a lane identifies the source and does not read it. Measured over all 2,960 catalogue questions: where the selector is silent (1,746 questions) **the pointer still names registers on 1,742 of them — 99.8% — and names THREE on 1,684, 96.4%.** It is structural: `_near_records` admits on one crude stem and `nearest_holdings` returns its top three regardless, so on a long question 'the three nearest' is 'the three that sorted first'. Against a mechanism that names three registers on 96.4% of declines, four-of-seven is what chance produces. **For #54 the Department match WAS real and declared, which is why the TTL-first fix worked — but the general inference does not follow and I should not have drawn it.** BUG-970's closing claim, that each name is 'one declared lay term away from being reachable', is false at scale: it would imply ~5,100 work orders across 44 registers. See BUG-1073; the log wording is now 'a disagreement between two matchers and a place to look', with the rate printed so a reader calibrates.
Fix_Approach:
