Title: publication_gate.is_decline does not recognise the project's own decline wording
Description: Measured 2026-09-30 while wiring BUG-897: is_decline() returns FALSE for the decline that opens 'I could not answer that from <building>s records.' That string is emitted by clarification.compose_abstract and is one of the commonest declines the system produces -- the held-out tail M shows it on six of 62 answers. is_decline is the project's shared decline classifier and other code reasons about publication from it.
Root_Cause: Not traced. It is marker-based, and CAVEAT-887 already records that marker-based decline detection cannot keep up with a system free to reword its declines -- one question produced THREE honest decline wordings in a day.
Fix_Approach: Whatever is done, CLAUDE.md's rule applies: every change to the marker list is verified against all 73 stored answers by a test, because an intermediate broader pattern moved two of them and was rejected for it (lessons #141). The decline leads are LITERALS in clarification.py and capability_agent.py, so a test could derive the marker set from the source that emits them rather than restating it.
Verification: Closed by BUG-992. The two markers were derived from the source that EMITS the decline (`clarification.compose_abstract`), not restated, and the audit that found this now parses 98 first-person-inability leads out of 45 modules so the next omission is found by a test rather than by a hand read.

Title: Occupancy 'at the moment' answers are wrong by two orders of magnitude and contradict their own statistics
Description: Asked live 2026-09-30, fresh chat each, resp_cache flushed. 'Which rooms are occupied at the moment?' -> '**Two rooms are occupied at the moment: Room 5.10 - Academic Office and Room 0.31 - Mechanical/Service Room.** ... while all other sensors listed report 0.00.' 'Which rooms are empty at the moment?' -> '**6 rooms are empty at the moment.** ... Across all 467 sensors the lowest occupancy recorded is 0, observed in six rooms' and names them. GROUND TRUTH, measured in the orchestrator container against sensordb.occupancy_data with the session pinned to +00:00, taking the latest row per uuid: 514 series, 131 read zero, 383 read NON-ZERO, min 0, max 21, mean 3.87. So 'two rooms occupied' is wrong against 383 and '6 rooms empty' is wrong against 131. The occupied answer also contradicts ITSELF in the same paragraph: it quotes 'across the 234 series, the mean occupancy count is 0.491 ... 119 series read zero', and 115/234 = 0.491, so its own statistics say ~115 series read non-zero while its headline says two. Three denominators appear across two turns -- 234, 467 and a graph count -- and none is 514.
Root_Cause:
ROOT CAUSE: the aggregate lane DECLINES the question, so the narrator supplies the headline. `parse_intent` needs a statistic word and 'occupied'/'empty' are in neither `_MAX` nor `_MIN`; `question_measurands` returns the EMPTY SET for all four phrasings, so `summary_ok` is False too and `wants_lane` returns None. Logged verbatim on all four live turns: `[aggregate] not claimed: measurand=occupancy place=False per_sensor=False readings=True`. EVERY FIGURE THE ANSWERS QUOTED WAS REAL and correctly fetched -- the two denominators it cited, 234 and 467, are the distinct SPACES carrying an occupancy series and the series the graph PLACES in a space. Both true; neither was the thing being counted.
FIX: a presence lane that reads each series' newest value, groups by SPACE, prefers the presence flag, and WRITES THE COUNT IN CODE -- entered only where `wants_lane` already returned None, so nothing that previously answered changes path.
THE TWO DID NOT SHARE A CAUSE, and separating them cost one extra ask rather than a day of theory. BUG-898 came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to two decimal places a day apart, on a series written to every minute; BUG-954's figures moved between asks. **A model does not repeat an invention; a file does.** That single observation split a 190x discrepancy on one quantity into a narration defect and a stale-file defect.
Fix_Approach: Log the bound uuids, the row count per uuid and the window for ONE of these turns before changing anything -- the same instruction BUG-880 carries, for the same reason. Then fix the half that disagrees with the store. A count answer must be computed from the filter over the declared denominator and must state that denominator, as the biggest-room answer now does ('266 spaces the floor plans give an area for; 62 more have no area recorded'). Until then this is a fabrication risk on a question a facilities manager will ask on day one.
Verification:
Measured against MySQL with the session pinned to +00:00: 514 series with a latest reading (380 non-zero / 134 zero), 512 of them fresh within 15 minutes -- so staleness and truncation are RULED OUT, not assumed away -- across 234 distinct spaces, with 467 series placed in a space.
LIVE 2026-09-30 after restart, caches flushed: 'Which rooms are occupied at the moment?' -> '**116 of the 234 spaces with an occupancy sensor have someone in them right now**; 118 do not, read between Wed 30 Sep 08:55 and Wed 30 Sep 08:55', eight rooms named and '108 more' (8+108=116). Was: two. The inverse phrasing gives 123 of 234 and the two AGREE EXACTLY despite still binding different series sets, because the grouping is on space.
THE PAST-PERIOD GUARD ALSO VERIFIED: 'Which rooms were occupied last Tuesday?' DECLINES rather than answering with present readings -- a 'right now' lane must not answer a past question with current data.
39 new tests; 695 pass / 0 fail on `-m unit` across every module touched.

Title: REGRESSION: 'Are there any unacknowledged alarms?' answers ONE of six and asserts there are no others
Description: Asked live 2026-09-30: 'Yes-there is one unacknowledged alarm recorded in the building: - **AlarmEvent_ab660858e9035204b469d87b3a79fd46** *Status:* unacknowledged. **No other unacknowledged alarms are present in the current records.**' The graph holds SIX: a SPARQL count of ontosage:AlarmEvent with FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?s ontosage:acknowledgedAt ?a } returns 6 (ab660858..., d0079208..., de870f75..., 8bd5d9f6..., 65a1bd18..., 3dd5ce1b...), all recordStatus 'detected'; 264 of 270 AlarmEvents carry acknowledgedAt. THIS IS A REGRESSION: BUG-774, logged 2026-09-18, records that this same question 'answers correctly (6 unacknowledged)'. It now answers 1, and the closing sentence turns an incomplete read into a positive false claim. Second defect in the same answer: the alarm is identified to the user only by its raw IRI fragment, although every AlarmEvent carries rdfs:label, alarmCondition, alarmPriority, effectiveFrom, aboutEquipment and (255 of 270) aboutSpace -- so the reader is given the one field they cannot act on and none of the six they could.
Root_Cause:
DIAGNOSED 2026-09-30, and the surprise is that NOTHING IS WRONG WITH THE FETCH. Asked three times with resp_cache flushed between, the same question named 1, then 6, then 0 alarms — and the orchestrator log for the 6-run shows the lane doing everything right:
  [ttl-route] metadata via held record class: AlarmEvent (270 instances)
  [sparql] record-class schema injected: AlarmEvent
     SELECT ?alarm WHERE { ?alarm a ontosage:AlarmEvent .
       FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?alarm ontosage:acknowledgedAt ?ackTime } }
  [modality_repair] rows=6
The LLM generated exactly the right SPARQL and the store returned exactly the right six rows. **The variance is entirely in the narration over those six rows** — which is why the route is stable (CAVEAT-891 / W6-01: routing IS deterministic; the answer is not) and why no amount of routing work would touch it. This is the clearest safety-relevant instance of that variance found so far: run 3 said 'none' over six rows including two HIGH-priority trips.
THE DETERMINISTIC COMPOSER DECLINED, AND CORRECTLY BY ITS OWN DESIGN. `register_projection._ineligible` carries an explicit early refusal — 'asks for the absence of something, which a lookup does not answer' — and 'unacknowledged' is exactly that: the absence of `acknowledgedAt`. In this run it did not even reach that branch, refusing instead with 'the register holds none of what the question singles out', because 'unacknowledged' is not a word the resolver can place at all. Either way the refusal is deliberate, so this is NOT a defect in the projection.
Fix_Approach:
TWO CANDIDATES, and the cheap one is much the better bet.
(1) CHEAP AND IN THE HOUSE IDIOM: state the ROW COUNT deterministically. The lane already has it — `[modality_repair] rows=6` — and a narrator that is handed 'six records match' cannot answer 'none'. This is BUG-937's lesson exactly (a figure a narrator can get wrong is a figure it should not be deriving) and BUG-936's (the comparison was computed, not narrated). It fixes the count without attempting the list, which is the right split: a partial list with a correct count is a usable answer; a confident 'none' is not.
(2) EXPENSIVE AND RISKIER: teach `register_projection` to compose absence-of-field questions, reversing a deliberate design refusal. That is a capability change in the most delicate resolver in the system, and BUG-948 showed what that costs — the plural fix there needed a sweep over all 2,960 catalogue questions to discover it was right 30 times and wrong 25. Do not attempt it without the same sweep.
SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT IN THE SAME ANSWER, and it reproduced in all three runs: the alarms are identified by RAW IRI FRAGMENT ('AlarmEvent_de870f7551565e9db97a0c21168cb124') while the graph holds an rdfs:label, an alarmPriority and an aboutSpace for every one of the six. Zero of three runs used a human label. A reader cannot act on a hash.

DONE 2026-09-30, candidate (1), and the diagnosis needed one correction first. RE-ASKED FIVE TIMES across two container states with resp_cache flushed between (three at 09:04-09:05, two at 09:24-09:25 after the design-occupancy restart). THE COUNT HAD ALREADY STOPPED VARYING: all five said SIX. The defect had moved, and to something worse -- FOUR OF THE FIVE then refused to call them unacknowledged:
  'There are **six** active alarm events ... None of the records include a field that indicates whether the alarm has been acknowledged, so we cannot say whether any of them have been addressed.'
  'the building's records only tell us that **6 alarm events** are stored in the model ... They do not include any information about whether those alarms have been acknowledged.'
Only one of five answered the question ('Yes -- there are 6 unacknowledged alarms'), and that one named none of them. Two of the six are HIGH priority.
THE CAUSE IS EXACT AND IT IS NOT THE COUNT. The query FILTERS OUT every record that CARRIES acknowledgedAt, so the rows that come back necessarily lack it -- the narrator sees a column that is never populated and reports a gap in the records. The rows' emptiness IS the answer and it was read as the absence of the field. The same blindness produced '6 alarm events are stored in the model' from a building holding 270: a result-set size with no filter attached looks like a population.
Neither fact is recoverable from the rows. Both are in the query. So:
(a) `_absent_properties` reads the three shapes the generator actually produced for this ONE question in one afternoon -- FILTER NOT EXISTS, MINUS, and !BOUND over an OPTIONAL -- rather than the one that happened to be in the log;
(b) `_absence_selection_meaning` states, in the facts block, that the rows are the records satisfying the condition and NOT the population, that the property is the SELECTION CRITERION and its absence is the answer, and that the count is N. The property is named in plain words ('acknowledged at'), never as a CURIE, because the narration prompt forbids field names in an answer;
(c) `_absence_selection_lead` puts the count in the ANSWER, written by the code: '**6 alarm event records match this question.**' Silent for a COUNT aggregate, where len(bindings) is 1 and leading with 1 would state the opposite of the truth;
(d) `_count_meaning` gains the filtered-set clause for the COUNT shape, which is where 'in total' came from.
Deliberately NOT attempted: composing the list. A partial list under a correct count is usable; a confident 'none' is not.
SECOND DEFECT, the raw IRI fragment: `_label_bare_subjects` fetches rdfs:label for rows that identify things only by IRI, so a human name no longer depends on whether the generated SELECT happened to ask for ?label -- which is exactly the kind of thing a generator varies between runs. Four guards: at most 40 rows, no existing readable column, exactly ONE IRI-valued variable (with two there is no way to say whose label it is), and a failure returns the rows untouched.
Verification:
Live 2026-09-30 (/v1, fresh chat, cache flushed). Graph checked against repository 'bldg': 270 AlarmEvent, 264 with acknowledgedAt, 6 without, recordStatus distribution resolved 262 / detected 6 / open 2. | INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED 2026-09-30 by SPARQL, and the graph makes the count exact rather than approximate: `o:acknowledgedAt` appears on 264 of 270 AlarmEvents, so EXACTLY SIX lack it. Each of the six carries a label, a priority and a space -- nothing is missing that would excuse omitting them:
  ALM-8BD5D9F6  HIGH    Circuit breaker trip - Electrical Breaker Panel - Floor 3
  ALM-DE870F75  HIGH    Frost protection trip - Air Handling Unit - Floor 4
  ALM-3DD5CE1B  MEDIUM  Earth leakage trip - EV Charging Station 2 - Parking Level
  ALM-65A1BD18  MEDIUM  Filter differential pressure high - Air Handling Unit - Floor 4
  ALM-AB660858  MEDIUM  Detector contamination warning - Smoke Detector - Floor 5 Lab Corridor
  ALM-D0079208  MEDIUM  Video signal lost - CCTV Camera - Floor 1 Corridor
TWO OF THE SIX ARE HIGH PRIORITY, and the answer closed with 'No other unacknowledged alarms are present.' That sentence is what makes this worse than a partial answer: a reader who acted on it would leave a circuit-breaker trip and a frost-protection trip unattended. THIS IS A REGRESSION: BUG-774's row records this same question answering all six correctly on 2026-09-18, so something landed since then that broke it. That makes it more tractable than an ordinary defect -- bisect the register/alarm path against the 2026-09-18 behaviour rather than treating it as new work. | FIX 2026-09-30: 25 offline tests, including the three live queries verbatim, the COUNT-aggregate case that must stay silent, the two ordinary queries that must gain nothing, and a pin that BOTH narration return paths publish the lead. 1,248 pass across every test file importing the four changed modules, 0 fail. NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE: the running container started 09:09:23Z, before the edits, so no live re-ask can exercise them. Needs a restart, then the same five-ask protocol. PASS is five answers each stating six and none saying the records do not record acknowledgement. | A/B ON THE REAL MODEL, 2026-09-30. The container predates the edits, so the narration was exercised directly instead: the six real rows from GraphDB, real gpt-oss:20b, the real prompt, four repeats each arm, interleaved so a drifting provider cannot favour one. The query used is run 2's verbatim -- `SELECT ?r` with FILTER NOT EXISTS and no ?label -- which is the harder case, because the rows are bare IRIs.
  BEFORE  4/4 got the count right, 0/4 named an alarm (raw IRI fragment every time), 1/4 denied the answer outright: 'The current records do NOT include an acknowledgment status ... Because that information is missing, we cannot say whether any of these alarms have been acknowledged or remain unacknowledged.'
  AFTER   4/4 opened '**6 alarm event records match this question.**', 4/4 named all six by label AND location (Frost protection trip - Air Handling Unit, Floor 4; Circuit breaker trip - Electrical Breaker Panel, Floor 3; ...), 0/4 denied anything. The log confirms the label lookup ran: '[sparql] labelled 6 of 6 bare IRI(s) in ?r'.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW, stated plainly: the harness isolates `_format_results`, so it does not reproduce the full turn. The live variance came partly from the query SHAPE -- one of the five live asks generated a COUNT aggregate, and 'in total' came from `_count_meaning` -- and the harness fixes the shape. The end-to-end re-ask is still owed and needs a restart.
BLAST RADIUS, measured over all 16,847 saved turns that carry a stored query: 12 (0.07%) select on a missing property and 7 (0.04%) would gain the deterministic lead. The change is invisible to the rest. The sweep also found the ONE non-alarm question of that shape, now a test: 'Is each asset linked to the correct parent, engineering system and served area?' selects the absence of three properties at once and returned 21 rows -- the same defect waiting on a different register, where a narrator could as easily have answered 'all of them are'. It also caught an ungrammatical singular ('1 alarm event record match this question').
LIVE RE-ASK 2026-09-30, discharging a check owed since 2026-09-17. Caches flushed (`resp_cache:*`, `cache:sparql*`), fresh chat id per question, asked on a HEALTHY orchestrator -- the first attempt failed outright because the process was in the runaway logged as BUG-1194 (40 GiB, unresponsive), which is itself the reason to state the process's state when reporting a live result. Memory held 1.33-1.59 GiB throughout.
SECOND QUESTION ONLY. Q: 'Is each asset linked to the correct parent, engineering system and served area?' -> 27.4 s. The narration reports FIELDS, not a verdict, and states the absence as a COUNT rather than as a hole in the records: '3 of the 24 assets have a parent recorded ... The remaining 21 assets have no parent recorded. All 24 assets have an engineering system recorded.' That is the shape the fix intended, on the one non-alarm instance the blast-radius sweep found.
THE ALARM QUESTION ITSELF IS STILL OWED: this row's PASS condition is five asks of 'Are there any unacknowledged alarms?' all stating six and none claiming the records do not record acknowledgement. Not run yet -- the first attempt died with the orchestrator (BUG-1194). Status stays FIXED_UNVERIFIED.
LIVE 2026-09-30, on a HEALTHY orchestrator (the first attempt died inside BUG-1194's runaway), caches flushed, fresh chat id per ask. **FIVE ASKS, AND THE ROW'S OWN PASS CONDITION IS MET: 5/5 state SIX, and 0/5 claim the records do not record acknowledgement.**
  [1/5] 28.8 s  'There are **6 unacknowledged alarms** currently recorded'
  [2/5] 28.5 s  'There are **6 alarms that have not yet been acknowledged**'
  [3/5] 14.0 s  'There are **6 alarms that have not yet been acknowledged**'
  [4/5] 24.3 s  'Yes-there are **6 unacknowledged alarms** recorded in the building model'
  [5/5] 36.3 s  '**6 alarm event records match this question.**' + all six grouped by floor
The P1 is discharged on both halves: the count no longer varies (it was 1, then 6, then 0 across three identical asks) and the refusal is gone (four of five previously said 'None of the records include a field that indicates whether the alarm has been acknowledged' -- false exactly because the query FILTERS OUT every record carrying `acknowledgedAt`).
**WHAT DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND IT SHOULD BE SAID PLAINLY.** The offline A/B behind this fix reported 'AFTER: 4/4 led with the count, 4/4 named all six with location'. Live, **1 of 5** named them: asks 1-4 give the count alone, and only ask 5 shows the `_absence_selection_lead` sentence and the labelled subjects. So the deterministic parts (count, no denial) hold every time and the NARRATION improvement is intermittent at roughly a fifth of the offline rate. That is the CAVEAT-891 pattern the row itself named: the route is deterministic, the answer is not. An A/B that isolates `_format_results` cannot measure what the whole turn does -- logged rather than folded into the pass.

Title: A clipped fetch window is narrated as the building's absence, in two different energy comparisons
Description: Two answers live 2026-09-30 assert that data does not exist when it does, and the quantity that is missing is exactly the part outside the fetch window. (1) 'How does energy use yesterday compare with the same day last week?' -> 'Because there are no separate readings for 2026-09-29 (yesterday) and 2026-09-22 (the same day last week), a direct day-over-day comparison cannot be calculated.' sensordb.energy_data holds 528 rows dated 2026-09-29 and 426 dated 2026-09-22. (2) 'Compare energy use this month and last month' -> 'The data set contains daily energy totals only for 2026-09-18 through 2026-09-30 ... Because no August figures are present, a comparison between this month and last month cannot be made.' energy_data runs from 2026-06-04 to 2026-09-30, 307,355 rows over 8 uuids; submeter_data from 2026-07-08, 113,882 rows over 16. The reported span 18-30 September is ~12 days, which is what a 1000-row-per-sensor cap yields at this cadence. Answer (1) also mis-describes the data it did read: it calls 2.59 kWh a floor's 'cumulative' reading, while the stored values on those days range 1.3-6.5.
Root_Cause: The window/cap and the narration disagree about what 'the data set' means. BUG-939 already owns the mechanism -- the fetch ignores the period the question names and a 1000-row-per-sensor cap clips it further. What is new and separately fixable is the NARRATION: having received a clipped window, the lane reports its edges as the building's record ('no August figures are present'), which converts a fetch limit into a false statement about the building. This is the 'four kinds of nothing' failure -- window-absence narrated as graph-absence.
Fix_Approach: Two independent changes, and the second is cheap and should not wait for the first. (a) Honour the named period (BUG-939). (b) Make the absence statement name its own window: a lane that read 2026-09-18..30 must say 'I read 18-30 September and found no August figures in that window', never 'no August figures are present'. The Boundary disclosure these answers already print proves the plumbing exists to state a scope; it states the METER scope and not the TIME scope.
Verification: Live 2026-09-30, both phrasings. Store measured in the orchestrator container, MySQL session time_zone '+00:00': energy_data COUNT/MIN/MAX and per-day counts for 2026-09-21..30; submeter_data likewise.
Refs: BUG-880; BUG-939; BUG-814; lesson 'four kinds of nothing'

Title: A plant-loop reading is presented as the building's temperature, with a false coverage claim and a raw IRI
Description: Asked live 2026-09-30: 'What is the current temperature of the heat pump water loop?' -> '**Across the building temperature is averaging 65.0 C**, ranging from 59.6 to 70.4 C. Based on 2 temperature sensors on 1 floor, the newest reading from each sensor in the last 60 minutes... This building records temperature on one floor only (Floor http://abacwsbuilding.cardiff.ac.uk/abacws#Rooftop); the other 5 floors have no sensor of this kind.' Three defects in four lines. (1) The scope word is wrong: 65 C is the heat pump water loop, and 'across the building temperature is averaging 65.0 C' reads as an indoor air temperature and is alarming nonsense as such. (2) The coverage claim is FALSE as written: the graph holds 296 brick:Temperature_Sensor and 288 brick:Air_Temperature_Sensor, with air-temperature points reachable on Floors 0-5; it is true only of the 8 Water_Temperature_Sensor / 4 Entering / 4 Leaving water sensors, and the sentence never says which kind 'this kind' is. (3) A raw IRI is printed to the user as a floor name.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. The binding itself is RIGHT -- it found the rooftop water-loop sensors, which is what was asked -- so this is a narration/scope-labelling defect, not a referent defect. The coverage sentence appears to be a generic per-floor availability note written for the resolved Brick class and then rendered without naming that class, which makes a true statement about water-loop sensors read as a false statement about temperature.
Fix_Approach: The precedent is BUG-883, which fixed exactly this shape for forecasts: a figure from N sensors must STATE its denominator and must not borrow a wider scope word. Here: say 'the heat pump water loop is averaging 65.0 C across its 2 water-temperature sensors', and if a coverage note is printed at all it must name the class ('no WATER temperature sensor is recorded on the other five floors'). Resolve the floor IRI to its label before rendering.
Verification: Live 2026-09-30 (route intent=sensor_data -> sparql). Graph checked: COUNT(DISTINCT ?s) by type for every class whose IRI contains 'Temperature' in repository 'bldg'.

Title: The alert lane binds the wrong measurand and reports success: a CO2 threshold becomes 'system_capability'
Description: Asked live 2026-09-30: 'Can you set up an alert when CO2 goes above 1000?' -> 'Alert created (ID: **2b75b5bd**). I'll notify you when **system_capability** > 1000.0. Use 'list my alerts' to manage your alerts.' Route intent=alert -> alert, node=alert_mgmt. The question names CO2 and the alert was bound to 'system_capability' -- a quantity the user did not ask for and which is not a measurand -- and the turn reported success. A user reading this reasonably believes a CO2 alert now exists. This is a change for the worse in the lane BUG-837 recorded as answering 'couldn't tell which measured quantity': a wrong binding silently accepted is worse than a decline, because the decline was visible and this is not.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. 'system_capability' reads like a default or a placeholder from the capability/automation path rather than anything the concept resolver produced -- the resolver maps CO2 correctly elsewhere in the same session (BUG-825's Room 1.06 answer binds the CO2 sensor). The suspicion to test first is that the alert lane never asks the resolver and takes a field from its own template.
Fix_Approach: Trace one turn and print what the alert record stored as its quantity and where that value came from. Then: an alert whose measurand does not resolve from the question must be REFUSED, not created under a default -- the same principle BUG-884 settled for floor binding ('returns NOTHING when no class resolves; binding arbitrary points is worse than what it replaces'). Echo the bound quantity back in the confirmation so a wrong binding is visible at creation. Also check whether the alert created here is live, and whether previous probes left similar mis-bound alerts behind.
Verification: Live 2026-09-30, one ask, /v1 fresh chat, resp_cache flushed. Alert ID 2b75b5bd was created by this probe and may want removing.

Title: 'Overdue as at 30 September 2026' is read from a frozen status field, and misses half the overdue records
Description: Asked live 2026-09-30: 'Which assets are overdue for maintenance?' -> '**3 of the 25 records in the Planned service schedule entry register are overdue** (as at 30 September 2026): SVC-01 due 17 September 2026, recorded as overdue; SVC-02 due 17 September 2026, recorded as overdue; SVC-16 due 16 September 2026, recorded as overdue.' SIX of the 25 have ontosage:nextDue before today: SVC-03 2026-09-06, SVC-16 2026-09-16, SVC-01 2026-09-17, SVC-02 2026-09-17, SVC-06 2026-09-18, SVC-08 2026-09-20. The three omitted ones carry a stale recordStatus: SVC-03 ('Carpet deep clean - Levels 1 and 2') reads recordStatus 'due' and rdfs:comment 'Due within the week' although its nextDue passed 24 days ago. The answer's own words give it away -- 'RECORDED AS overdue' is a field, '(AS AT 30 September 2026)' is a computation, and it made the second claim from the first.
Root_Cause: A date-relative claim answered from a static field. ontosage:recordStatus was authored on 2026-09-22 (retrievedAt) and does not move with the calendar, so it decays exactly as the overdue-calibration count did in TODO-484 (194 -> 201 -> 206 while the system stayed correct). Note the same field is CORRECT in the fire-safety register, where FSA-001 and FSA-027 both read recordStatus 'overdue' consistently with their nextTestDue -- so the register that is wrong is ServiceSchedule, and a reader that trusts recordStatus is right there and wrong here.
Fix_Approach: Compute overdue from nextDue against the asked-about date and say so, using recordStatus only as corroboration; where the two disagree, state the disagreement rather than choosing (the precedent is BUG-896, where the code states the conflict honestly and the data decision is the owner's). Separately, this is a DATA question for the owner: three ServiceSchedule rows carry a recordStatus their own nextDue contradicts.
Verification: Live 2026-09-30. Graph checked: all 25 ontosage:ServiceSchedule with nextDue, filtered to STR(?due) < '2026-09-30' returns 6; full triple dumps of SVC-01 (recordStatus overdue) and SVC-03 (recordStatus due, nextDue 2026-09-06, comment 'Due within the week').

Title: An ambiguous room name silently expands to six rooms, and the series labels collapse to bare digits
Description: Asked live 2026-09-30: 'How does humidity in Telecommunications Room this week compare with last week?' The comparison now runs (the refusal in BUG-775 is gone) and reports eighteen figures labelled '**0 mean**: 49.7 in both periods', '**1 mean**: 49.5 now against 49.7 before', through '**5 lowest**: 42.1 now against 41.8 before'. The graph explains the digits: the building holds SIX Telecommunications Rooms, one per floor -- Telecom_Room_F0 (Room 0.34) through Telecom_Room_F5 (Room 5.34) -- so the name the user gave resolved to six referents and the series were labelled with the floor digit alone. The answer never says the name was ambiguous, never says six rooms were read, and never says which room each digit is. A reader sees eighteen numbers and cannot attach one of them to a room.
Root_Cause: Two things, both in the presentation rather than the binding: (a) a multi-referent resolution is not disclosed -- reading all six is a defensible choice, but silently is not; (b) the series label is derived by stripping the shared prefix from the six room labels, which for 'Telecommunications Room - Floor N (Room N.34)' leaves the digit.
Fix_Approach: Disclose the expansion in one sentence -- 'Telecommunications Room names six rooms, one per floor; here is each' -- which is the same treatment build_assumptions already gives a forecast horizon and BUG-949 proposes for a space TYPE. Label each series with its room, not the residue of a prefix strip. Do not narrow this to one room: picking one of six silently would be worse than reading all six.
Verification: Live 2026-09-30 (route intent=compare -> sparql). Graph checked: rdfs:label CONTAINS 'telecommunication' returns Room0.34, Room1.34, Room2.34, Room3.38, Room4.34, Room5.34 and the six Telecom_Room_F0..F5 entities.

Title: A 'tomorrow' forecast is answered with a horizon that starts now and mostly covers today
Description: Asked live 2026-09-30 at about 05:42 building time: 'What will the temperature be **tomorrow** in Room 2.01?' The answer is headed '**Horizon:** next 24 hours | **As of:** 2026-09-30 05:42' and its prediction table starts '2026-09-30 05:00' and runs hourly from there -- so nineteen of the twenty-four rows are TODAY and only the last five reach 2026-10-01. The word 'tomorrow' appears nowhere in the answer and no reinterpretation is disclosed; the reader asked about one calendar day and was given a rolling window mostly covering a different one. This is the shape BUG-480 was fixed for on the historical side ('yesterday' must not be the rolling 24 hours) reappearing on the forecast side.
Root_Cause: The forecast lane takes a horizon in hours and 'tomorrow' maps to 24, rather than to the bounds of the local calendar day after today. CLOCKS in CLAUDE.md gives the correct procedure and it is not being followed here: choose the LOCAL day the word names, then convert its bounds with to_store.
Fix_Approach: Smallest honest fix first and it is disclosure, not arithmetic: print 'taking "tomorrow" as the next 24 hours from 05:42' so a wrong reading costs one correction rather than a wrong number -- the same remedy BUG-943 settles on for deictics. Then bound the horizon to the named day: forecast 2026-10-01 00:00-23:59 and say so. Do NOT change the historical-window code while doing it; three wrong fixes and a withdrawn P1 came out of measuring these paths through a non-UTC session (lessons #103).
Verification: Live 2026-09-30, one ask, route intent=trend -> sparql. Forecast bound Air Temperature Sensor installed-node 2.01 correctly (BUG-826's binding failure is gone); only the window is wrong.
Refs: BUG-826; BUG-874; BUG-946; BUG-480; BUG-943; lessons #103

Title: A recurring window ('overnight', 'this afternoon') is matched against STORE hours, so it is shifted by the building's UTC offset
Description: Measured 2026-09-30. detect_mask('how much energy is used overnight?') returns HourMask(22, 6) and the SQL it emits is `(HOUR(datetime) >= 22 OR HOUR(datetime) < 6)`. `sensor_data.Datetime` and every narrow table are UTC, and the orchestrator's adapters pin each session to +00:00, so HOUR() is the UTC hour. A reading recorded at 22:30 on the occupants' clock is 21:30 in the store and `mask.covers()` returns False for it; converted with to_local('Europe/London') the same row returns True. Under BST the whole window is an hour out at both ends, and the Python second layer in sql_agent.fetch_data_for_uuids has the same fault because it calls `_hour_mask.covers(_parsed)` on the raw stored stamp. Every 'overnight', 'after hours', 'around lunchtime', 'mornings' and 'afternoons' answer on this building is therefore about a window shifted by the offset -- a night-time baseline that includes 06:00 and excludes 22:00.
Root_Cause: V6-T40 built the mask as an HOUR() predicate so the filtering happens in the store rather than after the fetch, which is right for cost and wrong for the clock: the hours a word like 'afternoon' names are the occupants' hours, and HOUR() over a UTC column gives UTC hours. Nothing converts. CLAUDE.md's CLOCKS rule covers exactly this case -- 'choose the LOCAL day a word names, then convert its bounds with to_store' -- and a recurring window is the same problem repeated daily.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED here, and deliberately: the SQL half needs the predicate shifted by the zone offset (CONVERT_TZ, or the offset folded into the hour bounds, with DST making a fixed offset wrong twice a year), and the Python half is one line in sql_agent -- but the two must move together or they will disagree, and V6-T40's behaviour is verified. NOTE the new forecast-side reduction does it correctly: `forecasting/window_aggregate.reduce_to_requested_figure` converts each predicted step with to_local BEFORE applying the mask, and a test asserts the UTC and +2 answers DIFFER. So the system now has two readings of 'afternoon' until this row is done. Whoever takes it should make time_windows itself own the conversion so there is one.
Verification: Re-run the two-line probe above: a stored row at 21:30 UTC must be INSIDE 'overnight' for a building on UTC+1, and a row at 05:30 UTC must be OUTSIDE it. Then ask 'how much energy is used overnight?' and check the hours in the emitted predicate against the building's declared zone.

Title: A future bound compiles to 'now+1d', which no resolver in this system parses, leaving a window that starts NOW and never ends
Description: Measured 2026-09-30 by calling the classifier directly. 'Will floor 3 or floor 4 be warmer tomorrow?' compiles to start='2026-09-30 04:32:40', end='now+1d'. `dialogue_agent._resolve_relative_dt` only matches a PAST relative bound, so 'now+1d' passes through unresolved; `_sanitize_dt` in both SQL builders then rejects it and the end bound vanishes. What reaches the store is `datetime >= '<now>'` with no upper bound, which selects the handful of rows written since the question was asked -- or none. `sensor_binder.history_window` already drops a future window, but only for the `trend` and `forecast` intents, and this question classifies as `compare`.
Root_Cause: The intent prompt invites a relative bound and gives 'now-1d' as the example; the model reasonably answers a question about tomorrow with 'now+1d'. The resolver's regex has no '+' branch. Two readings of the same string then disagree: the compile thinks it set an end, the builder silently has none.
Fix_Approach: MITIGATED, not fixed. `sql_agent.resolve_named_window` now drops BOTH bounds when the resolved start is not in the past on the STORE clock (store_now(), never the local clock -- CLAUDE.md CLOCKS), and logs it, so the lane reads recent history instead of querying rows that do not exist. That is history_window's rule applied by the lane that issues the query, for every intent. The PARSER is still wrong and lives in dialogue_agent, which was outside this session's file boundary: either teach `_resolve_relative_dt` the '+' form or stop the prompt offering relative bounds at all. Until then a future end is dropped rather than honoured, which is right for a data window and wrong if anything ever legitimately needs one.
Verification: Offline: tests/test_the_period_a_question_names_is_the_period_fetched.py::test_a_window_that_starts_in_the_future_is_dropped. LIVE OWED: ask 'Will floor 3 or floor 4 be warmer tomorrow?' and read the log for '[sql] compiled window starts at ... which is not in the past on the stores' clock' followed by a fetch that returns rows.

Title: The row-cap disclosure is composed and tested but has only ONE of its two appenders; the response node's is owed
Description: BUG-939's live consequence was an answer reading 'Across **all** 1,000 recorded values' -- model prose, not the SQL lane's. The lane's `formatted_response` is only shown when it WINS the response dispatch; for a compare or analytics turn the narration wins and the lane's prose is never read. The window-substitution disclosure solves this by being appended TWICE: once in sql_agent's own prose and once in `_response_node`, guarded by `if _note not in final_response`. The truncation note now has the same structure -- `disclosure_gate.TRUNCATION_KEY`, `truncation_in()` and `truncation_note()` mirror the substitution pair, the marker carries `row_limit`, `rows_earliest`, `rows_latest` and `requested_window.label`, and sql_agent appends it to its own prose -- but the response-node half is NOT wired, because `orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py` was outside this session's file boundary.
Root_Cause: A fact about the ROWS can only be said by something that sees the rows, and the text that reaches the reader is chosen later. One appender covers one of the two paths, and it is not the path the defect was observed on.
Fix_Approach:
The disclosure is appended in `_response_node`, BESIDE its sibling the substituted-window note, and for the same reason: when the dispatch picks model prose the lane's own wording never reaches the reader. That is exactly how 'Across ALL 1,000 readings taken between 21 Sep 21:36...' got published TWO LINES BELOW the lane's own log line 'the set is TRUNCATED and its size is not a count of what exists'. The guard fired and nobody heard it.
Read from the STRUCTURED marker (`disclosure_gate.truncation_in`), never from prose — a check that guessed from wording would be wrong precisely where the wording is confident and the rows are not complete. Idempotent on the note's own text, and fails open.
THE NOTE STATES TWO FACTS BECAUSE EITHER ALONE MISLEADS: the row count is the size of a SAMPLE, so no figure derived from its length is a count of what the period holds; and the rows are the NEWEST ones, so the period actually covered begins later than the one asked for. 'Across all 1,000 recorded values' has both of those wrong at once.
Worth recording: `rows_capped` had been on the bus since BUG-479 with exactly ONE reader (`report_agent`) — a fact recorded rather than a fact used, for months.
Verification: Offline: 12 tests, incl. both facts of the note asserted separately, the marker-not-prose rule, idempotency, fail-open, and that the SIBLING substitution note is still present (they are siblings, not replacements). 1,008 pass across every test touching _response_node, disclosure_gate, resolve_named_window or _sql_node. LIVE RE-ASK OWED: a question broad enough to cap — the note must appear, and must NOT appear on the now-bounded 'this week against last week', which no longer truncates at all. | LIVE 2026-09-30, first appearance in a real answer: 'What is the maximum occupancy of room 2.15?' now carries '_At least one sensor returned the full 1000 rows this question reads per sensor, so these readings are a SAMPLE of the newest data and their number is not a count of what the period holds. The readings used run from 2026-09-28 04:52:18 to 2026-09-30 09:12:54. That is the newest part...' — exactly the claim that 'Across ALL 1,000 readings' used to make wrongly.
Refs: BUG-939; BUG-479; BUG-658 (the two-appender pattern); orchestrator/services/disclosure_gate.py; orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py::_response_node

Title: BUG-946 cannot be finished by routing alone: a two-sided forecast needs each side bound through the GRAPH, and a routing change without it would make the answer worse
Description: BUG-946 asks that 'Will floor 3 or floor 4 be warmer tomorrow?' reach the forecaster. Today it answers from current means and SAYS SO -- 'The data reflects current conditions; it does not indicate which floor will be warmer tomorrow' -- which is honest. The forecast lane forecasts ONE series: `_select_primary_sensor` picks the single best-matching sensor, and W2-02's aggregate path folds ALL bound sensors into one. Routed there as it stands, a two-floor question would be answered with one confident forecast of one floor, or of both floors folded together, presented as the comparison. That is strictly worse than an honest decline, so the routing rule was NOT added.
Root_Cause: By the time forecast_agent runs, both floors' sensors are in one bag and the only thing distinguishing them is the LABEL. Assigning a side from a label is BUG-884 exactly -- a floor question bound to the sensors NAMED for the floor rather than the sensors ON it -- and `data_coverage_audit.py` mis-files about 4,000 of 5,874 sensors that way, which is why its per-floor gaps cannot be trusted. Each side has to be bound floor -> spaces -> points, filtered by the resolved Brick class, which happens upstream of this lane.
Fix_Approach: The HONESTY half is built and tested: `orchestrator/services/forecasting/overlap_verdict.py` takes two already-bound, already-aggregated forecasts and returns a verdict -- no winner when the 95% intervals overlap, no winner when the gap is below the two decimals the figures are printed to (BUG-885 one decimal place down), a missing interval read as uncertainty rather than as certainty, and `render()` naming BOTH forecasts either way. 17 tests, including a guard that the module imports no regex engine and never reads a label, so side assignment cannot creep into it. What is OWED: (1) bind the two sides separately through the graph and produce two aggregated series; (2) run the existing aggregate-then-forecast path once per side; (3) THEN one routing rule in routing_contract.py, after `_r_forecast`, narrow to a comparison that names a FUTURE period and no past one, with test_precedence_order_is_pinned updated in the same commit and the probe green before and after.
Verification: Ask 'Will floor 3 or floor 4 be warmer tomorrow?'; PASS names two forecasts with their intervals and picks no winner while they overlap. The verdict half alone is verified offline by tests/test_two_forecasts_name_a_winner_only_when_they_separate.py.
Refs: BUG-946; W2-03; W2-01; W2-02; BUG-884; BUG-885; orchestrator/services/forecasting/overlap_verdict.py

Title: A calendar period is fetched with one whole period of margin, and the reason is a threshold in a module that must not be edited
Description: `requested_interval.calendar_period_bounds` resolves 'this week against last week' to THREE whole weeks, not two. The extra week is not slack: `series_summary._bucket_size` chooses its bucket unit from the span of the ROWS it receives and needs 1.5 units before it will bucket by that unit, and the rows can only reach NOW. An exact two-week fetch asked on a Wednesday holds 9.2 days, under the 10.5 that rule requires, so it would be bucketed by DAY and the comparison would be between two partial days -- the 291.7% rise BUG-936's fix exists to prevent. The same shortfall applies to a month pair asked on the 1st (745 hours against the 1,008 a month bucket needs), and to quarter and year pairs. Reaching one unit further back makes the span at least two whole units, which clears 1.5 for every unit and every weekday.
Root_Cause: Two modules answer 'how long is this window' -- one from the bounds and one from the rows -- and only the second decides the bucket. The margin makes them agree for the case that matters; it does not remove the second answer.
Fix_Approach: Accepted as the narrow fix, with the coupling PINNED rather than remembered: tests/test_the_period_a_question_names_is_the_period_fetched.py::test_the_span_still_buckets_by_the_unit_the_question_named calls `series_summary._bucket_size` on the span these bounds produce, for nine (question, unit, weekday) combinations, so a change to either side fails a test instead of silently changing an answer. The cleaner shape is for the bucket unit to come from the period the question NAMED rather than from the span -- `summarise_periods` already accepts a `bucket` argument that nothing passes -- but series_summary.py was outside this session's file boundary and it is a VERIFIED_LIVE module. Worth doing next time someone is in there.
Verification: 9 parametrised offline cases pinning the coupling; 45 tests in the new file; 579 pass across every test that imports sql_agent, requested_interval, series_summary or mysql_narrow_adapter.

Title: CAVEAT-784's mechanism is confirmed at the pattern level and is NOT repairable at the marker level
Description: Re-derived 2026-09-30, every number in CAVEAT-784 reproduces exactly: grader GOOD_DECLINE 42 -> 75, GOOD_ANSWER 52 -> 28, grader weird 36.1% -> 29.9%, hand 64.6% -> 61.2%, and 36 of the 75 are WEIRD by hand. The mechanism is now located in the source: ONE pattern, _DECLINE_PATTERNS[0] 'do(es) not (contain|record|include|indicate|provide|hold|show)', is the SOLE decline evidence for 63 of run 5's 75 GOOD_DECLINE rows and 56 of run 6's 69, and its precision as a decline detector falls 65% (run 4) -> 51% (run 5) -> 41% (run 6) as the census wording arrives. Three candidate redefinitions were measured against all 882 hand labels: shipped kappa 0.278; no_census 0.277 (WORSE); no_broad_beside_rows 0.305 (best, +0.027); drop_broad 0.235. The best candidate leaves the worst run's GOOD_DECLINE precision at 42.0%.
Root_Cause: Whether a stated absence is TRUE is not checkable from the answer text -- the grader's own reason string says so. No re-wording of a shape rule can distinguish a true absence from a false one, so the bucket is unfixable offline by construction, not by defect.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED BY RE-WORDING, deliberately: a 0.027 kappa gain would invalidate every previously recorded grader number while leaving the bucket unusable. Instead the grader now states its own limits (BUCKET_LIMITS_NOTE on every --grade and --gate) and refuses an uncalibrated comparison (BUG-987). The GOOD_DECLINE bucket must not be quoted as evidence of quality.
Verification: python scripts/audit_grader_calibration.py --section patterns --section candidates. The module's grader call is proved row-for-row identical to grade_run before any figure is printed. | DECISION 2026-09-30, mine: `no_broad_beside_rows` is NOT landed. It gains +0.027 kappa (0.278 -> 0.305), leaves the worst run's GOOD_DECLINE precision at 42.0%, and makes no bucket usable -- while invalidating every grader figure recorded to date. A change that costs the whole comparison history and still cannot be relied on is not worth 0.027. The finding underneath it stands and is the thing to act on: WHETHER A STATED ABSENCE IS TRUE IS NOT CHECKABLE FROM THE ANSWER TEXT, so this bucket cannot be fixed offline by construction -- it needs the graph, which is how tail M's seven false declines were found by hand.

Title: The grader gate reported GATE PASSED on the run5 -> run6 regression; it now refuses an uncalibrated comparison
Description: `grade_answers_rubric.py --gate` passes when the weird share falls. On run5 -> run6 it measured the share falling 29.9% -> 27.9% and named run 6 the best of six, while a hand read of the same 147 answers measured that run regressing 61.2% -> 65.3% weird (BUG-787). Verified 2026-09-30: of the five consecutive wave deltas the grader agrees with the hand read on the SIGN of four and is wrong on exactly that one, so the write-up's surviving claim -- 'trust its direction, not its value' -- does not hold for the delta that decided the freeze. Spearman over the six runs 0.754.
Root_Cause: The gate compared two runs whose declines are worded differently. The grader scores SHAPE and was calibrated on 294 answers written before the register-census wording existed, so the share moved because the answers were re-worded, not because they improved.
Fix_Approach: FIXED in scripts/grade_answers_rubric.py: `decline_profile` counts each decline pattern's firing rate per run and `wording_shift` reports any pattern that moves by >= 8 rows AND >= 10% of its old count; `gate` does not pass while a shift is present, whatever the share did, and the CLI prints GATE NOT CALIBRATED and exits 1. Thresholds calibrated on FIVE deltas, which is thin, and named constants rather than literals.
Verification: Before: run5->run6 exited 0 with 'GATE PASSED'. After: exits 1 with GATE NOT CALIBRATED, naming the pattern that moved (81 -> 72 rows). Fires on run1->run2, run4->run5, run5->run6; silent on run2->run3 and run3->run4, where the wording was stable and the direction was right. 48 pre-existing grader tests still pass; 11 new guard tests in tests/test_the_grader_gate_refuses_an_uncalibrated_comparison.py.

Title: What this grader MAY be quoted for: the WEIRD count is a lower bound, and nothing else is usable
Description: Measured 2026-09-30 over all 882 hand labels (6 runs x 147). WEIRD-bucket precision per run: 95.9 / 93.7 / 84.7 / 84.9 / 84.1 / 85.4 %; pooled 311/349 = 89.1% [85.4%, 92.0%] Wilson; recall 311/597 = 52.1%. GOOD_ANSWER precision is 38.5-43.2% in EVERY run -- worse than chance on a corpus that is 61-77% weird -- and GOOD_DECLINE is 42.0-62.5%. Pooled 3-way agreement 54.4%, kappa 0.278, and kappa falls every run from 0.451 to 0.160.
Root_Cause: A precision-oriented signal detector reported as if it were a classifier. The WEIRD rules fire only on a defect the text exposes, so they are nearly always right and often silent; the other two buckets are what is left over, which is not the same as evidence of quality.
Fix_Approach: Publish the lower bound, never the share: 'at least N of 147 answers carry a defect visible in the text'. The grader now prints this limit on every run. Any published quality number needs a hand read or a calibrated judge, not this instrument.
Verification: python scripts/audit_grader_calibration.py --section agreement

Title: BUG-785's '23 answers carry census text' does not reproduce, and was counted three different ways
Description: The same 147 run-5 answers have been counted 23 (READER-5, phase0_run5_read.md line 324), 17 (READER-6's mechanical recount, phase0_run6_read.md line 218) and 11 (an independent re-derivation, 2026-09-30). READER-5's own prose names 25 distinct rows as carrying the wording it counted as 23. The paraphrase series is further apart: published 1/1/8/6/34/19 against re-derived 0/1/5/2/17/14.
Root_Cause: READER-6's counts were produced by 'one regex per row' that was never committed, only described in prose, so the figure cannot be replayed. The only external check available is the row list: the re-derived detector reproduces READER-6's run-6 word-level rows EXACTLY (23, 26, 37, 38, 53, 61, 98, 107) and its run-6 count of 8, which is why the run-5 disagreement is attributed to the count and not to the detector.
Fix_Approach: The DIRECTION reproduces in every method (run 5 -> run 6 falls) and the LEVEL does not. Quote the direction; do not quote 23, 17 or 11 without the method beside it. The detector is now committed in scripts/audit_grader_calibration.py (CENSUS_FORMS) so the next count is reproducible.
Verification: python scripts/audit_grader_calibration.py --section census

Title: The claim-binding headline is measured on run 2 -- the WORST of the six runs -- and nothing says so
Description: CAVEAT-791's figures all reproduce exactly from docs/phase0/claim_binding_measurement.json: HEADLINE 52 of 703 unbound = 7.4% over 71 answers, PARTIAL 55.7%, 55 of 147 unassessable, and the headline partition covers 71/147 = 48.3% of the bank. The artefact's own generated_from names phase0_rerun.md.jsonl, which is RUN 2, whose hand read is 76.9% weird -- rank 6 of 6. docs/NIGHT_OF_2026-09-17_RESULTS.md quotes the 7.4% beside a six-run headline table without naming which run it came from.
Root_Cause: The measurement was taken early and the write-up was corrected for its PARTITION (the 2026-09-18 correction block) but never for its RUN. A partition caveat and a stale-run caveat are different problems and only one was recorded.
Fix_Approach: State the run beside the figure, or re-measure on the frozen state. The audit now derives and prints which run the artefact came from and that run's rank, so the omission cannot recur silently.
Verification: python scripts/audit_grader_calibration.py --section binding

Title: Four decline classifiers, one corpus, three different answers: 6 / 11 / 16 declines among the same 73
Description: Measured 2026-09-30 over the 73 stored supervisor-pack answers: publication_gate.is_decline calls 6 of them declines, grade_answers_rubric.is_decline calls 11, and regression_answerability.classify calls 16 (14 declined + 2 refused). A fourth classifier is an inline `decline_phrases` list in scripts/ttl_gap_audit.py. Against a set of 98 first-person-inability leads DERIVED by parsing orchestrator/ (45 modules), recall is 12.2% / 15.3% / 13.3%. Restricted to the three modules CAVEAT-952 names, publication_gate recognises 2 of 10 and misses all three literals of the commonest decline. | RE-MEASURED 2026-09-30 over 2,868 stored answers (docs/phase0/*.jsonl + the 73-answer pack), and BOTH the headline and the framing are now wrong. (1) THE HEADLINE IS STALE: publication_gate is 11 on the 73, not 6 -- BUG-992 added 'i couldn't answer that' -- so the split is 11/11/16, two totals not three. (2) THE MATCHING TOTAL IS NOT A RECONCILIATION, and this is the more important half: the two 11s overlap on THREE rows out of nineteen. pg-only {2,5,7,27,28,38,52,72}; grader-only {13,15,22,36,42,47,54,73}; 16 of 73 are a decline to exactly one of them. (3) NO ANSWER IN 2,868 IS CALLED A DECLINE BY ALL FOUR -- 0 unanimous, 1,632 unanimous-answer, 1,236 (43.1%) contested. Pairwise kappa 0.004-0.484, NEGATIVE (-0.042) for regression_answerability vs ttl_gap_audit. (4) ANCHORED TO 1,012 HAND LABELS where the label settles KIND (GOOD_DECLINE / GOOD_ANSWER only; WEIRD is excluded because a false decline and a fabricated answer share it), the four are NOT one concept with noise -- they are four points on a recall/false-decline trade-off: regression_answerability 28.9% recall and 0/535 wrong; publication_gate 14.9% and 11/535 (2.1%); grade_answers_rubric 52.6% and 162/535 (30.3%); ttl_gap_audit 6.5% and 9/535.
Root_Cause: CAVEAT-887, one level up: each classifier is an independently maintained marker list against a generated target, so they drift apart and no single one is authoritative. The derived-set recall figures are an UPPER BOUND on the gap because the derivation rule is syntactic and deliberately over-captures (a refusal and a transient read failure match it too).
Fix_Approach: scripts/audit_decline_markers.py derives the lead set from the emitting source rather than restating it, and tests/test_the_decline_classifiers_know_their_own_wording.py produces its fixtures by CALLING clarification.compose_abstract and fallback_wording.compose_unanswered, so a wording change moves the fixtures with it. The 73-answer split is pinned there. The durable fix is CAVEAT-887's: record the lane's own outcome on the bus and compare a FACT rather than re-deriving a kind from prose. | RECONCILED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY MERGING, 2026-09-30, and the decision is: THREE MUST DIFFER AND NOW HAVE A MEASURED JUSTIFICATION, ONE HAS NONE. regression_answerability is correctly the most conservative (0 false declines on 535 hand-confirmed answers) because for a GATE a manufactured regression is the expensive error (lessons #141); publication_gate is correctly conservative because a false decline there marks an answered turn as declined in the session summary the classification prompt reads; grade_answers_rubric is correctly the most permissive only in the sense that it is the KNOWN defect of CAVEAT-784/788 and a reader must be told it is still there. ttl_gap_audit's inline list has no defensible position on either axis and is CAVEAT-1349. Unifying them would move at least two off the point that is right for them AND invalidate every recorded figure, which is the CAVEAT-986 calculation again. The durable fix is unchanged and is a PRODUCT change handed back: nothing the server returns today says whether a turn declined -- ontosage_route says which lane, turn_outcome says whether the machinery ran (ok/partial/timeout/backend_unavailable/failed), and retrieval_outcome has the right vocabulary but is scoped to sensor retrieval and never surfaced on /v1.
Verification: python scripts/audit_decline_markers.py; pytest tests/test_the_decline_classifiers_know_their_own_wording.py -q (11 passed, 6 xfailed) | python scripts/audit_measurement_instrument.py --section classifiers; pytest tests/test_the_decline_classifiers_do_not_share_a_core.py -q (3 passed). It is false at the row level (3 of 19 overlap) -- lessons #160 inside the test written to prevent that class of error. The counts test is kept and now says it is the weaker guarantee.

Title: CAVEAT-952's live consequence: a turn that ended in the commonest decline is REMEMBERED as answered
Description: Reproduced 2026-09-30: publication_gate.is_decline returns False for all three surface forms of "I couldn't answer that [about X] from <building>'s records." Inside publication_gate.evaluate the miss is INERT, because the next guard (has_quantitative_claim) returns False and the turn publishes anyway. It is NOT inert in session_summary.outcome_of, which is the only other consumer and which returns OUTCOMES[0] ('answered') for such a turn. That summary is injected into the classification prompt on every /v1 turn (CAVEAT-910), so the model is told the previous turn was answered when it was declined.
Root_Cause: One shared marker list serving two callers with different tolerances. session_summary.py's own docstring says it reuses this classifier 'rather than adding a fifth decline classifier', which is right -- and it inherits the gap.
Fix_Approach:
Two markers added to `publication_gate._DECLINE_MARKERS`: "i couldn't answer that" and "i could not answer that". `_normalise` already folds the curly apostrophe, so two strings cover all three surface forms.
WHY IT MATTERED IN ONE PLACE AND NOT THE OTHER, which is the part worth keeping: inside `evaluate` the miss was INERT -- the next guard, `has_quantitative_claim`, catches a decline anyway, because a decline carries no figure. In `session_summary.outcome_of`, the only other caller, it was LIVE: a turn that ended in that decline was recorded as `answered`, and that summary is injected into the classification prompt on EVERY /v1 turn. The system was telling itself it had answered questions it had declined.
CLAUDE.md's rule for this list was followed rather than assumed (lessons #141). The two markers move FIVE of the 73 stored answers -- pack indexes 1, 4, 27, 37, 51 -- and every one OPENS with that decline, so the move is the point rather than a side effect. `"answer that from"` was tried and REJECTED: it also captures "I can answer that from the building's records: the mean is 22.9 C", which is an answer.
Verification: Offline 2026-09-30: all three surface forms now return is_decline=True and outcome_of='declined'; three genuine answers still return False/'answered'. 453 pass and SIX XFAILS FLIPPED TO XPASS across every test touching publication_gate, is_decline, session_summary or outcome_of. The pinned split of the 73 stored answers moved publication_gate 6 -> 11, which was predicted before the change and verified after, and **it now AGREES with the grader's 11** -- the first time two of the three classifiers have split that corpus the same way. The pack gate's 16 is still the outlier, so CAVEAT-887 stays open on it.

Title: The six hand reads are not a stationary label set, so every marginal delta from them is confounded
Description: CAVEAT-790's figures all reproduce exactly (run1->run6 28/17 p=0.135; run5->run6 5/11 p=0.210; run3->run6 16/16 p=1.000; run1->run5 28/11 p=0.009; high-confidence weird 60/68/65/60/55/59; low-confidence weird 14/7/1/2/1/1). What the row does not record is that the READER'S OWN confidence distribution moved with them: low-confidence labels over ALL rows run 31/18/6/8/5/14 of 147. Counting only the weird labels the reader was not unsure about, the bank is FLAT: 93 / 106 / 95 / 93 / 89 / 95. One unblinded reader read the same 147 answers six times knowing which run was which.
Root_Cause: A within-subject repeated read with no blinding and no second rater. The reader became more decisive between run 1 and run 3, and that change is indistinguishable in a marginal share from a change in the system.
Fix_Approach: Report the paired test, not the marginal share -- pairing survives the confound and the marginal count does not. The defensible claims, both readings: run 5 beat run 1 (as labelled 28/11 p=0.009, risk difference +11.6 pp [+3.5, +19.7]; complete-case on confident labels 22/4 of n=113 p=0.001, +15.9 pp [+7.6, +24.3]), and the FROZEN state run 6 did not (0.135 as labelled, 0.189 complete-case). Any future read needs a second rater on a sample and the run order concealed.
Verification: python scripts/audit_grader_calibration.py --section series --section mcnemar

Title: The decline's pointer and the register selector use DIFFERENT matchers, and the pointer is the more capable one
Description:
THIS IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND BUG-947's TELL. Four of the seven false denials hand-read on tail M named the right register in the same sentence as the refusal, and the parent row read that as 'a lane identifying the source and not reading it'. It is narrower and more actionable than that. The two halves of that sentence are decided by different string matchers:
  * the DECLINE's pointer (fallback_wording.compose_boundary_pointer and nearest_holdings) compares grounding_guard.content_terms, which SINGULARISES every word -- content_terms('escalation routes') == content_terms('escalation route') == {'escalation','rout'};
  * the register SELECTOR (record_registry.rank_record_classes) matches a declared lay term with \b<term>\b, which a trailing 's' ends.
Measured offline against the vocabulary as it stood at HEAD, with the guard-set snapshot of held classes: 'Are emergency contacts, duty managers and escalation routes current, reachable and authorised for tonight?' selected NO register, and its decline opened 'Example Building does keep Department, Approval and evidence record and Competency requirement records, which I can read for you.' The wording was never accidentally accurate. The decline is composed with the more capable matcher, so it can print the answer's location in the act of refusing.
Root_Cause: Two matchers for one decision, neither aware of the other. content_terms is deliberately crude (it is a stemmer for topic overlap); _term_pattern is deliberately exact (a lay term is a corpus-wide change, so it must not match loosely). Both choices are right for their own job and wrong together: whichever is more tolerant decides what the reader is TOLD, while the stricter one decides what is DONE.
Fix_Approach: Not closed by making them agree -- that was measured and rejected (CAVEAT-972). Closed by making the disagreement COUNTABLE, because a defect found by hand-reading 62 answers once is a defect nobody will notice recurring: fallback_wording.pointer_only_registers(question, held) returns the registers the decline WILL PRINT that the selector could not reach, and capability_agent._log_selector_gap logs them at INFO before both of that lane's decline paths. Each name is one declared lay term away from being reachable, so the log line is the work order for whoever owns that register's vocabulary (lessons #126: a fail-open component needs a count of how often it ACTED). Only the printed top-N is reported: counting every register the fuzzy matcher touches was tried first and is useless -- tail M #28 produced FIFTEEN names, a dump rather than a work order.
Verification: tests/test_a_decline_names_no_register_the_selector_cannot_reach.py (8 tests), which pins the disagreement at BOTH matchers, pins that only printed registers are counted, and pins that the counter cannot raise into a decline. tests/test_register_reach.py + tests/test_register_evidence_and_event_store.py stay at 109 passed (117 with the new file). 289 passed / 6 xfailed / 0 failed across the nine test files that import fallback_wording or clarification. LIVE IS OWED: the log line has not been seen in a container, because this session was forbidden to restart the orchestrator.

Title: CORRECTION to BUG-948: the qualifier mechanism provably cannot separate the two 'eligible alternative' questions
Description:
BUG-948's Fix_Approach prescribes two ordered steps and says the first one is available: 'The module already has the mechanism for exactly this -- qualifiers / _qualifier_score / _only_modifies -- and WorkspaceProfile's qualifier set is EMPTY.' Measured, that step does not work, and doing it first would have destroyed the very guard it was meant to protect plus the row it was meant to keep.
_qualifier_score('eligible alternative', ...) and _qualifier_score('eligible alternatives', ...) both return 0.00 for BOTH questions:
  row 53  'which currently eligible alternative SHOULD I ask the room team...'  -> 0.00
  RB-056  'what eligible alternatives EXIST?'                                  -> 0.00
So declaring the phrase a qualifier removes WorkspaceProfile from RB-056 (the guard's wish) AND from row 53, which tests/test_register_reach.py::test_a_register_the_building_holds_is_reached pins as WorkspaceProfile (BUG-749).
Root_Cause: _qualifier_score's attributive test asks whether the word FOLLOWING the term is in _FUNCTION_WORDS, as a proxy for 'followed by a noun'. Row 53 is followed by the modal 'should' and RB-056 by the verb 'exist'; neither is in the list, so both are read as attributive and score nothing. Grammatically both are in fact NON-attributive -- the phrase is the head in each -- so the two questions are grammatically identical at that phrase and no rule over grammar can separate them. Extending _FUNCTION_WORDS with modals would pass both tests and be dishonest: it would separate them only by the accident of which words the list happens to hold, and the next phrasing ('what eligible alternatives ARE available?' -- 'are' IS in the list) brings the over-capture straight back. That is BUG-893's lesson verbatim: a denylist over English cannot be finished.
Fix_Approach: No change made. Recorded so the next attempt does not spend the measurement again, and so BUG-948's step 1 is not treated as available. The phrase is irreducibly ambiguous, and the catalogue proves it BOTH ways: 'which three eligible alternatives are closest' (LT-005) is a WorkspaceProfile question and RB-056 is a Booking question, and they differ only in the surrounding vocabulary.
Verification: Measured with orchestrator.services.record_registry._term_score and _qualifier_score directly, offline, on both questions verbatim: term_score 40.00 / 42.00, qualifier_score 0.00 / 0.00, only_modifies False / False. The following words are ' should i ask the ' and ' exist? '.
Refs: BUG-948; BUG-947; BUG-749; BUG-893; BUG-545; lessons #153

Title: Automatic plural tolerance on declared lay terms: implemented, measured on 2,960 catalogue questions, and REVERTED
Description:
BUG-948's cost ('people write plurals constantly, so this is silently costing far more than the question that exposed it') is real, and a generic fix for it is not safe. Implemented as the module's OWN _plural() applied to each declared lay term in _terms_for -- the same rule already applied to the label and class-name seeds, so no regex change and no new mechanism -- and measured by diffing the register every catalogue question selects, against the same schema without the step:
  ALL TERMS:        79 of 2,960 questions move -- 65 gained a register, 14 changed, 0 lost. Read: of the 65 gains about 30 right, 10 partial, 25 WRONG; of the 14 changes 5 better, 7 worse, 2 neither. ONE guard fails by name (test_the_terms_rejected_for_over_capture_stay_rejected, RB-056).
  MULTI-WORD ONLY:  21 move -- 18 gained, 3 changed. Read: 11 right, 2 partial, 5 wrong; 1 change better, 2 worse. The SAME guard still fails.
The wrong direction concentrates in a handful of GENERIC-IN-THE-PLURAL declared terms, which is the finding worth keeping: 'barrier'->'barriers' (7 questions, nearly all wrong, because in this corpus a barrier is an impediment, not door hardware), 'event'->'events' (6 wrong), 'display'->'displays' (2 wrong), and two question FRAMES, 'which entrance'->'which entrances' (4 wrong) and 'which lift'->'which lifts' (1). A frame's plural quantifies over a set, so any question listing several nouns contains it incidentally.
Root_Cause: The scorer weights a term by len(term) x 2 for multi-word, so a long GENERIC phrase in the plural outranks a short PRECISE register name: RB-056 scored WorkspaceProfile 42.00 on 'eligible alternatives' against Booking 8.00 on 'bookings'. Plural tolerance is right for a specific phrase ('escalation route') and wrong for a generic one ('eligible alternative'), and nothing lexical distinguishes them -- see BUG-971 for why the qualifier mechanism cannot either.
Fix_Approach: REVERTED; record_registry.py is unchanged by this session. A safe subset exists and needs THREE interacting new rules -- multi-word terms only, plus an exclusion for terms that open with an interrogative or determiner, plus a ranking tier in which a class whose ONLY evidence is an inferred plural ranks below any class with a declared match. Together those give roughly 11 right / 2 partial / 0 wrong / 0 guard violations, and the tier rule has the useful property that it cannot move any question that ranks today, because before the change every match is declared. THREE new rules in the most delicate scorer in the system, unverifiable live in this session, is not a trade to make unattended. The alternative that WAS taken is TTL-first and needs no code at all: declare the plural the register wants (BUG-973). DO NOT re-apply plural tolerance without re-running this measurement; the numbers above are the baseline.
Verification: Diff harness over scripts/register_reach.py's Reach model (the same offline oracle the guard tests use), 2,960 questions from docs/smart_building_questions.csv, both variants, with the full move list read by hand. tests/test_register_reach.py + tests/test_register_evidence_and_event_store.py: 108 passed / 1 failed under the all-terms variant, and the failure is the guard that names WorkspaceProfile and RB-056 explicitly. 109 passed after the revert.
Refs: BUG-948; BUG-971; BUG-893; BUG-693; lessons #38; lessons #153

Title: Two of BUG-947's seven false declines fixed by declaring the vocabulary the register wants (tail M #54 and #7)
Description: Instance (54), 'Are emergency contacts, duty managers and escalation ROUTES current, reachable and authorised for tonight?', was declined with 'I could not find this in Abacws Building's documents' over a Department register that declares 'escalation route', 'duty officer', 'who do i contact' and 'out of hours' -- well written for exactly this question and defeated by one character (BUG-948). Instance (7), 'Do you have a maintenance crew?', was declined although six departments are recorded, one labelled 'Mechanical and Electrical Maintenance' -- an INSTANCE label, which lends no vocabulary to any matcher.
Root_Cause: (54) _terms_for adds a plural for the LABEL and the CLASS NAME seeds and deliberately takes a declared lay term WHOLE, so a register's own plural is only reachable if its author wrote it. (7) A genuine vocabulary gap: no declared term of any register matches 'maintenance crew', and the Department block's own screening note records that bare 'team'/'teams' was dropped on purpose (37 questions, 7 of which already compute in other lanes).
Fix_Approach:
TTL-first, design contract #2, zero code. ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl: Department gains the plurals of its unambiguous multi-word terms -- 'escalation routes', 'duty officers', 'service desks', 'contact routes', 'response targets', 'responsible departments', 'accountable owners' -- and the maintenance phrasings 'maintenance team', 'maintenance teams', 'maintenance crew', 'maintenance crews', 'maintenance department', 'maintenance staff'. WHOLE PHRASES ONLY: the bare team/teams screening is not reopened. This cannot over-capture a term nobody named here, which is the whole argument for it over automatic tolerance (CAVEAT-972).
It fixes ROUTING as well as wording: dialogue_agent's TTL-first short-circuit selects with held_record_class over the same vocabulary, so both questions should now reach the register lane instead of the capability lane's document decline. Checked offline that none of the overrides sitting after that short-circuit takes them away again (_READINESS_RE, WAYFIND_RE, DELIBERATE_RE, PLANT_READING_RE, measured_reading_question are all False for both).
Verification: Offline against the real TBox through the guard harness: 'what are the escalation routes' ranks Department 34.00 (was NOTHING), the #54 wording ranks Department 34.00, 'Do you have a maintenance crew?' ranks Department 32.00, and the questions the change must NOT move are unmoved -- RB-056 stays Booking 8.00 and row 53 stays WorkspaceProfile 40.00. Catalogue diff: 4 of 2,960 questions move, all gains, no losses and no changes; read, 2 right (both escalation-route questions), 1 partial (service desks), 1 WRONG ('what must we communicate to the next operator, shift or maintenance team?' is a handover question and now selects Department; it selected nothing before, so nothing was stolen from HandoverRecord). Guard violations 0 -> 0. tests/test_register_reach.py + tests/test_register_evidence_and_event_store.py 109 passed. LIVE RE-ASK IS OWED and needs a restart, which this session was forbidden: ttl_uploader scans ontology/ and SHA-skips unchanged files, so the changed SHA will re-upload the schema on the next boot, and record_registry's 300 s cache then re-reads the terms. Re-ask both tail M wordings plus 'what is the escalation route' (which must still work) and 'when is the recycling collected?' (which must still reach the waste register).
Refs: BUG-947 (instances 54 and 7); BUG-948; CAVEAT-972; design contract #2

Title: Nine further register plurals the catalogue wants, measured and NOT authorised here
Description: The multi-word plural measurement in CAVEAT-972 did not only find over-capture; it found eleven catalogue questions that gain the RIGHT register, and nine of them belong to registers outside BUG-947's seven instances. Each is one declared term away, and each is a corpus-wide change (lessons #38), so they are listed rather than made: WasteCollectionPoint 'collection points' (3 questions, all right); StakeholderGroup 'user groups' (2, both right); AccessibleRoute 'rest points' and 'step-free journeys' (2, both right); FireSafetyAsset 'fire compartments'/'doorsets' (1); WorkspaceProfile 'eligible alternatives' (1 right, and the SAME phrase is wrong in RB-056 -- do not add this one, see BUG-971); PublicEvent 'digital services' (1, partial).
Root_Cause: Same as BUG-973: a declared lay term is taken whole, so a register is reachable in the plural only if its author wrote the plural.
Fix_Approach: One register at a time, each with a catalogue diff and the guard set at 0 violations, the way BUG-973 was done. Do NOT batch them: the measurement is only readable if a move can be attributed to a term.
Verification: Terms identified by asking the offline harness which matched term drove each gain, over the same 2,960-question catalogue.

Title: BUG-947 instance (2) needs TWO owner decisions, not one triple
Description: BUG-947 records the ConfigurationPeriod fix as 'one triple'. Verified here, it is two changes and both are owner decisions. (a) ontosage:ConfigurationPeriod is declared in ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl with a label and a comment and NO subClassOf link to o:Record or o:IntervalRecord, so _DISCOVER_QUERY cannot see it and 2,175 instances (counted in input/bldg1_configuration_history.ttl) are invisible by construction. Title: BUG-947 instances (28), (32) and (58) are NOT register-vocabulary defects, and the counter now says so
Description:
Measured offline with both matchers, against the live-shaped held-class snapshot:
  (28) 'Before I start a long acquisition, are the approved power, network and ventilation services currently available, and what verified interruption risks remain?' -- selector: NO register. Decline prints 'does keep Operating regime, Asset engineering profile and Approval and evidence record records', which matches BUG-947's report almost exactly. No single declared term is missing; the question names three services and spans at least four registers, which is the C8 shape that test_a_security_records_question_claims_no_register_at_all was written to keep declining.
  (58) 'How does observed occupancy compare with the design assumptions for each space, peak, operating mode and shared-resource dependency?' -- selector: NO register; the turn reached the analytics/SPARQL lane (confirmed in outputs/query_results/owui_tailM-1790716027-58..., which shows the generated SPARQL and the occupancy sensors it bound), so the decline is composed by clarification.compose_abstract AFTER the data lanes failed. That is design-occupancy work, not register work.
  (32) 'why is pl 2.5 increasing' -- selector: NO register AND the pointer names none either, so the gap counter is correctly silent. BUG-947 already calls this a routing question.

Fix_Approach: Not fixed here, and deliberately not forced: routing lives in routing_contract/dialogue_agent and the occupancy lanes were owned by other agents this session. What changed is that all three now leave a countable trace -- BUG-970's log line reports exactly the registers the decline printed, so (28)'s three names appear in the log as a vocabulary question and (32)'s silence distinguishes it as a routing one. The decline's closing sentence in clarification.compose_abstract no longer ends 'or tell me which record this should be in' immediately after naming the records; it ends 'Ask about one of those and I will read them.'
