Title: Period buckets are labelled by the UTC calendar, so '2026-W40' in an answer is the UTC week, not the occupants'
Description: `series_summary._bucket_of` calls `when.isocalendar()` and `when.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')` on the STORED stamp, which is UTC. For a building on UTC+1 every week and day label is therefore an hour out at both ends: a reading at 23:30 local on a Monday is bucketed into the previous ISO week. It is the same fault as BUG-1000 one level up -- a calendar boundary computed on the store's clock instead of the building's. Visible consequence, introduced by BUG-939's fix and worth expecting rather than debugging: because `calendar_period_bounds` chooses the period LOCALLY (as CLAUDE.md's CLOCKS rule requires) and converts its bounds to UTC, the start of a week-pair fetch lands one hour inside the PREVIOUS UTC week, so the per-week listing carries a small leading bucket -- e.g. '2026-W37: ... covers 1 of 168 hours'. It is disclosed (BUG-936's older-end wording says the shortness is a fact about the query), it does not change the answer (`_names_this_against_last` takes the two NEWEST buckets, which are the two asked for), and it is noise in the listing.
Root_Cause: Two clocks. The window is resolved in the building's zone because that is what a person means by 'this week'; the buckets inside it are labelled in UTC because nothing converts before labelling. Either both should be local or both UTC, and local is the one the project has already chosen for every other calendar word.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED: series_summary.py was outside this session's file boundary and is a VERIFIED_LIVE module. The change is small -- convert `when` with `to_local(when, building_tz())` inside `_bucket_of` -- but it moves every bucket label in every existing answer, so it needs its own before/after and should land with BUG-1000 so the system has ONE reading of a calendar boundary rather than three.
Verification: Bucket a reading recorded at 23:30 local on a Monday: it must be labelled the week that Monday belongs to, not the one before. Then ask 'compare energy use this week against last week' and check no 1-hour leading bucket appears.

Title: The resolved window is used by the fetch but not written back to the bus, so start_date/time_range can now disagree with the rows
Description: BUG-939's fix resolves a named calendar period inside `sql_agent.fetch_data_for_uuids`, which is where the query is built. The BUS keys the resolution corrects -- `start_date`, `end_date` and `time_range` -- are written by the dialogue node and are not updated, so after a period-named turn the bus says '2026-09-16 04:31 to 2026-09-30 04:31' (the classifier's rolling 14 days) while the rows came from '2026-09-13 23:00 to 2026-10-04 22:59' (the two ISO weeks named, plus the bucket margin). `analytics_agent` and `verifier_agent` both read `time_range`, and the evidence record's requested_period is built from it. This is precisely the shape `requested_interval` exists to end: one fact with two answers, held by two parts of the system.
Root_Cause: The resolution had to go where the query is built, because that is the last point before the store and the only place inside this session's file boundary. The bus is written one node earlier, in `_orchestrator._dialogue_node`, and the lane cannot reach back to it.
Fix_Approach:
One assignment in the SQL node, with the window resolved there as well as in the lane. `sql_agent.resolve_named_window` fixed the BOUNDS (BUG-939) but `time_range` on the bus was left as the classifier wrote it — and `time_range` is what the analytics node, the verifier and the evidence record all read. The rows could come from one period while every downstream consumer described another: BUG-936's shape arriving through a different door.
IDEMPOTENCY VERIFIED RATHER THAN TRUSTED: resolving 'Compare energy use this week against last week' twice gives 2026-09-13 23:00:00 .. 2026-10-04 22:59:59 both times, so calling it in the node and again in the lane is safe. A question naming no period returns None/None from `default_lookback`, so the builders' own fallback still applies and the commonest question shape is untouched.
ONE DEFECT IN MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, caught by checking the real dict instead of assuming the sibling's shape: I wrote `_win.get('label', '')`, and the window dict has no `label` — it carries `source`, `unit` and `offsets`. That would have written an empty string on every turn and looked like a working disclosure. The bus now carries the fields that exist.

Title: BUG-941 has escalated: the system now FABRICATES what the user said
Description: Re-measured live 2026-09-30 with scratchpad/memory_probe.py (8 turns on /v1/chat/completions, ONE chat id, unique filler so nothing came from resp_cache, 40-86 s per turn). Turn 1: 'I am looking into air quality in room 5.01 specifically.' Turns 2-7: floor temperatures. Turn 8: 'Remind me which room I said I was looking into, and why.' -> 'You mentioned you were looking into **Room0.01**.' followed by a sensor count for that room and 'the model does not contain any information about why you were interested in that particular room'. Sources: Building model. The user said room 5.01 and never said Room0.01. On 2026-09-29 the same question produced an honest decline about the building's records (BUG-941, P2); it now produces a FALSE CLAIM ABOUT WHAT THE USER SAID, in bold, decorated with real sensor counts. The session summary naming room 5.01 was injected on that very turn -- measured, 'session summary injected (516 chars)' -- and never read.
Root_Cause: The same cause as BUG-941 with a worse consequence. No intent covers 'what did I say', the question's room-shaped vocabulary classifies it as data, and a data lane answers it. What changed between the two measurements is the lane's CONFIDENCE, not its correctness: the deictic now binds a place (BUG-943's recency reading, compounded), and the narration states that binding as a fact about the USER rather than about the building. A decline that is about the wrong subject is a routing defect; an assertion about what the user said is a fabrication (design contract #4), and it is the least visible kind -- there is no live value for the reader to check it against.
Fix_Approach: orchestrator/services/session_recall.py: a lane that answers from the session record and QUOTES rather than interprets. Every noun it can emit is a word the user typed, so Room0.01 cannot be produced from a transcript that does not contain it -- which is a stronger guarantee than checking the referent would be, because a checker can have a hole and an absent code path cannot. It recalls SUBJECTS and not VALUES and says so in the answer (W5-01 keeps figures out of the record by construction; quietly omitting them would leave the reader unable to tell a recall with no measurement from one whose measurement was merely absent). With nothing recorded it declines by naming the user's own word back: 'I have no record of you mentioning "room" in this conversation.'
Verification:
LIVE 2026-09-30 after restart, all three caches flushed, same 8-turn probe that produced the fabrication. The recall turn now answers:
  **From this conversation, in your own words:**
  - Turn 1 — "I am looking into air quality in room 5.01 specifically." (answered)
  - (6 other turn(s) in this conversation did not mention "room".)
  That is what you said; I have not added anything to it.
  Any reason you gave is in those words — I have not inferred one for you.
  I can recall what was **asked**, not what was answered: this session record keeps no
  measured values on purpose, so nothing above is a reading.
Counted mechanically on the answer: '5.01' appears 4 times, 'Room0.01' ZERO. It quotes the user's sentence verbatim, states how many turns did NOT mention the subject, disclaims inference, and states the figures-excluded constraint rather than leaving it implicit.
ANSWERED IN 1.0 s against 40-86 s for the data turns in the same conversation, because the lane is deterministic and makes no LLM call — which is also why it cannot fabricate.
GUARDS HELD, asked in the same run: 'What is the CO2 in the room I mentioned earlier?' -> sensor_data; 'What happened to the ticket I raised about the draught last week?' -> metadata; 'Can I ask about the humidity on floor 3?' -> observability. None moved to session_recall, matching the offline measurement that the rule moves exactly ONE question in 4,287 and that one is itself a recall question.
ROUTING CONTRACT: 60 -> 61 parse rules, appended LAST because it corrects whatever the classifier guessed rather than one particular wrong guess, with test_precedence_order_is_pinned updated in the SAME change. 221 pass across the contract, autowire and wiring tests; 54 across the session-recall set.
Refs: BUG-941; BUG-943; BUG-940; W5-04; CAVEAT-911; lessons #148

Title: CAVEAT-910 re-measured: narrowed by BUG-921, still live, and its wording is wrong
Description: CAVEAT-910 says an unbounded LLM summary 'is generated on EVERY /v1 turn'. Measured 2026-09-30 against the running stack, two ways. (1) Six hours of orchestrator log: 107 classifier MISSES, 1 HIT, and 13 '[dialogue_agent] Updating conversation summary' -- so it fires on 12% of turns, not all of them. (2) One 8-turn probe conversation: exactly 5 summarize calls, on turns 4-8. Both halves of the row need correcting rather than one. BUG-921's move of the cache lookup above the block is real and removes it on a HIT. What remains is the condition itself: state.summary is never loaded on /v1, so 'not state.summary' is always true, and the guard len(state.messages) > 5 is the only thing left -- which is false for a single-turn ask and true for every turn of a conversation from the fourth onward. The measured 12% is therefore an artefact of this stack mostly being asked single-turn questions by probes; in the MEMORY case, which is the case the row matters for, it is 100%.
Root_Cause: Unchanged from CAVEAT-910: a second, older rolling summary predating W5-01, on a different storage path (ConversationState.summary in Redis, populated only by the routes that restore state from Redis). What this row adds is that the two summaries now overlap: a figure-free bounded block (session_summary) and an unbounded one carrying figures (state.summary) are both in the classification prompt of a long conversation. Removing the older one is now a HONESTY change as well as a latency one, and the measurement to take first is whether any routing decision moves without it.
Verification: Measured from the live container log and from an 8-turn /v1 probe, 2026-09-30. Read from source: the cache lookup at dialogue_agent.py ~1353 precedes the summarize_history block at ~1370, confirming BUG-921's move.

Title: W5-03's core acceptance is ALREADY BUILT, and the row names the wrong store
Description: W5-03 reads 'A new chat starts blank... A user_memory Qdrant collection exists and is not used for this'. Checked before building anything (lessons #133, #136), and the seventh time a Wave row has asked for something that exists. orchestrator/services/user_preference_store.py (T35) is a REDIS store keyed 'user:pref:{user_id}:{category}' with a 365-day TTL -- per USER, with no conversation in the key, so it survives a new session by construction. It is wired at three call sites in _orchestrator.py: the analytics node overlays the user's personal comfort range onto the recipe thresholds, and the preference_management node carries _LIST_RE and _FORGET_RE subcommands over list_preferences / delete_preference / delete_all_preferences. user_id reaches the bus on all four chat routes (main.py 2625, 2876, 3447, 3942). So 'a returning user's stated preference is honoured in a new session, and can be listed and deleted' -- the row's acceptance, verbatim -- is met today. The Qdrant user_memory collection the row points at belongs to agent_memory.py and is a different feature.
Root_Cause: The row was written from a search for 'cross-session memory' and found the collection whose name says memory rather than the store that does it.
Fix_Approach: Two things are genuinely missing and neither is what the row asked for. (1) RECURRING SUBJECTS across sessions: turn_memory already carries a user_id column and a delete_user_turns erasure path, so a per-user subject history is derivable from rows that already exist -- nothing derives it. (2) The row's own privacy note, 'the user must be able to see and erase it', is met for preferences through the conversational lane and has NO API endpoint; erasure of turn_memory exists as a service method with no caller. NOT BUILT HERE: a new per-user memory surface is a new personal-data surface, and it wants the owner's decision on retention and visibility before code. Re-scope the row to those two items or close it.
Verification: Read from source 2026-09-30: user_preference_store.py (key format, TTL, the five methods), _orchestrator.py call sites ~4406, ~10393, ~10502, main.py user_id assignments on all four routes. Not re-asked live.

Title: W4-01 is BUILT end to end; only its own acceptance question does not trigger it
Description: W4-01 asks for 'a provenance intent over the previous turn' and says the system 'cannot say' where an answer came from. It can, and has since V7-T74. orchestrator/services/answer_provenance.py has is_provenance_question + render; routing_contract.py carries rule 'answer_provenance' as the FIRST parse-stage rule; capability_agent.py ~929 loads the PREVIOUS turn's state from Redis, reads intermediate_results['evidence_record'] and renders it, with an honest fallback when there is no prior record that refuses to reconstruct an explanation after the fact. What does NOT work is the row's own acceptance sentence: PROVENANCE_RE matches 'what is/are your sources' but not 'WHICH DATA SOURCES DID YOU USE', so the exact question W4-01 is graded on falls through to a data lane.
Root_Cause: The regex was written deliberately narrow -- its own comment says 'where did that come from' is provenance and 'where is the nearest toilet' is wayfinding -- and the which-form of the same question was never added.
Fix_Approach: ONE alternative in PROVENANCE_RE: r'|\bwhich (?:data )?sources? (?:did|do) you use\b'. NOT LANDED HERE: is_provenance_question is read by a routing rule, so widening it is a routing change, and the standing rule is the probe green before and after, one rule at a time, which this agent cannot run (it does not own restarts). Measure the widened pattern over the 4,287-question corpus before landing it, the way session_recall's detector was measured.
Verification: Read from source 2026-09-30: answer_provenance.py PROVENANCE_RE tested against the acceptance sentence (no match), routing_contract.py rule registration, capability_agent.py ~929-975. Not re-asked live.

Title: Four memory guard tests asserted a SQL parameter their own fake then ignored
Description: Found while moving the session-summary skip from SQL OFFSET to a Python slice (BUG-941 needs every turn AND the older ones, from one query). Four tests in tests/test_a_remembered_turn_carries_no_figure.py and one in tests/test_conversation_memory_e2e.py went red. Reading them showed the red was the honest signal and the GREEN had been the misleading one: _service_over returns a fixed row list whatever SQL it is handed, so get_session_summary(skip_recent=20) over ONE row returned that row in the test and would have returned nothing at all from a real Postgres. The tests pinned OFFSET as an argument and then never exercised what it does. test_rows_arrive_newest_first_and_are_rendered_oldest_first supplied exactly 3 rows against a default skip of 3 -- a real database would have returned zero rows and an empty block, and the assertion about ordering could never have failed for the right reason.
Root_Cause: A fake that is more permissive than the thing it stands for. The same shape as 'the measurement apparatus was wrong more often than the system' (lessons #20-22): four of five P1s in one earlier session were in graders.
Fix_Approach: The four tests now assert the OUTCOME of the skip instead of the argument that used to implement it: six turns in, the three newest absent from the block and the three oldest present. One new test pins the two-reader contract directly -- the recall lane receives every turn while the prompt block receives all but the newest few, from a single fetch with two parameters. The e2e test keeps exactly what it was about (subject kept, figure not) with skip_recent=0, so its one-row fixture is now a fixture a real store could produce.
Verification: 69 pass across the three memory test files after the change (was 63 pass / 5 fail during it). The new two-reader test fails if either slice is dropped.

Title: DIAGNOSIS of BUG-954: the aggregate lane declines every occupancy 'at the moment' question, so the count is the narrator's
Description: Proved offline AND live on 2026-09-30. Offline: `aggregate_lane.parse_intent` returns None for 'Which rooms are occupied at the moment?', 'Which rooms are empty at the moment?', 'How many rooms are occupied right now?' and 'Which rooms are unoccupied?' -- none holds a statistic word, and 'occupied'/'empty' are in neither _MAX nor _MIN. `summary_ok` is also False because `question_measurands` returns the EMPTY SET for all four (the lay-term table maps busy/crowded to occupancy and deliberately omits 'occupied'). So `wants_lane` returns None and the lane never claims the question. Live, all four turns logged verbatim: `[aggregate] not claimed: measurand=occupancy place=False per_sensor=False readings=True budget_hit=False`. The turn then fetched the readings and left the count to the narration. THE TWO DENOMINATORS IN BUG-954 ARE BOTH REAL AND BOTH CORRECTLY FETCHED: 234 is the number of distinct spaces carrying an occupancy series, 467 is the number of occupancy series the graph places in a space (measured: 512 series known to the graph, 467 placed, 45 not). The 'occupied' turn bound the 234 occupancy-STATUS series (values 0-1, mean 0.44) and the 'empty' turn bound all 467 (values 0-16), so the two phrasings answer over different populations. What nothing computed was the COUNT: the answers named five rooms under a headline of five while quoting '131 of 234 sensors' and '137 of 467 sensors' in the same paragraph.
Root_Cause: A count with no statistic word reaches no branch of a lane whose every branch is a statistic. `parse_intent` is documented as needing a statistic word, and that is right for a maximum or a mean; a count of PLACES matching a filter is a different shape and had no home. The narrator then answered with the rows it could name, which is BUG-936/BUG-937 one level up.
Fix_Approach: A `presence` branch in `aggregate_lane.try_answer`, entered only where `wants_lane` has already returned None, so nothing that was being answered changes. `aggregate_support.presence_question` decides the shape; `_answer_presence` reads each series' newest value, groups by the SPACE the graph places it in, and `render_presence` writes the count in code. The names printed are members of the list the headline counts, so the two cannot disagree.
Verification: pytest tests/test_the_presence_count_is_counted_not_narrated.py -q -> 27 passed. Driven end to end offline over the REAL 512 graph series and the REAL latest value per uuid (stub adapter, no stack): the lane answers '123 of the 234 spaces with an occupancy-presence sensor have someone in them right now; 111 do not', and an INDEPENDENT re-derivation over the same snapshot with no lane code gives spaces=234 occupied=123 empty=111 floor=6 unplaced=39 -- identical. NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE: needs an orchestrator restart, which this agent does not own. | VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-30 08:15-08:16, fresh chat per question, resp_cache AND cache:sparql flushed first, on the orchestrator the coordinator had just restarted (so the container held the fix). Log for both turns: `[aggregate] presence claim: wants=occupied` and `wants=empty`, where every earlier ask logged `[aggregate] not claimed`. The answers: 'Which rooms are occupied at the moment?' -> '**111 of the 234 spaces with an occupancy-presence sensor have someone in them right now**; 123 do not, read between Wed 30 Sep 08:15 and Wed 30 Sep 08:15' then eight named rooms 'and 103 more' (8 + 103 = 111, so the names account for the headline). 'Which rooms are empty at the moment?' -> '**123 of the 234 spaces ... have nobody in them right now**; 111 have someone', eight names 'and 115 more' (8 + 115 = 123). 40.6 s and 38.5 s, no timeout. THE TWO PHRASINGS NOW AGREE EXACTLY (111/123 both ways) although they still bind different series sets -- the log shows 234 series for 'occupied' and 467 for 'empty' -- which is CAVEAT-1043 mitigated by grouping on the space rather than on the series. The 'empty' turn, which bound both families, also printed the disagreement: '123 of these spaces carry a second occupancy series that disagrees at the same moment: a people counter reporting 14 to 19 people where the presence sensor reports nobody' (BUG-1042). | TWO LATER REFINEMENTS ARE NOT YET LIVE and need a restart this agent does not own: (a) the lead sentence now says 'spaces with an occupancy sensor' with a separate sentence counting which instrument decided each -- the live text above still says 'with an occupancy-presence sensor', which would be false in a building where some spaces carry only a counter; (b) a question naming a PAST period ('which rooms were occupied yesterday?') is now declined rather than answered from the newest reading. Both are covered by tests and both are proved offline against the real store; neither has run on a live turn.
Refs: BUG-954; BUG-809; BUG-825; BUG-936; BUG-937; orchestrator/services/aggregate_lane.py

Title: DIAGNOSIS of BUG-898: the analytics template reads a shared file nobody wrote, so a planner turn computed over an oxygen sensor's readings from 2025-12-17
Description: Re-asked live 2026-09-30, fresh chat, resp_cache flushed: 'How does observed occupancy compare with the design occupancy of room 1.25?' returned, in its Comparison section, 'the mean occupancy was 5 178.52 persons, the median 5 194.09 ... the most recent measurement, taken on 2025-12-17 00:24:26, recorded 4 401.86 persons'. EVERY FIGURE IS IDENTICAL TO THE 2026-09-29 REPORT, to two decimal places, a day apart, on a series written to every minute -- which is what separates a static file from a fabrication. The orchestrator log shows both halves: the SQL fetched 360 rows of 711b5b72-... (room 1.25's counter, values 11-15) and the executed code printed `Sensor : ac496048-0646-4278-8d74-98e24795efd4` with 119 data points. That uuid is Oxygen_O2_Percentage_Gas_Sensor_5.05. Found on disk: /app/outputs/data/current_data.json in the code-executor, 16,595 bytes, last modified 2025-12-17 00:24:56, holding exactly those 119 rows. ALSO MEASURED: no store in sensordb holds ANY row on 2025-12-17 -- every narrow table starts 2026-06 or later and the wide table has a gap between 2025-03 and 2026-03 -- so the timestamp could not have come from a query.
Root_Cause: `analytics_agent._get_template_code` builds code reading '/app/outputs/data/<data_filename>'. `data_filename` defaults to ONE shared name, 'current_data.json'. Only `workflow/_orchestrator.py` ever WROTE a file, and it writes a per-conversation one; `planner_agent._run_analytics` calls `analyze` with no filename at all. So every templated planner turn read the shared name -- a file last written nine months ago. The real rows WERE handed to the code as `raw_data_json` (base64-prepended by `_execute_code`); the template simply never looked at them.
Fix_Approach: Three changes, any ONE of which prevents it. (1) The template's setup now reads `raw_data_json` -- the rows this turn fetched -- and falls back to the file only when it is undefined. (2) `analyze` replaces the shared default with a name unique to the call, so no caller can land on it and two concurrent turns cannot collide. (3) `analyze` WRITES its own rows to that name, so the LLM-generated (non-template) path, which is instructed to read the file, reads this turn's data too.
Verification: pytest tests/test_the_analytics_template_reads_this_turns_data.py -q -> 7 passed, including one that EXECUTES the generated template with `raw_data_json` bound and asserts the output holds neither 4401 nor 5178. NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE: needs a restart. The stale file itself is left in place deliberately -- deleting it would hide whether the fix works, since a fixed system must answer correctly WITH it there. | VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-30 08:18, fresh chat, resp_cache AND cache:sparql flushed first, on the restarted orchestrator (source is bind-mounted, so the container held the fix). Same question, verbatim. THE COMPARISON SECTION NOW READS: '**Observed occupancy ranges from 13 to 17 persons** in Room 1.25 -- Conference/Seminar Room occupancy [persons]. The latest reading is 17 persons, the mean is 14.78 persons, and the median is 15 persons ... standard deviation of 1.33 persons.' The Sensor Readings section of the SAME answer says latest 17.0, range 13.0 to 17.0, mean 14.8 over 360 values. The two sections agree; the 190x gap between them is gone, and 4,401.86 / 5,178.52 / 5,194.09 / 294.91 / 9,993.36 and the 2025-12-17 timestamp appear nowhere in the answer. THE STALE FILE WAS LEFT IN PLACE on purpose -- /app/outputs/data/current_data.json still holds the oxygen sensor's 119 rows -- so this is the fix working WITH the trap present, not the trap being removed. STILL WRONG IN THAT ANSWER, AND NOT THIS ROW'S: both numeric sections say 'no design occupancy data is available for comparison' while the answer's own first line, prepended by the design-occupancy composition, says the room's design occupancy is 20 people. That is BUG-898's third defect, owned by W3-04.

Title: A room's people counter and its occupancy-status flag contradict each other in 136 of 233 rooms, always in the same direction
Description: Measured 2026-09-30 against sensordb.occupancy_data with the session pinned to +00:00, taking the latest row per uuid and joining to the space through the graph. 233 rooms carry BOTH a people counter (Room<N>_sat_occupancy) and a presence flag (Room<N>_sat_occupancy_status). They agree about whether anyone is present in 97 and DISAGREE in 136. All 136 disagree the same way: the counter reports 13-16 people while the flag reports 0. Not one room has the flag set with the counter at zero. Whole-store shape: 514 series with a latest reading, 380 non-zero and 134 zero; the value histogram is bimodal -- 256 series read 0 or 1 (the flags) and 258 read 11-21 (the counters). So 'which rooms are occupied' has no single true answer from this store: the counters say 233 of 233, the flags say 103 of 234.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed here, and it is a DATA question rather than a lane question. The one-directional pattern (counter high, flag zero) and the 13-16 band point at the dev-mode generator writing the two series independently rather than at a sensor fault. CLAUDE.md records that everything outside bldg1's wide table is synthetic and live-generated, so this is most likely a generator defect.
Fix_Approach: Not attempted. Until it is settled, the presence answer (BUG-1040) STATES the disagreement with its own count and band rather than choosing silently, which is the only honest option while both series exist. If the generator is the cause, the fix is to derive the flag from the counter at write time so the two cannot diverge.
Verification: scratchpad family_disagree.py: 233 rooms with both, 97 agree, 136 disagree, 136 of them counter>0 & status==0, 0 the other way. Re-runnable; the counts move with the publisher but the direction has not.

Title: Two phrasings of one occupancy question bind different series populations (234 status flags vs 467 mixed), so their answers are not comparable
Description: Live 2026-09-30, same building, minutes apart. 'Which rooms are occupied at the moment?' bound 234 series whose values run 0.00-1.00 with a mean of 0.44 -- the occupancy-STATUS flags only. 'Which rooms are empty at the moment?' bound 467 series whose values run 0-16 -- flags and people counters together. A reader asking the same question two ways gets two populations and no indication that they differ. This is separate from BUG-954's headline defect: both denominators were correctly fetched and correctly quoted.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed. The binding happens upstream of the aggregate lane, in the SPARQL that resolves the question's sensors; 'occupied' and 'empty' evidently resolve to different Brick classes. `aggregate_support.counts_people` exists precisely because the two families share one table, but it is applied when SUMMARISING, not when BINDING.
Fix_Approach: Partly mitigated by BUG-1040: the presence branch now groups by SPACE and prefers the presence flag per space, so both phrasings produce the same denominator (234 spaces) whichever series were bound. The binding itself is untouched and a question about occupancy that reaches another lane can still see either population.
Verification: Both phrasings asked live twice each, fresh chat, resp_cache flushed; the '234 series / mean 0.491' and '467 sensors / range 0-16' figures are quoted from the answers verbatim. Offline after the fix, both phrasings report the same 234-space denominator. | LIVE 2026-09-30: the binding difference PERSISTS (234 series bound for 'occupied', 467 for 'empty', both logged) and the answers no longer differ because of it -- both report 111 of 234 spaces. The mitigation is real; the binding defect is not fixed.

Title: Two of four occupancy 'at the moment' asks returned the 150 s timeout rather than an answer
Description: Live 2026-09-30, four asks (two phrasings, twice each), fresh chat and resp_cache flushed per ask. Asks 1 and 2 returned 'Your request took too long to process' at exactly 150.0 s; asks 3 and 4 answered in 49.0 s and 112.5 s. The orchestrator was serving another agent's turns concurrently throughout, so this is not attributed. Title: 2,833 per-conversation analytics data files have accumulated in the code-executor, one of them the stale file behind BUG-898
Description: `ls /app/outputs/data/ | wc -l` in the code-executor returns 2,833 files, the oldest dated 2025-12-17 and several over 2 MB. They are written by `workflow/_orchestrator.py` as <user>_<conversation>_data.json and never removed. One of them -- current_data.json, the shared default name -- was being read by every templated planner turn (BUG-898). The fix for that makes each turn write its OWN file, which adds to this pile rather than reducing it.
Root_Cause: Nothing owns the lifetime of these files. They are scratch input to a sandboxed process and outlive the turn that made them by design of omission, not of intent.
Fix_Approach: Not attempted, and deliberately not bundled with BUG-898's fix: deleting the files would have hidden whether that fix works. The durable answer is to stop using a file at all -- the rows are already handed to the code in-process as `raw_data_json`, and the template now prefers them -- and then to delete the write and the directory together. Until then a scheduled clean-up of files older than a day would bound the growth.
Verification: docker compose exec code-executor ls /app/outputs/data | wc -l -> 2833 (2026-09-30). stat current_data.json -> 2025-12-17 00:24:56. | THE BUG-1041 FIX MAKES THIS WORSE BEFORE IT MAKES IT BETTER, and that is stated here rather than discovered later: `analyze` now writes one file per ANALYTICS CALL (uuid4 name) where the main workflow wrote one per CONVERSATION, so the directory grows faster. It was the only way to make the LLM-generated path -- which is instructed in its prompt to read the file -- read this turn's rows. The template path no longer needs a file at all, so the write is redundant for it. The tidy fix, NOT attempted because it landed late on a green tree: move the write to after code generation and skip it when the generated code references `raw_data_json`, which would leave only the LLM-generated path writing anything. Measure the directory before assuming this is urgent -- these are small JSON files and 2,833 of them had accumulated over nine months without anyone noticing.

Title: The presence lane's own log line calls a series count a space count, and contradicts the answer it is logging
Description: `aggregate_lane.try_answer` logs `[aggregate] presence claim: wants=%s spaces=%s` and passes `aggregate.sensors`, which is `len(latest)` -- the number of SERIES read, not the number of spaces counted. Measured live 2026-09-30: the 'empty' turn logged `spaces=467` while the answer it produced said '123 of the 234 spaces'. The 'occupied' turn logged `spaces=234` and its answer also said 234, which is a coincidence of that turn's binding and makes the label harder to catch, not easier. A reader diagnosing the next occupancy defect from the log would take 467 for the denominator.
Root_Cause: The log was written from the `_result` field name rather than from what the field holds. Exactly the mislabelled-denominator class the lane was just changed to fix (lesson #139), one level down, in the instrument instead of the answer.
Fix_Approach: Log both and name each: `series=%s spaces=%s`, taking the space count from `len(occupied) + len(empty)`. Deliberately NOT applied in this session: the full unit suite had already been started over the current tree and editing a .py mid-run invalidates it (lesson #101), and changing code after a green measurement is how a regression lands unmeasured. It is a log string with no caller, so it can go in with the next change to this module.
Verification: docker compose logs orchestrator | grep 'presence claim' -> `wants=occupied spaces=234` and `wants=empty spaces=467`, against answers saying 234 spaces in both cases.

Title: A module reload detaches `settings`, so 25 test patches reach an object the product no longer reads
Description:
Found 2026-09-30 by three tests that passed alone, passed in a 42-test pair, and FAILED in the full 13,000-test suite -- writing to the real output directory instead of the tmp_path they had patched.
MECHANISM, demonstrated directly rather than inferred:
    aa.settings is cfg.settings   before importlib.reload(cfg):  True
    aa.settings is cfg.settings   AFTER  importlib.reload(cfg):  False
`tests/test_strict_secrets.py` calls `importlib.reload(cfg)` four times -- correctly, it is testing boot-time validation. The reload builds a NEW Settings object in `shared.config`, while every module that did `from shared.config import settings` at import time still holds the OLD one. A test that then does `from shared.config import settings` and patches THAT object patches something the product code no longer reads.
EXPOSURE: **25 patch sites across 8 test files** use `monkeypatch.setattr(settings, ...)`: test_analytics_repairs_inside_a_time_budget, test_compile_cache, test_flat_layout_loaders, test_locked_capability, test_observed_at, test_protect_enforcement, test_similarity_rebuild, test_undeclared_type_audit.
THE THREE THAT FAILED WERE THE VISIBLE TIP, AND THE LUCKY ONES. A patch that does not take effect usually leaves the test running against the REAL setting, which often still satisfies the assertion -- a vacuous PASS. Those are the ones to worry about: the same session already found five memory tests pinning a parameter their own fake then ignored (CAVEAT-1025), and this repo's own lesson is that the measurement apparatus is wrong more often than the system (lessons #20-22).
Root_Cause: `from X import y` binds the OBJECT, not the name. A later `importlib.reload(X)` rebinds `X.y` and leaves every prior importer pointing at the previous object. Ordinary Python; invisible in a single-file test run, which is why it survived.
Fix_Approach:
PATCH WHERE IT IS USED. `monkeypatch.setattr(target_module.settings, 'FIELD', value)` patches whatever object that module currently holds, and is correct whether or not a reload has happened. Done for the three failing tests.
THE OTHER 25 SITES ARE NOT AUDITED. Each needs asking: does the assertion still hold when the patch silently does nothing? If yes, the test is vacuous and proves nothing; if no, it is order-dependent and will fail the day the suite reorders. A test that derives the answer -- assert the OUTCOME through the module under test -- beats one that pins a parameter.
A cheaper systemic option worth considering: have `test_strict_secrets` restore the original object into `shared.config` after its reloads, so the detachment does not outlive the test that needs it.
Verification: The three failures reproduce as `test_strict_secrets.py` + the analytics file and pass 15/15 with the patch retargeted. Demonstrated the detachment directly with an identity check either side of the reload. The full-suite number after the fix is the confirmation that matters and is being re-run.
Refs: CAVEAT-1025 (the same shape in the memory tests); lessons #20-22; BUG-898

Title: DIAGNOSIS of BUG-1042: the presence flag is a random telegraph with no clock, and the counter has a floor
Description: The counter/flag contradiction is two generators, not one sensor fault. In mysql-dummy-publish-dev/sensor_signal.py, next_value branches on `dec == 0 and span <= 1.0`. The 234 Room<N>_sat_occupancy_status series are declared lo=0 hi=1 dec=0 in input/bldg1_narrow_publish_map.json, so span is exactly 1.0 and EVERY ONE takes the binary branch: seeded 1 with p=0.25, then flipped with p=_FLIP_P=0.08 per write, holding state otherwise. That branch never calls centre(), so it never reads `when` -- DIURNAL['occupancy']=0.9 is set and the flag never sees it. The 233 Room<N>_sat_occupancy counters are lo=0 hi=30, take the mean-reversion branch, and DO follow the day. MEASURED LIVE (2 h to 2026-09-30 09:13 UTC, session pinned +00:00): flag flip rate 428/5760 = 0.0743 against the generator's 0.08; counter min 13.0 max 25.0 avg 18.9 over 22,368 rows with ZERO reading 0. Hourly means over the last 10 days: counter 3.9 at 02:00 rising to 29.3 at 13:00 (range 25.4); flag 0.41..0.59 with no monotone shape (range 0.18, and its 09:00-11:00 bump is the publisher's uptime pattern, not a cycle). THE DIRECTION IS EXPLAINED BY THE COUNTER'S FLOOR: base = lo + (hi-lo)*(0.5*(1-swing) + swing*cycle) with swing=0.9 bottoms out at 30*0.05 = 1.5, plus a per-uuid phase term of +/-1.2, so the trough centre spans 0.300..2.700 and only 18 of 233 counters (7.7%) can round to 0 at all. A counter that is almost never 0 plus a flag that is a coin at every hour gives disagreement in one direction almost always.
Root_Cause: Two series describing one phenomenon are generated by two models that share no state and do not share a clock. The binary branch is a door-contact model -- correct for the 22 genuinely boolean points that also sit in this band (PIR, intrusion, booking status, lift state, EV charger state) and wrong for a presence flag, which is a VIEW of the count. Its own docstring says 'roughly one change an hour at a 300s cadence'; occupancy's cadence is 60 s (measured ~75 s live), so every room's presence flips about once every 16 minutes, all night.
Fix_Approach: FIXED IN THE GENERATOR (2026-09-30). mysql-dummy-publish-dev/sensor_signal.py: the binary branch now reads the SAME diurnal centre the continuous branch mean-reverts toward. Two new functions carry it. on_probability() turns centre() into a probability of being on -- so `when` is finally read on this branch -- and the branch runs a two-state Markov chain whose STATIONARY DISTRIBUTION is that probability, rather than a fixed-rate coin. a + b is pinned at 2*rate, which makes the flip rate at p=0.5 exactly what it was before, so a door contact (DIURNAL 0.0, centre a flat 0.5) is unchanged by construction rather than by inspection. The seed is now drawn from the current hour instead of a fixed p=0.25, so a restart at 03:00 no longer starts a quarter of the building occupied. SECOND HALF, separable and separately revertible: flip_rate_for() scales _FLIP_P by the point's own cadence against a new _FLIP_REFERENCE_CADENCE_S = 300. _FLIP_P is a probability per WRITE and its comment quotes a rate per HOUR; those are the same thing only at 300 s, which is why the 60 s occupancy flags changed five times as often as the file claimed. `contact` sits at 300 s so the factor is exactly 1.0 there. next_value() and flip_rate_for() also take an optional step_s for a caller writing at its own interval -- the gap backfill, see BUG-1139. NOT DONE, AND DELIBERATELY: the recommendation in this row's original text was to derive the flag from the counter at write time. That was not taken. It would couple two narrow tables inside the publisher and make the flag stop being an instrument; reading one clock achieves the same agreement (r=0.975, measured) without the coupling, and leaves the flag able to disagree with the counter for a REASON, which is what a separate sensor is for. NOT DEPLOYED. sensor_signal.py is COPY'd into the data-publisher image, not bind-mounted (md5 in the running container differs from the source as of 2026-09-30 12:20 UTC). It needs `docker compose build data-publisher && docker compose up -d data-publisher`, which is the owner's call. Until then the source is fixed and the deployed thing is not -- the BUG-343 pattern. HISTORY IS NOT REPAIRED and needs the owner: see BUG-1150 for the costed re-seed.
Verification:
OFFLINE SIMULATION, no database, no model, no container. scratchpad/sim_1130.py drives the edited generator for 5 simulated days over 30 sensors at the live 60 s cadence: hourly mean of the presence flag 0.066 at 00:00 rising to 0.946 at 13:00 (was 0.41..0.59 with no shape), and Pearson r between the flag's hourly mean and the COUNTER's hourly mean = 0.9956. Flip rate fell from 0.0802 to 0.0100 per write. Door contact unchanged: flip rate 0.0824 against the declared 0.08, hourly range 0.446..0.568 with no monotone shape. THE TESTS ARE NOT VACUOUS, which was checked rather than assumed. scratchpad/check_tests_are_not_vacuous.py monkeypatches the PRE-FIX branch back in and re-runs the same three measurements: day-vs-night 0.487/0.467 (test needs a 0.3 gap) FAIL, r against the declared shape 0.169 (needs 0.85) FAIL, r against the counter -0.096 (needs 0.9) FAIL. All three pass on the fixed code. The restored branch also reproduces this row's live measurement: 0.0802 flips per write against the 0.0743 measured in the store. tests/test_binary_points_read_the_clock.py, 16 tests, all passing -- and it also pins the source layout the anomaly scanner PARSES out of this file (it reads CADENCE_S with a regex over a 900-character window, so an integer-valued constant added nearby would be read as a cadence). Verified: still [60,60,60,120,120,300 x6,600,900,300], min 60, unchanged. NOT VERIFIED LIVE and cannot be without a rebuild + restart, which this agent does not own.
DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED IN THE IMAGE 2026-09-30. `sensor_signal.py` is COPY'd into the data-publisher image, NOT bind-mounted, so editing the source changed nothing that was running -- the BUG-343 pattern, and the agent that wrote the fix correctly refused to claim otherwise. Measured before: source md5 `8ae1509d...` vs container `07007cbe...`. Ran `docker compose build data-publisher && docker compose up -d data-publisher` (RECREATE, not restart). Measured after: source and container both `8ae1509d7cfee9a9a2d2527c6d011b3d`, and the publisher is inserting rows.
STILL OWED, and it is a wait rather than a task: the offline evidence is a flag hourly mean of 0.066 at 00:00 rising to 0.946 at 13:00 and Pearson r = 0.9956 against the counter (was -0.096). Confirming that LIVE needs a day of newly published rows. Re-measure hour-of-day means on a status uuid after 2026-10-01 and compare with the same uuid's 2026-09-29 rows; do not quote the offline figures as live ones.
Refs: BUG-1042; BUG-1040; BUG-954; BUG-1139; BUG-1150; mysql-dummy-publish-dev/sensor_signal.py; tests/test_binary_points_read_the_clock.py; input/bldg1_narrow_publish_map.json

Title: 1.54 million stored rows (3.65%) fall outside their declared band; the retroactive-band explanation covers ONE THIRD of them, not all
Description: Found while diagnosing BUG-1042 and much larger than it. New scripts/audit_declared_band_conformance.py compares every stored reading against the lo/hi its point declares in the publish maps (which carry the ontology's own typicalMin/typicalMax). Across 2,511 banded points and 15 narrow tables: 42,195,362 rows, 1,544,386 outside their declared band (3.660%). Worst tables: equipment_data 40.25%, iaq_data 34.39%, water_data 27.18%, parking_data 14.49%, submeter_data 12.23%, co2_data 6.01%, occupancy_data 5.83%. contact_data (6.9 M rows) and temperature_data (988 k) are completely clean. The occupancy counters alone hold 283,792 rows above their declared maximum of 30, reaching 194 people in a single academic office, all in August 2026. THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: the most recent out-of-band row in the entire store is 2026-09-16 20:42:25, and ZERO families violate on or after 2026-09-20. The current generator is clean.
Root_Cause:
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-30 12:10 UTC AND THE ORIGINAL EXPLANATION IS REFUTED FOR MOST OF THE ROWS. It is kept above rather than deleted, because what was believed is part of the record.
THE TEST. The dev publisher CLAMPS: sensor_signal.next_value ends with `value = max(lo, min(hi, value))`, so whatever band it is handed it cannot write outside it. Before the per-point bands existed it was handed the per-COLUMN default in `_NARROW_RANGES`. So every violation is either (RETRO) outside the new band but INSIDE the old column default, which is exactly 'a band authored later', or (OTHER) outside the old default too, which this publisher could not have written under EITHER regime.
MEASURED: 491,166 of 1,544,386 are RETRO (31.8%). The other 1,053,220 (68.2%) are not. The three biggest are not explained at all:
  equipment_data lighting_cct  474,318 violations, only 2,574 RETRO
  occupancy_data occupancy     283,792 violations, 0 RETRO - and its band [0,30] is IDENTICAL to the old column default (0,30), while the rows reach 194. A band that never changed cannot be a retroactive band.
  co2_data co2                 122,338 violations, 0 RETRO - band [400,1200] is also IDENTICAL to the old column default, while the rows reach 2510.4.
What IS genuinely retroactive is the binary family: ~250,000 rows on points now banded [0,1] that previously took the occupancy column's (0,30). That is a real narrowing with no migration and is the part that should be closed as by-design.
THE COMMIT ATTRIBUTION WAS ALSO WRONG. `git show a45bf47:bldg1/bldg1_narrow_publish_map.json` parses to 1,738 entries with 0 bands - IDENTICAL to its parent, so a45bf47 did not add the bands. The banded map (2,756 entries / 2,511 banded) and `orchestrator/services/publisher_map.py` (which is what actually attaches the bands, at boot, from the ontology) both first appear in a538bf6, 2026-09-18 10:03. The data cutover is 2026-09-16 20:42, which is BEFORE that commit, so the band cannot be what stopped the violations either.
=== THE COMMIT ATTRIBUTION IN THIS ROW IS WRONG, verified independently 2026-09-30 ===
The row (and my summary of it) said commit `a45bf47` added per-point lo/hi where the parent had none, making the bands retroactive. Counted straight out of git, from the PARKED path `bldg1/bldg1_narrow_publish_map.json` (the active building is renamed to `input/`, so the `input/` path returns nothing at any commit and looks like an absent file):
    a45bf47^   banded:    0 of 1,738
    a45bf47    banded:    0 of 1,738
    a538bf6    banded: 2,511 of 2,756
    HEAD       banded: 2,511 of 2,756
The banded map first exists at **a538bf6 (2026-09-18)** -- AFTER the 2026-09-16 20:42 data cutover this row is built around. A band that did not exist until two days later cannot be the retroactive constraint that explains rows written before it.
AND THE EXPLANATION COVERS ONLY A THIRD OF THE ROWS ANYWAY: of 1,544,386 violations, 491,166 (31.8%) are outside the new band but inside the old column default -- genuinely retroactive -- while 1,053,220 (68.2%) are outside BOTH, which the clamping publisher could not have written under either regime. The three largest families are not explained at all: `occupancy` (283,792 rows, band [0,30] IDENTICAL to the old default, rows reaching 194) and `co2` (122,338, band [400,1200] also identical, rows reaching 2510.4). **A band that never changed cannot be a retroactive band.**
So this row must NOT be closed as by-design. The genuinely by-design part is the ~250k binary-point rows narrowed from (0,30) to [0,1]; the rest is unexplained and stays open. Liveness is unchanged and is the reassuring half: 0 violations in the last 1 h and 24 h, every family, every table.
Fix_Approach:
DO NOT CLOSE AS BY-DESIGN. That was the recommendation and the measurement does not support it for two thirds of the rows: the largest families violate a band that never changed, so something other than a schema change wrote them. CAVEAT-1132 now has the writer for the second-largest (lighting_cct) and BUG-1171 has the line.
STILL CORRECT, AND NOW SHIPPED: the recommendation to give a band a VALID-FROM date. `orchestrator/services/publisher_map.py::_stamp_band_provenance` stamps `band_from` on every point whose band it writes or CHANGES, carries it forward untouched while the band is unchanged (so an unchanged map is not rewritten every boot), and records the WORDS 'unknown: this band predates the valid-from stamp' for a band that was already there - writing today's date onto those would assert something nobody measured. `scripts/audit_declared_band_conformance.py` now reads it and reports, per family, how many violations were written UNDER the band as opposed to before it, plus a header saying how many bands are undated. A marker nothing reads is not a disclosure (lesson #157), so the two changes are one change.
STILL RECOMMENDED AND NOT DONE: do not rewrite the 1.5 M readings. That part of the original recommendation stands unaltered.
Verification:
RE-RUN 2026-09-30, session time_zone printed '+00:00' before any query: 42,298,887 rows, 1,544,386 outside (3.651%). The violation count is IDENTICAL to the original run and the row total grew by 103,525 in seven hours of live publishing, so the original figures re-confirm.
THE RETRO/OTHER SPLIT: scratchpad/probe_band_era.py, in-container, UTC-pinned, comparing each family against BOTH the per-point band and the publisher's own `_NARROW_RANGES` copied verbatim from mysql_dummy_publisher.py. 491,166 RETRO / 1,053,220 not.
LIVENESS RE-CONFIRMED AND TIGHTENED: measured against the BAND (not against anything else), ZERO families violated in the last 1 hour or the last 24 hours, across every banded family in every table. The current generator is clean. Latest violating row anywhere: 2026-09-16 18:18:23.
GIT: `git show a45bf47:...` and `git show a45bf47^:...` both parse to 1,738 entries / 0 banded; `git log -S_attach_bands` names a538bf6 (2026-09-18) alone.
Refs: BUG-1042; CAVEAT-847; CAVEAT-405; a538bf6; BUG-1171; CAVEAT-1172; CAVEAT-1173; CAVEAT-1174; scripts/audit_declared_band_conformance.py; orchestrator/services/publisher_map.py

Title: SIX reading families, not three, are physically impossible - and the gases and lighting_cct are one defect with one line behind it (BUG-1171)
Description: The band audit surfaced three shapes that a band alone does not describe, and each would be quoted verbatim by a lane that trusts the store. (1) SENTINEL AS A READING: humidity_data holds 12 rows reading 99999.0 percent (family `humidity`, band [30,70]) and RH_Sensor_F4 one more; last 2026-09-03. 99999 is a no-data marker, and stored as a value it survives every range check that tests a MINIMUM and poisons any mean. (2) 0 KELVIN LIGHT: equipment_data `lighting_cct` declares [2700,6500] and holds 474,318 of 1,046,448 rows (45.33%) outside it, range 0.0..5408.0 -- so the maximum is BELOW the declared top and nearly half the readings sit under the floor, including 0. A correlated colour temperature of 0 K is not a dim light, it is an absent measurement. CCT_Sensor_F5_Lab is worse at 50.76%. (3) FOUR GASES, ONE SHAPE: nitrogen_dioxide, pm10, pm1 and formaldehyde each report EXACTLY 30,240 of 60,534 rows (49.96%) outside their band, every one of them below the floor, each series maxing out under its declared ceiling. Four independent gases agreeing to the row is not four sensor faults; it is one writer alternating a real value with a zero. Also equipment_data door sensors declare [0,100] and reach 757.
Root_Cause:
DIAGNOSED TO THE LINE 2026-09-30, which the row could not do when it was filed. The original guess - 'one writer alternating a real value with a zero' - is WRONG, and the true shape is simpler and worse.
THE ZEROS ARE A COMPLETE, GAPLESS BACKFILL. Measured: of nitrogen_dioxide's 30,240 zeros, 30,240 (100.00%) sit exactly on a ten-minute boundary, the window is 2026-08-12 00:00:00 .. 2026-09-15 23:50:00, and there are ZERO non-zero rows anywhere inside that window. Same for carbon_monoxide. For lighting_cct: 471,744 zeros, 100.00% on the ten-minute grid, window 2026-09-02 00:00:00 .. 2026-09-15 23:50:00, again zero non-zero rows inside it. The arithmetic closes exactly: 5,040 zeros per gas point = 5 weeks x 7 x 144 ten-minute slots; 2,016 per lighting_cct point = 2 weeks x 7 x 144.
WHO: `scripts/backfill_saturation.py --weeks 5` and `--weeks 2`, whose docstring says '10-minute history per room'. WHY ZERO: it calls `orchestrator/services/deliberation/synthetic_signals.py::modality_series`, which dispatches on the modality parsed out of `<space>_sat_<modality>` and models twelve of them. Everything else falls to `else:  # unknown modality: neutral zero signal, never invented physics` -> `out.append(0.0)`. BUG-1171 owns that line. The 'exactly half' pattern is an artefact: the backfill window happens to be about half of each point's history.
THE COUNT WAS WRONG BY A THIRD, AND THE INSTRUMENT IS WHY. It is SIX families, not four: nitrogen_dioxide, pm10, pm1, formaldehyde, carbon_monoxide and tvoc each hold EXACTLY 30,240 zeros over 6 points. Only four appear in the band audit because CO and TVOC have a band whose floor is 0, so their zeros are INSIDE the band and the audit cannot see them (CAVEAT-1173).
Fix_Approach:
STILL NOT ATTEMPTED, and now for a stated reason rather than for want of a diagnosis.
(a) THE SENTINEL - 13 rows of 99999.0 in humidity_data across 13 distinct uuids, 2026-08-26 .. 2026-09-03, and ZERO such rows in temperature_data, co2_data, iaq_data or light_data. Unchanged recommendation: absence is NULL or is not written; deleting 13 rows is a store write and is the owner's call.
(b) THE GASES AND lighting_cct - the writer IS now identified, so the block on changing anything is lifted, but the change is NOT made here for two reasons that are about this stack and not about the diagnosis. First, `synthetic_signals.py` is LOADED LIVE by the data-publisher from a read-only mount (`_GENERATOR_FILES` in mysql_dummy_publisher.py), so editing it changes what is being written right now, and store writes are the owner's. Second, `tests/test_synthetic_signals.py::test_unknown_modality_yields_zeros_not_invented_physics` PINS the zero fallback by name - it is a guard test asserting the current behaviour is intended, and overruling it is a design decision, not a bug fix (lesson #153). The change itself is one line: an unmodelled modality must write NOTHING, not 0.0, because 0.0 in a store is a reading. See BUG-1171.
(c) NOT STILL BEING WRITTEN, BUT NOT SAFE EITHER. Zero violations in the last 24 hours for every family. The zeros stop at 2026-09-15 23:50 because the backfill is a manual script, not a service - so the correct statement is not 'this is history' but 'this recurs the next time anyone runs the backfill'.
Verification:
All figures re-measured 2026-09-30 12:16-12:24 UTC, in-container, session pinned to '+00:00' and printed. scratchpad/probe_impossible_families.py, probe_gases.py, probe_zero_cadence.py.
(1) SENTINEL: humidity_data 13 rows >= 9999, 13 distinct uuids, 2026-08-26 13:06 .. 2026-09-03 12:45:43. CONFIRMS the original 12+1.
(2) lighting_cct: 234 points, 1,052,064 rows, 471,744 EXACTLY zero (44.84%), 2,574 strictly between 0 and 2,700, max 5,408 (below the declared 6,500), last zero 2026-09-15 23:50:00, zeros in the last 24 h = 0. All 234 of 234 points have written a zero. CONFIRMS 474,318 outside and refines it: the violation is essentially all zeros.
(3) SIX gases, each 6 points, each EXACTLY 30,240 zeros (49.5-49.7%), each first row 2026-08-12 00:00:00, each last zero 2026-09-15 23:50:00, each still writing real values now (last row 2026-09-30 12:22:17). Per point uniformly 5,040 of 10,147 - no point is dead and no point is clean.
(4) DOORS: 10 points in equipment_data banded [0,100], 3,329 rows above 100, max 757.798, last 2026-08-25 02:25:00. CONFIRMS.
(5) NEW, and not in the original row: 256 occupancy_data points banded [0,1] hold 361,272 rows above 1 and 369,309 non-binary values, max 194.0 - a Booking_Status of 189.484 and an IntrusionDetector of 194. CAVEAT-1172.

Title: input/bldg1_sensor_metrology.ttl is a stale snapshot - and regenerating it is NOT the safe no-op the fix note claims
Description: 799 of the graph's 3,512 points (22.8%) carry no ontosage:samplingIntervalS. The gap is not scattered, it is three whole families plus a tail: Occupancy_Status 234 (all of them -- every presence flag in BUG-1042), Lighting_Correlated_Color_Temperature_Sensor 234, PM2.5 210, and 550 under the bare brick:Sensor type. By contrast Occupancy_Count_Sensor is 257/257, Contact_Sensor 466/466 and Motion_Sensor 13/13 -- complete. input/bldg1_sensor_metrology.ttl holds 2,727 subjects and ZERO entries matching _sat_occupancy_status, _sat_lighting_cct or _sat_pm25.
Root_Cause: Not a query defect and not a modelling decision -- the file is a GENERATED SNAPSHOT that was never regenerated after later TTLs added points. Re-running its own generator against the live graph today produces 3,507 subjects, +780 on the file in place, including all 234 presence flags. The generator's SPARQL has always been general enough to find them; it simply ran before they existed.
Fix_Approach:
STILL NOT RUN, and the reason has changed from 'I do not own the restart' to 'the command is not safe as described'. The original note said 'ONE COMMAND ... NO INVENTION IS INVOLVED, which is why this is safe to run'. Measured against the file in place, regenerating would do three things, and only the first is the one the row asked for:
1. ADD 794 subjects (not 780), carrying 794 samplingIntervalS + 794 archivalIntervalS + 530 calibration regimes. By name family: occupancy_status 234, lighting_cct 234, pm* 222, then 6 each of water_flow_hot, carbon_monoxide, tvoc, formaldehyde, water_level, water_flow_chilled, gas, electric_power, nitrogen_dioxide, water_flow_rate, plus waste bins, damper positions and boiler water temperatures.
2. REMOVE 14 subjects, all VAV_Floor5_* (supply air flows and damper positions). The uploader PUTs the whole file into one named graph, so these would be DELETED from the graph. Checked: each of the 14 exists in the graph ONLY as metrology triples - no rdf:type, no timeseries reference - so they are orphans and removing them is arguably a cleanup. It is still a graph deletion the row does not mention.
3. MOVE 1,922 calibratedOn AND 1,922 calibrationDueOn dates, on subjects that already exist. This is the one that matters. `_calibration` computes `last = today - timedelta(days=age)`, so every date slides by the number of days since the file was last generated - here exactly 25 (the file in place has a maximum calibratedOn of 2026-09-05; the regenerated one, 2026-09-30). The file's OWN HEADER says 'deterministic, so regenerating produces an identical file and any diff means the graph changed'. That sentence is false: the dates are deterministic GIVEN today, and today moves.
THE NUMBER THIS CHANGES IN AN ANSWER: sensors reading as overdue for calibration goes 278 -> 248, a drop of 30, DESPITE 523 more sensors gaining a calibration regime. Nothing was calibrated; the clock moved. That is TODO-484's class of defect exactly ('markers that decay with the calendar, as the overdue-calibration count did: 194 -> 201 -> 206 while the system stayed correct').
RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE FOR THE OWNER, so the good half is not blocked on the bad: (a) decide whether the 14 VAV_Floor5_* orphans should go; (b) decide whether a calibration date may move because the file was regenerated - if not, the generator needs to preserve an existing calibratedOn rather than re-deriving it, which is a small change and is the durable fix; (c) only then run the command. Adding 794 intervals is worth having; buying it with 1,922 silently shifted calibration dates is not a trade anyone has agreed to.
Verification:
MEASURED 2026-09-30 by parsing both files with rdflib and diffing at TRIPLE level, not line level, because the uploader replaces the whole named graph. Regenerated to the SCRATCHPAD ONLY with `python scripts/generate_sensor_metrology.py --out <scratchpad>/bldg1_sensor_metrology_REGEN.ttl --today 2026-09-30`; input/ and the graph are both untouched and no container was restarted.
File in place: 11,241 triples over 2,727 subjects. Regenerated: 14,370 over 3,507. ADDED 794, REMOVED 14, common 2,713, of which 1,922 have a changed calibratedOn and calibrationDueOn (e.g. Air_Temperature_Sensor_2.05 2025-12-15 -> 2026-01-09; CO2_Level_Sensor_3.50 2026-01-10 -> 2026-02-04 - a uniform +25 days).
Overdue as of 2026-09-30: file in place 278 of 1,929 with a due date; regenerated 248 of 2,452. Script: scratchpad/diff_metrology.py and scratchpad/overdue_count.py.
The 14 removals confirmed orphaned by SPARQL: `SELECT ?p ?o WHERE { bldg:VAV_Floor5_East_Supply_Air_Flow ?p ?o }` returns five triples, all ontosage: metrology, and a COUNT of its timeseries ids is 0.

Title: CAVEAT-1045 corrected: the analytics output pile is 2.55 GB, not 'small JSON files', and the largest single file is 25.9 MB
