Title: A typo's digits are read as a room number, binding ONE sensor of 245 that the question never named
Description:
THIS IS THE REAL CAUSE OF BUG-947 INSTANCE (32), and it is not what that row says. Measured inside the orchestrator container, read-only, three identical runs:
    'why is pl 2.5 increasing'          -> intent=diagnosis  entities=['Room2.50_sat_pm25']
    'why is pm2.5 increasing'           -> intent=diagnosis  entities=['PM2.5']
    'why is PM2.5 increasing in room 5.01' -> intent=diagnosis entities=['Room_5.01']
The question names NO room. The classifier bound Room 2.50 because the typo's digits -- 'pl 2.5' -- appear inside the sensor name Room2.50_sat_pm25. The graph holds 245 PM2.5 sensors (BUG-947 says 210; re-counted here) and the turn was scoped to exactly one of them, chosen by a numeric coincidence. Then the diagnosis lane had nothing to say about one sensor and declined.
The referent-existence gate cannot catch it: Room2.50_sat_pm25 is real, 14 subjects carry that name. The referent EXISTS; it is simply not one the user named. That is the gap the gate was never built to close.
STABLE, not a sampling artefact: three runs, identical binding each time.
Root_Cause: Entity extraction matches a dotted number in the question against sensor and space NAMES. '2.5' is a measurand fragment here and a room number there, and nothing distinguishes them before the match is made. Same family as BUG-884 (naming a floor bound the sensors NAMED for it, not the sensors ON it) and BUG-883 (one sensor presented as the whole), arriving through a different door. register_projection already learned the opposite half of this lesson in BUG-950's sibling fix: 'a dotted number the question gives is now either a filter on the records that carry it or an unresolved word', added because 'How many bookings in Room 5.15 are confirmed?' was answered 11. There a dotted number was ignored; here it is over-bound.
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED HERE -- it lives in dialogue_agent / the entity resolver, outside this session's file boundary, and the routing contract's rules all run with the LAST one winning, so a change there needs the regression probe green before and after, one rule at a time.
WHAT I WOULD DO, in order of confidence:
(1) A dotted number may bind a SPACE only when a space word is present ('room', 'lab', 'office', a floor word) or the number matches a space id exactly. 'pl 2.5' has neither -- 2.5 is not the id 2.50, it is a substring of it.
(2) When a concept resolves to a measurand (here pm25_level -> brick:PM2.5_Level_Sensor, which resolved correctly for ALL five wordings tested), a numeric fragment belonging to that measurand's own name must not also be read as a place. The resolver already knows 'pl 2.5' IS the measurand.
(3) Failing both, bind building-wide rather than to one arbitrary sensor, and say the denominator -- lesson #139, which BUG-883 wrote for exactly this shape.
COST: (1) and (2) are narrow and testable offline; (3) is the aggregate lane, owned elsewhere. None is a register or vocabulary change, so BUG-947's instance (32) should be re-filed under this row and closed there.
Verification: Reproduced in the container (scratchpad probe, read-only: DialogueAgent.detect_intent on five wordings, 3 repeats of the failing one; SPARQL counts for the sensor and the class). PASS is: 'why is pl 2.5 increasing' binds no room, or binds every PM2.5 sensor and states the denominator. The control wording 'why is PM2.5 increasing in room 5.01' must still bind Room_5.01.
Refs: BUG-947 instance (32); BUG-950; BUG-884; BUG-883; CAVEAT-976; lessons #139

Title: RECOMMEND AGAINST exposing ConfigurationPeriod: its 2,175 rows record no change and no authorisation
Description:
BUG-947 cause (2) and CAVEAT-975 both treat the BMS-changes decline as a false denial over 2,175 held records, and prescribe exposing the class. Measured against the live graph, that premise does not hold.
EVERY ONE of the 2,175 ontosage:ConfigurationPeriod rows carries exactly six predicates -- type, effectiveFrom, configurationOf, configLocation, changeKind, periodSource -- and:
    changeKind   : ONE distinct value across all 2,175 -- 'first_observed'
    periodSource : ONE distinct value -- 'measured-earliest-observation'
    effectiveTo  : present on ZERO rows, so no period has ever been closed
    effective today (2026-09-30): ZERO rows
    approval / authorisation / setpoint predicate: NONE exists on the class
scripts/provision_configuration_history.py states the design in its own docstring: a commissioning date nobody recorded cannot be recovered, so it writes the earliest observation in the store 'with ontosage:changeKind "first_observed" saying so in the data'. These are ingestion stubs, one per point. They are not changes.
AND NO OTHER REGISTER HOLDS THEM EITHER: ApprovalRecord's 32 rows approve accessible routes, space use and cost lines -- read the register, there is not one BMS, setpoint or configuration approval in it.
Root_Cause: The row counted instances and inferred capability from the count. 2,175 rows of a class called ConfigurationPeriod look like a change-control register and are a provenance index. This is the measurement-apparatus lesson at the data layer: a number that looks sufficient, read without the rows behind it.
Fix_Approach:
RECOMMENDATION: do NOT add the subClassOf triple and do NOT give the class lay terms. Both halves were built and measured offline with scripts/register_reach.py against the schema on disk, so the cost is known rather than argued:
  variant A, 'rdfs:subClassOf ontosage:IntervalRecord' alone -- 0 of 2,960 catalogue questions change selection, 0 guard violations. It buys nothing on its own, exactly as CAVEAT-975 predicted, because the class carries no vocabulary.
  variant B, that triple plus ten obvious lay terms (bms change(s), configuration change(s), configuration history, change control, change record(s), setpoint change, commissioning record) -- 7 questions move, 6 gains and 1 taken from OperatingRegime, 0 guard violations. By this project's usual standard that is a clean vocabulary change.
IT IS STILL THE WRONG CHANGE, and the seven questions are the argument. AV-072 'is the detected configuration change authorised...', BM-018 'after an approved schedule or setpoint change, which intended controllers have not adopted...', BM-068, EA-042, IT-020, RC-056 'can every configuration change be traced from approved request through testing, deployment and rollback readiness?', SP-008. Every one asks about authorisation, adoption, traceability or rollback. The register holds none of those facts and has never recorded a change. Answering them from it reports 2,175 'configuration changes', all of kind 'first observed', none of them today -- a visible failure traded for an invisible one, which is the exact pattern the forward plan's Wave-A triage found five times.
WHAT WOULD MAKE IT RIGHT IS DATA, and it is the owner's to supply (CAVEAT-842's shape): a changeKind other than first_observed, an effectiveTo so a period can close, and an authorising actor. Until then the honest answer to BM-068 is 'no configuration change is recorded for today, and this building records no authorisation for one' -- which no current lane can say, because saying it requires reading the register the recommendation is not to expose.
SECOND-ORDER RISK, recorded so it is weighed once: effectiveFrom/effectiveTo are declared rdfs:domain ConfigurationPeriod and 2,349 subjects that are NOT ConfigurationPeriod use effectiveFrom (re-counted here; the xfail in test_event_and_capacity_provisioning.py says 1,321, measured 2026-09-17). On the bldg repository's rdfsplus-optimized ruleset nothing is mis-typed. On a FULL RDFS ruleset all 2,349 would infer as ConfigurationPeriod -- and with the subClassOf triple added, as IntervalRecord too. Widen those domains before anyone adds the triple, whatever else is decided.
Verification: Read-only SPARQL in the container: predicate census, distinct changeKind (1), distinct periodSource (1), effectiveTo count (0), effective-today count (0), approval-predicate probe (empty), domain-leak count (2,349). Offline: scripts/register_reach.py --schema <variant> --count ConfigurationPeriod=2175 --compare, both variants, guard 124 questions 0 violations each; the seven moved questions read verbatim from docs/smart_building_questions.csv. Schema variants were built in the scratchpad; ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl is UNCHANGED.
Refs: BUG-947 cause (2); CAVEAT-975; CAVEAT-842; scripts/provision_configuration_history.py; test_event_and_capacity_provisioning.py xfail (BUG-695); design contract #4

Title: CONFIRMED: BUG-947 instance (28) is not a vocabulary defect, and the register that looks closest says so itself
Description:
CAVEAT-976 judged (28) -- 'Before I start a long acquisition, are the approved power, network and ventilation services currently available, and what verified interruption risks remain?' -- not a register-vocabulary defect, from the absence of a missing term. Confirmed here from the positive side, which is stronger.
The register a reader would reach for is ContinuityProvision, and input/documents/continuity_provision_register.md closes with a section headed 'What this register does not record', whose first bullet is: 'Which service is running right now. This is the arrangement, not the live state.' The question asks for the live state.
Its 12 rows were read. Of the three services named, NETWORK has rows (CP-001 core network, CP-002 wireless); POWER has none; VENTILATION has none. So a term added to reach this register would answer a three-service question from one service's arrangements and present it as complete -- the C8 defect test_a_security_records_question_claims_no_register_at_all was written to keep declining, arriving on a different question.
Selector at HEAD: NOTHING ranks. Pointer: 'Operating regime, Asset engineering profile and Approval and evidence record'. None of the three records live service availability.
Root_Cause: A question spanning several registers plus a live-state clause no register holds. Not vocabulary.
Fix_Approach: No vocabulary change, and CAVEAT-976's verdict stands. The half that IS held and is silently dropped is the second clause: 'what verified interruption risks remain' is exactly what ContinuityProvision records -- CP-003, CP-006, CP-011 and CP-012 carry 'None identified' and CP-005 is Overdue, five answerable findings. register_projection already owns the right mechanism for a question only half a register can answer (res.unanswered: 'what is held is answered; what is not is named once, in the asker's own words'). Reaching it needs routing, not vocabulary, so it is not this row's change to make.
Verification: rank_record_classes and compose_boundary_pointer run in the container on the verbatim wording; the 12 ContinuityProvision rows and the register's own 'what this register does not record' section read from input/documents/continuity_provision_register.md.

Title: The decline's pointer names registers on 99.8% of declines, so the gap counter's 'one lay term short' was a work order that is usually wrong
Description:
BUG-970 made the pointer/selector disagreement countable, and closed with 'each name it returns is one declared lay term away from being reachable, so this log line is the work order for whoever owns that register's vocabulary'. Measured over ALL 2,960 catalogue questions -- the same offline Reach model the guard tests use, schema on disk, 2026-09-19 instance snapshot, 42 held classes -- that claim does not survive:
    selector selects NOTHING          : 1,746 of 2,960 (59.0%)
    of those, the pointer still NAMES : 1,742  (99.8%)
    names per decline                 : 3 in 1,684 cases, 2 in 39, 1 in 19, 0 in 4
That is roughly 5,100 'work orders' over a 44-register vocabulary. A fail-open signal that fires on 99.8% of the events it watches counts how often a DECLINE happened, not how often a vocabulary gap bit.
It is also wrong on the instances it was built to explain. BUG-947 (2), a BMS change-control question, is pointed at Approval and evidence record, Competency requirement and Compliance check -- the approval register was read and holds route, space-use and cost approvals, not one configuration approval. BUG-947 (28) is pointed at three registers none of which records live service availability (CAVEAT-1072). Neither set is one term from answering.
AND IT REFRAMES BUG-947'S HEADLINE TELL. 'Four of seven false declines named the right register in the same sentence as the refusal' has to be read against a mechanism that names three registers on 96.4% of declines (1,684 of 1,746). Sometimes naming a plausible one is what this does by construction; for tail M #54 the Department match was real and declared, and that is why BUG-973's TTL-first fix worked, but the general inference does not follow from the general mechanism.
Root_Cause: Structural, not incidental, and in two steps neither of which has a floor. fallback_wording._near_records admits a register on ONE shared crude content-term stem; nearest_holdings then returns its top-3 whether or not anything is genuinely near, because -- in BUG-950's own words -- 'with no overlap every score tied and ties keep the building's own order'. On a thirty-word stakeholder question almost every one of 42 registers clears a one-stem bar, so 'the three nearest' is 'the three that sorted first'.
Fix_Approach:
FIXED, WORDING ONLY, NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. capability_agent._log_selector_gap and fallback_wording.pointer_only_registers now state what the measurement supports: a name is a DISAGREEMENT between two matchers and a place to look, not evidence that the register holds the answer, and the ~99.8% rate is in the log line so a reader calibrates without re-deriving it. The message also says the pointer REACHES rather than the decline PRINTS, because only one of the two call sites prints any register -- the documents decline above it names none.
WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY. Tightening the pointer's admission bar was built and swept over the same 2,960 questions:
    head (today, one shared stem) : points on 1,742 of 1,746 (99.8%)
    long (one stem, >= 5 chars)   : 1,724 (98.7%)  -- buys almost nothing
    two  (>= 2 distinct stems)    : 1,314 (75.3%), 432 declines lose the pointer
    twolong                       : 1,277 (73.1%)
On the labelled instances 'two' is better three times and worse once: #7 goes from three names to Department alone, #54 to Department first of two, and #61 -- whose offer of 'Waste collection point records' BUG-947 names as part of the defect -- goes to NOTHING; but #2 moves to Compliance check and Waste collection point, which is no better. Adopting it would change decline wording on ~1,700 catalogue-shaped questions on the evidence of six labelled ones, with no live verification available this session. CAVEAT-972 is explicit that a corpus-wide wording change needs the moves read; 432 cannot be hand-read here. The sweep is recorded so the next attempt starts from it instead of re-deriving it.
NOTE THE ASYMMETRY that makes this worth returning to: the pointer decides WORDING only and never which register is READ, so a bar tightened here cannot produce a wrong answer -- only a shorter invitation or none. That is a materially safer place to tighten than rank_record_classes, where the same idea was rejected.
Verification: Offline sweep over docs/smart_building_questions.csv (2,960 questions) through scripts/register_reach.py's Reach model, four admission rules, plus the six labelled tail-M instances under each. New test test_a_name_is_a_disagreement_and_not_evidence_the_register_holds_the_answer pins the structure in memory: eight registers whose only shared vocabulary is the word 'record' are reached by none of them in the selector and named three at a time by the pointer. tests/test_a_decline_names_no_register_the_selector_cannot_reach.py 9 passed (was 8). tests/test_register_reach.py + test_register_evidence_and_event_store.py 109 passed, unchanged. flake8 F821/F823 clean; black clean on fallback_wording.py and the test, and the three hunks black still reports in capability_agent.py are the pre-existing ones of CAVEAT-977, none in the edited range. LIVE IS OWED for the log line only -- this session was forbidden to restart.
Refs: BUG-970; BUG-947; BUG-950; CAVEAT-972; CAVEAT-976; CAVEAT-977; lessons #126

Title: CAVEAT-922 settled: the 'communication' refusal is a life-safety guard, not a latency defect -- do not widen it
Description:
CAVEAT-922 records that all four slow register turns were one question failing on one word -- 'not composed deterministically: words the register's own records use but this could not place: communication' -- and asks whether the vocabulary should be widened. Reproduced offline against the real 12 evacuation rows, and the answer is no, with the worst-case spelled out.
The question is 'Which refuge points have a WORKING communication unit?'. The evacuation register's state column is free text:
    EV-001/2/4/5  'Communication unit tested and working'
    EV-003        'Communication unit FAULTY - no two-way audio'
If 'communication' were allowed to filter that text it would select ALL FIVE refuge points, EV-003 among them -- measured, not argued. The register's own note on EV-003 reads: 'A refuge point whose communication unit does not work is a place to wait with no way to say you are there.' Telling a wheelchair user that refuge point is working is the worst answer this register can produce.
The guard is also stopping a SILENT DROP, which is the less obvious half. Without it the deterministic path had already resolved 'kind: refuge point' and would have answered '5 of the 12 records match (kind: refuge point)' -- the words 'working' and 'communication' discarded with no sign. That is BUG-949's shape caught before it can happen.
The code says so already, at register_projection line ~1006: 'a word inside a free-text state or note ("tested and working") is not what a record IS, and a negation reads as its opposite.' It is right, and the 40x is the price of it.
Root_Cause: ontosage:provisionState carries, as prose, a fact that differs per kind of provision: comms working for a refuge point, a trained operator present for an evacuation chair, plans reviewed for a personal plan. The sibling status column HAS declared values (active/defective/overdue) and composes deterministically -- 'Which evacuation provisions are defective?' answers EV-003 and EV-007 in code, with no LLM. provisionState cannot be enumerated the same way because it is four different facts in one column.
Fix_Approach:
RECOMMEND CLOSING CAVEAT-922 AS BY-DESIGN, with the safety case above attached so it is not reopened as a latency row. Do not widen the projection's vocabulary and do not lower the bar for deterministic composition.
If the latency is ever worth paying down, the route is DATA and not code: split provisionState into a per-kind structured column with declared values, the way recordStatus already is in the same record document (ontology/record_documents/evacuation_provision.yaml). That is a record-document change with a corpus-wide blast radius and is not a latency decision either.
ONE THING WORTH CHECKING SEPARATELY, because CAVEAT-922's numbers understate it: MAX_ANSWER_ROWS=40 caps the DETERMINISTIC path only. The narration that this refusal falls back to was handed 18,609 characters for a 12-row register; nothing in this path caps rows, and TimetabledSession holds 686 and AccessEvent 679. Whether a decline on one of those reaches the narration with the whole register is not established here and is V7-T18's territory.
Verification: Offline probe of register_projection.resolve / _ineligible / deterministic_answer on the 12 rows parsed from input/documents/evacuation_and_peeps.md, five wordings. Reproduced verbatim: unplaced_text=['communication'], and the refusal string matches CAVEAT-922's log line exactly. The counterfactual was measured directly: a free-text match on 'communication' hits EV-001..EV-005, of which EV-003 is FAULTY. Controls compose deterministically and correctly -- 'Which evacuation provisions are defective?' -> EV-003, EV-007.

Title: An analytics answer invented a minimum equal to its maximum and reported a spread of 0 over a series whose true minimum is 0
Description:
Live 2026-09-30, 'What is the maximum occupancy of room 2.15?': '**30.00 people** is the maximum occupancy recorded ... Because only this sensor's data is available, the lowest recorded occupancy is also 30.00 people, giving a spread of 0 people.'
The series is NOT flat. The same lane's own statistics for the neighbouring room in the same batch report a minimum of 0 at 30 Sep 02:56, a mean of 12.6 and a day/night split of 22.9 against 3.51 -- a seminar room that empties overnight. A spread of 0 over an occupancy series is not a plausible value, and the stated REASON for it ('because only this sensor's data is available') is a non sequitur: one sensor has a range like any other.
Reproduced once in four asks of the same question, so it is generation variance rather than a constant.
Root_Cause:
NOT TRACED. What is known: the sandbox output for this turn was 108 characters ('[analytics] narration prompt 2649 chars (output 108, 1 sensor line(s))'), which is about one figure. The narrator was told to compare the figures with each other (narration rule 3, the no-standards branch), had only a maximum to compare, and manufactured the other operand rather than saying it did not have one. A prompt rule that asks for a comparison does not check that two things were given.
The pattern is BUG-937's exactly -- a figure the narrator derived rather than was handed -- and the likely fix is the same shape: the generated statistics template should emit min, mean and max together, or the comparison rule should be silent when there is one series and one figure. `series_summary.summarise_series` already computes all three, so the single-sensor analytics path may simply not be reading it.
Fix_Approach: Not attempted in this session -- it is a different lane from the three rows it was found beside, and inventing a fix from one observation is what lessons #145 warns about. First step is cheap and is the one to take: ask the question five more times, capture the sandbox output each time, and see whether the 108-character output ever contains a minimum. If it does not, the defect is in the statistics template, not the narration.
Verification: Observed once in four asks, live 2026-09-30, /v1, fresh chat, resp_cache and cache:sparql flushed. The contradicting statistics are in the same probe output, from the sensor_data lane on room 5.01.
Refs: BUG-953; BUG-937 (a figure the narrator derived); BUG-898; lessons #145

Title: 29 of 41 rooms report MORE PEOPLE THAN THE BUILDING SAYS THEY HOLD, live, up to 3.75x capacity
Description: Unlike CAVEAT-1131 this one is LIVE, not history. Measured 2026-09-30 09:33 UTC, session pinned '+00:00', latest reading per uuid against the capacities BUG-896 consolidated this morning: of the 41 rooms that carry both an hbco:roomCapacity and a simulated people counter, 27 are over capacity at this instant. Room5.07 holds 8 and reports 24 (3.0x); Room3.15, Room3.27 and Room5.06 hold 8 and report 23; Room2.13, Room4.11 and Room5.18 hold 12 and report 25. It is not a momentary peak: Room1.25 (capacity 20) exceeded its capacity in 947 of 1,941 readings over the last seven days (48.8%). Any lane that compares occupancy to capacity -- an overcrowding check, a room-booking suggestion, a safety question -- is reading a building that has been at double its design occupancy for a week.
Root_Cause:
UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE AND CORRECTED IN TWO PLACES.
THE FILE WAS NAMED WRONG. This row said the band comes from `scripts/generate_publish_map.py`. It does not: that script writes `<id>_extended_narrow_uuids.json`, a different map. The band on `<id>_narrow_publish_map.json` is attached at BOOT by `orchestrator/services/publisher_map.py::_attach_bands`, from the ontology, and `scripts/generate_publisher_map.py` (note the 'r') emits no band at all (CAVEAT-1174). Fixing the named file would have changed nothing.
THE NUMBERS WERE LOW. Re-measured independently 2026-09-30 12:10 UTC: 29 of 41 rooms, not 27, and the worst is 3.75x not 3.0x - six eight-person rooms peaking at 29-30. All 29 are over capacity at their LATEST reading, not only at a peak.
THE CAUSE STANDS: the graph declares exactly one band for people, `ontosage:OccupancyCount typicalMin 0 ; typicalMax 30` (one row, re-queried), so all 256 room counters are banded identically and the generator drives each to a diurnal peak at the top of that band whatever room it is in.
Fix_Approach:
FIXED GOING FORWARD, IN CODE, NOT DEPLOYED. `orchestrator/services/publisher_map.py::_apply_declared_room_ceilings` reads `hbco:roomCapacity` from the graph - a triple BUG-896 put there this morning - and lowers a people counter's ceiling to its own room's capacity.
IT ONLY EVER LOWERS, and that is a deliberate departure from this row's own proposal ('use that capacity as hi instead of the measurand's typicalMax'). A dry run showed the proposed rule would also RAISE eleven ceilings, Room2.15 from 30 to 40 - and BUG-1137 measures that room at 7.83 m2, so 40 people is 0.20 m2 each and the raise manufactures a reading impossible on floor area alone. The two directions do not carry the same risk: too small under-reports, too large asserts a crowd the room cannot hold. The ceiling is therefore min(typicalMax, capacity). COST OF THAT CHOICE, STATED: eleven counters in rooms declaring 40 or 50 keep the 30 they have today and stay under-reported.
THE POINT-TO-SPACE RELATION IS BOUND WITH A VARIABLE PREDICATE. This building spells it three ways - brick:hasLocation (41), rec:locatedIn (41), brick:isPartOf (12) - and the obvious query naming brick:isPartOf reaches only 12 of 53 uuids (measured). Lesson #161.
THIS ROW DEPENDS ON BUG-1137 AND SAYS SO. Every new ceiling is a capacity declared 'estimated, not certified', and BUG-1137 holds evidence that 20 of the 42 are implausible against floor area. Capping only means a wrong capacity under-reports rather than over-reports, which is why the dependency is tolerable - but a counter capped at an estimated capacity is still not a fire-safety measurement, and the map records that on every entry it touches (`hi_basis`).
MIGRATION COST, IN ROWS, NOT ADJECTIVES: 447,865 of 1,099,040 stored rows (40.8%) across 29 rooms sit above the new ceiling, earliest 2026-07-08 10:11. NOT re-seeded - that is the owner's call and CAVEAT-1131's recommendation is not to rewrite history. The rows keep their old band's valid-from, and the new ceiling is stamped `band_from` = the day it lands, so the audit separates the two by itself.
DEPLOYMENT CAVEAT, AND IT IS NOT SMALL: `refresh_publish_map` is called from main.py ONLY when `summary['uploaded']` is truthy, i.e. only when the TTL uploader actually ingested a changed file. A plain restart does NOT rebuild the map. The publisher then has to be recreated to reload it ('docker compose up -d data-publisher'), not restarted.
Verification:
MEASUREMENT, independent of the original: scratchpad/probe_occupancy_vs_capacity.py, read-only, in-container, MySQL session printed as '+00:00'. Capacities read from the LIVE GRAPH (not from the TTL text), 53 counter uuids across 41 distinct rooms, no uuid reaching two different capacities, 1 of the 42 capacity rooms (Room1.04) having no counter. 29 of 41 rooms exceeded capacity in the last 7 days AND at their latest reading; Room3.15/3.26/3.27/5.06/5.07 declared 8 and peaked at 30 (3.75x).
CODE: `pytest tests/test_a_counter_is_capped_by_its_own_room.py tests/test_a_provisioned_point_is_fed.py tests/test_publisher_map_covers_what_is_watched.py` -> 37 passed. black + flake8 --select=F821,F823 clean.
DRY RUN AGAINST THE LIVE GRAPH, WRITING NOTHING (scratchpad/dryrun_in_container.py, which never calls _rebuild): 36 bands would change, 30->8 x7, 30->12 x9, 30->15 x3, 30->20 x14, 30->25 x3; zero raised. Room5.07 goes 30 -> 8.
NOT VERIFIED LIVE: no container was restarted and no map was written, so nothing here shows the PUBLISHER honouring the new ceiling. That check is owed and is what would move this row past PARTIALLY_FIXED.
SCOPE, STATED: 36 of 233 room counters. The other 197 declare no capacity and keep the 0..30 band, so this narrows the defect rather than closing it.
Refs: BUG-896; BUG-1137; BUG-1042; BUG-1130; CAVEAT-1131; CAVEAT-1174; orchestrator/services/publisher_map.py; tests/test_a_counter_is_capped_by_its_own_room.py

Title: CAVEAT-841 re-measured: still exactly 132, BUG-896 did not shrink it, and FOUR of its own figures are wrong
Description: STILL TRUE, and the count is exact: 132 of 225 rooms disagree with the drawings today, 0 rooms have changed since 2026-09-17, and the graph holds 225 room subjects against 225 in the drawing fixture with no room present on one side only. ALL 132 DIFFER IN BOTH TYPE AND LABEL -- label_only=0, type_only=0 -- so none is cosmetic. Largest direction: 82 teaching -> office, of which 57 are Laboratory -> Enclosed_Office. FOUR CORRECTIONS TO CAVEAT-841's OWN TEXT. (1) 'Four owner answers' is FIVE: docs/phase0/room_identity_cascade.md section 5 carries a fifth, the six Appendix-B ambiguous rooms (chiefly 4.07 Cyber Security, laboratory or teaching room). All six sit OUTSIDE the 132 and block nothing. (2) '~866 register rows across 22 docs' is 864 across 23 -- the cascade doc's table omits waste_returns_register (7 rows). (3) '1,132 sensor labels' is right for saturation points and UNDERCOUNTS the real relabel: 1,156 labels embed an old room DESCRIPTION (1,132 saturation + 24 waste-bin points) and 1,468 labelled points sit in a changed room. (4) THE BOOKING FIGURES ARE 13 DAYS STALE AND STILL MOVING: '5,112 over capacity (104 future)' is now 6,775 (1,108 future), and the 18 unoccupied rooms hold 932 rows against 680. data-publisher keeps a rolling 14-day forward booking window, so the future half grew roughly tenfold.
Root_Cause: Unchanged and correctly diagnosed in CAVEAT-841. What is new is that BUG-896 DID NOT SHRINK THIS ROW, which is worth recording because it would be easy to assume it had: 42 rooms carried a capacity before the consolidation and 42 after, 0 dropped and 0 added, and 0 rooms have a post value that is not one of their pre values -- the reconciliation took the lower of a disagreeing pair and re-derived nothing. Rooms whose capacity agrees with the drawing's stated person count: 0 before, 0 after. BUG-896 relocated the disagreement into one file with a basis, which makes the eventual fix simpler; it did not make it smaller.
Fix_Approach: SPLIT IT, and Stage 1 needs only two of the five answers. THE 15 ROOMS WHOSE CURRENT LABEL ASSERTS A SERVICE OR SAFETY FUNCTION THE DRAWING DENIES CARRY ZERO TIMETABLED SESSIONS -- the overlap with the 42 session-bearing rooms is EMPTY -- so correcting them regenerates no timetable at all: 15 rooms, 0 sessions, 125 saturation labels, 45 register rows in 13 docs, against 132 / 646 / 1,132 / 232 for the full pass. Those 15 are Room 0.01, 0.04, 0.05, 0.31, 0.32, 0.33, 0.34, 1.34, 2.34, 2.44, 3.38, 4.34, 4.38, 5.34, 5.44. It removes 'Server Room' from a 168 m2 teaching room, 'Mechanical Plant Room' from a 30-person seminar room that also holds an asbestos record, and 'Main Reception' from a 120-seat lecture theatre. It needs owner answers 1 and 2 only. RECOMMENDATIONS ON THE FIVE, each with its consequence: (Q1 reception) NO, 0.19 is a 3-person post room; create bldg:MainEntrance a brick:Entrance as a non-room space on Floor 0 and move the entrance kit onto it -- the graph already models bldg:Rooftop and bldg:BuildingExterior as non-room spaces, so there is precedent, and 0.01 becomes the 120-seat theatre it is drawn as. (Q2 plant room) DO NOT INVENT ONE -- the graph does not put plant in a room at all today (AHUs and breaker panels are floor-scoped, boilers/chiller/heat pump are on bldg:Rooftop); the plant room exists only in register prose, so correct the prose. ONE CARVE-OUT: do not relocate the asbestos flue remnant by inference; record it 'location unconfirmed - Estates to verify', because a wrong asbestos location is worse than a missing one. (Q3 atrium) YES, MODEL IT, but as bldg:Atrium a brick:Atrium and NOT as Room1.04 -- otherwise once 1.04 becomes a seminar room the referent gate declines 'the atrium' as no such space, which is a worse answer than 'the atrium is not instrumented'. (Q4 room 2.26) REFUTE THE DRAWING: '120S Lecture Theatre' in a 27.44 m2 outline is 0.23 m2/person, the only room of 225 whose own drawing count does not fit its own outline, and the staged correction would turn it into a brick:Auditorium -- manufacturing a second impossible claim. Drop it from the mechanical pass, type it brick:Conference_Room, flag the outline for re-measurement. (Q5 Appendix B) DEFER; the six cost nothing to leave. AND ONE THING NEEDING NO ANSWER AT ALL: re-measure the booking figures AT APPLY TIME rather than quoting them from any plan, because they grow daily.
Verification: MEASURED BY A SUB-AGENT OF THIS SESSION, NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY THE AGENT FILING IT. Rooms counted as DISTINCT subjects FROM <http://www.ontotext.com/explicit> so inference could not inflate them. input/bldg1_abacws_metadata.ttl proved byte-identical to HEAD:bldg1/ (modulo CRLF), which is what establishes 'nothing has changed since 2026-09-17'. Title: 20 of the 42 declared room capacities are physically impossible -- 40 people in 7.83 m2, below the means-of-escape minimum
Description: Of the 42 rooms that now carry hbco:roomCapacity in input/bldg1_occupancy_capacity.ttl, 20 declare a capacity below 1.0 m2 per person, which is under Approved Document B's means-of-escape maximum occupancy for a room. Worst: Room2.15 40 people in 7.83 m2 (0.20 m2/p), Room4.13 40 in 10.12 (0.25), Room5.15 and Room5.16 40 in 11.0 (0.28). Twelve of the 20 are 10-11 m2 cellular offices declared at 12 to 30 people. Separately, 14 of the 42 disagree with an explicit person count written on the drawing (Room0.01 declares 50 against the drawing's 120; Room5.05 declares 20 against 90; Room1.25 declares 20 against 8), and all 41 rooms present in both sources disagree with the staged correction's figure.
Root_Cause: Not diagnosed to the line and it does NOT need room identity settled first -- that is what makes it separable. The figures were carried forward unchanged through BUG-896 from the building's own maxOccupancy, and BUG-896 was explicitly a consolidation rather than a re-derivation, so it neither introduced nor could have caught this. Nobody has ever checked a declared capacity against the room's own area.
Fix_Approach: OWNER DECISION, and the recommendation is WITHHOLD THE 20 RATHER THAN CORRECT THEM. input/bldg1_occupancy_capacity.ttl states its own standard: 'a capacity with no basis cannot be told apart from a certified fire capacity, and an estimate quoted as a limit is a safety claim nobody made'. A figure of 40 people in 7.83 m2 is that failure in its most dangerous form -- it reads as a limit, it is an estimate, and it is an estimate that is wrong in the direction that gets people hurt. Either drop those 20 hbco:roomCapacity triples, or replace each with the area-derived value carrying the basis 'derived from floor area at 2.0 m2/person; not certified'. About 20 lines in one file, NO CASCADE, and it does not depend on CAVEAT-841. NOT DONE HERE: that file belongs to BUG-896's owner and this agent was told to stay clear of every TTL declaring maxOccupancy or roomCapacity, so this is a proposal and nothing in it has been applied. PREFER WITHHOLDING TO DERIVING: 2.0 m2/person is itself a convention, and replacing one unsourced number with another unsourced number is a smaller improvement than it looks.
Verification: MEASURED BY A SUB-AGENT OF THIS SESSION, NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY THE AGENT FILING IT. Said plainly because this project has been bitten by exactly this: a figure restated at one remove reads like a second confirmation and is not one. Every number below carries the command that produced it, so it is re-runnable; treat it as one measurement, not two. Capacities read from input/bldg1_occupancy_capacity.ttl (read-only) and divided by each room's area from the drawing fixture. Cross-check that BUG-896 left no residue: 0 maxOccupancy or roomCapacity triples remain in the two files it moved them out of. Per-room sheet in the session scratchpad as capacity_compare.csv.

Title: Nine service rooms were typed BY ROOM NUMBER, not by function: every *.34 is a Telecom_Room and every *.44 a Server_Room
Description: A sub-pattern inside CAVEAT-841's 132, and worth separating because it is one generator artefact rather than nine independent errors. Every room numbered *.34 is typed brick:Telecom_Room and every *.44 brick:Server_Room, regardless of what the drawing says the room is. Room0.34 Telecom_Room is a 96-person lecture theatre on the drawing; 1.34 is a 60-person computer room; 2.34, 4.34 and 5.34 are PhD research and student rooms; 3.38 Telecom_Room is a 48-person seminar room; 2.44 Server_Room is a 5-person PhD research room; 5.44 Server_Room is '60P Teaching' at 168.33 m2. EXACTLY ONE of the nine is right -- Room4.44, and it is the only room the drawing labels 'Server Rm'.
Root_Cause: A room-number heuristic standing in for a function lookup. One right answer out of nine is what a positional rule produces when the position happens to be meaningful once.
Fix_Approach: No separate fix needed -- all nine sit inside CAVEAT-841's 132 and eight of them inside the 15-room Stage 1 described in CAVEAT-1136, so correcting Stage 1 corrects them. Filed separately because the PATTERN is the useful part: if a room number produced these types, the same heuristic may have produced others, and that is worth one grep before the correction is trusted as complete. It is also the clearest single example of why the 15 are the ones to do first: 'where is the server room' currently answers with a 168 m2 teaching space.
Verification: MEASURED BY A SUB-AGENT OF THIS SESSION, NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY THE AGENT FILING IT. Title: CAVEAT-1060's 25 unaudited settings patches: 15 of 25 were vacuous, and the 2 truly detached ones both passed
Description: Audited all 25 monkeypatch.setattr(settings, ...) sites across the 8 files CAVEAT-1060 named, by MEASUREMENT rather than by reading. Two throwaway pytest plugins did it. (1) A NEUTER plugin wraps MonkeyPatch.setattr and turns every Settings patch into a no-op, which answers the only question that matters -- does the assertion still hold when the patch does nothing? (2) A REACH plugin reloads shared.config after collection, exactly as test_strict_secrets.py does mid-session, and reports for each patch whether the object being patched is the one the product module reads. RESULT, current tree with a building active: 15 of 25 sites VACUOUS (the assertion held with the patch neutered), 10 load-bearing, and 0 order-dependent in the sense of going red. TWO sites were genuinely DETACHED by the reload -- test_analytics_repairs_inside_a_time_budget.py:129 (WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_S; the test imported settings in the function body, post-reload, while analytics_agent holds the pre-reload object) and test_observed_at.py:114 (BUILDING_TIMEZONE; the test bound at module scope, pre-reload, while evidence/assemble.py imports inside the function and reads the post-reload one). BOTH PASSED ANYWAY, which is the prediction lesson #159 made: the three that failed were the lucky ones. The other 23 reach the object the product reads, but three files did so only because test and product happened to bind in the same style.
Root_Cause: `from X import y` binds the OBJECT. A reload of X rebinds X.y and leaves every prior importer on the old one, so two Settings instances are alive for the rest of the session and a patch lands on whichever the test happened to capture. Whether that is the right one depends on the binding style of BOTH sides -- module-level in the test AND module-level in the product agree; function-level in both agree; one of each does not. Nothing in the test expresses which it needs.
Fix_Approach: Patch WHERE IT IS USED. For a product module that binds at import time, patch <module>.settings (test_similarity_rebuild -> om.settings, test_locked_capability -> _wo.settings, test_analytics_repairs -> _aa.settings). For a product module that imports inside the function, patch the LIVE object by resolving it at call time (test_observed_at -> _cfg.settings, flat_layout and compile_cache and protect_enforcement and undeclared_type_audit already do this with an import in the test body). Where the assertion was ALSO vacuous, it was strengthened to derive the answer instead of restating the parameter: the repair budget now pins the documented 120.0 fallback and is parametrised over 0/None/''/garbage/-30 plus a second test proving 300 -> 150.0, and test_gate_silent_when_flag_off runs the same fixture with the flag ON and OFF so the flag is provably the difference. tests/test_settings_patches_reach_the_product.py now fails the build on the one form that is never provably right (module-level `from shared.config import settings` + a bare setattr on it), found by parsing rather than by matching text.
Verification: With the neuter plugin loaded, the five repaired files went from 3 failures to 11 -- i.e. 8 assertions that used to hold with their patch disabled no longer do. With the reach plugin (reload after collection) every one of the 25 sites now resolves to the module that reads it: analytics_agent, _orchestrator, ontology_manager as module-level holders, document_indexer and assemble via the live object. pytest tests/test_strict_secrets.py <the 8 files> tests/test_settings_patches_reach_the_product.py -> 94 passed, and 69 passed again with DATASOURCE_TOGGLES_ENABLED=false PROTECT_ENFORCE=shadow (the parked defaults CI sees).

Title: Nine of the 25 patch sites are vacuous in one environment and load-bearing in the other, and the difference is an untracked .env
Description: Measured with the neuter plugin twice, once as the tree stands (a building active, .env present) and once with the parked defaults exported. shared/config.py defaults DATASOURCE_TOGGLES_ENABLED to False; the developer .env sets it true. So in the ACTIVE state the eight monkeypatch.setattr(settings, 'DATASOURCE_TOGGLES_ENABLED', True) sites in test_locked_capability.py are no-ops and their tests pass on the ambient value, while the single False site is load-bearing; in the PARKED state -- what a fresh clone, CI and Workflow rule 8 see -- it is exactly the other way round. PROTECT_ENFORCE has the same shape (default 'shadow', .env 'off'). The consequence that matters: in the parked state, four test_locked_capability tests asserting `is None` would pass with the gate never reached at all if their patch ever detached, because the flag is already off.
Root_Cause: A boolean precondition pinned by a patch is only load-bearing when it differs from the ambient value, and the ambient value here comes from a file that is deliberately not in git. The test's own meaning therefore depends on which building is active -- the same class of dependence test_strict_secrets.py's docstring already forbids for itself ('nothing here may depend on an untracked file').
Fix_Approach: Cannot be removed by choosing a better patch target; a flag has two values and the ambient one is sometimes right. What CAN be removed is the silent case: a test that asserts the NEGATIVE outcome should prove the flag is the cause by exercising both values against one fixture, which is what test_gate_silent_when_flag_off now does. The remaining eight sites are preconditions for positive assertions and are correct in both states. Recorded here so the next reader does not measure one state and generalise.
Verification: Neuter run, active .env: test_gate_silent_when_flag_off fails, the eight True sites pass. Neuter run with DATASOURCE_TOGGLES_ENABLED=false: test_gate_fires_for_disabled_source, test_gate_picks_matching_disabled_source and test_gate_forbids_source_by_role fail instead, and test_gate_silent_when_flag_off passes. Both runs on the same tree, minutes apart.

Title: A test patched BUILDING_ID to the value BUILDING_ID already had
Description: tests/test_flat_layout_loaders.py::test_document_index_all_buildings_flat set BUILDING_ID to 'bldg1' and then asserted index_building was awaited with 'bldg1'. 'bldg1' is the shared/config.py default (the Settings constructor even logs a warning saying so) and the active .env value. An index_all_buildings that ignored the setting entirely and hardcoded the name would have passed. The patch reached the product correctly -- this one was vacuous by construction, not by detachment, which is why the reach measurement alone would have called it healthy.
Root_Cause: A patch whose value equals the ambient value tests nothing, and nothing in the test says what it is supposed to differ from.
Fix_Approach: Patch to 'bldg_flat_probe', an id no building in this repo uses, and assert on that. The assertion is then about the plumbing instead of about the default.
Verification: Passes as written; fails under the neuter plugin, which it did not before. Two other sites of the same kind were found and are recorded under CAVEAT-1110 (four True patches on GRAPHDB_USE_SIMILARITY, whose default is True in both the active and the parked state).

Title: Six XPASS: a non-strict xfail left on a test that had been fixed, and XPASS is a state nobody reads
Description: All six XPASS in the unit suite are the same parametrised test, tests/test_the_decline_classifiers_know_their_own_wording.py::test_the_shared_classifier_calls_every_emitted_decline_a_decline, marked xfail against CAVEAT-952 (publication_gate.is_decline not recognising "I couldn't answer that from <building>'s records"). CAVEAT-952 was closed by BUG-992 earlier the same day and is FIXED in this tracker; verified directly rather than inferred -- is_decline now returns True for both leads the row names. The marker carried strict=False, so the six went from xfail to xpass and the suite total did not move: xpassed is reported separately and is neither a failure nor a pass. The file's own docstring had PLANNED for this ('the day the marker is added this reports XPASS rather than breaking the suite'), and the plan worked exactly as written and still nobody acted on it. CAVEAT-991's Verification column also still reads '11 passed, 6 xfailed', which is now 17 passed.
Root_Cause: A non-strict xfail cannot tell you it has started passing. It downgrades an unexpected pass to a status that no CI gate and no habit reads, so a fix that lands leaves no trace in the suite.
Fix_Approach: Marker removed; the six assert plainly and the sibling test_the_shared_classifier_still_recognises_what_it_was_written_for keeps the original wordings pinned so a future widening cannot drop one (CLAUDE.md's standing rule, lessons #141). The file docstring now records why the non-strict marker went unnoticed rather than repeating the plan that failed. The other three xfails in the unit suite (test_event_and_capacity_provisioning, BUG-695 modelling debt) are still failing and are correct; test_capability_e2e.py:187 is marked live and is outside -m unit.
Verification: pytest tests/test_the_decline_classifiers_know_their_own_wording.py -q -rxX -> 17 passed, 0 xfailed, 0 xpassed (was 11 passed / 6 xpassed). This is a +6 change in the suite's pass count and it is a marker removal, not new coverage.

Title: Three source-reading assertions still window by character count, and one of them could have matched an unrelated statement
Description: Swept tests/ for lesson #151's shape. 551 substring-of-source assertions exist across 354 files; the ones windowed by CHARACTER COUNT -- the form the lesson says never to use -- are three: test_a_grounded_answer_is_not_discarded_for_its_phrasing.py (block[:400] after a src.index(...)-200 offset, and a second at src[i:i+900]), test_a_rewrite_may_not_invent_a_place.py (block[:400]), and test_event_and_capacity_provisioning.py ('GENERATED by scripts/' in text[:2000], a file-header check and the mildest of the three). The rewrite one was the sharpest: it asserted 'return None' inside a 400-character window, and `return None` is common enough that a window catching an UNRELATED one would have looked exactly like a pass. Measured: the block is ~290 characters, so the window was the whole remainder of the function and bought nothing while costing the assertion its stability.
Root_Cause: A character window is a bet on how much code and prose sits around the line of interest, and both grow. lessons #151 recorded three such assertions breaking in one day with no behaviour change, one of them widened twice rather than fixed.
Fix_Approach: Rewrote all three assertions in the two behaviour-bearing files to read the PARSED tree: find the IfExp whose body calls reword_handover_phrasing and assert its condition mentions 'grounded'; find the If whose test mentions whole_register and assert its body clears _meta; find the If whose test mentions rewrite_invents_a_place and assert its body contains `return None`. A formatter can reflow any of that and the checks still hold, and each now fails loudly if the construct disappears altogether rather than silently matching something else. The text[:2000] header check is left alone.
Verification: pytest tests/test_a_grounded_answer_is_not_discarded_for_its_phrasing.py tests/test_a_rewrite_may_not_invent_a_place.py -q -> 17 passed. black --line-length 100 then re-run: still 17 passed, which the old assertions could not have promised.

Title: 83 tests would pass against an empty result as readily as a correct one, and one of them was already checking nothing
Description: Two AST sweeps over tests/. (A) EMPTY COLLECTION: 68 tests whose every assertion sits inside a loop over a COMPUTED iterable, with nothing in the body checking the collection is non-empty. Zero items means zero assertions and a green result. The riskiest read on inspection: test_the_building_holds_it_and_says_so::test_no_building_literal_entered_the_vocabulary over reach.held -- lessons #153 already recorded record_classes() returning 0 from the host because GraphDB resolves to a container name, which here would report 'no building literal entered the vocabulary' about a vocabulary never read -- and test_every_figure_points_at_a_row::test_every_decision_is_explainable over rep.claims, where a binder that bound nothing satisfies 'every decision is explainable'. (B) FILTERED LOOP, the sharper shape: 15 tests where the collection can be full and the test still runs zero assertions, because an in-loop `continue` filtered everything out. One of those was ALREADY vacuous, not hypothetically: test_agent_methods_exist parametrises over orchestrator/agents/*.py including __init__.py, which declares no class at all, so that parameter had always reported a pass for a file it never examined.
Root_Cause: lessons #20 one level up: 'couldn't check' and 'checked, found nothing' render identically. A loop that is the whole test is a fail-open path with no count of how often it acted.
Fix_Approach: Added the count. Title: A reload rebuilds the Settings CLASS too, so an isinstance check goes blind on exactly the stale objects
Description: Found while building the audit instrument for CAVEAT-1060. The first reach plugin identified a Settings object with isinstance(target, shared.config.Settings) and reported 16 of the 25 patch sites as not existing at all. importlib.reload rebuilds every class the module defines, so an instance created BEFORE the reload is not an isinstance of the class the module exposes AFTER it -- and the pre-reload instances are precisely the ones a detachment audit is looking for. Matching on type(target).__name__ == 'Settings' and .__module__ == 'shared.config' found all 25.
Root_Cause: Ordinary Python: reload re-executes the module body, so `class Settings` is a new class object. Identity-based type checks silently narrow to post-reload instances.
Fix_Approach: Any tool that has to recognise settings objects across a reload must match on class name and module, not on class identity. Worth knowing for anything else in this repo that isinstance-checks a Settings, a model or a dataclass that a test may have reloaded.
Verification: Same plugin, same run, two detectors: isinstance reported 19 patch events and missed every module-level-bound one; the name-based detector reported 35 and matched the 25 static sites exactly.

Title: The gap backfill turns every binary point into a deterministic office-hours square wave, so one series has two contradictory models on adjacent days
Description: scripts/backfill_narrow_gap.py::_shape has NO binary branch. It applies the same continuous diurnal formula to every point and then rounds: centre = lo + (hi-lo)*(0.5*(1-swing) + swing*cycle), jitter = (hi-lo)*0.06. For a 0/1 occupancy flag with swing 0.9 that is centre = 0.05 + 0.9*cycle with a jitter of +/-0.06 -- far too small to flip int(round()) except at the crossing -- so the value is 0 whenever centre < 0.5 and 1 whenever centre > 0.5, crossing at exactly 07:00 and 19:00. A perfect square wave, IDENTICAL for every series, because the only per-sensor term is a phase that moves the value by at most 0.06. MEASURED IN THE STORE, and it matches the simulation hour for hour: over the backfilled days 2026-09-25 to 09-28 the 234 presence flags have an hourly mean of 0.00 from 20:00 to 05:00 and 1.00 from 08:00 to 17:00, transitions at 06-07 and 18-19, pooled range 1.000. Over the live days 09-29 to 09-30 the same flags sit at 0.45-0.56 with no shape at all. THE SAME SERIES THEREFORE HOLDS TWO CONTRADICTORY MODELS ON ADJACENT DAYS: 'was room X occupied last Friday' reads a tidy working day, 'is room X occupied now' reads a coin. BLAST RADIUS: 722 binary points in the narrow publish map -- 466 contact_data and 256 occupancy_data. The contacts get a different wrong shape rather than the same one, because _DIURNAL['contact'] is 0.0, which makes centre a flat 0.5 and the rounding a 50/50 coin decided by phase.
Root_Cause: A value model written for continuous quantities applied to points that have only two states. The live generator (mysql-dummy-publish-dev/sensor_signal.py) has exactly the branch this one lacks -- `if dec == 0 and span <= 1.0` -- so the two writers were never going to agree. Note the symmetry with BUG-1130, which is the same defect inverted: the LIVE generator gives a presence flag no clock at all, and the BACKFILL gives it a perfect clock and no independence. Neither is a building.
Fix_Approach: FIXED IN THE GENERATOR (2026-09-30), by deletion rather than by addition. scripts/backfill_narrow_gap.py no longer has a value model: _shape and _DIURNAL are GONE, and the module imports mysql-dummy-publish-dev/sensor_signal and calls the same next_value() the live publisher calls. Adding the missing binary branch here would have left two near-identical diurnal tables in two files, which is exactly how these two writers came to disagree; one model is the only durable statement. The import is a HARD dependency with an explicit ImportError -- a silent fallback to a local copy would restore the defect the moment the directory moved. _RANGES stays, relabelled: it is a BAND table for points whose publish-map entry declares no lo/hi, not a value model. Two consequences worth naming. (a) The per-sensor offset was `(i % 7) / 7.0 - 0.5` -- seven offsets shared out by list position, so a sensor's whole backfilled history was a function of where it sat in a list. sensor_signal derives a stable offset from the uuid instead. (b) A binary point is a HELD STATE, not a function of the timestamp, so main() now resets per-uuid state before each sensor and walks that sensor's gap forward in time; and it passes step_s=step.total_seconds(), because a hold-and-flip rate tuned for 60 s writes applied to 15-minute writes mixes fifteen times too slowly and the daily swing comes out muted rather than absent. That argument was added to sensor_signal for this caller. NOT DONE, and owed to the owner: recording WHICH DAYS ARE BACKFILLED. A lane still cannot tell a backfilled day from a lived one. That needs a provenance column or a side table and a write to the store, so it is a migration, not a generator change. ROWS ALREADY WRITTEN ARE NOT REPAIRED -- see BUG-1150 for the costed re-seed.
Verification: OFFLINE SIMULATION and a source check; no store was written. scratchpad/sim_backfill_after.py drives the fixed _value_from over 3 days x 12 sensors at the 15-minute backfill step. Presence flag: pooled hourly mean 0.021 at 00:00 to 0.965 at 13:00, and the 12 sensors are NOT identical at any hour -- the square wave's signature was all 234 flags carrying the same value at every backfilled timestamp. Door contact stays flat (0.38..0.60, no monotone shape), occupancy count 2.1..27.3, temperature 20.9..23.1. tests/test_backfill_uses_one_value_model.py, 9 tests, all passing. One of them is a SOURCE check on purpose: a reintroduced local _shape would satisfy every behavioural test if it were tuned to, because the failure mode is not a wrong curve but a SECOND curve that drifts. It pins an ASSIGNMENT rather than a mention -- the first draft failed on the comment explaining why _DIURNAL is gone, which is the guard being imprecise rather than the source being wrong. Also pinned: the backfill and the publisher return the SAME reading for one point at one instant under one seed. NOT VERIFIED LIVE. Running the backfill writes rows, and this agent did not.
Refs: BUG-1130; BUG-1042; CAVEAT-890; CAVEAT-1131; CAVEAT-1140; BUG-1150; scripts/backfill_narrow_gap.py; mysql-dummy-publish-dev/sensor_signal.py; tests/test_backfill_uses_one_value_model.py

Title: CAVEAT-890 describes a backfill method that no script in this repo implements, for 1.29 million rows now in the store
Description: CAVEAT-890 records two backfills on 2026-09-29 totalling 1,291,228 rows and states the method: 'Values are never invented: each is sampled from that same series' OWN history at the SAME HOUR OF DAY from the fortnight before the hole, so a drift detector or a peer comparison sees shape rather than uniform noise; an ENUM column's value is copied verbatim.' The script it names in Refs, scripts/backfill_narrow_gap.py, does not do that. It GENERATES every value from a sine formula in _shape and reads no historical value at all -- its only SELECT is `SELECT uuid, MAX(datetime)` to find where each gap starts. Searched: the repo holds backfill_db_sensor_ttls.py, backfill_events.py, backfill_narrow_gap.py and backfill_saturation.py, and no script matches on 'same hour', 'fortnight' or 'hour of day' for a backfill. AND THE STORE AGREES WITH THE CODE RATHER THAN WITH THE PROSE: the backfilled presence flags are a deterministic square wave reproducible from backfill_narrow_gap._shape hour for hour (BUG-1139), which is neither sampled history nor what the live generator writes.
Root_Cause: Not established, and deliberately left open rather than guessed. Two possibilities and they have different consequences: either the 2026-09-29 run used an ad-hoc script that was never committed, in which case 1.29 M rows were written by code nobody can read; or the description is simply wrong, in which case the rows are formula-generated and the tracker overstates their fidelity. The evidence available here favours the second for the occupancy flags at least, because they match the committed script exactly -- but that is one family out of nineteen tables and it is not a proof about the rest.
Fix_Approach: OWNER DECISION, and it is a question only the person who ran it can answer: WHICH SCRIPT WROTE THE 2026-09-29 BACKFILL? If an uncommitted one, commit it -- 1.29 M rows whose generator is not in the repo cannot be reproduced, audited or reasoned about, and CAVEAT-890 itself exists because someone claimed 19 tables after checking ten. If the committed script did it, correct CAVEAT-890's method sentence, because 'values are never invented' is the load-bearing claim in that row and it is the opposite of what _shape does. RECOMMENDED EITHER WAY, and it is the durable half: mark the backfilled intervals in the store or in the graph so a lane can say 'this window is filled, not observed'. That is the same shape as ontosage:capacityBasis -- a reading with no basis cannot be told apart from a measurement -- and it is what would stop CAVEAT-890's own recommended coverage check from reporting a filled hole as real data.
Verification: Read scripts/backfill_narrow_gap.py in full: _value_from -> _shape is the only value path, and grep for SELECT returns one statement, `SELECT uuid, MAX(datetime) FROM <table>`. `ls scripts/ | grep -i 'backfill|gap|fill'` for the candidate set; grep across scripts/*.py for 'same hour', 'SAME HOUR', 'fortnight', 'hour of day' returns only conformance_report.py, grade_anomalies.py, rebase_energy_interval_reads.py and refresh_record_dates.py, none of which is a backfill. Store side: BUG-1139's two measurements. NOT ESTABLISHED and not claimed: whether the other eighteen tables' backfilled rows also match the committed script. Only the occupancy flags were checked against it.

Description: THE STORE COUNTS IN CAVEAT-903 ARE EXACT AND THE 'DECLARED' SIDE IS NOT. Re-measured in-container with the session pinned '+00:00': sensor_data_synth holds 106 distinct uuids and THE GRAPH DECLARES ALL 106 -- 0 undeclared, not 69. Corrected per store (store / graph-declared / truly undeclared): sensor_data_synth 106/106/0, plant_data 88/44/44, occupancy_data 514/512/2, light_data 242/241/1, noise_data 236/235/1, water_data 13/13/0. THE BUILDING-WIDE UNDECLARED TOTAL IS 48, NOT 69. CAVEAT-903's '37 declared' came from input/.sensor_map.cache.json, which is NOT the declaration and does not track the graph -- it reports water_data 7 where the graph declares 13, and occupancy_data 486 where the graph declares 512. THE FROZEN STREAMS ARE 70, NOT 8: the '00000000-<tag>-...' family is 106 hand-authored placeholders declared in input/bldg1_enhancements.ttl since its first commit, whose own header says 'UUIDs of the form 00000000-XXXX-... are PLACEHOLDERS'. 36 are still writing; 70 stop dead at 2026-09-16 17:22:39. AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS A DUPLICATE: all 70 frozen streams belong to sensors carrying a SECOND, live timeseries reference, and all 36 live ones are their sensor's only reference. Graph-wide, sensors with more than one timeseries reference number exactly 70, all with n=2 -- precisely this set. THAT IS BUG-531's LIVE SET, now measured at 70 rather than its recorded 77, and every duplicate is a dead synth stream being merged into a live twin's statistics. ONE MORE CLAIM OF CAVEAT-903 IS FALSE: 'an undeclared stream is invisible to every check' -- orchestrator/services/sensor_silence.py run today returns declared=3543 probed=3543 reporting=3473 silent=70 never=0 not_probed=0, and NAMES all 70.
Root_Cause: ONE PREDICATE THE LINKER CANNOT SEE, and it is the same class as BUG-481. scripts/link_unlinked_sensors.py line 139 selects candidates with `FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?p ref:hasExternalReference ?r . ?r ref:hasTimeseriesId ?u }`, but input/bldg1_enhancements.ttl links its placeholders with `ashrae:hasExternalReference`. The graph does not bridge the two in that direction -- joining the 00000000- family under ref: returns 0 and under ashrae: returns 106 -- so the script concluded that 70 ALREADY-LINKED points were unlinked and wrote each a second link (69 into input/bldg1_sensor_links.ttl, the 70th, Water Main Flow, into input/bldg1_timeseries_extension.ttl). The 2026-09-16 17:22:39 freeze is the publisher being repointed onto those new links: input/bldg1_extended_narrow_uuids.json went from 106 synth entries to 36 between ccdce42 (09-10) and a538bf6 (09-18), and the 70 dropped are exactly the dual-referenced ones. plant_data's 44 orphans are a DIFFERENT and older event -- 30 dead at 2026-08-26 13:36 (the CAVEAT-361 instant) and 14 at 2026-09-28 23:45, in no TTL and no publish map: superseded generator seeds.
Fix_Approach: RETIRE, NOT DECLARE -- which is the opposite of what CAVEAT-903's framing implies, because declaring is what already happened, twice, and the duplicate IS the defect. Delete the 70 superseded `ashrae:hasExternalReference` blocks from input/bldg1_enhancements.ttl (those whose ref:hasTimeseriesId is one of the 70 frozen uuids) and KEEP the 36 whose synth reference is their sensor's only link. No new triples anywhere. NOT A DATA DECISION: every one of the 70 sensors keeps a live stream already declared and already published, so nothing loses coverage. Mechanically all 106 blocks are terminal (`] .`, zero `] ;`), so each retirement deletes a five-line block and changes the preceding `;` to `.` -- about 350 lines of 1,463 -- and because the uploader PUTs the whole named graph the references are removed rather than shadowed. WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT TIDYING: it closes BUG-531's entire live set at once, so the SQL lane stops merging a series that ended on 2026-09-16 into the statistics of its live twin. NOT RUN: input/ is the active building and ttl_uploader would write the graph on the next boot, which is a store write this agent does not own. DO NOT DECLARE THE 48 GENUINE ORPHANS (44 plant_data, 2 occupancy, 1 light, 1 noise): the building would claim 48 sensors that last wrote on 2026-08-26 / 09-16 / 09-28 and never will again -- 48 manufactured permanent silence findings. THE ONE REAL OWNER DECISION is whether to delete those orphans' ~380k rows from MySQL; proposed, not run. If the owner would rather not delete, the cheap alternative is a store-side check that fails when a table holds a uuid the graph does not declare -- the direction scripts/reconcile_watched_and_fed.py does not cover, and the one that would have caught all 48 on the day they appeared.
Verification:
MEASURED BY A SUB-AGENT OF THIS SESSION, NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY THE AGENT FILING IT. Stated plainly because a figure restated at one remove reads like a second confirmation and is not one. Graph: COUNT(DISTINCT ?u) over ref:hasTimeseriesId + ref:storedAt against repository `bldg` from the host -- distinct SUBJECTS and distinct uuids throughout, never triple counts. The ashrae:/ref: split confirmed by running the same join under each predicate (0 vs 106). GRAPH: sensors by distinct timeseries ids went {1: 3473, 2: 71} -> {1: 3544, 2: 0}.
THE TWO COUNTS OF 70+1 ARE THE SAME 71, CUT DIFFERENTLY, and it is worth writing down because either split alone looks like a discrepancy. BUG-1143 splits on the uuid shape: 70 carry a `00000000-` placeholder, and `feed_ahu_runtime_floor5` carries two ordinary uuid5s. I split on provenance: 70 appear in `bldg1_sensor_links.ttl`, and `Water_Flow_Sensor_Main` does not. Each split names a different 71st because each names a different 70. Both total 71; all 71 are retired. BUG-1143's advice to RE-COUNT rather than quote the old figure of 77 is exactly right and is why the number moved.

Title: LANDMINE: scripts/generate_publish_map.py would silence the 36 streams it publishes -- and the other 1,050 it would delete were already inert
Description: The narrow publish map on disk is NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE BY ITS OWN GENERATOR. `python scripts/generate_publish_map.py --dry-run` reports '32 sensor(s) mapped ... 2511 excluded': it would write 32 entries and delete 1,086, among them the 36 synth streams that are still publishing. Two causes compounding. (1) Its _QUERY uses `ref:hasExternalReference` and so sees ZERO of the 106 sensors that input/bldg1_enhancements.ttl links with `ashrae:hasExternalReference` -- the same predicate blindness as BUG-1141 and BUG-481. (2) Its `_already_published` guard now excludes 2,511 uuids that the narrow map has since absorbed, so the very points it should emit are the ones it skips. Nobody has run it since the map was last hand-extended, so the damage is latent rather than done.
Root_Cause:
A generator and its output drifted apart while both kept working. The map was extended by other means (a45bf47 rewrote it from 1,738 unbanded entries to 2,756 banded ones, per CAVEAT-1131) and the generator was never re-run, so nothing exercised it and nothing failed. A script that is never run cannot report that it has stopped agreeing with its own artefact.
=== MEASURED 2026-09-30, and it PARTLY shares BUG-531's cause but NOT mostly ===
`generate_publish_map.py` carries the same predicate blindness, at lines 79 and 96: both its queries traverse `?sensor ref:hasExternalReference ?r` alone. Counting distinct uuids that also declare a `ref:storedAt`:
    visible via `ref:` only : 3,507
    visible via ANY predicate: 3,544
    blind spot               :    37
Those 37 are exactly the sole-reference points on `database1_synth`, declared with `ashrae:` in `bldg1_enhancements.ttl`, and 36 of the 37 are LIVE. So the script cannot see 36 working series, and the `?anyRefPred` fix applied to `link_unlinked_sensors.py` is needed here too.
**BUT 37 IS NOT 1,086, AND I AM NOT GOING TO PRETEND IT IS.** The dry run reports it would delete 1,086 of 1,118 entries, and predicate blindness accounts for 37 of them at most. The live maps hold 2,771 entries against 1,118 in the dry run's view, so the larger part of the loss is something else -- most likely the narrow-table registry filter or `_already_published` -- and it has NOT been diagnosed. Naming one cause for a number it cannot account for is how a landmine gets defused on paper and not in fact; today has already produced two of my own inferences that did not survive being measured.
STATUS UNCHANGED, and the advice stands: DO NOT RUN THIS SCRIPT. Fixing the predicate is necessary and demonstrably not sufficient.
