Title: BUG-531's live set is 71, not 70 and not 77 -- and the 71st is a different defect that BUG-1141's fix would not catch
Description: Independently re-counting BUG-1141's headline gave 71 where it says 70, so the difference was chased rather than rounded away, and it turned out to matter. Counting sensors with more than one distinct ref:hasTimeseriesId across ANY reference predicate: 71 sensors, every one with exactly n=2, against 3,473 with exactly one. Of those 71, SEVENTY hold a '00000000-' placeholder -- BUG-1141's set, and its figure is correct for what it describes. The seventy-first is feed_ahu_runtime_floor5, which carries two ordinary uuid5 references and no placeholder at all: 95dd12c6-f506-5c3f-a836-2ae38545f3bc, declared in input/bldg1_sensor_links.ttl and present in the narrow publish map, so live; and 0fa68f99-b446-5ea9-4813-96d9016cb6d9, declared in input/equipment_linkage.ttl and in no publish map, so dead. Same shape as the other 70 -- one live link and one stale one -- from a DIFFERENT pair of files. For the record, BUG-531 recorded this set as 77; both later counts are below that, so the figure has moved and should be re-counted rather than quoted.
Root_Cause: Two files declare a timeseries reference for the same point and neither knows about the other. The 70 come from the linker's predicate blindness (BUG-1141); this one does not, so it has its own cause, not yet traced. What the two share is the absence of any constraint saying a point has at most one timeseries reference -- nothing anywhere enforces that, which is why two independent mechanisms both produced it.
Fix_Approach: Fix it with the other 70 but as a SEPARATE edit, because BUG-1141's proposed change -- deleting ashrae:hasExternalReference blocks from input/bldg1_enhancements.ttl -- does not touch input/equipment_linkage.ttl and would leave BUG-531 at 1 rather than 0. Remove the dead 0fa68f99-... reference from input/equipment_linkage.ttl. NOT RUN: input/ is the active building and ttl_uploader would write the graph on the next boot. THE DURABLE FIX IS NEITHER EDIT: add a SHACL shape or a boot check asserting at most one ref:hasTimeseriesId per point, so the next mechanism to do this fails loudly on the day it does it instead of being found by a lane quietly averaging two series together. Two unrelated causes producing the same defect is the argument for a constraint rather than two more fixes.
Verification:
Measured directly against repository `bldg` from the host, this agent's own query, COUNT(DISTINCT ?u) per subject with HAVING(?n > 1) -- distinct uuids per distinct subject, so neither inference nor multi-typing can inflate it. Distribution returned n=1 for 3,473 sensors and n=2 for 71, with none higher; the 3,473 independently matches the reporting count the silence lane returned in BUG-1141, which is a useful cross-check between two unrelated instruments. The 70/71 split confirmed by grouping the uuids per sensor and partitioning on whether any is a '00000000-' placeholder: 70 yes, 1 no. File locations found by grepping input/ for each uuid. | FIXED 2026-09-30 as part of BUG-531, and verified against the graph rather than against the row that predicted it. `link_unlinked_sensors.py` filtered on `ref:hasExternalReference` alone while 71 points carried only `ashrae:` (or, for two, `brick:`), so all 71 looked unlinked and each was given a second series. The filter now binds `?anyRefPred` and all 71 dead duplicates are retired from `bldg1_enhancements.ttl` (70) and `equipment_linkage.ttl` (1). GRAPH: sensors by distinct timeseries ids went {1: 3473, 2: 71} -> {1: 3544, 2: 0}.
THE TWO COUNTS OF 70+1 ARE THE SAME 71, CUT DIFFERENTLY, and it is worth writing down because either split alone looks like a discrepancy. BUG-1143 splits on the uuid shape: 70 carry a `00000000-` placeholder, and `feed_ahu_runtime_floor5` carries two ordinary uuid5s. I split on provenance: 70 appear in `bldg1_sensor_links.ttl`, and `Water_Flow_Sensor_Main` does not. Each split names a different 71st because each names a different 70. Both total 71; all 71 are retired. BUG-1143's advice to RE-COUNT rather than quote the old figure of 77 is exactly right and is why the number moved.
Refs: BUG-531; BUG-1141; CAVEAT-903; V12-34; input/equipment_linkage.ttl; input/bldg1_sensor_links.ttl

Title: A new audit script opens a MySQL session without pinning its time zone
Description: tests/test_db_sessions_pin_utc.py::test_every_mysql_session_pins_its_time_zone fails naming scripts/audit_declared_band_conformance.py:91. That file is UNTRACKED -- new work in flight while this test-integrity pass ran -- so this is reported, not fixed: scripts/ is another owner's area this session. Reproduces in isolation (2 failed, 2 passed on the four-test slice), so it is not a concurrency artefact.
Root_Cause: BUG-403 pinned every MySQL session to '+00:00' because sensor_data.Datetime is a TIMESTAMP that MySQL converts to the SESSION zone on read. A connection opened without init_command=UTC_SESSION_INIT reads the same rows an hour out under BST, and NOW() there does not mean what NOW() means to every other reader. The repo already learned this three times (BUG-518/519/538, all withdrawn after a default-zone hand measurement misled the fix).
Fix_Approach: Pass init_command=UTC_SESSION_INIT from shared/db_clock.py, which is what the failure message says. One line, and the guard test then passes.
Verification: pytest tests/test_db_sessions_pin_utc.py::test_every_mysql_session_pins_its_time_zone -q

Title: The building-literal guard fires on a '#' comment, because its prose detector only knows docstrings
Description: tests/test_sensor_linking.py::test_the_script_carries_no_building_literal fails with 'linker hardcodes bldg1'. Measured which line: exactly one, scripts/link_unlinked_sensors.py:142, and it is a comment -- '# ONLY the ashrae: form -- `bldg1_enhancements.ttl` authors them that way.' The other three mentions in that file are inside docstrings and are correctly excluded. So scripts/check_building_literals.py::_prose_lines treats a module or function docstring as prose but not a '#' comment inside a body, and the guard therefore reports a behavioural hardcoding where there is only an explanatory sentence. Reproduces in isolation. NOT FIXED HERE on purpose: the file is another owner's in-flight edit, the guard is enforcing design contract 3, and editing a guard test to suit yourself is lessons #153.
Root_Cause: A literal scanner that classifies prose by docstring only. A '#' comment is prose by every reasonable reading and by the intent of contract 3, which is about what the CODE resolves at runtime.
Fix_Approach: Two honest options and the owner should pick: (a) widen _prose_lines to treat a line whose first non-whitespace character is '#' as prose -- the narrow, behaviour-preserving change, and the same scanner is used by the literal guard across five trees so it would apply everywhere at once; or (b) reword the comment to name the file generically. (a) is better: a comment that cannot name a real file is a comment that explains less.
Verification: pytest tests/test_sensor_linking.py::test_the_script_carries_no_building_literal -q. The single offending line was isolated by running _prose_lines over the file and printing every non-prose line carrying a literal.
Refs: scripts/check_building_literals.py; scripts/link_unlinked_sensors.py; lessons #153; CLAUDE.md design contract 3

Title: Two source-reading tests failed mid-run and passed in isolation, because the tree moved under a 16-minute suite
Description: In the full -m unit run, test_a_topic_answers_only_questions_about_it::test_the_capability_lane_answers_only_from_subject_topics and test_absent_referent_metrics::test_the_gate_is_reached_for_measurement_questions_not_only_metrics_ones both failed at 15% and 17%, each asserting a substring of inspect.getsource(CapabilityAgent.answer). Both PASS in isolation minutes later. The source they were handed is a NEW thin wrapper -- answer() now calls _answer_unchecked() and adds a terse-status guard -- which means the logic they look for moved into the inner method. orchestrator/agents/capability_agent.py was being edited by another owner while the suite ran. This is lessons #101 exactly ('a long run PINS the tree; editing any .py mid-run makes every inspect.getsource test read the wrong lines'), observed rather than recalled.
Root_Cause: Two causes stacked. (1) Concurrent editing during a long run, which makes any getsource assertion unreliable and is not a defect in either test. (2) A real, pending consequence of that refactor: once it lands, both tests must read _answer_unchecked, because a substring assertion on a wrapper method is looking at the wrong function. Neither test is wrong today -- they will be the moment the wrapper is committed.
Fix_Approach: For the owner of the capability refactor: point both assertions at the method that now holds the logic, or better, read the whole class source rather than one method so a wrapper cannot hide it. For anyone measuring: a full-suite number taken while four agents edit orchestrator/ is not attributable, and a failure that does not reproduce in isolation should be checked against the clock before it is chased.
Verification: Full -m unit: 4 failed / 13,223 passed / 54 skipped / 3 xfailed / 0 xpassed in 16m28s. Re-run of the four failing ids alone: 2 failed, 2 passed -- these two are the two that passed.

Title: A whole FAMILY of boolean points held counts until 2026-09-16 -- and the root cause first written on this row was wrong (CORRECTED 2026-09-30)
Description:
THE SURVIVING SERIES IS THE WRONG QUANTITY FOR PART OF THE 71, and retiring the duplicate reference (BUG-531) did NOT fix this. That change removed the MERGE, not the mismatch, and it must not be claimed as fixed by that row.
`link_unlinked_sensors.py` maps a point's Brick class to a MODALITY and then generates values shaped like that modality. It maps `brick:Occupancy_Status` onto `occupancy`, so a booking-status point -- whose own rdfs:label reads 'Booking Status - Seminar Room 1.25 (available=0 / booked=1)' -- was seeded with an occupancy COUNT reaching 189.48, mean 9.38. A status is not a count, and the label says so in the graph.
MEASURED over the 71 formerly-duplicated pairs by comparing each side's range: 31 pairs disagree by more than 2x or are outright disjoint. The six Booking_Status points are the clearest (0..1 against 0..189); Door_Sensor_Main_Entrance reads 0..752.81 for a door.
WHY P2 AND NOT P1: it can no longer corrupt a DIFFERENT series' statistics, and every affected point is a demo-extension point rather than one of the building's real sensors. It is still a figure a reader would take at face value, and the label makes the contradiction legible to anyone who looks.
Root_Cause:
CORRECTED ON THE RECORD, 2026-09-30, by measurement rather than by re-reading. THE ORIGINAL ROOT CAUSE WAS WRONG. It said link_unlinked_sensors.py maps brick:Occupancy_Status onto the `occupancy` modality. It does not, and did not: config/saturation_modalities.yaml lists Occupancy_Status under the `occupancy_status` modality ONLY, and `occupancy` lists Occupancy_Count_Sensor, Occupancy_Sensor and Motion_Sensor. Running the script's own class_to_modality() returns Occupancy_Status -> occupancy_status, whose PROFILES entry carries `binary: 1`. THE LINKER WROTE 0/1, WHICH IS CORRECT. MEASURED, which is what settles it. e3d4ed39-...-2cbc14 (Booking_Status_Room1_25, and the surviving uuid IS the linker's uuid5 of the point IRI) splits into four eras by cadence and decimal signature: 2026-07-08..08-21, 96 rows/day, 900 s step, 0 decimals, values 0/1 -- that is the linker, --days 30 --step-min 15, and it is right; 08-22..08-25, 600 s step, 3 decimals, to 189.484 -- a different writer; 08-26..09-01, 900 s step, integers 0..30 -- the gap backfill under the `occupancy` count range; 09-02..09-16, ~1,000 rows/day, 0..30 -- the live publisher under an older publish map. From 2026-09-17 the same uuid is 0/1 again. THE REAL CAUSE IS THE DECLARED BAND, NOT THE MODALITY MAP, and it is already TTL-first: generate_publish_map.py takes lo/hi/dec from the ontology's own o:measuresQuantityKind -> o:typicalMin/Max on the most specific Brick class. The graph declares brick:Occupancy_Status -> o:BinaryState 0..1 dec=0 and brick:Occupancy_Count_Sensor -> o:OccupancyCount 0..30 dec=0. Regenerating the map on 2026-09-17 is what ended the defect. AND IT IS WIDER THAN SIX BOOKING POINTS. Every boolean point in occupancy_data shows the same era: EV_Charger_2_State_Sensor 53.2% of rows outside [0,1] (to 188.16), PIR_Lighting_Floor5 62.7% (to 186.68), PIR_Lighting_Floor0 61.2%, PIR_Lighting_Floor3 61.6%, IntrusionDetector_Floor1 57.1% (to 194.0), each of the six Booking_Status points ~54% -- and EVERY ONE of them stops at the same instant, 2026-09-16 14:35:13.
=== I WAS WRONG TWICE ON THIS ROW. BOTH CORRECTED 2026-09-30, BOTH RE-MEASURED ===

(1) THE ROOT CAUSE I WROTE IS FALSE. I said `link_unlinked_sensors.py` maps `brick:Occupancy_Status` onto the `occupancy` modality and so generated count-shaped values. It does not and did not. `config/saturation_modalities.yaml` lists `Occupancy_Status` under the **`occupancy_status`** modality, whose profile carries `binary: 1`. Running the script's own `class_to_modality()` returns `Occupancy_Status -> occupancy_status` and `Occupancy_Count_Sensor -> occupancy`. **The linker wrote 0/1, which is correct.** I inferred the mapping from the VALUES I saw instead of asking the mapper, which is lesson #133/#136 in a new costume: ask the running system before describing what it does.

(2) THE TENSE WAS WRONG, AND THAT MATTERS MORE. I reported the range as '0..189.48, mean 9.38' as though it described the point now. It describes the point's WHOLE HISTORY. Measured per day on the live uuid (e3d4ed39-e6f8-53ea-9b6c-5ca1dd2cbc14):
    days with any value > 1 : 26, first 2026-08-22, last 2026-09-16
    LAST 48 HOURS          : 1,088 rows, **0 above 1**, range 0.000..1.000
So this is a DATED BLOCK OF HISTORICAL DATA, not a live generator defect. The era ends at the instant the publish map was regenerated on 2026-09-16, and every boolean point in `occupancy_data` stops at the same moment.

WHAT THE REAL CAUSE WAS: the DECLARED BAND, on a path that is already TTL-first. `generate_publish_map.py` reads `lo/hi/dec` from `o:measuresQuantityKind -> o:typicalMin/Max`; the graph declares `Occupancy_Status -> o:BinaryState 0..1` and `Occupancy_Count_Sensor -> o:OccupancyCount 0..30`. Regenerating the map on 2026-09-16/17 is what ended the era. Attribution by cadence and decimal signature identifies at least four writers across the series' life, including a 600 s / 3-decimal era reaching 189.484 that is none of the suspects I named.

IT IS ALSO WIDER THAN THE SIX BOOKING POINTS: PIR_Lighting_Floor5 62.7% of rows out of band, IntrusionDetector_Floor1 57.1% (to 194.0), EV_Charger_2_State_Sensor 53.2% -- all ending at the same instant.

REVISED SEVERITY AND DISPOSITION: P2 -> P3. Nothing is being written wrongly now; a guard (`scripts/audit_status_point_bands.py`, ontology-driven, 249 status points, 0 violations) prevents a repeat. **Recommendation: do NOT re-seed.** ~180,000 rows across ~29 boolean points with one clean era boundary — and a dated block of visibly-wrong generated data is more honest than one silently rewritten. The owner decides; the cost is recorded here so the decision is informed rather than implied.
Fix_Approach: SPLIT INTO WHAT IS FIXED GOING FORWARD AND WHAT NEEDS THE OWNER. FIXED GOING FORWARD -- and it was already fixed before this row was written, by the 2026-09-17 publish-map regeneration, which this row did not know. MEASURED 2026-09-30: across all 2,511 points that declare a band, ZERO are being written outside it in the last 48 hours (scratchpad/probe_live_band_breaches.py). ADDED, because the thing that was missing was not a fix but a GUARD: scripts/audit_status_point_bands.py. It asks the ontology, not the point's name -- a point is boolean when its class reaches brick:Status, brick:Alarm or brick:Command through rdfs:subClassOf*, which is a closure and not a `*_Status` regex (design contract #3: a name list is a building literal one level down). THE RULE IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL AND THAT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: Status implies boolean, but Sensor does NOT imply continuous -- brick:Contact_Sensor is a Sensor and reads 0/1, and 479 points on this building are exactly that, so the converse rule would have reported 479 false positives on its first run and been switched off by its second. Live result today: 249 declared status points, all with a boolean band, 0 violations. NEEDS A DATA MIGRATION THE OWNER MUST AUTHORISE -- NOT DONE, NOTHING WRITTEN. COSTED: ~650,937 rows in occupancy_data sit outside their declared band, of which the boolean family is roughly 180,000 across ~29 points (six Booking_Status, five PIR_Lighting, EV charger and intrusion states, and the rest of the 0..1 band in that table); equipment_data holds a further 480,167 (40.0%) and iaq_data 215,197 (34.2%), though those are not all quantity errors. THE WORK: (1) pick the era boundary per uuid -- for this family it is one instant, 2026-09-16 14:35:13, which makes the predicate trivial and auditable; (2) decide DELETE versus REGENERATE. Deleting leaves a two-month hole that every 'compare this month with last' question falls into; regenerating means re-running the fixed generator over the era, which is ~30 minutes of writes for the boolean family and needs the publisher stopped first so two writers are not in the table at once. (3) Either way, RECORD THAT IT HAPPENED -- CAVEAT-1131 already says rewriting history to match a later model destroys the evidence that the disagreement existed, so the era and the decision belong in a provenance record before a single row moves. ESTIMATE: half a day including the backup and a subject-level before/after diff; the risk is not the SQL, it is that a partial pass leaves two models in one series again. RECOMMENDATION: do not re-seed. The band audit already reports the era, the guard now prevents a repeat, and a generated history that is visibly wrong in a dated block is more honest than one silently rewritten to look right.
Verification: FOUR READ-ONLY PROBES, session pinned '+00:00' and the zone printed each time; nothing was written to any store. scratchpad/probe_1150a.py -- per-uuid history, last-6h split, and the count of rows above 1 with its span: for all six Booking_Status points the >1 rows span 2026-08-22 to 2026-09-16 14:35 and the last 6 hours are 0/1 only, distinct=2. scratchpad/probe_1150b.py -- attribution by cadence and decimal signature, which is what identifies the writer: 900s/0dp, 600s/3dp, 900s/0dp-to-30, ~75s/0dp. scratchpad/probe_live_band_breaches.py -- 2,511 banded points, ZERO breaching in the last 48 hours. scripts/audit_declared_band_conformance.py (existing, run not edited) -- the family-wide view and the shared 2026-09-16 14:35:13 end. Graph queries: the six points are typed brick:Occupancy_Status and inferred brick:Status, never brick:Sensor; the surviving uuids equal uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, <point IRI>), i.e. the linker's. tests/test_status_points_are_generated_as_booleans.py -- 15 tests, all passing, including the live-marked run against the real graph and publish maps. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that every point's declared band is the RIGHT quantity. It establishes that every point is written inside the band its ontology declares. Door_Sensor_Main_Entrance is inside its declared 0..100 and is still the wrong quantity -- see BUG-1161.
Refs: BUG-531; CAVEAT-903; BUG-1130; BUG-1139; BUG-1161; CAVEAT-1161; CAVEAT-1131; scripts/audit_status_point_bands.py; tests/test_status_points_are_generated_as_booleans.py; BUG-1130; BUG-1139; BUG-1161

Title: LLM_TIMEOUT_S=180 did not fire on a 3,239-second call: no turn has an effective upper bound
Description:
Regression-gate case 8/51 took 3,412 s end to end and ANSWERED NORMALLY. The orchestrator log localises the wait to ONE HTTP call:
    11:06:33,431  dialogue_agent: 'Calling LLM for intent detection'
    12:00:32,887  httpx: POST host.docker.internal:11434/api/generate  200 OK
    12:00:33,014  dialogue_agent: 'LLM Response received (length: 385 chars)'
**3,239 s inside one request. No TimeoutError. No retry line. No degraded marker.** `LLM_TIMEOUT_S` is present in the container environment and resolves to 180.0 inside the running process (checked with importlib, not from .env), and `llm_manager.generate` wraps `_generate_once` in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=LLM_TIMEOUT_S)`. Both classifier paths reach it: `_classify_llm_call` -> `generate_structured` -> `self.generate`.
WHY THIS IS P1 RATHER THAN A LATENCY CURIOSITY: a configured bound that does not bind means NO TURN IN THIS SYSTEM HAS AN UPPER BOUND. A 57-minute answer in front of an audience is a demo-stopping event and it happened on an ordinary question ('Find me a quiet, well-lit room on floor 3...'). It also makes every latency figure in this repo unfalsifiable, which is CAVEAT-500's complaint one level down, and it inflates any harness's wall clock without moving its pass rate -- so a green run says nothing about whether the system is usable.
Root_Cause:
UNDETERMINED, and deliberately recorded as undetermined rather than guessed. What is ESTABLISHED by measurement:
  * NOT runaway generation (CAVEAT-727): the completion is 385 CHARACTERS, and     there were zero `empty_completion` / `LLM-DEGRADED` / `retry backoff` lines     in the surrounding 90 minutes.
  * NOT many calls or a retry storm: exactly one POST to /api/generate.
  * NOT machine sleep: Kernel-Power shows the only suspend at 12:06:49-12:07:02     (13 s), well AFTER the window.
  * NOT a host-wide freeze: the data-publisher wrote rows in 55 of the 75     minutes spanning the window, with its usual scattered single-minute gaps     and no 54-minute hole. The machine was working the whole time.
  * NOT CPU starvation, which CAVEAT-942 called 'the obvious candidate': the     unit suite had finished (13,228 pass, exit 0) and the ONLY workload was the     gate, which was itself blocked on this call.
  * NOT a missing async path: `langchain_ollama` 0.2.3 defines `_agenerate` and     `_astream` natively on `OllamaLLM`, so the call is genuinely awaited and a     `wait_for` cancellation should be deliverable.
  * Model state was healthy: `/api/ps` shows gpt-oss:20b fully resident     (size_vram 12,748,796,722, no CPU spill), num_ctx 16384,     OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1.
So a timer that should have fired at 180 s did not, on a live async path, on a host that was demonstrably running. I could not close that gap from the client side and am not going to assert a mechanism I have not shown.
=== LIKELY SUPERSEDED BY BUG-1194, 2026-09-30 ===
Two hours after writing this row I found the orchestrator at **40.02 GiB and 3210% CPU**, unresponsive, with Docker still reporting `healthy` from a frozen check. After a restart: 1.326 GiB, 6.43%. An event loop on a process in that state may not reach its timer callbacks at all, which would explain a 180 s `wait_for` failing to fire without anything being wrong with the timeout code or with Ollama. **Re-test this row against a HEALTHY process before spending anything on the client/transport theory** -- I eliminated a lot of candidates here and the one I could not see was the state of the process doing the eliminating. The 40 GiB was measured after the wedge, not during this call, so the link is a hypothesis and not yet a finding.
Fix_Approach:
TWO THINGS, and only the first is a fix.
1. INSTRUMENT IT so the next occurrence is diagnosable rather than reconstructed: log the elapsed time of every LLM call at WARNING above a threshold; set an explicit per-request timeout on the ollama/httpx client itself rather than relying solely on `asyncio.wait_for`, because a transport deadline cannot be defeated by anything the event loop does; and capture the host Ollama server log with OLLAMA_DEBUG=1 across a gate run, since only that side can account for the 54 minutes.
2. Then diagnose. Reproducing needs a gate-length run, so this is not a five-minute job and should not be attempted by guessing at the timeout code.
NOT ATTEMPTED IN THIS SESSION: a live regression gate was mid-run and this touches the call path every lane uses. Changing it under a running measurement would invalidate the measurement and hide the defect.
=== A SECOND DEADLINE, IN A DIFFERENT PLACE, 2026-09-30 ===
The root cause is STILL UNDETERMINED and this row is not claimed as diagnosed. What has changed is that `asyncio.wait_for` is no longer the only thing between a turn and forever, plus one new piece of evidence that makes the loop-starvation explanation much harder to avoid.
NEW EVIDENCE, and it is arithmetic on values already in the repo: `.env` sets WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_S=0, and `shared/config.py` derives `max(120, int(LLM_TIMEOUT_S)*2 + 60)` = 420 s at LLM_TIMEOUT_S=180 -- confirmed in the running process (`settings.WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_S` reads 420.0). `_orchestrator.execute` wraps `self.graph.ainvoke(state)` in `asyncio.wait_for(timeout=420)`. Case 8 ran 3,412 s END TO END AND ANSWERED NORMALLY, so THE 420 s DEADLINE DID NOT FIRE EITHER. Two independent deadlines, written in the same idiom, nested one inside the other, both silent on the same turn. One `wait_for` bug is possible; two is not. The economical reading is the one BUG-1194 offers -- a loop that was not running its timer callbacks -- and it is now a good deal more than a guess, though still not a measurement of that turn.
THE FIX: a transport-level deadline on the HTTP client, which does not depend on our `wait_for` at all.
  * `_transport_timeout_s()` = LLM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_S, else LLM_TIMEOUT_S * 1.5 + 15 (285 s at the default). DELIBERATELY LONGER than LLM_TIMEOUT_S so that on a healthy loop `wait_for` still fires first and every existing retry path behaves byte-for-byte as before. This layer only acts when that one did not.
  * `_ollama_client_kwargs()` -> `OllamaLLM(client_kwargs={"timeout": httpx.Timeout(285, connect=10)})`. Connect is short because a refused model server is a fast failure; the long budget belongs to the READ, which is where the 54 minutes of silence happened.
  * `ChatOpenAI(timeout=...)` on all three hosted clients too. RESIDUAL, stated: the OpenAI SDK retries twice on its own, so that path's worst case is three transport timeouts rather than one. Left alone because it is not the active provider and the change is unmeasurable from here.
  * If a future langchain-ollama drops `client_kwargs`, `_initialize_ollama` logs a WARNING naming this defect rather than losing the protection silently, and a test asserts the field still exists.
  * `_is_retryable` and `classify_llm_error` now match httpx timeout exceptions BY TYPE NAME. `str(httpx.ReadTimeout())` is frequently the EMPTY STRING, and every classifier in the module works on `str(error).lower()` -- so without this a transport timeout would have been bucketed "other" and refused a retry, i.e. the code handling the fix would have mislabelled it.
INSTRUMENTATION, because the 3,239 s was recovered by subtracting two log timestamps by hand: every call through `generate` now measures itself. Over LLM_SLOW_CALL_WARN_S (default 60 s) it logs at WARNING with the elapsed time, the prompt length and the completion length; and when the elapsed time EXCEEDS LLM_TIMEOUT_S it appends "OVERRAN LLM_TIMEOUT_S=180s WITHOUT FIRING", which is the entire diagnosis in one line. Failures and timeouts log their elapsed time too.
HONEST LIMIT, because the alternative is a false sense of cover: httpx implements its timeouts with anyio, which on the asyncio backend is STILL a loop timer. This catches a silent provider on a HEALTHY loop -- the shape actually observed, since the connection was open and nothing arrived for 54 minutes -- and it does NOT survive a fully starved loop. The container memory ceiling added under BUG-1194 is what covers that case.
Tests: tests/test_llm_transport_deadline.py (14).
Verification:
=== MEASURED END TO END 2026-09-30, INSIDE THE RUNNING CONTAINER ===
The premise first, because the reason this hole existed is that nobody had looked: `ollama` 0.6.3's `BaseClient.__init__` types `timeout` as `Any` DEFAULTING TO None and passes it straight to httpx. Out of the box an Ollama request has NO TRANSPORT TIMEOUT AT ALL. `langchain_ollama` 0.2.3 carries a `client_kwargs` field and does `Client(host=..., **client_kwargs)` / `AsyncClient(...)`, so a timeout set there reaches both. Both facts are asserted by tests, so a package upgrade that changes either one fails rather than silently removing the cover.
THE PROOF: a socket bound inside the container that ACCEPTS the connection and never writes a byte -- BUG-1191's exact shape, since httpx logs `200 OK` when the response HEADERS arrive and on the day that was minute 54. The same `OllamaLLM(...).ainvoke("hello")` was pointed at it twice, with LLM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_S=12 so the test is short:
    WITHOUT client_kwargs: STILL HANGING at 40.0 s (the harness's own bound; a real turn has none)
    WITH    client_kwargs: gave up after 12.0 s -- ReadTimeout('')
Note the empty message on that exception, confirmed on the real object rather than a constructed one. It is precisely why the classifiers now match by type name.
LIVE after the orchestrator was recreated at 14:17:10Z: the boot log reads `Ollama options: keep_alive=30m num_ctx=16384 num_predict=8192 transport_timeout=285s`, and one ordinary question ("How many temperature sensors are there in the building?") answered HTTP 200 in 16.552 s with a correct counted answer -- so the new client kwarg changes nothing on the normal path.
NOT CLAIMED: that this explains or fixes the 3,239 s call. It does not. It means a repeat of it is bounded at 285 s by a mechanism that does not share `wait_for`'s failure mode, and that the next one will say its own elapsed time at WARNING instead of having to be reconstructed.
NOT YET SEEN IN PRODUCTION: no live call has hit the 285 s deadline, because none has come close since. Status is FIXED on the measurement above, not VERIFIED_LIVE on a production timeout.

Title: scripts/generate_publisher_map.py raises AttributeError on this building's plant map, so the 2,756-entry narrow map is not reproducible either
Description: `sibling_uuids()` globs every *_publish_map.json and iterates `data.values()`, calling `(entry or {}).get('uuid')` on each. bldg1_plant_publish_map.json's top-level values are the string 'plant_data' and a list, so the call raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'` outside the try that wraps json.loads. Found while fixing BUG-1142, which is the same defect in the mirror-image guard of the sibling script -- there it failed SILENTLY (collected 0 uuids), here it fails LOUDLY.
Root_Cause: Both guards assume a publish map is a flat mapping of uuid -> entry. Two of this building's four are not: the plant map nests points under groups[*].roles[*] and the waste map under bins[*].roles[*]. NOT DONE HERE: fixing it changes what the narrow map's generator claims, and that generator writes the 2,756-entry map, so the change wants its own before/after dry run rather than riding along with BUG-1142's.
Verification: MEASURED: importing sibling_uuids and calling it against input/ raises AttributeError. A deep walk of the two maps finds 44 and 24 uuids that the shallow walk finds 0 of. Their overlap with the current narrow publish map is 0, so no double-write exists today -- the defect is that the generator cannot run, not that its output is wrong.

Title: 245 of the narrow publish map's 2,756 points carry no declared band and generate on the publisher's column default
Description: input/bldg1_narrow_publish_map.json has two entry shapes: 2,511 with lo/hi/dec and 245 without. The 245 are not a predicate problem -- measured, 0 of them are in the reference-predicate blind spot.
