Title: A failed turn streamed the user's own question back as the assistant's answer
Description: On /v1/chat/completions with stream=true -- the branch Open WebUI uses BY DEFAULT, so the one real users run -- any exception inside the workflow produced HTTP 200, a normal SSE body, finish_reason "stop", data: [DONE], and an answer consisting of THE USER'S OWN QUESTION. Nothing in the body said the turn had failed. The non-streamed branch of the same endpoint returned "I wasn't able to process your request. Could you try rephrasing your question?" for the identical failure. MEASURED against the real WorkflowOrchestrator on a graph that raises: execute() returned the apology, stream_execute() produced 'What is the temperature in room 7.42?' -- the question that had just been asked. This is the worst shape a failure can take here: a confident-looking 200 that a grader scores, a user reads, and a harness counts as an answer.
Root_Cause: TWO facts that are each harmless alone. (1) main.py appends the current user turn to state.messages BEFORE handing the state to the workflow, so messages[-1] is the USER's message until a lane appends an answer. (2) stream_execute catches a workflow exception and yields {"error": <str>, "state": state} -- where `state` is the PRE-graph state. main.py's step reconstruction then picks that ConversationState (the "error" value is a str, so the loop skips it), and read the answer as final_state.messages[-1].content. execute() does not have the same shape because its handler APPENDS an assistant message before returning.
Fix_Approach: Read the last ASSISTANT message, never simply the last message: _assistant_answer(state, error=...) in main.py, used by BOTH branches so they cannot drift. Falls back to the same wording execute() uses, and when stream_execute reported an error string it is mapped through WorkflowOrchestrator._user_friendly_error so a timeout/rate-limit/connection failure reads the same on both paths. The error is also logged at ERROR, which it was not. Fixing the EXTRACTION rather than that one error path also covers any future route that ends without an answer.
Verification: REPRODUCED before the fix and green after: test_a_workflow_error_is_not_streamed_as_the_users_own_question and test_a_workflow_error_reads_the_same_on_both_paths in tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py (12 tests, 6 of them red before the change). The failing-orchestrator fake in that file mirrors the REAL stream_execute handler, which was driven directly against a raising graph to establish the shape rather than assumed. Regression: 186 tests across the nine existing files that touch /v1/chat/completions pass unchanged. || NOT DEPLOYED: the fix is in the source tree only. The orchestrator runs uvicorn WITHOUT --reload (checked: docker inspect Config.Cmd), so the container is still on the pre-fix code and a restart is owed before any live re-verification. I was asked not to restart it. || NOT SEEN LIVE: seven live questions on 2026-09-30 all succeeded, so this path was never entered. Its frequency in production is UNKNOWN -- what is established is the shape, not the rate.
Refs: orchestrator/main.py (openai_chat_completions streaming branch, _assistant_answer); orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py (stream_execute, execute, _user_friendly_error); tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py; CAVEAT-656

Title: ontosage_llm_degraded and ontosage_evidence_record rode only the non-streamed body, so real users' turns carried neither
Description: MEASURED LIVE on the running stack, 7 questions asked both ways: the non-streamed body carried ontosage_evidence_record, ontosage_llm_degraded, ontosage_intent, ontosage_route and ontosage_plan_trace; the streamed final chunk carried only the last three, on all 7. ontosage_llm_degraded is how a grader learns not to score an outage's apology as behaviour (V5-BUG-177), and ontosage_evidence_record is the turn's statement of what it rests on (V6-T02). Open WebUI streams by default, so both were absent from exactly the turns real users produce -- the endpoint whose comment says it is 'the endpoint Open WebUI and every OpenAI-compatible client actually use' was the one missing them.
Root_Cause: The two fields were added to the non-streamed return dict in separate earlier changes (V5-BUG-177, V6-T02). The streaming branch's final chunk was extended later (TODO-657, W04, W6-02) with intent/route/plan_trace and nobody re-derived the full set. Two places holding their own answer to 'what does a turn report' -- the same shape as the V12-08..11 family.
Fix_Approach: Add both to the streaming final chunk's `extra`, at the TOP level of the chunk exactly as the other three ride, which an OpenAI client ignores. Pinned by a SET COMPARISON, not a list of names: the test asserts the non-streamed body's ontosage_* keys are a SUBSET of the streamed final chunk's, so the next field added to one and not the other fails it.
Verification: test_the_streamed_final_chunk_carries_the_same_ontosage_fields_as_the_body and test_the_streamed_evidence_record_is_the_same_record in tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py, both red before the change. Live evidence of the gap: scratchpad/caveat656_live.json (5 questions) and caveat656_coldcold.json (2), 'fields only on the NON-STREAMED body: [ontosage_evidence_record, ontosage_llm_degraded]' on 7 of 7. || NOT DEPLOYED: the fix is in the source tree only. The orchestrator runs uvicorn WITHOUT --reload (checked: docker inspect Config.Cmd), so the container is still on the pre-fix code and a restart is owed before any live re-verification. I was asked not to restart it.
Refs: orchestrator/main.py (openai_chat_completions streaming branch, _assistant_answer); orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py (stream_execute, execute, _user_friendly_error); tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py; CAVEAT-656; TODO-657; V6-T02; V5-BUG-177

Title: An exception mid-stream truncated the SSE body with no error and no [DONE]
Description: The streaming generator had no exception handler, and the endpoint's own try/except cannot help it: the generator body runs AFTER the handler returned its StreamingResponse. Anything raising inside it therefore ended the response by simply stopping -- no error chunk, no finish_reason, no data: [DONE] -- and a client renders whatever arrived as a finished answer. Worse, the Postgres transcript write sat UNGUARDED between the assembled answer and the first content chunk, so a store being down cost the reader THE WHOLE ANSWER, not just the transcript. Demonstrated: with save_message raising, the request aborted after '</details>' having streamed no answer at all. The dead handler _unused_oai_chat_completions in the same file has had the error chunk since it was written; the live one never got it.
Root_Cause: A StreamingResponse's generator is outside the request handler's exception scope, which is easy to miss because the `return StreamingResponse(...)` sits inside the try. And the transcript write was ordered before the content chunks for no reason other than where it was pasted.
Fix_Approach: Wrap event_generator in guarded_event_generator, which on any exception emits an apology content chunk, a finish_reason chunk carrying ontosage_stream_error (so a grader can DROP the row rather than score an apology) and [DONE]. CancelledError is re-raised untouched -- a client that went away is not an error to report. sse_chunk moved out of event_generator so the handler can frame a chunk. Separately, the transcript write is now best-effort: a store being down may not withhold a computed answer.
Verification: test_a_generator_level_exception_is_surfaced_not_truncated and test_a_persistence_failure_does_not_swallow_the_answer in tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py. Before the change the second one aborted the ASGI response with the raw RuntimeError; after it the full answer streams and [DONE] arrives. || NOT DEPLOYED: the fix is in the source tree only. The orchestrator runs uvicorn WITHOUT --reload (checked: docker inspect Config.Cmd), so the container is still on the pre-fix code and a restart is owed before any live re-verification. I was asked not to restart it.
Refs: orchestrator/main.py (openai_chat_completions streaming branch, _assistant_answer); orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py (stream_execute, execute, _user_friendly_error); tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py; CAVEAT-656

Title: /chat/stream shares BUG-1211 exactly: a failed turn streams the user's own question back as the answer
Description:
BUG-1211 was found on `/v1/chat/completions` and fixed there. **The same defect was live in `/chat/stream` and the fix did not reach it**, because it had been pinned to the endpoint where it was noticed rather than to the condition that produces it.
THE CONDITION, and it is what makes this a class rather than an incident: an endpoint is affected when it (a) drives `orchestrator.stream_execute` and (b) ships `state.messages[-1]` as the answer. `main.py` appends the user turn to `state.messages` BEFORE the graph runs, and `stream_execute` reports failure as `{'error': ..., 'state': <PRE-GRAPH state>}` -- so on a raising graph `messages[-1]` is the USER'S OWN QUESTION, returned at HTTP 200 with `finish_reason: 'stop'` and nothing indicating failure.
Checked all three answer-shipping routes rather than assuming:
  /v1/chat/completions (streaming)    stream_execute + messages[-1]  ->  FIXED (BUG-1211)
  /chat/stream         line 3517      stream_execute + messages[-1]  ->  **WAS STILL LIVE**
  /chat                line 2759      execute() + messages[-1]       ->  NOT affected; `execute()` appends an assistant message even on failure
WHY IT MATTERS FOR A USER-FACING RELEASE: a user asks a question, the workflow raises, and they are shown their own question as the answer with no error. That is the precise failure design contract #4 forbids -- a plausible-looking response that is not grounded in anything.
Root_Cause: A fix applied at the SITE rather than at the CONDITION. The `/v1` work correctly introduced `_assistant_answer` (read the last ASSISTANT message) and correctly wired both `/v1` branches to it, but nothing looked for the other consumers of `stream_execute`. There were two, in the same file.
Fix_Approach:
`/chat/stream` now calls `_assistant_answer(final_state)`. `/chat` is left calling `execute()` but now selects the last ASSISTANT entry explicitly rather than the last entry -- not a bug fix there, but it means all three sites share ONE rule instead of two of them depending on a precondition a reader has to go and verify. It keeps `assistant_entry.metadata`, which is why it does not use `_assistant_answer` itself.
PINNED BY CONDITION, NOT BY SITE: `tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py::test_every_streaming_endpoint_reads_the_last_ASSISTANT_message` parses the AST and fails on ANY site that ships `messages[-1]` as an answer. **It found the `/chat` site on its first run**, which is how I learned the third route existed -- the instrument found it, not the reading.
Verification:
13/13 pass in `tests/test_the_streaming_branch_is_the_one_users_get.py`, including the new AST test and the 12 from the `/v1` work. `flake8 --select=F821,F823` clean; `orchestrator/main.py` parses.
NOT VERIFIED LIVE: the orchestrator runs uvicorn with no `--reload`, so none of this is in the running container. A restart is owed and is deliberately deferred -- a 60-question tail-N measurement is mid-flight and restarting would corrupt it.

Title: The local LLM client had no transport timeout at all, so one asyncio deadline was the only thing between a turn and forever
Description:
Split out of BUG-1191, which is about a deadline that did not FIRE. This is about a deadline that did not EXIST.
MEASURED inside the running container against the installed packages, not inferred from documentation:
    ollama 0.6.3  BaseClient.__init__(self, client, host=None, *, follow_redirects=True, timeout: Any = None, ...)
    -> httpx.Client(base_url=..., timeout=None, ...)
`timeout=None` in httpx means NO TIMEOUT ON ANY PHASE. So every local LLM call this system has ever made was protected by exactly one thing: the `asyncio.wait_for(LLM_TIMEOUT_S)` in `llm_manager.generate`. On 2026-09-30 that one thing did not fire and a call ran 3,239 s.
DEMONSTRATED, not argued -- a socket that accepts the TCP connection and never writes a byte, which is BUG-1191's exact observed shape (httpx logs `200 OK` when response HEADERS arrive, and on the day that was minute 54):
    WITHOUT client_kwargs: still hanging at 40.0 s
    WITH    client_kwargs: ReadTimeout('') at 12.0 s
WHY IT IS P1 AND NOT HYGIENE: 'no turn has an upper bound' is a demo-stopping property in front of real users, and a single point of failure for a bound is not a bound. It also makes every latency figure in this repo unfalsifiable, which is CAVEAT-500 one level down.
A SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING IT: `str(httpx.ReadTimeout())` is frequently the EMPTY STRING, and `_is_retryable` / `classify_llm_error` both work on `str(error).lower()`. A transport timeout would therefore have been classified "other" and refused a retry -- the code handling the new deadline would have mislabelled it as an unknown permanent failure.
Root_Cause:
`langchain_ollama.OllamaLLM` builds its `Client`/`AsyncClient` from a `client_kwargs` dict that this repo never passed, and the underlying `ollama` client defaults `timeout` to None. Nothing was wrong with any code that was written; a default was accepted without being read. The same omission is in the three `ChatOpenAI` constructions, where the SDK's own 600 s default applied instead.
The deeper cause is the one worth keeping: a timeout was configured (LLM_TIMEOUT_S=180), present in the environment, resolvable in the process and wired into the call -- so every check anyone would think to make said the call was bounded. It was bounded in exactly one layer, and nobody had asked which.
Fix_Approach:
`_transport_timeout_s()` in `orchestrator/llm_manager.py`: LLM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_S if set, else LLM_TIMEOUT_S * 1.5 + 15 = 285 s at the default. Deliberately LONGER than LLM_TIMEOUT_S so `wait_for` still wins on a healthy loop and no existing retry path changes behaviour.
`_ollama_client_kwargs()` -> `client_kwargs={"timeout": httpx.Timeout(285, connect=10)}`, guarded by a check that the field still exists (a WARNING naming this row if a future release drops it) and by a test.
`timeout=` on all three `ChatOpenAI` clients. RESIDUAL: the OpenAI SDK retries twice itself, so that path's worst case is 3x the transport timeout; `wait_for` still bounds it on a healthy loop. Not the active provider, so left.
`_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_TYPES` matched by TYPE NAME in `_is_retryable` and `classify_llm_error`, because the message is empty.
Documented in `.env.example` with the measurement, so the next reader does not have to rediscover the None.
Verification:
The black-hole measurement above, run inside ontosage-orchestrator against the real installed packages: 40.0 s still hanging without, ReadTimeout('') at 12.0 s with.
LIVE: boot log `Ollama options: keep_alive=30m num_ctx=16384 num_predict=8192 transport_timeout=285s` after the recreate at 14:17:10Z; one ordinary question answered HTTP 200 in 16.552 s, so the normal path is unchanged.
tests/test_llm_transport_deadline.py, 14 cases. Two of them assert the PREMISE rather than the fix -- that ollama still defaults timeout to None and that OllamaLLM still exposes client_kwargs -- so a package upgrade that removes the cover fails a test instead of removing it silently.
NOT VERIFIED_LIVE: no production call has hit the 285 s deadline, because none has come near it since.
NOT CLAIMED: that this explains BUG-1191's 3,239 s. It bounds a repeat; it does not diagnose the original.

Title: A container health status freezes when the container's processes cannot run, and no healthcheck setting changes that
Description:
Recorded so that BUG-1194's healthcheck fix is not read as more than it is.
REPRODUCED 2026-09-30 on a throwaway container from the orchestrator image, carrying the NEW healthcheck (15s/10s/3, curl --max-time 8). It was healthy, then `docker pause`d at 14:03:02.3. For the next 2m22s of polling:
    Status = unchanged, FailingStreak = 0, and the newest entry in State.Health.Log stayed at 14:02:51.6 exit=0 "ok"
No new probe was ever recorded. The status simply stopped being about the present -- which is BUG-1194's frozen `healthy` exactly, produced on demand.
WHAT THE SHORTER INTERVAL ACTUALLY BUYS, measured in the same session on the same image with the app frozen by SIGSTOP but the container still able to run an exec: 60.6 s to `unhealthy` against 171 s for the old settings. So the new settings help at the EARLIER, RECOVERABLE stage -- a process that is alive and not answering -- and do nothing once the container can no longer run a process at all. Those are two different failures and only the first one is now caught quickly.
ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE REAL INCIDENT, stated so the reproduction is not over-sold: `docker ps` renders a paused container as `(Paused)`, which is a visible clue. The wedged orchestrator was NOT paused -- it was running and too starved to fork -- so it rendered as `Up 3 hours (healthy)` with no clue at all. The stale-status MECHANISM reproduces; the misleading rendering does not.
Root_Cause:
Docker's health monitor runs the probe as an exec INSIDE the container. When the container's processes cannot be scheduled -- paused, or, as on the day, on a host at 86% memory -- the exec never completes, so no result is recorded, so the last result stands. `docker ps` renders a stale PASS identically to a fresh one; there is no staleness in the rendering at all.
This is a property of where the probe runs, not of how it is configured. Any in-container probe has it.
Fix_Approach:
NOT FIXABLE by healthcheck configuration; mitigated from two other directions, both landed under BUG-1194.
1. The memory ceiling (mem_limit 8g, memswap_limit 8g). A container that dies at 8 GiB never reaches the state where it cannot run its own probe, and `exited (137)` with `OOMKilled=true` is a status that cannot go stale.
2. The watchdog's INFO line every 30 s. It runs in an OS thread, so it keeps writing for as long as the process exists at all. `docker logs --since 2m ontosage-orchestrator | grep watchdog` returning NOTHING is a positive wedge test that needs no exec, no /health and no healthcheck -- i.e. it cannot be defeated by the thing that defeats all three.
TRIAGE RULE, and it belongs in anyone's first two commands: never read `docker ps` health alone. `docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}} streak={{.State.Health.FailingStreak}}'` plus the NEWEST entry in State.Health.Log. Note that `(index .State.Health.Log 0)` is the OLDEST of the last five, not the newest -- the snippet in CLAUDE.md's debugging section uses index 0 and therefore reads the oldest retained check. Take the last element.
Verification: The pause experiment above (2m22s of unchanged status with a last check going arbitrarily stale) and the SIGSTOP experiment (60.6 s new vs 171 s old, with probe exit codes 28 vs -1). Both on throwaway containers from the live orchestrator image; the running service was not disturbed by either.

Title: A removed remediation step leaves its NUMBER behind, so the reader sees an empty list item
Description: Tail N (2026-09-30, 5 of 60 real survey questions, docs/phase0/tail_N_2026-09-30_read.md): 'is there a separate mailroom for large packages' and four others returned the honest decline followed by a numbered onboarding block whose item 1 rendered EMPTY -- 'You can add it -- no code changes needed: 1. 2. Point it at its readings ...'. A numbered list whose first item is blank is a defect for every reader, whatever their role.
Root_Cause: grounding_guard.strip_schema_remediation removes a matching CLAUSE. When the list is laid out one step per line it drops the whole line and the survivors keep their original numbers, so a three-step list becomes '2.' and '3.'. When the list has been reflowed onto one line the clause is a SENTENCE, and _SENTENCE_SPLIT_RE splits '... needed: 1.' from '**Describe it in the ontology** -- upload a TTL ...' -- so the description goes and the bare '1.' stays. Reproduced offline in both shapes. NOTE: the product's own multi-line text is well formed; five recorded live answers in docs/phase0/phase0_baseline.md.jsonl carry items 1, 2 and 3 intact, so the 'empty item 1' in the tail N read is this stripper's output (or the hand read's transcription), not the hint as composed.
Fix_Approach: Factored the clause removal into grounding_guard._strip_clauses and gave it two hygiene passes: _tidy_ordinals drops a step number with nothing behind it and renumbers what survives on that line, and _renumber_ordered_lines renumbers a run of 'N.' lines from 1 so a list never starts at 2. Both no-op unless a removal actually happened on that line, and both leave a number that is a reading ('21.4 C', 'Floor 3.') untouched.
Verification: Offline: tests/test_no_internal_vocabulary_reaches_a_non_admin.py -- test_a_removed_step_does_not_leave_an_empty_numbered_item, test_a_list_a_reader_sees_still_counts_from_one, and five byte-for-byte cases proving an ordinary answer is unchanged. Mutation-checked: with _tidy_ordinals and _renumber_ordered_lines stubbed to identity the suite fails. 714 tests across the 22 files touching grounding_guard pass. NOT re-asked live -- no live model call was made this session.

Title: The non-admin guard withholds the INSTRUCTION to edit the model but not the VOCABULARY it is written in
Description: Measured: strip_schema_remediation over the sensor enablement hint removes 'upload a TTL ...' and leaves 'give each sensor a ref:hasExternalReference -> ref:hasTimeseriesId (the column/uuid) plus ref:storedAt (a key from database_registry.yaml)' entirely intact. None of those names anything a visitor, an occupant or a facility manager can see or change (design contract 6: users need no SQL/SPARQL/schema knowledge).
Root_Cause: _SCHEMA_REMEDIATION_RE matches a VERB plus an ontology word (extend/add/update/upload/enrich + ontology|tbox|ttl|schema|...). A sentence that merely USES the schema has no such verb, so it is not remediation by that definition and survives. The rule was enforced on the imperative and not on the vocabulary, which is the half a language model writes when it narrates the TBox.
Fix_Approach: Added grounding_guard.names_internal_schema / strip_internal_schema over four families: a namespaced term (ref:/brick:/ontosage:/hbco:/s223:/qudt:/rdfs:/owl:/xsd:), a .ttl/.yaml/.yml/.jsonld/.rq filename, a query language or serialisation (SPARQL, TTL, turtle file, TBox, RDF, triplestore) and the join identifiers (uuid, timeseries id, named graph). Wired into _ground_semantic_fallback beside the existing schema-remediation withholding, non-admins only. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: a bare Brick class name ('Air_Temperature_Sensor'). The same contract says this system serves experts, and stripping it would be the guard acting wider than the defect (lessons #135).
Verification: Offline: tests/test_no_internal_vocabulary_reaches_a_non_admin.py -- every decline producer (grounding_guard.enablement_hint x 5 kinds, building_profile.enablement_hint, referent_resolver._typed_clarification x 4 kinds) called for every non-admin role derived from ROLE_PERMISSIONS plus five absent/malformed roles: 0 leaks. Mutation-checked: stubbing names_internal_schema fails the suite. NOT re-asked live.

Title: WITHDRAWN: 'eleven other reader-facing strings name machinery with no role gate' -- all eleven were checked and all eleven are gated
Description: AS FIRST LOGGED (wrong): an AST scan of every non-docstring string literal in orchestrator/ -- grepping the VOCABULARY, not the sentence -- found eleven pieces of chat prose naming ref:/brick:/ontosage: terms, .ttl and .yaml filenames or 'uuid', and I recorded them as ungated. AS CHECKED (correct): every one of the eleven is either behind a for_admin branch or never reaches a chat reader at all. observability.describe x2 -- `if not for_admin: return line` before both Unlock lines. retrieval_outcome -- the string sits in the admin_remedy slot of _WORDING and describe() returns `result.remedy if for_admin else result.next_step`. asset_state_service._answer_schedule -- passes for_admin through to _decline. unmodelled_entities.correction_text -- `if for_admin:` appends it. _orchestrator._deliberate_node x2 -- `if reader_is_admin_in(state):` appends it. evidence/meter_boundary -- the literal is named _ADMIN_REMEDY and statement() takes for_admin. self_description.describe -- `elif for_admin:`. capability_agent._answer_unchecked -- `if reader_is_admin_in(state):`. evidence/matrix.assess_shape -- has NO caller in orchestrator/ at all; its only user is scripts/build_observability_matrix.py, an offline report.
Root_Cause: THE MISTAKE WAS MINE AND IT IS THE ONE THIS REPO KEEPS RECORDING (lessons #145): I verified that the LITERAL exists, not that the CODE emits it. A string literal carrying internal vocabulary is not a leak; the branch that reaches it is what decides. An AST scan over literals cannot answer that question and must not be reported as though it had. Every one of the eleven had to be read.
Fix_Approach: Nothing to fix. Recorded rather than deleted, because the negative result is worth having: the admin-only rule introduced on 2026-09-17 was applied at ELEVEN independent sites across eight modules, by eight different mechanisms, and it holds at all of them. The only place it did not hold was the one this session fixed -- text a language model writes in its own words, which no source-level gate reaches (BUG-1232).
Verification: Measured, site by site, by reading the branch around each literal: orchestrator/services/observability.py:184,199,214; orchestrator/services/retrieval_outcome.py:106,255-267; orchestrator/services/asset_state_service.py:507-516; orchestrator/services/unmodelled_entities.py:152,166; orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py:8477,8585; orchestrator/services/evidence/meter_boundary.py:126-134; orchestrator/services/self_description.py:226; orchestrator/agents/capability_agent.py:1075; orchestrator/services/evidence/matrix.py:127 (no orchestrator caller). Also measured: no call site in orchestrator/ passes for_admin=True unconditionally except main.py:4779, which is inside /api/v1/admin/observability/matrix, itself behind require_permission('system:admin'). That condition is now pinned by tests/test_no_internal_vocabulary_reaches_a_non_admin.py::test_no_call_site_hands_the_remediation_out_unconditionally.

Title: scripts/ask_questions.py silently ignores --email unless --v1 is also passed, so a run can be labelled with the wrong role
Description: Tail N records 'asked as facility01@example.com (facility_manager)' and yet its answers carry grounding_guard.enablement_hint's admin-only block. Both cannot be true: measured, reader_is_admin returns True for role 'admin' and False for facility_manager, analyst, operator, occupant, readonly, an unknown role, a blank role and a missing one; facility01 is facility_manager in the live Postgres; and the live orchestrator log shows /v1 resolving 'facility01@example.com' -> 'facility01' (role=facility_manager). So a run whose answers contain that block did not reach the capability lane as facility01.
Root_Cause: In ask_questions.py main(), --email is read ONLY inside the `if args.v1:` branch. Without --v1 the harness logs in through capture_golden_baseline._login, which uses ADMIN_USERNAME / ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env, and posts to /chat -- so every question is asked as the admin account (.env ADMIN_USERNAME=admin@ontosage, role admin) while the operator believes they are asking as the account they named. The flag is accepted, parsed and discarded without a warning.
Fix_Approach: Not changed this session (the harness is not in scope). Two options: make --email without --v1 an error, or have the /chat path forward the identity too. Until then, a role-dependent finding must be confirmed from the orchestrator log line '[forwarded-user] <email> -> <user> (role=...)' rather than from the command that was typed.
Verification: Measured: reader_is_admin over every role in ROLE_PERMISSIONS; `SELECT username, email, role FROM users` in the live postgres-user-data container; docker logs ontosage-orchestrator | grep forwarded-user; and the argument handling read out of scripts/ask_questions.py main(). The tail N run's own log window had already rolled over, so which branch that run took is INFERRED from the text it produced, not read from a log.

Title: SAFETY: an evacuation QUESTION was filed as an URGENT safety report and answered with a ticket number
Description: Tail N #5, live 2026-09-30. 'if the main exit is blocked by smoke, what is the alternative route' answered: 'Thank you - your safety report has been logged as REP-F9828F. Category: Safety report. Priority: URGENT. Status: OPEN. An administrator has been notified.' A person asking where to evacuate got a ticket number and no route. CLAUDE.md states the rule this breaks verbatim: 'Fault/suggestion/safety STATEMENTS -> report-intake ... Questions are NOT reports.'
Root_Cause: TWO gates, and each one alone would have been enough to hide the other. (1) semantic_router.report_intake_intent computes is_question as q.endswith('?') or q.startswith(_REPORT_QUESTION_STARTS). The sentence carries no question mark and opens with 'if', which is in neither test, so is_question was False; 'smoke' is in _REPORT_SAFETY_PHRASES; the function returned 'safety_report' and the contract rule report_intake_statement then forced that intent from seven classifications (measured over 19 candidate intents offline: 7 forced, 3 already report intents). (2) The one rule that answers this shape, emergency_action_is_a_procedure, could not have rescued it either: is_emergency_action_question was False, because 'what is the alternative route' matches none of _ACTION_FRAME's shapes (no 'I/we', and 'route' was not a procedure noun). Fixing only gate 1 would have left the question with no lane (lesson #154).
Fix_Approach: Gate 1: _HYPOTHETICAL_QUESTION_RE in semantic_router - a message OPENING with a hypothetical (if / in case / in the event / should / supposing / suppose / imagine) and then asking a WH-question is a question. Narrow twice: the opener must be first, so a leading fault STATEMENT is still judged by the existing multi-sentence rescue; and the tail must be a wh-word, never a bare auxiliary, so 'since the lift is broken, can someone fix it' still files. Gate 2: _ACTION_FRAME in emergency_procedure gains 'what is/are the <qualifier> route/exit/way/path/stairs' where the qualifier is an escape word, plus 'which way/route/exit do I...'; EMERGENCY_ACTION_RE still requires an emergency within 60 chars. Gate 3: emergency_action_is_a_procedure drops 'safety_report' from its intent bail-out, so the classifier's own label cannot block it - what protects a real report is report_intake_intent, checked on the next line.
Verification: OFFLINE. Contract routed from 24 candidate intents: the question now reaches 'capability' (the building's evacuation procedure) from 20 of them, including safety_report, and reaches no intake lane from any. BLAST RADIUS measured over the 7,196 distinct questions this project holds (survey corpus + every docs/*.jsonl bank): report_intake_intent changes on 7, and all 7 are the same shape - 'if the muster point is unsafe due to weather, where is the backup', 'if smoke is detected in a riser, which areas need to be cleared first', 'if a smoke detector triggers at ngiht, who gets alerted', 'if water is found leaking near electrics, how is the hazard contained' x3, and the defect itself. ZERO genuine reports moved. is_emergency_action_question changes on 4, all evacuation-route questions. Tests: tests/test_routing_contract.py (18 + 11 cases) and tests/test_routing_accuracy.py (6 cases). NOT VERIFIED LIVE - uvicorn runs without --reload and the owner holds restarts. The live ask made this session returned intent 'recommend', which the contract does not claim, so it declined honestly instead of filing: the route is non-deterministic (CAVEAT-891) and one green ask would not have shown the defect.

Title: 'repairman' was parsed as a report ID, and so were 'reporting' and 'represent'
Description: Tail N #40, live 2026-09-30. 'can you call for a repairman?' answered 'I couldn't find a report with ID **REP-AIRMAN**. Double-check the ID (format REP-XXXXXX).'
Root_Cause: ReportIntakeService._report_re was r'\bREP[- ]?[A-Z0-9]{6}\b' with IGNORECASE: an OPTIONAL separator followed by six LETTERS. 'rep'+'airman' matched, and so did 'reporting', 'represent', 'repairing', 'replacing', 'repeating', 'reproduce'. The pattern is used by classify_action as well as extract_report_id, so any message containing one of those words was routed to the STATUS branch - 'are all the smoke detectors reporting as online right now?' was a report-status lookup.
Fix_Approach: Require HEX: r'\bREP[-_ ]?[0-9A-F]{6}\b'. A real id is _new_report_id()'s output, 'REP-' + uuid4().hex[:6].upper(), so hex costs nothing real. _normalise_id is unchanged, so 'REP-F9828F', 'rep f9828f' and 'REPF9828F' all still resolve.
Verification: OFFLINE. Over the same 7,196-question population the pattern changes on 17, and every one is a false positive REMOVED - repairman x2, reporting x6, REPORTING, repairing x2, replacing, repeating, reproduce, represent, and two more. No real identifier is lost: the three accepted spellings are pinned by test. tests/test_routing_accuracy.py::test_tail_n_report_id_is_not_any_word_starting_with_rep. NOT VERIFIED LIVE (restart owned by the user). RESIDUAL: with the id gone, classify_action returns 'create' and the intake node's own is_question_not_a_fault guard (True for this text) answers from the records instead of filing - honest, but 'can you call for a repairman?' still has no lane that explains how to raise a maintenance request. Not forced; see BUG-1247.

Title: an inline floor-plan keyword override discards a COMPOSED clarification, undoing BUG-719's fix
Description: Tail N #12, live 2026-09-30, and re-measured this session. 'This room is far too hot. Where is a nearby area that I can go to cool down?' answered with a floor picker - 'Ground Floor / Floor 1 / ... Which floor would you like to see?' - in 1.2 s, before any lane ran.
Root_Cause: MEASURED route: {'decision_source': 'override', 'intent_from_dialogue': 'clarification', 'intent_after_overrides': 'floor_plan', 'final_node': 'floor_plan', 'overrides_applied': ['floor_plan_keyword_detection']}. The deictic guard in dialogue_agent.detect_intent had already decided correctly that 'this room' names no room and had composed the question to ask back (BUG-719, measured 5/5 good on unseen questions in the same run); it returns before apply_contract runs, so no contract rule could reach the turn. Then the inline override in _route_from_dialogue_impl matched floor_plan_service.is_floor_plan_query on the two words 'where is' and replaced the clarification. 'clarification' is in the META group, which _data_intents does not cover, and it was not in _floor_plan_protected.
Fix_Approach: Add 'clarification' to _floor_plan_protected, but ONLY when a question was actually composed (state.clarification_question non-empty). A bare clarification label with no question still falls through to the picker, because the alternative there is the generic 'Could you please provide more details about your question?'.
Verification: OFFLINE, three tests in tests/test_routing_accuracy.py: the composed clarification survives, a bare one still reaches the picker, and 'show me the floor plan of floor 3' from intent 'general' is untouched. REACH measured: 164 of 7,196 questions trip is_floor_plan_query, and the override can only claim the five META intents (clarification, general, greeting, planner, self_description) because every data and standalone intent is already excluded - so at most one of five labels is narrowed, and only when a question was composed. NOT VERIFIED LIVE.

Title: 'which areas are currently overcrowded?' reaches a different wrong lane on every ask - and is deliberately NOT routed, because the building cannot answer it
Description: Tail N #30 answered '## Anomaly Detection - No sensor data available for anomaly detection' plus a floor-plan menu. Re-asked live this session it was classified 'planner' and answered '## Sensor Data Analysis - No occupancy data available' while binding AIR QUALITY sensors. Offline the contract sends it to 'observability' from every weak intent. Three lanes, three asks, none of them right, and the contract claims neither 'anomaly' nor 'planner'.
Root_Cause: Two separate things. The VARIANCE is classifier mood (CAVEAT-891): the contract has no rule for this shape, so whatever label the LLM picks stands. The deeper one is that the question cannot be answered honestly today: 'overcrowded' is occupancy against CAPACITY, and input/bldg1_occupancy_capacity.ttl holds 62 hbco:roomCapacity figures, every one carrying an ontosage:capacityBasis that says 'estimated ... Not certified - Estates holds the authoritative figure', against hundreds of occupancy series. BUG-954 (P1, OPEN) has the occupancy count itself wrong by about 190x on the same quantity.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED, ON PURPOSE. Routing it to the deliberation lane would produce a confident ranking - 'Room X is overcrowded' - built on 62 uncertified estimates and a count that is known to be wrong, which is a safety-adjacent claim nobody made. The present failure is visible to the reader; that one would not be. The order is: fix BUG-954, then decide whether capacity is authoritative enough to compare against, then route. DELIBERATE_RE already carries 'crowded' and 'busy', so the routing half is one word and a tolerated adverb once the data half holds.
Verification: The reason for not fixing is pinned by tests/test_routing_accuracy.py::test_tail_n_overcrowded_is_recorded_as_open_not_silently_routed, which asserts the capacity file still says 'Not certified', so a later session cannot quietly point this at a ranking lane. Live route measured once this session: intent 'planner', decision_source 'registry', no overrides.

Title: a question about whether alerting EXISTS was answered with the alert-creation form
Description: Tail N #50, live 2026-09-30. 'are there alerts for unusual energy patterns or wastage?' answered 'I haven't created an alert yet. I need the value that should trigger it...' - a configuration form, to someone asking what the building offers.
Root_Cause: The classifier labels it 'alert' and nothing takes it back. _r_automation_needs_a_shape exists for exactly a mislabelled alert intent, but both of its tests (_AUTOMATION_SHAPE_RE and _STRONG_SHAPE_RE) match on the literal word 'alerts', so the question looks like a well-formed request to create one. The difference is the FRAME, not the nouns: asking whether something is there against asking for it to be set up.
Fix_Approach: New contract rule alert_existence_is_a_capability, placed DIRECTLY AFTER automation_needs_a_shape because it corrects it and the last rule wins (lesson #122). From-set is two intents wide (alert, automation_capability), so it can move nothing another lane claimed. Guarded four ways: a control command or a report, STANDING_ALERT_RE, ALARM_HISTORY_RE, and a now-scoped question (right now / currently / active / ongoing / outstanding / today / this week) all stand it down. The SUBJECT decides what 'provide' means: the building/system may provide, give, send or issue; you/I/we may only have, get, offer, support or receive.
Verification: OFFLINE, and the subject split was MEASURED rather than assumed. Over 7,196 questions the first draft moved 18 and one was wrong - 'Could you provide a priority alert to the facilities team if any standby loads exceed a certain threshold' is a request to SET ONE UP. A threshold cue cannot separate the two ('are there alerts if energy consumption exceeds expected thresholds?' is an existence question carrying the same words); the subject can. After narrowing it moves 19, and every one is an existence or capability question. Tests: 4 in tests/test_routing_contract.py, 2 in tests/test_routing_accuracy.py, plus the precedence pin. NOT VERIFIED LIVE.

Title: 'Can the building remind me to adjust lighting?' was executed as an actuation command and answered with a setpoint form
Description: Tail N #52, live 2026-09-30: 'to request a change I need which setpoint and the value to set'. The question asks whether the building can remind anyone of anything; nothing in it asks for a change.
Root_Cause: SemanticRouter.is_control_command returned True - _CONTROL_VERB_TARGET_RE saw 'adjust lighting' - and the contract's actuation_control rule then forces 'control' from EVERY intent, so the classifier's label was irrelevant. The guard that exists to stop this, _AUTOMATION_CAPABILITY_Q_RE, requires an autonomy ADVERB (automatically / by itself / on its own / without me) within 40 characters of the subject, and this question has none.
Fix_Approach: Widen _AUTOMATION_CAPABILITY_Q_RE with two alternatives on the same building/system/it/ontosage subject: '... remind|notify|alert|warn|prompt|nudge|message|email|text me|us|staff|occupants|anyone' and '... let me|us know'. Being told about something IS the autonomy cue. The subject constraint is what keeps it safe: 'can YOU turn the lights off' is still a command, exactly as the guard's own docstring has always said.
Verification: OFFLINE. Over 7,196 questions is_control_command changes on exactly 2, both the intended shape: 'Can the building remind me to adjust lighting?' and 'Can the system remind me to close blinds?'. No genuine command moved; five representative commands are pinned by test (open the windows on floor 3, can you please unlock the door, adjust the lighting in room 5.01, dim the lights in the atrium, keep the doors unlocked). With the guard in place the contract reaches 'automation_capability' from every weak intent, which the honest-capability lane answers. Tests: tests/test_routing_accuracy.py, 5 + 5 cases. NOT VERIFIED LIVE.

Title: 'can you call for a repairman?' has no lane that says how to raise a maintenance request
Description: Opened by BUG-1242 rather than fixed with it. With the report-id over-capture gone the message no longer produces nonsense, but it still has no good answer: classify_action returns 'create' and the intake node's is_question_not_a_fault guard (True here) diverts it to metadata and answers from the graph. The honest answer is 'I cannot contact anyone on your behalf; here is how a request is raised', which is what the control lane says for external actions.
Root_Cause: EXTERNAL_ACTION_KWS carries only email/send/forward/activate shapes, so 'call for a repairman', 'get someone to come out' and 'ring maintenance' are not recognised as asking the assistant to contact a third party.
Fix_Approach: NOT ATTEMPTED this session. Adding 'call' to a keyword set that forces 'control' from every intent is exactly the widening this repo has been burned by (lessons #124, #135, #154) - 'call' is also 'what do you call this room', 'on-call rota' and 'call point' (the building has fire call points). It needs a shape, measured against the 7,196-question population, not a keyword.

Title: 'what is the evacuation route?' on its own still misses the emergency-procedure lane, because EMERGENCY_ACTION_RE needs the frame and the emergency to be two separate tokens
Description: Found while fixing BUG-1241 and left alone. EMERGENCY_ACTION_RE is (FRAME)[^?.!]{0,60}(EMERGENCY) or the reverse, so a sentence whose only emergency word is INSIDE the frame satisfies neither half. 'what is the evacuation route?' matches the frame on 'evacuation route' and then has no separate emergency token left, so is_emergency_action_question is False. 'if a fire starts on floor 3, what is the safest evacuation route' works because 'fire' supplies the second token.
Root_Cause: The two-token structure is the pattern's safety property - it is what keeps 'what is the nearest exit?' and 'what is the quickest route to room 5.01?' out - so the gap is a consequence of a deliberate design, not an oversight.
Fix_Approach: Not changed. A self-sufficient third alternative (an escape-qualified route noun where the qualifier is itself an emergency word) would close it, but it widens a safety-relevant pattern for a question outside the six this session was asked to fix, and it was not measured. Logged so the next session can decide with the measurement in hand.
Verification: is_emergency_action_question('what is the evacuation route?') is False before and after this session's change - measured, not assumed.

Title: ALARM_HISTORY_RE reads 'do you HAVE alerts for X' as 'HAVE there been alerts', so an existence question is answered as a record question
Description: Found while measuring BUG-1245's blast radius. ALARM_HISTORY_RE's first branch is have|has|had|were|was|did within 40 characters of alarm(s)|alert(s), which matches 'do you have alerts for high CO2?'. alarm_history_is_a_record runs at index 25 and the new existence rule at index 30, and the new rule stands down when ALARM_HISTORY_RE matches - so the behaviour is unchanged from before, and the question is answered from the alarm records rather than from what alerting exists.
Root_Cause: 'have' as a possession verb and 'have' as a perfect auxiliary are not separated by the pattern.
Fix_Approach: Not changed: 'metadata' is a defensible destination, the shape is not one of the six tail-N defects, and narrowing a pattern that TODO-490 exists to keep wide needs its own measurement.
Verification: Measured offline: intent 'alert' + 'do you have alerts for high CO2?' routes to 'metadata' via alarm_history_is_a_record, before and after this session's change.

Title: _AUTOMATION_SHAPE_RE knows 'alert' and 'warn' but not 'alarm', so an alarm question labelled 'alert' is sent to the capability lane as shapeless
Description: Found while measuring BUG-1245's guards. 'are there any active alarms at the moment?' with intent 'alert' routes to 'capability' via automation_needs_a_shape, because _AUTOMATION_SHAPE_RE alternates over automat|notif|alert|remind|warn|trigger|standing|schedul|whenever|... and has no 'alarm' at all. The question asks for live state and gets the capability chain.
Root_Cause: The alert vocabulary is spelled out in three separate patterns in routing_contract (_AUTOMATION_SHAPE_RE, _STRONG_SHAPE_RE, ALARM_HISTORY_RE) and only the last one knows the word 'alarm'. A list duplicated is a list that diverges.
Fix_Approach: Not changed. Adding 'alarm' to the two shape patterns is one word, but automation_needs_a_shape returns 'capability' from two intents and the effect was not measured over the question population this session. Pre-existing and unchanged by BUG-1245's rule, which stands down on a now-scoped question.
Verification: Measured offline before and after this session's change: identical route ('alert' -> 'capability' via automation_needs_a_shape), so BUG-1245 neither caused nor fixed it.

Title: Tail N's 'six false declines that name the right source' are FOUR causes, not one; two are register vocabulary and are fixed TTL-first
Description:
docs/phase0/tail_N_2026-09-30_read.md groups six of its eight false declines under BUG-947's heading -- 'the answer names the right reading or register in the same sentence as the refusal' -- and closes 'One fix -- make the selector read what the pointer already found -- would move six of these.' ALL SIX WERE RE-ASKED LIVE on 2026-09-30 (healthy stack, caches flushed, a fresh chat id each, facility01@example.com) and all six reproduce. The container log says they have four distinct causes and only ONE of them is the mechanism the row names.

Title: The answer-relevance gate deletes a data lane's answer and leaves a decline that says the records could not answer -- FOUR of tail N's six false declines
Description:
MEASURED LIVE, 2026-09-30, one container log, four consecutive turns. Each question routed correctly, its lane fetched real readings, an answer was produced, and the gate replaced it with _unanswered_response:
  #23 humidity: 275 UUIDs bound and fetched -> 'relevance gate replaced a sensor_data answer: OFF_TOPIC (Does not address change, only gives current values.)'
  #43 return air temperature: six AHU points on plant_data -> 'OFF_TOPIC (Does not provide return air temperature, gives unrelated building averages.)'
  #45 water consumption: 1,000 rows of the Building Main water meter, analytics executed successfully -> 'OFF_TOPIC (Provides data, not explanation of monitoring method.)'
  #46 reserved spaces: the events lane ran and wrote events_result -> 'OFF_TOPIC (does not address reserved spaces question.)'
THE GATE'S VERDICT IS RIGHT IN ALL FOUR. What replaces the answer is not. _unanswered_response opens 'I couldn't answer that from Abacws Building's records', which is FALSE on a turn that has just read 275 humidity series or 1,000 water-meter rows -- and clarification.compose_abstract then completes it with the pointer's nearest holdings, which for a question that names its quantity puts THAT QUANTITY FIRST. That is the whole of tail N's 'the system names the right source in the same sentence as the refusal' for these four: the source is named because the question named it and the turn read it, and then the answer was deleted. No register selector and no matcher disagreement is involved (cf. BUG-1073 -- do not read the pointer as evidence).
THIS IS BUG-873 REOPENED ON THE TWO LANES ITS FIX DID NOT LIST. BUG-873 (P1, 2026-09-23) established the principle in _orchestrator._relevance_gated's own comment: 'when a lane has just answered FROM THOSE RECORDS, that sentence is not a cautious decline, it is a false statement about the building'. Its guard, _grounded_evidence_behind, recognises evidence_dossier, aggregate_result (with figures or baseline), comparison and forecast_result -- and NOT sql_result, NOT analytics_result and NOT events_result, which are the three lanes that produced these four answers.
Root_Cause: _grounded_evidence_behind is a whitelist of four bus keys, and the deliberation, aggregate, comparison and forecast lanes are the four it lists. The principal data path -- sparql -> sql -> analytics -- writes sql_result and analytics_result and is not on it, and the events lane writes events_result and is not either. BUG-873's own history shows the shape: the forecast lane was missed by the first version of that guard and added after a live failure, with a comment saying so. This is the same omission twice more. lessons #157's twin: a marker with too few readers is indistinguishable from no marker.
Fix_Approach:
NOT CHANGED IN THIS SESSION, DELIBERATELY, and the reasoning is the point of this row.
THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT SAFE UNATTENDED. Adding sql_result/analytics_result/events_result to _grounded_evidence_behind would stop the gate replacing on essentially every data turn -- and the data lanes are where the gate is MEASURED BEST. Its own docstring: 'accurate on the DATA lanes (sensor_data 17/30 weird flagged, 0/10 good; events 8/9)'. Disabling its action on the lanes it is good at, on the evidence of four hand-read instances, is exactly the trade CAVEAT-972 and BUG-1073 refused. #43 is the case that proves it: there the answer really was about something else, and suppressing it was protective.
THE FIX THAT IS SAFE IS TO CHANGE WHAT THE REPLACEMENT SAYS, NOT WHETHER IT HAPPENS. The gate keeps its action; the sentence stops asserting the false thing. On a replacement where the turn DID read the building (sql_result rows, analytics_result, events_result), the decline should say so -- 'I read <building>'s <quantity> readings, but what I could put together did not answer <what was asked>' -- instead of 'I couldn't answer that from <building>'s records'. The signal is already on the bus: _relevance_gated writes results['relevance_gate']['replaced'] before it calls _unanswered_response. This cannot restore a wrong answer and cannot lose a right one, which neither alternative can claim.
BEFORE DOING IT, GREP FOR WHO PATTERN-MATCHES THE CURRENT LEAD. publication_gate.py quotes it verbatim in a comment and at least one decline classifier keys on it; a wording change that silently stops a decline being recognised as a decline is BUG-876/BUG-886/CAVEAT-887 a fourth time (lessons #141). Every change to that marker list is already required to be verified against all stored answers by a test.
SEPARATELY AND SMALLER: #43's answer should not have been about building averages at all -- see BUG-1255.
LANDED 2026-09-30, exactly as recommended above: the gate keeps its action and the SENTENCE stops asserting the false thing.
WHAT CHANGED. `clarification.lead_read_but_off_topic` is a second opening for `compose_abstract`, selected by a new `read_but_off_topic` flag: "I couldn't put an answer together{ about X} from <building>'s records -- I did read them, but what I could make of them did not answer the question you asked." The nearest-holdings TAIL is byte-identical to before, so only the first sentence moves. `_unanswered_response` sets the flag from TWO signals, both required: `results['relevance_gate']['replaced']` (an answer was DELETED -- the only case in which the default sentence is false) and a new `_store_rows_read(state)` > 0 (this turn COUNTED rows out of a store). It logs which way it went at INFO so the case is countable rather than hand-read (lessons #157).
`_grounded_evidence_behind` IS UNTOUCHED AND MUST STAY UNTOUCHED. `_store_rows_read` is a separate, positive-only function: it decides only what a decline may SAY, never whether an answer may be DELETED. tests/test_the_relevance_gate_gap_tail_n_measured.py still passes unchanged -- the gap it pins is deliberately still open -- and the new file asserts the three keys are still absent from the guard.
IT IS DELIBERATELY NARROW. Only a counted read qualifies, because the sentence asserts "I did read them". A lane that ran and fetched nothing does NOT qualify: BUG-1271, "what is the average sound level" answered with a list of eight floors, is the same gate firing correctly on a turn that read no store, and it keeps the older, weaker wording. `_count_sql_rows` is REUSED from verifier_agent rather than re-derived (it already knows the three shapes the SQL lane writes -- BUG-508). The events lane qualifies only on a concrete count, because it returns success=True for `referent_not_found` and `unrecognised`, which are declines.
A LATENT DEFECT THIS CHANGE WOULD HAVE ACTIVATED, FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: `relevance_gate` was NOT in `_PER_TURN_LANE_KEYS`. Harmless while nothing on the response path read it; once `_unanswered_response` reads `replaced`, a stale one makes THIS turn's decline say "I did read them" about the PREVIOUS question. Added, with the test.
THE GATE'S REASON IS NOT SHOWN TO THE READER. `verdict.reason` is model-generated prose ("Does not address change, only gives current values.") and the tail-N read already carries an internal-text concern; showing it would also be non-deterministic turn to turn (CAVEAT-891). The reason stays in the log, where the developer is.
WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the four upstream defects are untouched. The gate was RIGHT in all four and in BUG-1271 as well -- five instances, three independent root causes -- so this fix makes the failure HONEST and VISIBLE, it does not make the answer right. BUG-1255 (#43), BUG-1271 and the humidity-change and monitoring-method lanes are the real work and are still open.

Title: Tail N #45 misses the reach lane on ONE LETTER in the asker's own spelling, not on any matcher defect
Description: 'how is water consumption montored here?' is a question about HOW something is monitored -- the observability/reach lane's own subject, which answers 'what can you measure in this building?' by naming all 45 modalities. Measured offline: observability.CAN_MEASURE_RE.search('how is water consumption montored here?') is False, and on the same sentence spelled 'monitored' it is True, via the alternative '\bis\s+.{0,30}\b(?:instrumented|monitored|measured)\b'. The asker typed 'montored'. The question then fell to intent=analytics, fetched 1,000 rows of the Building Main water meter, narrated them, and the answer-relevance gate deleted it with the correct verdict 'Provides data, not explanation of monitoring method' (BUG-1252). So the reading named in the refusal -- 'the readings of entering water temperature, leaving water temperature, water flow' -- is real and the building does monitor water; the reach lane simply never got the question.
Root_Cause: A deterministic vocabulary gate over free text has no spelling tolerance, by design. The surrounding machinery does not either at this point: the HBCO concept resolver ran and bound Building_Water_Meter correctly from 'water consumption', so the SUBJECT was understood and only the SHAPE word was misspelt.
Fix_Approach:
RECORDED, NOT FIXED, and deliberately not proposed as a matcher change. Loosening CAN_MEASURE_RE for typos is the class of fix BUG-948 and CAVEAT-972 both measured and rejected, and lesson #154 records that this particular regex needs a negative case list as much as a positive one ('collect' is what happens to WASTE here). If it is ever worth doing, the place is a normalisation step ahead of the gates, measured over the 2,960 catalogue and the guard set like any other vocabulary change -- not an alternative added to this pattern.
AND THE PRIZE IS SMALLER THAN I FIRST WROTE, corrected here rather than quietly. The first draft of this row said 'the cheaper reading is that the reach lane would have answered this correctly'. I then asked it. MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-30, cache flushed, fresh chat id: 'how is water consumption monitored here?' routes to intent=observability with Building_Water_Meter bound and the HBCO concept water_usage resolved, the reach lane RUNS -- and the answer is 'Which space did you mean? I can say what is measured in a particular room, floor or zone, but I need to know which one before I can answer whether it is instrumented.' That is lessons #154 VERBATIM, on the same regex, eleven days later: the entry test (CAN_MEASURE_RE) and the internal branch (OPEN_QUESTION_RE) are DIFFERENT gates, and a question scoped to one QUANTITY with no place clears the first and not the second. So correcting the spelling turns a false decline into an honest clarification request, which is better and is not an answer. The remaining work is the internal branch: a reach question naming a MEASURAND and no place should answer about that measurand across the building -- this one holds a 'Water Usage Sensor - Building Main' in litres/day plus water flow, hot and chilled meters -- rather than ask which room.
Verification:
Offline, both spellings, against observability.CAN_MEASURE_RE and OPEN_QUESTION_RE at HEAD: the misspelt form matches neither; the correctly spelt form matches CAN_MEASURE_RE via '\bis\s+.{0,30}\b(?:instrumented|monitored|measured)\b'.
LIVE, 2026-09-30, both asked on the same healthy stack with resp_cache flushed and a fresh chat id each: the misspelt form -> intent=analytics, 1,000 water-meter rows fetched and narrated, answer deleted by the relevance gate (BUG-1252); the corrected form -> intent=observability, entities ['Building_Water_Meter'], '[observability] q=...' in the log, and 'Which space did you mean?' to the reader.
