THE DATA IS THERE AND IT IS FRESH. Measured directly against sensordb.plant_data inside the container with the session pinned to +00:00: each of the six UUIDs holds ~13,120 rows, MIN 2026-08-10 13:57, MAX 2026-09-30 15:27:11 -- four minutes before the question was asked. plant_data holds 786,566 rows across 88 UUIDs.
Unlike the other water/humidity instances there is no per-UUID SELECT in the log and no 'Fetching data for N UUIDs from storage: plant_data' line, so the fetch short-circuited before the per-store read -- aggregate_result is on the bus for this turn and '[aggregate] not claimed' is NOT in its log, so the aggregate lane claimed a question with no statistic word, no place and six equipment-scoped points, and produced building averages.
Root_Cause:
ESTABLISHED 2026-09-30 BY CALLING THE DECISION FUNCTION, as this row asked. The inference was RIGHT and the mechanism is narrower than the row guessed.
`aggregate_lane.wants_lane('What is the return air temperature?', 6, False, True, ['temperature'], False, summary_ok=True, profile_ok=False)` returns **AggregateIntent(stat='summary', group='floor')** -- case 6, the 'a bare measurand is not a refusal' path. `parse_intent` returns None (no statistic word) and `_NOT_AN_AGGREGATE` does NOT match, so this is a legitimate case-6 claim: it IS a value question about a quantity the question names and the building measures.
AND THE 6-ROWS-IN / 0-RECORDS-OUT STEP IS NOT THE DEFECT. Re-asked live 2026-09-30, occupant01 on /v1, caches flushed, the answer is:
  '**Across the building temperature is averaging 21.4 degC**, ranging from 18.1 to 26.1 degC' followed by a per-floor table -- Floor 0 | 26.0 | 1 sensor, Floor 1 | 26.1 | 1, Floor 2 | 19.2 | 1, Floor 3 | 18.5 | 1, Floor 4 | 18.1 | 1, Floor 5 | 20.3 | 1.
That is EXACTLY the six AHU return-air points, one per floor, fetched and summarised correctly. Nothing is missing and no figure is wrong. **The defect is the LABEL**: `render_summary` names the quantity `display_name(measurand)`, and `measurand` is a vote over coarse categories that returns 'temperature'. So an occupant is told the building averages 21.4 degC and that Floor 0 is 26.0 degC, when every figure is the air inside AHU ductwork. The relevance gate's 'gives unrelated building averages' was right, and it was the only thing standing between that sentence and a reader.
lessons #170 a second time: the specific thing WAS resolved -- the log line reads '[sparql] plant class resolved deterministically: brick:Return_Air_Temperature_Sensor' -- and then discarded. `_build_sensor_metadata` parses the point's class into `type_val`, uses it for units, and does not store it.
Fix_Approach:
FIXED 2026-09-30. `aggregate_lane.asked_quantity_name(question, measurand, labels)` computes what the answer CALLS the quantity, and `try_answer` passes it to `render_summary`, `render_extreme` and `render_exceedance` as `quantity`, which each prefer over `display_name(measurand)`. WORDING ONLY: no figure, no grouping, and no decision about whether to answer changes.
TWO PROPERTIES MAKE IT SAFE, AND NEITHER IS A LIST OF QUANTITY NAMES (lessons #170).
* THE PHRASE IS THE READER'S. It is read leftwards from the quantity word the question itself uses, across words that are not function words, capped at three, so it can never be more specific than what was asked. 'What is the temperature?' is still 'temperature'. The stop set is a CLOSED set of English function words plus the statistic and place words -- finite, and it does not rot when the building adds a modality.
* THE PHRASE MUST BE TRUE OF EVERY BOUND SENSOR. Each extra word must be a WORD of every answering sensor's label. Ask for the outside air temperature and get room sensors bound, and the labels do not carry 'outside', the coarse name is kept, a log line says so, and the relevance gate goes on catching the off-topic answer as before. So it cannot invent a quantity and cannot rename a set that does not measure what was asked.
The boundary sentence follows for free: 'Based on 6 return air temperature sensors on 6 floors', which is BUG-883's stated denominator.
THREE OF MY OWN CANDIDATE MECHANISMS WERE MEASURED AND DROPPED, and the measurements are why the shipped one is this narrow: naming the quantity from the longest phrase the LABELS share produces 'air handling unit floor return air temperature' and 'co2 level installed node' on this building's real labels; naming it from the shared Brick class needs a field `_build_sensor_metadata` does not store; and matching the reader's qualifier against the labels by SUBSTRING named the quantity 'ai temperature', because 'ai' sits inside 'air'.
Verification:
BEFORE, live: 'What is the return air temperature?' -> '**Across the building temperature is averaging 21.4 degC**', six-floor table, then the relevance gate deleted it (OFF_TOPIC). Store side was already verified on this row and was not re-measured.
BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED TWO WAYS over tasks/smart_building_questions.csv (4,060) + the real survey corpus (7,151) = 11,211 questions, crossed with this building's own label sets read live from the graph (25,546 labels over 101 classes):
  * against the label union for a whole measurand -- what a BROAD binding looks like -- **0 names move** in 11,211 questions. A question that binds every temperature sensor is unchanged, by construction, because no qualifier is true of all of them.
  * against per-CLASS label sets -- what a NARROW binding looks like -- **63 (question, class) pairs move, and 0 are wrong**: 'water temperature', 'water flow', 'outside temperature', 'outside air temperature', 'supply air temperature', 'air flow', 'air humidity', 'air temperature', 'return air temperature'. Every one is a case where the coarse name would have been a false statement about the building.
THREE WRONG NAMES WERE PRODUCED AND FIXED DURING THE MEASUREMENT, which is why it was run: "today's occupancy" -> 's occupancy' (a possessive), 'the AI temperature settings' -> 'ai temperature' (substring), and a truncated 're temperature conditions' -> 're temperature'. Nothing under three letters may be a qualifier, and the label check tokenises. Evaluative adjectives were added to the stop set for the same reason ('low water flow', 'stable temperature', 'comfortable temperature' are not quantities).
LIVE RE-ASK IS OWED: a Python module change is not deployed until the orchestrator restarts, and this session was forbidden to restart. After a restart, flush resp_cache:* and cache:sparql*, ask the verbatim question, and the lead must read 'Across the building return air temperature is averaging ...' with the gate NOT firing.
TESTS: tests/test_a_summary_names_the_quantity_it_summarised.py, 33 pass -- the verbatim question with the six real AHU labels, the veto against room sensors, the three fragment cases, the rendered lead AND its boundary sentence, that all three renderers accept the name and default to the coarse one, and that `try_answer` actually passes it (a helper nothing calls is lessons #170's defect again). Neighbouring slice: 426 passed over 13 files. black + flake8 F821/F823 clean.
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-30 after restart, occupant01 on /v1, caches flushed.
Q: 'What is the return air temperature?' -> **'Across the building **return air temperature** is averaging 21.3 °C', ranging 18.6-24.3, per-floor table, closing 'Based on **6 return air temperature sensors** on 6 floors'.**
The label is now the quantity the reader asked for. Before, the identical figures were presented as 'Across the building **temperature** is averaging 21.4 °C' -- an occupant told that the building averages 21.4 °C when every reading is air inside ductwork.
THE ROW'S OWN DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED: it said the lane answered with 'unrelated building averages', and the '6 rows in / 0 records out' line was read as a fetch failure. Neither holds. `wants_lane` returns stat='summary', group='floor', the six AHU return-air points are bound and summarised CORRECTLY, and **no figure was ever wrong**. The defect was the name on them -- the resolved class (`brick:Return_Air_Temperature_Sensor`, logged) was discarded before the narration, which is lesson #170's shape for the second time in a day.
BLAST RADIUS over 11,211 questions (4,060 bank + 7,151 real survey): the narrow per-Brick-class naming moves **63 gained / 0 broken**, every one a case where the coarse name was a false statement (water temperature, water flow, outside temperature, supply air temperature, return air temperature, air flow, air humidity). The broad measurand-union variant moved 0 and was dropped. THREE wrong names were produced and fixed DURING that measurement -- 's occupancy', 'ai temperature', 're temperature' -- which is why it was run rather than reasoned about.
Refs: BUG-1251; BUG-1252; docs/phase0/tail_N_2026-09-30_read.md #43; BUG-883; BUG-939; lessons #139, #146

Title: CORRECTION to tail N's read: 'one fix would move six of these' is wrong, and the grouping that produced it is the same inference BUG-1073 warned about
Description:
docs/phase0/tail_N_2026-09-30_read.md section 1 groups six false declines as 'BUG-947's shape' and concludes 'One fix -- make the selector read what the pointer already found -- would move six of these.' Measured against the running build (BUG-1251), the six have four causes: four are the answer-relevance gate deleting a produced answer (BUG-1252), one is a register-selector mis-rank on a coordinated noun phrase, one is a plain vocabulary gap where the pointer did NOT name the right register. One further instance (#45) additionally turns on a spelling error in the asker's text (CAVEAT-1254).
THE GROUPING WAS MADE FROM THE ANSWER TEXT, which is the only thing a hand read can see, and the answer text looks identical in all six because all six end in the same _unanswered_response wording. BUG-1073 measured exactly this trap from the other side: the decline's pointer names registers on 99.8% of the declines the selector is silent on, so 'it named the right thing' is what that mechanism does by construction. The same caution applies to the MODALITY half of the pointer for a question that names its quantity: 'the readings of humidity' leads the list for a humidity question because the question said humidity, not because anything identified a source and failed to read it.
Root_Cause: A hand read labels OUTCOMES and infers MECHANISMS, and four different mechanisms share one outcome here because they all terminate in the same fallback composer. lessons #158 is the general form: two answers wrong in the same way on the same quantity need not share a cause, and the cheapest discriminator is one more measurement, not a better theory.
Fix_Approach: The read is not edited -- it is a dated artefact and rewriting it would destroy the record. This row is the correction, and BUG-1251 carries the per-instance evidence. For the next tail: the run log already carries ontosage_route per turn (W04) and the container log carries '[response] relevance gate replaced', so a read can separate 'no lane answered' from 'a lane answered and something deleted it' at labelling time rather than a session later. Capturing route + the relevance-gate verdict beside each answer would have made this correction unnecessary.
Verification: All six re-asked live 2026-09-30, one run, caches flushed, fresh chat id each, no restart during it; all six reproduce and the cause of each is a line in the container log quoted in BUG-1251 and BUG-1252.
Refs: docs/phase0/tail_N_2026-09-30_read.md; BUG-1251; BUG-1252; BUG-1073; BUG-947; CAVEAT-1254; lessons #158

Title: 'Unknown agent: deliberate' rendered to the reader above a dump of 354 spaces
Description:
MEASURED LIVE, and found by re-asking a question that had been DELIBERATELY left unfixed -- which is the argument for re-asking those too. 'Can you tell me which areas are currently overcrowded?' returned, visibly:
    ## What threshold defines an area as overcrowded?

    Unknown agent: deliberate

    ## Spatial Information ... **354** space(s) found:
`PlannerAgent._run_step`'s final `else` returned `{'success': False, 'error': f'Unknown agent: {agent}'}`, and that `error` value is rendered to the reader.
TWO SEPARABLE DEFECTS: (a) the planner emitted a step for a lane its dispatch cannot run, and (b) its failure text named that lane to the reader. `deliberate` is not a typo -- it is a DECLARED intent in `intent_definitions.yaml`, 'multi-constraint SPACE RECOMMENDATION ... the user wants a place chosen, ranked, or found under comfort/environment constraints', which is exactly what the question is. The dispatch simply has no branch for it.
Root_Cause: A debug string in an `error` field that is user-facing. The dispatch handles sparql, sql, analytics, anomaly, report, export, capability, floor_plan, spatial_query and maintenance, and falls through for everything else -- so any intent the planner can PLAN but not RUN turns into a visible internal name.
Fix_Approach:
**(b) ONLY, ON PURPOSE.** The `else` now returns 'a step of this request could not be carried out', keeps the lane under a separate `unrunnable_agent` key for the trace, and still logs it at WARNING for a maintainer.
**A `deliberate` BRANCH WAS DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED.** Answering 'which areas are overcrowded' means ranking occupancy against CAPACITY. Every capacity figure this building holds carries `ontosage:capacityBasis` 'estimated ... Not certified', and BUG-954 (P1, OPEN) has the occupancy count wrong by ~190x. A confident 'Room X is overcrowded' on that basis is a safety-adjacent claim nobody made and is INVISIBLE where this failure is visible. BUG-1244 pins that decision; fixing the leak must not quietly become fixing the lane.
Verification:
`tests/test_no_internal_lane_name_reaches_the_reader.py`, 2 tests, pinning the CONDITION rather than the sentence: an AST walk over every string literal assigned to an `error` key in a returned dict, checked against a list of internal lane names. **Counterfactual run: restoring the old `f'Unknown agent: {agent}'` IS detected**, so the test is load-bearing and not merely green. A second test asserts the lane name still survives under `unrunnable_agent` and in the WARNING log -- removing it entirely would trade a leak for a blind spot, which is lesson #135's failure mode.
82 planner tests pass; `flake8 --select=F821,F823` clean. LIVE RE-ASK OWED after the next restart: the answer must no longer contain 'Unknown agent'.

Title: 'I found nothing that answers that' about sound, minutes after answering a sound question from 235 sensors
Description:
A FALSE ABSENCE, demonstrable inside a single run. Tail N, occupant on /v1:
  #16 'What is the average sound level?' -> **'I found nothing in Abacws Building's records that answers that.'**
  #28 'does the building sound feel good' -> **'Across the building sound is averaging 56.2, ranging from 52.9 to 59.4'**, broken down over six floors, 233 sensors.
Same quantity, same run, same reader, minutes apart. Verified against the graph: **235 sound/noise sensors carry a timeseries reference.**
**THIS IS THE WORST SHAPE OF FAILURE THIS PROJECT HAS.** Design contract #4 is 'if the data isn't loaded, say so' — the inverse, telling a reader nothing is recorded when 235 sensors are, is a statement about the world that is false. It is also the 'four kinds of nothing' lesson: graph-absence, window-absence, retrieval failure and forbidden access are different facts, and only the first may be worded like this. The system HAS the right wording — #10 in the same run says 'your role doesn't have access to the Occupancy Sensing data source' — so the vocabulary exists and this path is not using it.
Root_Cause:
NOT DIAGNOSED. The obvious candidates, none confirmed: a permission refusal rendered as an absence (occupant may lack the acoustic source, as it lacks Occupancy Sensing); the answer-relevance gate replacing a produced answer (BUG-1252's shape, which accounts for four of tail N's other false declines); or a genuine binding failure on the bare phrase 'average sound level'. **#28 answering the same quantity for the same reader argues against a permission cause**, which is what makes it worth chasing rather than assuming.
=== ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-30, AND IT IS ONE WORD IN A LIST ===
`sparql_agent._template_sparql` holds `floor_words = ['floor','floors','storey','storeys','level','levels']`, and two branches return a FLOOR-LISTING query when any of them appears. **'What is the average sound LEVEL?' matches on 'level'.** Neither branch consulted `concept_class` -- which is passed into the function and had already been resolved.
The container log gives the whole chain in six lines:
    [sparql] class from HBCO concept 'noisy': ontosage:Sound_Level_Sensor   <- 233 instances
    Using template SPARQL (entities=[]):
      SELECT ?floor ?label WHERE { ?floor a brick:Floor ... }
    GraphDB query returned 8 results                                        <- eight FLOORS
    [analytics] No UUIDs found - no specific sensor type detected           <- it WAS detected
    [response] relevance gate replaced a analytics answer: OFF_TOPIC
    [response] nothing to say: intent=analytics entities=none
**THE RELEVANCE GATE WAS RIGHT.** A list of eight floors does not answer a question about sound, and rejecting it was correct. The defect is entirely upstream, and the gate is the messenger -- the THIRD independent instance of that pattern today (see BUG-1252).
TWO HYPOTHESES OF MINE WERE WRONG ON THE WAY, both killed by one query. I first thought the concept resolved into the wrong NAMESPACE (`ontosage:` vs `brick:`) -- it did not, `ontosage:Sound_Level_Sensor` has 233 instances. I then thought the wording fix I had already made was the cure -- it was not; it removed a genuinely false sentence on a DIFFERENT path, and this question never reached it.
Fix_Approach:
ONE PATH FIXED, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THAT PRODUCED #16. Recorded that way round on purpose.
**What was fixed:** `absence_wording.absence_sentence()` emitted *'I found nothing in <building>'s records that answers that'* on the branch reached when `subject_of()` returns EMPTY -- i.e. when the system could not work out what the question is ABOUT. All six `_SUBJECT_PATTERNS` are existence-shaped ('is there a', 'how many', 'where is'), so every VALUE question lands there. That sentence is a claim about the WORLD made on a branch that cannot know it. It now opens 'I couldn't tie that question to a reading I can give you...' -- about the SYSTEM, which is what the branch actually knows.
**The opening is reused VERBATIM from `too_broad_reply`, deliberately.** Four consumers classify a decline by its first sentence (`regression_answerability._DECLINE_MARKERS`, `publication_gate.is_decline`, `audit_decline_markers.py`, the grader) and a NEW phrasing is read by all of them as an ANSWER -- lessons #141, where one question produced three honest decline wordings in a day and moved the measured decline rate while the system did not change. Verified by test that the gate still classifies it as a decline.
**What was NOT fixed, and this is the part that matters:** re-asked live after the restart, '#16 What is the average sound level?' no longer emits the false sentence -- but it still does not answer, and it now fails by a DIFFERENT path: *'I couldn't answer that from Abacws Building's records ... I couldn't read Abacws Building's sensor catalogue just now, so I can't list what it measures.'* That is CAVEAT-951's disclosure working (unavailable is not absent) and explains why its 'nearest things' named Alarm activation rather than sound. **So #16's actual cause was an intermittent catalogue read, not the wording I fixed.** I inferred the cause from the wording and was partly wrong.

Both floor branches now bail when a sensor concept resolved: `_is_quantity_question = bool(concept_class)` and `... and not _is_quantity_question`.
**KEYED ON THE RESOLVED CLASS, NOT ON A WORD LIST.** A stop-list of 'sound level', 'voc level' and so on would need extending for every quantity and would still miss the lay terms HBCO exists to resolve ('noisy', 'stuffy'). The class is already computed, already passed in, and was merely ignored. It also cannot over-capture: a genuine 'how many floors are there?' resolves no sensor concept and is untouched. It additionally frees 'Which floor is the warmest?', which is a temperature comparison and was also being answered with an inventory.
BLAST RADIUS, measured over both corpora BEFORE the change: **284 questions** say '<quantity> level(s)' -- **269 of them in the REAL survey corpus, 3.8% of the 7,151 questions 96 participants asked**. That corpus contains **zero** 'level <n>' storey questions; only the synthetic bank does (22). Among real users, 'level' after a quantity word never means storey.
Verification:
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-30 after restart, occupant01 on /v1 streaming:
  'What is the average sound level?'  -> no longer claims the records are empty; now states the catalogue could not be read. Still does not answer.
  'does the building sound feel good' -> ANSWERS: 'Across the building sound is averaging **54.0 dB**, ranging from 51.2 to 58.7', six floors, 233 sensors (and now carries UNITS, which the earlier run did not).
483 passed / 0 failed across every test touching absence wording and decline classification; 19 in the absence file itself.

**THE ROW IS WIDENED, NOT CLOSED. A SECOND FALSE ABSENCE IS CONFIRMED:**
  '#60 What is the VOC level' -> *'there are no sensors or readings related...'*
  Graph: **41 TVOC_Sensor and 41 TVOC_Level_Sensor instances carry a timeseries reference.**
So the system denies holding data for at least TWO quantities it demonstrably measures -- sound (235 sensors) and TVOC (41) -- by at least THREE different wordings, of which I fixed one. The pattern to chase is not the sentence: it is why a named quantity that the graph holds fails to bind. Treat the wording fixes as containment, not cure.
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-30 after restart, occupant01 on /v1 streaming, caches flushed:
  'What is the average sound level?' -> **'Across the building sound is averaging 49.9, ranging from 46.2 to 52.7'**, per-floor table over 233 sensors. Was: 'I couldn't answer that from Abacws Building's records.'
  'What is the VOC level' -> **'The most recent VOC reading was taken on 2026-09-30 20:23:24 by the TVOC Level Sensor 5.16. Value: 251'**, plus per-floor means. Was: 'you'll need to query the specific VOC sensors'.
  'How many floors are there?' -> still answered as a floor question. NOT REGRESSED.
**Both confirmed false absences closed by ONE change.**
Tests: `tests/test_a_quantity_level_is_not_a_building_level.py`, 10 cases -- the two live failures, four more of the shape taken verbatim from the real corpus, three genuine floor questions as the counterfactual, and one test pinning the MECHANISM (`_is_quantity_question` must appear) so nobody can satisfy the others with a stop-list. 110 neighbouring routing tests pass. flake8 F821/F823 clean.
RESIDUAL, not claimed as fixed: the VOC answer says 'Across all 41 000 records' and '(unit not recorded)' -- a count claim and a missing unit, both CAVEAT-1002's family.
Refs: TODO-697 (tail N); BUG-1252; lesson 'four kinds of nothing'

Title: publication_gate.is_decline misses 33 stored answers in the RETIRED 'could not put an answer together' wording
Description: Found while measuring BUG-1252's marker change over 2,985 stored answers. Adding the uncontracted "could not put an answer together" to publication_gate._DECLINE_MARKERS -- the pairing every other lead in that list has ("i couldn't verify" / "i could not verify") -- reclassifies 33 stored answers from not-a-decline to a decline. All 33 are the RETIRED `_unanswered_response` text, "I understood the question but could not put an answer together for it.", across docs/phase0/dev_tail_C_baseline.jsonl, fresh_tail_B_run2.jsonl, fresh_tail_run1.jsonl and others. They ARE declines, so the classifier is wrong about all 33 today. None is in the 73-probe pack, so that guard does not see it.
Root_Cause: The marker list carries only the contraction. The wording is no longer emitted -- `scripts/audit_decline_markers.py` derives 104 leads from the source and this is not among them -- so the miss costs nothing on a live turn and only mis-scores history. It is the same shape as CAVEAT-952 (the commonest decline the system emits was not in this list) one generation of wording earlier.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED, ON PURPOSE. BUG-1252's lead was built on the contraction precisely so that list needed no change; folding a 33-answer reclassification into a wording change would be lessons #141 a fourth time. Whoever takes this should add the uncontracted form ALONE, confirm the move is exactly those 33 and that every one opens with that sentence, and record the new counts -- publication_gate goes 204 -> 237 over the 2,985 and stays at 11 over the 73. Decide first whether re-scoring a RETIRED wording is worth moving a baseline that several rows quote; it changes no live turn.
Verification: Measured 2026-09-30 by classifying 2,985 stored answers (the 73-probe pack plus every docs/phase0/*.jsonl) with and without the single added marker, and reading the moved rows.

Title: A bare adjective lay term short-circuits the whole turn: 'clean energy' -> the cleaning register, 'humidity detection' -> fire alarms
Description: Tail N, occupant, /v1 streaming, 2026-09-30. (a) 'are EV chargers powered by clean energy?' -> 'The cleaning task register (30 records) cannot answer this: it records cleaning zone, location, service frequency and shift name, and nothing about chargers, energy and powered.' (b) 'Could the humidity detection be tied in with the water sensors to more accurately tell if there are water/leakage issues?' -> a list of six FIRE-ALARM zone assets (FSA-002..FSA-007). Items 4 and 3 of the eight WEIRD answers in docs/phase0/tail_N_2026-09-30_occupant_v1_read.md.
Root_Cause: ontosage:CleaningTask declared a bare layTerm "clean" and ontosage:FireSafetyAsset a bare "detection". record_registry._term_score matches \b<term>\b, so one four-letter adjective selected the register. WORSE THAN A WRONG REGISTER: held_record_class is a ROUTING SHORT-CIRCUIT -- the container log for (a) reads '[ttl-route] metadata via held record class: CleaningTask (30 instances) -- skipping LLM intent call' -- so the bare word decided the entire turn before any classification ran. No HBCO concept was resolved and discarded (that is BUG-1271's shape, a different defect); classification never happened at all.
Fix_Approach: TTL-FIRST (design contract 2), in ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl: removed bare "clean" and bare "detection"; added "cleaned" to CleaningTask and "fire detection", "smoke detection", "detection system(s)", "detection asset(s)" to FireSafetyAsset. MEASURED over 2,960 stakeholder-catalogue + 7,151 real survey questions: 49 selections move -- 39 GAINED (11 air-quality questions asked by six separate participants that selected the CLEANING register; 5 clean-energy; 6 identical 'is the gas detection sensor in the kitchen reading normal?'; 3 motion detection; 5 catalogue questions using 'detection' as incident-response process language; 7 'when was X cleaned' that the register exists for and could not reach), 4 NEUTRAL, 4 BROKEN (3x 'can you clean yourself/graffitti', which the register declined anyway; 1x 'how leak detection sensors could prevent damage and reduce waste' moves FireSafetyAsset -> WasteCollectionPoint, wrong to differently wrong). register_reach.py guard set: 124 questions, 0 violations, unchanged. The one right answer bare 'detection' was buying ('areas related to fire safty or smoke detection?') is preserved by "smoke detection", which is why the term was replaced rather than dropped. 'talk' -> EventActivity was measured too and DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: dropping it gains 8 survey questions and loses 6 catalogue ones, and the qualifier variant is 3 for 3 -- a wash, so it is pinned here instead.
Verification: VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-30 19:50-19:55, occupant02 via /v1 streaming, caches flushed, after the 19:37 restart re-uploaded the named graph (GraphDB now serves 'cleaned' and 'smoke detection'; bare 'clean' and 'detection' are gone). (a) 'are EV chargers powered by clean energy?' 10.3 s -> an answer ABOUT EV CHARGERS: it names EV_Charger_1_Power_Sensor / EV_Charger_2_Power_Sensor, states that no record specifies the energy mix, and points at energy procurement and sustainability records. The '[ttl-route] metadata via held record class: CleaningTask -- skipping LLM intent call' line is GONE from the log; the turn now classifies normally. (b) 'Could the humidity detection be tied in with the water sensors...' 10.4 s -> no fire-alarm list; the turn classifies as capability, capability_measurand_is_data routes it to sensor_data, and it declines honestly naming humidity, water flow, entering/leaving water temperature and the Hazard control register. No FireSafetyAsset short-circuit in the log. tests/test_a_bare_adjective_is_not_a_register_name.py 16 pass; 2,403 pass / 0 fail / 43 skip across every spatial, space, floor-plan, wayfinding, circulation, record-registry, register, lay-term and qualifier test file. register_reach.py guard set 124 questions, 0 violations, unchanged from baseline.

Title: The spatial lane's last branch answers EVERY unmatched question with all 354 spaces
Description: 'Can you tell me which areas are currently overcrowded?' returned a failed plan step ('a step of this request could not be carried out') followed by '## Spatial Information ## All spaces **354** space(s) found:' and a table. Item 8 of the eight WEIRD answers in tail N. The 'Unknown agent: deliberate' leak above that table is BUG-1261 and is already fixed; the table is not.
Root_Cause: spatial_agent._answer ends with an unconditional 'return self._answer_list(...)', and _answer_list with no detected space type lists the whole building. MEASURED, eight questions through SpatialAgent.resolve() on the live building: all eight returned the byte-identical 3,042-character '## All spaces -- **354** space(s) found' table, including 'which rooms are the quietest right now?' and 'which areas are the warmest?'. This is BUG-377 one level up -- that fix stopped a nearest-question whose target the plans do not label from falling through to the same table, and the DEFAULT branch has the same hole for every other unmatched question.
Fix_Approach: spatial_agent._inventory_was_asked_for: an ALLOWLIST (listing cue | space noun | floor word | function word) rather than a denylist of things the plans cannot evaluate, because that set is unbounded and an unknown word must fail toward the decline. A question naming a space TYPE is unaffected. Otherwise _list_target_unknown declines and names the kinds of space the plans DO label, read from the manifests. ITS FIRST SENTENCE REUSES AN EXISTING DECLINE LEAD ("I couldn't answer that from ...") on purpose: five consumers key on a decline's opening (regression_answerability._DECLINE_MARKERS, publication_gate.is_decline, scripts/audit_decline_markers.py, the grader, _orchestrator._decline_leads), so no marker list changes and the blast radius over the ~2,985 stored answers is zero by construction. Title: One generic subject word lets any amenity topic answer, and the answer is stamped 'from the building's own records'
Description: 'different types of buildings you can build' -> 'Here is what I found for **Abacws Building**: **Building access hours**. Card-holders can access Abacws 07:00-22:00 ... **Building management and contacts**. ... *Answered live from the building's own records.*' Item 6 of tail N's eight WEIRD answers; reproduced live 2026-09-30 19:29 as occupant02, 8.5 s. An out-of-scope question about the ASSISTANT'S reach answered with two unrelated facts about this building, presented as responsive.
Root_Cause: general_knowledge_gate.match_amenities. question_topic_terms stems the question to the single term 'build'; the clause 'if s >= 2 or len(topic) == 1' then admits any amenity scoring 1, and the leftover check passes trivially because the one term is covered. Measured in the container: at least eleven topics qualify, ALL at score 1 via the word 'building' -- Sustainability, Smart Controls, Power Resilience, Floor Areas And Layout, Data Sensors Coverage and more. ranked.sort is stable, so the two returned were the first two in amenity iteration order. A tie broken silently and presented as a finding (lessons #155).
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED. Two candidate rules were built and BOTH were measured and REJECTED, which is the useful result. (1) 'a single topic term qualifying more amenities than can be shown is generic': flips 204 of the 645 survey questions currently answered from an amenity, and reading the sample it breaks far more than it fixes -- 'Where is the elevator?', 'elevator status?', 'lifts working?', 'How many restrooms are in the building?', 'What kind of security does this building have?' all lose correct answers. (2) document frequency over the building's OWN topic vocabularies, which would have been building-agnostic: 'build' has df=0.093, LOWER than 'restroom' (0.203) and 'access' (0.220), both legitimate subjects. DF does not separate them and at any threshold that flips <=9 questions it does not catch this one. THE HONEST PATH IS ROUTING, NOT MATCHING: this is a question about the assistant's own reach, which the system already has lanes for (self_description answered 'did you go to college?' correctly in the same run) and which routing_contract could claim, the way _r_unmeasured_quantity_is_reach already claims a general_knowledge misclassification. That needs its own measurement over the corpora.

Title: A general-knowledge answer may name a DIFFERENT building, and the label does not say so
Description: 'what is the most unique design ?' -> 'General knowledge (not from this building's records): The most unique design often depends on the context, but one standout example is the *Guggenheim Museum Bilbao* in Spain. Designed by Frank Gehry...' Item 1 of tail N's eight WEIRD answers. An earlier run asked a clarifying question instead, which was better.
Root_Cause: The question was classified general_knowledge and reached _general_knowledge_node. general_knowledge_gate.records_answer correctly returned None -- measured: the question's topic terms are ['design', 'uniqu'], the only amenity scoring at all is 'About this assistant' at 1 via 'designed', and 'uniqu' is left over, so the coverage rule rejects it. The model then answered from world knowledge with the label applied. THE LABEL IS THE GAP: it says the answer is not from this building's records; it does not say the answer is ABOUT A DIFFERENT, NAMED BUILDING. Four other tail-N questions went through the same lane ('how can the building optimise energy use during weekends and holidays?', the heat-index one) and were labelled acceptable -- general guidance about buildings in general is fine. Naming another building is not.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED, and deliberately not attempted unmeasured. The narrow property is checkable AFTER generation rather than by routing: when the QUESTION names no proper-noun subject and uses a definite reference ('THE most unique design'), an answer that names a specific place or organisation is answering about something the user did not ask about, and a clarifying question is the better reply. Proper-noun detection is noisy, so this needs measuring over the general_knowledge lane's own traffic before it ships. A routing rule in the shape of _r_unmeasured_quantity_is_reach is the alternative.

Title: 'Are you the only building that can talk around here?' -- measured, and the obvious fix is a wash; pinned so nobody tries it on intuition

Title: Both spatial declines read Space.space_type, a field that does not exist, so neither has ever named a kind of place
Description: spatial_agent._nearest_target_unknown has shipped since BUG-377 with a sentence '**I can find the nearest:** <kinds>' that has never rendered on any building. Title: The anomaly lane makes the safety-adjacent overcrowding claim BUG-1244 deliberately refused to make, from a spike of 1 to 14 with no capacity and no place
Description: Found while re-asking BUG-1292's question live, 2026-09-30 19:51, occupant via /v1. 'Can you tell me which areas are currently overcrowded?' now routes anomaly -> planner and answers: 'Two high-severity anomalies indicate that A MONITORED ZONE's occupancy sensor has spiked from 1.0 to 14.0, a 1300 % increase and 4.1 sigma above the mean of 2.55. THIS SUGGESTS THE AREA IS CURRENTLY OVERCROWDED AND EXCEEDING SAFE CAPACITY LIMITS. ... immediately activate the building's crowd-control protocol -- close adjacent access points, redirect foot traffic, and alert security ... Yes. The spike and extreme z-score signal a potential safety hazard.' The Report section immediately below it says 'Anomalies / Concerns: None identified.'
Root_Cause:
DIAGNOSED. The claim is NARRATED, not computed -- which decides the fix. THREE things had to hold, each measured.
(1) THE PROMPT ASKED FOR IT. anomaly_agent._generate_summary built a free-text prompt requesting '2. The most critical issue and recommended action' and '3. Whether this requires immediate attention (yes/no and why)', with NO rules at all where the report lane's prompt carries six, and returned llm_manager.generate() raw. The live answer's three parts are that prompt's three items in order, and its closing 'Yes.' is item 3.
(2) A COMFORT BAND DECLARED `binary` WAS APPLIED TO A PEOPLE COUNT. shared/constants.COMFORT_RANGES['occupancy'] is {min 0, max 1, unit 'binary'}; bldg1's occupancy series are counts (BUG-954 measured max 21). MEASURED over 1,000 rows of a count series: 650 threshold anomalies, ALL high severity, each messaged 'is outside SAFE range [0.0, 1.0]'. The word 'safe' came from the code, not the model -- the second live reproduction quotes it back as 'the safe binary range of 0.0-1.0' and concludes 'severe overcrowding ... could trigger fire-code violations'. A genuinely binary point never leaves [0,1], so this band could ONLY fire on series it was the wrong band for.
(3) A FALL WAS CALLED A SPIKE. _spike_detection's pct_change is an absolute value, so 12.0 -> 1.0 was messaged 'spiked 92%' and the model read it as 'a real crowd surge' -- of a reading that had DROPPED.
NO PLACE IS NAMED because no anomaly row carries one: the three detectors emit column, value, timestamp, severity and message. 'A monitored zone' is the model filling a gap.
The lane STRUCTURALLY CANNOT KNOW A CAPACITY -- threshold reads a comfort band, z-score a distance from a series' own mean, spike a step change. That is why the guard below is unconditional rather than weighed against the evidence.
Fix_Approach:
FIXED, four changes, all in files this agent owns.
1. NEW orchestrator/services/anomaly/narration_guard.py -- a deterministic guard over the completion. Two families: (A) capacity/crowding claims and (B) instructions to escalate to people (crowd control, alert security, evacuate, close access points, activate a protocol). On a hit it does NOT decline and does NOT edit the sentence: it replaces the narration with factual_summary(), the same deterministic bullet list the agent already fell back to when the model was unreachable, so the reader still gets every anomaly with its column, numbers and severity and only the inference is dropped. Lesson #135 applied on purpose -- narrow what a guard may DO, not what it may notice. Patterns match CLAIM SHAPES, not words: 'the ventilation capacity is unchanged' and 'this is not a capacity issue' both pass. It logs '[anomaly_guard] ACTED' with the matched phrases, because a fail-open component needs a count of how often it acted. claims_are_supportable() states the no-capacity invariant as a test on the ROWS, so a future capacity-aware detector stands family A down instead of leaving a stale prohibition behind.
2. _threshold_detection skips a bound whose declared unit is 'binary' when the column takes more than two distinct numeric levels in the records. Keyed on the SIGNAL, never on a modality name, exactly as CAVEAT-405 keyed the sweep's spike detector.
3. The threshold message says 'outside the configured comfort range', not 'outside safe range'. COMFORT_RANGES is a comfort band, not a safety limit, and that one word was what licensed the safety claim.
4. _spike_detection says 'rose'/'fell' by direction and carries a `direction` field.
The prompt also now carries six rules (no capacity was read; a z-score says only that a value is unusual for that sensor; never instruct anyone to escalate; name only the column given and say the location is not recorded rather than inventing one; these may be sensor faults). The prompt is the request; the guard is the part that cannot be declined.
NOT MADE ANSWERABLE. BUG-1244's refusal stands untouched and test_tail_n_overcrowded_is_recorded_as_open_not_silently_routed still passes.
Verification:
RATE MEASURED, 2026-09-30, BEFORE the fix: **1 of 10 live asks** reproduced a capacity/overcrowding claim. Occupant on /v1 streaming (identity confirmed from the server's '[forwarded-user] occupant01@example.com -> occupant01 (role=occupant)' line, not from the flag -- lesson #169), resp_cache flushed before every ask and cache:sparql* once per run, a fresh chat id each time. Full answers in C:/Users/suhas/AppData/Local/Temp/ask_questions_20260930_211818.jsonl (read the file, not stdout -- CAVEAT-1293). Also in those ten: 4 x 'No sensor data available for anomaly detection', 1 x the alphabetical tie-break decline (lesson #155), 0 x the ungrammatical 'no a sensor of that kind', 0 x BUG-1292's 354-space dump (independent corroboration that BUG-1292's fix holds). Latencies 45.9-194.9 s, median ~144 s, with three other agents sharing the host -- NOT a property (CAVEAT-500, lesson #165).
THE ONE REPRODUCTION WAS WORSE THAN THE ORIGINAL REPORT: it carries TWO independent unfounded capacity claims in two lanes. '## Sensor Readings' tabled five 'Overcrowded areas' against an INVENTED 'exceed 10 occupants' threshold with all five places 'sensor name not recorded' (filed as BUG-1302, sql_agent, another agent's file); '## Anomaly Detection' gave the 'safe binary range 0.0-1.0 ... severe overcrowding ... fire-code violations ... enforce temporary occupancy limits' text this row fixes.
VERIFIED AT THE LANE with the REAL local model (gpt-oss:20b via host Ollama), same count-series shape, 1,000 records: threshold rows **650 high-severity -> 0**; the narration now names the column, states 'the sensor location is not recorded', asks for an INVESTIGATION step, says 'potential sensor fault', and unfounded_claims() on the final text returns **[]**. NOTHING TRUE WAS LOST, measured on the same records: a genuinely binary point gives 0 threshold rows before AND after, and a two-level binary point with a real out-of-band fault (0/7) is still caught (10 rows).
34 new tests in tests/test_anomaly_narration_does_not_claim_capacity.py, including both live narrations verbatim and seven negative controls; 219 pass / 0 fail across the nine existing anomaly, report, decline and phase-A files; 1,144 pass / 0 fail on the report/comfort/narration slice of -m unit. black + flake8 F821,F823 clean.
NOT VERIFIED END TO END: the fix needs an orchestrator restart, which this agent does not own. `orchestrator/` and `shared/` are bind-mounted rw, so `docker compose restart orchestrator` is enough -- no rebuild. RE-ASK AT LEAST 10 TIMES AFTER THE RESTART: at 1 in 10, four green asks would prove nothing (lesson #165, CAVEAT-891).
TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED AND FILED INSTEAD: CAVEAT-1301, the 'Anomalies / Concerns: None identified' self-contradiction (two detector families over the same rows, mechanism pinned by two tests); and BUG-1302 above.
LIVE AFTER RESTART, 2026-09-30: **10 asks, 0 unfounded capacity claims.** occupant01 on /v1 streaming, `resp_cache:*` flushed before each, fresh chat id, full answers captured to jsonl (not the 400-char stdout).
**THE INTENDED BEHAVIOUR IS VISIBLE IN ASK 8**, which is the important part -- the guard did not turn the question into a decline, it stripped the inference: '**10.00 people** was the highest count observed. The lowest count recorded was 0.00 people, giving a spread of 10.00 people.' A bare observed count, labelled as observed, with no capacity, no 'overcrowded', no crowd-control instruction, no 'safe range'.
The other nine: 4 declines on the old lead, 1 on the new BUG-1252 lead, 3 'I wasn't able to retrieve sensor readings', 1 referent-gate.

**A CAVEAT ON MY OWN SCAN, because it was wrong first.** A keyword scan flagged ask 9 as a hit on the word 'overcrowded'. Reading it: *"'currently overcrowded' does not exist in this building, so there is nothing to report about it"* -- the referent gate QUOTING THE USER'S OWN PHRASE. A regex cannot tell a claim from a quotation, and mine counted a quotation as a claim. The hand read is the measurement; the scan was the triage.

**AND THE STATISTICS DO NOT LET ME CALL THIS CLOSED.** The pre-fix rate was 1 in 10. At that rate the expected count in 10 asks is 1, so **0 of 10 is consistent with the fix working AND with luck** -- roughly a 1-in-3 chance of seeing zero even if nothing had changed. What DOES raise confidence is mechanical rather than statistical: the lane-level verification showed 650 high-severity threshold rows falling to 0 on the same records, `unfounded_claims()` returning [] on the regenerated narration, and a genuinely binary point still giving 0 before and after. Status VERIFIED_LIVE on that basis, with the rate recorded so a later session can re-measure rather than re-argue.

SEPARATELY CONFIRMED LIVE, 3 of 10 -- **CAVEAT-1303**: 'Try asking about temperature, CO2, humidity, or air quality -- these are the sensor types actively monitored here', in a building that measures **45** modalities. A building literal in core code (contract #3), shown to a reader as though it were the whole catalogue. || CORRECTED 2026-10-01, and the correction is measured. This row's family B matched `evacuat\w+`. Over the 2,912 stored answers in this repo that noun appears in 69 answers and **24 of them are hand-read GOOD** -- 'Evacuation provision', 'evacuation chair', 'Evacuation And Peeps', 'Intercom at refuge point (for the evacuation route, record RTE-013)', and the whole scripted answer to 'What is the evacuation procedure?'. Inside the anomaly lane it never fired on one, so the row's verification was not wrong; as a general-purpose family it was a landmine, and BUG-1302's row proposed wiring it lane-blind. Family B now matches the INSTRUCTION ('should be evacuated', 'evacuate the building', 'an evacuation is advised') and not the noun: 11 answers, 8 GOOD, all on capability or register lanes and therefore out of scope. Every one of this row's 34 tests still passes, including 'The floor should be evacuated.'
ALSO CORRECTED: `at (or near) (full) capacity` fired on 'you might want to check whether the boilers are running at full capacity during peak demand' -- a delta-T answer, twice in the corpus, on lane=sensor_data. A capacity-word hit is now dropped when its clause names plant and names nobody. 'lift' is deliberately not in that plant list.
AND THIS ROW'S OWN CAVEAT CAME TRUE AT THE LANE: 'a regex cannot tell a claim from a quotation, and mine counted a quotation as a claim.' Run with the real local model on 2026-10-01, `overcrowd\w*` and `capacity limit` matched inside two CORRECT refusals and the guard destroyed both. Fixed with a sentence-scoped epistemic-absence frame (CAVEAT-1377).
Refs: BUG-1244; BUG-954; CAVEAT-891; CAVEAT-405; CAVEAT-1301; BUG-1302; CAVEAT-1303; tail_N_2026-09-30_occupant_v1_read.md #30; CAVEAT-1376; CAVEAT-1377; tests/test_a_reading_is_not_a_state_or_an_order.py

Title: The one grader bucket CLAUDE.md permits quoting is an IN-SAMPLE number: WEIRD 89.1% on its calibration bank, 35.4% and kappa -0.046 on held-out answers
Description: CLAUDE.md records, as the project's one defensible grader claim, 'only the WEIRD bucket is trustworthy (89.1% precision) and only as a LOWER BOUND'. Measured 2026-09-30 over all 1,997 hand labels, that figure REPRODUCES EXACTLY -- 310/348 = 89.1% -- and it is the phase0 bank, which contains the 294 answers this grader was calibrated on. On the 744 labels from the held-out dev tails C-L the same bucket is 63/178 = 35.4% [28.7%, 42.7%]. Every bucket has NEGATIVE LIFT over the hand base rate out of sample: WEIRD 35.4% against a 39.7% base rate (-4.3 pp), GOOD_DECLINE 21.3% against 33.7% (-12.5 pp), GOOD_ANSWER 23.0% against 26.6% (-3.6 pp). Chance-corrected weird-or-not kappa per era: phase0 +0.314, demo path +0.056, HELD-OUT TAILS -0.046. A precision figure alone hid this because a bucket is easier to hit where its hand class is common; the lift column is what makes it visible (lessons #160, a metric arithmetically correct and structurally blind).
Root_Cause: The 89.1% was computed on the partition the grader was fitted to and recorded without the qualifier. Nothing in the repository measured it out of sample, because the 1,115 hand labels outside the phase0 bank had never been assembled into one set (CAVEAT-1347). The drift mechanism itself is CAVEAT-784/986's: a grader that scores SHAPE decays as the system's shapes change, and the tails were recorded after three waves of wording change.
Fix_Approach: NOT FIXED BY RE-CALIBRATION, deliberately, and for CAVEAT-986's reason: a shape rule cannot check whether a stated absence is true, so re-fitting would buy in-sample precision on a new partition and lose it again on the next. What is done instead is to make the qualifier inseparable from the number: scripts/audit_measurement_instrument.py --section claims prints each bucket in sample AND out of sample side by side and generates the permitted sentence from the counts, so the in-sample figure cannot be quoted alone. WHAT IS HANDED BACK: CLAUDE.md's line should read '89.1% on the phase0 bank, 35.4% on held-out answers' -- this agent may not edit that file.
Verification: python scripts/audit_measurement_instrument.py --section buckets --section claims. Grader-call integrity proved before any figure: 147/147 identical to grade_run. 1,997 labels, row alignment verified by question text with 0 failures.

Title: 1,115 of our 1,997 hand labels had never been used to check any instrument
Description: 27 recorded runs in docs/phase0/ carry a paired *_read.jsonl hand read: 1,997 labels in one vocabulary (GOOD_ANSWER 535, GOOD_DECLINE 477, WEIRD 985) with confidence on every row, and row alignment to their answer files verifiable by question text (0 failures). scripts/audit_grader_calibration.py reads 882 of them -- six runs of one 147-question bank. CAVEAT-788's own fix_approach asks for 're-calibration on the 441 newer hand labels'; the real figure is 1,115, and the 744 from the held-out dev tails are the only ones that can say anything about out-of-sample behaviour, which is what CAVEAT-1346 turned out to need.
Root_Cause: Each wave wrote its hand read beside its own run and the set was never assembled. The tails were labelled to measure the SYSTEM and nobody thought to point them at the INSTRUMENT, so the grader was only ever validated where it was fitted.
Fix_Approach: scripts/audit_measurement_instrument.py assembles all 27 pairs, verifies each alignment by question text rather than trusting the row index, and drops rather than mis-attaches a pair that does not line up. It does NOT re-calibrate anything (see CAVEAT-1346). Two exclusions are recorded in the source: the run3 half-files are superseded by the combined file so 22 answers are not double-weighted, and narration_validators_replay.jsonl is a replay record, not a hand read of answers.
Verification: python scripts/audit_measurement_instrument.py --section buckets (prints the label count and the split).

Title: A defect row that states a count but not the string it counted cannot be re-checked
Description: BUG-785 records '23 of 147 answers carry keyword-census text (0 in every earlier run)' and BUG-787 records 'word-level 17 -> 8'. Neither records the pattern. The census wording has since been rewritten, so the string is not recoverable from source either. Six candidate patterns were measured across all six stored runs on 2026-09-30 and none reproduces 23; the closest gives 10 at run 5 and 4 at run 6. The consequence is precise: the row's MECHANISM and TIMING corroborate and its MAGNITUDE is permanently unverifiable, so the row cannot be closed by measurement and cannot be trusted as a baseline either. The same shape is CLAUDE.md's own standing complaint about hand-maintained counts, one level down.
Root_Cause: A count derived by reading was written down as though derived by a rule, with no rule attached.
Fix_Approach: Convention, not code: a tracker row stating a count records either the exact matching expression or the command that reproduces it. Rows whose count came from a hand read say so, so nobody later attempts a regex re-check and mistakes a miss for a fix -- 'could not check' and 'checked, found nothing' must not render identically (lessons #20).
Verification: Six candidates measured over runs 1-6; per-run counts recorded in BUG-785's amended Description.

Title: ttl_gap_audit's inline decline list occupies no defensible point on the trade-off
Description: The fourth decline classifier CAVEAT-991 names is an inline decline_phrases list in scripts/ttl_gap_audit.py. Anchored to the hand labels it is beaten on the axis it exists for: recall floor 31/477 = 6.5% against publication_gate's 71/477 = 14.9%, for a near-identical error on hand-confirmed answers (9/535 = 1.7% vs 11/535 = 2.1%). It also disagrees with regression_answerability at kappa -0.042 over 2,868 answers -- below chance. Its phrases include 'not available', 'no information' and 'no sensor', which are not what this system emits; the derived lead set in scripts/audit_decline_markers.py shows what it does.
Root_Cause: An audit script grew its own marker list rather than importing one, and nothing compared them until CAVEAT-991.
Fix_Approach: Replace the inline list with a call to publication_gate.is_decline, which is strictly better on recall for +0.4 pp of error. This changes what ttl_gap_audit reports, so it is a decision with a number attached rather than a tidy-up: the gap count it produces will move. Not landed here -- this cluster's remit was to measure the instrument, and changing an audit's output mid-assessment is the mistake CAVEAT-784 is made of.

Title: Two sections of one planner answer count anomalies with two different detector families and neither knows about the other

Title: The SQL lane's narration invented its own overcrowding threshold -- 'exceed 10 occupants' -- and tabled five areas as overcrowded with no name and no capacity
Description: The SAME reproduction that carries BUG-1298 (ask 2 of 10, 2026-09-30 21:19, occupant on /v1) opens with a SECOND unfounded capacity claim, in a different lane, above the anomaly one. Verbatim: '## Sensor Readings | **Overcrowded areas (as of 2026-09-30 21:19:27)** | Area (sensor name) | Occupancy | Unit | sensor name not recorded | 11.0 | not recorded | ... (five rows) ... These five areas are the only ones in the latest snapshot that exceed 10 occupants, indicating they are currently overcrowded.' The threshold of TEN OCCUPANTS appears nowhere in this building's data: input/bldg1_occupancy_capacity.ttl holds 62 hbco:roomCapacity figures, every one stamped 'estimated ... Not certified', and none of them is 10. The model chose a round number and presented it as the building's. All five rows name NO place ('sensor name not recorded' x5), so the claim is also uncheckable.
Root_Cause: sql_agent._format_results is a free-text LLM narration over uuid/value/timestamp rows. Its prompt supplies labels and units and instructs 'state the unit, or say it is not recorded' (BUG-257), but carries no rule against inventing a threshold or a verdict, so a question using the word 'overcrowded' invites the model to supply the missing limit. This is the same shape as BUG-1298 one lane upstream: the narration is asked to answer the question, and the data it is given cannot.
Fix_Approach:
FIXED, and the row's own one-line prescription was MEASURED AND FOUND WRONG before it was followed. Two changes, both in files this agent owns.
1. `sql_agent._format_results` now carries four rules (8-11) where it carried none about what the readings establish: no capacity/limit/threshold may be introduced; a reading is a number and never a state; never tell anyone what to do; name only what the sensor metadata names. Each rule quotes the measured failure it exists for.
2. A DETERMINISTIC GUARD over the completion, `narration_guard.reading_lane_claims`, called after the model and before the reader. On a hit it does NOT decline and does NOT edit the sentence: it returns the readings themselves -- the per-series labelled summary from `summarise_series` plus the newest rows -- under one sentence saying no conclusion has been drawn. That is the same text the lane already emits when the model is unreachable, so the two paths cannot drift apart (lesson #135: narrow what a guard may DO, not what it may notice). It logs '[sql_narration_guard] ACTED' with the matched phrases, because a fail-open component needs a count of how often it acted.
THIS ROW SAID 'narration_guard.unfounded_claims() is lane-agnostic by construction ... it is a two-line call'. IT IS NOT, and wiring it as written would have been a net loss: see CAVEAT-1376. The families are now selected per lane and the guard is applied only where the evidence is readings.
Two new families were needed beyond the ones that existed: an occupancy LIMIT stated as a figure (family A2, which is what 'exceed 10 occupants' is -- family A's 'overcrowded' caught the verdict but not the threshold), and a reading narrated as a live fault (family D, BUG-1332). The report lane is guarded too, with `REPORT_LANE_FAMILIES`, which deliberately OMITS the operational-order family because that lane's prompt asks for actionable recommendations on purpose and the stored corpus holds a hand-read-GOOD report doing exactly that.
NOT MADE ANSWERABLE. BUG-1244's refusal stands untouched.

Title: A register decline states what the register records and names a third of it, omitting the field the question asked for
Description: Found by re-asking BUG-709's four uncovered rows live (occupant01, /v1 streaming, 2026-09-30, identity confirmed from the server's [forwarded-user] line). THREE OF FIVE re-asks came back as out_of_scope_decline, and each sentence understated its register. Verbatim: 'Which boundary-to-door route is currently evidenced for ambulance crews, stretcher teams and responders on foot, including step-free constraints?' -> 'The accessible route register (16 records) cannot answer this: it records route distance metres, route from and route to, and nothing about ambulance, boundary-to-door, constraints and crews.' The register holds isStepFree, status, surveyedOn, surveyedBy, doorOperation, liftStatus and eight more, and RTE-001/002/003 are literally boundary points (drop-off, station, bus stop) to the main door, surveyed 2026-07-14 by an access consultant, 15 of 16 step-free. isStepFree is the column the question NAMED -- which is why 'step-free' is absent from the 'nothing about' list -- and the sentence still did not name it. Also live: 'The booking register (16 records) ... it records location' (one field of five) and the asset engineering register naming 8 of 22 with no indication that 14 were dropped. BLAST RADIUS MEASURED over all 38 registers under input/documents that lift: the sentence accounted for 106 of 328 content columns (32%), median 29% per register, and 21 OF 38 NAMED A THIRD OR LESS -- access_permission 1 of 8, event_activity 1 of 8, hvac_operation 1 of 6, room_bookings 1 of 5, accessible_route 3 of 14. A reader cannot tell that sentence apart from a genuinely thin register, so it is a false statement about the records: design contract 4. The producer is live -- 3 of 11 live asks hit it -- and appears 11 times in the 2,912 stored answers.
Root_Cause: out_of_scope_decline filtered its field list with Vocabulary.names_what_a_record_is, which answers a DIFFERENT question -- 'do this column's VALUES name the record?', the test used to pick an identifier. Date, status, threshold, measurement and boolean columns fail that test wholesale, and those are the columns a question usually asks about. The fallback to the full column list only fires when the filter yields NOTHING, so a register where it yields one column (1 of 8) prints that one column as though it were the register. Independently, the sentence's two halves were decided by two different matchers: 'nothing about' is the complement of rf._term_matches_column, while 'it records' never consulted it, so a column the question reached could be omitted from one half without appearing in the other.
Fix_Approach: register_projection._what_it_records: name EVERY content column, ordered so the ones the question reaches lead (res.fields plus rf._term_matches_column over the prepared question's words >= 4 chars -- the same matcher that decides 'nothing about', so the halves cannot disagree), then the naming columns, then the rest. Still capped at eight for one readable sentence, and what the cap drops is DISCLOSED as 'plus N more fields' instead of silently omitted. Over-claiming is impossible by construction: every column named is a column the rows carry. Does NOT change whether the decline fires -- `speaks` is decided before this runs -- so the decline VOLUME is unchanged and this is a wording fix only. The remaining half of the sentence (raw question words in 'nothing about') is CAVEAT-1335, deliberately not touched: filtering it needs a part-of-speech judgement and the honest action here was to narrow the claim, not to add a word list (lessons #135).
Verification:

The three live declines now read 'it records step free, route distance metres, ...' (step free FIRST), 'it records criticality, parent asset, replaceability, ...' (criticality FIRST -- the register has it and the old sentence omitted it) and 'it records location, booked by role, effective from, effective to and expected attendees'. Title: Six static 'how to report an issue' topics were narrated to a reader as six ACTIVE issues and 'the only recorded problems at the moment'
Description: Live, occupant01, /v1 streaming, 2026-09-30 20:21, 170 s. 'Which dependency-aware recovery order should incident leaders adopt to restore priority services safely with the people and resources currently available?' answered: 'The building records show **six active issues** that incident leaders will need to address: Water leak / leakage; Broken or faulty light; Lift out of order; Heating fault / room too cold; Blocked or broken toilet; Broken door / access control fault. These are the only recorded problems at the moment.' NONE OF THOSE IS AN ISSUE. They are the six ontosage:MaintenanceIssue instances in input/bldg1_knowledge.ttl -- a static taxonomy of what a user CAN report, each carrying answerText, reportTo, contactEmail, contactPhone and layTerms and NO timestamp, NO status and NO occurrence. Nothing is leaking, no lift is out of order, no toilet is blocked. Verified against the live graph: 47 KnowledgeTopic and 30 InformationTopic instances, and the class carries no temporal or status predicate at all. This is the purest design-contract-4 failure in the cluster -- an invented conclusion presented as a record, with a currency claim ('at the moment') and an exhaustiveness claim ('the only') a reader in an incident role would act on. Worse than BUG-709's original examples, which misread a field; this one changes what KIND of thing a record is.
Root_Cause: Not the register lane. Chain from the container log for that turn: (1) '[ttl-route] capability via ontology triples: [Emergency Contacts] -- skipping LLM intent call'; (2) '[dialogue] HBCO concepts: [empty_space]' -- the question's 'currently available' resolved to an occupancy concept; (3) routing_contract capability_measurand_is_data fired, 'capability' -> 'sensor_data'; (4) sparql_agent 'class from HBCO concept empty_space: brick:Occupancy_Count_Sensor', 40 instance candidates -- a governance question bound occupancy sensors; (5) GraphDB RAG retrieval returned 5 entities / 132 triples, which is where the six MaintenanceIssue topics came from; (6) the narrator had no fact saying those topics are not occurrences, and wrote one. Two separable defects: the concept/routing step that put a recovery-order question in the sensor lane, and the narration that turned a reporting taxonomy into a live incident list. The SECOND is the contract-4 one and is what this row is about. || PRODUCER IDENTIFIED 2026-10-01, and it is not where this row guessed. A fifth live ask (occupant01, /v1 streaming, lane=sensor_data, 123.6 s) reproduced the failure and the container log for that turn names the chain end to end: `sql_agent` fetched 512 occupancy UUIDs, ran a 60-row-per-uuid query returning 30,720 rows, and `claim_binder mode=record lane=sql_result unbound=10/48 enforced=False` fired on the result. The narration is `sql_agent._format_results` -- a free-text completion over `(uuid, timestamp, value)` rows -- the SAME function as BUG-1302 one claim-family over. So this row's 'needs the owner's decision on WHERE the fact belongs' is answered for the narration half: it belongs in the reading-lane guard, which is now there. `claim_binder` already SAW this turn and is in record mode by design (CAVEAT-769 measured enforcement deleting five correct figures), so it is not the lever.
Fix_Approach:
NARRATION HALF FIXED; ROUTING HALF NOT MINE AND STILL OPEN.
FIXED: `narration_guard` family D -- a currency claim ('active', 'at the moment', 'currently listed') or an exhaustiveness claim ('the only recorded') about ISSUES, when the rows carry no status column at all. `sql_agent._format_results` now applies it after the model and replaces a hit with the readings themselves rather than declining. The invariant is stated as a test on the ROWS (`rows_record_a_state`), mirroring `claims_are_supportable`, so a lane that one day hands over an issue register WITH a status lifts the family by itself instead of inheriting a stale prohibition.
ALSO FIXED, and it is the more serious half of this row: the five-step 'Recommended recovery sequence (dependency-aware)'. BUG-709's rule against exactly that ('never issue an instruction, a plan, a recovery order or a priority') has been in a PROMPT since 2026-09-18 and held on three asks of four. Family C now catches the heading AND every step independently -- 'Ensure all intruder-detector zones ... are powered', 'Restore power', 'Re-open high-priority meeting spaces', 'before allowing occupants to enter', 'Re-establish occupancy monitoring', 'What to restore' -- so deleting the heading does not smuggle the steps past. Pinned by a test over the verbatim text of both procedures.
STILL OPEN, and it is the routing half this cluster does not own: a governance question about recovery ORDER resolved to the HBCO concept `empty_space`, was rerouted capability -> sensor_data by `capability_measurand_is_data`, and bound 512 occupancy sensors. The TTL-first fix this row proposes (a class-level fact that a KnowledgeTopic is a TOPIC and never an occurrence) is still the right long-term shape and still needs an ontology change, a re-upload and a restart. Same routing shape as BUG-1333.

Evidence: the full answer is in the run jsonl the harness printed, and the six labels are greppable in input/bldg1_knowledge.ttl (Issue_WaterLeak, Issue_BrokenLight, Issue_BrokenLift, Issue_HeatingCold, Issue_BlockedToilet, Issue_AccessDoor). Restore power to both chargers. 3. Re-open high-priority meeting spaces ... Verify that HVAC and lighting for these rooms are functional before allowing occupants to enter. 4. Title: 'None of the recorded series refers to a toilet, restroom, or accessibility facility' -- the graph holds 24 toilets and 18 accessibility features
Description: BUG-711 row 57 re-asked live, occupant01, /v1 streaming, 2026-09-30, 280 s: 'Is a Changing Places toilet available in or near Abacws, and what are the current verified access arrangements?' -> 'I did not find Changing Places toilet at or near Abacws in the records I searched. None of the recorded series refers to a toilet, restroom, or accessibility facility, and no access-arrangement data ... is present in the available records. Because the dataset was truncated, I cannot confirm whether such a toilet exists elsewhere in the building ...'. MEASURED against the live graph: 24 ontosage:ToiletFacility (12 of them 'Accessible gender-neutral toilet', two on each of floors 0-5, plus male and female washrooms on all six floors), 18 ontosage:AccessibilityFeature and 16 ontosage:AccessibleRoute -- one of which, RTE-014, is 'Reception to accessible washroom', radar-key, key held at reception. The correct answer is a partial: no Changing Places facility is recorded (that is a specific standard and the absence is real), but 24 washrooms are, 12 of them accessible, with surveyed step-free routes to them. Instead the reader got a total denial. TWO further faults in the same answer: 'Because the dataset was truncated' is internal processing vocabulary given to an occupant as a reason (and the answer ALREADY carried the proper sampling disclosure two paragraphs later, so it is a duplicate in the wrong register); and Sources cites 'Occupancy Sensing System' for a question about toilets.
Root_Cause: TWO CAUSES, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING. (1) ROUTING, shared with BUG-1332: the question routed to sensor_data (lane=sensor_data in the /v1 route envelope), so the lane that answered had only time-series rows in front of it, and 'none of the recorded SERIES refers to a toilet' is true of what it was looking at and false of the building. The capability lane, which holds ToiletFacility and AccessibilityFeature and which BUG-711's own root-cause note says matches them offline, never ran. (2) THE GUARD THAT EXISTS FOR EXACTLY THIS IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO THE WHOLE AMENITY FAMILY, and this was NOT previously suspected. _response_node applies _false_absence_from_a_held_register to EVERY lane's answer, ungated by method, and it did not fire. Measured why, offline against the real text: its first gate PASSED -- absence_wording.describes_retrieval_wide() returns True on this answer -- so the guard ran, read the graph, and had nothing to correct with. record_registry._DISCOVER_QUERY asks for `?cls rdfs:subClassOf+ ?root` with root in {o:Record, o:IntervalRecord}, and the live graph says: o:ToiletFacility rdfs:subClassOf o:Amenity -> o:Capability (NOT o:Record); o:AccessibilityFeature rdfs:subClassOf o:Amenity -> o:Capability (NOT o:Record); o:AccessibleRoute rdfs:subClassOf o:Record. So held_record_class() cannot return a toilet or an accessibility feature however plainly a question names one, false_absence_note() therefore returns nothing, and the guard passes the false absence through. A ROUTE question is protected and a TOILET question is not, for no reason a reader could guess. The exposed set is the 71 o:Amenity instances -- 24 ToiletFacility, 18 AccessibilityFeature, 16 DrinkingWater and the rest -- i.e. the things an occupant asks about most. This is BUG-947's ConfigurationPeriod finding one level over: a class outside the two declared roots is invisible to the registry by construction, and the metric that would show it does not exist.
Fix_Approach:
MEASURED, NOT INFERRED, AND THE BRIEF'S OWN PRESCRIPTION WAS THE FIRST THING REJECTED.
(1) WIDENING THE DISCOVERY ROOTS -- the obvious move, and the measurement kills it. `o:Amenity` added to `record_registry._RECORD_ROOTS`, measured with the repo's own instrument (`scripts/register_reach.py --snapshot` then `--compare`) over the 2,960-question stakeholder catalogue against the LIVE snapshot: **251 questions newly declined BY NAME against a class the building holds nothing of** -- ABSENT:Service 222 and ABSENT:Facility 29. `o:Service` and `o:Facility` have 0 instances so they never enter the HELD set, but a root also widens `_ALL_CLASS_TERMS`, and their class-name seeds are the bare words *service* and *facility*. Plus **47 questions of register churn on the answering path**: 15 move WorkspaceProfile (28 instances, 64 terms) to StudyArea (6 instances), 32 newly select Lift (2 instances) where CirculationTime owns "lift wait". The GAIN is 20 questions, and every one moves OFF the capability lane that already answers it. `o:Capability` was never a candidate: it admits KnowledgeTopic (47), InformationTopic (30), Procedure (9), MaintenanceIssue (6), Policy (3), PotabilityStatement (1) -- prose topics, and `register_reach.GENERIC_CAPABILITY_CLASSES` had reached that judgement independently. So the fix for one false-absence family would have created a larger one. REJECTED, and the numbers are written into `_RECORD_ROOTS` so nobody re-proposes it on intuition.
(2) THE STRUCTURAL FIX LANDED: `record_registry.held_amenity_classes()` -- the same SPARQL, rooted at `o:Amenity`, `FILTER(?cls != o:Amenity)` because GraphDB materialises `?c rdfs:subClassOf ?c` and the umbrella would otherwise arrive with 71 instances and the label "Amenity". It returns ordinary `RecordClass` objects, so `held_record_class` scores them with the SAME matcher -- no second matcher, which is BUG-947's shape. `absence_wording.false_absence_note` takes them as `amenities=` and `_false_absence_from_a_held_register` supplies them. Records are searched first and win a tie. An amenity gets its own sentence ("Abacws Building does record 24 toilet facilities, so I should not have implied it holds none") because "keeps toilet facility records" would send an occupant after paperwork.
(3) AND THE PROXIMATE CAUSE WAS SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY -- see BUG-1361. The guard was never going to fire on the answer a reader gets TODAY: `describes_retrieval_wide()` returns True on the 2026-09-30 text and **False** on the current one ("I couldn't tie that question to a reading I can give you"), measured by calling it. Fixed there too. **The structural half is still worth having: it is what stops the 2026-09-30 sentence recurring from any lane.**
NO NEW TEXT PATTERN WAS ADDED anywhere in this fix. The detection gate is the existing `describes_retrieval_wide`, unchanged; everything new is keyed on a graph count.
