Title: BUG-218's shipped 70.4%-precision operating point was calibrated on a FIVE-document corpus; the building now has 41, so the signal is near-inert
Description: Measured, not inferred. corpus_stats.COMMON_TERM_FRACTION is 0.4 and is documented in its own comment as measured on a 5-document corpus, where it gives a limit of 2 documents: 'limit <= 2, 26% of off-topic flagged, 6% of on-topic, 70.4% precision <- shipped'. input/documents now holds 41 files. So the limit today is int(41*0.4) = 16, and of the 4,625 distinct stemmed terms in the corpus exactly **59 (1.28%)** exceed it. A passage can therefore only be graded COMMON when every one of its shared terms is in that 59-word set, which over the 7,151 real survey questions is true of 96 (1.3%) and over the 4,060-question catalogue of 7 (0.2%). The shipped signal is not wrong, it is mostly switched off, and the 70.4% figure the row quotes no longer describes the system. Also worth knowing before anyone tunes it: the 59 COMMON terms now include genuinely topical building nouns -- room(33), servic(28), manager(26), lift(26), laboratory(26), access(25), plant(23), floor(23), fire(22), work(21), control(21), rout(20), maintenanc(19), water(18), alarm(17), atrium(17) -- and the building's own name, abacw(41). Lowering the fraction to restore the old limit would make 'fire', 'lift' and 'alarm' stop counting as evidence, which is the 47%-false-positive hedge BUG-218 measured and rejected, arriving by a different route.
Root_Cause: The threshold is expressed as a FRACTION of the corpus precisely so that corpus size would not change its behaviour, and that is the right design -- but the PRECISION it was calibrated to is a property of a particular corpus, and a 5-document corpus of thresholds and manuals has a completely different term distribution from 41 per-register documents that all share 'review', 'register', 'owner', 'due' and the building's name in their front matter. The fraction survived the corpus growing; the number quoted beside it did not, and nothing recomputes it.
Fix_Approach: NOT a code change and deliberately no re-tuning: a threshold sweep on today's corpus needs a hand-labelled set of today's document-citing answers, and the old 377-answer label set is from a build two routing generations ago. What is owed is the MEASUREMENT, not a new constant. Logged so the 70.4% is not quoted again as though it were current.
Verification: Computed from orchestrator/services/corpus_stats.document_frequencies('bldg1') against the live input/documents: 41 documents, limit 16, 4,625 distinct terms, 59 COMMON. Question-side exposure computed over paper/Survey analysis and results/corpus/classified_corpus.csv (7,151) and tasks/smart_building_questions.csv (4,060).

Title: A register decline's 'nothing about ...' half prints raw question words that name nothing a building could record
Description: The other half of BUG-1331's sentence, found in the same reading and NOT fixed with it. out_of_scope_decline ends 'and nothing about {beyond[:4]}', where beyond is res.unanswered -- the question's own words, as written. Live 2026-09-30: 'nothing about categories, justify, no-shows and owner-led' and 'nothing about combined, condition, cost and funding'. From the stored answers: 'nothing about abnormal-period, censoring, exclusion and locked', 'nothing about match, mode, strategy and zone', 'nothing about locked, minimizing, reduce and thermostat', 'nothing about cafe, overflowing and pronto', 'nothing about area-approval, effective, interval and prerequisites'. 'justify', 'combined', 'minimizing', 'reduce' and 'effective' are verbs and adjectives from the question; no building records them, and naming them back at the reader is the census-as-veto wording BUG-709's own verification says was removed from the register narration, surviving in a different producer. 11 of 2,912 stored answers carry the sentence, and 3 of 11 live asks on 2026-09-30 hit it, so the exposure is real but small.
Root_Cause: res.unanswered is built from res.unresolved with only three filters -- length >= 4, not a qualifier word, not a status-group word -- and no notion of whether a word could name a thing at all. grounding_guard.unmatched_terms already solves the same problem for a different caller by dropping manner adverbs and words about the conversation, and returning the surface spelling rather than the stem; that judgement was never applied here.
Fix_Approach: DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED in this pass. Separating 'justify' from 'criticality' is a part-of-speech judgement, and the honest options are a word list (which design contract 3 forbids in core code) or a morphological rule, which needs measuring over the catalogue before it ships -- a rule that drops '-ify', '-ize' and '-ed' would also drop 'certified', 'verified' and 'authorised', every one of which names a real column in these registers. Logged with the instances so the measurement starts from evidence.
Verification: Instances above are verbatim: three from the live run of 2026-09-30, the rest from grep over docs/phase0/*.jsonl.

Title: aggregate_lane case 6 re-admits every question parse_intent REFUSED, so a CHANGE, FORECAST or TIME-OF-DAY question is answered with a snapshot of the window
Description:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-30, occupant01 on /v1 streaming, both caches flushed, three consecutive turns. `aggregate_lane.parse_intent` returns None for TWO different reasons and case 6 -- the 'a bare measurand is not a refusal' summary -- could not tell them apart. Either no statistic word was found (a bare measurand, which case 6 exists for) or `_NOT_AN_AGGREGATE` matched, which is the module SAYING SO: its own comment reads 'Questions that use an aggregate word but ask for something else: a forecast, a change over time, or a time of day'. Case 6 re-admitted all of the second kind.
  'Has the humidity changed significantly in the past hour?' -> bound and fetched 275 humidity series, answered with a window summary; the relevance gate deleted it (OFF_TOPIC, 'does not address change, only gives current values') and the reader got BUG-1252's decline. This is tail N #23.
  'How has the temperature changed over time?' -> the same, deleted the same way.
  "how's the air quality index trending over the last few hours?" -> **the gate did NOT fire** and 'Across the building air quality is averaging 69.2 level' was shipped as the answer to a TRENDING question. So the gate is a messenger, not a backstop, and this family reaches readers.
FALSIFIED BY CALLING THE DECISION FUNCTION, NOT INFERRED FROM THE LOG (lessons #146): wants_lane('Has the humidity changed significantly in the past hour?', 6, False, True, ['humidity'], False, True, False) returned AggregateIntent(stat='summary', group='floor') before the fix and None after, with _NOT_AN_AGGREGATE.search() = True in both cases.
Root_Cause: One line: `return AggregateIntent('summary', 'floor', ...) if summary else None` in `wants_lane`, reached whenever `parse_intent` returned None, with no reference to WHY it returned None. The guard the module already had was placed in `parse_intent` and bypassed by the path added later. lessons #156's shape -- a narrowing that a downstream branch silently undoes.
Fix_Approach:
KEYED ON THE MODULE'S OWN REFUSAL, NOT ON A SECOND WORD LIST. `wants_lane` now consults `_NOT_AN_AGGREGATE` in the summary branch and returns None, logging '[aggregate] not claimed: the question asks about a change, a forecast or a time of day, which a summary of the window cannot answer' so the case is countable. A second regex beside `_NOT_AN_AGGREGATE` was deliberately NOT written: two parts of the system holding their own answer to one question is the shape this repo keeps paying for, and a test pins that the gate reads `_NOT_AN_AGGREGATE` itself.
ORDER IS THE CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT: the gate sits BELOW the `profile` branch, so a time-of-day question ('When is the building busiest?') still reaches the hourly profile even though `_NOT_AN_AGGREGATE` matches 'when'. Pinned by test.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: no answer becomes correct. The lane declines and the question falls through to the breadth refusal (`too_broad_reply`, which names two narrower questions) or the per-sensor read. Per design contract #4 and the task's own rule, a decline beats a statistic nobody asked for -- but the CURE for a change question is a lane that computes the change, which does not exist. Not claimed as fixed.
Verification:
BLAST RADIUS MEASURED OVER BOTH CORPORA BEFORE THE CHANGE -- tasks/smart_building_questions.csv (4,060) + paper/Survey analysis and results/corpus/classified_corpus.csv (7,151) = 11,211 questions. 979 are claimed by case 6 today. **171 move**: 91 asking how something CHANGED, 32 about the future, 24 about when, 24 asking HOW something is monitored (BUG-1317, the same gate). MOVES BROKEN: 0 found. Every real-corpus question in the two non-delta families was HAND-READ -- 19 future, 16 when -- and every one is a capability or explanation question that no building-wide mean answers: 'Will I get alerts if air quality is poor?', 'When noise levels are too high how does the building help block that out?', 'Can alerts be sent when air quality is too low?'. The 59 real-corpus delta questions are 'is the CO2 trend rising fast enough to signal poor ventilation?', 'Has the air quality suddenly decreased?', 'How has the temperature changed over time?' and similar -- a snapshot answers none of them.
NOT MEASURED, AND SAID SO: the user-visible outcome AFTER the fall-through, for all 171. Two of the three live cases already ended in a decline, so for those the change is the same outcome reached earlier and without fetching 275 series; the third (air-quality trending) moves from a wrong answer to a decline. A restart is needed to re-ask any of them, and the session was forbidden to restart.
TESTS: tests/test_a_summary_names_the_quantity_it_summarised.py, 33 pass -- the three live questions and four more of the shape verbatim from classified_corpus.csv, four counterfactual bare-measurand questions that MUST still be summarised, a genuine total that must still parse, the profile ordering, and a mechanism pin. Neighbouring slice re-run green: 426 passed over 13 aggregate/comparison/summary/floor files. black + flake8 F821/F823 clean.
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-30 after restart, and this was the case that proved the gate is NOT a backstop.
Q: 'how's the air quality index trending over the last few hours?' -> **'The air quality index **fell by 17.8 levels (a 20.4 % decrease)** from 10:00 to 20:00. The highest hourly mean was 89.8 at 12:00, and the lowest was 69.4 at 20:00 ... declined steadily after the 12:00 peak.'** A trend, for a trending question.
Before the fix this question **SHIPPED** 'Across the building air quality is averaging 69.2 level' AS THE ANSWER, with the relevance gate SILENT -- while the sibling humidity and temperature change questions were caught and deleted. So 'the gate will catch a wrong-question answer' is not a safety net: it caught two of three.
CAVEAT-1002's truncation disclosure rides along correctly ('these readings are a SAMPLE of the newest data ... not the whole of it').

Title: 'how is X monitored' is parsed as a TOTAL and answered with readings -- 24 questions, 23 of them from the real survey corpus
Description:
Tail N #45, re-asked live 2026-09-30 to establish whether it still reproduces. IT DOES, and the shape has changed: 'how is water consumption montored here?' is no longer deleted by the relevance gate, it now ANSWERS -- '**Water Flow Sensor HotWater recorded the highest flow rate of 26.10 L per min.** The other flow sensors show latest rates between 19.40 L per min (Floor3) and 25.40 L per min (Floor1)' -- which is a data dump for a question about the MONITORING METHOD. The gate's earlier verdict on this question, 'Provides data, not explanation of monitoring method', was exactly right.
MEASURED BY CALLING parse_intent DIRECTLY: it returns stat='total', group='building', because `_TOTAL` matches `consum\w*` and the question says 'consumption'. `wants_lane` then returns that intent through its case 3 (a total of something measured as a rate). `summary_ok` was False, so this is NOT case 6 -- a different entry point from BUG-1316, on the same module.
OVER BOTH CORPORA, 101 questions have the 'how is X monitored' shape and the aggregate lane claimed 24, of which 23 are from the REAL survey corpus: 'How do you measure noise levels in dB?', 'how is humidity monitored', 'How do you track occupancy?', 'How does the building detect poor air quality?', 'How do you monitor water usage and flow rate?', 'How is relative humidity monitored in the building?', 'How does the building sense temperature in real time?'. Each was answered with a building mean of the quantity it names.
Root_Cause: `_TOTAL`'s `consum\w*` and the `_MEAN`/`_MAX` words fire on the quantity a method question names, and nothing in `parse_intent` asked whether the question is about the readings at all. `aggregate_support.is_readings_question` is exactly that test and is consulted ONLY for `summary_ok`, so the parsed paths never see it.
Fix_Approach:
`_MONITORING_METHOD` added to `_NOT_AN_AGGREGATE`: 'how is/are/do/does/did/can/could <up to 4 words> monitored|measured|tracked|recorded|detected|sensed|calculated|computed|collected|gathered|determined|assessed'. One regex covers BOTH entry points, because `parse_intent` consults it and BUG-1316's new gate consults it too -- so a method question is refused whether or not it names a statistic. Deliberately NOT added to `_NOT_READINGS`, which would have reached only the summary path that was already declining these.
CONTAINMENT, NOT CURE, and the row must not be read as claiming otherwise: the 24 move from a statistic to a decline. The right answer to 'how is humidity monitored' comes from the metadata or capability lane, and routing already sent these to sensor_data/analytics, so declining here does not deliver them there. That is a routing question and was not touched.
Verification:
Measured over both corpora before and after: 101 questions match the shape, the lane claimed 24 before (23 real-corpus) and claims 0 after. MOVES BROKEN: 0 -- every one of the 24 was read and every one is a method question. 'How much water did we use this week?' still parses as stat='total', pinned by test, so a genuine consumption question is untouched.
The 91+32+24 temporal movers of BUG-1316 are counted separately; the two changes together move 171 of 11,211.
TESTS: six of the 24 verbatim, in tests/test_a_summary_names_the_quantity_it_summarised.py (33 pass), asserting both that parse_intent returns None and that wants_lane declines.

Title: BUG-1317's method pattern is keyed on the VERB, so the verbatim question that found it -- 'how is water consumption montored here?' -- still is not caught
Description:
Recorded this way round on purpose. The fix for BUG-1317 stops the aggregate lane claiming 24 method questions, and the one question that started the investigation is NOT among them, because it spells 'monitored' as 'montored'. Verified by calling parse_intent on the verbatim string after the fix: it still returns stat='total', group='building'.
The real survey corpus misspells freely -- 'montored', 'rainwter', 'buidling', 'ventilaton', 'temperture', 'HAW HAS THE TEMPERATURE CHANGED' -- and every pattern in this system that keys on an English verb or noun has the same blind spot. Extending the pattern with each observed typo is the stop-list failure lesson #170 was written about; the answer is a spelling-tolerant matcher (edit distance 1 on the verb stem), which is a piece of work in its own right and belongs to whoever owns the matchers.
Root_Cause: A literal-alternation regex cannot match a string one character away from its alternatives. Not a defect in the fix; a boundary of the technique.
Fix_Approach: Not fixed. Two options, neither taken here: (a) a one-edit-distance match on the verb stems inside `_MONITORING_METHOD`, measured over both corpora for over-capture; (b) run the question through a spell-normaliser before any matcher sees it, which would help every pattern in the system at once and is the larger and better answer. Measure the over-capture before either: 'montored' is one edit from 'monitored' but so are many real words.
Verification: Reproduce: call orchestrator.services.aggregate_lane.parse_intent('how is water consumption montored here?') -- returns AggregateIntent(stat='total', group='building'). The correctly-spelled 'how is water consumption monitored here?' returns None.

Title: 'This building does not have workplace occupancy sensors' -- a FALSE ABSENCE over 501 occupancy series, and the guard built for this sentence detected it and stood down
Description:
Found while re-verifying BUG-710 row 88 live, 2026-09-30, occupant01 on /v1 streaming, both caches flushed. Question, verbatim: 'Which workplace peaks and troughs are stable enough to plan for, and how do they vary across weekdays, term phases, projects and exceptional periods?'
Answer, verbatim: "The building's records do not contain any data on workplace occupancy, so we cannot identify stable peaks or troughs for planning purposes. - **Sensor type missing**: *This building does not have workplace occupancy sensors.* - **Available information**: The building model only records organisational capabilities, department scopes, assistance contacts, policy owners, stock items, and positional data. None of these provide real-time or historical occupancy metrics." It then advises the reader to **install occupancy sensors**.
MEASURED AGAINST THE GRAPH, distinct points carrying a timeseries reference: Occupancy_Count_Sensor **257**, Occupancy_Status **243**, Parking_Occupancy_Sensor **1** -- **501 occupancy series**. The sentence is a statement about the world and it is false, and it tells a reader to buy hardware the building already has.
THIS IS A CHANGE IN KIND FROM WHAT BUG-710 RECORDED, AND FOR THE WORSE. That row logged row 88 as 'No readings were found for the requested sensor(s) ... Try a more recent time window' -- a WINDOW-absence, which is honest about what it does not know. It is now a GRAPH-absence, which is the one wording the 'four kinds of nothing' lesson says may never be used unless the graph is empty. Same row, worse failure.
Root_Cause:
TWO parts, and the second is the interesting one.
(a) `sparql_agent`'s reasoning prompt instructs, verbatim: 'If the user asks for a sensor type that is NOT in the ontology, clearly state: "This building does not have [sensor type] sensors."' The question resolves no sensor class -- 'workplace peaks and troughs' names occupancy only by implication -- so the context handed to the model held registers and no points, and the model did as instructed. A BINDING failure rendered as a graph-absence: BUG-1271's residual pattern, 'why a named quantity that the graph holds fails to bind'.
(b) THE GUARD FOR EXACTLY THIS SENTENCE RAN AND STOOD DOWN, and this was MEASURED by calling it, not inferred (lessons #146). `absence_second_chance.find_lack_claims` on the verbatim answer returns ONE claim, kind='does_not_have', subject='workplace occupancy sensors', lack_terms=['occupancy', 'workplac']. So detection is perfect. The rewrite then requires every content word of the claimed-missing thing to be accounted for by what the building holds -- the module's own words, 'deliberately conservative ... so "embodied carbon" is not held by a carbon-monoxide sensor' -- and no occupancy sensor accounts for 'workplac'. The module's docstring names this exact sentence ('This building does not have occupancy sensors' (467 occupancy series exist)) as the thing it was built to catch, and ONE adjective defeats it.
Fix_Approach:
NOT FIXED IN THIS SESSION, DELIBERATELY, and the reasoning is the point of the row.
The obvious fix -- relax 'every content word must be accounted for' to 'the HEAD noun must be' -- is precisely the trade `absence_second_chance` already reasoned about and wrote down, with a worked counter-example. Widening it on the evidence of one hand-read instance is what CAVEAT-972 and BUG-1073 refused. It needs measuring against the stored answer corpus (the 73-probe pack plus every docs/phase0/*.jsonl, ~2,985 answers) for how many TRUE absences it would start rewriting into false reassurances -- which is the worse direction.
The other end is better and is where I would start: (a) the prompt instruction in `sparql_agent` licenses a claim about the BUILDING from a context that only shows what THIS QUERY returned, and the honest form is about the query ('I could not find <type> in what I searched'); (b) 'workplace peaks and troughs' should resolve to occupancy through HBCO, and does not.
OWNERSHIP: `orchestrator/services/absence_wording.py` and the decline-wording cluster are another agent's this session.
|| MEASURED BOTH DIRECTIONS 2026-10-01 AS THE ROW ASKED, AND THE ANSWER IS: **DO NOT RELAX IT.** The previous agent's refusal was right and there is now a number behind it.
POPULATION, COMPLETE RATHER THAN SAMPLED. Every stored answer this project holds -- `Datasets/System evaluation/Evidence pack - 73 probes/answers.jsonl` plus all 60 `docs/phase0/*.jsonl` -- is **2,137 answers once de-duplicated on (question, answer)**, and the product's own `find_lack_claims` finds **13 lack claims in all of them**, 13 distinct subjects: barometric meter sensors, beightness, brief corridor, car parking, efficiency, escalator, floor 13, occupancy sensors, parking garage, swimming pool, turbine, underground parking, workplace occupancy sensors.
RUN THROUGH THE PRODUCT'S OWN `GraphReach.holds()` AND THROUGH THE SAME SENSOR ARM WITH THE ACCOUNTING RELAXED TO THE HEAD NOUN, on identical evidence: rewritten today 1 ('occupancy sensors' -> occupancy, 256 series); rewritten by both 1; **rewritten ONLY by the relaxation 1** -- 'workplace occupancy sensors' -> occupancy, 256, which is TRUE and is this row; rewritten by neither 11; LOST by the relaxation 0. So on the historical corpus the relaxation is 1 gain, 0 losses.
THAT IS NOT A LICENCE, AND THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE SET. 13 sentences cannot bound a rule's risk, so the module's own worked counter-example and its nearest neighbours were run directly. Over 17 subjects the relaxation produces **4 new rewrites and 3 of the 4 are FALSE REASSURANCES**:
    'embodied carbon'         -> "This building **does** measure energy submeter (6 series)"   FALSE
    'embodied carbon sensors' -> same                                                          FALSE
    'street noise sensors'    -> "This building **does** measure noise (234 series)"            FALSE  (234 INDOOR sensors; street noise is a different thing, and an adjective changing the referent is the exact shape of the defect)
    'workplace occupancy sensors' -> occupancy, 256                                             TRUE
One true rescue against three false reassurances, and the false ones are in the direction the row calls worse. Two probe rows hit a `sensor_binder` TimeoutError, so 3 is a LOWER bound. The relaxation is not even consistent where it helps: 'individual desk occupancy sensors' has head 'occupancy' and is NOT rescued, because the binder does not bind that phrasing.
HONEST LIMIT OF THIS MEASUREMENT: the 17 counter-examples are hand-chosen as a stress set, so they establish that the false direction is REAL and common, not its base rate.
SO THIS ROW STAYS OPEN AND THE FIX BELONGS AT THE OTHER END, exactly as its own Fix_Approach said: `sparql_agent`'s reasoning prompt licenses "This building does not have [sensor type] sensors" -- a claim about the WORLD -- from a context showing only what ONE query returned. The honest form is about the query. Not attempted here: it touches every sparql turn and would need its own measurement over the catalogue, which this session did not have the budget for. A measured refusal is the result; the prompt is the next move.
Verification:
PARTIALLY FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-01, occupant01 on /v1, both caches flushed, after restart.
**THE FALSE CLAIM IS GONE.** The row's own recommendation was taken -- not the guard relaxation it argued against, but the other end: `sparql_agent`'s reasoning prompt no longer licenses a claim about the BUILDING from a context that shows only what ONE query returned. Instruction 3 was:
    'If the user asks for a sensor type that is NOT in the ontology, clearly state: "This building does not have [sensor type] sensors."'
and is now:
    'The data above is WHAT ONE QUERY RETURNED, not an inventory of the building. If a sensor type the user asked about is not in it, say so ABOUT THE SEARCH -- "I could not find [sensor type] in the records I searched" ... NEVER write that the building does not have it ... For the same reason, never advise anyone to install, buy or fit equipment.'
**MEASURED BLAST RADIUS over 2,861 de-duplicated stored answers: 11 answers (0.38%) claim the building lacks something, and 3 of the 11 are demonstrably FALSE** -- all occupancy, over 501 series, including 'Is there anyone in the lobby?' answered 'This building does not have occupancy sensors'. The other eight are barometric pressure, free-cooling and FCUs, which this building genuinely lacks; for those the new wording is weaker and still true.
LIVE RESULTS:
  * the row's verbatim question now declines honestly -- 'I couldn't tie that question to a reading I can give you, so I have no figure for it' -- with **no absence claim and no hardware advice** (it had told the reader to INSTALL occupancy sensors);
  * 'Is there anyone in the lobby?' -> 'I could not find any occupancy or lobby-presence sensor **in the records I searched**' -- the new wording, scoped to the search.
**WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND THE ROW STAYS OPEN FOR IT: root cause (a)'s BINDING half.** The building holds 501 occupancy series and a question about workplace occupancy still binds none of them, so the honest sentence is now true and still unhelpful. That is BUG-1271's residual -- why a named quantity the graph holds fails to bind -- and it is a different piece of work. The guard relaxation this row argued against was NOT attempted.
Tests: `tests/test_a_failed_search_is_not_an_absent_sensor.py`, 8 pass, pinning that no variant of the old instruction returns and that the hardware prohibition stays. Slice `-k 'sparql_agent or sparql or absence'`: 281 pass.

Title: 'The guard is lane-agnostic by construction, it is a two-line call' was measured false: wiring it as written would have rewritten 24 hand-read-GOOD answers
Description: BUG-1302's Fix_Approach prescribed the fix in one line: 'narration_guard.unfounded_claims() is lane-agnostic by construction and catches this text as written -- it is a two-line call.' Measured over every stored answer this repo holds (2,912: the 73-probe evidence pack plus every docs/phase0/*.jsonl, 1,465 hand-read), the two families as they stood would have altered 75 answers and **26 of them are hand-read GOOD**, 24 from family B alone. The casualties include 'What is the evacuation procedure?' -- a SCRIPTED DEMO QUESTION -- 'is there a muster point outside the building?', 'how do you monitor security cameras?', 'Which refuge points are defective, and who owns them?' and 'Who owns the evacuation chairs?'. Every single one is a capability or register answer QUOTING A RECORDED PROCEDURE.
Root_Cause: The families were written from one lane's failure and their names generalise further than their patterns do. Family B matched the NOUN `evacuat\w+` and `emergency services`; family A matched `at (or near) (full) capacity`. Inside the anomaly lane, whose rows are z-scores and comfort bands, neither could fire on a recorded fact, so 34 passing tests and a live 10-ask run said nothing about what happens elsewhere. **A guard's SCOPE is part of the guard, and it is the part that a single lane's verification cannot measure.** The distinction the patterns could not make -- between quoting a procedure the building records and inventing one -- is not a property of the text; it is a property of which rows produced it.
Fix_Approach: Three things, not one. (1) Family B rewritten to match the instruction rather than the noun: 69 answers -> 11, all on non-reading lanes. (2) A plant-context exclusion for capacity words, after 2 of the 4 reading-lane hits turned out to be 'the boilers are running at full capacity'. (3) `reading_lane_claims(text, rows, families=...)`, called ONLY by lanes whose evidence is readings, with `REPORT_LANE_FAMILIES` for the report lane, which is allowed to recommend an action. The four blast-radius numbers are pinned by tests that read the real corpus, and one of those tests asserts that the register, capability and sparql modules do NOT import the guard.
Verification: Final blast radius, same corpus: 18 answers altered lane-blind, 9 hand-read GOOD; 2 of the 295 recorded-reading-lane answers, 0 GOOD; 0 of the 58 report/recommend answers. All seven measured live failures still caught verbatim. The 24-GOOD measurement is itself kept as a test (`test_the_noun_only_families_would_have_been_a_disaster`, lower bound 19 after the narrowing) so the reason for the design cannot be forgotten and quietly reverted.

Title: My own guard destroyed two CORRECT refusals, because 'overcrowded' reads the same inside a claim and inside a denial
Description:
Verified at the lane with the real local model (gpt-oss:20b on host Ollama), 2026-10-01, driving `sql_agent._format_results` over occupancy-count rows shaped like bldg1's. Both completions had OBEYED the new prompt rules and said so:
  'These figures reflect the most recent measurements. No capacity limits or thresholds were supplied, so no assessment of overcrowding or safety limits can be made.'
  'Because no capacity or threshold figures are available, I can't determine whether any of these areas are overcrowded.'
The guard replaced BOTH with a bullet list of statistics. These were the best answers the lane has ever given to that question and the guard deleted them.
Root_Cause: `overcrowd\w*` and `capacity limit` match unconditionally. BUG-1298's docstring claims the patterns 'match CLAIM SHAPES, not words' and offers two examples that happen not to match; it does not hold for a sentence that names the claim in order to deny it. BUG-1298's own Verification already recorded this shape one level up -- 'a regex cannot tell a claim from a quotation, and mine counted a quotation as a claim' -- where a keyword scan miscounted the referent gate quoting the user. **The same defect, in the same cluster, two days apart: this is the apparatus being the bug for the third time.** And it is worse here than there, because there it corrupted a measurement and here it would have reached a reader.
Fix_Approach: A sentence-scoped absence frame: a family hit whose own clause carries an epistemic-absence marker ('no capacity/limit/threshold/figure/record', 'not recorded/supplied/available', 'cannot/can't/unable to', 'do not have/hold/contain/record', 'no X is recorded') is not a claim. Deliberately EPISTEMIC rather than any negation, so 'the area is not merely busy, it is overcrowded' is still caught. Clause boundaries include `|`, so the five 'sensor name not recorded' cells in BUG-1302's own table cannot excuse the prose beneath them -- pinned by a test. The residual hole (a claim phrased with an absence marker beside it) is accepted on purpose and stated in the code: a missed claim leaves the prompt rule as the only defence, which is where we already were, while a destroyed refusal costs a correct answer, and that is the worse of the two.
Verification:
Both destroyed completions are now negative controls in tests/test_a_reading_is_not_a_state_or_an_order.py, verbatim, with five more of the same shape, plus two tests that the frame is not a general escape hatch. 87 pass / 0 fail across the two guard files (53 new + the 34 existing, unchanged). Re-run at the lane with the same real model afterwards. Blast radius fell from 22 answers to 18 lane-blind and from 11 hand-read-GOOD casualties to 9, with every measured live failure still caught.
THE SECOND FINDING IS THE MORE USEFUL ONE AND IT IS INFERRED FROM TWO ASKS, NOT MEASURED AT SCALE: with rules 8-11 in the prompt, the model refused correctly BOTH times it was asked the two questions that had produced BUG-1302 and BUG-1332. The prompt rules may be doing most of the work; the guard exists because BUG-709 measured the same kind of rule holding 3 times in 4. Neither number is a rate -- two asks and five asks respectively.

Title: One HBCO lay term ('available') threw away THIRTY of the building's own amenity triples, and the reader was told there was nothing to read
Description:
Split out of BUG-1333 because it is the PROXIMATE cause of that row's live failure and it is far wider than toilets. Measured live 2026-10-01, occupant01 on /v1 streaming, both caches flushed, ONE ask. Question, verbatim: 'Is a Changing Places toilet available in this building?' Answer: 'I couldn't tie that question to a reading I can give you, so I have no figure for it.' `lane=sensor_data`, 21.1 s.
THE CONTAINER LOG FOR THAT TURN HAS THE WHOLE THING IN THREE LINES:
  [ttl-route] capability via ontology triples: ['Accessible gender-neutral toilet - Floor 0 (one end)', ... 30 labels, twelve of them accessible toilets, one per end of each of floors 0-5 ...] - skipping LLM intent call
  [dialogue] HBCO concepts: ['empty_space']
  [routing-contract] capability_measurand_is_data: 'capability' -> 'sensor_data'
The deterministic amenity probe DID fire, DID claim the turn, and the concept-stage rule overruled it. Every one of the probe's 24 veto clauses was measured False for this question, so nothing was wrong before the rule. The route envelope reports `intent_from_dialogue: 'sensor_data'` and `overrides_applied: []`, so it does not even record that dialogue said `capability` -- reading the envelope alone, this looks like a classifier error.
Root_Cause:
`hbco:empty_space` (ontology/hbco_mappings.ttl) declares the BARE lay term "available" alongside "empty", "vacant", "unoccupied", "available desk". So any question containing that adjective resolves an occupancy measurand, `grounding_guard.has_measurand_concept` returns True, and `_r_capability_measurand_is_data` converts the turn to a data lane -- discarding whatever the capability probe had already resolved.
THE DEEPER FAULT IS THAT THE PROBE'S RESULT WAS NEVER ON THE BUS. It existed for the length of one log line. `_orchestrator`'s concept-stage context was built with THREE keys (intent, concepts, entities), so a rule could not have consulted it however it was written. Lesson #170 one layer up -- a resolved value logged and then discarded -- and lesson #157's twin: not a marker with one reader, a marker with none.
That rule already carried EIGHT word- or shape-based carve-outs, each added after a live wrong answer. A ninth would have been the nineteen-`and not`-clauses pattern this repo has already named as the tell.
Fix_Approach:
KEYED ON THE GRAPH, AND THE TTL-FIRST OPTION WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED FIRST.
REJECTED (a): remove the bare "available" lay term. It is wrong in BOTH directions (lesson #141). Counted word-bounded over 4,060 catalogue questions and the 7,151-row real survey corpus: 130 and 94 contain "available", and 122 of the 130 carry no other occupancy term, so real occupancy questions lose their measurand -- 'can the system notify me if a desk becomes available nearby?', 'which rooms have recently become available?', 'can i get a real time map of available spaces across the building?' -- while the amenity questions in the same list are the ones being broken today: 'water available?', 'coffee available?', 'seating available?', 'Is there a fire exit map available on each floor?', 'Can I navigate to the nearest available restroom?', 'Are there any accessibility features available near me?'. One word cannot separate them.
LANDED (b): put the probe's result where the decision is made, and let the building's own triples outrank a lay term. (1) `dialogue_agent`'s amenity short-circuit returns `capability_amenity_facts` (a count) and `capability_amenity_labels` (for the log). (2) `_orchestrator` persists it and -- this is the load-bearing half -- ADDS IT TO THE CONCEPT-STAGE CONTEXT, which is the only thing a rule can see. (3) `_r_capability_measurand_is_data` stands down when that count is non-zero, and logs that it did so, so the stand-down is countable.
NARROW BY CONSTRUCTION SO BUG-225 IS NOT REOPENED: a question that asks for a VALUE still moves, tested with `metered_quantity_question` / `measured_reading_question` / `_AGGREGATE_SHAPE_RE` -- the tests their own rules already use, so there is one definition of each and not two. 'How many parking bays are free right now?' still reaches a data lane; that case is pinned by a test, because the capability lane once answered it with the building's CATERING amenities over a parking sensor holding 5,090 rows.
NO TEXT PATTERN IS INVOLVED anywhere in this fix. The predicate is an integer count of graph matches.
Verification:
LIVE, occupant01 on /v1 streaming, both caches flushed, one ask each side of the fix, orchestrator restarted between them by the coordinator (I do not restart).
BEFORE 00:20 -- `lane=sensor_data`, 21.1 s, 'I couldn't tie that question to a reading I can give you, so I have no figure for it.'
AFTER 00:52 -- `lane=capability`, `intent_from_dialogue=capability`, `final_node=capability`, **1.1 s**, and the answer names 'Accessible gender-neutral toilet - Floor 0 (one end)', '(other end)' and 'Floor 1 (one end)' with the location text for each, footed 'Answered live from the building's own records'.
The running process was confirmed to carry the change before the ask -- `held_amenity_classes` present, `false_absence_note` signature carrying `amenities`, `capability_amenity_facts` in the rule's source, container StartedAt 23:37:58Z -- because verifying the file is not verifying the process.
OFFLINE: the capability resolver returns 30 facts at score 5 for this verbatim question (12 accessible toilets among them), measured inside the container with the product's own SPARQL executor. An earlier probe of mine reported 0 facts and THAT WAS MY APPARATUS -- I had passed `run_sparql_select`'s `{'ok','rows'}` shape to a resolver whose `_bindings` expects raw SPARQL JSON. Corrected before anything was concluded from it.
TESTS: tests/test_an_amenity_is_something_the_building_holds.py -- 30 amenity triples outrank the lay term for both phrasings of the question; the rule still returns sensor_data at 0 facts (the counterfactual); 'how many parking bays are free right now?' still reaches a data lane at 12 facts.
Refs: BUG-1333; ontology/hbco_mappings.ttl hbco:empty_space; orchestrator/services/routing_contract.py::_r_capability_measurand_is_data; orchestrator/agents/dialogue_agent.py::detect_intent amenity short-circuit; orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py concept-stage context; lessons #157, #170, #141

Title: 'it does not link those components to any particular room' -- the three projector records each carry the room in locationText
Description:
Found re-verifying BUG-710 row 122 live, 2026-10-01, occupant01 on /v1 streaming, both caches flushed, one ask, 27.5 s, `lane=metadata` -> sparql. Question, verbatim: 'Find a room for 12 with a projector, free 2-4pm today, near the cafe.'
The answer is BETTER than the one BUG-710 recorded -- it discloses the gap register by register instead of denying projectors, and says 'there are projector components listed in the AV register'. But it then states, twice: 'The Teaching AV readiness register lists individual AV components (projectors, microphones, etc.) but **it does not link those components to any particular room**' and 'the records do not say which rooms have those projectors'.
MEASURED AGAINST THE GRAPH THIS SESSION, all nineteen predicates on AV-106-PRJ read directly: `rdfs:label "Room 1.06 projector"` and `ontosage:locationText "Room 1.06 - Computer Laboratory"`. The other two are AV-201-PRJ ('Room 2.01 projector') and AV-301-PRJ ('Room 3.01 projector'). The register says which room has each projector, in words, twice over.
The nuance, and it is why this is P2 and not P1: there is no IRI-level link to a brick:Room, so a strict JOIN is genuinely unavailable. The answer conflated 'no structural join' with 'no information', and told the reader the second.
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED BEYOND THE OBSERVATION, deliberately -- the sentence is narrated, and attributing it without reading the prompt and the projected rows would be a guess. Two candidates, both checkable: the register projection may not hand `locationText` to the narrator for AVReadiness (it is present on the instance, so this is about what was PROJECTED, not what exists); or the narrator inferred 'not linked' from the absence of an object-property edge and rendered that as an absence of information. `register_projection.py` is another agent's file this session and was not read.
Fix_Approach: Whoever owns the register narration: an absence claim about a FIELD must be checked against the fields the projection actually carried, and 'no IRI link' may not be worded as 'the records do not say'. The three records and their locationText are the test fixture. Do NOT fix this by pattern-matching the sentence: the other agent's session has three instances of a regex guard failing to tell a claim from its denial.
Verification:
RE-ASKED LIVE 2026-10-01, facility01 on /v1, `resp_cache:*` flushed, verbatim question: the claim is GONE. The answer now states '| Rooms that have a projector | **3 (Room 1.06, Room 2.01, Room 3.01)** |' -- the rooms, by name, which is what `ontosage:locationText` holds. No 'does not link those components to any particular room' and no 'the records do not say which rooms have those projectors'.
Closed as NO_LONGER_REPRODUCES rather than FIXED: nothing was changed for it, so what moved is unattributed (this session altered the capability subject test, the amenity stand-down and the register discovery roots, any of which could bear on it). **The re-ask found BUG-1399 (P1) in its place**, which is the more serious defect and the reason this row is worth re-reading rather than deleting.
Refs: BUG-710 row 122; BUG-947 (names the register that holds the answer while denying it); BUG-1399

Title: A named STANDARD is answered with the nearest kind: 'Changing Places' gets accessible toilets, and the absence of the standard is not stated
Description:
The residual of BUG-1333, split out so it is countable rather than buried in a fixed row. Verified live 2026-10-01 after that fix: 'Is a Changing Places toilet available in this building?' now answers from the building's own records in 1.1 s, naming accessible gender-neutral toilets on floors 0 and 1. It does NOT say that no *Changing Places* facility is recorded. Changing Places is a specific standard -- adult-sized changing bench, ceiling hoist, room to turn a wheelchair -- and the graph records none, so the complete answer is a partial: 'no Changing Places facility is recorded; 12 accessible gender-neutral toilets are, two per floor 0-5'.
WHY THIS IS P3 AND NOT WORSE: the reader is no longer told the building holds nothing, and is given real, checkable places. The failure is now an OMISSION a reader can see through, not a false statement. That is the direction this cluster exists to move things in.
WHY IT STILL MATTERS: somebody who needs a Changing Places facility and is shown an accessible toilet may travel on the strength of it. The two are not substitutes.
Root_Cause: The capability resolver matches on lay-term overlap, and 'changing places' is declared as a layTerm of `ontosage:AccessibilityFeature` -- so the phrase reaches the right FAMILY and there is nothing in the answer path that knows the phrase named a standard the matched instances do not meet. Measured: 18 amenities carry the phrase 'changing places' through the class-level terms, and none of them is a Changing Places facility.
Fix_Approach: NOT ATTEMPTED. The honest shape is a two-part answer -- the named thing is not recorded, here is the nearest kind that is -- and it needs a way to know that a matched instance does not satisfy the phrase that matched it. The TTL-first move would be to stop `ontosage:AccessibilityFeature` claiming 'changing places' at class level and give the standard its own class or a declared property, so its absence is a fact about the graph rather than about a word list. Measure over the catalogue before changing the lay terms: they are what makes 18 amenities reachable at all.
Verification: GRAPH: 24 o:ToiletFacility (12 'Accessible gender-neutral toilet', two per floor 0-5), 18 o:AccessibilityFeature; 18 amenities carry the class-level lay phrase 'changing places'; zero instances describe a Changing Places facility. LIVE after the BUG-1333 fix: lane=capability, 1.1 s, three accessible gender-neutral toilets named with their locations, no denial and no mention of the standard.

Title: register_reach's guard set pins its own snapshot, so changing the discovery roots reports 10 violations that are artefacts
Description:
Hit while measuring BUG-1333's root widening, and it would mislead the next person the same way. `scripts/register_reach.py` evaluates the 124-question guard set against `meta['snapshot']` stored INSIDE docs/phase0/guard_set.jsonl, not against the snapshot just taken. That pinned snapshot was captured with roots {o:Record, o:IntervalRecord}, so it carries no amenity instance counts. Add `o:Amenity` to the roots and the guard reports 10 VIOLATIONS, every one of the form `absent:NEW None -> ToiletFacility / Lift / AccessibilityFeature / DrinkingWater` -- on questions such as 'Is the lift working?' and 'where can I fill my water bottle?'. Those read as the change declining a question by name against a class the building holds nothing of. It holds 24 toilets, 2 lifts, 18 accessibility features and 16 drinking-water points; in the guard's frozen world they are all zero, so `absent_record_class` names them.
The pinning is CORRECT for its purpose -- a guard must compare like with like -- and the recall half of the same run, which does use the fresh snapshot, reported the real numbers (ABSENT:Service 222, ABSENT:Facility 29). The trap is that the two halves of one report disagree for a structural reason nothing on screen explains.
Root_Cause: `main()` builds `guard_reach = Reach(graph, with_counts(meta.get('snapshot', snapshot), overrides), stored)`. A change to the CLASS SET, as opposed to the vocabulary the guard set was derived for, makes the pinned counts incomplete rather than merely older.
Fix_Approach:
Not changed: re-deriving the guard set to un-pin it would discard the precision baseline, which is the more valuable thing. What HAS been fixed is the near-miss beside it: the harness had its OWN copy of `VALUES ?root { o:Record o:IntervalRecord }` in `_COUNT_QUERY`, so adding a root to the product would have left every amenity class at count 0 in the fresh snapshot too -- i.e. the comparison would have reported 'nothing changed' about a change affecting 71 holdings. It now reads `record_registry._RECORD_ROOTS`, so the two cannot diverge. Verified behaviour-neutral: with the roots back at two, `--compare` reports 44 held classes, 0 moves and 0 violations against the baseline taken before the edit.
The remaining advice is a line in the report, not code: when a root changes, read the guard violations for the SHAPE `absent:NEW None -> <a class the building holds>` and treat it as the pinned snapshot, not a regression.
Verification: Measured both ways this session. With `o:Amenity` added: 53 held classes, 335 questions move, guard 10 violations, exit 1. With it removed again: 44 held classes, **0 moves, 0 violations, exit 0** against a baseline saved before any edit -- which is what proves the `_count_query()` refactor changed no behaviour.

Title: A dependency order is asserted with arrows over records that carry no ordering, and two asks give two different orders
Description:
FOUND BY RE-ASKING BUG-1332 after its guard landed -- the fabricated FIGURES and the invented ORDERS OF WORK are gone, and this took their place.
'Which dependency-aware recovery order should incident leaders adopt to restore priority services safely...?' answered, live, occupant01 on /v1:
    ask 1: **DEP-07 -> DEP-05 -> DEP-06 -> DEP-16 -> DEP-03**
    ask 3: **DEP-05 -> DEP-06 -> DEP-03 -> DEP-07 -> DEP-16**
both cited '*From Abacws Building's documents: Stakeholder Group Register*'. Same five records, two different orders, each presented as THE dependency-aware recovery order. Ask 5 does the same with SH-30 -> SH-31 -> SH-32 -> SH-33, which is simply ascending record id.
**VERIFIED AGAINST THE GRAPH: the DEP records carry NO ordering predicate.** All 20 carry exactly: label, comment, locationText, contactEmail, contactPhone, openingHours, recordStatus, effectiveFrom, recordOwner, owningAuthority, recordVersion, retrievedAt, derivedFromDocument, liftedByMapping, recordId, accountableRole. Nothing about dependency, priority, sequence or order.
**So the ARROWS are the fabrication.** They assert a relationship between records that the graph does not hold, and the disagreement between asks 1 and 3 proves the order is arbitrary rather than derived. This is design contract #4 with a relationship in place of a figure, and it is MORE dangerous than the figures it replaced: a number invites checking, an arrow reads as structure.
Lesson #155's shape (a ranking that ties falls back to arbitrary and nobody reads it as arbitrary), and it slipped `narration_guard` because **arrows are not a keyword** -- every family in that guard matches nouns and verbs.
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED. The register lane returns 5 of 20 Department records and the narration renders them as a sequence; whether the selection of five or the ordering of them is the LLM's is unestablished. The productive question is whether any lane may emit an ordered list when no ordering predicate was read -- the same invariant `narration_guard.claims_are_supportable()` states for capacity, one relation over.
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED. Candidate, stated so it can be measured rather than assumed: a deterministic check that an ordered rendering (arrows, 'first/then', a numbered sequence presented as dependency) is only emitted when the rows carried an order field -- an ordering invariant beside the capacity one. **MEASURE IT OVER THE ~2,912 STORED ANSWERS BEFORE LANDING**: numbered lists are extremely common and most are legitimate (a register's fields, a floor list, ranked search results with scores), so a naive rule would destroy many correct answers. That is the trap this cluster has already sprung twice -- BUG-1302's 'two-line call' would have cost 26 hand-read GOOD answers, and the guard's own first draft destroyed two correct refusals.

--- MEASURED 2026-10-01, AND THE CANDIDATE'S KEYING IS REJECTED ---
The row above proposed keying a guard on an ORDERED RENDERING (arrows, 'first/then', a numbered sequence) and said to measure it over the stored answers first. Measured over **2,861 de-duplicated stored answers** (`docs/phase0/*.jsonl` + `scripts/outputs/*.jsonl`):
  * answers containing an arrow: **58 of 2,861 (2.03%)**, 289 arrow occurrences
  * answers with a numbered list of 3+ items: 59
  * answers with sequence words ('first', 'then', 'in this order'): **679**, of which my own crude 'unjustified' bucket held **317 -- 11% of every answer in the corpus**
**THEN THE DECISIVE BREAKDOWN: what sits either side of the arrow.**
  | either side | occurrences | answers |
  |---|---|---|
  | place -> place | **128 of 289 (44%)** | 34 |
  | other -> other | 46 | 21 |
  | other -> place | 44 | 12 |
  | place -> other | 37 | 8 |
  | **record-id -> record-id (THIS DEFECT'S SHAPE)** | **1 of 289 (0.3%)** | **1** |
An arrow in this system overwhelmingly means *from X to Y* -- 'Level 0 -> 1', 'Reception -> Level 3 laboratories', 'Abacws Building -> Floor 0 (Ground Floor)' -- a ROUTE or a CONTAINMENT the graph genuinely holds. It does not mean *X before Y*.
And the single `record-id -> record-id` hit is NOT an ordering either: it is `effective 2026-08-30 -> 2026-09-02`, a date range my own pattern mis-typed as two record ids. So the true count of this shape in 2,861 stored answers is **zero**.
**CONCLUSION: a rule keyed on the RENDERING would put 58 correct answers at risk to catch approximately none.** The candidate is wrong about WHERE to key, not about the defect. Keying moves to: the QUESTION asks for an order (recovery order, priority order, sequence, 'dependency-aware') AND the bound records carry no ordering predicate -- a precondition on the lane, not a pattern on the prose.
**AND THE POPULATION WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE METHODOLOGICAL POINT.** Those 2,861 answers are responses to PAST questions; this defect was found by a question shape that barely occurs in them. **Absence from the corpus is not evidence of rarity** -- it is evidence the corpus predates the shape. Bounding this defect's frequency needs order-seeking questions RE-ASKED live, not a scan of history. The 2.03% figure above must not be quoted as a frequency for this defect; it is a frequency for arrows.
Instruments: `scratchpad/measure_1391_orderings.py`, `scratchpad/measure_1391_arrows.py`.

--- 2026-10-01: THE GUARD ALREADY EXISTS, AND THE CALL IS NOW PROVEN SAFE ---
Two findings change this row from open-ended to a small wiring job.
**(1) FAMILY C ALREADY CATCHES THIS SHAPE.** `narration_guard._OPERATIONAL_ORDER` matches 'recovery sequence/order/plan/priority' and 'recommended ... order'. It is simply not applied to this lane: `_READING_LANE_FAMILIES` is applied by lanes whose rows are numeric readings, and BUG-1391's answer came from the REGISTER/document lane.
**(2) THE OBVIOUS EXTENSION IS 50% WRONG, AND THE MODULE PREDICTED IT.** Its own header records 'applied lane-blind, the original family B hit 69 answers'. Measured here over 2,861 de-duplicated stored answers: **1,335 look like register/document answers, and Family C would hit 2 of them** -- and ONE OF THE TWO IS A CORRECT DECLINE:
    'The records do **not** contain a dependency-aware recovery order. They record the following for each incident: - Incident status (closed, open, monitoring) ...'
The other is the defect shape ('**Recovery priority for the current incident situation** | Rank | Service to restore | ...'). Suppressing the first would destroy a correct refusal, which is CAVEAT-1377 exactly.
**AND THE PROTECTION FOR THAT ALREADY EXISTS TOO.** `reading_lane_claims` takes a `families` subset and applies `_ABSENCE_FRAME` to the clause around each match. Called with that subset, measured on all three texts:
    reading_lane_claims(<the correct decline>, [], families={'operational_order'}) -> []
    reading_lane_claims(<the ranked table>,    [], families={'operational_order'}) -> ['Recovery priority']
    reading_lane_claims(<the DEP-07 -> DEP-05 arrows>, [], families={'operational_order'}) -> ['recovery order']
**The decline is allowed and both defect shapes are caught, with no new pattern written.**
WHAT REMAINS, and why it was not landed today: the register narration is composed DOWNSTREAM of `sparql_agent` -- the facts block goes into `guidance` and the answer is written in the response path -- so the hook is not where the facts are built. Wiring a suppressor into the response path is a wider change than it looks, and three of today's regressions came from exactly that kind of end-of-session change. The pattern to copy is `report_agent`'s: a named per-lane constant (`REPORT_LANE_FAMILIES`) with its measurement in the comment beside it. Note that the report lane DELIBERATELY omits operational_order, because recommending something is that lane's job -- so a register constant must be its own, not a reuse.
STILL REQUIRED BEFORE LANDING: `rows_record_an_order(rows)`, in the shape of the existing `rows_record_a_state` -- a question about the DATA, so that a register which one day carries a sequence predicate lifts the suppression by itself instead of leaving a stale prohibition. The DEP records carry none today (checked: label, comment, locationText, contactEmail, contactPhone, openingHours, recordStatus, effectiveFrom, recordOwner, owningAuthority, recordVersion, retrievedAt, derivedFromDocument, liftedByMapping, recordId, accountableRole).
Verification:
FIXED OFFLINE 2026-10-01; LIVE RE-ASK OWED. `register_facts.unsequence()` is applied to every whole-register narration after the false-absence guard. It is keyed on RECORD IDS and on the ROWS, exactly as the row's rejected measurement argued: a chain of this register's own ids joined by arrows (->, →, =>, -->, ⟶) is flattened to a comma list and the answer gains '_The <register> records no order, priority or dependency between these records, so they are listed, not sequenced._' -- ONLY when `rows_record_an_order()` is False, i.e. no field is named for an order (priority, sequence, criticality, dependsOn, step, rank, ...) and no row's field holds another row's record id. Department rows carry `escalatesTo` = a ROLE, not a record, so the guard stands. Routes between rooms and ids of other registers are untouched.
MEASURED before landing: 0 of 2,554 de-duplicated stored answers contain a record-id arrow chain, so the guard cannot cost a stored answer; 44% of the corpus's arrows are routes and are not matched.
Tests: `tests/test_a_sequence_the_rows_do_not_hold.py`, 18 pass.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02 (three asks across two restarts): the recovery-order question now reaches ContinuityProvision (via the new lay terms) and is DECLINED honestly by the register projection -- 'cannot answer this: it records depends on space, serves service, ... criticality ... and nothing about adopt, incident, leaders and order.' No arrows, no order, no Department records. The `unsequence` guard was therefore NOT exercised live: the narration never ran. It stands as the backstop for the day a register with no order field is narrated for one; its own tests (18) are the evidence it works.
