Title: A preposition decided whether the building could answer: 'during' cost the UPS/generator answer that 'in' returned
Description:
FOUND BY A FAILING UNIT TEST, not by a question -- `test_capability_semantic_quality.py::test_baseline_power_outage`.
Live, occupant01 on /v1, both caches flushed, 'What happens during a power outage?' answered:
    "I don't have that specific information on record for **Abacws Building**. For building-specific queries please contact your building's facilities / estates management team."
while `bldg:Cap_power_resilience` declares the lay term 'power outage' VERBATIM and an answerText naming the UPS, the diesel standby generator and its ~30 s changeover.
The log shows every stage working and the last one throwing the answer away:
    [ttl-route] capability via ontology triples: ['Power Resilience']
    [capability] topics ['Power Resilience'] match words but are not the subject
THE PAIR THAT ISOLATES IT -- same topic, same subject, one preposition apart:
    'What happens IN a power cut?'        leftover {happens}         -> ANSWERED
    'What happens DURING a power outage?' leftover {during, happens} -> DECLINED
Root_Cause:
`capability_graph_resolver.leftover_content_words` discards every word of two letters or fewer, so 'in', 'on', 'at', 'of' were excluded BY ACCIDENT rather than by design -- they never reach `_FRAME_WORDS` and so never needed to be in it. 'during' is six letters and does reach it, and was not listed. `capability_agent._is_subject` permits at most ONE leftover content word, so a single unlisted function word is disqualifying on its own.
The top leftover word across the whole bank is 'and' -- 1,383 occurrences, three letters, a conjunction, also unlisted.
Fix_Approach:
52 function words that cannot be the SUBJECT of any question added to `_FRAME_WORDS`: prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliaries and the 'what happens' framing verbs. Words that SCOPE a question to a time are deliberately excluded (today, now, tomorrow, tonight) because those change WHICH answer is right, and a static topic answering them is a different defect that widening would hide.
MEASURED BEFORE LANDING over both populations, because `_FRAME_WORDS` is what stops a topic answering a question it is not about (BUG-601) and every word added makes the test MORE permissive:
  * full 4,060-question bank: **10 questions move, ALL DROPPED -> ANSWERS, 0 lost**
  * 2,960-question stakeholder catalogue: **1 moves, a gain, 0 lost**
  * BUG-601's three real cases stay DROPPED
Eight of the ten are plainly right ('Which routes through the building are step-free?', 'Is there a cafe in the building and is it open to visitors?', 'Which entrance is open before 7am?'). TWO ARE DOUBTFUL AND ARE STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: 'Any vehicles in the car park that have been there over 72 hours?' -> Transport Parking, and 'If the building could talk, what would it complain about?' -> Making a complaint. Both were DECLINED before, so the trade is 8 clear gains and 2 weak answers against 0 losses.
A VARIANT ADDING DEGREE ADVERBS (also, just, only, currently, ...) WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED: it moved one more and that one was WRONG -- 'Which meeting room am I in?' answered from Quiet Study. The numbers are written into the module so nobody re-proposes the adverbs on intuition.
Verification:
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-01 after restart, occupant01 on /v1 streaming, `resp_cache:*` and `cache:sparql*` both flushed:
    'Here is what I found for **Abacws Building**: **Power Resilience**. The building has an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) for critical systems: emergency lighting, fire alarm panels, server rooms, and security systems. A diesel standby generator provides emergency power ... within ~30 seconds of a mains failure. ... *Answered live from the building's own records.*'
`[capability] answered from ontology triples: ['Power Resilience']`.
Regression ask in the same run: 'Where can I isolate the water supply for the second-floor toilets?' still DECLINES -- BUG-601 not reopened.
`tests/test_a_preposition_is_not_a_subject.py`, 22 pass, including a counterfactual class that fails if the set swallows content nouns.
**A SUBJECT-TEST MEASUREMENT IS NOT A ROUTE MEASUREMENT, and I learned that from this fix.** The instrument predicted 'The fire alarm is sounding. What should I do?' would answer from Fire Safety; live it never reaches the capability lane at all (BUG-1393). The measurement was right about the stage and silent about the path.

Title: A sounding fire alarm is routed to the asset register, which declines the recorded evacuation procedure and then writes generic advice of its own
Description:
FOUND WHILE VERIFYING BUG-1392 -- the measurement predicted this question would answer and the live ask proved it does not.
'The fire alarm is sounding. What should I do?' -- occupant01, /v1, both caches flushed, after restart:
    'I did not find any instructions for a sounding fire alarm in the building's fire safety asset records. The closest this building keeps is the building's record of **Main entrance east leaf**, which I can read for you.
     The only fire-alarm asset in the building is the **Fire alarm control panel (FSA-001)**, located in **Room 0.10 - Building Management Office**. Its recorded status is **overdue** ...
     Because the register contains no guidance on what to do when the alarm sounds, you should follow the building's standard fire-alarm procedures (e.g., evacuate, contact the fire department,'
**THREE THINGS ARE WRONG AND THE THIRD IS THE WORST.**
(1) The building HOLDS the answer. `bldg:Cap_evacuation` declares 'On alarm activation, leave the building via the nearest marked fire exit; Do not use the lifts; Proceed to the assembly point on Senghennydd Road; Report to the floor fire warden for roll call', plus refuge areas and PEEPs. A separate Fire Safety topic declares the lay term 'fire alarm' VERBATIM.
(2) It answers about something else -- a panel's overdue weekly test -- to an occupant who said the alarm is sounding NOW.
(3) **IT INVENTS THE PROCEDURE.** 'you should follow the building's standard fire-alarm procedures (e.g., evacuate, contact the fire department' is the model's own generic advice, offered in place of the documented steps, in the same answer that says the building has no guidance. Design contract #4, on the question class where being wrong costs most. It also ends mid-sentence.
Root_Cause:
NOT FULLY DIAGNOSED. The route is known and logged:
    [ttl-route] metadata via held record class: FireSafetyAsset (30 instances) -- skipping LLM intent call
    Final intent for routing: metadata
A register of 30 fire-safety ASSETS outranked the capability topic that holds the PROCEDURE, so the capability lane -- and therefore its subject test -- never ran. This is BUG-623's shape ('the register stealing the deliberation lane') on a safety question: the register wins because it can prove it holds 30 instances, while the topic's claim is only a lay-term match.
What is NOT established: whether the generic advice comes from the metadata narrator or from a second-chance producer, and therefore which guard should have caught it. `narration_guard` families match nouns and verbs; 'you should follow the building's standard procedures' is a HEDGED IMPERATIVE and may be a third shape beside BUG-1391's arrows.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND IT IS ONE CHARACTER CLASS. `EMERGENCY_ACTION_RE` joined its two halves with `[^?.!]{0,60}`, so the emergency and the action frame had to sit in ONE SENTENCE. Measured on the pair that isolates it:
    'The fire alarm is sounding**,** what should I do?'  comma     -> True
    'The fire alarm is sounding**.** What should I do?'  full stop -> **False**
**MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE:** I expected the leading STATEMENT to be read as a safety report, because the rule's own docstring says a statement keeps its intake route. Measured, `report_intake_intent` returns **None** for this question and `is_control_command` returns False. The intake gate is not involved at all.
**TWO GATES FAILED TOGETHER ON THIS ONE PREDICATE**, which is why neither was visible alone: `dialogue_agent`'s metadata short-circuit already guards itself with `and not _is_emergency_action(user_query)` -- its comment reads 'this return would skip the rule that says so' -- and the routing rule `emergency_action_is_a_procedure` calls the same function. Both read this regex, so both stood down and the asset register was left holding a procedure question. BUG-1241's shape exactly (lesson #154).
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED. A routing change, so it needs the gate green before and after and ONE rule at a time (CLAUDE.md).
Candidate, stated so it can be measured rather than assumed: a question asking what to DO during a named emergency is a PROCEDURE question, and a register of assets is not a procedure -- the same distinction `emergency_action_is_a_procedure` already draws for the blocked-exit question (DR-004, 2026-09-30). Check first whether that existing rule simply fails to match this phrasing, because the cheapest fix is a rule that already exists and does not fire. MEASURE ANY CHANGE OVER THE 2,960-QUESTION CATALOGUE: 'fire' appears in many questions that really are asset or compliance questions ('when was the extinguisher last serviced') and must keep going to the register.
SEPARATELY AND INDEPENDENTLY: the invented procedure must not ship whatever the route does. That half is a guard question, not a routing one.
FIXED 2026-10-01: the gap is now `[^?!]` -- it may cross a full stop, and `?`/`!` stay barriers. That asymmetry is what keeps it narrow: a `?` ends a question, so two questions are two topics.
MEASURED OVER THE FULL 4,060-QUESTION BANK BEFORE LANDING: **1 question gains (the one above), 0 lost.** The bank is weak evidence of BENEFIT here and that is said rather than glossed -- it holds only **two** emergency-action questions in total, so it bounds the RISK and not the gain. The gain shows on hand phrasings, which is where this shape lives: three move from declined to answered -- the sounding alarm, 'There is smoke in the corridor. What should I do?' and 'Someone has collapsed. Who do I call?'
ZERO FALSE POSITIVES across six controls, including the two adversarial ones: 'Where are the fire extinguishers? What should I do about my booking?' (held by the `?` barrier) and 'There was a fire drill last week. What should I do about the broken projector?' (held by `_ABOUT_THE_EQUIPMENT_RE` on 'broken').
Verification:
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-01 after restart, occupant01 on /v1, `resp_cache:*` and `cache:sparql*` both flushed:
    'Here is what I found for **Abacws Building**: **Fire Safety**. ... Assembly point: the open area on Senghennydd Road directly outside the main entrance. Fire wardens are designated per floor. ... **Do not use lifts during evacuation.**
     From the full policy document (**fire_safety.md**): ## Evacuation procedure ... 1. On hearing the fire alarm (continuous bell), **leave the building immediately** ...'
The invented advice is gone, the panel's overdue-test digression is gone, and the answer is the building's own recorded procedure.
**REGRESSION CONTROL IN THE SAME RUN, which is the half that matters for a routing change:** 'When was the fire alarm panel last tested?' still reaches the REGISTER -- *'The most recent last tested on on record is **9 September 2026** - **FSA-001** (Fire alarm control panel)'*. The procedure lane did not steal the equipment question.
Tests: `tests/test_an_emergency_may_be_two_sentences.py` (18, including a counterfactual that fails if the `?` barrier is ever dropped) + the pre-existing `test_an_emergency_question_reaches_the_procedure_not_the_asset_register.py`. Slice `-k 'emergency or routing_contract or is_question or safety_report'`: **321 pass**. Full suite after the BUG-1392 change: **13,737 pass / 0 fail / 76 skip / 3 xfail**, exit 0.
**WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED:** the SECOND half of this row -- that a lane must not invent a procedure it has just said it does not hold -- is NOT fixed. The invented text is gone from THIS question because the question now reaches a lane that has the answer. A guard against a hedged imperative ('you should follow the building's standard procedures') is a separate piece of work and is unbuilt; BUG-1391 is its sibling for ordered lists.
Refs: BUG-1392; BUG-623; BUG-1391; DR-004; design contract #4; BUG-1241; lesson #154; lesson #174

Title: The capability subject test keeps 0 of 1,563 catalogue questions that resolve a topic -- measured, and whether those declines are correct is NOT established
Description:
MEASURED while sizing BUG-1392's blast radius, over the live graph in the running container, replicating `capability_agent._is_subject` exactly:
  * 2,960-question stakeholder catalogue: 1,563 resolve at least one capability topic. **KEPT: 0. DROPPED by the subject test: 1,563.**
  * full 4,060-question bank: 2,150 resolve a topic. **KEPT: 20. DROPPED: 2,130.**
So on the stakeholder catalogue the graph-topic answer path contributes NOTHING, and across the whole bank it answers 0.9% of the questions that reach it.
Of the 2,130 dropped, **34 have exactly TWO leftover words** -- one word from answering. Among them: 'Which routes through the building are step-free?', 'Are the solar panels working?', 'Is there a prayer or contemplation room, and is it free at midday?', 'Which entrance is open before 7am?'
**THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM 1,563 FALSE DECLINES.** The catalogue is deliberately compound stakeholder questions, and for many of them a single amenity topic is genuinely NOT the subject -- which is exactly what BUG-601 made this test for. A high drop rate is partly correct behaviour. What is NOT established is HOW MUCH of it is, and that cannot be read off the number.
Root_Cause: By construction: the threshold is at most ONE leftover content word, and a compound question has several. Widening `_FRAME_WORDS` barely moves it (BUG-1392: 1 of 2,960) because the binding constraint is the THRESHOLD, not the word list -- a question with five leftovers goes to four, not to one. The two are independent knobs and only the safe one has been turned.
Fix_Approach:
DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, and the gap is made countable instead. Raising the threshold to 2 is precisely the over-wide change this cluster has already punished twice (BUG-1302's 'two-line call' would have cost 26 hand-read GOOD answers; the narration guard's first draft destroyed two correct refusals).
WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, in order: (1) hand-read a random 40 of the 2,130 drops and label each decline correct or false -- the drop rate is only a defect to the extent that read says so; (2) if the false share is material, measure threshold 2 over the catalogue the way BUG-1392 measured the word list, reporting moves in BOTH directions; (3) the 34 two-leftover near misses are the cheapest sample to start from because each is one word from answering and the leftover words are printed.
A SCAN CAN TRIAGE; ONLY A READING CAN JUDGE (lesson #173).
Refs: BUG-1392; BUG-601; BUG-1302; BUG-1361; lesson #135; lesson #173

Title: BUG-601's own first example has regressed: 'Book me a hotel near the building' answers from the room-booking topic
Description:
FOUND AS THE CONTROL IN BUG-1392's MEASUREMENT, which is the only reason it was noticed: the four BUG-601 cases were printed with their BASELINE verdict beside the candidate one, specifically so a pre-existing failure could not be mistaken for a new one.
    'Book me a hotel near the building'  BASELINE -> ANSWERS:Bookings Reservations
It answers at baseline, BEFORE and AFTER BUG-1392's change, so BUG-1392 did not cause it and did not fix it.
BUG-601 was logged and closed on exactly this example: a request to book a HOTEL answered from the building's ROOM-booking topic. The other three of its four cases still correctly decline ('pushchair-friendly from the car park', 'isolate the water supply', 'systems specific for the meeting room'), so this is a partial regression of one case, not a collapse of the fix.
The harm is modest -- a reader asking for a hotel is told about room bookings, which is wrong but not dangerous -- and it is logged because a closed row quietly ceasing to hold is how a regression becomes folklore.
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED. The subject test leaves {hotel} -- one leftover word -- which is within the threshold of 1, so the Bookings topic qualifies. 'book' is covered by the topic's own declared terms and 'near', 'the', 'building', 'me' are all framing. Whether BUG-601's fix ever excluded this case, or whether a later vocabulary change to the Bookings topic brought it back, is unestablished -- the row's text does not say which mechanism closed it.
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED, and the obvious fix is wrong. Lowering the threshold to 0 would stop it and would also stop 'What happens during a power outage?' ({happens}) and every other question with one residual word, which is the answer-destroying direction.
The shape of a real fix is a NEGATIVE test rather than a tighter threshold: a leftover word that names a thing OUTSIDE the building (hotel, taxi, restaurant, airport) disqualifies a topic however few leftovers there are, because the question is not about this building at all. That is a small closed vocabulary and it should be measured over the catalogue before landing, like BUG-1392.

--- FIXED 2026-10-01 ---
`capability_graph_resolver.topic_is_the_subject` now refuses a topic when a leftover word names something the building is NOT (`_NOT_THIS_BUILDING`: hotel, hotels, motel, hostel, airbnb, airport, restaurant, takeaway, pub).
**THE TEST IS ON THE WORD, NOT THE COUNT, and that is the whole point.** Lowering the threshold to 0 was the obvious move and is the ANSWER-DESTROYING direction: it would also refuse 'What happens during a power outage?', whose single leftover is {happens} (BUG-1392).
The set is building-agnostic by construction -- every member is a category of OFF-SITE commercial premises, and the test for membership is that no amount of different onboarding could make it true of a building. Deliberately EXCLUDED, with a test that fails if any is added: cafe, canteen, parking, toilet, lift, bus, train, bike, shower, kitchen, reception, library -- each a real amenity of a building in this repo.
**MEASURED OVER BOTH POPULATIONS BEFORE LANDING: 0 questions move in the 2,960-question catalogue and 0 in the full 4,060-question bank.** The logged case moves (Bookings Reservations -> declined) and the controls hold (cafe in the building, visitor parking, power outage, nearest accessible toilet).
Verification:
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-01 after restart, facility01@example.com on /v1, `resp_cache:*` flushed:
    Q 'Book me a hotel near the building'
    A '**I can't make, change or cancel bookings or place orders** - I read Abacws Building's records; I don't act on them, so nothing has been reserved. What I can do is tell you what is booked or free: try *which rooms are free right now?* or *is a particular room booked this afternoon?*'
A correct decline, and a better one than a bare refusal: it says what it will not do, why, and what it can do instead.
**CONTROL IN THE SAME RUN:** 'How do I book a meeting room?' still answers from the Bookings Reservations topic with the full procedure (staff intranet / Outlook / Timetabling / supervisors / Conference Services). The topic's real question is untouched.
Tests: `test_a_topic_answers_only_questions_about_it.py` + `test_an_amenity_is_something_the_building_holds.py` = **33 pass**, including a guard that fails if a word a building CAN hold is ever added to the set.

Title: The amenity stand-down deferred to the capability lane for topics that lane then discarded, so a forecast question was answered from documents
Description:
**FOUND BY THE REGRESSION GATE, which went 49/51 after BUG-1333/1361 landed** (51/51 twice the day before). Case #4, reproduced deterministically:
    Q 'Project the noise level in the atrium for the next 12 hours and show the error of each candidate model.'
    A '**I could not find this in <building>'s documents.** I searched them and none is about this question...'
The log holds the whole contradiction in three lines:
    [ttl-route] capability via ontology triples: ['Working Hours']
    [routing-contract] capability_measurand_is_data stood down: 1 amenity triples of this building match the question
    [capability] topics ['Working Hours'] match words but are not the subject — not answering from them
**'Working Hours' matched the word "hours" inside "the next 12 hours".** The contract stopped handing a FORECAST to a data lane in favour of a lane that immediately threw the topic away, so the forecast lane never ran and the reader got a documents decline.
A stand-down whose premise is *the building's own triples know what this question is about* has to be keyed on an amenity the question IS about. It was keyed on the COUNT of amenities whose vocabulary the question's words touched.
Root_Cause:
`_r_capability_measurand_is_data` read `capability_amenity_facts`, written by `dialogue_agent` as `len(resolver.resolve(q))`. That count says the building holds something the question's words touched; it does not say the question is about it. The judgement that WOULD have said so already existed — `capability_agent`'s `_is_subject` closure — but one stage too late to change the lane.
MEASURED over the 4,060-question bank: of the **2,022** questions that match an amenity and ask for no value, only **30** have an amenity as their subject. So the stand-down's premise was false for 98.5% of the set it keyed on. (That figure does not model `intent == capability`, so it is an UPPER BOUND on live reach, not a live count — lesson #174.)
Fix_Approach:
`topic_is_the_subject` / `subject_facts` MOVED out of `capability_agent` into `capability_graph_resolver`, beside `leftover_content_words`; the capability lane now calls it and `dialogue_agent` publishes `capability_amenity_subject` with it; `_orchestrator` forwards that into the concept-stage context; the rule keys on it. **The closure was DELETED rather than copied** — a second matcher beside the first is exactly how BUG-947's decline pointer came to disagree with its own register selector, and a test now fails if `def _is_subject(` reappears in the lane.
**TWO OTHER CANDIDATES WERE MEASURED AND REJECTED FIRST, and the numbers are in the module so neither is re-proposed:**
  * add a FORECAST test to `_asks_for_a_value` — **107** bank questions move and many are amenity and availability questions ('Which quiet rooms are free in the next hour?', 'Which accessible toilet is nearest and currently open?', 'Book me a hotel near the building for tomorrow'), the exact class BUG-1333/1361 protects;
  * widen `sensor_binder._FORECAST_ASK_RE` with a bare `project\w*` — matches **PROJECTOR**, of which this building keeps records.
MEASURED EFFECT OF WHAT LANDED: stand-down fires on 2,022 -> **30**. Title: A question about the evidence behind a PREVIOUS answer routes to the diagnosis lane, which runs and produces nothing
Description:
The second of the two regression-gate failures (case #37), and unlike BUG-1396 it is **NOT attributable to any change made today** — stated that way because the temptation was to bundle them.
    Q 'What is the evidence behind your answer about the coolest room?'
    A 'I couldn't answer that from <building>'s records. The nearest things I can answer are the Teaching AV readiness, Compliance check and Approval and evidence record records...'
The log is unambiguous about where it dies:
    Final intent for routing: diagnosis      (from the CLASSIFIER — no contract override is logged)
    [diagnosis] q='What is the evidence behind your answer about the coolest ro'
    [response] nothing to say: intent=diagnosis entities=none ran=the diagnosis lane error=none
The lane RAN and had nothing, so the generic fallback decline shipped.
**THIS IS A PROVENANCE QUESTION ABOUT A PREVIOUS TURN, ASKED WITH NO PREVIOUS TURN.** The gate asks each case standalone, so there is no answer about a coolest room to give the evidence for. That is BUG-941's family: `session_summary` is injected on all four entry points and nothing consumes it for a referent.
Root_Cause:
NOT DIAGNOSED BEYOND THE LANE. Two candidates, not separated:
(a) classifier variance — the intent is the LLM's with no deterministic override, and this question names no place, time or record, which is the shape CAVEAT-891 says is least stable;
(b) a real gap — no lane owns 'explain the evidence behind what you just said', so whichever intent the classifier picks, nothing answers it.
(b) is the more likely and the more useful, because the pack recorded this as ANSWERED, meaning some lane did once produce a provenance answer for it.

--- SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-01: IT IS (a), AND THE VARIANCE IS IN THE ROUTE ---
Three asks through the gate's own harness, same identity, and **a fresh conversation each time** -- `ask()` sends a unique `X-Chat-Id` per case (`regr-<stamp>-<n>`), so none of them had the benefit of a prior turn and my isolated `--only 37` runs were NOT the artefact I suspected they might be:
  * full gate run 1  -> DECLINED, 35.3 s
  * `--only 37`      -> DECLINED,  9.7 s   (`Final intent for routing: diagnosis`, then
                                            `[response] nothing to say: intent=diagnosis
                                             entities=none ran=the diagnosis lane error=none`)
  * full gate run 2  -> **ANSWERED**, 31.2 s, `first_pass_failed=False` (no retry):
        '**Best match: Room 5.56 - Research Laboratory** (floor Floor5, score 0.8637 out of 1 ...) 1. Room 5.56 - score 0.8637 (temperature: 20.818) 2. Room 5.69 - score 0.8257 (temperature: 21.046) 3. Room 5.63 - score 0.8067 (temperature: 21.16) **Assumptions:** ...'
**So the same question reaches TWO DIFFERENT LANES across identical asks** -- `diagnosis`, which runs and produces nothing, or the ranking lane, which answers with scored rooms and an assumptions block. 2 of 3 decline.
That makes it a ROUTING instability, not a generation one, and it is a concrete counter-example to the determinism result recorded on 2026-09-29 ('10 questions x 5 asks, 0 of 10 unstable'). That measurement was on ten OTHER questions; this one names no place, no time and no record, which is the shape CAVEAT-891 identifies as least stable.
**CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE, and it is the reason this row stays open after a 51/51:** the gate reported **51 of 51, first-pass, zero retries, zero cache hits** immediately after this question had declined twice. A 51/51 containing a known intermittent is not a clean 51/51, and quoting it as one is how a flake becomes invisible. Re-ask #37 explicitly whenever the gate is used to decide anything.
Still NOT fixed, and the earlier note stands: a provenance question needs a prior turn to be about. Note too that the answering run did not actually give EVIDENCE for a previous answer -- it answered the underlying question ('which room is coolest') with a ranking. Both behaviours are defensible; having both at random is not.
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED. Before any fix: establish which of (a) and (b) it is by asking it 5x and reading the `Final intent for routing` line each time — if the intent varies it is (a), if it is diagnosis every time it is (b). That is one cheap measurement and it decides the whole approach.
DO NOT add a routing rule for it first. A provenance question needs a prior turn to be about; routing it somewhere that also cannot see the prior turn moves the decline, not the defect.
ONE MEASUREMENT ARTEFACT TO AVOID WHEN RE-ASKING: the first re-ask carried '**I couldn't read <building>'s sensor catalogue just now**' and that sentence was MINE and SPURIOUS — `_measured_modality_counts` has a 5 s timeout and I had just flushed `cache:sparql*` and restarted, so the catalogue read timed out on a cold cache. It is absent once the cache is warm. Do not chase it.
Verification: FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02. It is (b): no lane owned 'explain the answer you just gave'. A question about the ASSISTANT'S previous answer -- 'your/that/the last answer', 'what you said', 'how did you get/arrive at', 'the evidence behind your answer' -- is now a session-recall question (`session_recall._ABOUT_MY_ANSWER`), the one lane that reads this conversation's own record. MEASURED over the 4,060 bank: 4 moves, all about the assistant's answers; a first draft also matched 'can I see the last RESULT' (a data question) and 'the reading behind that NUMBER', so result/figure/number are excluded. Live, fresh conversation: 'What is the evidence behind your answer about the coolest room?' -> '**Nothing has been asked in this conversation yet**, so there is nothing for me to recall' (lane=session_recall, deterministic -- it had reached diagnosis on 2 of 3 asks). With a prior turn the lane quotes the question it answered; it does not reproduce the evidence, which is BUG-941's still-open half. Tests in `tests/test_how_a_thing_is_done_is_not_a_reading.py`.

Title: The regression gate's saved JSON does not record the verdict the run reported, so the artefact reads as a pass
Description:
`regression_answerability.py` prints `REGRESSED` per case and `REGRESSED: [4, 37]` at the end, then saves a JSON whose every row carries `"verdict": "GOOD"`.
The two are not contradictory — `verdict` is the pack's stored HAND-READ label and `status` is what the run computed — but `status` is **never written to the file**. The saved keys are n, question, verdict, expected_kind, got_kind, seconds, error, answer, first_pass_failed.
**So the artefact of a 49/51 run shows GOOD on all 51 rows.** It is derivable (`expected_kind != got_kind`) and nothing in the file says so. Anyone reading the JSON later — or a script summarising it — concludes the gate passed.
Found while reading the two regressions behind today's 49/51, and logged because this project's recurring failure is an instrument that cannot reproduce its own conclusion (lessons #172, CAVEAT-1346).
Root_Cause: `results.append({**{k: r[k] for k in ("n", "question", "verdict", "expected_kind")}, ...})` carries the pack's label and omits the computed status.
Fix_Approach: One key: add `"status": status` to the saved row, and the summary counts with it. NOT done in this change because the gate was mid-use as the arbiter of a routing fix, and editing the instrument while it is deciding a question is how a measurement becomes unattributable.

Title: 'there is no room that meets the capacity requirement' for a room for 12, while 28 spaces record 12 or more and the three projector rooms hold 30, 25 and 25
Description:
FOUND BY RE-ASKING BUG-1362, which no longer reproduces -- the projector denial is gone and the answer now NAMES the rooms ('Rooms that have a projector | 3 (Room 1.06, Room 2.01, Room 3.01)'). This took its place and is worse.
Live, facility01@example.com on /v1, `resp_cache:*` flushed, verbatim:
    Q 'Find a room for 12 with a projector, free 2-4pm today, near the cafe.'
    A 'I did not find any room that satisfies all of the requested criteria ...
       | Rooms that can seat 12 people | **0** |
       | Rooms that have a projector | 3 (Room 1.06, Room 2.01, Room 3.01) |
       ... **Because no workspace has a seat count of 12, there is no room that meets the capacity requirement.** Consequently, I cannot identify a suitable room ...'
**MEASURED AGAINST THE GRAPH, no namespace asserted (see Root_Cause for why that matters):**
  * `roomCapacity`: 42 values, min 8, max 50, **36 of them >= 12**
  * `seatCount`:    28 values, min 6, max 48, **18 of them >= 12**
  * **28 distinct spaces record room for 12 or more people.**
**AND THE THREE PROJECTOR ROOMS ARE AMONG THEM:** Room 1.06 (roomCapacity 30, 'Level 1 computer lab 1.06' seatCount 30), Room 2.01 (25), Room 3.01 (25). So the two criteria this building DOES record -- capacity and projector -- are both satisfied by all three rooms it had already named one line earlier, and the answer concluded there is none. The other two criteria (2-4pm availability, cafe proximity) are honestly disclosed as not recorded, which is correct and is not the defect.
Root_Cause:
THREE CAUSES, AND THE FIRST IS SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN.
(1) **'for 12' IS READ AS AN EQUALITY, NOT A FLOOR.** The answer's own words are 'no workspace has a seat count OF 12', and that is literally true: the `seatCount` values are 6, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30, 48 -- **none is exactly 12**. A request for a room for 12 is satisfied by a room for 30. An equality test returns 0 here and will return 0 for almost any party size, because an exact seat count is a coincidence.
(2) **ONE OF TWO CAPACITY FIELDS WAS IN VIEW.** `seatCount` sits on WorkspaceProfile; `roomCapacity` sits on the Brick room classes (Conference_Room 18, Laboratory 14, Break_Room 4, Office 4). The lane fetched WorkspaceProfile only, so the 36 roomCapacity values >= 12 were never visible.
(3) **A REGISTER SHORT-CIRCUIT CLAIMED A FOUR-CONSTRAINT QUESTION, bypassing the lane built for it.** From the log:
    [ttl-route] metadata via held record class: WorkspaceProfile (28 instances) — skipping LLM intent call
    Final intent for routing: metadata
    [sparql] whole-register fetch: WorkspaceProfile (28 instances, 23 fields) — no SPARQL generated
`deliberate` ranks rooms on several criteria and demonstrably works (the same day it answered gate case #37 with 'Best match: Room 5.56 ... score 0.8637' over three ranked rooms). `DELIBERATE_RE` MATCHES this question ('find a room'), so the only thing keeping it out is `_r_...is_deliberate`'s third condition, `has_measurand_concept` -- and capacity, projector, 2-4pm and cafe-proximity resolve no measurand. That condition is deliberate and well-argued in its own docstring; it simply has no answer for a multi-constraint question with no sensor quantity in it.
**NOTE THE DATA WAS IN THE PROMPT.** The fetch carried 23 fields including `seatCount`, so cause (1) is a NARRATION defect over facts the lane supplied correctly -- the same family as BUG-955, where the fetch was perfect every time and all the variance was in the narration.
**AND MY OWN FIRST PROBE SAID THE OPPOSITE.** It asserted `o: <http://www.ontosage.org/ontology#>` and asked `?s a o:WorkspaceProfile`, got ZERO capacity triples, and printed 'the register really holds nothing at 12 or above'. The class is not in that namespace. One step from logging a defect about a field that is not missing -- the figures above come from matching the PREDICATE's local name with no namespace asserted at all.
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED, deliberately, and the reason is this session's own record: five candidate fixes were measured today and FIVE were rejected (a forecast test that moved 107 wrong questions, a `project\w*` that matches PROJECTOR, an arrow-keyed ordering guard where 44% of arrows are routes, a threshold relaxation, a bare-lay-term removal). An un-measured fix in this cluster ships a wrong answer.
THREE CANDIDATES, in increasing blast radius, each needing its own measurement:
  (a) **Cause (1) alone, and it is the cheapest and the biggest win.** A party size in a question is a FLOOR. Nothing routing-related changes; the register facts block states the constraint as '>= 12' so the narration cannot read it as equality. Measure over the catalogue by counting questions containing 'for N people'/'room for N'/'N of us' and re-asking a sample -- this cannot over-capture because it changes an arithmetic reading, not a lane.
  (b) Cause (2): the capacity view should span both predicates. TTL-first alternative worth pricing FIRST: give WorkspaceProfile rows the room's `roomCapacity`, or state both with their basis (`capacityBasis` is 'estimated; carried forward unchanged' on 42 Spaces, so any figure must carry that caveat -- BUG-1244's requirement).
  (c) Cause (3): let a multi-constraint room request reach `deliberate` without a measurand. **Highest risk and measure it hardest** -- `DELIBERATE_RE` matches a lot, and relaxing the measurand condition re-opens exactly what its docstring says it was added to stop ('which approved nearby space is suitable for a brief quiet pause?' converted into a reading). Count bank questions matching DELIBERATE_RE with no measurand before touching it, and run the 51-case gate before and after.
Do (a) first and re-ask this question: if the three projector rooms come back, (b) and (c) may be worth less than they look.

--- CAUSE (1) FIXED 2026-10-01: THE SIZE IS COUNTED IN CODE AS A FLOOR ---
`register_facts._at_least_lines`, beside the counting this module already does, because the whole reason it exists is that arithmetic left to the narration comes back wrong (BUG-581). It states nothing unless the question names a size AND the register holds a numeric column of people -- a count against a floor nobody asked for is noise, and inventing a capacity column is worse.
**VERIFIED IN THE PROMPT against the real rows** (read from the graph with NO namespace asserted, because asserting one is what made my first probe report the opposite):
    '- THE SIZE IN THE QUESTION IS A MINIMUM, NOT AN EXACT VALUE. **18 of 28** records with a recorded seatCount (seat count) are 12 or MORE: WS-01 (48), WS-26 (30), WS-25 (30), WS-03 (30), WS-02 (30), WS-09 (28), ... and 3 more. A record of 48 satisfies a request for 12. NEVER say none meets it because no value equals 12 exactly, and never report a count of records whose seatCount is exactly 12.'
That 18 of 28 is the figure independently measured from the graph on this row.
**MEASURED BLAST RADIUS over the 4,060-question bank: 15 questions name a size (0.37%).** All 17 original matches were READ rather than counted, which found **two false positives**, both real bank questions and both now excluded: *'passes 200 **person-hours** since last clean'* (a unit, not a party) and *'will hold 22 **degrees** and low noise'* (a temperature). A unit after the number is the tell. The digit cap is THREE, not four, because 'readings for **2026**' was read as a party size of 2026.
**AND A TEST CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN CODE:** I matched column words with `[A-Za-z]+`, which takes camelCase as a SINGLE token -- so `roomCapacity` came back as {'roomcapacity'} and matched nothing, while `seatCount` matched only because 'seatcount' happened to be in the word set. The module's other column matcher already splits on `[A-Za-z][a-z]+`; using a second spelling is how two matchers for one judgement begin to disagree (BUG-947).
Tests: `tests/test_a_party_size_is_a_floor_not_an_equality.py`, **21 pass**, including the exact live `seatCount` values (none equals 12, eighteen exceed it), a genuine-shortfall case, `roomCapacity` as well as `seatCount`, and silence when either half is missing. **359 pass** across all eleven test files that cover `register_facts`.
Verification:
PARTIALLY FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-01, facility01@example.com on /v1, `resp_cache:*` flushed before EACH of three asks, after restart:
**THE FABRICATED 'NO' IS GONE 3 OF 3.** No 'seat count of 12', no 'Rooms that can seat 12 people | 0', no 'there is no room that meets the capacity requirement' in any ask.
**THE RIGHT ANSWER APPEARS 1 OF 3** (ask 2), and it is the answer the building can defend:
    'The only workspace that satisfies the **size** (12 or more seats) and has a **projector** recorded in the AV register is: **WS-02 - Level 1 computer lab 1.06** - Seat count: 30 (Workspace profile) - Projector: AV-106-PRJ (Teaching AV readiness) - status ready. The records do **not** contain any information about: whether the room is free between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. today; its proximity to the cafe.'
Note it says '12 or MORE seats' -- the floor line, used. And 'the only' is not a fabrication: 1.06 is the one room in the WorkspaceProfile-and-AV intersection at >= 12.
Asks 1 and 3 DECLINE honestly instead ('The records do not indicate whether a room has a projector ... They do record seat counts, booking status'), naming what is held without using the count.
**SO THE SEVERITY MOVES FROM CONFIDENTLY WRONG TO INCONSISTENTLY USEFUL, which is the right direction and is not a complete fix.** The residual is CAVEAT-891 exactly: the facts are deterministic and in the prompt, and whether the narration uses them is not. Causes (2) and (3) on this row are untouched, and a projection decline can still pre-empt the narration before the counted line is read.
**WHAT I DID NOT CLAIM:** the first post-fix ask declined, and I nearly attributed that to the fix. It is the same narration variance seen across the three asks, not an effect of the change -- the counted line was verified present in the prompt independently.
Refs: BUG-1362; BUG-1396; BUG-955; BUG-1244; lesson #133; lesson #136; BUG-581; CAVEAT-891; lesson #176

Title: Three new test files lacked `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`, so 61 tests were deselected by the suite that gates a commit
Description:
The `unit` marker in this repo is EXPLICIT -- `pytest.ini` declares it and no conftest applies it automatically. Three test files written on 2026-10-01 (`test_a_preposition_is_not_a_subject.py`, `test_an_emergency_may_be_two_sentences.py`, `test_a_party_size_is_a_floor_not_an_equality.py`) omitted it.
All 61 tests passed when invoked BY NAME, every time, and **protected nothing**: `pytest -m unit` -- the suite Workflow rule 8 runs before a commit, and what CI sees -- deselected all of them.
**THE TELL WAS IN THE SUMMARY LINE AND IT IS WORTH KNOWING:** after adding 21 tests the run read `13742 passed ... 1357 deselected` where the previous run read `13742 passed ... 1336 deselected`. **`passed` did not move and `deselected` rose by exactly the number of tests added.** A green run with an unchanged pass count after adding tests is the signature of this mistake.
Same family as CAVEAT-1060 (a settings patch that patched something the product no longer read) and the three vacuous-guard findings before it: the worse half of a test defect is the half that never goes red.
Root_Cause: `pytest.ini` line 26 declares `markers = unit: fast, isolated unit tests` and `--strict-markers`, but strict-markers only rejects UNKNOWN markers; it cannot require that a file carry one. Nothing in `tests/conftest.py` auto-marks by filename, so an unmarked file is silently outside every marker-selected run.
Fix_Approach:
All three files marked, verified: `pytest -m unit <the three files>` now collects and passes **61**. Each carries a note saying the marker is not automatic and naming the summary-line tell, so the next author of a new test file sees it.
NOT DONE, and it is the durable fix: a test that FAILS when a file under `tests/` contributes zero tests to `-m unit`. That would have caught this on the first run instead of on a careful reading of a deselected count, and it is the same shape as `test_reserved_keys_have_writers.py`, which derives the answer from the source instead of trusting prose. Worth doing before the next batch of test files.
Verification: `pytest -m unit` on the three files: **61 passed**. Before the marker they contributed 0 to that selection while passing 61/61 when named directly.

Title: A correct decline carries a sampling disclaimer and cites three sensing systems it never used
Description:
FOUND BY THE REGRESSION GATE reporting case #70 as `declined -> answered`, which it is NOT. Verbatim, facility01 on /v1:
    Q 'What is the air pressure in room 2.01 right now?'
    A 'I'm sorry, but there is no air-pressure sensor recorded for Room 2.01, so I can't provide a current value. _At least one sensor returned the full 60 rows this question reads per sensor, so these readings are a SAMPLE of the newest data and their number is not a count of what the period holds. The readings used run from 2026-10-01 04:22:18 to 2026-10-01 09:23:15. That is the newest part of the last 30 days, not the whole of it._ --- *Sources: `Building model` `Sensor data` `Lighting Sensing System` `Acoustic Sensing System` `Occupancy Sensing System`*'
**THE FIRST SENTENCE IS CORRECT AND VERIFIED.** Room 2.01's recorded points are air temperature, CO2, zone air humidity, door contact, illuminance, noise, occupancy and window contact. There is no pressure point. (The 'Air Pressure Sensor' subjects in the graph are Brick CLASS and NodeShape definitions, not instances of this building -- which is why this had to be checked against the graph rather than read off the answer.)
**THE REST OF THE ANSWER IS NOISE AND IT IS NOT HARMLESS.** A reader is told 'the readings used run from 04:22 to 09:23' and shown three sensing systems as SOURCES, in an answer that used no readings at all and provided no value. It implies data informed a conclusion that was drawn from the absence of data. The disclaimer is correct boilerplate attached to the wrong kind of turn.
Root_Cause:
NOT DIAGNOSED. The sampling disclaimer and the Sources block are appended by the response path from what the turn FETCHED, and the turn did fetch -- it reached a data lane, pulled 60 rows per sensor for the room's other modalities, found no pressure series, and declined. So the fetch really happened and the provenance really lists what was read; what is wrong is attaching either to a turn whose answer is 'no such sensor is recorded'.
Not attributed to any change made today. The SUBSTANCE of this answer matches the recorded baseline (a decline the pack's hand read judged GOOD); only the trailing material differs, and nothing measured today shows when that trailing material started appearing.
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED. The shape of it: a turn that provides NO figure should not carry a sampling disclaimer about rows it read, and should cite as sources only what its answer rests on -- here the building model, which is what establishes the absence.
Measure first how many stored answers pair a decline with a sampling disclaimer; the disclaimer exists because a truncated sample reported as a total is a worse defect, so the rule must suppress it ONLY where no figure is given, never where one is.
Verification:
FIXED OFFLINE 2026-10-01 for the DISCLAIMER half; the Sources block is NOT changed. `disclosure_gate.gives_a_figure(text)` is True when the answer states a number that is not a date, a clock time, a record id, a room/floor number or an image link; the response node attaches the truncation note only when it is True. Any note already in the text is cut first -- its own '60 rows' is a number, and the first draft of the test split on the wrong phrase and returned True on BUG-1401's own text.
MEASURED over 3,046 stored answers (phase0 + outputs + gate JSONs): 57 carry the note, 5 would lose it, and ALL 5 state no figure -- four pressure declines for Room 2.01 and 'No purity measurement is available'. 52 keep it. 781 of 3,046 answers are judged no-figure overall, which is the declines and the room lists.
NOT FIXED: the `*Sources:*` line still lists the sensing systems a declining turn read. Separate measurement owed before touching it.
Tests: `tests/test_a_no_figure_turn_carries_no_sampling_note.py`, 17 pass.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02: 'What is the air pressure in room 2.01 right now?' -> 'I don't have an air-pressure reading for Room 2.01.' with NO sampling note. The `*Sources:*` line still lists Lighting / Acoustic / Occupancy Sensing Systems the turn read -- the half this row leaves open, deliberately unmeasured.

SOURCES HALF FIXED 2026-10-02 (offline; live re-ask owed). `provenance.tags_for_answer()` keeps every tag when the answer states a figure and only the non-reading tags (model, documents) when it does not; `is_reading_source` is keyed on the tag's STORE (mysql/postgres/timescale/cassandra/influx/mongo/compute) and the live_sensors/analytics ids. MEASURED first over 2,554 stored answers: 322 cite a sensing or metering system, **12 state no figure and all 12 are declines** -- the set this changes. In the course of measuring, `gives_a_figure` was found to call 29.81, 47.56, 25.70 and '13 persons' NO figure (a bare two-decimal stripper meant for room ids, and a date pattern with no month); both tightened toward KEEPING the note, the 57-note set still drops the same 5, and the corpus's no-figure count fell 781 -> 623. Tests: `tests/test_a_decline_cites_no_reading_source.py` (4); provenance slice 135 pass.

SOURCES HALF: the three-sensing-system footer could not be re-asked tonight on the air-pressure question (not in the live rounds); `tags_for_answer` is unit-tested and the response node is wired. Live re-ask owed on 'What is the air pressure in room 2.01 right now?'.

BOTH HALVES VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02 09:45 through the gate's own harness (case #70): the SQL lane was still appending the note to ITS OWN prose before the response node ran (the first fix only guarded the response node's append); the same `gives_a_figure` test now runs at the lane's append site. Answer: a plain decline, no sampling note, Sources = Building model only. The gate's classifier now reads it as declined -> declined, so CAVEAT-1402's misread is gone with it.

Title: The gate cannot tell a correct decline that gained a disclaimer from a question that wrongly started answering
Description:
Gate case #70 was reported `REGRESSED  declined -> answered`, and the answer DECLINES -- correctly, verifiably, in its first sentence. The harness classified it as 'answered' because of an appended sampling disclaimer and a Sources block (BUG-1401).
So a run that is **51/51 in substance** was reported as 50/51, and the one flagged case is the only one whose answer was read by hand. That is the better failure direction -- a false alarm costs a reading, a missed alarm costs a defect -- but it is still an instrument error and it is the FOURTH distinct one found in this gate today (the others: `--token` silently defaulting to empty, case #1 answered from cache in 0.1 s, and the saved JSON not recording its own verdict, CAVEAT-1398).
**AND THE LABEL IS STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO BE RIGHT HERE.** `status` is computed as `'BETTER' if r['verdict'] != 'GOOD' and kind == 'answered' else 'REGRESSED'`. For a case whose pack verdict IS 'GOOD' and whose recorded kind is 'declined' -- a decline the hand read APPROVED -- any move to 'answered' can only be labelled REGRESSED, whether it is a fabrication or a formatting change. The two outcomes that matter most are collapsed into one word.
Root_Cause: Two independent weaknesses. (1) The decline classifier reads prose and a decline with trailing boilerplate stops looking like one -- CAVEAT-887's point exactly: nothing the server returns SAYS whether a turn declined, so all four classifiers in this repo guess from text. (2) The BETTER branch is gated on the pack verdict rather than on the recorded kind, so it cannot fire for a GOOD decline.
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED, and deliberately not bundled with CAVEAT-1398's one-key fix, which was made while the gate was idle rather than mid-arbitration.
The durable fix is the one CAVEAT-887 already names and nobody has built: a lane records its own outcome on the bus and `/v1` returns it, so the gate reads a fact instead of guessing from prose. `retrieval_outcome` already has the right vocabulary and never reaches `/v1`.
The cheap half, worth doing first: make the BETTER/REGRESSED branch consider the recorded KIND, and classify the decline on the answer's FIRST sentence rather than the whole string -- five consumers in this repo already key on the first sentence for exactly this reason.

Title: A barometric-pressure question was answered with AHU filter differential pressure, three orders of magnitude out, after the lane silently dropped the qualifier it could not support
Description:
FOUND WHILE VERIFYING BUG-1319 -- one of its control questions. Live, facility01 on /v1, caches flushed:
    Q 'What is the barometric pressure in the building?'
    A '**Across the building pressure is averaging 19.1 Pa**, ranging from 0.0 to 51.5 Pa' with a per-floor table of six sensors.
**THE SIX BOUND SENSORS ARE ALL AHU FILTER DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE.** Read from the graph: 'Air Handling Unit - Floor N filter differential pressure', typed `Filter_Differential_Pressure_Sensor` -- the pressure drop across an air-handling unit's filter, which indicates a clogged filter. **Barometric pressure is ~101,325 Pa.** This building holds NO barometric sensor, so the honest answer is that it cannot be given.
**AND THE LANE KNEW.** It logged, before answering:
    [aggregate] qualifier 'barometric' not carried by all 6 bound sensor names - keeping 'pressure'
It detected the mismatch, dropped the reader's qualifier, and said nothing about having done so. The design note beside that branch reasoned that the coarse name is 'at least not a claim about a quantity nobody measured' -- true of the NAME, and not enough: the FIGURES are of another physical quantity.
NOT A REGRESSION FROM THE BUG-1319 PROMPT CHANGE, checked rather than assumed: the route is `sensor_data` -> sparql -> sql -> aggregate_lane, and the reasoning prompt edited for BUG-1319 is on `_retrieve_context`'s RAG path, which this turn did not take. The qualifier-drop is this session's own earlier work on `aggregate_lane` (absent from HEAD).
Root_Cause:
`asked_quantity_name` is wording-only by contract. Where the reader's qualifier is not carried by EVERY bound sensor name it returned the coarse measurand, so a barometric question was summarised under 'pressure' -- which is true of the sensors and is not the quantity asked about.
**AND THE LABELS IT JUDGES ARE ABBREVIATED, which is why the first version of the fix did nothing.** The lane reads `metadata[uuid]['label']`, and live those are **'AHU F5 Filter DP', 'AHU F2 Filter DP', ...** -- short display names in which 'differential pressure' is 'DP'. The word 'pressure' is absent, so reading leftwards from it found nothing. The graph's own `rdfs:label` carries the full phrase; the lane does not see it. That cost two probes to establish, because the decision was logged WITHOUT the labels that produced it.
Verification:
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-01 after restart, `resp_cache:*` flushed, facility01 on /v1. The question now DECLINES, and the mechanism is the point:
    [aggregate] qualifier 'barometric' not carried by all 6 bound sensor names - naming what they DO carry: 'AHU Filter DP pressure' (from labels ['AHU F5 Filter DP', ...])
    [response] relevance gate replaced a sensor_data answer: OFF_TOPIC (Provides AHU filter pressure, not barometric pressure.)
    [response] the relevance gate deleted a sensor_data answer; rows visibly read this turn=6 -- the decline WILL say the records were read
Reader sees: 'I couldn't put an answer together from Abacws Building's records - I did read them, but what I could make of them did not answer the question you asked.'
**THE FIX ADDED NO GUARD; IT GAVE AN EXISTING GUARD THE INFORMATION IT NEEDED.** The answer-relevance gate had been silent on this turn not because it was wrong but because the answer called itself 'pressure', which is not off-topic for a pressure question. Naming the quantity truthfully made the mismatch visible and the gate declined on its own -- and the decline honestly states the records WERE read (BUG-1252).
CONTROLS IN THE SAME RUN, both still answering: 'What is the temperature in room 5.01 right now?' -> 24.74 °C with range and mean; 'What is the CO2 on floor 3?' -> 898 ppm with the floor's low and high named by sensor.
Tests: `tests/test_a_dropped_qualifier_names_what_was_measured.py`, 15 pass, including the abbreviated live labels, that the per-sensor token (F0..F5) is dropped, that the reader's unsupported qualifier is never echoed, and four fall-back cases. Slice `-k 'aggregate or quantity_name or qualifier'`: **202 pass**.

Title: Tail O: 60 unseen real-corpus questions as an occupant, hand-read — 36/60 acceptable, 0 fabricated
Description:
TAIL O, 2026-10-01: 60 questions drawn from the real survey corpus by `scripts/draw_tail.py --name O --n 60 --seed 20261001`, **excluding every one of the 1,352 questions that appears in any stored answer file** (tails C-N, the demo path, the probe packs). Mix 53 LOOKUP / 5 AGGREGATION / 2 MULTI_STEP against the corpus's own 88/9/3. Question file sha256 7f3681c35937f53b697fa6de14d459c17a1d17043e07b8900c2cf45d4024e877.
**IDENTITY CONFIRMED FROM THE SERVER, NOT THE FLAG** (lesson #169): `[forwarded-user] 'occupant01@example.com' -> 'occupant01' (role=occupant)`. `/v1/chat/completions`, streaming, `resp_cache:*` flushed before each ask. Every answer recorded in FULL -- no 400-character window this time (CAVEAT-1293).
**RESULT, second pass (the 14 provider failures re-asked on a healthy LLM):**
  GOOD 24 | DECLINE-OK 12 | **DECLINE-BAD 11** | **WEIRD 13** | **FABRICATED 0**
  **Acceptable 36/60 = 60.0%. Unacceptable 24/60 = 40.0%.**
**RESULT, first pass (provider failures counted as failures, which is this project's own rule): acceptable 27/60 = 45.0%, provider failures 14.**
**ZERO FABRICATED FIGURES, for the third independent set of 60 unseen real questions.** The failures are false declines and wrong-quantity bindings, both visible to a reader; no invented number was found.
**NOT PRESENTED AS A REGRESSION AGAINST TAIL N's 46/60 = 76.7%.** Two confounds, neither resolved: tail O excludes 1,352 previously-asked questions and is therefore a harder residue, and these labels are mine while tail N's came from an earlier pass -- a stricter reader produces a lower number from the same system. Settling it needs ONE reader labelling both sets.
**THE FAILURE PROFILE: false declines dominate at 11 of 60 (18.3%)**, and six are provable against the graph -- filters (30 cleaning-task records the SAME question had listed on its first pass), parking (a `parking_data` store and a Transport Parking amenity), 'any movement?' (501 occupancy series), 'Room available now?' (the longer phrasing answers it with 5 of 18 rooms named), lighting (a `Lighting` capability topic), continuity (12 ContinuityProvision records). Wrong-quantity or misread answers: 13 of 60 (21.7%).
**WHAT WORKED, STRUCTURALLY:** the clarification lane refused 'this room' correctly twice, the RBAC refusal named the role and the remedy, privacy was answered correctly when asked directly, and the capability lane gave specific grounded answers on catering, CCTV, wellbeing, sustainability, HVAC zoning and power resilience.
Evidence: `docs/phase0/tail_O_2026-10-01_read.md` (every answer, its label and the reasoning for the contested ones), plus the four jsonl captures beside it.
Root_Cause: N/A -- this row is the measurement, not a defect. The defects it found are BUG-1405 (a headline contradicting its own table), BUG-1406 (the false-decline cluster), BUG-1407 (wrong-quantity binding), BUG-1408 (internal content to the reader) and CAVEAT-1409 (the environment that contaminated the first pass).
Fix_Approach: The next measurement should be read by whoever read tail N, over BOTH sets, to separate a stricter reader from a changed system. Until then neither 76.7% nor 60.0% can be quoted as a trend -- only as two numbers from two readers.
Verification:
60 of 60 captured; 14 re-asked after the provider was restored; all 74 answers on disk in full. Labels and reasoning in `docs/phase0/tail_O_2026-10-01_read.md`.

--- RE-ASKED AFTER THE FIXES: THE FIRST VALID BEFORE/AFTER THIS PROJECT HAS ---
Same 60 questions, same reader, same identity (`role=occupant` confirmed from the server's own line), same endpoint, same labels. Nothing differs but the build. **That is what makes it readable as a trend, and why tail N vs tail O was not** -- those had different sets AND different readers.
Both bases are second-pass: the BEFORE run's 14 provider failures were re-asked on a healthy provider before labelling, and the AFTER run had **zero** (0 breaker-open lines, provider verified before and after -- the check lesson #182 exists for).
| label | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| GOOD | 24 | 26 | +2 |
| DECLINE-OK | 12 | 16 | +4 |
| **DECLINE-BAD** | **11** | **11** | **0** |
| **WEIRD** | 13 | **7** | **-6** |
| **FABRICATED** | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| **ACCEPTABLE** | **36/60 = 60.0%** | **42/60 = 70.0%** | **+10.0 pp** |
**7 questions moved into acceptable, 1 moved out, 44 unchanged, 8 changed class while staying unacceptable.**
MOVED IN: mould (a general-knowledge answer instead of a dump of AccessPermission IRIs); water purity (*'No purity measurement is available. These values describe flow, not water purity'* -- the quantity mismatch now stated rather than hidden); temperature-by-crowding (the 71 degC water mixing gone); **filters** (it now DISCLOSES the 30 cleaning-task records it previously denied, split 24 scheduled / 3 added / 2 suspended); **'any movement?'** (now answers from the intruder detectors instead of declining over 501 occupancy series); flow-sensor leak detection; and kitchen standby power (the raw AutoCAD markup gone).
MOVED OUT (1): 'I want to know more about flow rate and how those sensors can be used to save residents' money' now answers with *'Across the building flow is averaging 285, ranging from 0.0 to 818'* over six single-sensor floors -- a mixed-scale aggregate with no unit, where it previously declined.
**HOW MUCH OF THE +6 IS ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE FIXES, HONESTLY: about three of seven.** The kitchen-markup case is directly BUG-1407; the water-purity and crowding cases are the quantity-naming and medium-mixing work (BUG-1403, BUG-1405). The mould, movement, filter and flow-sensor cases moved without a change aimed at them -- lane and generation variance, the CAVEAT-891 effect, and it cuts both ways.
**WHAT DID NOT MOVE IS THE MORE IMPORTANT NUMBER: false declines are flat at 11 of 60 (18.3%) and are now the single dominant failure mode** (BUG-1406). Six remain provable against the graph.
**AND A NEW CONFIDENTLY-WRONG ANSWER APPEARED, which is the worst shape:** 'Are there any free parking spots available right now?' -> *'**There are no free parking spots available at the moment.** The latest readings from the EV charger status sensors ... show a value of 0 for each charger.'* A definite claim about parking availability, derived from two EV CHARGER status points.
