Title: A building-wide temperature headline reads 27.6 °C ranging to 71.0 °C directly above its own per-floor table showing 23.0–23.9 °C
Description:
FOUND BY TAIL O #39, occupant01 on /v1. Question: 'Do you adjust temperature based on how crowded it is?'
    '**Across the building temperature is averaging 27.6 °C**, ranging from 7.2 to 71.0 °C.' -- followed immediately by its own table: Floor 0 23.9, Floor 1 23.0, Floor 2 23.8, Floor 3 23.9, Floor 4 23.9 ...
**THE HEADLINE CONTRADICTS THE TABLE IN THE SAME ANSWER.** Tail O #32, asked minutes earlier on the same quantity, produced a consistent pair: 'averaging 23.8 °C, ranging from 15.4 to 25.1 °C' over the same per-floor figures.
**71.0 °C IS NOT ROOM AIR.** It is a heating circuit or flow temperature. So the building-wide statistic folded plant temperatures in with room air while the table showed room sensors only -- BUG-521's quantity-mixing shape, which averaged 900 ppm of CO2 with 21.5 °C because the narrow column is called `value`.
A reader shown '71.0 °C' in a building answer would reasonably conclude something is dangerously wrong.
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED. Two things are established: the figures disagree WITHIN one answer, and the same question shape produced a consistent answer in the same session, so this is not a constant property of the lane. The candidate is the bound set for the headline statistic differing from the set behind the table -- a superset including plant/flow temperature points. `units.aggregation_decision()` exists for exactly this class of mistake (V12-04) and should be checked for whether this path calls it.
Fix_Approach: NOT ATTEMPTED. Start by reproducing with the bound UUIDs logged, then compare the set behind the headline with the set behind the table -- the defect is almost certainly that they are different sets, and the fix is that a headline may only summarise the rows the table shows. **A test that the headline's min/max lies within the table's min/max would have caught this**, and that invariant is cheap, deterministic and lane-agnostic.
Verification:
**MY DIAGNOSIS ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE BEFORE THE FIX IS DESCRIBED.**
I logged it as 'a headline contradicting its own table'. It does not. The full stored answer has a SEVENTH table row I never saw, because my own dump cut the text at 330 characters:
    | Floor http://<the building's namespace>#Rooftop | 50.6 | 7.2 | 71.0 | 8 |
The headline's 7.2-71.0 range is supported by the table exactly. **Fourth truncation-induced error in one session** (lesson #176), and the one that would have sent the fix to the wrong place -- `aggregate_lane` already guards mean-against-range and that guard was working.
**THE REAL DEFECT IS WORSE AND IS NOW FIXED.** Those eight 'Rooftop floor' points are **Gas Boiler 1 and 2, Chiller 1 and Heat Pump 1 entering and leaving WATER temperatures**, read from the graph: `Water_Temperature_Sensor`, `Entering_Water_Temperature_Sensor`, `Leaving_Water_Temperature_Sensor`. **71.0 degC is boiler leaving water; 7.2 degC is chilled water.** Brick puts those classes under `Temperature_Sensor`, so a question about temperature bound them along with room air, and the building mean came out at 27.6 degC against ~23.8 for the rooms -- BUG-521's shape, which averaged 900 ppm of CO2 with 21.5 degC because the narrow column is called `value`.
MEASURED: 534 temperature points carry a timeseries; a temperature question binds 296; **8 of those 296 carry a water class and 288 do not.** (The 235 `Lighting_Correlated_Color_Temperature_Sensor` points, in Kelvin, were already excluded and stay excluded.)
FIX: `sensor_binder.QuantitySpec.matches` refuses a point whose Brick class names a medium other than room air, unless the quantity itself declares such a class OR the QUESTION names the medium (`medium_named`, stamped at the single exit of `detect_quantities`). Keyed on the standard Brick class name, so it is building-agnostic by construction -- design contract #3.
**THE FIRST VERSION HAD NO SUCH LIFT AND A GUARD TEST CAUGHT IT:** `test_the_heat_pump_loop_temperature_binds_both_water_points` failed, correctly -- a reader who asks for 'the heat pump water loop' must get water (lesson #153).
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-01 after restart, occupant01 on /v1, cache flushed:
  * 'Is any area overheating right now?' -> **288 temperature sensors on 6 floors**, averaging **23.5 degC**, range 16.0-25.9. The Rooftop plant group is gone, the count fell by exactly the 8 water points, and the mean dropped from 27.6 to a plausible room figure.
  * 'What is the current temperature of the heat pump water loop?' -> 2 sensors, 64.2 degC, range 58.5-70.0. The lift works.
Tests: `tests/test_water_temperature_is_not_room_temperature.py`, 20 pass, including that the exclusion set names water and nothing else, that air classes are absent from it, and that the medium stamp is applied on ONE path so no future return can forget it. Slice `-k 'sensor_binder or binder or aggregate or quantity'`: **633 pass**.

--- PART 2, FOUND BY TAIL P (2026-10-02) AND FIXED, VERIFIED LIVE ---
'Should the building's target temperature shift ... to save energy?' (lane `recommend`) -> 'averaging 25.8 degC, ranging from 6.4 to 71.7' with '| Floor Rooftop | 50.1 | 6.4 | 71.7 | 8 |' -- the same eight boiler/chiller/heat-pump WATER points, back. The binder's exclusion only ran on its POPULATION path; a concept that resolves to the broad class (`setpoint_recommendation` -> Temperature_Sensor) is fetched directly by the sparql agent, 296 rows, on any lane, and `recommend` is not a binder intent. The rule now runs on the RESULT ROWS at the seam (`sensor_binder.drop_foreign_medium_rows`), before the intent gate, keyed on the row's class, label or IRI local name saying both a foreign medium AND 'temperature' (so a water FLOW sensor is untouched), unless the question names the medium. Three attempts to land it: the first read the wrong level of the result envelope (the lane returns {'results': <SPARQL document>}), the second read only a `label` column the entity-less template does not return. Live: 288 sensors / 21.8 degC on the recommend lane, log '[sensor_binder] dropped 8 water/plant point(s) from a 296-row result'; the heat-pump loop question still returns its water (63.1 degC). Tests: `tests/test_water_points_are_dropped_from_every_lanes_result.py` (10).
Refs: TODO-1404; BUG-521; BUG-1403; V12-04; BUG-1407; lesson #153; lesson #176

Title: False declines are the dominant failure mode: 11 of 60 unseen questions, six provable against the graph
Description:
FOUND BY TAIL O (TODO-1404). 11 of 60 answers (18.3%) decline a question the building can answer. Six are provable from the graph or from another answer in the same run:
  * **'how often are the filters cleaned and maintained?'** -> 'The register does not record any information about filter cleaning or maintenance' -- while the FIRST PASS of the same question listed **30 cleaning-task records** (CLN-0001..CLN-0030, scheduled). ServiceSchedule=25 also exists, and the six AHU filter differential-pressure sensors ARE a filter-clogging measure. **The re-ask is worse than the first pass: a false absence over records it had just enumerated.**
  * **'Room available now?'** -> declines, while 'Which meeting room is available immediately?' answers with 5 of 18 rooms NAMED. Same question, two outcomes, same session.
  * **'Are there any free parking spots available right now?'** -> declines (the first pass answered with MEETING-ROOM booking status). A `parking_data` store and a Transport Parking amenity exist.
  * **'any movement?'** -> declines, over 501 occupancy series.
  * **'are lights automatically adjusting properly to current conditions?'** -> declines and names Asset status, Condition survey and Fire safety, while a `Lighting` capability topic exists declaring 'lighting, light, lux, brightness, dim, bright, lights, led, natural light, daylight'.
  * **'How does it ensure the most important systems keep running?'** -> declines; ContinuityProvision=12 records exist.
Also in the set: 'Is there a warmer area than the lobby?' (296 temperature sensors), 'What is the function of your building?' (`bldg1_description.ttl` exists), 'power saved?' (energy and submeter series), 'Are there any areas currently under maintenance restrictions?' (ClosurePeriod=10, WorkOrder=24), and **"'cafeteria' does not exist in this building"** when the building has a cafe that another answer in the same run names with its opening hours.
Root_Cause: NOT ONE CAUSE, and that is the finding. At least four distinct mechanisms are visible: a synonym miss rendered as a flat non-existence claim (cafeteria/cafe); a phrasing-length sensitivity (the same availability question answers when longer); a register selector that cannot reach a register the decline's own pointer names (BUG-947's shape, still live); and a binding failure over series the graph holds (BUG-1319's open half). They share only the OUTCOME.
Fix_Approach: NOT ATTEMPTED as a cluster, deliberately -- 'one fix moves six' has been measured false on this exact shape before (2026-09-30: four of six were not declines at all). Each of the six provable instances should be re-asked with the bound set logged, and filed to the mechanism it belongs to. The filter case is the best starting point because the SAME question enumerated the records on one pass and denied them on the next, which bounds the cause to the narration or the selector rather than the data.
Verification:
SIX OF THE ELEVEN WORKED, EACH TO ITS OWN MECHANISM, offline 2026-10-01; live re-ask owed:
  * parking -> BUG-1411 (binder; the decline and the confident wrong answer were the same chain, which bound 512 occupancy points instead of the one parking point).
  * cafeteria -> `referent_resolver._holds_amenity_kind` now also matches a class's or instance's `o:layTerms`, not only the CamelCase class name; `ontosage:Cafe` already declared 'cafeteria' in the TBox and the building holds a Cafe. Schema-keyed.
  * continuity -> TBox lay terms on ContinuityProvision ('keep running', 'important systems', 'critical systems', 'if the power fails', 'ride through', ...). MEASURED over the 4,060 bank in-container with the live record classes: the first draft (with 'resilience' and 'redundancy') moved 25 primary registers, 20 of them compound stakeholder questions those words hijacked (3 stolen from CostLine, 1 from Contract); without them, 6 moves, five plainly right.
  * filters -> TBox lay terms on ServiceSchedule ('filter change', 'service frequency', 'how often are they maintained', ...). The graph holds 'AHU filter change, all units' in ServiceSchedule and 3 'Coil clean and filter change' WorkOrders; CleaningTask had won on 'cleaned' alone. 0 bank moves.
  * building function -> BUILDING_INFO_KWS gains 'function of the/this/your building', 'purpose of ...', 'what is the building used for', 'what kind of building'. 0 bank matches; the profile lane reads brick:buildingPrimaryFunction = 'Education'.
  * handicapped parking -> AccessibilityFeature lay terms ('handicapped parking', 'disabled bays', 'accessible bays'). 0 bank moves.
  * maintenance restrictions -> ClosurePeriod lay terms ('maintenance restrictions', 'under maintenance', 'out of action'). 'out of service' was added and REMOVED: `test_no_unreviewed_lay_term_is_claimed_by_two_registers` showed AssetStatus already owns it, correctly. 0 bank moves.
NOT WORKED: 'Room available now?' -- the events lane ANSWERED and the relevance gate deleted it as OFF_TOPIC ('Does not address room availability'); BUG-1252's shape, upstream of the gate, not diagnosed further. 'lights adjusting' (now answers with illuminance readings, WEIRD), 'power saved?' (too vague; DECLINE-OK), 'warmer area than the lobby' (compare lane, BUG-879 family).
Tests: `tests/test_the_vocabulary_a_question_reaches_a_register_by.py`, 15 pass.

LIVE 2026-10-02, after three restarts -- six of the eleven re-asked, each on its own fix:
  * continuity -> ANSWERED IN FULL from the register (the 8 high-criticality services, their alternative paths, ride-through minutes and proof-test dates). TWO fixes were needed, not one: the lay terms got the question to the register, and the register's out-of-scope decline then refused it with 'nothing about ensure, important and running' -- the words that had SELECTED it. `resolve` already discounts register terms; `out_of_scope_decline` was the one caller not passing them, and the sparql call site was not passing them to `answer_before_narration` either. Both now do. One narration wobble remains: the summary says '6 of the 8 high-criticality services are verified' and then lists two low-criticality ones among the six -- CAVEAT-891 territory, the counts are the register facts'.
  * filters -> 'cleaned on a **quarterly** basis ... AHU filter change, all units -- service frequency: quarterly' from ServiceSchedule. The first terms I added did not match the question's own wording ('filters cleaned'); the second set does (2 bank moves, both toward ServiceSchedule, both reasonable).
  * cafeteria -> the referent gate no longer refuses ('cafeteria' is a declared lay term of ontosage:Cafe, read even when the word is in no field); the lift-learning question then declines honestly from documents, which is right -- nothing records lift scheduling. 'Is there a cafe in the building?' control: answers with the cafe and its hours.
  * building function -> '**Abacws Building** -- primary function: **Education**.' from brick:buildingPrimaryFunction. THREE things stood in the way: no vocabulary (fixed in BUILDING_INFO_KWS + the profile 'type' facet), the override's intent gate excluding the classifier's own `metadata` guess, and -- the one that cost two restarts -- `cache:intent:*`, a THIRD cache that replays a stored classification and skips the parse-stage contract entirely (logged as 'Cache hit for intent detection'). Flushing resp_cache and cache:sparql* is not enough after a ROUTING change. CAVEAT-1413.
  * maintenance restrictions -> 'There are no areas currently under maintenance restrictions. The records list 10 closure periods ... past ... future' from ClosurePeriod.
  * handicapped parking -> the accessibility register's step-free entrance at the parking level and the hearing loop; grounded, partial (no accessible-bay record exists to cite).
NOT MOVED: 'Which workplace peaks and troughs...' -- the HBCO terms now resolve `busyness` and `occupancy_trend` (confirmed in the log), but the classifier sends it to `compare`, which needs two sides and declines; BUG-1319's binding half is now a ROUTING question. 'Room available now?' -- not re-asked; the relevance gate deletes the events answer (BUG-1252's shape).

2026-10-02: the 'lights adjusting' instance is answered from the Lighting topic (BUG-1415). Remaining of the eleven: 'Room available now?' (gate deletion, BUG-1252), 'power saved?' (vague; honest decline is right).
Refs: TODO-1404; BUG-947; BUG-1319; BUG-1073; BUG-1411; BUG-1252; lesson #184; CAVEAT-1413

Title: Internal content reaches the reader: raw AutoCAD markup as a room label, an incident log dumped for a door question, and bare IRIs
Description:
FOUND BY TAIL O (TODO-1404). Three instances in 60, and this is the live half of BUG-785's family (internal text to a reader), re-confirmed rather than inferred:
  * **#58** 'in this kitchen area, how much vampire power do appliances draw after hours?' -> a spatial table whose Label column reads `\pxqc;{\fArial|b0|i0|c0|p34;\H1.6x;0.16\P\H0.625x;Kitchen}` -- **raw AutoCAD MTEXT formatting codes**, unrendered, presented as the room's name.
  * **#21** 'Are the doors locked' -> a raw dump of the Incident and Near Miss Log, including 'LEV left running; room ventilated | Container placed too close to the sash' and 'INC-2026-005 | Lift entrapment, two occupants, 18 mi...'. Wrong register, and a lift-entrapment incident surfaced to someone asking about door locks.
  * **#17** 'what role does mold play in indoor pollution?' -> a list of **AccessPermission** instances with bare IRIs (`bldg:access/APG-001`, `bldg:access/APG-002`, ... 'and 23 more'), 237 s.
Also adjacent: **#27** printed a raw QUDT unit URI (`http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/L-PER-MIN`) in a water-purity answer.
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED, and the three have different sources. #58 is the DWG/DXF label pipeline passing MTEXT control codes through unparsed -- the floor-plan manifest stores the raw string. #21 and #17 are register/document dumps reaching the reader when the lane could not summarise. #27's URI comes from a unit field rendered verbatim.
Fix_Approach: NOT ATTEMPTED. #58 is the most tractable and the most clearly wrong: MTEXT codes have a known grammar and the label should be the decoded text ('Kitchen'), decided in the DWG pipeline where the manifest is built, not at render time. The other two belong with whatever decides that an unsummarised register may be shown raw -- the answer should name the register and offer to read it, which this system already does well elsewhere.
Verification:
--- PART-FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-01: the two leaks with a single cause each ---
**(1) A BARE IRI AS A FLOOR NAME.** The same temperature answer printed, in its table and again in its closing sentence, `Floor http://<namespace>#Rooftop`. Every other floor keys on a bare number, so the render path had only ever been exercised with '3' -- a NAMED location becoming a group is what exposed it. Fixed with `aggregate_lane._floor_name`, applied at all **seven** sites that render a floor key; the grouping KEY is untouched because sorting and matching use it. Numeric floors render identically (asserted for -2..11). Live: 'Floor Rooftop'.
**(2) RAW AUTOCAD MTEXT AS A ROOM NAME.** `\pxqc;{\fArial|...;Kitchen}` reached a reader as a room's label. MEASURED across this repository's floor-plan manifests: **26 of 354 spaces** carry such codes in their stored label. The DWG pipeline has always stripped them at INGEST; the manifests on disk predate that and **nothing stripped them on the way OUT**. Fixed in `shared.utils.strip_drawing_markup` and applied by the `Space` MODEL itself, so every consumer validates through it rather than each printing site needing to remember; `dwg_pipeline._strip_mtext_codes` now delegates to the same function, so the ingest and the read cannot disagree about what a label is (BUG-947's and BUG-1396's shape). All 26 clean, 0 dirty, plain labels byte-identical. Live: 'Where is the kitchen?' -> Rooms 2.66, 3.18, 5.26, no markup.
**STILL OPEN ON THIS ROW:** the register dumps -- an Incident and Near Miss Log shown for 'Are the doors locked' and bare `bldg:access/APG-001` IRIs for a question about mould. Those are a different cause (an unsummarised register shown raw) and are not fixed.
**AND WRITING THE FIX COST ME THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE MORE:** a building literal in a docstring (caught by the literal guard, third time today) and a shell heredoc that turned `\\f` into a form feed and `\\(.)`into `\(.)`-- one of which was a VALID regex that would have silently matched nothing (lesson #125).

--- THIRD PART, offline 2026-10-01; live re-ask owed: 'Are the doors locked' ---
The raw incident log is no longer the worst of it: the AFTER capture reads 'Yes, the door was secured; access log reviewed. *From the building's documents: Accessible Route Register, Incident And Near Miss Log.*' -- a past event about ONE door, composed from a passage, read back as the present state of all of them. `passage_relevance.is_live_state_question()` detects a yes/no question about a physical thing's PRESENT state ('are the doors locked', 'is the lift working', 'is the heating on today'); the capability lane then declines to compose from documents and says why, naming the documents it would have used. MEASURED over the 4,060 bank: 2 matches, both live-state asks ('Is the heating on today?', 'Are the solar panels working?'). 'open'/'closed' count only with an explicit 'now', because 'Is the building open today?' is an opening-hours question a document DOES answer.
Tests: `tests/test_a_document_does_not_answer_a_live_state.py`, 18 pass.
The mould question (#17) now answers from general knowledge plus the humidity rule and no longer dumps APG IRIs -- unchanged by anything here, CAVEAT-891 variance.

If the building records a live point for it, ask for that point's current reading." The 'Yes, the door was secured' is gone. Remaining on this row: nothing reproduced in this round.

Title: The host cycled Docker three times and killed Ollama mid-measurement, and the system's answers degraded silently rather than erroring
Description:
During tail O the host restarted the Docker stack at least twice (every container 'Up About a minute', `RestartCount=0`, `OOMKilled=false`, `ExitCode=0` -- a clean external stop/start, not a crash) and **killed Ollama, which did not come back**: `ollama.exe` was absent from the host process list and `127.0.0.1:11434` returned nothing.
**HOST MEMORY WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM** -- 95.2 GiB total, 56.4 GiB free, 40.8% used, largest process `vmmemWSL` at 11.3 GiB. This is NOT BUG-1194's shape, and checking that first is what stopped an hour going into the wrong explanation.
**WHAT THE SYSTEM DID ABOUT IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** It did not error. It returned *"I wasn't able to generate an answer just now. Please try asking again in a moment"* (6 times) and *"Here are the readings themselves. The readings could not be summarised. No conclusion has been drawn from them"* (8 times) -- **14 of 60 answers, every one of them honest and none of them an answer.** The orchestrator logged `circuit breaker is OPEN - the ollama provider has been unresponsive` 134 times. A reader would see a system that is up and unhelpful, which is the correct behaviour and is indistinguishable, from the answer alone, from a system that cannot answer the question.
Three long background runs were killed by the cycles (exit 4 each time): the first tail O pass at 17 of 60, the re-ask at 6 of 14, and the `ollama serve` wrapper.
Root_Cause: The Docker cycling is external and unattributed -- not memory, not OOM, not the container's own exit. Ollama runs as a host process outside compose, so nothing in the stack restarts it when the host takes it down. The degradation reached the reader as honest non-answers because the circuit breaker and the lane fallbacks both worked.
Fix_Approach:
FOR THE MEASUREMENT, done: check `127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags` and `docker logs | grep -c 'circuit breaker is OPEN'` BEFORE and AFTER any quality run, and treat a non-zero breaker count as invalidating. Run long captures in short bursts that survive a restart.
FOR THE SYSTEM, not attempted and worth a decision: a provider outage currently produces 14 honest non-answers rather than one visible 'the model is unavailable' state. For a trial that distinction matters -- a user cannot tell 'the building does not know' from 'the model is down', and only the second is worth retrying. The breaker already knows; nothing the reader sees says so.
Verification:
FIXED 2026-10-01. `circuit_breaker.model_is_unavailable()` reads the shared 'llm' breaker, and the general-knowledge fallback now distinguishes the two causes:
    'The language model this assistant uses is not responding at the moment, so I can't write an answer. **This is not a gap in the building's records** - the same question should work once it is back. Please try again shortly.'
The ordinary wording is kept for the other case, because a question that genuinely cannot be answered must not blame the model -- a test asserts both are present.
HALF_OPEN counts as unavailable: a probing breaker is not a working model, and the reader should still be told to retry. The check never raises -- a fallback path must not fail while explaining a failure, and a test sets the registry to None to prove it.
**WHAT IS NOT FIXED:** the other eight shapes this outage produced ('the readings could not be summarised') come from different lanes and still carry no cause. The general-knowledge path was taken first because it produced six of the fourteen.
Tests: `tests/test_a_dead_model_says_so.py`, 6 pass, with the shared breaker singleton restored by a fixture so the registry is left as it was found. Slice `-k 'circuit or breaker or general_knowledge'`: 60 pass.

SECOND SHAPE FIXED 2026-10-01: `sql_agent`'s 'The readings could not be summarised.' now says, when `model_is_unavailable()`, 'The language model that writes the summary is not responding at the moment, so the readings are listed without one. This is not a gap in the building's records; the same question should summarise once it is back.' The ordinary wording is kept for every other failure.

Title: Two kitchen counts a minute apart: three from the room records, two inferred from waste-bin sensor names
Description:
FOUND WHILE VERIFYING BUG-1407's label fix, which is the only reason two asks sat side by side. Live, occupant01 on /v1, same restart, cache flushed:
    Q 'Where is the kitchen?'
    A '**The building records a Kitchen on floors 2, 3 and 5:** - Floor 2: Room 2.66 - Floor 3: Room 3.18 - Floor 5: Room 5.26 _From the building's own room records._'
    Q 'How many kitchens are in the building?'
    A 'There are **two kitchens** in the building. ... - **Floor 2 Kitchen** - indicated by the sensor `WasteBin_Fill_F2_Kitchen` (recycling bin fill level sensor). - **Floor 3 Kitchen** - indicated by the sensor `WasteBin_Fill_F3_Kitchen` ... These sensors confirm that each kitchen has a dedicated waste-bin monitoring point.'
**THREE AND TWO, A MINUTE APART.** The first answer is right and says where it came from. The second counts rooms by looking at SENSOR NAMES, finds two waste-bin sensors, and reports the count of sensors as the count of kitchens -- then offers the sensor names as confirmation, which is circular. Room 5.26 has no waste-bin sensor and therefore does not exist as far as that answer is concerned.
Also prints internal sensor identifiers (`WasteBin_Fill_F2_Kitchen`) to a reader.
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED. A 'how many X' question went to a lane that had sensors in hand and counted them, while 'where is X' went to the room records. BUG-877B's shape -- a confident 'all rooms have a temperature sensor' narrated from a TOTAL sensor count -- and the same lesson: a count of instruments is not a count of the things they are attached to.
Fix_Approach: NOT ATTEMPTED. The pair is the test case: the two questions should agree, and the room records are the authority for how many rooms of a kind exist. Worth checking first whether the spatial lane that answered 'where' can be reached by 'how many', because the right answer already exists one lane over -- the recurring finding of lessons #133 and #136.
Verification:
FIXED OFFLINE 2026-10-01; live re-ask owed. DIAGNOSED FROM THE LOG: intent metadata -> `[sparql] resolved ['Kitchen'] -> 2 point(s), e.g. ['bldg:WasteBin_Fill_F2_Kitchen', 'bldg:WasteBin_Fill_F3_Kitchen']` -- the entity was resolved to POINTS and the narration counted them. `room_type_lookup.answer_live('How many kitchens are in the building?')` already returns '**3 rooms are recorded as Kitchen** ... Floor 2: Room 2.66, Floor 3: Room 3.18, Floor 5: Room 5.26' from the room records (probed in-container); the metadata lane simply never asked it (lessons #133/#136 again). `SPARQLAgent._rooms_of_kind` now asks it FIRST in `generate_query`, restricted to the 'rooms' shape so the floor-plan lane keeps 'which floor is X on'. MEASURED over the 4,060 bank: the lookup claims 0 of 2,281 rooms-shaped questions, so the hook acts only on the plain shape.
Tests: `tests/test_a_count_of_rooms_comes_from_the_room_records.py`, 5 pass.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02: 'How many kitchens are in the building?' -> '**3 rooms are recorded as Kitchen** (2 Staff Break Room / Kitchen, 1 Kitchen): Floor 2 Room 2.66, Floor 3 Room 3.18, Floor 5 Room 5.26 _From the building's own room records._' (lane metadata, method room_records). 'Where is the kitchen?' still answers the same three. The pair agrees.

Title: 'There are no free parking spots available at the moment' asserted from two EV charger status points
Description:
FOUND BY THE TAIL O RE-ASK (TODO-1404). Live, occupant01 on /v1, cache flushed:
    Q 'Are there any free parking spots available right now?'
    A '**Answer** There are no free parking spots available at the moment. The latest readings from the EV charger status sensors (both measured at 2026-10-01 18:08:57) show a value of **0** for each charger. The sensor units are not recorded, so the value is simply a numeric reading.'
**TWO EV CHARGER STATUS POINTS ARE NOT A PARKING OCCUPANCY SURVEY.** The answer states a definite, actionable fact about the whole car park from two chargers whose unit it admits in the same breath it does not know. A reader deciding whether to drive in is told there is no space.
This is the WORST shape in the taxonomy -- confident and wrong -- and it is a REGRESSION in kind on this question: the previous pass answered with meeting-room booking status, which was useless but did not assert a conclusion.
A `parking_data` store and a Transport Parking amenity exist; `Parking_Occupancy_Sensor` is 1 point in the graph, so whether the building can answer this at all is a separate question from whether it may answer it from EV chargers.
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED. The binding found EV-charger status points for a parking question and the narration turned '0' into 'no free spots'. Two candidate mechanisms, not separated: the binder matching 'parking' vocabulary to charger points, and the narration drawing an availability conclusion from a status value whose meaning it says is unrecorded. The second is the dangerous half -- a value with no declared unit should not become a definite claim.
Fix_Approach:
NOT ATTEMPTED. The medium/quantity rule landed for temperature in BUG-1405 is the same shape one domain over: an EV charger's status is not a parking bay's occupancy, and the exclusion belongs on the CLASS. Measure it the same way -- count how many parking-ish points are chargers against how many are occupancy -- before changing the binding.
Independently and more cheaply: a value whose unit is 'not recorded' should not support a definite claim. The answer says so itself in the sentence after the claim.
Verification:
FIXED OFFLINE 2026-10-01; LIVE RE-ASK OWED (restart pending at the time of writing).
DIAGNOSED FROM THE CONTAINER LOG OF THE TURN, not guessed:
    [dialogue] HBCO concepts: ['parking_availability', 'empty_space']
    [sparql] class from HBCO concept 'parking_availability': ontosage:Parking_Occupancy_Sensor (1 candidate)
    Generated SPARQL ... returned 0 results  (the model's query was malformed)
    [sensor_binder] population bind for the building: 0 retrieved -> 512 bound (occupancy)
So the right class WAS found and the fallback binder then bound every occupancy point. Two defects in `sensor_binder.detect_quantities`, both in how a resolved CONCEPT is homed on the catalogue: (1) the home modality was the FIRST catalogue entry sharing any class, so {Occupancy_Count_Sensor, Parking_Occupancy_Sensor} was homed on plain occupancy (1 class in common) instead of parking_free (2), and the catalogue's label discriminator ('parking') was never copied onto the spec although the docstring said it was; (2) the bare lay term 'available' resolves `empty_space`, which maps to every occupancy class, and nothing preferred the specific sibling over the generic one.
FIX, keyed on the CATALOGUE'S STRUCTURE (a label-split sibling), no word and no building: `_home_modality` picks the modality sharing MOST classes (a tie goes to the one WITHOUT a discriminator -- 'how many people' is occupancy, not parking; the first draft had that backwards and `test_how_many_people_binds_the_count_sensor_only` caught it), the concept spec inherits `label_contains`, and `_prefer_label_split` drops a generic spec that shares a class with a label-split spec the reader asked for by name. The EV charger points (brick:Occupancy_Status, label 'Charging State Sensor - EV Charger N') cannot pass label_contains=('parking',); the one `building_sat_parking_free [bays]` point can.
Measured: the binder slice 479 pass + 61 place tests; bank blast radius run in-container (see the row's next update for the count).
Tests: `tests/test_a_parking_question_binds_the_parking_point.py` (synthetic catalogue, no building assumed), 13 pass.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02 00:48, occupant01 on /v1, both caches flushed: 'Are there any free parking spots available right now?' -> 'At 2026-10-02 00:48:45 there was **1 free parking spot** (reported by the sensor *building parking_free [bays]*) ... average 2.78, min 1, max 5.' The ONE parking point is bound; the two EV-charger flags are gone; the confident 'no free parking' is gone. 'How many parking bays are free right now, including accessible ones?' -> '1.00 bays are free right now' from the same point.
BANK BLAST RADIUS, measured in-container with the live resolver over the 4,060 bank (1,699 questions resolve a concept): 155 change their detected specs. In the 60 printed, every change is a NARROWING to the catalogue's own label discriminator -- lift_status 39, waste_fill 7, parking 3, filter_pressure 2 -- plus 6 window-concept cases that inherited 'door' from a tie between door_contact and window_contact (both own exactly {Contact_Sensor, Open_Close_Status}). That tie is now AMBIGUOUS and inherits nothing (`_inherited_discriminator`), pinned by test; the run predates that fix and those 6 revert. `equipment_working` is dropped on 3 lift questions, correctly (`_prefer_label_split`).
RESIDUE, new row CAVEAT-1412: the parking point's unit is narrated as 'people' / '2.78 people' -- the catalogue's unit for Occupancy_Count_Sensor is applied to a bay count.
Refs: TODO-1404; BUG-1405; BUG-1406; design contract #4; lesson #184; CAVEAT-1412

Title: A parking-bay count is narrated with the unit 'people'
Description: Found verifying BUG-1411. 'Are there any free parking spots available right now?' -> '1 free parking spot (reported by the sensor building parking_free [bays], unit people) ... the average number of free spots was 2.78 people'. The point is typed brick:Occupancy_Count_Sensor and ontosage:Parking_Occupancy_Sensor; the catalogue's unit for the Brick class ('people') is applied to a bay count. The number is right; the unit word is wrong.
Root_Cause: The unit comes from the MODALITY (occupancy -> people), not from the point. The label itself says '[bays]'. Not diagnosed beyond that.
Fix_Approach: TTL-first: give the point a unit triple (brick:hasUnit or the catalogue's unit field for parking_free = bays) and let the label-split modality carry its own unit. Check how the catalogue declares units per modality before touching the narration.
Verification:
FIXED 2026-10-02 (offline; live re-ask owed). DIAGNOSED: the parking modality ALREADY declares `unit: bays` in config/saturation_modalities.yaml; `modality_units.unit_for_sensor` took the FIRST spec whose `matches()` passed, and the generic `occupancy` entry ('persons') precedes `parking_free` in the file and matches the same class. Now the matching spec WITH a label discriminator wins -- the rule the binder applies when it homes a concept (BUG-1411), one module over. Tests: `tests/test_a_bay_count_is_not_a_people_count.py` (3, synthetic specs); slice `-k 'unit_for_sensor or modality_units or units'` 49 pass.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02 03:22: 'Are there any free parking spots available right now?' -> 'there are 2 free parking **bays** available ... average number of free bays was 1.27'. The unit is bays.
Refs: BUG-1411; BUG-521 (a quantity's unit must come from the quantity)

Title: A third cache, cache:intent:*, replays a stored classification and skips the routing contract
Description: Cost two restarts and three live re-asks on 2026-10-02. 'What is the function of your building?' kept routing metadata -> sensors after a routing-contract change that offline provably sent it to capability. The log line is 'Cache hit for intent detection: <hash>' -- `dialogue_agent` caches the DECISION keyed on the question (`decision_cache_key`, BUG-889), and the parse-stage `apply_contract` runs only on the uncached path, so a cached turn never sees a new or changed rule. Flushing resp_cache:* and cache:sparql* (the two the runbooks name) does not touch it. Nine keys were live under cache:intent:bldg1:general:<hash>:<hash>.
Root_Cause: The intent cache stores the POST-contract intent and the contract is inside the cached region. A routing rule is therefore not deployed for any question asked in the cache's lifetime before the rule changed.
Fix_Approach: Either run `apply_contract` AFTER the cache read (the contract is cheap and deterministic, so re-applying it to a cached classification is correct and makes a rule change take effect immediately), or key the cache on a hash of the contract's rule list. Until then: flush `cache:intent:*` with the other two after any routing change, and the runbooks say so. `scripts/ask_questions.py` flushes resp_cache only.
Verification: FIXED 2026-10-02 at the ROOT, not the runbook. `decision_cache_key` already carried a contract fingerprint -- `_routing_contract_fingerprint()` hashed the rules' NAMES and ORDER only. A rule BODY and a keyword list it reads (BUILDING_INFO_KWS) changed, no rule was added or reordered, and every cached decision stayed valid. The fingerprint now hashes `inspect.getsource(routing_contract)` as well, so any edit to the module retires the decisions it produced on the next restart; no flush step to remember. Tests: `tests/test_the_decision_cache_retires_when_a_rule_body_changes.py` (3). The three-flush runbook line stays true for the OTHER two caches and for a change made without a restart.
Refs: BUG-1406; BUG-889; BUG-662; lesson (flush both caches) -> three

Title: 'The other 5 floors have no sensor of this kind' computed from a capped candidate fetch, not from the graph
Description: Found live 2026-10-02 (occupant01, /v1): 'Are the CO2 levels normal?' -> 'Based on 8 CO2 sensors on 1 floor ... This building records CO2 on one floor only (Floor 5); the other 5 floors have no sensor of this kind.' The graph holds **280** CO2 points with a timeseries across the floors (checked by SPARQL, no namespace asserted). Tail P #47 ('How is the air quality right now') carried the same sentence over 34 of 68 handed sensors. BUG-881's shape: a lane told a reader what the BUILDING lacks from what the FETCH contained.
Root_Cause: concept -> class -> `_get_instances_for_class(limit=40)` returned 8 candidates -> a template over those 8 -> the aggregate lane's completeness note inferred every other floor's absence from the ranked set it was handed. Absence on a floor is a fact only the graph can state; nothing asked it.
Fix_Approach: FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02. `aggregate_support.build_floors_with_class_query` asks the graph which floors hold a point of the measurand's classes along the stated path (point -> space -> floor, the one scripts/floor_modality_matrix.py reads); `missing_floors_note` now says 'records no <noun> sensor on Floor X' ONLY for floors the graph shows empty and 'Floor A and Floor B also record <noun>, but those sensors were not in this read' otherwise; with no graph answer it claims nothing about sensors. The one-floor-only sentence requires the graph's agreement. Live: 'Are the CO2 levels normal?' -> '... Floor 0, Floor 1, Floor 2, Floor 3 and Floor 4 also record CO2, but those sensors were not in this read.' Tests: `tests/test_a_floor_is_sensorless_only_when_the_graph_says_so.py` (8). NOT fixed: the fetch itself still reads 8 of 280 -- the sentence is honest, the sample is still a sample.
Verification: See Fix_Approach; verified live 2026-10-02 03:21 after restart and a three-cache flush.

Title: 'How does the building do X?' answered by the reading lane with a table of readings -- 8 of tail P's 14 WEIRD
Description: Tail P (60 never-asked questions, 2026-10-02): 'how are water leak detected in hard to see areas?' -> nine flow readings plus an INVENTED four-step detection procedure; 'what systems are in place to ensure that the server room does not overheat?' -> the outside-air temperature; 'How are common areas managed to maintain comfort during busy times?' -> a list of occupancy sensors; 'are lights automatically adjusting properly?' (tail O #7, twice) -> a decline naming three unrelated registers while the Lighting topic says 'lights automatically adjust to maintain target lux levels'. Right subject, wrong kind of answer. The HVAC operating regime (REG-008 parking ventilation, REG-009 server-room cooling), the Lighting topic and the continuity register hold the real answers.
Root_Cause: Two mechanisms, both measured. (1) The question names a measurand ('temperature', 'noise', 'air quality'), so `capability_measurand_is_data` -- or the classifier itself -- sends it to a fetch; `ungrounded_question.handoff` knew design-standard, adequacy and advice shapes but not HOW-IS-IT-DONE. (2) In the capability lane, `topic_is_the_subject` permits ONE leftover content word, and the mechanism frame ('automatically', 'adjusting', 'properly', 'current', 'conditions') is five, so the Lighting topic was discarded as not the subject (CAVEAT-1394's threshold, met from the other side).
Fix_Approach:
FIXED. `ungrounded_question.mechanism_question` (how does/is/are ... managed, controlled, detected, kept, prevented, ensured ...; 'what systems are in place'; 'what does the building/AI do if'; 'is/are ... automatically'; 'where does ... come from'), excluding any present-value ask, hands the question to the capability lane. MEASURED over the 4,060 bank: 12 matches; 16 of tails O+P. `topic_is_the_subject` discounts `_MECHANISM_FRAME` (no subject noun in it) for that shape only; a real second subject ('pollen exposure during the spring' vs Smart Controls) still leaves three words and still fails, and BUG-601's plain asks are untouched.
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02 08:40, viewer01 (role=readonly, confirmed from the server's [forwarded-user] line) on /v1, three caches flushed after restart. 7 of 10 mechanism questions answer from the building's own topics or regimes: lights x2 (Lighting topic), overheating (HVAC zoning + regime), common-area comfort (300 lux presence-detected lighting, hvac_operation.md), server room (environmental alarms, continuity register), car park air (REG-008, CO-linked), temperature stability (a continuity-register fragment -- grounded but thin). Three decline honestly instead of inventing (leak detection, AI air-quality action, noise origin). Tests: `tests/test_how_a_thing_is_done_is_not_a_reading.py` (30).
Verification: VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-02 08:40, viewer01 (role=readonly, confirmed from the server's [forwarded-user] line) on /v1, three caches flushed after restart. Routing/contract slices 247 + 307 pass; literal guard clean.
Refs: BUG-1406; CAVEAT-1394; BUG-601; BUG-1396; tail P read; lesson #186

Title: A QUESTION about what the building does is routed to `control` and refused as a command
Description: Tail Q (2026-10-02, occupant01): 'If 3 people enter a room and the sensors see 2 leave do the lights turn off?' and 'Do ozone sensors alert people or do they just activate ventilation or filtration?' -> 'You don't have permission to control building systems (role: occupant)'. Neither is a command; both are questions about behaviour, and the routing precedence rules say questions are not commands.
Root_Cause: NOT DIAGNOSED. 'turn off' / 'activate' inside a question is read by `is_control_command`; the question-not-command guard (tests/test_a_question_is_never_an_actuation_command.py) does not cover the 'if ... do the X turn off?' and 'do X alert ... or activate' shapes.

Title: Every follow-up that points at the PREVIOUS REPLY failed: ordinal, 'that report', 'there' over several rooms, a location statement, 'the two'
Description: 20-conversation battery (docs/phase0/conversations/, occupant01, 47 turns, read in full): 14 of 27 follow-up turns acceptable. Every follow-up that SUPPLIES a value worked; every one that POINTS at what the assistant just said failed -- 'what is the temperature in the first one?' after ten rooms (no rewrite, a decline); 'the first one, is it booked today?' -> 159 bookings for the BUILDING; 'how warm is it there?' after three kitchens -> the model picked one (2.66, then 'the kitchen'); 'is it free this afternoon?' after Room 1.06 -> the register LABEL pasted into the rewrite; 'I am in room 3.01' after a nearest question -> answered from the documents; 'which of the two is busier?' after the user named 1.06 and 2.01 -> asked which two.
Root_Cause: Three causes. (1) `_is_followup_query` split on whitespace so 'one?' was not 'one' and knew no location statement, so the rewrite never ran. (2) BUG-940's guard `rewrite_invents_a_place` refuses ANY assistant-named place, including the one in the reply being replied to. (3) The model's rewrite is a guess when the reply named several rooms, and pastes labels when it named one.
Fix_Approach: Deterministic resolvers in context_switch that read ONLY the reply being replied to or the user's own earlier turns, run BEFORE the follow-up gate and before any model: resolve_ordinal, resolve_report_reference, resolve_sole_room_anaphor ('it'/'there' -> 'room X' when the reply named exactly one), resolve_location_statement, resolve_pair_reference; ambiguous_reference ASKS which when the reply named several (coref_ambiguous_places -> clarification in detect_intent); previous_reply_named_it lets the guard accept the reply's own room while BUG-940's six-turns-back case stays refused (pinned). `_is_followup_query` tokenises on words.
Verification: Live pass 2 (occupant01, resolvers BEFORE the gate, full answers in docs/phase0/conversations_2026-10-02_reask2.jsonl): c02 'the first one' -> the reading of node 2.13 (24.49 C); c05 'which of the two is busier?' -> compare lane, 'Room 1.06 is busier' (27 vs 24 people); c06 'that report' -> 'Report REP-565C10 ... Status: OPEN'; c08 'I am in room 3.01' -> 'The toilet nearest 3.01 is on the same floor: Male washroom - Floor 3'; c13 'it' -> 'room 1.06' (the events lane then declined: BUG-1432); c19 'the first one, is it booked today?' -> '1 booking for Room 1.06 today'. c03 (three kitchens) asked which only after the concept-stage rescue was taught the marker (pass 3, reask3.jsonl). Title: The deliberation lane's answer contradicts itself: '(noise: 60.342, occupancy_status: 0.776) (no data: occupancy_status)' on one row
Description: c21 'Which quiet rooms are free in the next hour?': 'The readings don't separate these spaces', three academic offices at ~60 dB named as what was measured, each row carrying a value AND 'no data' for the same modality; 4 occupancy_status readings 1.18-1.39 excluded as outside 0..1. Root_Cause: DIAGNOSED 2026-10-04 (contradiction half): a duplicate constraint for one modality (occupancy_status resolved via two source phrases) put ONE real-valued and ONE None-valued CriterionScore into the same ScoredCandidate.criteria list; build_dossier's dict-comprehension kept whichever came last while data_gaps is a SEPARATE list appended independently, so a modality with a real value could still be listed as a gap. DIAGNOSED 2026-10-07 (banding half, no code defect found): no code anywhere attaches the word 'quiet' to a specific reading; it appears only in clarify_policy.build_assumptions' disclosure of how the user's lay term 'quiet' was interpreted (scored as minimize noise against the cited WHO 30-70 dB(A) band), and the scorer's own utility for 60.342 dB is 0.24 -- closer to the band's bad end than its good one, never labelled 'quiet'.

Changed to prefer a non-None value over None regardless of order; a genuine gap (no value anywhere) still reports as a gap. 2026-10-07: the 'calls 60 dB quiet' half was investigated and needed no fix -- StandardsEngine carries no noise/sound parameter to migrate the band to, and the WHO 30-70 dB(A) citation is the same real, cited standard already pinned by test_scorer_unanchored.py; the wording concern was the bug report's own paraphrase of the Assumptions disclosure sentence, not a mislabel in the rendered answer.
Verification: tests/test_g5_dossier_row_does_not_contradict_itself.py (2/2): the exact live contradiction shape no longer occurs, and a genuine data gap with no value anywhere is still reported. Full unit suite green alongside it. 2026-10-07: tests/test_bug_1424_render_text_consistency_and_noise_band.py (5/5) exercises render_answer() end to end (not only the dossier structure): confirms no rendered row ever pairs a real value with a 'no data' marker for the same modality, confirms 60.342 dB scores utility 0.24 under the WHO band (not 'quiet'), and confirms the only occurrence of 'quiet' in the rendered text is the honest Assumptions disclosure, never a per-row verdict. Title: The gate's air-pressure decline marker had gone stale; the answer was never wrong
Description: Running the 51-case gate alone after today's evidence-panel work, case #70 ('What is the air pressure in room 2.01 right now?') reported REGRESSED declined -> answered. Root_Cause: A marker string in scripts/regression_answerability.py's _DECLINE_MARKERS pinned one exact phrasing; the live decline's wording changed without the marker being re-measured. The fourth instance of this gate's own instrument going stale on this exact case family (CAVEAT-1398, CAVEAT-1402, BUG-1401 precede it).
Fix_Approach: Added 'there is no recorded air-pressure sensor' to _DECLINE_MARKERS alongside the older phrasing (both now recognised). Verified: 0 of the 73 stored pack answers reclassified (57 answered / 2 refused / 14 declined, unchanged).

Title: Gate case #70's decline wording varies between asks (CAVEAT-891's shape); not a marker gap
Description: After fixing CAVEAT-1414's marker drift and re-verifying clean, re-running the gate a THIRD time produced a THIRD distinct wording for the same decline: 'I'm sorry, but there is no air-pressure sensor listed for Room 2.01, so I don't have a current pressure reading to share.' -- matching neither the original marker nor the one added for CAVEAT-1414. The route and the DECISION (decline) are stable across all three asks; only the LLM's phrasing of the decline varies.
Root_Cause: This decline is LLM-narrated, not templated, so its exact wording is not deterministic across identical asks -- the same class CAVEAT-891 documents extensively elsewhere in this project ('the route is deterministic, the answer is not').
Fix_Approach: DELIBERATELY NOT adding a third fixed-substring marker. Chasing LLM phrasing variance with literal markers is open-ended and has been measured to not converge elsewhere in this project. The underlying BEHAVIOUR (the system correctly declines; no fabricated pressure value) is unaffected and is the property that matters. If this case keeps flagging, the right fix is a semantic decline classifier for this one case, not another string.
Verification: Confirmed across three live asks on 2026-10-03: the ANSWER always declines honestly; only the gate's STRING classifier disagrees with itself about the wording.

Title: A register's overdue-but-unmarked facts were gated on the question's wording
Description: register_facts.passed_due_not_marked only ran when the question matched _OVERDUE_RE (overdue|past due|late|behind schedule|out of date|lapsed). A question like 'is this approval still valid?' never saw the records this function already finds past their due date but not marked overdue -- six of forty-three approvals in the measured case (TRIAL_TRACKER.csv row E3).

Fix_Approach: Removed the _OVERDUE_RE.search(question) gate from passed_due_not_marked. The caller's own completeness_line() already filters out anything the narration already mentioned and returns '' on an empty list, so the change is additive only: a register question with no overdue-but-unmarked rows is unaffected.
Verification: tests/test_a_register_answer_is_counted_not_narrated.py 26/26, including two new tests for the exact acceptance wording and the inverted old assertion documented inline.

Title: analytics_agent ignores the named calendar day -- 'yesterday' and 'the day before yesterday' give an identical window
Description: Found while verifying G7/BUG-1430 live. 'How much energy did the building use yesterday?' and the same question with 'the day before yesterday' in place of 'yesterday', asked as two FRESH, independent, non-follow-up conversations, returned a BYTE-IDENTICAL answer: 382 kWh over '02 Oct 23:08 - 03 Oct 22:48' for both. Two calendar days apart named, one window computed.
Root_Cause: aggregate_lane logged 'not claimed: measurand=None' for this question both times, so its calendar_day_bounds-aware window resolver (aggregate_lane.py ~line 348) never ran. The question falls through to analytics_agent (LLM Python-code generation), which does NOT import requested_interval.calendar_day_bounds at all (confirmed by grep across the orchestrator tree) and appears to generate a fixed 'most recent ~24h' window irrespective of which calendar day, if any, the question names. Two causes, both measured in source. (1) calendar_day_bounds scanned an unordered dict and took the first bare-word match, so 'the day before yesterday' resolved one day back, the same window as 'yesterday'. (2) analytics computed over whatever rows the fetch returned, and the fetch window is set upstream; nothing narrowed the rows to the named day.
Fix_Approach: FIXED. requested_interval: longest-phrase day resolution (_named_day_word) with 'day before yesterday' = 2 days back. New rows_in_window() and restrict_to_named_day() keep only the rows inside the named day (store clock, inclusive; aware timestamps converted to UTC). _analytics_node narrows data once, before the deterministic path, the saved file and the LLM code; AnalyticsAgent.analyze narrows too, and its no-data message names the day. Fails open and says so (checked=False) when no row has a readable timestamp. Not changed: state.query_results and the upstream fetch window.
Verification: tests/test_bug1437_named_day_narrows_analytics.py 15/15: 'the day before yesterday' resolves to 2026-10-05 (was 2026-10-06 before the fix; pre-fix behaviour read from HEAD source, not run), the two named days give different store windows, rows are kept per named day, timezone-aware rows compare in UTC, fail-open path, analytics no-data names the day asked about. Related existing suites (test_a_named_day_is_a_date_not_a_duration, test_the_requested_interval_is_resolved_once, test_the_period_a_question_names_is_the_period_fetched, test_past_window_fold, analytics tests): 139 passed with the new file. black and flake8 F821/F823 clean. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: whether the upstream fetch covers the named day on a running stack. If it does not, the answer now declines for that day rather than computing over other rows.

Title: isort --profile black silently used 88 columns instead of this project's 100
Description: The night's own final clean suite run found one failure: test_d11_panel_is_wired_into_response_node.py pinned a one-line import that isort had wrapped into a 3-line parenthesized form with a trailing comma (black's 'magic trailing comma' then refuses to re-collapse it). The import fit in 97 chars at its indentation -- under this repo's 100-column limit, over isort's --profile black bundled 88-column default. Every lint command run this session used 'isort --profile black -q <files>' with no --line-length flag, so black (invoked with --line-length 100) and isort (silently 88) disagreed on every line in that 12-char gap.
Root_Cause: --profile black configures STYLE conventions, not line length -- it does not inherit a project's own --line-length override passed to black separately.
Fix_Approach: Collapsed the one import the suite actually caught, then swept all 17 files touched this session with 'isort --profile black --line-length 100' + 'black --line-length 100' together. 7 files had the same latent wrap (none behaviour-changing); re-ran every test file touched tonight fresh (124/124) to confirm. Going forward this session's own lint commands always pass --line-length 100 to both tools together.
Verification: 124/124 across every test file edited or added tonight, run fresh after the fix. Lesson #194.

Title: 'Working Hours' absorbs any question using 'close'/'open'/'what time', winning over a more specific topic
Description: Found while live-verifying F11. 'and what time does it close?' after a reply naming the Café correctly rewrites to 'what time does the cafe close?' (F11 working as designed), but the capability resolver then answers with the BUILDING's generic Working Hours topic, not the Cafe's own hours. Working Hours declares the bare lay terms 'close', 'open', 'what time' -- common framing words for ANY amenity's hours, not unique to the building's own operating schedule.
Root_Cause: subject_facts judged each matched topic alone. 'what time does the cafe close?' matched the generic Working Hours topic and the catering topic. Working Hours declares 'close' and 'what time', so after those were covered it was left with {cafe}: one word, inside the single-word allowance, so it qualified. Catering's own terms cover 'cafe' but not 'close' or 'time', so it was left with {time, close} and failed. The generic hours topic answered.
Fix_Approach: capability_graph_resolver: (1) _subject_leftover is now the ONE place the leftover is computed (topic_is_the_subject and subject_facts both read it). (2) An opening-hours SHAPE (_HOURS_QUESTION_RE) strips _HOURS_FRAME words for every topic, as the mechanism and quantifier shapes already do. The shape is what makes them frame: 'hours' in 'the next 12 hours' stays a subject (BUG-1396, pinned). (3) subject_facts drops a topic whose leftover contains a word that a matched topic FULLY explaining the question (empty leftover) declares. A looser variant (any other topic's declared word) was measured and rejected: it dropped right answers on guest wifi, fire exit from the kitchen and a car-park question. Same matcher throughout (no second matcher added).
Verification: Offline, not live. Real topics from bldg1_capabilities.ttl (read only): before, 'what time does the cafe close?' -> ['Working Hours']; after -> ['Catering Amenities']. 'when does the cafe open' -> both before, Catering only after. 'what time does the building close?' still -> Working Hours. Blast radius over 4,207 bank questions with the resolver's own _score as the match: matched 2,194 before and after; subject set moved on 2 questions. 'Does your building have smoke detectors' Smoking Policy dropped (improvement); 'What's the fire assembly point' Emergency Evacuation dropped, Fire Safety kept (its answer text also gives the assembly point). Measured again 2026-10-07 over docs/smart_building_questions.csv (4,060 rows; 2,117 with a candidate; bldg1 triples; the resolver prefilter): the integration rule-1/rule-2 variant moved 1 subject set (Q052 nearest fire exit from the third-floor kitchen: Fire Safety lost, Catering kept, wrong) and this variant moved 1 (Q213 Emergency Evacuation dropped, shared assembly point still answered); the two variants disagree on exactly those two. Routing-contract stand-down calls subject_facts too; its bank effect is the same 2 questions. Tests: tests/test_bug1439_hours_question_names_its_subject.py (12 pass and 2 strict xfail; the cases of tests/test_bug_1439_specific_topic_beats_the_hours_frame.py were folded in and that file removed; its integration rule-1/rule-2 variant was NOT kept), plus 2,708 passed over 103 related unit files. LIVE RE-ASK OWED: after a reply naming the cafe, ask 'and what time does it close?' and confirm the cafe's hours. NOTE: BUG-1438 (FIX_TRACKER, integration tree) describes this same defect, Working Hours absorbing a cafe closing question; this row is its fix. BUG-1438 is left OPEN for the owner to close against this row.

Title: /api/v1/admin/sensors/health reported EVERY sensor stale -- a 1-hour local-vs-UTC offset, not a dead publisher
Description: Called live while discharging H6's owed check. ALL 2,860 assessed sensors returned state=stale, every one at exactly 60.0 minutes old, which reads exactly like the data publisher had stopped an hour ago. It had not: data-publisher was 'Up 46 hours' and actively inserting rows; MAX(datetime) for a checked co2 sensor was ~1 minute old in UTC.
Root_Cause: orchestrator/main.py sensors_health() computed BOTH `now` (UTC, correct) and `local_now` (the building's local zone, BST=UTC+1), then passed local_now.replace(tzinfo=None) -- not now -- to assess_sensor(), against stamps that are naive UTC (every store is UTC, BUG-403's family). A UTC-vs-local comparison produced a systematic ~60-minute offset on every single sensor uniformly, which is what made it look like a dead publisher rather than a measurement bug.
Fix_Approach: One-line change: now.replace(tzinfo=None) in place of local_now.replace(tzinfo=None). now was already computed correctly two lines earlier in the same function and simply never used for this comparison.
Verification: Live before/after via the real endpoint as admin: stale count 2,860 -> 0; the same sensor's age_minutes went from 60.0 to 0.2. tests/test_h6_sensor_health_uses_utc_not_local_time.py 3/3, including a test that reproduces the exact bug shape (a UTC timestamp against a one-hour-ahead naive clock) so the defect's shape stays on record.

Title: A tracker-id-shaped citation inside an rdfs:comment LITERAL ships as real graph data, in both a new E5 file and the pre-existing shared schema
Description: test_tracker_ids_never_reach_a_reader_or_the_model.py's shipped-TTL walk failed on 'BUG-194' found as a graph literal, not a developer comment. Two independent sources: (1) scripts/generate_precedence_ttl.py's own document_derived tier comment (introduced this session, E5) wrote "...BUG-194's shape." into input/bldg1_source_precedence.ttl's rdfs:comment; (2) ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl -- building-AGNOSTIC, shipped into every building via ttl_uploader as urn:ontosage:ttl:ontosage_schema.ttl -- carries the same reference on ontosage:derivedFromDocument's own rdfs:comment, pre-existing and unrelated to this session's work. A tracker id inside DATA (not a `#` comment) is exactly the thing prompt_hygiene.strip_tracker_ids exists to never need to strip from a reader-facing answer -- it should simply never be there.
Root_Cause: Prose referencing an internal ticket by its tracker-style id (BUG-NNN) was written directly into a string destined to become RDF graph data (an rdfs:comment literal), in two unrelated authoring passes. The shape regex `(?:BUG|CAVEAT|TODO|KNOWN|FIX)-\d{1,4}[A-Z]?` makes no distinction between a developer's internal citation and a building's own data once both are literal text in the graph.
Fix_Approach: Removed the tracker-id citation from both comments, keeping the substantive explanation (what the rank means / what the marker prevents) without naming an internal ticket. Regenerated input/bldg1_source_precedence.ttl and re-uploaded it live (sha changed, confirmed in ttl_uploader's log) after flushing all three caches. Widened test_no_id_the_shipped_ttl_carries_is_mistaken_for_a_tracker_id's glob to also scan ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl -- it reaches more buildings than any single bldg1_*.ttl file and had never been covered.
Verification: Found by the full unit-suite checkpoint, 2026-10-04 (14,341 pass before this fix). Live SPARQL against the bldg repository confirmed BUG-194 present in urn:ontosage:ttl:ontosage_schema.ttl before the schema fix and absent after, on both graphs, following a restart + re-upload + triple cache flush. tests/test_tracker_ids_never_reach_a_reader_or_the_model.py 16/16 fresh, including the widened glob now covering the schema file.

Title: Day energy headline is the last reading of the day, not the day's total (4.44 kWh shown, 374.42 kWh actual)

Description: BUG-1442 fixed sparql_agent._floor_scoped_sparql and aggregate_lane.measurand_from_classes to read the quantity from the graph's Brick class. Title: "When was room 2.01 last comfortable?" live-routes to the AV readiness register and answers about projector/display/microphone status
Description: Diagnosed before any fix was attempted: a comfort-HISTORY question ("when was room 2.01 last comfortable?") reached readiness_check and was answered from the AV register's projector/display/microphone status -- no source and date relevant to comfort at all. No deterministic rule matched the AV register for this shape: neither record_registry term scoring nor any _READINESS_RE branch fires on "comfortable". The TTL's comfort terms sit on ontosage:Intent_Comfort / hbco:overall_comfort / hbco:thermal_comfort, which answeredBy Src_TimeSeriesDB/Src_Analytics -- not readiness.
Root_Cause: The LLM intent classifier is picking `readiness_check` directly on a broad reading of its own description ("is a space ready to be used..."), since no deterministic rule claims the question either way before classification.
Fix_Approach: Added one parse-stage routing_contract.py rule, comfort_history_not_readiness, placed directly after readiness_check: fires ONLY when the incoming intent is already readiness_check AND the query matches a narrow when/how-long-ago/last-time + comfort(able) regex AND does NOT match _READINESS_RE. Title: An energy-total headline for a named day presents a partial-day sum as the whole day's total, with no coverage disclosure
Description: Live: "The building consumed 690 kWh on 6 October" headlined the sum of readings that covered only 14:02 to 22:53 of that day (9 of 24 hours, store/UTC time printed with no local conversion) as though it were the day's total. series_summary.summarise_energy_totals() computes the sum and the measured first/last stamps (~line 298 and ~294-295) but the only coverage instruction was advisory prompt text (~309-317, "if it is shorter, say so") that the model read and ignored. evidence/completeness.py (BUG-1444, this round) measures gaps from a DECLARED cadence (ontosage:archivalIntervalS) and only fires on an explicit "is complete"/"no gaps" prose claim -- it has no caller in the energy path and does not fit this shape (no completeness claim is made; the defect is a silent OMISSION, not a false claim), so a local first/last-vs-window check was built in summarise_energy_totals itself instead, per the task's own allowance.
Root_Cause: FETCH VS DATA (read-only, no live DB in this worktree -- LEANS DATA, NOT CONFIRMED): bldg1 declares only 6 energy_data UUIDs (Electrical Energy Meter, Floor 0-5, bldg1_narrow_publish_map.json), so MAX_FETCH_ROWS(200000)//6=33333 and BUG-591's row-limit scaling (interval_hours*120) would give ~2880 rows/meter for a 24h window when start_date AND end_date are both set -- comfortably above any plausible cadence, making the mysql_narrow_adapter.py:234 ORDER BY datetime DESC LIMIT per-uuid cap an unlikely cause for just 6 meters. A genuine structural gap WAS found: requested_interval.calendar_day_bounds/_CALENDAR_DAYS only recognises relative words (yesterday/today/the day before yesterday); an explicit date like "6 October" is NOT resolved by it, so dialogue_agent's BUG-480 override (line ~2156) never fires for it and both the SQL fetch bounds AND analytics_agent's restrict_to_named_day (BUG-1437) post-filter fall back to whatever the LLM's own time_range extraction produced for that turn -- non-deterministic by construction. Whether the 14:02 start is the energy_data table genuinely holding no earlier rows that day (plausible given bldg1's documented real-snapshot-plus-dev-mode-topup hybrid) or an LLM-mis-resolved start_date could not be settled without a live query.
Fix_Approach: Deterministic fix only (not prompt wording): summarise_energy_totals() gained window/tz_name params; when the measured stamps do not reach both ends of window (30-min jitter margin), the quotable headline itself switches from "Total over the period" to "Partial-period sum" and states the covered span in building-local time (THE READINGS FETCHED COVER ONLY HH:MM to HH:MM), never relying on the model to add the caveat. analytics_agent.analyze() resolves window from _named_window (BUG-1437) falling back to state.intermediate_results start_date/end_date (the bus bounds the sql node actually used, which also covers an absolute date), and passes window/tz_name through to _format_analysis (which has no `state` of its own) at both its call sites. The fetch-side investigation (mysql_narrow_adapter/sql_agent MAX_FETCH_ROWS) was read-only and inconclusive; no adapter change made -- too risky to guess at without a live query and a narrow 6-meter energy set makes it an unlikely primary cause.
Verification: Offline only. New tests/test_energy_total_states_partial_coverage_bug_1449.py (7 cases): partial-day coverage states the measured span and switches headline wording; full-day coverage (00:00-23:45) keeps the plain "Total" wording with no caveat -- the exact live-verification the coordinator must also run (ask for a day with data from 00:00 and confirm no false caveat appears); small edge jitter (<30 min) is not flagged; a real one-sided gap is flagged; no-window callers get BUG-1447's original wording unchanged; an unparseable window fails open. Title: A question about the PROVENANCE of the previous answer had no lane -- BUG-1427 closed
Description: Two shapes, both measured live/offline this session. (1) "what evidence supports that?" / "what data backed that up?" matched NEITHER answer_provenance.PROVENANCE_RE nor session_recall._ABOUT_MY_ANSWER and fell through to general_knowledge -- no lane at all, confirmed with apply_contract() (routing stayed 'general_knowledge', zero rules applied). (2) "what is the evidence behind your answer?" / "how did you arrive at that?" / "what was your previous answer based on?" are -- by design, BUG-1397, VERIFIED_LIVE -- routed to session_recall, the one lane that can say whether there was a previous answer. But the lane could only quote the past QUESTION back (session_recall.answer()), never the previous ANSWER's own recorded evidence_record, so asking for a BASIS produced "I have no record of you mentioning 'evidence', 'behind' or 'answer'" -- a confusing non-answer when a basis really was recorded one turn back (BUG-1397's own Verification field names this as its still-open half).
Root_Cause: (1) is a vocabulary gap in PROVENANCE_RE -- the regex only covered 'evidence behind/for' and the D7 phrasings, never the 'evidence SUPPORTS/BACKS/CONFIRMS it' shape. (2) is architectural: session_recall_node never read the evidence bus key at all -- it only had NOTES_KEY (the user's own past questions), so a question about the ASSISTANT's basis had nothing to read even though capability_agent's sibling 'how do you know that?' block (V7-T74) already proved the exact same Redis read works.
Fix_Approach: (1) widened PROVENANCE_RE with two new alternatives for the 'supports/backs/confirms' and 'backed/supports ... up' shapes, measured over docs/smart_building_questions.csv (4,060 rows) before shipping: is_provenance_question() hits went 4 -> 5, exactly 1 new move ('what evidence supports it' inside a wait-time question), 0 lost, 0 overlap with the existing pattern or with session_recall's own detector. Deliberately did NOT touch the two phrasings test_d7_provenance_detector_widened.py pins as session_recall's -- 'evidence behind/for your answer' and 'how did you arrive at that' stay exactly as BUG-1397 left them. (2) added answer_provenance.load_previous_turn_record() (the same redis_manager.load_state(conversation_id) read capability_agent's provenance block already does, factored out so the two lanes share one implementation) and session_recall._render_previous_answer_evidence(), called from session_recall_node BEFORE the quote-based answer() whenever the query matches _ABOUT_MY_ANSWER and a previous turn exists. It renders the previous turn's evidence_record through the SAME answer_provenance.render() the inline evidence panel uses -- sources by label ('CO2 Sensor 204', never a bare UUID), the kind of claim, when retrieved -- and falls through to the existing quote-based answer() untouched for every query that is not about the assistant's own answer (BUG-941's lane is unaffected). Honest declines: a record that legitimately assembled to NOT_ASSESSABLE (no lane produced evidence) renders as that, honestly, via the same render(); a previous turn with the evidence_record key entirely absent (old cached turn, or assembly raised) gets a new, named decline distinct from 'nothing asked yet'; no previous turn at all keeps the pre-existing 'Nothing has been asked in this conversation yet' message verbatim.
Verification: Unit-verified with a stubbed two-turn conversation: turn 1 recorded an evidence_record (sensor reading, 1 source), turn 2 asked 'What is the evidence behind your answer?' and 'How did you arrive at that?' -- both narrate the source by label, the claim kind ('observed -- read from an instrument'), and omit the raw UUID (tests/test_bug_1427_provenance_of_the_previous_answer.py, 20 cases). Confirmed a plain 'what did I ask you about earlier?' still uses the quote-based path unchanged. Confirmed against docs/smart_building_questions.csv that the PROVENANCE_RE widening adds exactly 1 hit (4 -> 5) with 0 regressions on D7/D7-LIVE/BUG-1397's own pinned cases -- full runs of test_answer_provenance.py, test_d7_provenance_detector_widened.py, test_d7_live_provenance_question_is_not_rewritten.py, test_how_a_thing_is_done_is_not_a_reading.py, test_a_question_about_the_conversation_is_not_about_the_building.py (one pre-existing, unrelated failure reproduced identically on df0b1e5 before this change -- test_the_detector_does_not_fire_on_the_catalogue, not touched by this fix), test_d2_d3_provenance_dict_shape.py, test_d11_d16_d18_inline_evidence_panel.py, test_scenario_boundary.py, test_evidence_projection_storage.py, test_evidence_always_on.py and test_routing_contract.py (396 passed; no parse-stage Rule object added, so the rule count/order pin is unchanged) -- all green.
